articles.excerpt: Crystal Palace at Craven Cottage. In case any fellow Fulham fans still have PTSD from facing Oliver Glasner’s 5-2-3, it’s probably worth putting out there that not all systems with the same numerical formation do the same things. Pierre Sage was hired to offer continuity for a squad built to play five at the back, but still offers Palace some new tactical dynamics. The issue is, player departures (both rumoured and actual) have meant his summer has perhaps been more about personnel than patterns. So, what should we expect in a clash of two sides hunting their first points of the season at the Cottage this Saturday? A summer of change Palace, like Fulham, have experienced a summer of change both in the dugout and on the pitch. Key men Maxence Lacroix and Daniel Muñoz have followed Oliver Glasner out the door, whilst the likes of Jean-Philippe Mateta, and Ismaïla Sarr were unsettled by links to big moves themselves. As a result, the XI that started against Man City on Friday night included only five players who started the FA Cup Final against them just over a year ago. articles.body: Man Utd: £54m Chelsea star’s reaction to INEOS interest emerges Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso and Manchester United manager Michael Carrick Chelsea winger Pedro Neto did not fancy a move to Manchester United and play under manager Michael Carrick, according to a report. According to TEAMtalk Man Utd were among the clubs that showed interest in signing Neto from Chelsea in the summer transfer window. The reliable transfer news outlet has claimed that Tottenham Hotspur, Liverpool and Manchester City also had ‘tentative interest’ in the Portugal international winger. Neto joined Chelsea from Wolves in the summer of 2024 for £54million. The 26-year-old, who is under contract at Chelsea until the summer of 2031, has made 106 appearances for the London club so far in his career, scoring 20 goals and providing 19 assists in the process. The Portuguese star has been assured by Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso that he will play a major role for the Blues this season. READ: Record-breaking Chelsea star already planning to leave in January after Xabi Alonso decision Pedro Neto did not fancy Man Utd transfer TEAMtalk has reported: ‘However, despite knowing that there was interest in him, Neto’s preference was to remain at Chelsea and fight for his place under Alonso. ‘We understand the 26-year-old has been guaranteed a role in Alonso’s plans and is very keen to show the new head coach that he can be an important player for the Blues.’ Chelsea made Cristian Romero mistake While Chelsea fans will be pleased that Neto did not leave for Man Utd or any other club, Gary Neville believes that the club’s owners, BlueCo, should have signed Cristian Romero from Tottenham Hotspur in the summer transfer window. Romero left Tottenham for Atletico Madrid this summer, and former Man Utd defender Neville believes that the Argentina international central defender would have been perfect for Alonso’s Chelsea. Neville said about Chelsea and Romero on The Overlap : “They conceded 60 odd goals Romero last season for Tottenham, I know he didn’t play all the time, but your eyes don’t deceive you about a player. make his debut against Ipswich Town this weekend. Press conferences for Gameweek 3 However, when speaking at Thursday’s press conference, Andoni Iraola hinted that bench duty may beckon at first. “He trained well with us. If everything goes well in today’s training, he will definitely be available for tomorrow. “I see him in a good place. He has trained with us, I think, three [times]. It’s true that he hasn’t had minutes in pre-season but he has been training normal with the group [at PSG]. Then it’s a decision that we have to make. I think he is in a good place but we also have to consider that he hasn’t had minutes in the pre-season games. – Andoni Iraola on Bradley Barcola “I think we preferred, in the end, to have the best players, than a player that maybe is specific only for that position. I think I’m very used, from my previous teams, to demanding all the wingers play on both sides. “I know they normally have their preferred position, but we’ve been playing with Víctor [Munoz], with Cody [Gakpo], with Rio [Ngumoha] in pre-season, in competition now, on the right side. I think probably all of them have played more on the left, but I would say, I’ve seen them in a good place on the right. Probably Rio is more specific for the left side, but I think he has also shown the willingness to improve and play on the right. “Even Bradley [Barcola], I think he’s very open and I think he can play right and left. He started actually more on the right side when he started with Olympique Lyonnais. “Obviously, it will depend on the match-ups, on what we consider for every game, but I’m happy with the four wingers we have and I’m sure we are going to be able to cover those two positions.” – Andoni Iraola on Liverpool’s inability to sign a right winger FPL reveal Barcola’s price + two others Injury-wise, Hugo Ekitike (Achilles), Conor Bradley (knee), Giovanni Leoni (knee), Joe Gomez (muscle) and Federico Chiesa (muscle) remain out for the Reds. Gomez is the only one due back before the September international break. “The closest one is Joe. Joe will probably start training with us next week. It has gone normally, the recovery from a muscle injury, more or less we were expecting the time on this. I hope we can have him before the break, let’s say. “I think the next one probably should be Giovanni Leoni. I think the plan is also to start training during the break, with the group. I think even Fede should be around those dates. Probably Conor, and especially Hugo, will go later, yes.” – Andoni Iraola With the ongoing injuries at right-back, Iraola was asked about the conversations he’s had with Dominik Szoboszlai about moving him into the back four, as happened in Gameweek 2, and whether he sees the Hungarian as an ongoing option at full-back. “I think since I started here, I’ve talked to a lot of players about the position where they prefer to play. But I haven’t found any situations where any player has told me, “No, I don’t want to play here.” I think everyone has shown the right attitude. I more or less know the preferred position of everyone. Sometimes it’s the same, I think, from them. Sometimes I say, “Okay, I see you maybe more here,” and we have discussions. But everyone is ready to help. “If we have to play him as a right winger, as a right-back, as a left-back, I think he’s ready to do it. I think he wants to help the team first. And I think it’s good also to have players who can cover different positions, especially now, probably, that we have some injuries and we need this versatility from the players. Having players like Dom, for me, is very valuable because even in the game, they allow me to change their positions. “Definitely, we look thin [at right-back], yes. But if you take two players from every position injured, you will always look thin. And now we are in that situation. That’s why I value Dom Szoboszlai, who can play right-back, [and] Ronald Araújo, who can also play right-back.” – Andoni Iraola on Dominik Szoboszlai and the versatility of his players Cody Gakpo is staying with the Reds after touted moves to Tottenham Hotspur and Manchester City failed to materialise, and Iraola is happy to have him still aboard. “Cody is a very smart player. I think also my relationship with him has been very honest since the beginning. He has performed with us, I would say, very well in all the pre-season games, in all the games. He scored the first day, assisted the next one. “He was always aware of the situations in the market. We were constantly talking with each other. He’s trained very well and I hope we keep him at the same level. I’m sure it’s going to be like this. I think he’s in a good place physically, mentally, and I’m very happy to keep Cody because, for me, he’s a very valuable player.” – Andoni Iraola on Cody Gakpo 0 Comments Login to Post a Comment No comments have been submitted for this post yet. FPL Q&A September 3 118 comments 3 September 2026 118 comments Five-time top 1k finisher Tom Freeman hosts our weekly Fantasy Premier League (FPL) Q&A, answering your burning questions. FPL Gameweek 3 Wildcard best team + pros/cons of using Score More Points. Win More Mini Leagues. Join FFScout. Q: Iliman Ndiaye (£6.0m) – keep or transfer out? If the latter, which players would you recommend in a similar price bracket? Via Ian Hart A: Iliman Ndiaye has swapped Merseyside for Manchester this week, in a deal which could rise to £65m. It’s a tricky situation for owners, myself included. Longer term, I think he’s a sell. Firstly, he won’t be on penalties anymore, certainly not with Erling Haaland (£15.5m) around. I don’t think he’ll be a nailed-on starter, either, given Manchester City’s squad depth, which you can see below via the excellent @4lex_mcfc Even when Ndiaye does start, he probably won’t play the full 90 minutes, which will subsequently impact his ability to hit the defensive contribution (DefCon) threshold. Regardless of minutes, City’s wingers don’t have as much defensive work to do anyway. Looking ahead, I think there’ll be too much week-to-week uncertainty to own Ndiaye, unless a positional rival suffers an injury. This week, at home to Coventry City, you’d think he’ll start on the bench. But with Porto on Tuesday, in Portugal, plus the Manchester derby next weekend, we could see some early substitutions, particularly if City have established a comfortable lead. Is Ndiaye worth keeping for potentially 20-25 minutes v Coventry, then? Probably not, but I do think we should carefully monitor Enzo Maresca’s Friday presser before we reach any final decisions. As you can probably tell, I’m still mulling this one over! If you do want to transfer Ndiaye out this week, I like Anton Stach (£6.0m), Mamadou Sangare (£5.7m) and Pascal Gross (£5.5m), mainly due to their multiple routes to points. Stach, for example, is top among midfielders for DefCons so far, with 32. He is also Leeds United’s primary set-piece taker. Q: Triple Captain Erling Haaland (£15.5m) – yes or no? Via ViperStripes A: I’ve already looked at some of the pros and cons in a standalone article, which you can read here Overall, however, I like this approach. Personally, I don’t think Coventry will offer much resistance at the Etihad Stadium, especially if we use the trip to Arsenal in Gameweek 1 as a blueprint. The Porto fixture on Tuesday isn’t ideal, but Haaland is in good physical condition. There will have been seven full days’ rest between the Crystal Palace and Coventry games, too. I’m planning to Wildcard in Gameweek 4, which rules Cole Palmer (£9.6m) out as an option at home to Hull City. I also don’t want to leave it until mid-December, when Haaland plays Hull, so I’m pretty sure I’ll Triple Captain Haaland in Gameweek 3. Q: Who are the best £4.5m defender options over the next few Gameweeks, excluding Ezri Konsa (£4.4m)? Via IAWC (It’s a Wonderful Cruyff) A: It’s still early days, but outside of Konsa, I like Kristoffer Ajer (£4.5m) the most in this price bracket. He is one of just four defenders who have banked DefCon points in both Gameweeks so far, and should continue to be a decent option while Sepp van den Berg (£4.9m) is out injured, perhaps longer. Due to his DefCon potential, I’d be happy to play Ajer in any of these fixtures: Amar Dedic (£4.5m) meanwhile has started really well at Newcastle United. I don’t see any reason why Tino Livramento (£4.9m) would take his place for now, but he is back in training, which gives me some hesitation about picking him out. Instead, Nico Elvedi (£4.5m) could be a nice cheap route into the Leeds United defence, given Joe Rodon’s (£4.5m) 8-10 week absence due to a hamstring injury . I think he’ll chip in with DefCons and the odd attacking return. Above: Teams sorted by expected goals conceded (xGC) in 2026/27 Q: Are Rayan Cherki (£7.7m), Phil Foden (£7.0m) and Antoine Semenyo (£8.5m) still good options given Manchester City’s new arrivals? Via Under My Cucurella A: Cherki, Foden and Semenyo are all really nice options this week, for obvious reasons. If I had to pick one for Gameweek 3 in isolation, I’d slightly favour Foden. He supplied a couple of assists at Selhurst Park last week. He also missed two big chances and generated the highest expected goals (xG) of any Man City player, with 0.87. “Phil is adapting a little bit wide. We know that he’s not a winger but we are trying to find a solution. I think, when [it was] the last 10 minutes, 15 minutes, he was inside, you can see that he was enjoying a little bit more. But again, the attitude was very good and this is what we need.” – Enzo Maresca on Phil Foden In light of the above, I think Foden will probably end up competing with Cherki for the No 10 role, with Semenyo, Jeremy Doku (£7.4m) and Ndiaye the primary options on the flanks. With the Champions League getting underway next week, all of them could be subject to rotation. We subsequently need much more time to assess it all. Once everything settles down, I wouldn’t be surprised if Enzo Fernandez (£6.9m) emerges as the second-best City attacker after Haaland, but let’s see how it unfolds in the coming weeks. Q: What impact might Matias Fernandez-Pardo (£6.0m) have on Yoane Wissa (£6.1m) at Newcastle United? Q: Do you prefer Lewis Hall (£5.1m) or Malick Thiaw (£5.0m)? Q: Is getting all three of Yoane Wissa, Anthony Elanga (£6.1m) and Hall a bit too much Newcastle United, despite their good fixtures? Via Better off with a pin and a blindfold, F4L + Lost for Wirtz A: You’d think Fernandez-Pardo will be eased in gently. That should allow Wissa to continue up top, certainly against Bournemouth in Gameweek 3. Longer term, Fernandez-Pardo could potentially lead the line, with Wissa in the ’10’. It’s the same position Wissa played against Liverpool in Gameweek 1. He produced four shots in that game, so I don’t think a slightly more withdrawn role would blunt his appeal, especially if he’s on penalties. As for the defenders, I’d pick Hall, mainly due to his all-round points potential, including open-play attacking threat, set-pieces and DefCons. Finally, Elanga has started the season really well. However, I remain a bit sceptical, particularly with matches against Leeds United, Hull and Coventry coming up, where there will naturally be less space for him to exploit. Personally, I’d prefer Stach, Sangare and Gross. 118 Comments Login to Post a Comment Previous First Last » Next Skout 14 mins ago How many mins do we think Ndiaye gets vs COV? articles.title: FPL GW3 Differentials: 5 Low-Owned Players to Target
articles.source_type: Gameweek rankings, captain picks, low-owned differentials, match previews and predicted line-ups
articles.body: FPL GW3 Differentials: 5 Low-Owned Players to Target | RotoWire FPL GW3 Differentials: 5 Low-Owned Players to Target Five FPL differentials to target in Gameweek 3, from John Egan at £4.0m to Anthony Elanga at £6.1m. Low-owned picks with repeatable roles and upcoming fixtures. September 3, 2026 Share By: Jonny Black September 3, 2026 FPL Differentials Mock Draft Simulator Prep for your 2026 Fantasy Football draft with free, unlimited drafts, and real-time grades. FPL GW3 Differentials: 5 Low-Owned Players to Target Gameweek 3 is shaping up as a popular Wildcard week, which makes finding low-owned players with secure roles especially valuable. These five GW3 differentials all offer a combination of minutes, role, underlying involvement and upside that could separate your squad from the template. For the full player order, see our FPL Gameweek 3 Rankings Check RotoWire's predicted lineups and injury report in the days before the deadline to confirm all starters, and keep an eye on any late fitness news that could affect the picks below. Player Club Price Ownership GW1-2 Points John Egan Hull £4.0m 4.3% Phil Foden Man City £7.0m 5.0% Kai Havertz Arsenal £7.5m 7.0% Anthony Elanga Newcastle £6.1m 8.1% Kevin Schade Brentford £6.0m 3.9% John Egan , Hull City $4.0m | 4.3% ownership | 17 total points Sometimes on a Wildcard, a budget player is all that makes the rest of the squad work, and Egan is exactly that. Only four defenders in all of FPL have scored more points through the opening two gameweeks. Egan operates as the central center-back in a Hull back three, which means he sees the majority of his side's defensive action. That has been clear across GW1 and GW2, where he picked up 21 and 13 defensive contributions, respectively, with the majority coming as clearances. That volume makes him one of the most reliable DEFCON accumulators at the budget end of the market. Hull will not sustain their clean sheet run all season, but at £4.0m with this kind of consistent underlying output and minimal price, Egan is worth building around. Phil Foden , Manchester City $7.0m | 5.0% ownership | 10 total points Manchester City are the popular team for a Gameweek 3 Wildcard given their home fixture against Coventry, and with no clean sheets this season it makes sense to load up on attackers. Foden has started both games on the right under manager Enzo Maresca, provided two assists in the 4-1 win over Crystal Palace and crucially played the full 90 minutes. Manchester City made a flurry of signings on the final days of the transfer window, but Foden should remain central to Maresca's plans, particularly over the next few gameweeks. At 5.0% owned, he sits on the edge of differential territory and will not stay there long if he delivers against Coventry. Kai Havertz , Arsenal $7.5m | 7.0% ownership | 8 total points Havertz may be the lowest scorer on this list through two games, but he's played the full 90 minutes for one of the best teams in the league in each of them. He showed his goalscoring ability with a goal in the opener against Coventry and again in the Community Shield victory over Manchester City. The one area that may frustrate in certain gameweeks is his shot volume, having taken only one shot in each game, but his movement and positioning inside the box suggest that will improve as Arsenal settle into their rhythm. In a forward pool that remains thin at every price point, 90 minutes and a defined starting role at Arsenal counts for a great deal. Anthony Elanga , Newcastle $6.1m | 8.1% ownership | 17 total points Elanga has become a main attacking outlet for Newcastle and has scored two of their four league goals this season. His pace is his point of difference and has made him devastatingly effective on the counter-attack. What feels different about him this season is his finishing. He has taken two shots in each game and put three on target, and his composure in front of goal has noticeably improved, though a lot of that is related to how his team plays under a new manager. Newcastle don't face another Big Six side until Arsenal in Gameweek 11, with two newly promoted sides arriving in Gameweeks 5 and 6. That fixture run makes him one of the more compelling mid-price holds of the Wildcard window. Kevin Schade , Brentford $6.0m | 3.9% ownership | 13 total points Brentford have been one of the best sides of the opening two gameweeks, scoring four goals in two games they mostly controlled, and Schade offers a value route into that attack at £2.0m less than Igor Thiago Against Spurs in GW1, Schade took five shots, all from inside the box, and created a chance. Against Leeds in GW2 he took three shots from inside the box and again created a chance. The underlying numbers across both games point to a player generating high-quality opportunities consistently. For Wildcard managers wanting Brentford representation without spending £8.0m on Thiago, Schade is the most efficient entry point into one of the division's most productive attacks. Final Thoughts The biggest mistake in GW3 is chasing points without checking whether the role is sustainable. Elanga, Foden and Schade have the clearest combination of secure minutes and repeatable attacking involvement, while Egan offers the strongest budget route into DEFCON production. The best low-owned GW3 targets are the players whose roles should continue, not simply the ones who scored last weekend. And that is the sheer number of developing talents that have been discarded, loaned, sold, and forgotten about since Klopp’s time on Merseyside. From future club captain Trent Alexander-Arnold choosing Real Madrid — after the Reds lifted their first Premier League title in front of fans for 35 years, no less — to Harvey Elliot’s recent La Liga loan departure. After a torrid year at Aston Villa , the look on the Englishman’s face as he fielded questions from the Valencia media was… not pleasant to witness. Trent Alexander-Arnold should never have left Liverpool (Image credit: Getty Images) Young players once deemed to be Liverpool’s future, talents that the German was able to extract the very best from, have gone from a Carabao Cup -winning unit, and making reliable cameo appearances in both European competitions and the Premier League, to being spread around here, there and everywhere. Instead, the Reds have spent big in their two previous transfer windows - their total expenditure on attackers alone exceeds £500 million - and lost the heart and soul that made Klopp’s reign so special, and so successful. The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week. Is it a surprise that Slot was able to win a Premier League title? He inherited a team whose muscles and minds had been ruthlessly shaped by the German — one that also included a career-best and still-hungry Mohamed Salah — and rode that wave to English top-flight glory. But, depressingly, the cost of that victory has likely set Liverpool back by years. To win it, Slot decided against using the German’s youngsters in any meaningful capacity, going full-throttle on extracting the last dregs of mentality and fitness that had been instilled in the core Reds by Klopp. But a once wise decision — or at least one that felt wise, at the time — continued into the 2025-26 season, and questions surrounding Liverpool’s mentality quickly surfaced. When Reds legend Salah told the press last December that he felt he was being forced out of the club, tensions reached their boiling point Salah shouldn't have left, either (Image credit: Alamy) If the club’s hierarchy could make an all-time superstar feel this way, an individual that had lifted Liverpool onto his shoulders and dragged them to the previous term’s Premier League-winning finish line, how was it making ‘Klopp’s Kids’ feel, behind the scenes? Jarell Quansah? A lacklustre game to start the season versus Ipswich Town in 2024-25, and few opportunities after. Now, he’s at Bayer Leverkusen , and receiving England call-ups. Bobby Clark? He once ran riot for the Reds during their Europa League campaign in 2023-24. Now, he’s at Derby County , with three goal involvements in his first four Championship matches this term. Jayden Danns? A scouser through-and-through, one who bagged twice versus Southampton in the FA Cup , no less, during Klopp’s swansong season. He’s back in the Liverpool Under-21s, and last appeared for the first team 12 months ago, again versus Southampton — for 15 minutes. James McConnell? He’s in the Under-21s, too. And, finally, Bajcetic, who appeared in 27 games across the German’s final two seasons at the helm, even delivering a Man of the Match-worthy performance in 2023’s Merseyside derby at Anfield? He’s gone, and wrote today on Instagram : “I never planned to write a goodbye message, because I was where I always wanted to be. This current Liverpool is hardly recognisable, in comparison with that which Klopp possessed. (Image credit: Alex Pantling/Getty Images) “I fought all the injuries and adversities with the motivation of paying back the love and trust you showed me… We will never know what could have been.” And perhaps the Spaniard is a slightly different case — a talent thwarted by injuries, and dealt an unfair hand throughout his Premier League career. But maybe seeing his fellow Carabao Cup-winning youngsters be loaned elsewhere, and denied first-team minutes, witnessing the standards drop on Merseyside, weaker training sessions, weaker performances, weaker mentality, weaker leadership, all in the aftermath of Klopp’s departure… perhaps that also played a role in Bajcetic’s recovery, or lack thereof. Under the German, Liverpool became a family. Under his successor, that family became estranged. Can Iraola turn back the clock? That remains to be seen, but the damage cannot be reversed. As the saying goes, it’s all up from here — but is it? Let's hope so. TOPICS Kedar Bayley Freelance Writer Kedar Bayley is a trained journalist specialising in culture reporting. As a fan of Liverpool FC, he writes on the Reds often. Knowledgable about all things sports, cinema and television, you can find his words in Screen International, FourFourTwo, Manchester Evening News and more. articles.title: Sage on what each of his new signings will bring
articles.excerpt: Pierre Sage was asked about the impact Crystal Palace's transfer deadline day business will have on his squad, as the Eagles prepare to face Fulham on Saturday (15:00 BST).
articles.source_type: Sage press conferences, named XIs, injury updates
articles.body: Skip navigation Sage on what each of his new signings will bring First-team 3 hours ago Pierre Sage was asked about the impact Crystal Palace's transfer deadline day business will have on his squad, as the Eagles prepare to face Fulham on Saturday (15:00 BST). Squad numbers revealed for our deadline day arrivals The Eagles managed to bring in four new players before the window closed, with defenders Honest Ahanor and Ben Chilwell, midfielder Quinten Timber and attacker Darío Osorio all arriving. They joined prior arrivals Dwight McNeil, the returning Evann Guessand, Óscar Mingueza, Takehiro Tomiyasu, Zavier Gozo, Anan Khalaili and Axel Disasi as Palace completed their summer transfer window business. It leaves with Sage with options across the pitch and could give him some tough team selection decisions to take over the coming weeks, starting with Saturday's trip to Craven Cottage. The Palace Manager spoke during his pre-match press conference about what his new recruits will bring to the team. "Honest [Ahanor] the centre-back we signed because we need one, especially a lefty [left-footed]," Sage said. "He's a young player with a lot of perspective. We will see what he is able to do." "With [Quinten] Timber, we needed this kind of player. We have four players in that position, but they are all similar. He is maybe more box-to-box. "For Osorio, we need a player with his speed in this position. He is able to shoot from far and he has scored a lot of goals like this. "And for Ben [Chilwell], he knew the club. He knows the city. "I know him because he was one of my opponents last year [at Lens] with Strasbourg. I like the player. I like the guy. "He will give us experience, he's a really good player. He can play two positions. He can play wing-back, but he played centre-back a lot of the time last year. "He will give us a lot of confidence as well, because he is a happy guy." When asked how long he thinks it will take the new signings to gel together, Sage stated that every player is different and that he will assess, on a case-by-case basis, when each player is ready. "Sometimes the player is ready because they have already played and trained with their [former] club," he explained. "Sometimes they need the time. "It depends on the case. The most important thing is to put in the player who is able to win. "That’s my job, to choose this player." articles.body: Shanade Hopcroft returns to Crystal Palace Skip navigation Shanade Hopcroft returns to Crystal Palace Announcement 4 hours ago Crystal Palace Women are delighted to announce that midfielder Shanade Hopcroft has returned to the club. The 28-year-old joins the club on a two-year deal and will wear the No. 24 shirt. Hopcroft first signed for Palace in 2023 from London City Lionesses, having begun her career at Chelsea’s Academy. In her first season in red and blue, she was voted the Women’s Players’ Player of the Season by her Crystal Palace teammates and was crucial to our historic Women's Championship title win and subsequent promotion to the Women's Super League. Playing as a creative midfielder, she made 27 appearances that season - scoring six times and providing three assists. After a 2024/25 campaign disrupted by injury, Hopcroft hit the ground running for the 2025/26 season in the Women’s Super League 2. She made 11 appearances in all competitions, scoring one goal – a sensational long-range strike against Birmingham City – before joining the Blues for the remainder of the WSL2 season. Hopcroft now returns to South London after helping Birmingham earn promotion to the WSL. Manager Jo Potter said: "Everyone is delighted to have Shanade back at the club. "We all know how much she can offer, and I'm looking forward to seeing her play for us again." Upon returning to the club, Hopcroft said: "I’m so happy to be re-joining the club. "I feel like I’m home, and now I can’t wait for the season to start!" To mark Shanade's return to the club, we are offering fans a special discount on tickets to our Everton game on Sunday. In spite of a high scoring GW across the board, a section of managers are preaching the necessity of an early WC with many selecting GW3 as the perfect opportunity. A larger group have decided that GW3 is the best use of the Triple captain chip, with Haaland in good form, fully rested and City facing Coventry at home. Regardless of your plans this Gameweek, we’re confident that our FPL GW3 Scout Picks will be of use to all managers! Our AllAboutFPL Scout Picks picked up a huge 113 points in FPL GW2 , beating the Official Scout Picks’ score of 96. That means it’s all square ahead of FPL GW3… GW 1 GW2 AAFPL Team 113 Official FPL Team As always, our Scout Picks will be based on the eye test, stats, analysis, and in this case also Pre-Season. FPL GW3 Fixtures FPL GW3 Scout Picks FPL GW3 Scout Picks – Goalkeeper Kelleher (5.0m) is our FPL GW3 Scout Picks goalkeeper. Brentford have been a pleasant surprise so far this season, over performing the middling to low expectations that many punters had prior to GW1. Brentford, Brighton and Bournemouth are a special set of teams who we always think are going to ‘fall off’ after a great year, only for them all to incrementally improve. It’s like we always forget that all three are simply really well run clubs… The Bees conceded 0.76xG (0 goals) against Spurs in GW1 and 1.61xG (1 goal) in GW2. Importantly, in that second match they conceded just 1 big chance (the goal which DCL scored), and outside of that conceded just 1 shot on target and 0.84xG from shots mostly from outside of the box. FACT: Kelleher is the 5th highest scoring ‘keeper after GW2 Sunderland on the other hand, Brentford’s opponents for FPL GW3, have somewhat underwhelmed thus far. While they looked alright in their second game against Fulham, they really struggled against Ipswich in GW1, failing to create much of note against a promoted side which went on to concede 5 to Manchester United in GW2 . Sunderland don’t create a lot of chances, illustrated by the fact that they finished last season with the third lowest xG in the league, and Brentford have proved to be a good defensive unit so far this campaign, so we’re backing Kelleher to pick up some points in FPL GW3! The Italian is the joint-highest scoring defender in FPL pre-GW3 having picked up a huge 20 points across his first two fixtures this season. The LB is a nailed option in an Arsenal backline that is once again proving itself to be a robust unit. Furthermore, Calafiori offers a high level of attacking output – both he and White occupied extremely advanced positions in the left and right half spaces when Arsenal were in possession against Villa in GW2. While Konsa will be a popular pick going into GW3 due to the injury concerns around Mosquera (which Arteta subsequently dispelled, but with Arteta you never know!), both Calafiori and White represent great value at 5.6m and 5.5m respectively due to their high attacking potential and security of minutes. Ajer could also be considered as a safer DC option , though his DC ceiling is lower against Sunderland than it was against Spurs and Leeds. Finally we have Liverpool’s captain Virgil Van Dijk . Liverpool’s defence has been shaky to say the least over the first two games of the new season, conceding two to Newcastle and two to Forest. Admittedly, against Forest the Reds looked a bit more solid, conceding one goal from a long ball and a spot of miscommunication and one from a penalty. This LFC defence is not yet as solid as it could/should be, but with time Iraola will surely be able to implement his system and get this team up and running. Liverpool face Ipswich away in FPL GW3 , and while Ipswich have scored 3 goals across their first 2 matches in the premier league we think that VVD still represents great value in FPL for this match. Virgil’s appeal comes from his versatility of point scoring – the LFC captain scored 8 goals and provided 3 assists in all competitions last season as well as scoring 30 DC points and 10 bonus points across Liverpool’s premier league campaign. Despite their difficult start, we’re backing Liverpool and VVD in FPL GW3. FPL GW3 Scout Picks – Midfielders We’ve selected a midfield four of Gakpo (7.0m), Schade (6.0m), Foden (7.0m) and Cherki (7.6m) for our FPL GW3 Scout Picks team… Let’s start with the Manchester City duo. Manchester City welcome Coventry City to the Etihad in FPL GW3 for a fixture which many FPL managers are targeting. While there is a lot of focus on Haaland due to the triple captain possibility, Foden and Cherki also deserve their time in the limelight for this excellent fixture against a newly promoted team. This is one of the last times in the first half of the season that City players will have a full week of rest between fixtures , making it an even better fixture to target as we know the players will be well rested and fully fit going into FPL GW3. Coventry lost their first two matches in the PL, losing 3-0 to Arsenal and 0-1 to Hull in gameweeks 1 and 2. While they looked better against Hull this will surely be a more challenging test for Lampard’s side. Foden and Cherki are City’s best two attackers (outside of Haaland) to target considering their form, security of minutes and underlying numbers. Cherki has 2 goals and 2 assists to Foden’s 2 assists thus far and both players are averaging well over 1xGI/90 after the first two games . Cherki is the man in form and is understandably the more popular pick, but Foden is a great differential at a slightly lower price point and could be an excellent punt for this game before City’s new attacking singings are introduced into the mix and take minutes awya from both assets. Gakpo comes into the team to replace Szoboszlai having impressed in GW1 and 2, bagging a goal involvement in both matches. The dutchman looks nailed in this new-look Liverpool attack in spite of Barcola’s signing, with his late move away from the club falling through at the last minute. Last season Gakpo scored 7 goals and 5 assists last year, averaging 0.54xGI/90 in a tumultuous season for the Reds . He proved his worth by playing off the right for Liverpool in FPL GW2 and will likely continue in this role for the forseeable. While Szoboszlai is still the best Liverpool midfield pick in the long term, Gakpo looks like a great punt for GW3 due to Liverpool’s favourable fixture against a side that conceded 6 goals across their first 2 fixtures . Gakpo is in great attacking form and looked dangerous in both games – the dutchman occupies more advanced positions and is far more involved in the attack than Szoboszlai and is therefore a better option for those looking to profit from Ipswich’s poor defensive record and the attacking potential that this represents. Our final midfield pick is Brentford’s Schade . We’re going for a Brentford triple up for their attractive fixture against Sunderland in FPL GW3 and Schade is by far the most attractive attacker going into this one. Schade represents excellent value at just 6.0m and while Sangare will be a popular pick following his huge haul against Spurs in FPL GW1, Schade offers more consistent attacking returns and higher haul potential than Sangare. Schade was the 5th highest scoring Brentford asset last season and the third highest amongst midfielders and forwards behind Outtara and Thiago. This season Thiago has failed to impress and has looked a shadow of his former self after two GWs while Outtara has lost his place in the team to new signing Anthony. Schade therefore is the most attractive option and has shown himself capable of attacking big spaces in behind the opposition and often representing the outlet on long balls and counter attacks. Last season Schade scored 8 and assisted 3, averaging 0.53xGI/90 – on par with more expensive assets like the aforementioned Gakpo. Further Read: FPL GW3 Wildcard Drafts – Pros, Cons, Tips and Players to Target FPL GW3 Scout Picks – Forwards Our forward line consists of Wissa (6.1m), Haaland (15.5m) and Isak (9.0m)… Haaland naturally keeps his spot in the team and takes the captains armband from Bruno for Manchester City’s attractive fixture against Coventry. This pick needs little explanation really, but I’ll give it a go… Haaland is in good form having scored twice against Palace in GW2. In GW1 City created more than enough chances for Haaland to score, and he was unlucky not to – this new manager and system are clearly still trying to work to Haaland’s strengths, so it is understandable why he’s such a popular pick for this great fixture against promoted Coventry in FPL GW3 Wissa comes into the team for Newcastle’s fixture against Bournemouth . Wissa has finally nailed down a spot in this Newcastle team following a challenging first season in black and white. The forward has bagged a goal and assist in his first two matches for Newcastle this season and will be confident of more goal involvements in the coming weeks over what is a positive fixture run for Newcastle United in the short term. articles.body: Liverpool: Carragher tells Iraola to have brutal ‘conversation’ with £60m Liverpool midfielder and change his mind Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola and Jamie Carragher Jamie Carragher has said that Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola needs to change Dominik Szoboszlai’s role in the team. Szoboszlai is a midfielder by trade, but the Hungary international was deployed at right-back on many occasions last season. The Liverpool midfielder scored 13 goals and gave 12 assists in 53 matches in all competitions last season. Of those games, Szoboszlai, who cost Liverpool £60million when they signed him from RB Leipzig in 2023, played 10 times as a right-back and 10 matches as a right-winger. Liverpool manager Iraola has used Szoboszlai in central midfield this season. However, former Liverpool defender Carragher believes that Iraola needs to change the Hungarian’s position and play him at right-back. READ: Keane blasts four Liverpool stars with Iraola’s side ‘all over the shop’ in first two matches Dominik Szoboszlai should play at right-back for Liverpool Carragher said about Szoboszlai on The Overlap “I have never believed Szoboszlai is a central midfield player. “You would know the role better than me, Roy (Keane). “Now, he signed a new contract, and I can only imagine in those talks, they were desperate for him to stay, he has almost said, I want to play midfield because he has moved around a bit. “And he started the season in central midfield. “I don’t see him as that. Rio Ngumoha reaches decision on signing a new contract at Liverpool after Barcola arrival “For me, in a midfield, he’s a Jordan Henderson – runner, energy with probably more of a goal threat really, but Liverpool don’t play that way. “And he is not really a classic number 10 really. “His actual best role could possibly be at right-back because he can get a lot of the ball, he can run, he almost plat that Trent role for you from there, but there’s no way I think he’s going to want to play there because he has probably signed a contract for £350 grand a week, to put a midfield player to right-back, and you have just done this big thing, he’s the vice-captain. “I just think that’s a conversation Iraola has got to have going forward because the midfield is not right and he’s part of that midfield not being right. “Whether he ends up going to right-back and how they can dress it up to that is not just being right-back, you are actually going to run the game from there.” During a press conference on Thursday, Iraola said that he will use Szoboszlai at right-back if he has to. The Liverpool manager said: “I haven’t found any situation where a player has said he doesn’t want to play in a position. “We have discussions, but everyone wants to help. “If we have to play Dom as a right winger, as a right-back or a midfielder, he wants to help the team first. “We have some injuries now, and we need the versatility of the players, players like Dom. “Even in the game, they have to change positions.” READ NEXT: Liverpool have gone ‘full Woodward on meth’ but fans are optimistic Liverpool Dominik Szoboszlai Related Articles Joe Williams 03 Sep 2026 Carragher slams ‘really poor’ Liverpool star by declaring he’s ‘the Darwin Nunez of full-backs’ Jamie Carragher has criticised Milos Kerkez’s performances for Liverpool and branded him “the Darwin Nunez of full-backs”. articles.excerpt: AFC Bournemouth goalkeeper Ðorðe Petrović has earned two nominations for the Premier League’s Coca-Cola Save of the Month award for August. Petrović produced a superb display between the posts as Marco Rose’s side picked up their first Premier League point of the 2026/27 campaign, with two of his saves now recognised among the best made across the division during August. The Cherries goalkeeper is one of only four players represented on the six-save shortlist, alongside Hull City’s Konstantinos Tzolakis, Everton’s Jordan Pickford and Liverpool’s Alisson Becker. Tzolakis, like Petrović, has two saves in contention for the award. Supporters can watch all six nominated saves and vote for their favourite, with voting open until 12pm on Monday 7th September . articles.body: Arsenal Champions League fixtures, games, results, squad, standings and schedule 2026/27 Skip to content Football News Champions League News Arsenal Champions League fixtures, games, results, squad, standings and schedule 2026/27 Key details on Arsenal's 2026/27 Champions League campaign Ben Miller Last Update: 26 minutes ago 3 min read Add us as a preferred source on Google Arsenal are aiming to go one better this season than their defeat in the 2025/26 Champions League final against Paris Saint-Germain. The reigning Premier League champions won their eight league phase games and remained unbeaten over 90 minutes throughout last season’s competition. Arsenal also ensured they have reached the knockout stage in each of their Champions League appearances since the 2000/01. Check out Arsenal’s fixtures, results and squad for the 2026/27 Champions League, as well as a look at their schedule. Table of Contents Arsenal Champions League fixtures, results 2026/27 Arsenal Champions League standings 2026/27 Arsenal full Champions League schedule 2026/27 Arsenal confirmed Champions League confirmed squad 2026/27 English teams in the Champions League: Why are there five clubs? When is the Champions League final? English teams in the Champions League: Why are there five clubs? Arsenal, City, United, Villa and Liverpool qualified as the top five teams in the Premier League. England was awarded an extra position as a result of UEFA’s co-efficient rankings, which are based on the overall performances of nations across European competition over a season. Villa also won last season’s Europa League , which would have earned the Villans a place in the Champions League had they not qualified through their league position. When is the Champions League final? The final will take place on June 5 2027 at the Estadio Metropolitano in Madrid, which has been Atletico Madrid’s home since 2017. That could be a good omen for English teams: two Premier League sides reached the final when Atleti’s home previously hosted the showpiece in 2019, Liverpool beating Tottenham 2-0. How to watch Arsenal in the Champions League: TV channel TNT Sports and Amazon Prime Video have the live broadcast rights to the Champions League in the UK. Amazon have first pick of the Tuesday games, with all the other matches shown on TNT Sports. BBC Sport also has highlights rights. articles.body: Premier League: Andoni Iraola praises Bradley Barcola ahead of Ipswich clash | Flashscore.com All Football Premier League US Open Transfer News Features Champions League Formula 1 Darts Snooker Cycling Golf NFL Most read on Flashscore News Transfer News LIVE: Richarlison set for move to Turkey, Ajax sign Adingra Aguero backs Jesus to shine at Barcelona: 'He can easily score 10 or 15 goals' Antonsen seals comeback-win against rising Chinese star as favorites crash out in Shenzhen Reiss Nelson finds new home days after Arsenal exit, returns to Feyenoord Liverpool's Iraola praises new superstar signing ahead of Ipswich Town clash Zack Oaten / Tribal Football Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola REUTERS Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola has spoken to the media ahead of Friday's clash against Ipswich Town. Liverpool will travel to face promoted side Ipswich Town at Portman Road on Friday in search of their first win of the season following 2-2 draws against Newcastle United and Nottingham Forest Liverpool have twice needed late equalisers to avoid defeat, with Dominik Szoboszlai scoring a last-minute equaliser against Newcastle and summer addition Victor Munoz bagging a late goal against Forest. Iraola ’s start has been mixed, with fans waiting to see his side finally kick into gear. However, with Ipswich's last victory a 1-0 win at Anfield in December 2000, the Reds are the firm favourites heading into this clash. The good news is that new signing Bradley Barcola could add a new element to the side as he arrived from Paris Saint-Germain earlier this week and could make his debut against The Tractor Boys. Iraola delighted to keep Gakpo and Barcola Iraola first spoke on Barcola and Cody Gakpo , whose move to Manchester City never surfaced this summer, leaving the pair competing for a place in attack until at least January. The Spaniard said: "We are very happy with Bradley, it was our priority to sign a very, very good player in those positions. He has also come with the right mentality. I like that he wanted Liverpool a lot. "He wanted to come here. It's a good first sign, and being the player he is, he has come with the willingness to help us. He is playing well for us, and if everything goes well in training today, he will definitely be available for us tomorrow. "My relationship with Cody has been very honest from the beginning. He has played very well for us so far. He was always aware of the situation in the market, we were constantly talking, I hope we can keep him at the same level. He is in a good place physically and mentally, and I'm very happy to pick him." Is Barcola ready to start: "Good question. I see him in a good place. He has trained for us, it's true he hasn't had minutes in pre-season. He has been training, and it's a decision we have to make. But we have to consider he hasn't had minutes in pre-season games." Poor starts frustrates Iraola Liverpool won both Premier League meetings during the 2024/25 season, recording a 2-0 victory at Portman Road before winning 4-1 at Anfield. Iraola's side are expected to pick up three points on Friday despite being away from home. Iraola was next asked if he is frustrated by not picking up a win in his first two games and what threat Ipswich could pose in front of their home supporters. "Definitely. If you don't win, you are frustrated. It's only two games, but we need to win. This game tomorrow, the first two games weeks are the most difficult, but I'm much more comfortable now the market is closed, and we know who we are. We have to perform and do our job. "Ipswich are a team in terms of they won their first game at home. Even the other day, in the first half, they were the better team until United got the 2-1 and the game went open. We have to be ready, give our best." Szoboszlai at right back? Jeremie Frimpong has struggled in defence for Liverpool, with the fullback being criticised for his poor defending and abysmal crossing ability so far this season. Iraola was asked about the lack of depth at right back with Conor Bradley still ruled out and suggested Szoboszlai could fill it at the back. "Challenge in the squad now is we don't have Conor there at right-back. That's why I value Dom at right-back as he can play there. Versatility in the player helps us go through the moments when we have injuries. "In midfield we have good numbers. Now it's a matter of getting the right calls from myself. I'm finding now the best combinations and we are going through a period now where we will play a lot of games, and we'll have a chance to see the options we have and the combinations we have. It's a matter of coaching." Follow the game with Flashscore. English Premier League The 2026/27 Premier League season is underway. articles.body: Team News: Sage updates on Sarr ahead of Fulham Skip navigation Team News: Sage updates on Sarr ahead of Fulham First-team 5 hours ago Pierre Sage has confirmed that Crystal Palace will be without Ismaïla Sarr when they take on Fulham on Saturday (15:00 BST), but revealed no additional injuries had been picked up following the last game against Manchester City. The Eagles make the short trip to Craven Cottage on Saturday, returning to league action after an eight-day gap. Ismaïla Sarr missed the defeat to Manchester City at Selhurst Park last time out and will not be available for this one. However, Sage has no fresh injury concerns for the trip to west London. “Sarr needs time to recover," he told his pre-match press conference. "He is injured at the moment." When asked about Jean-Philippe Mateta 's availability, Sage added: "They cannot play. As I said last time, Mateta is injured, now for three weeks. “Everyone else, apart from our long-term injuries; Chadi [Riad] and [JP] Mateta, every other player has recovered well.” Sage also has fresh options at his disposal after four players signed on transfer deadline day, with Honest Ahanor, Ben Chilwell, Quinten Timber and Darío Osorio all arriving. When asked about their arrival, Sage said: "We are happy with the four players who signed at the end. “We have enough players. We did what we decided to do – that’s a success." articles.title: Harwood-Bellis' journey back to the big time
articles.excerpt: Taylor Harwood-Bellis’ second senior appearance came in the UEFA Champions League as Pep Guardiola showed his faith in the then 17-year-old on the biggest stage. Coming on for the latter stages of a group stage victory against Dinamo Zagreb was reward for the defender’s development in sky blue and followed on from his debut in a League Cup tie against Preston North End. A maiden senior goal on his FA Cup debut arrived days shy of his 18 th birthday in January 2020, one of eight appearances he made for the Citizens. It was the result of a journey that started at the age of six, when the Stockport native joined City’s academy, and which included back-to-back FA Youth Cup finals, winning the prestigious competition in 2020. But with first-team opportunities at a premium as Guardiola’s team racked up titles at home and abroad, Harwood-Bellis set about forging his own path in the game. Loan spells at Blackburn Rovers, Anderlecht, Stoke City, Burnley and Southampton provided invaluable experience and game time, and it was at St Mary’s where he found a permanent home. articles.title: Jaguars' Early-Season Backup QB Decision May Not Be as Clear as You Think
articles.excerpt: The Jacksonville Jaguars made the move for Quinn Ewers for a reason, but it might be too soon for him to be the team's No. 2 quarterback.
articles.source_type: Gameweek squads, team news round-ups, deadline reminders
articles.body: Jaguars' Early-Season Backup QB Decision May Not Be as Clear as You Think Jacksonville Jaguars quarterback Quinn Ewers (10) walks off the field after an NFL Jaguars practice at the Miller Electric Center, Tuesday September 2, 2026 in Jacksonville, Fla. [Doug Engle/Florida Times-Union] | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars made a noteworthy addition at the quarterback position this weekend, but the dust has yet to settle when it comes to the depth chart behind Trevor Lawrence. Lawrence is entering his sixth season as the Jaguars' franchise quarterback, and he has opened with three different backup quarterbacks behind him in the last three seasons: C.J. Beathard, Mac Jones, and Nick Mullens. Will new quarterback Quinn Ewers be the fourth? Last weekend's trade and the construction of the roster, which had Ewers on the 53-man roster 24 hours after he joined the team, might suggest yes in some cases. But in this case, the answer might not be so clear. Jacksonville Jaguars quarterback Quinn Ewers (10) throws as he debuted as a Jaguar during an NFL Jaguars practice at the Miller Electric Center, Tuesday September 2, 2026 in Jacksonville, Fla. [Doug Engle/Florida Times-Union] | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect The QB2 Role The addition of Ewers a day before the Jaguars' roster cut to 53 certainly implied that he is set to be the long-term backup of Trevor Lawrence, but that might be the wrong way of looking at it for Week 1 and the short-term. Instead, the addition should say more about the quarterback room at large and how the Jaguars are using roster mechanisms to improve the depth. By trading for Ewers and keeping him on the 53-man roster, the Jaguars were able to land a quarterback to upgrade the room with the impending release of Carter Bradley. Had the Dolphins waived Ewers, he would have been subject to a waiver wire in which the Jaguars were No. 24 in the claim order, making it far from a guarantee they would land him. After the trade for Hunter Long was completed, this could be viewed as trading a future seventh-round pick to ensure they would not get lept in the waiver wire. At the same time, Mullens is not a player who would be subject to the waiver wire since he is a veteran. With those types of players, teams often release them at cut down day with the understanding that the player would return to the practice squad , since no team can simply claim the rights to their contract. Jacksonville Jaguars quarterback Nick Mullens (14) warms up during an NFL Jaguars practice at the Miller Electric Center, Tuesday September 2, 2026 in Jacksonville, Fla. [Doug Engle/Florida Times-Union] | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect The Jaguars could ensure they would have Mullens on the practice squad; they could not do the same for Ewers. The Jaguars can continue to keep Mullens on the practice squad without worry about another team trying to sign him to the active roster, another luxury they would not have with Ewers on the practice squad instead of on the 53. That basically boils it down to this: instead of seeing Ewers as No. 2 and Mullens as No. 3, perhaps we should look at them as simply the two passers behind Lawrence on the depth chart. "Yeah, Nick's presence here, it means a ton. His familiarity of the system, itâs like having another coach in the room. Certainly being able to understand that he can operate our offense in the way that it's intended to is something that we don't want to just separate from," Jaguars general manager James Gladstone said on Tuesday. Jacksonville Jaguars Executive Vice President of Football Operations Tony Boselli, left, Jacksonville Jaguars head coach Liam Coen, center and Jacksonville Jaguars General Manager James Gladstone walk off the field after an NFL Jaguars practice at the Miller Electric Center, Tuesday September 2, 2026 in Jacksonville, Fla. [Doug Engle/Florida Times-Union] | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect "That was a real conversation, an authentic conversation we had to have with Nick, and appreciate very much the way we went about it and the professionalism he showcased. He's such a great teammate, such a great partner in this, and is pouring right back in, starting out on our practice squad, and we'll see how it all unfolds here as we get into the season." When viewing the situation from those lens, it certainly seems like the door would be open for Mullens to still be the Jaguars' No. 2 quarterback for at least the start of the season as Ewers learns the offense. Expecting Ewers to be prepared and ready to go into a game for any potential scenario by Sept. 13 would seem ambitious, and the way the Jaguars constructed the roster gives them the flexibility to not have to force that scenario. "He's obviously having to get up to speed right now. Wanted to make sure we kept Nick [QB Nick Mullens] as well here in terms of, Week One, what does that look like? And is he up to speed?" Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said on Wednesday. "But also, the amount of work that Nick puts in to the rest of the guys, the crew. I wanted to make sure that, hey, are we continuing to put ourselves in the best position to be successful as an offense, if and when something were to happen to Trevor [QB Trevor Lawrence].â Ewers is an interesting addition to the quarterback room and could very well be the injection of talent their signal-caller depth chart needs. But for now, it might be early to annoint him as the No. 2 vs. the Cleveland Browns. Add us as a preferred source on Google Follow Loading recommendations... articles.title: Who Is North Carolina's Best? No. 19 Hough Hosts Providence Day in Battle of State Champions
articles.excerpt: Defending state champions Hough and Providence Day meet in a Week 3 North Carolina high school football showdown featuring two unbeaten teams loaded with Division I talent.
articles.source_type: Gameweek squads, team news round-ups, deadline reminders
articles.body: Who Is North Carolina's Best? No. 19 Hough Hosts Providence Day in Battle of State Champions Providence Day takes its 2-0 record up against nationally ranked Hough, on Friday, as these North Carolina high school football powers clash for state supremacy. | Providence Day/X It's only Week 3 of the North Carolina high school football season, and no state championship will be won Friday night. But when Hough hosts Providence Day , two reigning state champions will share the same field in a matchup that could help settle an early-season debate: Who is the best high school football team in North Carolina? The contest will be streamed live on the NFHS Network Hough, the defending NCHSAA Class 8A state champion, enters the matchup ranked No. 19 nationally by High School On SI . Providence Day is the defending NCISAA Division I champion and has been a regular presence in national rankings in recent seasons. And because they compete under separate governing bodies, there won't be a postseason rematch. It's public vs. private, champion vs. champion, with statewide bragging rights at stake. Providence Day Has Built a Championship Program Providence Day has established itself as one of North Carolina's most successful programs under coach Chad Grier, who has won eight NCISAA state championships â four each at Providence Day and Davidson Day. The Chargers have also earned national recognition in recent seasons, appearing in national rankings while building schedules designed to test themselves against some of the region's top programs. Providence Day's dominance within the NCISAA has led the Chargers to regularly challenge prominent public-school programs. This season's opening stretch includes Myers Park, Rolesville and Hough. Both Teams Enter 2-0 Hough has done nothing through two weeks to suggest its No. 19 national ranking is misplaced. The Huskies opened with a 15-10 road win over defending South Carolina state champion Northwestern as Marshall quarterback commit Ethan Royal threw two touchdown passes. Hough's defense held Northwestern to 195 total yards. The Huskies were even more impressive against Cardinal Gibbons, rolling to a 35-10 victory while limiting the Crusaders to just 85 yards of offense. Royal completed 15 of 19 passes for 285 yards and four touchdowns without a turnover. Providence Day Is Already Battle Tested So far, so great. The Chargers dismantled Myers Park 49-13 to open the season as new quarterback Cam Cater threw for 267 yards and three touchdowns while Tre Geathers had a 26-yard pick six. It was over by halftime when the Chargers led 42-6. Then came a 34-0 rout of Rolesville. Cater threw for 330 yards and four more touchdowns. Division I recruits Braylen Clark and Ethan Dempsey each had two touchdown receptions. Division I Talent It will be all over the field. Providence Day's Division I recruits include Griff Galloway (DL, Kentucky), Moses Poku-Kankam (S, Rutgers), Steele Fletcher (WR, Wake Forest), Dempsey (UNC-Charlotte), Cooper Hodson (OL, Delaware), Caleb Cooper (S, Penn State), Brennan Drummond (S), Geathers (S, Florida), Clark (5-star), Nate Dollard (CB, 4-star). Hough's top recruits include Joshua Dobson (5-star CB, South Carolina), Davion Jones (4-star S, South Carolina), Royal (Marshall), Moreno Fisher (OL, Virginia) and Treveon Pegues (OL, North Carolina A&T). articles.excerpt: Arsenal are protecting their long-term interests in teenage midfielder Ethan Nwaneri. The Gunners have reportedly inserted a recall option into Nwaneri's season-long loan move to Borussia Dortmund. According to transfer expert Fabrizio Romano, writing for CaughtOffside , the Gunners have the right to break the loan agreement early and bring the 19-year-old back to North London during the January transfer window should they choose to exercise it. To avoid a scenario where the midfielder's progress stalls on the bench, Arsenal have opted to sanction a temporary departure to Germany. And having seen previous young loanees suffer from a lack of minutes, the Gunners wanted to ensure they retained full control of the arrangement, allowing them to step in if Nwaneri's game time in Germany does not meet expectations. A serious knee injury to Dortmund's new, creative midfielder Giannis Konstantelias on his debut motivated the Bundesliga club's late-in-the-window pursuit of Nwaneri. The Arsenal hierarchy's hope is for Nwaneri to perform at a high level in the Bundesliga, using the experience to prove he can handle first-team demands in the Premier League. If all goes according to plan, the England youth international will return to the Emirates next summer to stake a claim for a far more involved role in Arteta's first-team squad. Captain Poll Chip Strategy FPL Gameweek 3 Wildcard best team + pros/cons of using September 3 192 comments 3 September 2026 192 comments Still umming and ahhing over whether to use your Wildcard in Gameweek 3 of Fantasy Premier League (FPL)? Or are you still tinkering with the right balance of players after activating it? If either of those applies, we’ll assess the pros and cons of deploying the chip ahead of Friday’s deadline, before providing a couple of draft ideas Score More Points. Win More Mini Leagues. Join FFScout. PROS Jump on Man City The most obvious reason: Manchester City are at home to winless, goalless Coventry City. A leaky Manchester United then follow, with visits of Sunderland and Ipswich Town also to come in the next five Gameweeks. You may have started the season without Erling Haaland (£15.5m) in your side, or the short-term lure of Rayan Cherki (£7.7m) – whatever the longer-term reservations about game-time – may be too much to resist. No team, in any other fixture from Gameweeks 1-6, are projected to score as many goals as City (2.81) this weekend. The domino effect of the final summer transfers This is the first Gameweek that takes place after the closure of the transfer window, and there was plenty to dissect on deadline day. Iliman Ndiaye (£6.0m) to Manchester City, for example. A great move for the Senegalese winger on paper, but he may/will lose reliable-90-minute-man status, penalties and DefCon-amassing abilities in one fell swoop. We’ve documented more of the FPL winners and losers on deadline day in this piece A quantum of Tzolis doubt + Konsa’s cut-price availability A Gameweek 2 half-time withdrawal has put the willies up some Christos Tzolis (£6.5m) owners. He’s now the second-most-sold player of Gameweek 3. Is it time to offload the Greek winger? It may be somewhat premature but there’s no question that his Gameweek 3 pitch-time now looks iffy, and who knows what lies beyond it. In any case, a Gameweek 3 Wildcard can help you get your Arsenal house in order. Cristhian Mosquera (£5.5m) is now a rotation risk, as well as Tzolis. On the flip side, we’re not likely to get a reliable £4.4m starter in the Arsenal defence any time again soon, so Ezri Konsa is shooting up in popularity now that he has his first minutes under his belt. Pre-season reservations about the early-season game-time of Bukayo Saka (£9.5m) – due to his World Cup participation – have also been put to bed. Post-Bench Boost redistribution of funds If you played your Bench Boost in Gameweek 1 or 2, as 1.15 million Fantasy managers did, then you might want to redistribute your funds now that you don’t want, or even need, four playing substitutes. You will likely have gone without a £4.0m goalkeeper in your initial squad, for instance, in order to have two starting shot-stoppers to ‘boost’. Now, especially if you’re setting and forgetting an option like David Raya (£6.0m) or Bart Verbruggen (£4.5m), you might be content to have your back-up goalkeeper be the cheapest possible option. Similarly, if you’ve gone down the 4-4-2/3-5-2 route, there’s the option of just spending the least amount you possibly need (£4.5m) on a non-playing third forward. That frees up funds to be lavished on your starting XI, with perhaps just one or two reliable subs needed. CONS Still need to see new signings bed in Waiting even another couple of Gameweeks would give FPL managers more evidence on reliability of minutes and tactical roles. How will the arrival of Enzo Fernandez (£6.9m) and Ayyoub Bouaddi (£5.5m) impact Nico O’Reilly (£6.5m) and Josko Gvardiol (£5.6m), for example? Enzo Maresca has only used O’Reilly in a midfield role so far but with Enzo especially now aboard, is it going to be a straight fight between O’Reilly and Gvardiol at left-back? Are we really ready to draw conclusions on two weeks of data? The biggest issue is that we’ve only seen two Gameweeks of Premier League football. A strong or poor opening couple of performances doesn’t necessarily tell us how a player or team will perform over the coming weeks, especially with squads being strengthened and weakened on deadline day. Spurs could quickly improve, for example, with new bodies on board and others returning from injury. How many were willing to write Bruno Fernandes (£12.0m) off after a Gameweek 1 blank, only for him to smash his best-ever FPL score the following weekend? Can’t Triple Captain in Gameweek 3 Using the Wildcard now means you can’t use another chip in Gameweek 3 – and the Triple Captain is mightily tempting. Rate My Team (RMT) does project higher points for Cole Palmer (£9.6m) in Gameweek 4 and Haaland again in Gameweek 7 than the Norwegian this week, but will the start of the UEFA Champions League impact on these premium players’ minutes in future Gameweeks? A week early for Chelsea assets It’s fair to say that an early-season Wildcard is going to go quite heavy on Chelsea assets, given the favourable run ahead: However, as you can see above, first comes the daunting test of Arsenal away. A Chelsea double-up/triple-up will likely be the way to go after this weekend but would you want to be fielding the Blues at the Emirates? Booking in a transfer – say, Cherki to Morgan Rogers (£7.5m) or Fernandes to Palmer – in Gameweek 4 would be one way to go. As could benching one or two Chelsea picks this week in favour of someone else. Of course, with seven goals scored in two Gameweeks, you might be perfectly content to field Pedro and co even against the might of the Arsenal defence! GAMEWEEK 3 WILDCARD DRAFT On the subject of ‘booking in a transfer’, here’s what we’ve put together for a Gameweek 3 Wildcard. As mentioned above, Cherki and/or Fernandes could become Rogers and/or Palmer in Gameweek 4. It’s a fairly template front three, with Newcastle embarking on the following favourable run from this weekend (and especially from Gameweek 5) onwards: The ‘100% DefCon hit rate’ trio of Kristoffer Ajer (£4.5m), Lewis Hall (£5.1m) and Mamadou Sangare (£5.7m) features, as does the obligatory Arsenal defensive double-up. Tyrick Mitchell (£4.5m) is the fifth defender, with the intention of covering a tricky period for our main four in Gameweeks 11-12 (and he is playable in Gameweek 4): Kjell Scherpen (£4.5m) was about the best back-up ‘keeper we could find to cover Bart Verbruggen’ s (£4.5m) iffier fixtures in Gameweeks 5, 8 and 9, but there’s a strong argument for Carl Rushworth (£4.5m) and maybe even Bernd Leno (£4.5m), too – not that Ipswich, Coventry or Fulham have convinced defensively so far, and you may want to simply set and forget Verbruggen regardless of any trickier tests: BRUNO, PALMER + HAALAND DRAFT! Finally, is it possible to house all of Palmer, Bruno and Haaland? We’ve attempted it in this draft, sacrificing a second playing ‘keeper and Cherki, and downgrading Hall, Mitchell and Wissa to the assist-making Amar Dedic (£4.5m), the DefCon-amassing John Egan (£4.0m) and Everton striker Thierno Barry (£5.5m), who looks to have been the biggest winner of all on deadline day. 192 Comments Login to Post a Comment Previous First Last » Next Fuddled FC 3 hours, 41 mins ago Is Cherki worth paying the extra over Foden? articles.title: Nascimento and Williams reflect on PSG win
articles.excerpt: Goalscorers Adler Nascimento and Seb Williams reflected on Crystal Palace Under-21sâ impressive 2-1 victory over Paris Saint-Germain at Sutton on Wednesday night.
articles.source_type: Sage press conferences, named XIs, injury updates
articles.body: Nascimento and Williams reflect on PSG win Skip navigation Nascimento and Williams reflect on PSG win Academy 6 hours ago Goalscorers Adler Nascimento and Seb Williams reflected on Crystal Palace Under-21s’ impressive 2-1 victory over Paris Saint-Germain at Sutton on Wednesday night. The win saw the Young Eagles make a perfect start to their Premier League International Cup campaign. The competition brings together 16 Premier League 2 sides and 16 invited European clubs, with the teams split into four groups of eight. Each English side faces the four European opponents in their group once. Palace are in Group C alongside PSG, Jong PSV, Sunderland, RSC Anderlecht and FC Porto, with their four fixtures taking place at Sutton United’s Borough Sports Ground. Nascimento opened the scoring in stunning fashion, bending a sublime free-kick over the wall and into the top corner, before Harry Lee saved a penalty on the stroke of half-time. Williams then doubled the advantage early in the second half with a trademark half-volley. Although Noa Bezeme pulled one back for PSG, Palace held firm to secure three points. “I think we knew it was going to be a tough game,” Nascimento said. “We knew how they play. They like to be cute on the ball, but we knew we had to defend well, and that's exactly what we did. “We took our chances when we had them.” The result made it back-to-back victories for Darren Powell’s side following Friday’s 2-0 win at Aston Villa, while also extending their unbeaten start to three games. “I thought we started the season really well,” Williams said. “I think every game we just built and improved. Obviously, Arsenal in the first game, 1-1, and then 2-0 against Villa. “Against a top team like PSG, we've done well. We just keep building on performances, and who knows what can happen this season.” Nascimento has been in fine form, scoring all five of Palace’s goals during pre-season before finding the net against Villa and PSG. “I just want to keep it up,” he said. “It's a hot start, but the season's not three games long. It's however many, so just keep going, really. “Just keep the form going, keep the foot on the gas.” Williams’ second-half strike was another fine finish, but the forward was quick to credit the build-up. “I think it was a good ball that crossed it in, and as soon as it got to Benji, I knew he was going to set me, because he's an unselfish player. “Then I just hit it as hard as I could, and it's gone in.” The victory puts Palace top of Group C on three points, with Jong PSV and Sunderland on one and PSG yet to register a point, with each side having played once. And having been involved when the Young Eagles’ won the competition in 2023/24, Nascimento is keen to go one better this time around. “It's good to start over, and it's always important to win the first game,” he said. “Some of us know what it's like to go all the way to the final, so we just want to replicate that, to be honest.” Next up is a different challenge, with Palace facing Swindon Town in the EFL Trophy. With a longer break before then, Williams highlighted the importance of keeping standards high. “I just feel like we've got to keep pushing each other in training,” he said. “I feel like this team has got really good morale in the changing room. We're all really close, so if we just keep this up, good things can happen.” Related News Academy Club Under-21s Related News More News

articles.body: Fantasy College Football Picks: Top DraftKings Week 1 CFB DFS Targets, Values for Thursday 9/3/26 The college football season kicked off last week for a small slate, but now every team gets in on the action for Week 1. This is a great chance to dive into college football DFS. DraftKings has a CFB $120K Thursday Kickoff [$30K to 1st] contest, with $30,000 going to first place. You can enter the contest for just $18 here Quarterback Stud Katin Houser, Illinois vs. UAB, $8,300 Katin Houser was a good get for Illinois in the transfer portal. Houser started his career in the Big Ten at Michigan State but was unable to win the starting job long-term. He transferred to ECU and had two very good seasons as QB1 there. He is now back in the Big Ten for one more season, as he hopes to prove he can compete at the highest level. Houser starts off with a very comfortable matchup against UAB. Last season, the Blazers had one of the worst defenses in football, ranking 130th in defensive EPA/pass. Houser should start his Illinois career with a stellar performance. Value Julian Lewis, Colorado at Georgia Tech, $6,700 Julian Lewis was able to take over as starting quarterback at Colorado by the end of his freshman season. He got some solid game experience under his belt and should be ready to perform as the Week 1 starter this season. Georgia Tech really struggled against the pass last season, ranking 115th in defensive EPA/pass. While this Colorado program might not be where Lewis hoped it would be when he signed with the Buffaloes, he is a very talented player and should have a productive season. Running Back Stud Justice Haynes, Georgia Tech vs. Colorado, $8,100 Justice Haynes had a strong junior season at Michigan, rushing for 857 yards and scoring 10 touchdowns. He is now at Georgia Tech, which has had a great running game under Brent Key. Haynes should be an efficient back who gets plenty of touches this season. Colorado gave up 222.5 rushing yards per game last season, the second-most of any school in the nation. Haynes should run wild in this game and put up big numbers in his first outing as a Yellow Jacket. Value Sawyer Seidl, Wake Forest vs. Akron, $5,500 Sawyer Seidl had an excellent 2025 season at North Dakota. He ran for 897 yards and scored 17 total touchdowns with the Fighting Hawks last season. Now, he is moving up to the FBS level to tote the rock for Wake Forest. The Demon Deacons get a comfortable Week 1 matchup against Akron. Seidl won’t have to face a much higher echelon of athletes than he was accustomed to at the top level of the FCS yet. He should run the ball efficiently in this game and is a strong value play in DFS at running back or FLEX. RELATED College Football Week 1 predictions, picks: Best Bets Cheat Sheet Wide Receiver Stud Danny Scudero, Colorado at Georgia Tech , $6,000 Danny Scudero led the nation in receiving yards in 2025. He caught 88 balls for 1,297 yards and 10 touchdowns for San Jose State, a remarkable campaign at any level. Now, he joins the Buffaloes to be the primary target for Julian Lewis. Scudero should be ready to step in and perform in the Big 12 right away. Last year against Stanford, he had 11 catches for 135 yards and two touchdowns. That was the last time he faced an ACC opponent. Scudero will be ready for Georgia Tech and should start his Colorado career with a bang. Value Marcel Williams, Akron at Wake Forest, $4,200 Marcel Williams had a strong first season with Akron in 2025. He led the team with 45 catches and 641 receiving yards. Williams’ only downfall is that he struggled to find the end zone, only scoring twice last season despite being the team’s top receiver. If he is able to get into the end zone more often, he could become a very productive fantasy player in 2026. Reese Poffenbarger is a talented quarterback who has bounced around as a backup over the past couple of seasons but is ready to step in and be the QB1 for the Zips this season. He should feed Williams early and often in this matchup. articles.excerpt: With many Fantasy Premier League managers turning to their Wildcards in Gameweek 3, we use Solio Analytics' projections to compare different FPL team structures, identify the best players to target and assess the impact of the transfer window.
