They got their wish when the 29-year-old came on as a substitute in the opening day defeat to Brentford, but it wasn’t long before he was causing concern once again. After the game, De Zerbi confirmed (via London Evening Standard ) that Maddison had “suffered a small injury in his shoulder,” and it’s thought he could be out for a couple of weeks at least. Speaking to the club website, the Spurs boss added: “I think with James, we have to find the right plan… We have to work consistently for three, four weeks, and then he's a different player - a different player on the pitch, outside the pitch.” Maddison has completed just five full 90-minute games for Spurs since signing for the club in 2023 (Image credit: Alex Pantling/Getty Images) It says it all that Maddison has completed just five full 90-minute games for Spurs since signing for the club in 2023. That’s a real problem, especially considering Tottenham’s other option in that position, Xavi Simons , is out of action until at least early 2027, having suffered the same ACL injury as Maddison, only seven months later. There is one positive to take from the current Tottenham injury list, however, with Dejan Kulusevski finally back in full training after more than 15 months on the sidelines. Spurs will have to be patient with the Swedish ace, but he could well fill that number 10 role when he’s back to his best. The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week. In the meantime, it looks like Matheus Fernandes will be filling the gap, but that’s far from ideal and not where he has been signed to play. Ten regrets (Image credit: Getty) After signing so many players this summer and rebuilding the squad to De Zerbi’s liking, many had expected that a number 10 would be among the new additions. It wasn’t to be. Morgan Gibbs-White has long been linked with Tottenham , but he stayed at Nottingham Forest. Meanwhile, the likes of Cody Gakpo and Iliman Ndiaye were strongly mooted as potential signings, and they could have eased the pressure in the space behind the striker, but the Liverpool man stayed at Anfield while Ndiaye ended moving to Man City at the last minute. It could be that Tottenham go for a playmaker in January instead, but by that point, will it be too late? Spurs have the potential to challenge at the top this season given the quality of the squad, but not having adequate options in the number 10 role will limit them. In Luca we trust Luca Williams-Barnett is just 17, but could be handed an opportunity in the No.10 position (Image credit: Getty Images) But Tottenham could already have a solution to their problem, and it’s staring Robert De Zerbi right in the face. While the Italian coach clearly favours experience over everything, particularly Premier League pedigree, he’s also taken a liking to Tottenham’s teenage sensation, Luca Williams-Barnett, who plays centrally as an attacking midfielder/forward. Fans in N17 are already raving about the 17-year-old, and rightly so. He’s already flown through the youth ranks and has found himself on the fringes of the first team since the second half of last season. A strong pre-season with plenty of minutes has seen Williams-Barnett’s stock rise further, while he’s already made an appearance for the Lilywhites this term in the 5-1 win over Charlton in the Carabao Cup , coming off the bench after 78 minutes. Spurs have pedigree for producing highly-rated youngsters. Harry Kane is a prime example, but the likes of Alfie Devine, Dane Scarlett, Troy Parrott, Harry Winks , and Oliver Skipp have all tried and failed to make the necessary impact in North London. Mikey Moore and Jamie Donley could still do that, but they’re now out on loan, leaving Williams-Barnett as the most promising prospect in the building right now. Giving the teen substantial minutes this season would not be a token gesture. He absolutely has the quality needed to finally become the next big academy graduate at Tottenham. Williams-Barnett’s skillset includes dazzling dribbling, incredible vision, and an unbelievable level of swagger and flair for someone so young. He’s the kind of maverick Tottenham – and indeed, any club – dream of producing. To let him tread water in the reserves this season would be criminal. Spurs cannot let another exciting young talent stagnate until he decides to move on in search of first-team football. Instead, De Zerbi needs to embrace the vitality and fearlessness Williams-Barnett brings and allow this rough diamond to flourish. Adding a splash of youth could be the perfect way to balance what is a very experienced team. Williams-Barnett is the kind of player who can produce moments of magic, something Spurs have been severely lacking in the last couple of years. While Maddison and Simons are injured, it would surely make sense to give a homegrown talent his chance, rather than shoehorning other midfielders into a role they’re not comfortable in. The supporters would love to see Williams-Barnett get an opportunity; the player himself would almost certainly rise to the challenge, and it could well be the kind of decision that ends up saving Tottenham tens of millions of pounds. articles.body: Who is the top scorer of 2026? Can Harry Kane hold off Kylian Mbappe? Harry Kane celebrates another Bayern goal Kylian Mbappe scored a ludicrous 58 goals for Real Madrid in 2025 , which was 10 goals more than nearest challenger Harry Kane. But Kane was out of the blocks like a bullet in 2026, having already opened up a lead over the field and raced to the 30-goal landmark in the Bundesliga for the season. The criteria: All club goals in all competitions for clubs in Europe’s top 10 leagues. Minutes per goal is your tie-breaker when players are level on goals scored, which at this point a lot of them are. Who are the top scorers of 2026 from across Europe? 10) Vedat Muriqi (Fenerbahce) – 17 goals A veteran of the Turkish Super Lig, Muriqi rejoined Fenerbahce in the summer after finishing second to Kylian Mbappe in the Pichici Trophy race despite former club Mallorca succumbing to relegation. The forward has started with three goals in six games. 9) Marius Mouandilmadji (Samsunspor) – 17 goals Mouandilmadji didn’t score at all in the league between September and December of 2025 but started the year flying in Conference League and Turkish Cup runs. Then he carried that form into the league, including a two-goal haul in an unlikely 4-1 win over Galatasaray. 8) Kylian Mbappe (Real Madrid) – 17 goals A hat-trick against Real Sociedad catapults him into this list; it’s his first in La Liga since May 2025. 7) Vinicius Jnr (Real Madrid) – 18 goals The top scorer for Real Madrid in a year when they have once again won absolutely nothing. He was then made the sixth-highest-paid player in the world. Has now got off the mark in the 2026/27 season. 6) Talisca (Fenerbahce) – 18 goals The Brazilian has casually scored five goals in 2026/27 for Fenerbahce, who have significantly strengthened this summer but kept Talisca leading the line. 5) Raphinha (Barcelona) – 19 goals Now playing up front for Barcelona after the departure of Robert Lewandowski and started the 26/27 season with five goals in three games. He could score a boatload of goals in this team. 4) Donyell Malan (Roma) – 20 goals Absolutely the January signing of the season, the Dutchman’s goals taking the Italian capital club back into the Champions League. Then he opened the new season with five goals in two games. 3) Vangelis Pavlidis (Benfica) – 21 goals A season that began in July has already reaped 11 goals for the Greek striker, who has pulled his team through Europa League qualifying and grabbed a hat-trick in a 7-0 win in the league. 2) Luis Suarez (Sporting) – 23 goals Not that one. The 28-year-old Colombian seamlessly replaced Viktor Gyokeres and has scored goals for fun, including a double in the Champions League v PSG and another in the comeback win over Bodo/Glimt. Couldn’t find the goal Sporting needed at the Emirates, though. Ended the season as the top scorer in the Portuguese league with 28 goals but his goal in the cup final was in vain as Sporting surprisingly lost to Torreense. After a poor World Cup, he is already off the mark in 26/27. 1) Harry Kane (Bayern Munich) – 33 goals Last year’s runner-up had another excellent start to 2026, which began with an 8-1 win over Wolfsburg and took in the career 500-goal mark in February. There’s little wonder that Bayern are so keen to nail him down to a new contract. The serial winner scored in both legs of the Champions League quarter-final win and semi-final defeat to Real Madrid and Paris Saint-Germain respectively, before wrapping up his Bundesliga campaign with a hat-trick in much the same way he delivered Bayern the DFB Pokal against Stuttgart. He played two whole games for Bayern Munich without a goal this season before the cup gave him the chance to open his account with a brace. articles.body: Arsenal injury, suspension list and return dates vs. Chelsea: Declan Rice, Jurrien Timber, Cristhian Mosquera latest - Sports Mole Menu Loading... Premier League Gameweek 3 Arsenal Sep 6, 2026 4.30pm Emirates Stadium Chelsea Arsenal injury, suspension list and return dates vs. Chelsea: Declan Rice, Jurrien Timber, Cristhian Mosquera latest Ben Knapton 03 Sep 2026 05:55 , Last updated: 03 Sep 2026 05:55 Â© Iconsport / SPI Two for two in their Premier League title defence, Arsenal now face the team billed by many to run them the closest this year - Chelsea. The Gunners host the Blues in Sunday's high-profile top-flight London derby, seeking to maintain their perfect starts both points-wise and clean sheets-wise after seeing off Coventry City and Aston Villa. Bukayo Saka's scrappy finish was all that was needed for Arsenal to take down Villa 1-0 on Monday, but the triumph did come at a cost for Mikel Arteta. Here, Sports Mole rounds up all of Arsenal's latest injury and suspension news before their showdown with Chelsea, who are only below the Gunners in the Premier League table on goal difference after a chaotic 4-3 win over Brighton & Hove Albion. Declan Rice © Iconsport / PA Images Status: Minor doubt Type of injury: Unspecified Possible return date: September 6 (vs. Chelsea) Declan Rice was observed limping back to the dugout after being substituted late into the win over Villa, raising some concern over his fitness for the weekend. However, there was no firm word from Arteta after the game, and no news may be good news as far as Arsenal are concerned. Cristhian Mosquera © Iconsport / Allstar Picture Library Ltd / Alamy Status: Minor doubt Type of injury: Strain Possible return date: September 6 (vs. Chelsea) Cristhian Mosquera was brought off in the 79th minute of the win over Villa with an apparent issue, but Arteta revealed that the Spaniard was "about" to feel something, rather than pulling a muscle in that exact moment. As a result, Mosquera is expected to be given the all-clear for Sunday, but his minor concern may open the door for Ezri Konsa to make his first start. William Saliba © Iconsport / Johnny Fidelin/Icon Sport Status: Out Type of injury: Back Possible return date: November 21 (vs. Newcastle United) William Saliba will be out for months after exacerbating a back injury during the World Cup, and the Frenchman is thought to be targeting a return towards the end of 2026. Jurrien Timber © Iconsport / Every Second Media/Alamy Live News Status: Out Type of injury: Groin Possible return date: September 12 (vs. Sunderland) Jurrien Timber should finally be closing in on a return from the groin injury that has plagued him for months, and a comeback in September is not out of the question, but the London derby is likely to come too soon. articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz recovers from slow start to get past Jaime Faria | Flashscore.com All Football Transfer News Premier League US Open Features Champions League Darts Snooker Golf Cycling MLB NFL Most read on Flashscore News Transfer News LIVE: Richarlison set for move to Turkey, Ajax sign Adingra Aguero backs Jesus to shine at Barcelona: 'He can easily score 10 or 15 goals' Man City confirm joint British record signing of Enzo Fernandez from Chelsea Antonsen seals comeback-win against rising Chinese star as favorites crash out in Shenzhen Carlos Alcaraz recovers from slow start to get past Jaime Faria AFP Carlos Alcaraz is through to the US Open third round. CHARLY TRIBALLEAU / AFP Defending champion Carlos Alcaraz overcame an early wobble to book his place in the third round of the US Open on Wednesday, recovering from a set down to defeat Portugal's Jaime Faria in four sets. Alcaraz , who is playing in New York after returning from a four-month layoff due to a wrist injury, defeated his 72nd-ranked opponent 4-6, 6-0, 6-3, 6-2 in 2hr 40 min at the Arthur Ashe Stadium. Alcaraz, who will face China's Wu Yibing in the third round, blamed his first set problems on a failure to convert a golden break point opportunity that would have given him a 4-2 lead. Instead, Faria leveled at 3-3 and then broke Alcaraz in the next game to go 4-3 up. Tough match for me. Obviously the first set, I was feeling great, I had break point, I missed it, " Alcaraz said. After that I was in a rush. I did't take time, I wasn't patient and that obviously cost me the break. Against someone like Jaime, he's serving 140, 141 (mph), it's very difficult. I tried to stay calm ... think good things are going to happen again. Match stats: Faria vs Alcaraz Flashscore Faria meanwhile was left ruing his inability to build on an impressive opening set. The 23-year-old's serve fell apart in the second while Alcaraz upped the tempo and began to find a telling extra zip in his groundstrokes. Although Alcaraz had to save two break points in the opening game before holding, it was all one-way traffic thereafter. Faria was broken three times as Alcaraz went through the gears to take control of the contest. The Spaniard's momentum extended into the third set, with Faria broken again to go 2-0 down. Faria hit back with a break of Alcaraz's serve to make it 2-1, but was soon back in trouble after being broken in the next game to trail 3-1. The set went with serve thereafter as Alcaraz took a 2-1 lead. Alcaraz went a double break up in the fourth to move into a 5-1 lead and served out to seal victory. Sign up AFC East Buffalo Bills Miami Dolphins New England Patriots New York Jets AFC North Baltimore Ravens Cincinnati Bengals Cleveland Browns Pittsburgh Steelers AFC South Houston Texans Indianapolis Colts Jacksonville Jaguars Tennessee Titans AFC West Denver Broncos Kansas City Chiefs Las Vegas Raiders Los Angeles Chargers NFC East Dallas Cowboys New York Giants Philadelphia Eagles Washington Commanders NFC North Chicago Bears Detroit Lions Green Bay Packers Minnesota Vikings NFC South Atlanta Falcons Carolina Panthers New Orleans Saints Tampa Bay Buccaneers NFC West Arizona Cardinals Los Angeles Rams San Francisco 49ers Seattle Seahawks AFC East Buffalo Bills Miami Dolphins New England Patriots New York Jets AFC North Baltimore Ravens Cincinnati Bengals Cleveland Browns Pittsburgh Steelers AFC South Houston Texans Indianapolis Colts Jacksonville Jaguars Tennessee Titans AFC West Denver Broncos Kansas City Chiefs Las Vegas Raiders Los Angeles Chargers NFC East Dallas Cowboys New York Giants Philadelphia Eagles Washington Commanders NFC North Chicago Bears Detroit Lions Green Bay Packers Minnesota Vikings NFC South Atlanta Falcons Carolina Panthers New Orleans Saints Tampa Bay Buccaneers NFC West Arizona Cardinals Los Angeles Rams San Francisco 49ers Seattle Seahawks Rumor Mill Peacock PFT Shop 49ers DE Sam Okuayinonu not on team flight to Australia, questionable with foot injury Michael David Smith Michael David Smith Published September 3, 2026 05:18 AM Facebook Twitter Email The 49ers are on their way to Australia, but defensive end Sam Okuayinonu is not with them. Shortly before departure, the 49ers announced that Okuayinonu would not be on the team flight to Melbourne for next week’s game against the Rams. Okuayinonu has a foot injury. Ordinarily, when a player doesn’t make a team flight, that means he’s not going to play in the game, but the 49ers are currently classifying Okuayinonu as questionable. Depending on how his foot responds to treatment in the coming days, it’s possible that he’ll fly to Australia separately. Okuayinonu is an important part of the 49ers’ defense: Last year he started 12 games in the regular season and both playoff games. This year he’s expected to be a backup but get plenty of snaps in the defensive line rotation, if he’s healthy. The 49ers’ other players, including tight end George Kittle and defensive end Nick Bosa, are on the plane. Kittle and Bosa are both rehabbing from injuries and there were concerns that they might not be ready for Week One, but from all indications they’re both ready to go against the Rams. The 49ers are flying to Australia a full week early to adjust to the time change and prepare on-site. The Rams are not arriving in Australia until the day before the game. articles.body: Top CFL Week 14 DraftKings Plays and Strategy | RotoWire CFL DFS Picks and Cheat Sheet for Week 14 on DraftKings The Alouettes' Tyson Philpot has been the gold standard for CFL receivers in 2026, and he draws an enticing Week 14 matchup against the vulnerable Lions pass defense. Updated on September 3, 2026 1:10AM EST Share By: Juan Carlos Blanco @jcblanco22 Updated on September 3, 2026 1:10AM EST DraftKings CFL DFS Picks Mock Draft Simulator Prep for your 2026 Fantasy Football draft with free, unlimited drafts, and real-time grades. CFL DFS Picks and Cheat Sheet for Week 14 on DraftKings The CFL's Week 14 slate is spread out over Labour Day weekend, kicking off Friday with a Lions-Alouettes clash and then wrapping up with a Monday doubleheader that features the 8-3 Elks. We also have an idle day Saturday and a marquee Blue Bombers-Roughriders battle Sunday. As customary, we'll break down multiple options for each roster spot and also offer a trio of core plays to consider making the centerpiece of your lineups. Quarterback Plays for CFL Week 14 Davis Alexander MTL at BC ($10,100): Alexander is putting together a stellar season that's seen him complete 72.5 percent of his passes and average a career-high 332.5 passing yards per game, while also mustering an elite 24:2 TD:INT across 11 contests. Alexander's most recent masterpiece came just last week against the Blue Bombers, when he threw four touchdown passes without an interception while registering 28.0 DK points, his eighth tally of greater than 23 DK points this season. The Lions have been about middle of the pack against the pass, allowing 298.0 passing yards per game. However, BC has surrendered a co-league-high 23 touchdown passes as well, along with the fourth-most completions of 30+ yards (21). Meanwhile, Alexander is averaging a career-high 10.2 yards per attempt and has a league-high 29 completions of at least 30 yards, making this a premium matchup. Cody Fajardo , EDM at CGY ($10,000): Fajardo is in the midst of a career-best season in his own right, as he's already tied a career high with 18 touchdown passes and is averaging a career-high 306.2 passing yards per contest. He's added another three scores on the ground as part of his 218 rushing yards, and he'll enter a favorable Week 14 matchup with three straight tallies of greater than 21 DK points. The opposing Stampeders make for good targets, as Calgary is surrendering 318.4 passing yards per game and has also conceded a co-league-high 23 touchdown passes to tie them with BC for the dubious lead in that category. Calgary has also conceded the second-most completions of 30+ yards (24), while Fajardo is averaging a solid 9.2 yards per attempt and has 18 completions of 30+ yards. Tre Ford HAM vs. TOR ($9,500): Ford is the current flavor of the month when it comes to the Tiger-Cats' ongoing attempts to stabilize the QB position following Bo Levi Mitchell 's serious ankle injury earlier this season. Ford's current starting stint is technically his second following Mitchell's injury, and he seems to be locked into a rhythm at the moment in terms of his play. Ford has accrued 19.5 and 24.5 DK points in his two most recent starts in Weeks 12 and 13, throwing for 356 and 212 yards in that pair of contests. The Argonauts could well facilitate an extension of Ford's encouraging stretch of play, as Toronto has been very vulnerable to the pass all season. The Argos are surrendering 318.7 passing yards per game at 9.4 yards per attempt, along with an elevated 68.9 percent completion rate. Then, Toronto has also given up a league-high 27 completions of 30+ yards, setting up Ford, who already has eight completions of 30+ yards, for some potential downfield success. ALSO CONSIDER Chad Kelly TOR at HAM ($10,300) Running Back Plays for CFL Week 14 Zander Horvath BC at MTL ($10,600): Horvath's breakout season continued in fine fashion in Week 13, when he compiled a career-high 50.4 DK points on the strength of 164 rushing yards and four touchdowns against the Redblacks. The versatile back also has a tally of 40.1 DK points this season, and he's recorded 14.6 DK points or greater on seven occasions already despite starting the season in a minor role behind veteran James Butler . Horvath is being consistently used in the passing game as well, affording him a very solid floor regardless of matchup. The Alouettes have given up a relatively modest 98.6 rushing yards per game, but they've done so at an elevated clip of 5.6 yards per carry. Montreal has also given up the third-most rushing touchdowns (14), and the Als have yielded the fourth-most runs of 10+ yards (38). Meanwhile, Horvath already has a league-high 13 rushing touchdowns and 15 rushes of 10+ yards, including six of 20+. With an average of 6.0 yards per carry and a 21-205-3 receiving line, Horvath's fantasy floor is among the top at any position. Brady Oliveira WPG at SSK ($9,600): Oliveira continues to deal with an ankle injury this week, but that issue didn't prevent him from recording over 100 rushing yards in each of the last two games while posting DK-point tallies of 17.9 and 20.8 DK points. The versatile veteran is actually averaging 22.5 DK points over the five games dating back to Week 8 against the Stampeders, and he comes into Week 14 just 44 rushing yards short of his fifth straight 1,000-yard season. Oliveira is averaging a career-high 6.2 yards per carry as well, and his 27 runs of 10+ yards are second only to the Elks' Justin Rankin 's 29. The Roughriders present as a tough on-paper matchup against the run, as they've allowed the second-fewest rushing yards per game (72.5). However, they've allowed it at a clip of 4.6 yards per carry and have given up 25 runs of 10+ yards, suggesting Oliveira could continue churning out strong production as long as he's able to suit up and the Blue Bombers stick with the run. ALSO CONSIDER: Dedrick Mills CGY vs. EDM ($8,600); Quali Conley , SSK vs. WPG ($6,800) Wide Receiver/Slotback Plays for CFL Week 14 Tyson Philpot MTL vs. BC ($10,700): The caliber of Philpot's season is such that even when he has a slight downturn in yardage, he still churns out highly useful fantasy production. The most recent example is the last two games, when Philpot has recorded 28.5 and 21.7 DK points despite posting respective tallies of 75 and 87 receiving yards in those contests. Philpot has gotten there with the help of nine- and seven-catch efforts, as well as three total TDs that brought his season total to a career-best 10 in that category. The vulnerabilities of the Lions defense against the pass were already detailed in Rourke's entry, and Philpot is well-equipped to exploit BC's penchant for allowing chunk plays downfield, considering he has a league-leading 1,316 receiving yards and 10 catches of 30+ yards. Philpot also has a CFL-high 116 targets, affording him a very reliable floor that's helped lead to a season average of 27.3 DK points per contest. Damonte Coxie TOR at HAM ($9,600): Coxie's rapport with Chad Kelly has continued to blossom throughout the season, and the speedy receiver comes into Week 14 having eclipsed 22 DK points in three of the past four games. Coxie just posted his third 145-yard-plus tally of the season in Week 13 as well, getting to 146 yards on just five catches versus the Roughriders. Coxie has already compiled a career-best 943 receiving yards, making it very possible he reaches the 1,000-yard mark for the first time in his career during this game. The opposing Tiger-Cats have surrendered a 70.4 percent completion rate on the season, as well as 18 touchdown passes. Hamilton has done a good job limiting big plays, but Coxie has proven capable of producing in all three passing windows. He's averaging a robust 16.8 yards per catch and has the second-most second-down receptions in the league (21), and Coxie also carries a solid floor considering he's averaging 8.2 targets per contest. Austin Mack EDM at CGY ($9,400): Mack has enjoyed a highly productive reunion with Fajardo this season in Edmonton, with the veteran duo recreating a lot of the magic they'd managed during the 2023 campaign in Montreal. Mack is already within striking distance of his second 1,000-yard season – the first having come in that aforementioned season with the Alouettes – and he's recorded a career-high seven touchdowns across 11 games as well on the way to an average of 17.7 DK points. per contest. As already detailed in Fajardo's entry, the Stampeders have been highly vulnerable against the pass. Calgary has especially had trouble preventing big plays downfield, while Mack is averaging 15.6 yards per reception and has six catches of 30+ yards. The veteran receiver is also averaging just under eight targets per game, and while Mack has the fifth-most yards after the catch in the CFL (302), the Stamps have surrendered the fifth-most yards after reception in the league (1,288). Jermaine Jackson BC at MTL ($5,600): Jackson's week-to-week production has been a bit hard to trust, but that volatility is baked into his very reasonable salary. Additionally, the speedy slotback has already flashed a particularly impressive ceiling on two occasions, scoring 29.9 and 19.8 DK points in a pair of games. The latter total just came in Week 13 against the Redblacks, only two games after Jackson also had an impressive 89-yard effort versus the Stampeders. The Alouettes have generally done a good job limiting big plays through the air, as they've yielded a league-low 12 completions of 30+ yards. However, Montreal has surrendered 287.5 passing yards per game and 19 touchdown passes, along with the third-most yards after the catch in the CFL (1,333). Meanwhile Jackson is averaging a stellar 19.2 yards per reception and already has four catches of 30+ yards on only 29 total receptions, and he's averaging a stout 7.4 yards after the catch per grab as well. ALSO CONSIDER KeeSean Johnson SSK vs. WPG ($9,900) Team Defense Plays for CFL Week 14 Hamilton Tiger-Cats ($3,700) vs. Toronto Argonauts: The Ti-Cats may not have fully maximized their potential against Stamps backup quarterback Josh Love in Week 13, but Hamilton still recorded an interception and three more sacks. The Ti-Cats are up to 12 interceptions (third most in the CFL) and 18 sacks, and they rank No. 3 in total yards and No. 2 in passing yards allowed. The matchup against the Argonauts' offense, particularly the passing attack, is no picnic, but there should be some sack and turnover opportunities. Toronto's Chad Kelly has already tossed 17 interceptions in 11 games, and he's also taken 20 sacks. The Ti-Cats are also tied for the third-fewest total touchdowns allowed (35), and they already picked Kelly off once while sacking him twice during the first meeting of the season between the teams back in Week 6. While the Argos are very likely to still pile up some formidable numbers through the air, the Ti-Cats could well make their selection worthwhile with multiple sacks and turnovers. CFL DFS Cheat Sheet for Week 14 Cody Fajardo , QB Brady Oliveira , RB Austin Mack , WR Total salary expenditure: $29k We're looking to lock in some floor with this trio and also take advantage of a strong matchup for the Elks' passing game. Fajardo has already tied a career high with 18 touchdown passes, and he's completing over 70.0 percent of his passes for the fifth straight season. He and Mack have an enticing matchup against a Stampeders defense allowing well over 300 passing yards per game, while Oliveira is putting together another outstanding all-around season that has him just 44 rushing yards short of his fifth straight 1,000-yard campaign. articles.title: Two Massive Games On Deck For Class 4A Of Iowa High School Football
articles.excerpt: Week 2 will see Cedar Rapids Xavier play Western Dubuque while Sergeant Bluff-Luton heads to Lewis Central.
articles.source_type: Gameweek squads, team news round-ups, deadline reminders
articles.body: Two Massive Games On Deck For Class 4A Of Iowa High School Football Xavier's Ty Weiss (4) runs with the ball Nov. 20, 2025 during the Class 4A state football championship against the Pella Dutch at the UNI-Dome in Cedar Falls, Iowa. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect When it comes to Iowa high school football, there may be no deeper division than Class 4A. Cedar Rapids Xavier is the reigning state champion in Class 4A, but there are several teams that would like nothing more than to knock them off. The Saints will be on the road in Week 2, as they take on Western Dubuque in one of those key early-season showdowns. Another sees Sergeant Bluff-Luton head to Council Bluffs to play Lewis Central. More : Seven Canât-Miss Week 2 Iowa High School Football Games Cash Parks, Cedar Rapids Xavier Look To Keep Win Streak Alive Will Buchman Stadium be the site for the end of the Cedar Rapids Xavier run of victories? The Bobcats would like nothing more than that. Western Dubuque scored a one-sided 48-21 decision over Dubuque Wahlert Catholic in Week 1, as Iowa State University commit Drew Bergfeld rushed 14 times for 138 yards and scored two touchdowns. Brady Rissman threw for 118 yards and a pair of touchdowns, as Willie Williams, Jr. caught six passes for 91 yards and a score from Rissman. But will they be enough? The Saints rolled through North Scott, 33-7, and have won five of the last six vs. Western Dubuque, including a 21-13 victory last fall. Cash Parks threw a pair of touchdowns and ran in another, throwing for 158 yards. Dawson Doyle stepped right in as the lead running back, rushing 16 times for 119 yards, as Ty Weiss was unstoppable, catching seven passes for 125 yards and two scores. Oh, and Weiss also kicked through a successful 50-yard field goal and threw a 34-yard touchdown pass to Connor Clark. The defense for the Saints racked up four quarterback sacks and eight tackles for loss, recovering a fumble. Warriors, Titans Set For Showdown Last year, Sergeant Bluff-Luton made the transition from Class 3A to Class 4A without skipping a beat, starting with a 30-27 victory over Lewis Central. To start 2026, the Warriors handled Sioux City Bishop Heelan, 21-10, as Justin Ehlers completed 7 of 10 for 170 yards and three touchdowns. Gavin Ahrendt had two receptions for 88 yards, as both went for scores. And despite all that, the vaunted Sergeant Bluff-Luton rushing attack was strong again, led by Ryan Husenâs 74 yards on just nine carries. As a team, the Warriors averaged almost six yards per rush. The stars for Lewis Central shined bright in a 48-41 victory over North Polk, as Braydan Doss rushed 25 times for 164 yards with three touchdowns while Braxton Parks had eight receptions for 84 and a score. Eric Corrill completed 11 of 15 for 128 and two scores while Camden Dahlheim was 8-for-12 for 95 yards. Add us as a preferred source on Google Follow Loading recommendations... articles.body: Arsenal vs Chelsea Prediction, Lineups & Team News | RotoWire Arsenal vs Chelsea Prediction, Predicted Lineups & Team News Arsenal vs Chelsea prediction, predicted lineups, team news, injuries and odds for Sunday's Premier League clash at the Emirates Stadium. September 2, 2026 Share By: Adam Zdroik @RotoZdroik September 2, 2026 Game Previews Mock Draft Simulator Prep for your 2026 Fantasy Football draft with free, unlimited drafts, and real-time grades. Arsenal vs Chelsea Prediction, Predicted Lineups & Team News Arsenal host Chelsea at the Emirates on Sunday with both sides unbeaten on six points, which is where the similarity ends. Arsenal have scored four without conceding, while Chelsea's first two matches have produced 12 total goals. Our Arsenal vs Chelsea prediction favors Mikel Arteta's side to make that difference in control count. Chelsea have not kept a clean sheet in 18 consecutive league matches, their longest run since 1960-61. Xabi Alonso has won both of his Premier League games in charge and described the second, a 4-3 victory over Brighton, with the words: "I am not excited." This preview covers predicted lineups injury news , head-to-head history, the tactical matchup and a score prediction for Sunday's Premier League game in north London. When & Where to Watch (USA) Sunday, Sept. 6 at 4:30 PM BST / 11:30 AM ET / 8:30 AM PT Venue: Emirates Stadium, London English TV: USA Network Spanish TV: Telemundo Streaming: Peacock, Fubo, Sling Blue, Hulu + Live TV, DirecTV Stream Arsenal vs Chelsea Lineups & Injury News Arsenal vs Chelsea Predicted Lineups Predicted lineups: Arsenal are projected in a 4-2-3-1 with one change from the side that won at Villa Park, as Ezri Konsa comes in for Cristhian Mosquera , who has a hamstring scare. Chelsea are projected in the 3-4-2-1 Alonso has used throughout, with Reece James at right wing back in place of Malo Gusto and Emiliano Martinez keeping the goalkeeper's shirt he took a week after signing. RotoWire Premier League Lineups Gameweek 3 · Premier League Arsenal vs Chelsea Lineups update automatically. View Preview mode. Live lineup feed not yet available — showing projected starters. This widget updates automatically when official lineups drop. Arsenal ARS Chelsea CHE Predicted Predicted Arsenal Predicted Lineup not yet posted Check back closer to kickoff Chelsea Predicted Lineup not yet posted Check back closer to kickoff Confirmed Predicted Lineups via RotoWire Arsenal predicted starting XI (4-2-3-1): David Raya Ben White Ezri Konsa Gabriel Riccardo Calafiori Declan Rice Myles Lewis-Skelly Bukayo Saka Martin Odegaard Christos Tzolis Kai Havertz Chelsea predicted starting XI (3-4-2-1): Emiliano Martinez Levi Colwill Wesley Fofana Maxence Lacroix Pedro Neto Reece James Romeo Lavia Jorrel Hato Cole Palmer Morgan Rogers Joao Pedro Check the Premier League injury table and the player news feed before kickoff because there are still some questions. Arsenal Team News & Injuries William Saliba remains out with the back problem he aggravated at the World Cup, while Jurrien Timber is still weeks from full training after groin surgery. Cristhian Mosquera is the immediate question. He completed 90 minutes at Villa Park before reporting that he felt as though something was coming in his hamstring. Arteta described it as precautionary rather than an injury, but it is enough for Ezri Konsa to be projected for his first Arsenal start against the club he left less than two weeks ago. Bruno Guimaraes is available after missing the opener with a groin issue, although he remained on the bench at Villa. Viktor Gyokeres is also fit but has yet to play a Premier League minute this season, with Kai Havertz retaining the center-forward spot. That leaves center-back as the only obvious change from the side that has opened the season with consecutive clean sheets. Chelsea Team News & Injuries Moises Caicedo is Chelsea's biggest fitness concern. After missing the start of the season, he returned from the bench against Brighton only to come off again within minutes. Alonso said Caicedo was cautious after feeling discomfort rather than suffering a new injury, but his availability remains uncertain. Jordan Henderson and Marco Palestra are also doubts. Chelsea's deadline moves have changed the spine of the side. Enzo Fernandez has joined Manchester City, while Emiliano Martinez has replaced Robert Sanchez in goal and made several important saves in the 4-3 win over Brighton. Wesley Fofana is available again after serving his two-match suspension, while Levi Colwill continues to be managed carefully after last season's injury. Geovany Quenda and Estevao were both options from the bench against Brighton. Chelsea are close to full strength numerically, but the defense remains unsettled and Caicedo's fitness could determine how Alonso sets up his midfield. Arsenal vs Chelsea Head-to-Head Record These clubs have met 215 times, with Arsenal winning 88 to Chelsea's 66 and 61 drawn. In the Premier League alone it is 67 meetings, Arsenal 27, Chelsea 20, and 20 draws. The current run is emphatic. Arsenal are unbeaten in the last ten meetings across all competitions, winning seven and drawing three, and unbeaten in the last nine in the league. They have won their last four home league games against Chelsea, their best such run since taking five straight between 1990 and 1994. Chelsea's last win over Arsenal was a 2-0 at the Emirates on Aug. 22, 2021, five years ago. Arsenal vs Chelsea Tactical Analysis Arsenal have not conceded a goal. Coventry were beaten 3-0 with Havertz, Saka and Odegaard scoring, and Aston Villa lost 1-0 at home without registering a single shot on target, which meant Raya made no saves. Arteta's summary of the Villa game was about the two halves of the job: "when we had to suffer, we did suffer, and when we had to be really dominant, we were." He has done it without Saliba and without Timber, which is the strongest argument yet for the way he spent this summer, five signings around the 50 million mark rather than one enormous one. Chelsea are the most watchable team in the league and possibly the least controlled. They led Brighton 3-0 inside 32 minutes and won 4-3, and along the way conceded 74.4 percent possession, the highest figure recorded against Chelsea since 2003-04, and completed 146 passes, their fewest in a Premier League game in the same span. Before that they won 3-2 at Fulham. Alonso is only the fourth manager to oversee seven or more goals in his first two Premier League games, after Bobby Robson, Michael Laudrup and Marcelo Bielsa, and he keeps describing it as a process rather than a plan working. The 18-game clean-sheet drought is the number that decides how this reads. Chelsea have conceded in every league game since the middle of last season, and they are walking into a side that has scored four goals in two games from a settled front line. Joao Pedro is the counterweight and he has been extraordinary, producing a goal, an assist and an own goal against Brighton, only the sixth player in Premier League history to manage all three in one match, while winning 13 duels. Cole Palmer is the swing. Alonso has been explicit about needing him: "if we want to have a good team we need a great Cole." Palmer scored the winner at Fulham and the decisive fourth against Brighton after a 10-goal league season, and he looks reset. Against Arsenal's double pivot of Rice and Lewis-Skelly, whether he can find the pocket in front of Gabriel and Konsa is most of Chelsea's route in. Arsenal vs Chelsea Key Matchups Joao Pedro Gabriel and Ezri Konsa The best in-form forward in the league against the only defense yet to concede, with the added wrinkle that the man marking him may be making his Arsenal debut from the start. Joao Pedro has three goal involvements in two games and thrives on chaos, drifting off the front and arriving late rather than standing still. Konsa is an experienced Premier League center back who spent last season doing exactly this job for Villa, but he has played 20-odd minutes for Arsenal and this is a London derby at a full Emirates. Gabriel is the constant, and Arsenal have not needed him to be brilliant yet. Cole Palmer Declan Rice and Myles Lewis-Skelly Chelsea's two No. 10s are Palmer and Morgan Rogers , and Arsenal's answer is a double pivot rather than a single holder. Rice is doing the job he has always done, and Lewis-Skelly next to him is the more interesting half, a converted left back being used in central midfield rather than in defense. Palmer has scored in both league games and both came from him picking up possession outside the box and driving at goal. If Arsenal's pivot lets him turn, Chelsea will get their goal. If they do not, Chelsea have to score from the wing backs. Arsenal vs Chelsea Odds Arsenal are favored at home between -143 and -165 with the draw settled around +275, but Chelsea's price is the one to look at: +350 at BetMGM out to +420 at FanDuel. A 70-cent spread on the away side of a London derby says the books are valuing Chelsea's back three differently rather than reacting to anything in the team news. Arsenal Corners & free kicks: Declan Rice Bukayo Saka Bruno Guimaraes Christos Tzolis Martin Odegaard Penalties: Viktor Gyokeres Bukayo Saka Martin Odegaard Bruno Guimaraes Chelsea Corners & free kicks: Reece James Pedro Neto Cole Palmer Penalties: Cole Palmer Danny Welbeck Gyokeres is listed first on Arsenal penalties and has not been on the pitch, so Saka is the man in possession of that job with Odegaard behind him. Chelsea's list has thinned considerably, with Enzo Fernandez gone to Manchester City, Estevao a substitute and Valentin Barco out on loan, which leaves James and Palmer to do almost all of it. Arsenal vs Chelsea Prediction Arsenal have kept two clean sheets, are unbeaten in ten against this opponent and have not lost a home league game to Chelsea in three attempts. Chelsea have scored seven, which is why this will not be quiet, but they have also conceded five and have not shut anyone out in 18 league games. That is a team that will trade, and trading with a settled Arsenal front line at the Emirates is how you lose by two. Joao Pedro and Palmer are good enough to get one, and I expect they will. I do not expect Chelsea to keep pace at the other end. Score Prediction: Arsenal 3-1 Chelsea Upcoming Fixtures Arsenal travel to Sunderland on Sept. 12 and Chelsea host Hull City the same day, with both clubs starting their Champions League campaigns in the following midweek. Arch Manning, Texas Longhorns (+750) 2025 Stats: 3,163 pass yds | 36 total TDs | 399 rush yds | 61.4 comp% Week 1: Vs Texas State — Saturday at 3:30 PM ET Arch Manning will get to shake off the rust against a Texas State team that allowed 31.2 points per game last year (T-104th). A comparable opponent would be San Jose State, who Manning put up five total touchdowns against last season and 318 yards. Manning’s Heisman campaign really doesn’t start until Week 2 when Ohio State comes to town, but then again, his Heisman case might end there too. 2. Jeremiah Smith, Ohio State Buckeyes (+1400) 2025 Stats: 87 rec | 1,243 yds | 13 total TDs | 14.3 ypc Week 1: Vs Ball State — Saturday at 12:30 PM ET In 2024, Jeremiah Smith posted six receptions for 92 yards and two touchdowns against Akron. In 2025 versus Texas, Smith again caught six passes, but totaled 43 yards and didn’t score in a 14-7 win. In 2026, Ohio State has Ball State on deck and Smith will likely find himself in the end zone at once. Smith has scored a touchdown in nine out of 11 career conference games with Texas being both exceptions (OSU at Texas in Week 2!). 3. Darian Mensah, Miami Hurricanes (+1100) 2025 Stats: 3,973 pass yds | 34 pass TDs | 66.8 comp% | 6 INTs Week 1: At Stanford — Friday at 9:00 PM ET Darian Mensah takes over a Miami offense that’s tailor-made for him. The Hurricanes averaged 30.0 points per game last year (T-32nd) and will absolutely blow past that this year. Stanford allowed 29.2 points per game in 2025 (87th) and will have a hard time containing Mensah will all these new toys on offense. Mensah is my pick for the Heisman and I think worth taking at +1100 if you’re a betting person. The Heisman could come down to Miami at Notre Dame on November 7 and be Mensah versus CJ Carr . It seems like the two could be on a collision course. Whoever wins that game will have a good chance at 11-1 or 12-0. Ohio State opens with Ball State, so a near perfect game is expected of Sayin. True Freshman WR Chris Henry Jr. (6-foot-5 195 lbs) will make his Buckeyes debut and could be a red zone target for Sayin early in the season. 5. Ole Miss and Louisville meet in Nashville, TN where the two offenses will look to gain a rhythm in the Music City. Without Lane Kiffin , Ole Miss scored 41, 39, and 27 on Tulane, Georgia, and Miami during the College Football Playoff. In Chambliss’ two regular season games versus non-conference opponents last year, he totaled five touchdowns and 640 passing yards against Tulane and The Citadel. 6. Once Oregon goes to Illinois, that kickstarts seven consecutive games the Ducks will alternate time zones. Oregon’s schedule isn’t easy, but Dan Lanning will have Moore and the Ducks ready for the PAC-12 preseason favorite Boise State in Week 1. Hoover should be able to shred the North Texas defense. With 11 games of 300-plus passing yards and another 11 games with three or more passing touchdowns over the last two seasons, I wouldn’t be surprised if Hoover is unleashed right out the gate. 8. Notre Dame opens with Wisconsin this year, a team that had 32 sacks in 2025 following 17 in 2024. Carr was only sacked 12 times through 12 games last season. Staying upright and avoiding turnovers will be how he finds success without their top two running backs from a year ago. 10. articles.title: When Does Lanterns Episode 4 Come Out on HBO?
articles.excerpt: Lanterns is gearing up for a juicy flashback episode, which could answer some critical questions from the start of the series. Sam Connon breaks down everything you need to know before Episode 4 of the latest DC Universe project to hit HBO airs on Sunday night. The post When Does Lanterns Episode 4 Come Out on HBO? appeared first on DraftKings Network .
articles.source_type: Captain picks ranked with reasoning, gameweek rankings, DFS targets
articles.body: When Does Lanterns Episode 4 Come Out on HBO? Lanterns took a page right out of the prestige TV handbook with its most recent flashback episode, dividing audiences in the process. The Green Lantern show has had more in common with True Detective than Superman from the start, though, porting co-creator Damon Lindelof’s Watchmen vibes directly into James Gunn’s rebooted DC Universe. If you are ready to jump right back into the superhero-centered mystery, here is everything you need to know before Lanterns Episode 4 premieres: When does Lanterns Episode 4 come out? Season 1 Episode 4 will premiere on HBO 9 p.m. ET Sunday, September 6 . It will be available to stream on HBO Max at the same time. The episode is expected to have a runtime around 52 minutes. Like The Penguin House of the Dragon and most other major HBO titles, Lanterns will release one episode a week – all on Sunday nights. There will be eight episodes in Season 1, as there were for both seasons of Peacemaker and The Penguin . As a result, the finale will air on Sunday, October 4. (Warning: Spoilers for Lanterns Episode 3, Superman, Peacemaker and Supergirl ahead.) Who will show up this episode? Lanterns spent most of Episode 3 in the past, giving us a look at younger versions of several characters. We should be firmly back in 2016 and 2026 for at least Episode 4, meaning the main cast will be taking center stage once again. Here is a look at who could appear in Episode 4: Aaron Pierre as John Stewart Kyle Chandler as Hal Jordan Ulrich Thomsen as Thaal Sinestro Kelly Macdonald as Sheriff Kerry Kane Garret Dillahunt as William Macon Poorna Jagannathan as Zoe Macon Jason Ritter as Billy Macon Paul Ben-Victor as Antaan Laura Linney as Lianna Nathan Fillion as Guy Gardner Sherman Augustus as John Stewart Sr. Nicole Ari Parker as Bernadette Stewart Romeo Brown as Aaron Stewart Jade Ramirez as Jessica Jordan Henry Samiri as Adolescent Hal Jordan Shea Pritchard as Noah Macon Cary Christopher as Adolescent Noah Macon Paula Patton as TBD What to expect in Lanterns Episode 4? Fresh off an extended flashback in Episode 3, Episode 4 will pick up right where Episode 2 left off. Hal went to visit his old mentor, Sinestro, in a space prison to find out what he knows about the Manhunters. Sinestro turned the tables on Hal, though, and changed the topic to John’s status as a Green Lantern. At the very least, Hal knows that the Guardians hand-picked John to replace him rather than to simply back him up. Back on Earth, Hal and John are going to keep investigating the dead aliens and the shady Macon family in Nebraska. In the teaser, we even see Hal willingly give John the ring for some recon. John is in for an eventful episode, since the trailer also shows brief moments of him hooking up with Zoe, meeting with William Macon, witnessing an explosion outside his motel and getting in a car crash. The Guardians of the Universe are still keeping an eye on everything, too, with Lianna poised to return. There’s also the matter of the 2026 timeline, where Hal is dead and Guy Gardner presumably has the ring. Nathan Fillion is set to appear after debuting in Superman and making a cameo in Peacemaker Season 2, but we haven’t gotten any of the flash forward timeline since the season premiere. Guy probably won’t show up in 2016, where the bulk of the story has been taking place, so his role in the story is still largely unknown. There is no official synopsis for this week’s episode, but there is the preview for Lanterns Episode 4: Lanterns FAQs When does Lanterns come out? Lanterns Episode 4 will premiere at 9 p.m. ET on Sunday, September 6. The next six episodes will drop once a week at the same time. Where can I watch Lanterns Lanterns is available to stream on HBO Max. All other shows and movies in the newly-rebooted DC Universe are also available on the streaming service if you are looking to catch up, from Creature Commandos and Peacemaker Superman Supergirl , meanwhile, is only available for video on-demand and isn’t expected to be on HBO Max until later this month or October. Will there be another season of Lanterns HBO has not publicly renewed Lanterns for a second season. However, according to a report from Jeff Sneider , the network has hired Halt and Catch Fire co-creator Christopher Cantwell to produce and write a potential Season 2. When does the next DC project come out? Following Lanterns ‘ eight-week run on HBO, the next DC film or TV show will be Clayface . The horror-adjacent movie about the titular shape-shifting Batman villain will hit theaters on October 23, 2026. articles.title: Blue Jays Prospect Johnny King Turning Heads in First Double-A Stint
articles.excerpt: Toronto Blue Jays pitching prospect Johnny King has looked impressive so far in his first few starts for the Double-A New Hampshire Fisher Cats.
articles.source_type: Gameweek squads, team news round-ups, deadline reminders
articles.body: Blue Jays Prospect Johnny King Turning Heads in First Double-A Stint Johnny King, a pitcher for the Dunedin Blue Jays, pitched against the Fort Myers Mighty Mussels at Hammond Stadium on Saturday, Aug. 2, 2025. King is a Naples High School alum and two-time baseball player of the year. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect One of the Toronto Blue Jays' top pitching prospects, left-hander Johnny King, just threw arguably his best start yet at Double-A. King, Toronto's No. 3 prospect on MLB Pipeline , tossed five shutout innings for the Double-A New Hampshire Fisher Cats on Wednesday. The 20-year-old gave up no runs on three hits and one walk while striking out eight in New Hampshire's 1-0 loss to the Binghamton Rumble Ponies, the Double-A affiliate of the New York Mets This performance marks King's second consecutive scoreless outing following his recent promotion to Double-A. The eight strikeouts also tie his season high and represent the most punchouts he's had in a start for the Fisher Cats. With New Hampshire's regular season scheduled to wrap up soon, the Blue Jays prospect will undoubtedly look to build on his recent success to end his 2026 campaign. How has Johnny King pitched in 2026? Johnny King, a pitcher for the Dunedin Blue Jays, warms up in the bullpen before a game against the Fort Myers Mighty Mussels at Hammond Stadium on Saturday, Aug. 2, 2025. King is a Naples High School alum and two-time baseball player of the year. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect The Blue Jays selected King with a third-round pick in the 2024 MLB Draft out of high school. And so far, the 20-year-old has quickly climbed through the minors, making his Double-A debut in just his second season in Toronto's farm system. Overall, King has a 2.91 ERA in 25 starts across two minor league levels this year. He's also racked up 134 strikeouts in 102 innings this season. In 2025, the 6-foot-3 lefty posted a 2.48 ERA and 105 strikeouts in 61 2/3 innings. King began 2026 by making his High-A debut. In 21 starts for the Vancouver Canadians, the young southpaw had a 3.21 ERA and 112 strikeouts in 84 innings. That success led to the top prospect's promotion to Double-A in August. And in his first four starts for the New Hampshire Fisher Cats, the left-hander has a 1.50 ERA with 22 punchouts in 18 innings. The Fisher Cats' regular season ends on Sept. 13. Since King pitched on Wednesday, he'll most likely make just one more Double-A start in 2026. Based on his performances so far with New Hampshire, though, the 20-year-old could begin next year at Double-A but quickly be promoted to Triple-A. And if that's the case, a strong first stint at Triple-A could set the top prospect up to join the Blue Jays ' rotation in late 2027. articles.title: Greg McElroy Clears the Air on Kalen DeBoer Ahead of Alabama-East Carolina Game
articles.excerpt: Rumors of the impending demise of Tide coach Kalen DeBoer may be greatly exaggerated per ESPN's Greg McElroy.
articles.source_type: Gameweek squads, team news round-ups, deadline reminders
articles.body: Greg McElroy Clears the Air on Kalen DeBoer Ahead of Alabama-East Carolina Game Despite an offseason of criticism, Alabama coach Kalen DeBoer has his backers, at least according to ESPN personality Greg McElroy (Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images) | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Alabama Crimson Tide begin the 2026 season in an unfamiliar place-- outside the Top 10. And some critics (most notably, ESPN personality Paul Finebaum ) have depicted Tide coach Kalen DeBoer as being on a hot seat. But another SEC personality (and former Alabama stansdout) used a recent appearance on ESPN's Get Up to correct the record. McElroy's Take-- and His Disagreement with Finebaum ESPN analyst Greg McElroy began by noting the source of many of the most prominent rumors of dissatisfaction around the Alabma program. "Don't get me wrong, I love Paul [Finebaum] and Paul is the best at stirring up conversation, there's no denying that," said McElroy. "In an effort to push back on the very Finebaumian response that is Kalen DeBoer in defeat or disappointment is out, let me just correct the record for a second. Kalen DeBoer is in absolutely no jeopardy of losing his job." McElroy did not dispute that DeBoer opens year three of his Alabama tenure under significant pressure to win, but noted that the leverage in the Alabama/DeBoer relationship lies heavily with the coach and not with the school. "Is there pressure to perform?" asked McElroy. "Of course, it's Alabama. Just like there is at Ohio State... or Oklahoma. I think that when you look at Kalen DeBoer, he was offered a blank check by Michigan at the end of last season. He decided to turn that down, therefore, he got a contract extension at Alabama because of leverage he had at that situation..... The group is rallying behind Kalen DeBoer. So anyone who suggests that there's not alignment in Tuscaloosa is just flat-out wrong." Buyout Finances McElroy cited a figure of approximately $67 million to buy out DeBoer's Alabama contract. At the moment, only Jimbo Fisher's massive Texas A&M buyout would cover a larger figure. That said, the Alabama job is at the epicenter of college football and DeBoer's struggles are wearing thin. Alabama's Up-and-Down History Alabama is 20-8 in DeBoer's first two seasons. The eight losses over two seasons are the most the Tide have registered since The end of the disastrous Mike Shula tenure in 2006 and Nick Saban's lean first season in 2007. Between the retirement of Bear Bryant in 1982 and Nick Saban's hiring a quarter-century later, Alabama had more downs than ups. The Tide cycled through Ray Perkins, Bill Curry, Gene Stallings, Mike DuBose, Dennis Franchione, Mike Price (who lost the job before coaching a game), and then Mike Shula. That run included more losing seasons (five) than conference titles (three) or national titles (one). But Saban restored Alabama to glory with six national championships and top ten seasons in every year after his initial 2007 campaign through his 2023 retirement. He has also left a high standard for DeBoer to follow, although obviously, reasonable minds can differ about how exactly how warm DeBoer's seat is. CHARLY TRIBALLEAU / AFP Top seeded Aryna Sabalenka cruised into the third round of the US Open Wednesday, crushing Russian qualifier Polina Iatcenko 6-1, 6-1. Sabalenka slapped winners practically at will past Iatcenko , a 22-year-old qualifier in her first Grand Slam singles main draw. Night atmosphere is always the best atmosphere, " Sabalenka said. Match stats: Sabalenka vs Iatcenko Flashscore A four-time Grand Slam champion who has triumphed in New York the last two years, Sabalenka relishes the hard courts of Flushing Meadow. But she has struggled in recent months, suffering disappointing losses at both the French Open and Wimbledon and turning in middling performances at hard court warmup tournaments ahead of the US Open. But against 160th-ranked Iatcenko she raced to a 5-0 lead before Iatcenko managed to get on the board. Sabalenka dropped just four points on serve in the opening set and was broken just once to give Iatcenko her only game of the second set. Sabalenka responded by winning the next three to secure the win. I'm happy with my level. I've been working really hard, but I feel like I'm moving away from trying to be perfect on court, " she said. I know that you cannot be perfect, and I'm just trying to work with what I have right now, " added Sabalenka, who will play 92nd-ranked Kamilla Rakhhimova of Uzbekistan in the third round. articles.title: Chargers Injury News Creates More Questions for Week 1 and Beyond
articles.excerpt: The Chargers make roster moves to adjust for an injury and it creates some questions.
articles.source_type: Gameweek squads, team news round-ups, deadline reminders
articles.body: Chargers Injury News Creates More Questions for Week 1 and Beyond Jim Harbaugh | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect It was a little easy to miss it in the chaos of final cuts, waiver wire action and practice squad additions, but the Los Angeles Chargers moved a pretty big name to injured reserve this week.Â And with Denzel Perryman going to injured reserve to start the season, the transition to defensive coordinator Chris OâLeary loses a leader and gets just a little bit more complicated for Week 1.Â After all, thereâs no clear-cut starter to take Perrymanâs place on a depth chart that didnât do much to add new faces at what seemed like a pretty straightforward spot in the middle of the defense.Â Thatâs not to say this is an emergency situation like the alarm bells that keep ringing about the offensive line in front of Justin Herbert. But itâs hard to compare to that why didnât they do more? situation, obviously.Â Denzel Perryman injury analysis Denzel Perryman | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Getting up there in age and on one-year contracts or not, Perryman is still an important piece. Over 10 appearances last year, Perryman played about 52 percent of the Chargersâ defensive snaps.Â Perryman will now miss at least four games, though comments from head coach Jim Harbaugh kept the return timeline ideas very open.Â "I know it will be a minimum of four games," Harbaugh said, according to Eric Smith Chargers.com . "I don't know if it will take that long. Close to it, it depends on the rehab and things. I don't think it will be too much longer than that though."Â Harbaugh also has no plans about naming a starter next to Daiyan Henley.Â "Not naming a starter today, but Del'Shawn, Troy, ton of confidence in them and Marlowe and also Junior and Lander," Harbaugh said, per Smith. "We feel like we got a good, deep group there." Clearly, the Chargers have options:Â Troy Dye Del'Shawn Phillips Marlowe Wax The Chargers also have two names on the practice squad they can call up for depth over the first month of the season:Â Junior Colson Lander Barton Troy Dye has filled in admirably in the past when injury hit the linebacker core. Del'Shawn Phillips is such a fantastic presence on special teams that there is always a chance the coaches wonât want to expose him to additional wear and tear on the base defense often.Â Former undrafted standout Marlowe Wax could always use the situation as a sort of audition during the regular season, too. The way he has knocked aside other projects like Junior Colson has made him undeniable and perhaps an actual threat to develop into a starter.Â Regardless, the stability the Chargers wanted when bringing back Perryman for yet another season is now lost for an unknown amount of time and outsiders wonât start to get answers about how the team deals with it until next week. articles.title: US Open LIVE: Sabalanka cruises through as Ostapenko suffers shock exit, Alcaraz to come
articles.source_type: Live scores, results archive, fixtures and match detail
articles.body: US Open LIVE: Alcaraz & Sabalenka out to reach third round | Flashscore.com All Football Transfer News Premier League US Open Features Champions League Darts Snooker Golf Cycling MLB NFL Most read on Flashscore News Transfer News LIVE: Richarlison set for move to Turkey, Ajax sign Adingra Man City confirm joint British record signing of Enzo Fernandez from Chelsea Aguero backs Jesus to shine at Barcelona: 'He can easily score 10 or 15 goals' Antonsen seals comeback-win against rising Chinese star as favorites crash out in Shenzhen US Open LIVE: Alcaraz leads Faria after Sabalenka and Svitolina progress Flashscore Updated Sabalenka is looking to reach the third round REUTERS / Mike Segar / Flashscore The second round gets underway today at the US Open, with defending champions Carlos Alcaraz and Aryna Sabalenka among the headline names in action. Keep track of all the latest results right here! 04:55 CET - The latest players to move on is 22nd seed Valentin Vacherot , who defeated Kamil Majchrzak 6-4, 4-6, 7-6 (3), 6-2, and Tommy Paul, who also needed four sets to get the better of Dino Prizmic 6-2, 6-3, 5-7, 6-4. Match stats: Prizmic vs Paul Flashscore 04:25 CET - A couple more matches have just been completed. On the women's side, number nine seed Elina Svitolina battled her way past Maya Joint 6-2, 6-7 (6), 6-4 in a little over two hours. Despite serving for the match during the second set, the Ukrainian had to show her mettle in the decider to move on. As for Matteo Berrettini, his run at Flushing Meadows comes to a close as he falls 3-6, 6-3, 6-4, 7-6 (4) Mariano Navone . The world number 49 had more than half the unforced errors to his opponent, which played a large part in his ability to find a way through. 03:50 CET - Home favourite Frances Tiafoe gets the job done in straight sets, beating Rei Sakamoto 6-3, 7-6 (3), 7-5 Match stats: Sakamoto vs Tiafoe Flashscore After getting through the first set with little trouble, the American was given a stern test by the Japanese qualifier. The last two sets took over two hours, with Tiafoe finding a way through. 03:10 CET - Alexander Bublik enjoyed a straight set win over Adrian Mannarino , winning 6-3, 6-1, 6-1 . With 16 aces, the Kazakh star cruised through to the third round. Match stats: Bublik vs Mannarino Flashscore It was much more work for Ekaterina Alexandrova , however, as she needed three sets to outlast Kimberly Birrell 6-1, 2-6, 6-3 . The number 18 seed converted four of her nine break point opportunities as part of the win. Elsewhere, Stefanos Tsitsipas got past Lloyd Harris 6-7 (1), 6-3, 7-6 (4), 6-4 , while Jiri Lehecka prevailed 6-4, 6-2, 6-4 over Toby Samuel 02:05 CET - It was a comprehensive performance from Aryna Sabalenka as she breezes past Polina Iatcenko 6-1, 6-1 Match stats: Sabalenka vs Iatcenko Flashscore Having a first serve percentage of 76%, the world number one broke the qualifier on six occaions as she finished her second round match in just 54 minutes. 01:30 CET - Iva Jovic wins a tricky first round match against Magdalena Frech 7-5, 6-3 in a match that lasted two hours and nine minutes. The number 14 seed was broken twice in each set in a hard-faught affair, but her 27 winners to her opponent's 10 paved the way for her to move on. 01:15 CET - After nearly throwing away the third set, Canada's Dennis Shapovalov makes it through after getting the better of Luca van Assche 6-0, 6-4, 7-6 (7) Match stats: Shapovalov vs van Assche Flashscore After losing serve twice while serving for the match, the 27-year-old found his way past the Frenchman in the tiebreak, closing things out on the third match point. He will be up against Ben Shelton in his next match. 00:50 CET - Zizou Bergs moves on at Flushing Meadows after the Belgian beat Carlos Taberner 6-3, 3-6, 6-2, 6-2 Match stats: Bergs vs Taberner Flashscore Bergs, seeded 31st for the tournament, hit 11 aces while winning 82% of his first serve points as he makes it to the second round of the year's final major. Next for him will be Dutchman Jesper de Jong in the second round. 00:25 CET - Number 30 seed Jelena Ostapenko is out of the US Open after suffering a 4-6, 6-1, 6-2 loss to Germany's Tatjana Maria Match stats: Maria vs Ostapenko Flashscore It was an excellent response from the world number 83 after losing the opening set. Breaking Ostapenko six times in the match, Maria won 12 of the last 14 games to triumph. She will face Nikola Bartunkova in the next round. 23:02 CET - Rafael Jodar is out of the US Open! After following up his run to the French Open quarter-finals with some stunning performances in Montreal and Washington, many saw the 19-year-old as a title contender in New York, but he's fallen well short, losing 6-2, 6-1, 6-1 to Lucky Loser Yunchaokete Bu Jodar was a long, long way best, but let's take nothing away from Bu, who had never won a Grand Slam match before this tournament but is now into the third round thanks to an utterly dominant display, in which he dropped just five points on his first serve, forced 16 break points and faced none. As a result, Jodar becomes the highest-seeded player ever (13th) to lose to a Lucky Loser at the US Open. 22:38 CET - One of the USA's biggest hopes is through, with Ben Shelton coming through a real test against former top-10 player Hubert Hurkacz Hurkacz more than held his own, with the final three sets all lasting either just under or just over an hour, and had the Pole converted one of two chances to break and go 5-4 up in the final one, things could have been different. Ultimately though, Shelton marches on, and the 2023 semi-finalist is undoubtedly one of the favourites for the title. Key match stats Flashscore 22:31 CET - Wimbledon runner-up Karolina Muchova has moved through with a superb performance, decimating Katie Boulter 6-1, 6-0 in just 57 minutes. There are few better sights in tennis than Muchova at her best, and she treated us to that today, with some of her 14 winners being absolute stunners. 22:20 CET - Many matches in New York have been suspended due to rain, including a potential upset, with Spanish sensation Rafael Jodar 6-2, 6-1, 4-1 down to Yunchaokete Bu. 21:19 CET - Marta Kostyuk's hopes of reaching a third consecutive Grand Slam semi-final remain very much alive, with the 11th seed beating 2017 US Open champion Sloane Stephens 6-1, 7-5 to advance. After losing the first set badly, Stephens regrouped well and made the match a real contest in the second, but after failing to convert a set point at 5-5, she lost her serve and couldn't recover. Key match stats Flashscore 20:04 CET - We have an upset! Four-time quarter-finalist Andrey Rublev is out, with the 23rd seed losing 6-7, 6-2, 6-4, 6-4 to Daniel Merida Aguilar 19:20 CET - On the men's side of the tournament, former champion Daniil Medvedev looks to be hitting form at the perfect time, with the Russian dispatching Sebastian Gorzny in straight sets, 6-1, 6-3, 7-5 Victory marks back-to-back wins for Medvedev for the first time since Wimbledon, as he prepares to face either Arthur Rinderknech Jaume Munar in the third round. In what's turning out to be a wide-open men's draw, Medvedev could well fancy his chances of a deep run this fortnight... 18:48 CET - Third seed and 2024 runner-up Jessica Pegula has made light work of fellow American Sofia Kenin , with the 32-year-old romping to a 6-3, 6-1 victory in a measly 57 minutes on Arthur Ashe Stadium. Pegula didn't face a single break point in the contest, winning 86% of points behind her first delivery, while hitting 18 winners to only eight unforced errors. She faces former finalist Leylah Fernandez next, who defeated Mananchaya Sawangkaew straight sets Key match stats Flashscore 18:24 CET - Former world number four Jasmine Paolini has sealed her spot in the third round after a convincing 6-4, 6-1 triumph over compatriot Lucrezia Stefanini The popular Italian fired down 20 winners across the two sets, and will face either 16th seed Sorana Cirstea or France's Diane Parry for a place in the last 16. 17:59 CET - Taylor Townsend is the first woman through to the third round in New York, with the American absolutely crushing Australia's Taylah Preston 6-1, 6-1 in just 49 minutes. The 30-year-old, who reached the fourth round at Flushing Meadows last year, won all 23 points behind her first serve in a hugely dominant display against her error-strewn opponent. Key match stats Flashscore 16:48 CET - First up on Arthur Ashe Stadium this afternoon, third seed Jessica Pegula takes on compatriot Sofia Kenin , with Pegula looking to reach the US Open third round for a seventh successive year. Follow point-by-point coverage from 17:30 CET. Win probability Flashscore 14:00 CET - Good afternoon and welcome to our coverage of the US Open, as the second-round action gets underway at Flushing Meadows! We're just a few hours away from play getting started in New York, with women's third seed Jessica Pegula coming up against fellow American and former Australian Open champion Sofia Kenin in a fascinating second-round clash. Also in early action, 2021 champion Daniil Medvedev faces Sebastian Gorzny , while Diana Shnaider and Jasmine Paolini take on Karolina Pliskova and Lucrezia Stefanini , respectively. Later, in the night session on Arthur Ashe Stadium, top seed and defending champion Aryna Sabalenka takes on qualifier Polina Iatcenko , before Carlos Alcaraz continues his comeback from injury against Portugal's Jaime Faria Elsewhere, Ben Shelton Elina Svitolina Alex de Minaur and Karolina Muchova also take to the court on a jam-packed Wednesday. articles.title: Is Jordan Love a fantasy must-add after Josh Jacobs news?
articles.excerpt: Charlie Cummings breaks down the fantasy football fallout from the Josh Jacobs news, analyzing Packers quarterback Jordan Love. The post Is Jordan Love a fantasy must-add after Josh Jacobs news? appeared first on DraftKings Network .
articles.source_type: Captain picks ranked with reasoning, gameweek rankings, DFS targets
articles.body: Is Jordan Love a fantasy must-add after Josh Jacobs news? The news of Josh Jacobs’ suspension sent shockwaves through the NFL. A high-profile player being accused of serious crimes has sparked a lot of reaction across the league, and the NFL is taking it seriously by placing Jacobs on the commissioner’s exempt list. While there are bigger concerns than football here, the Packers are without a running back, and that has significant effects on the fantasy prospects of every player in their lineup. Does this news make Jordan Love a must-add in fantasy formats? Let’s break it down. 2026 Fantasy Outlook: Jordan Love This will be Love’s fourth season as a starting quarterback in the NFL, all under Matt LaFleur in Green Bay. In his three seasons under center, Love has finished fifth, 17th, and 15th in fantasy scoring among quarterbacks. And it’s no coincidence that the dropoff in production stems from Josh Jacobs’ arrival. In the season before Jacobs arrived, Green Bay ranked 22nd in rushing attempts and 15th in pass attempts. LaFleur couldn’t get much production from his Aaron Jones-AJ Dillon running back timeshare, so he was forced to lean on Love in what was essentially his rookie season. That resulted in Love throwing for over 4,000 yards with 32 touchdowns through the air and four on the ground, along with 247 total rushing yards. He was a rock-solid fantasy QB1. During the first year of Jacobs’ tenure with the Packers, Green Bay jumped up to fifth in total rushing attempts, while plummeting to 30th in pass attempts. Now that LaFleur had his bell cow, the Packers could lean on the run, and Love took a backseat. He finished a respectable 17th out of all quarterbacks despite missing two games, largely due to strong passing TD production and overall efficiency. That stayed true in 2025, when Green Bay was seventh in rush attempts and 27th in pass attempts. Once again, Love produced low passing totals, relying on touchdowns and efficiency. RELATED Is Jadarian Price a must-start while Zach Charbonnet is out? Curiously, Jacobs’ arrival seems to take a lot of value away from Love’s rushing. During his first season as a starter, Love scrambled 50 times for 247 yards and four scores, good for 48.7 fantasy points. In the two years since, Love has scrambled 72 times for 282 yards and just one score. That’s a meager 19.1 fantasy points per season as a rusher. While Love’s lack of scrambling over the last two years may be a question of opportunity, there’s no denying the drop in efficiency, and LaFleur may not want his franchise quarterback putting his body on the line unnecessarily. Ultimately, I don’t see Love being any different from a fantasy perspective without Jacobs, largely because of the potentially dire state of the Green Bay backfield. MarShawn Lloyd, who has missed 33 of 34 NFL games and has six carries to his name, leads the depth chart. Chris Brooks is the current backup and has limited experience as a change-of-pace option. And the third stringer is Kaleb Johnson, a Steelers third-round pick in 2025 who didn’t survive his second training camp with Pittsburgh. Perhaps LaFleur and their offensive line can cobble together a good rushing attack. Still, there is a very real possibility that Green Bay wields one of the most toothless rushing attacks in the league as long as Jacobs is sidelined. There is near certainty that Love’s passing attempts will increase, both because of the game plan and the game script. But that will almost certainly come with a drop in efficiency. He has been elite in the touchdown-to-turnover game in the past few seasons, and it will be a hard ratio to maintain if the offense leans on him first and foremost. The week-to-week volatility has certainly increased, but Love’s standing as a low-end QB1 hasn’t changed; he’s still the kind of quarterback you want to pair with another to play the matchups.
