So, we're back with an updated list of Running Back Tiers to guide users in late-summer drafts. Rankings are cool and all, but as any fellow fantasy nerd knows: Tier-based drafting is really where it's at. This is because — get this — sometimes us alleged fantasy experts can be wrong, so it's best to embrace this horrifying reality by grouping similarly ranked players into tiers instead of pretending like we're going to get every single individual ranking correct. Cool? Cool: What follows are my preseason RB tiers along with some quick fun facts as well as one bigger picture question for each individual tier As always: It's a great day to be great. Reminder: You can check out all of Ian's rankings and content with a premium RotoWire subscription Use code "Ian35" for 35% off Check out my updated QB tiers here Tier 1: Your Fantasy Draft's First Two Picks RB1 Jahmyr Gibbs Career average of 5.4 yards per carry ranks fifth … ever … and the explosive 24-year-old is also lethal as a pass-catcher (only Bijan Robinson and Christian McCaffrey have more receptions the last three seasons). RB2 Bijan Robinson Quite possibly planet Earth's RB1 if the aliens invaded the planet and forced us to play a football game to save humanity. Only CMC racked up more PPR points from receiving than Robinson last season, but no RB averaged more yards per route run (1.88). Key question: Who deserves the nod as Mr. 1.01? Here's the four-pronged case for Gibbs: 1. We are potentially looking at the world's best real-life running back . I wouldn't blame anyone for rolling with Bijan or someone like Saquon Barkley Jonathan Taylor ; just realize Gibbs' career average of 5.4 yards per carry ranks fifth … ever … and he's also lethal as a pass-catcher 2. This is one of the league's more fantasy-friendly offensive environments for an RB. Nobody has scored more points than the Lions the last three seasons. Goff's immobility results in a ton of checkdowns (Lions RBs collectively rank seventh in targets since 2023). The scheme and offensive line have provided the third-most rushing yards *before* contact per carry since drafting Gibbs (and they were still 4th in a down 2025). Bringing in offensive coordinator Drew Petzing could even further help matters, considering he managed to produce the league's sixth-most efficient rushing offense in terms of EPA per designed rush while leading the Cardinals 3. A true workhorse role is finally here. This was usually the one concern when debating Gibbs vs. Bijan or CMC in past years: The presence of David Montgomery capped the projectable touch ceiling. Not anymore! RotoWire Projections only have Bijan (375) topping Gibbs (344) when it comes to total touches this season. Gibbs has averaged an absurd 24.4 PPR points per game in 14 career contests with Montgomery playing less than a third of the offense's snaps. 4. Gibbs remains smack dab in the middle of his prime. The 24-year-old talent is directly in the age range that has produced the most elite fantasy seasons at the position. Additionally, availability is the best ability, and Gibbs has played in 49 of a possible 51 regular-season games since entering the league. Yes, Bijan is also an ultra-talented, three-down workhorse in the middle of his best years, but the difference in overall offensive firepower is what has me leaning Gibbs at the top of drafts. Preseason Vegas implied team totals have the Lions sitting pretty as the league's No. 1 ranked scoring offense while the Falcons are … tied for 24th. For up-to-the-minute updates on injuries, news and everything going on around the NFL, head to RotoWire's NFL Fantasy Football News Today or follow @RotoWireNFL on X. Tier 2: The Best RB in Fantasy Football History RB3 Christian McCaffrey CMC is the RB1 in career PPR points per game. He had more PPR points from just receiving (236.4) than Saquon Barkley had overall (232.3) last season! Key question: Should we be concerned about CMC following such a high-volume season? To try to get a better feel for whether RBs do indeed tend to crash out following a high-usage season, I looked at the 30 instances of an RB getting 350-plus touches in a single season from 2015-2024 and what they managed to achieve in their following campaign. The results ( you can see a full chart here Average games played the next season AFTER having 350-plus touches: 13.3. The median was 16 (including playoffs). However, things have been better in recent years, as 12 of the last 13 qualifiers (sorry CMC) played at least 13 games the next season. Average PPR points per game the next season dropped to 16.6 (-3.9). Not ideal, though this still produced pretty solid average (RB14.7) and median (RB12) position ranks. Average yards per carry went from 4.7 to 4.1 (-0.6). Again, not great, but natural regression from a great season is probably more so the culprit as opposed to an arbitrary touch number. Ultimately, I believe big workload numbers to probably be something we should address on a case-by-case basis as opposed to trying to find a definitive rule of thumb. Does David Johnson dislocating his wrist in Week 1, 2017 really mean we shouldn't draft Christian McCaffrey in 2026? It's also worth noting that so much of CMC's dominance comes from his receiving ability. The aforementioned dropoff in yards per carry isn't something to be as worried about when looking at someone who easily led the position in PPR points per game from purely receiving production. You shouldn't need more than one hand to count the number of overall players you're drafting over McCaffrey in 2026. Stay informed with fantasy football news and track usage roles with the NFL depth charts Tier 3: Choose Your Baller RB1 Fighter RB4 Chase Brown The RB11 in PPR points per game the last two seasons should clear 300 touches with good health inside what sure looks like could be one of the league's highest-scoring offenses. RB5 James Cook Yes, his booms have been somewhat reliant on big-play touchdowns inside a high-scoring offense. Also yes, what's the ceiling here if the Bills stay good *and* ask Cook to handle more pass-catching work? RB6 Saquon Barkley One year removed from looking like the best RB alive, Eagles RBs averaged 1.45 (7th) yards *before* contact per carry in 2025 compared to 2.25 (1st) in 2024. RB7 Jonathan Taylor Averaged 27 PPR points per game (RB1) in Weeks 1-10 … and 12.6 (RB23) in Weeks 12-18 once Daniel Jones was injured. RB8 Kenneth Walker Ranks second and 11th in tackles avoided per carry (27%) and explosive rush rate (8.9%) since entering the NFL in 2022. Chiefs RBs during that same timeline rank last in both metrics. RB9 Derrick Henry There have only been four instances of an RB scoring 15-plus PPR points per game in a season the last decade … and two were by King Henry in 2024 and 2025. RB10 Omarion Hampton The expected bell-cow of the potentially high-flying Herbert-McDaniel offense absolutely dominated in Weeks 1-5 compared to after returning from his fractured ankle in terms of yards per carry (4.8 vs. 4.0), yards after contact per carry (3.8 vs. 2.9) and tackles avoided per rush (33.3% vs. 17.2%). RB11 De'Von Achane The all-time RB leader in yards per carry in the Super Bowl era also ranks second in PPR points per game from receiving at the position since 2024. Achane might be at the top of this tier if it wasn't for, you know, him playing in arguably the worst offensive environment in the NFL. Key question: Can running backs in BAD offenses still put up good fantasy numbers? This is important when discerning whether De'Von Achane should be prioritized inside this long tier when the Dolphins (29th in Vegas preseason scoring ranks ) are widely expected to be one of the lower-scoring offenses in the league this season. To get a better idea of this, I looked at the relationship between every position's top-12 performers during the past decade of action *with* their offense's eventual scoring rank. Verdict: It's certainly possible — 14 RBs (11.7%) have posted top-12 fantasy numbers on a per-game basis while operating inside a bottom-10 scoring offense — but not exactly ideal . In fact, only top-performing QBs (+0.43) have a higher r-correlation coefficient than RBs (+0.29) the last decade; top fantasy WRs (+0.11) and TEs (+0.13) have been far less dependent on working in a high-scoring ecosystem. However, a look at the specific running backs who managed to buck this trend reveals a bunch of players who offered a LOT of upside in the pass game. Running backs to post top-12 fantasy numbers in a bottom-10 scoring offense since 2016 pic.twitter.com/FDy7LjRRv5 — Ian Hartitz (@Ihartitz) July 10, 2026 Overall, this group of backs averaged 52 receptions (median 50) during these productive seasons on bad offenses. Derrick Henry is the only qualifier with less than 40 since 2018! This should give at least a little bit of relief to Achane believers, though he does have to grapple with the reality that Malik Willis ranks first in scramble rate (14.5%) the last two seasons. Tua Tagovailoa (2.1%) comes in at 56th among 62 qualified QBs. I've had a hard time taking Achane before the mid-to-back half of Round 2 because of these concerns. Tier 4: Sometimes Boring Vets and banged-up youngsters RB12 Javonte Williams The reigning RB12 in PPR points per game got paid and (again) finds himself as the only show in town as THE running back, y'all, in an offense that could lead the league in scoring and it wouldn't surprise anyone. RB13 Ashton Jeanty RB1 and RB3 in tackles avoided and yards after contact per carry *when* given the benefit of gaining just one yard before contact. What if Klint Kubiak makes that luxury a more consistent reality in 2026? articles.body: Chelsea transfer news: Xabi Alonso attacker 'worried' about role at Stamford Bridge as Premier League minutes dry up - Sports Mole Menu Loading... Chelsea transfer news: Xabi Alonso attacker 'worried' about role at Stamford Bridge as Premier League minutes dry up Lewis Nolan 02 Sep 2026 23:10 Â© Iconsport / Daniel Weir, SPP Sport Press Photo. /Alamy Live News Chelsea winger Estevao is worried about his role under Xabi Alonso at Stamford Bridge this season, the latest report has claimed. The Blues are preparing for their third clash of the Premier League season, with the club set to face Arsenal at the Emirates on Sunday. Alonso will head into the match unable to make changes to his squad following the closure of the transfer window on Tuesday. The Blues failed to sign all of their targets, including Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara , though there is still significant quality throughout the team. Chelsea's forward line is especially strong, but the strength of the club's attack is reportedly worrying winger Estevao, with ESPN Brazil claiming that the 19-year-old believes his opportunities could be limited. © Iconsport / PA Images Estevao transfer news: Could he leave in January window? The report also states that lack of minutes could force Estevao to leave in the January transfer window, and some of his fears are justified. Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers and Joao Pedro have looked like one of the Premier League's most exciting trios so far this season, and they are certain to be seen as starters for a significant portion of the campaign. Chelsea will not be competing in any European competition this term, meaning there is a realistic chance that the club play under 50 games. The lack of matches will limit opportunities for many squad members, and Estevao may find it difficult to force his way into the starting XI. © Iconsport / PA Images What should Chelsea do in the January transfer window? While it may be frustrating for Estevao, Chelsea would do well to remind the youngster that he is just 19, and has plenty of time to break through into Alonso's plans. The Brazilian also suffered a serious hamstring injury in 2025-26, and he must be managed carefully in order to avoid suffering further setbacks. If Estevao agitates for a transfer in January, then the Londoners should consider selling him if his presence becomes detrimental to squad harmony, though the winger is talented enough to play his part in a successful Chelsea side. articles.title: Running Back Dierre Hill Jr. Speaks Candidly on Oregon’s Changing Offensive Line
articles.excerpt: With the Oregon Duck football team's first kick-off of the 2026 season against Boise State right around the corner, running back Dierre Hill Jr. gave insight into how the offensive line rotation under coach A'lique Terry opens up the ground game.
articles.source_type: Gameweek squads, team news round-ups, deadline reminders
articles.body: Running Back Dierre Hill Jr. Speaks Candidly on Oregonâs Changing Offensive Line Nov 18, 2023; Tempe, Arizona, USA; Oregon Ducks offensive lineman Iapani Laloulu (72) against the Arizona State Sun Devils at Mountain America Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-USA TODAY Sports | USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Connect Back at the beginning of August, No. 2 Oregon Ducks football coach Dan Lanning shared that the offensive line would likely take on a rotation style of six to eight athletes. With several un-proven talents that offensive line coach A'lique Terry explained in spring practice needed the 2025 season to continue developing, plus a handful of promising freshmen talent like Immanuel Iheanacho and Tommy Tofi, Oregon's trenches enter 2026 with an aura of mystery outside of senior center Iapani "Poncho" Laloulu. Jan 9, 2026; Atlanta, GA, USA; Oregon Ducks offensive lineman Iapani Laloulu (72) prepares to snap the ball against the Indiana Hoosiers during the third quarter of the 2025 Peach Bowl and semifinal game of the College Football Playoff at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Dierre Hill Jr. Details Offensive Line Impact For sophomore running back Dierre Hill Jr., returning with a mostly-reconstructed offensive line isn't as big a pressure as learning his own role in the Ducks' schemes (harkening to coach Lanning's "do your job" phrase). Hill spoke more about how the rotating line impacts how the ground game moves after a Tuesday media availability. âNah, it's really, see that's the thing about us here. We have great coaches that, obviously, we got a lot of guys moving in and out with the O-line, but coach Terry leads the O-line , the O-line law firm. He leads them very well, and our coach [Ra'Shaad Samples] makes sure we knows our tracks and knows what gap to hit on certain runs," Hill said. âSo that helps us. I mean, it's really not hard because whenever you focus on your preparation and or if you focus on the process, and the results will take care of itself. So just making sure I know my tracks and know where the run's supposed to hit, and if it doesn't, then I know there's something wrong with the O-line," Hill added. Hill emphasized that both Samples and Terry working together at a "high level" is a major aid for himself and his teammates to zero in on perfecting their exact job, relying on their coaches to help it all meld together during game time. Over two fall scrimmages, it appears the coaches are happy about their combinations for front seven. Fighting Ducks quarterback Dylan Raiola, left, hands off the ball to Fighting Ducks running back Dierre Hill Jr. during the Oregon Ducks annual spring game on April 25, 2026 at Autzen Stadium in Eugene, Oregon. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Rotating Against Boise State With such a vast room of trench talent ranging from longtime veteran interior man Dave Iuli, to 2025 relief lineman Fox Crader looking for a bigger role in 2026 , don't be surprised if multiple personell groups hit the field against Boise State. Lanning shared more about the potential of using different faces in the trench during a pregame media availability. âIf you look at every position on our team throughout the years, you've seen changes throughout the season. Do we have some guys we feel comfortable going into the game with? Yes," Lanning said. "Are there still guys playing above the line ball at multiple spots? Yes. So, will you see one group? No. I think you'll probably see some different guys in the lineup throughout, and thatâs because theyâve earned that and theyâve worked through that." Oregon football coach Dan Lanning speaks during a press availability on Aug. 26, 2026, at the Hatfield-Dowlin Complex in Eugene. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Against Boise State Though Oregon's opening game against Boise State is meant to be mostly a roster evaluation for one of the top rated teams in the nation, the Broncos still bring veteran edge rushers to challenge the Ducks' trenches. Lanning himself admitted that in previous years, practicing with one or two rotations in fall camp didn't immediately result to success through in-game action. Starting with Boise State, Lanning and Terry will continue to evaluate which line rotation rises to the top. "Thatâll be the same with every position on our team. We have some guys who are prepped and ready, and we feel like weâre going to put them in the best position to be successful," Lanning said. Facebook and Instagram for the latest news. articles.title: Georgia Tech Coach Brent Key Gets Candid on Deion Sanders' Return to Atlanta
articles.excerpt: Colorado Buffaloes coach Deion Sanders earned high praise from Georgia Tech coach Brent Key ahead of their season-opening rematch in Atlanta, where Key believes Coach Prime's presence could add another layer to an already highly anticipated matchup.
articles.source_type: Gameweek squads, team news round-ups, deadline reminders
articles.body: Georgia Tech Coach Brent Key Gets Candid on Deion Sanders' Return to Atlanta Aug 24, 2024; Dublin, IRL; Georgia Tech head coach Brent Key before the game against Florida State at Aviva Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Tom Maher/INPHO via USA TODAY Sports | USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Connect The Colorado Buffaloes are in Atlanta, preparing to take on Georgia Tech in a season-opening rematch of last year's thriller at Folsom Field. And this year's matchup is shaping up to be just as exciting. Part of what makes the matchup so intriguing is that Colorado coach Deion Sanders was once a star for the Atlanta Falcons, eventually becoming an NFL icon and two-sport star in the city after signing with the Atlanta Braves. Mar 1992; West Pam Beach, FL, USA; FILE PHOTO; Atlanta Braves outfielder DEION SANDERS in a spring training portrait at West Palm Beach Municipal Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Photo By USA TODAY Sports (c) Copyright USA TODAY Sports | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect All of that wasn't lost on Georgia Tech coach Brent Key, who discussed the upcoming matchup on Tuesday and what Coach Prime's return to Atlanta could mean for Thursday night's game. Ties to the "A" Oct 21, 1990; Anaheim, CA, USA; FILE PHOTO; Atlanta Falcons defensive back Deion Sanders (21) walks onto the field prior to a game against the Los Angeles Rams at Anaheim Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Peter Brouillet-USA TODAY NETWORK | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect While Georgia Tech will have the benefit of playing at home, Coach Key knows the Yellow Jackets won't be the only team with plenty of local support inside Bobby Dodd Stadium. "They've got some guys from Georgia," Key said during his Tuesday press conference in Atlanta. "They're going to have a ton of people here to watch them. I'm sure they've played against a lot of the guys that are on our team." Colorado's roster boasts 17 listed players from the state of Georgia, including former five-star quarterback Julian "JuJu" Lewis , who will play a major role in the Buffs' ability to find success against the Yellow Jackets. Apr 11, 2026; Boulder, CO, USA; Colorado Buffaloes quarterback Julian Lewis (10) prepares to pass the ball during the spring game at Folsom Field. Mandatory Credit: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect However, the one person on Colorado's sideline who Key believes could attract the most fanfare is Coach Prime himself. On Tuesday, Key didn't hesitate to comment on the significance of Sanders' return to Atlanta, making it clear that his presence could carry as much weight as any player on the field. "It's not far-fetched; it's the truth," Key said. "Deion is probably the biggest sports celebrity to ever play in the city of Atlanta, and he's coming back home." Coach Prime returns to Atlanta ð pic.twitter.com/B2snlBkW1a â Colorado Buffaloes Football (@CUBuffsFootball) September 2, 2026 However, this isn't the first time Sanders has returned to Atlanta as a head coach. In 2022, Coach Prime led Jackson State to the Cricket Celebration Bowl at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. Although the Tigers lost in heartbreaking fashion, Sanders' return to Atlanta as Colorado's coach gives him another opportunity to make his presence felt in the city that helped make him a star. The Deion Sanders Effect Unknown date; Atlanta, GA, USA; FILE PHOTO; Atlanta Falcons defensive backs Tim McKyer (22) and Deion Sanders (21) in the endzone at Fulton County Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Photo By Manny Rubio-USA TODAY Sports | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect For Key, Sanders' impact in Atlanta goes far beyond what he accomplished during his playing days. Key compared Sanders' return to Atlanta to Tom Brady coaching at North Carolina and returning to face Boston College, highlighting how much he believes Sanders meant to an entire generation of sports fans in Atlanta. "I equate it kind of like, say, Tom Brady's coaching North Carolina and they go play BC," Key said. "I mean, it's a big deal, especially for somebody that grew up in the 80s. I mean, golly, he was the top of the top, the premier guy that everybody wanted to be when they were growing up." Sep 1989; Atlanta, GA, USA; FILE PHOTO; Atlanta Falcons cornerback Deion Sanders in action during the 1989 season at Fulton County Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Photo By Manny Rubio-USA TODAY Sports | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Sanders was selected No. 5 overall by the Atlanta Falcons in the 1989 NFL Draft and quickly became one of the city's biggest sports stars thanks in part to his larger-than-life persona. In Atlanta, Sanders became "Prime Time," transforming himself from another player on the field into a cultural icon. His personality, athleticism, and ability to excel in both football and baseball made him one of the most recognizable athletes in the world. Now, more than three decades after Sanders first arrived in Atlanta, his return could add to an already electric atmosphere inside Bobby Dodd Stadium, where Colorado will be looking to spoil the Yellow Jackets' home opener. Big-Game Atmosphere Nov 22, 2025; Atlanta, Georgia, USA; Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets cheerleaders ride the Ramblin' Wreck car on the field before a game against the Pittsburgh Panthers at Bobby Dodd Stadium at Hyundai Field. Mandatory Credit: Brett Davis-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect While Sanders' Atlanta ties add another interesting layer to an already exciting season-opening matchup, Key believes the game itself has all the ingredients to create the type of environment college football fans have been craving all offseason. "Two new coordinators that have had success against us," Key said. "The defensive coordinator has had success against us. They've got good players. We've both been head coaches the same amount of time at our respective schools." Key believes those factors have only added to the intrigue surrounding Thursday night's matchup. "So you put all of those things together, and you create an environment for a really big college football game that recruits want to come to," Key said. "And that's what we want every game here at Bobby Dodd to be." Now, the wait is finally almost over for Colorado and college football fans alike. Colorado and Georgia Tech will take the field Thursday at 6 p.m. on ESPN , where the Buffs will look to turn Sanders' homecoming into the first road win of the season and avenge last season's 27-20 loss in Boulder. articles.body: OKC Thunder Looking To Get Back On Right Side Of One Of NBA's Best Rivalries May 30, 2026; Oklahoma City, Oklahoma, USA; Oklahoma City Thunder center Chet Holmgren (7) drives against San Antonio Spurs forward Victor Wembanyama (1) in the fourth quarter during game seven of the western conference finals for the 2026 NBA playoffs at Paycom Center. Mandatory Credit: Alonzo Adams-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect One of the best clashes of next season will feature the Thunder.Â Basketball is best when some of the best teams are playing, and luckily for OKC fans, the Thunder make up half of the formula. Having won a championship so recently, it seems like every opponent gives OKC its all. This has made for some great games and tests for Oklahoma City, and recently has brought one of the biggest rivalries in the entire league.Â The San Antonio Spurs emerged as one of the brightest teams in the league last year, and challenged the Thunder for the Western Conference throne. San Antonio would eventually get the better of them in a Western Conference Finals Series, that was some of the best basketball seen all year. Now, with the two teams expected to open up the entire season on opening night, the rivalry is crowned as one of the best in the league.Â ESPN recently released an article on the 10 best rivalries to watch this upcoming season, and to no surprise, the Thunder and Spurs were high on the list, sitting at No. 2. Cameras captured an aggressive block by Judkins on a stumbling Hall. articles.title: Reiss Nelson finds new home days after Arsenal exit, returns to Feyenoord
articles.source_type: Line-ups, goal scorers, cards, substitutions, possession and xG per match
articles.body: Soccerway All Transfer News Premier League LaLiga Ligue 1 Serie A Bundesliga Champions League Europa League Conference League World Cup Reiss Nelson finds new home days after Arsenal exit, returns to Feyenoord Paul Winters Updated Reiss Nelson during Arsenal's preseason friendly against Girona Photo by ALEX CAPARROS / GETTY IMAGES EUROPE / GETTY IMAGES VIA AFP Reiss Nelson has shockingly returned to Feyenoord just days after his Arsenal contract was terminated. The 26-year-old Reiss Nelson left Arsenal after 18 years at the club, as the parties agreed to terminate the Londoner's contract. Outside of loan spells at Hoffenheim Feyenoord Fulham , and Brentford , Nelson played 90 games across all competitions for Arsenal, for whom he made his senior debut in 2018. Feyenoord confirmed the signing of Nelson on Wednesday afternoon, with the Englishman having penned a one-year contract in Rotterdam. "It’s absolutely great to be back here," Nelson said on the club website . "I had a wonderful year at Feyenoord and always felt at home there. That’s why it feels good to be back at (training complex) 1908." Nelson spent the 2021-22 season with Feyenoord, during which they reached the UEFA Conference League final. Nelson scored 4 goals and provided 7 assists in 32 games for the Rotterdam club. "I’ve always kept up with Feyenoord, and it’s been great to see the progress the club has made. The fact that we’re kicking off a new Champions League season next week is a fine example of that. I’m going to do everything I can to make a contribution to the team as soon as possible and can’t wait to pull on this shirt again." Feyenoord entered the final day of the summer transfer window looking for a left winger and a striker after the departures of Leo Sauer and top scorer Ayase Ueda. After Nelson's transfer, it's unlikely that the club will find a new striker. As the summer transfer window ramps up, Flashscore has everything you need to keep up with breaking news, rumours and analysis. articles.title: Chelsea likely to resist free-agent move despite Wijnaldum link, sources tell Flashscore
articles.source_type: Line-ups, goal scorers, cards, substitutions, possession and xG per match
articles.body: Soccerway All Transfer News Premier League LaLiga Ligue 1 Serie A Bundesliga Champions League Europa League Conference League World Cup Chelsea likely to resist free-agent move despite Wijnaldum link, sources tell Flashscore Dean Jones Chelsea have a midfield dilemma REUTERS / David Klein Chelsea have looked at the free agent market but are expected to wait until the January transfer window as they consider their midfield options in the wake of a chaotic deadline day. The Blues have become aware of an opportunity to sign former Liverpool midfielder Georginio Wijnaldum after their plans for deadline day ended in disappointment. Chelsea had been closing in on a deal for Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara , only for the Ligue 1 club to pull out of the agreement at the last minute. With Enzo Fernandez ’s £125million move to Manchester City allowed to go through, Chelsea are now a player short in midfield and must decide whether to address the problem immediately or wait until January. The club can still sign free agents outside the transfer window, but sources indicate the expectation had been that Chelsea would make do with the squad they have following the collapse of the Camara deal. Reports linking Wijnaldum with a move to Stamford Bridge were played down by Chelsea officials on Wednesday. However, there is an understanding that the 35-year-old’s quality and experience may be of interest to Xabi Alonso, particularly after the Chelsea head coach also brought in Jordan Henderson during the summer. Chelsea do have a number of options in central midfield. Moises Caicedo Romeo Lavia Valentin Barco and Henderson are the natural choices, but the club have used Reece James and Malo Gusto in midfield, too. There is also a possibility of Chelsea experimenting further with their existing squad, with sources indicating that Jarrel Hato could be tried in midfield while teenager Reggie Watson may even get an opportunity. That would allow Chelsea to wait until January before making significant investment in the position. Wijnaldum most recently played for Al Ettifaq in Saudi Arabia, having previously represented Paris Saint-Germain , Liverpool, Newcastle United PSV and Feyenoord . He also won 90 caps for the Netherlands before retiring from international football. For now, though, Chelsea appear set to show patience and trust their existing options after being left frustrated by Monaco’s late decision to withdraw from the Camara deal. articles.title: Is Tyler Shough the best deep quarterback sleeper in 2026 fantasy football?
articles.excerpt: Tyler Shough showed flashes of an excellent quarterback as a rookie last year. Is he the best deep sleeper at quarterback in fantasy football this season? The post Is Tyler Shough the best deep quarterback sleeper in 2026 fantasy football? appeared first on DraftKings Network .
articles.source_type: Captain picks ranked with reasoning, gameweek rankings, DFS targets
articles.body: Is Tyler Shough the best deep quarterback sleeper in 2026 fantasy football? We’re firmly into fantasy football draft season, meaning now is the time to get an edge on your leaguemates and dive into analysis. Sleepers can be the difference between making the playoffs and missing them entirely, but who are the names to watch for moving forward? The quarterback position has been devalued in recent years, meaning fantasy managers can wait later than ever to select a field general. Whether you’re punting it outright or just taking a backup with a little bit of upside, Tyler Shough is undoubtedly a top name to target. Here’s why. Is Tyler Shough a top fantasy quarterback sleeper? There were plenty of takes when the Saints selected Tyler Shough in the second round of last year’s NFL Draft, and most of them weren’t very positive. The Louisville product spent seven seasons in the NCAA and dealt with various injuries before finally breaking out in his final collegiate campaign. He finished that year with a 62.7% completion rate, 3,195 passing yards, 23 passing touchdowns and six interceptions. He didn’t contribute much with his legs and was far older than most prospects at age 26 entering his first professional campaign, so critiques of his upside didn’t appear invalid. It took some time for Shough to finally get on the field, losing the quarterback competition to Spencer Rattler and having to wait until Week 9 before finally taking over the starting job. He wasn’t exactly dominant from the jump, but the then-rookie soon showed signs of promise. In his nine games as a starter, Shough completed 69.2% of his 295 passes for 2,265 yards, 10 touchdowns and five interceptions. He also rushed 42 times for 174 yards and an additional three scores. It’s not flashy production in terms of raw counting stats, but contextually, there are a lot of positives to glean. The Saints simply weren’t a great team last year. They won just six games, but then again, five of those came with Shough under center and four of the victories came in the last five weeks. The quarterback also didn’t have much surrounding talent to work with. Yes, Chris Olave put forth a breakout campaign and formed clear chemistry with the rookie gunslinger, and Juwan Johnson also emerged as a legitimate weapon at tight end. There was virtually no run game, though, as an aging Alvin Kamara regressed and dealt with injuries. To top it all off, 2025-26 was the first season of Kellen Moore’s tenure as a head coach. Looking a little bit further into the production, it’s clear that Shough actually played quite well as a starter. The completion rate obviously jumps out, and he threw at least one touchdown in seven of his nine starts while eclipsing 250 passing yards five times. Down the stretch he really turned it up with 272, 308, 333 and 259 yards over his final four outings, three of which New Orleans won. He was efficient and made the right play when it mattered. RELATED Is Tucker Kraft the best middle-round tight end target in 2026 fantasy football? For fantasy purposes, Shough finished as the overall and per-game QB26, but bear in mind he didn’t play half the season and did see snaps in multiple games with just a handful of passes in relief. As a starter only, he averaged 18.73 FPPG, which would’ve made him the QB10 in per-game production if extrapolated to the full campaign. The names he’d have finished between? Dak Prescott and Justin Herbert. That’s very impressive given that Shough wasn’t throwing for massive yardage totals on a weekly basis, nor did he have a single game with three passing touchdowns. That does mean his ceiling was capped, as he didn’t score more than 23 fantasy points in any game; yet, the floor was steady with at least 17 points in seven of his nine starts. Once again, consider the context of the weapons he had, too. Heading into 2026, Shough is a major candidate to outperform his late-round ADP in fantasy and improve on his game in the real NFL. He’s entering his second pro season and is firmly entrenched as the starter, so there’s added stability now that he isn’t in a position battle coming into the year. Moreover, continuity of coaching means plenty as Moore also heads into year two at the helm of this New Orleans franchise. If that’s not enough, look at the new talent the organization added this offseason. The Saints should have a much-improved run game after signing halfback Travis Etienne, while first-round pick Jordyn Tyson provides a high-upside WR2 to work alongside Olave – assuming Tyson can stay healthy). Those factors should have fantasy managers feeling bullish on Shough’s outlook. We’ve seen the floor for the second-year starter already since he made the most of the surrounding environment last year. It also helps that he can create points with his rushing ability, tallying 22+ yards on the ground in four of his nine starts. With better weapons to work with moving forward and a full offseason in this system for both he and his offensive-minded coach, there are few better values than Shough at the quarterback position in drafts. articles.title: Bailey departs for Olympiacos
articles.excerpt: Aston Villa can confirm that Leon Bailey has completed a permanent transfer to Olympiacos. Since joining the club in 2021, Leon has been a key part of our recent journey and he leaves the club having played his part in Villa winning the UEFA Europa League last term. He joined from Bayer Leverkusen and went on to make 163 appearances in claret and blue, scoring 23 goals and registering 25 assists. His sparkling 2023/24 campaign, in which he netted 14 times, helped the club qualify for the UEFA Champions League for the first time. An exciting winger, capable of both scoring and assisting, Leon was a popular figure among his teammates and around the training ground with his exuberant personality, and he leaves Aston Villa with the very best wishes of everyone at the football club.

The situation has stirred very strong feelings. Via Amanda Christovich of Front Office Sports , Georgia Attorney General Chris Carr has urged the SEC to react harshly, if LSU follows through on its plan to play players who hope to return to college after offseason and preseason stints in pro football. “If LSU does in fact roster one or more pro athletes or demonstrates concrete plans to do so, we would strongly encourage the SEC to take all measures available to address this conduct, up to and including suspending and/or removing LSU from the Conference,” Carr wrote in a Wednesday letter to the SEC. “College sports are for college athletes only, and we are grateful that the SEC has taken swift action to maintain that standard,” Carr added. “However, rules cannot be ignored or twisted to benefit one coach, one institution, or one program, and we refuse to stand by while that happens.” Carr’s message comes amid reports of internal chatter regarding the potential taking of “extreme measures” against LSU, up to and including expulsion. The issue ultimately will be decided by the courts. For players who are seeking retroactive application of the NCAA’s new five-year rule, none of this is their fault. Regardless, the stakes are potentially high. articles.body: U21s Report & Highlights: Palace secure statement win over PSG Skip navigation U21s Report & Highlights: Palace secure statement win over PSG Match reports 1 day ago Williams 62' Adler Nascimento 6' Bezeme 74' Crystal Palace Under-21s made it three games unbeaten with a 2-1 victory over Paris Saint-Germain in their Premier League International Cup opener at Sutton United’s Borough Sports Ground on Wednesday night. Adler Nascimento opened the scoring in stunning fashion, bending a sublime free-kick over the wall and into the top corner, before Harry Lee produced a superb penalty save on the stroke of half-time to preserve the lead. Seb Williams doubled the advantage early in the second half in trademark fashion, striking a crisp half-volley into the back of the net, and although Noa Bezeme pulled one back for PSG, Darren Powell’s side held firm to secure an impressive opening victory in the competition. Summary: Powell makes three changes from the Villa win, bringing Judd, Danaher and Casey into the XI. 1: Walker-Smith’s looping header is denied by a fine diving save. 5 – GOAL: Nascimento gives us the lead with a stunning free-kick. 12: The PSG forward strikes over the bar. 15: Lee makes a strong save with his legs. 20: Walker-Smith pokes wide of the post. 23: Casey can’t beat the ‘keeper one-on-one. 32: PSG striker fires high over the bar. Two minutes are added on… 45 (+1): Lee makes a brilliant penalty save to preserve Palace's lead. 45 (+2): PSG hit the underside of the bar. HT: Palace U21s 1-0 PSG U21s 48: Judd produces a crucial block inside the area. 51: Whyte’s miscued effort is gathered comfortably. 57: Lee tips behind a powerful strike from the left-channel. 59: Boly lashes well wide of the post from range. 61: Sealey is on for his competitive debut 62 – GOAL: Williams crisp half-volley doubles our lead. 74 – Goal: Bezeme halves the deficit for PSG. 80: Williams’ half-volley is gathered. 87: Sealey pulls it back to Casey’s, but his low strike is blocked on the line Four minutes are added on… FT: Palace U21s 2-1 PSG U21s After opening their Premier League 2 campaign with a 1-1 draw at Arsenal, Darren Powell’s side claimed their first three points with a 2-0 smash-and-grab victory over Aston Villa on Friday. Buoyed by that unbeaten start, the Young Eagles turned their attention to the International Cup, with Powell making three changes as Jasper Judd, Euan Danaher and Benji Casey came into the XI. Casey was rewarded with a start after opening the scoring against Villa. There was plenty of excitement on the bench, too, with first-year U21 Khyan Frazer-Williams, summer signing Amaari Sealey, and U18s Ajean-Ray Greaves and Raihaan Anderson all in line to make their competitive debuts. Palace came agonisingly close to an opener inside the first minute. Seb Williams floated a free-kick into the penalty area, where Charlie Walker-Smith’s looping header forced Alessandro Longoni into a fine diving save before the danger was eventually scrambled clear. A few minutes later, Palace had their opener – and what an opener it was. Dragged down on the edge of the area, Nascimento dusted himself off to take the resulting free-kick and produced a moment of magic, whipping it over the wall and into the top corner. The ‘keeper could only stand and watch as it nestled beyond his reach. Wow. Just wow. The Young Eagles pushed hard to capitalise on their momentum and double their advantage, but PSG weathered the early storm. The pendulum soon swung the other way, with the visitors offering a few warning signs of their own. A pull-back found an onrushing forward, who fired over the bar first time, before Lee produced a strong save with his legs to keep out a low-driven effort from close range. On 20 minutes, Palace were firmly in the ascendancy. Makai Bernard-Ferguson sent a dangerous delivery flashing across the face of goal, before Walker-Smith poked an effort wide. The defender then lofted a clever ball in behind to release Casey, who raced through one-on-one, only to be denied by Longoni. Palace continued to move the ball well, but their rhythm was repeatedly disrupted by a series of cynical PSG challenges, much to the growing frustration of the crowd. As the half entered its final third, the Parisians began to enjoy more possession and probe the Palace backline, but they were struggling to seriously test Lee. Powell’s side were pinned deep inside their own half and finding it difficult to escape, but the Young Eagles stood firm. PSG were unable to penetrate the Palace defence, with their pressure producing little of note. The board went up to indicate two minutes of added time, and suddenly the game burst into life. A rush of blood from Casey, desperate to make amends after losing possession in a dangerous position, saw him concede a penalty with a clumsy sliding challenge. But Lee carried his inspired form from Friday’s win over Aston Villa into this contest, producing an outstanding diving save to push away Quentin Ndjantou’s spot-kick. From the resulting corner, PSG struck the underside of the bar as Palace survived another scare. Fortunately, the Young Eagles went into the break ahead, with Nascimento’s stunning free-kick and Lee’s heroics from the penalty spot the difference. Palace made a bright start to the second half, with Casey threatening in behind before being penalised for a foul as he challenged for the ball. PSG threatened at the other end, but Jasper Judd made a crucial block to deny Idder inside the area. The Young Eagles continued to press for a second, forcing turnovers in dangerous areas, but the ball would not fall kindly for them, with Tyler Whyte’s miscued effort comfortably gathered by Longoni. Approaching the hour mark, Lee tipped a powerful strike from the left channel behind, before David Boly lashed an effort well wide of the post. Powell introduced attacking midfielder Sealey shortly afterwards, handing the summer signing his competitive U21 debut. Palace then doubled their advantage in style. Danaher found Gibbard down the left, who curled a ball into Casey on the right side of the area. He cleverly side-footed it into the path of the onrushing Seb Williams, who unleashed a crisp half-volley into the back of the net. The visitors continued to withstand a succession of Palace shots and crosses, but they were eventually rewarded for their persistence. On 74 minutes, Bezeme got in behind and halved the deficit, punishing the Young Eagles for failing to make the most of their earlier chances. Powell responded with a double change to inject fresh legs, including in-form U18s captain AJ Greaves, who was handed his competitive U21s debut. Palace continued to pile on the pressure, with a series of pinball-like scrambles inside the PSG box seeing shots repeatedly blocked. Williams then went close again, his half-volley well saved as the game entered its final 10 minutes. In the dying embers, Casey had a golden opportunity to put the game beyond doubt. Having weathered another PSG storm, Palace broke at pace, with Sealey released down the left. He squared for Casey in acres of space, but after a slick exchange between the pair, the forward’s effort was blocked on the line amid a sea of PSG bodies. Four minutes of added time were signalled, and the visitors continued to pile on the pressure. But Palace remained resolute, with an audacious effort from Sealey, straight at the ‘keeper, proving the final action of the contest. The result extends Powell’s side’s unbeaten start to three games and, more importantly, secures an opening victory in Group D of the International Cup. The Young Eagles sit top of the group on three points, with Jong PSV and Sunderland both on one point and PSG on zero, with all four sides having played once. The Young Eagles now face a lengthy break before returning to action against Swindon Town in the EFL Trophy (Tuesday, 15th September, 19:00 BST), with hopes high that they can carry this momentum into their next challenge. Palace XI: Lee (GK); Judd (Adams-Collman, 77), Okoli, Walker-Smith; Whyte, Williams (Anderson, 84’), Danaher, Gibbard; Casey, Nascimento (Greaves, 77’), Bernard-Ferguson (Sealey, 62). Subs not used: Fasida, Hill, Frazer-Williams. articles.body: College Football Week 1 Start/Sit Picks for Fantasy Lineups | RotoWire College Fantasy Football Week 1 Start/Sit Picks College football Week 1 fantasy start/sit picks by conference, with sleepers, busts and matchup-based advice to set your lineup. September 2, 2026 Share By: Chris Morgan @ChrisXMorgan September 2, 2026 Start vs. Sit Mock Draft Simulator Prep for your 2026 Fantasy Football draft with free, unlimited drafts, and real-time grades. Welcome back. After a bit of an appetizer in terms of Week 0, largely eschewed for fantasy-related matters when it comes to college football, we have arrived at Week 1. That means I have returned for another season of Start vs. Sit. Things have changed, as they always do in college football. I will have a section for the Pac-12 again after a couple of years without that conference in play. A couple more FCS teams have become FBS teams, and every team is playing in a conference that totally makes sense geographically speaking. Here are my players to start and players to bench for Week 1. Obviously, a lot of FBS teams have FCS opponents this week. I generally try to avoid those early in the year when they are to be expected. You don't need me to tell you that the Georgia Bulldogs are good plays against the Tennessee State Tigers, you know? AAC Starts and Sits START Michael Van Buren , QB, South Florida vs. Florida International I immediately backed myself into the corner with the whole FCS opponent thing, because in Week 1 the AAC is mostly a mix of teams playing FCS schools or teams on the road serving as resume-boosting opponents that aren't too challenging to teams like Florida or Duke. South Florida, though, is hosting another school from the Sunshine State, Conference USA's Florida International. The Panthers allowed 249.9 passing yards and 30.0 points per game in 2025. That means I have returned for another season of Start vs. Sit. Things have changed, as they always do in college football. AAC Starts and Sits START Michael Van Buren , QB, South Florida vs. Florida International I immediately backed myself into the corner with the whole FCS opponent thing, because in Week 1 the AAC is mostly a mix of teams playing FCS schools or teams on the road serving as resume-boosting opponents that aren't too challenging to teams like Florida or Duke. South Florida, though, is hosting another school from the Sunshine State, Conference USA's Florida International. The Panthers allowed 249.9 passing yards and 30.0 points per game in 2025. Van Buren took over as LSU's quarterback down the stretch last season, including throwing for 267 yards and three touchdowns in the bowl game against Houston, which may have secured him the South Florida job. SIT Jahiem White , RB, North Texas at Indiana White was a good back for West Virginia for a few years, until a knee injury cut his 2025 season off early. The North Texas exodus left an opportunity for a Big 12 back to drop down a bit in terms of level of competition, but there are questions about White's health, and also why he is now playing for an AAC school undergoing massive turnover. Plus, while the defense isn't exactly the same of course, Indiana only allowed 77.2 rushing yards per game last year, so it would have to get a lot worse before this would be a matchup not to avoid. ACC Starts and Sits START Adam Mohammed , RB, California vs. UCLA A classic ACC vs. Big Ten matchup for you here in Week 1. Mohammed's role with Washington last season was erratic, but in the last four games of the season he had one with three touchdowns and two others with over 100 yards. One of those games with over 100 yards? It came against the Bruins, who allowed 190.4 rushing yards per contest in 2025. SIT Bryant Wesco , WR, Clemson at LSU It's pretty clear that the toughest situation for any ACC offense in Week 1 is Clemson having to travel to Baton Rouge for a battle of Tigers. LSU's defense was good last year, and if you are a believer in the assessing power of SP+ (which I, by and large, am), LSU was third in defensive SP+ in the last preseason ranking. Wesco was playing some excellent football before a concerning neck injury last season, and he may get back to that point, but he's also playing in his first real game since suffering a concerning neck injury last October. Big Ten Starts and Sits START Turbo Richard , RB, Indiana vs. North Texas Richard ran for over 100 yards with two touchdowns in each of his last two games with Boston College. This may have paved the way for his move to the defending champs, and while he is not guaranteed to be the lead back, he's in the mix, and this matchup is enticing. Generally speaking, people agree North Texas will be worse this year. Neal Brown is a good coach, but he's offensively inclined, and North Texas allowed 215.7 rushing yards per game last season. SIT Abu Sama , RB, Wisconsin at Notre Dame It's probably telling that Sama's two best games in 2025 came against Colorado and Oklahoma State, two lousy defenses. Luke Fickell used the money boosters promised him to bring Sama over from Iowa State, but Wisconsin starts the season with a brutal Sunday matchup. A lot of people are picking Notre Dame to win the title, and while that is some wisdom-of-the-crowds stuff, Notre Dame finished in the top 12 in rushing yards and points allowed per game last year. Big 12 Starts and Sits START Isaiah Marshall , QB, Kansas vs. Long Island University I couldn't really avoid FCS opponents with the Big 12, so I figured I'd use this as a chance to make a note of Kansas' new quarterback. He was a backup last year and didn't really play, but now the job is his. Long Island University is your favorite cupcake's favorite cupcake, so this is a great chance for Marshall to ease into being a college starter. SIT DJ Lagway , QB, Baylor vs. Auburn The flipside of a bunch of matchups with FCS teams is there aren't many offenses to avoid come Week 1 in the Big 12. Given that, Baylor facing Auburn, even at a neutral size, stands out. Lagway got two seasons at Florida and, frankly, showed he can't really hack it as a high-level college quarterback. If you remove games against FCS opponents, Lagway threw more interceptions than touchdowns with the Gators. Conference USA Starts and Sits START Roman Gagliano , QB, Middle Tennessee State vs. Murray State It is my contention that Gagliano saved Derek Mason's job last year. As a redshirt freshman, he started the last three games of the season, totaled eight touchdowns against zero turnovers, and led the team to two of its three wins. Now, it's Gagliano's job from the get-go, and he starts the season against an FCS school in Murray State. SIT Jmariyae Robinson , WR, Missouri State at Texas A&M Generally speaking, the Conference USA teams that didn't schedule an easy opponent are the easy opponent. Robinson impressed in his first FBS season, picking up 44 catches for 632 yards and seven touchdowns. All in all, he may be fine, but this is a trip to Texas A&M. It's not likely to go well. MAC Starts and Sits START Nick Devereaux , WR, Eastern Michigan vs. San Jose State Here's an interesting matchup as both of these teams played in Week 0. San Jose State's defense was torn up by USC's offense. I grant you Eastern Michigan is not as good as USC, but there is an opportunity here at home against SJSU. In EMU's opener, Devereaux had six catches for 71 yards and a score, and that comes after he finished last season with 34 catches for 510 yards and seven scores. SIT Jalen Buckley , RB, Western Michigan at Michigan Buckley has been a star for Western Michigan. In two of the last three seasons he's finished with over 1,000 yards, and he's had at least nine rushing touchdowns in all three campaigns. Of course, being a MAC team often means tough road games early, and being a Directional Michigan team often means having to visit a Big Ten team looking to score an easy win. Buckley will probably be fine, but Week 1 is likely to be brutal. Mountain West Starts and Sits START Tama Uiliata , WR, Hawaii vs. UNLV Hawaii lost to Stanford in Week 0, but led in the fourth quarterback, and this isn't about winning or losing anyway. The Rainbow Warriors threw the ball 52 times, and Uilata had eight catches for 62 yards and a touchdown. That was on the mainland, and playing in the islands tends to offer a real home-field advantage to Hawaii. UNLV had a below-average defense last season, and in its home opener in Week 0 allowed 418 total yards and 27 points to Memphis. SIT Taron Dickens , QB, Northern Illinois at Iowa Here's a nice reminder that Northern Illinois is now a Mountain West team. Dickens put up video-game numbers last season…at West Carolina. Not only is he moving up to the FBS level, his first start will be on the road against Iowa. The Hawkeyes only allowed 172.7 passing yards and 16.1 points per game last season, and this defense is likely to be reliable until Kirk Ferentz retires. Pac-12 Starts and Sits START Javen Jacobs , RB, Utah State vs. Idaho State Welcome back, Pac-12! Jacobs started his college career with Arizona State, so he's back in the Pac-12, now with Utah State. Last year he averaged 6.6 yards per carry and scored five rushing touchdowns. Though that was in only 65 carries, he also caught 43 passes for 379 yards and three scores. The Aggies' first game in their new conference is against an FCS school in Idaho State. SIT Kirby Vorhees , RB, Washington State at Washington An Apple Cup right out of the gate! Wazzu has been through a lot of turmoil, on the conference and coach fronts, the last few years. Vorhees has stuck around after managing 576 yards and five touchdowns last season. Washington's defense was stout last year, though, especially against the run. The Huskies only allowed 100.1 rushing yards per game. SEC Starts and Sits START Anthony Evans , WR, Mississippi State vs. Louisiana-Monroe Evans joined Mississippi State from Georgia, where he didn't make much of an impact. That changed quickly, as he had 67 catches for 831 yards and four touchdowns for the Bulldogs in 2025. Louisiana-Monroe was interesting last season, not particularly bad against the pass or the run, but still allowing 31.9 points per game. The program tends to be one of the lesser lights of the FBS, and certainly the kind of team Mississippi State expects to light up at home. SIT Dilin Jones , RB, LSU vs. Clemson Not a single SEC team is playing on the road in Week 1, and only Mississippi is playing a ranked team, 24th-ranked Louisville. Lane Kiffin seems to have settled on Wisconsin transfer Jones as his lead back, but Jones only averaged 3.9 yards per carry last season. Given that Clemson only allowed 105.5 rushing yards and 20.5 points per game in 2025, I think Jones' LSU debut will be spoiled. Sun Belt Starts and Sits START Jordan Lovett , RB, Troy vs. Sam Houston Troy's offense wasn't very good last year, but this matchup is too good to avoid. Somebody should be able to take advantage of it, why not presumed lead back Lovett? He only had one good game last year, but in that game he ran for 113 yards and two touchdowns against Louisiana. Sign up AFC East Buffalo Bills Miami Dolphins New England Patriots New York Jets AFC North Baltimore Ravens Cincinnati Bengals Cleveland Browns Pittsburgh Steelers AFC South Houston Texans Indianapolis Colts Jacksonville Jaguars Tennessee Titans AFC West Denver Broncos Kansas City Chiefs Las Vegas Raiders Los Angeles Chargers NFC East Dallas Cowboys New York Giants Philadelphia Eagles Washington Commanders NFC North Chicago Bears Detroit Lions Green Bay Packers Minnesota Vikings NFC South Atlanta Falcons Carolina Panthers New Orleans Saints Tampa Bay Buccaneers NFC West Arizona Cardinals Los Angeles Rams San Francisco 49ers Seattle Seahawks AFC East Buffalo Bills Miami Dolphins New England Patriots New York Jets AFC North Baltimore Ravens Cincinnati Bengals Cleveland Browns Pittsburgh Steelers AFC South Houston Texans Indianapolis Colts Jacksonville Jaguars Tennessee Titans AFC West Denver Broncos Kansas City Chiefs Las Vegas Raiders Los Angeles Chargers NFC East Dallas Cowboys New York Giants Philadelphia Eagles Washington Commanders NFC North Chicago Bears Detroit Lions Green Bay Packers Minnesota Vikings NFC South Atlanta Falcons Carolina Panthers New Orleans Saints Tampa Bay Buccaneers NFC West Arizona Cardinals Los Angeles Rams San Francisco 49ers Seattle Seahawks Rumor Mill Peacock PFT Shop Jed York, 49ers’ brass are making plans in advance of potential suspension Mike Florio Mike Florio Published September 2, 2026 09:23 PM Facebook Twitter Email With 49ers owner Jed York facing a potential suspension as a result of his recent no-contest plea on charges arising from a recent prostitution arrest in Ohio, the powers-that-be are making plans now in the event York isn’t available later. “Let’s have conversations beforehand so that we know exactly where his wishes are,” G.M. John Lynch recently told Tim Kawakami of The TK Show , via 49ersWebZone.com. “And you can’t do that for everything because issues come up, like [the] trade deadline. You don’t know until you know, and there’s so many factors that go into that. But we’ll be prepared for everything because we’ve put in the work, we’ve put in the communication beforehand.” Even without a suspension, the dynamic has changed. York moved from California to Youngstown. He’s not around like he used to be. “If he’s not going to be here, Jed, we’ve got to talk on a regular basis,” Lynch said. “He knows that, we know that, we’ve done that. Now, to the regularity that we normally do, because conversations kind of come up organically, no, but it’s probably led to a lot more scheduled meetings where, in the past, it was more organic. “Yesterday morning, [coach] Kyle [Shanahan] and I were on a Zoom with Jed and had a great discussion about a variety of things. And so that communication is critical, I think, to keep everybody on the same page. And Jed, he’s been a great sounding board over the years. He trusts us.” It’s not ideal, and it illustrates the value of having ownership who is in the building every day — but who doesn’t excessively meddle in the football operation. It appears that the 49ers had found a sweet spot previously, when York lived and worked in the area. Now, it’s different. He’s not there on a regular basis. And, if/when he’s suspended, Lynch and Shanahan won’t have access to York at all (absent burner phones). Whether that makes this better or worse won’t be known until it happens. For now, the only certainty is that it is, and will be, different. Add favorite players, teams, and leagues with an NBCUniversal Profile Continue

articles.body: Fantasy Baseball Lineup Updates and Notes: AL Latest Changes | RotoWire Fantasy Baseball Lineup Lowdown: American League Trends Stay up to date on all the latest lineup and playing time changes around the American League, including Luke Keaschall settling into the leadoff spot for the Twins. September 2, 2026 Share By: Ryan Boyer @RyanPBoyer September 2, 2026 Fantasy Baseball Lineup Lowdown Mock Draft Simulator Prep for your 2026 Fantasy Football draft with free, unlimited drafts, and real-time grades. The goal with Lineup Lowdown is simple: we're looking for trends which could help identify players that might be undervalued or overvalued. Who is playing more/less? Who is moving up/down? This week, we will be focusing on players from the American League. Trending Up Luke Keaschall , 2B/OF, Minnesota Twins Keaschall began the 2026 campaign as the Twins' No. 3 hitter, but a poor start led to a quick move down in the batting order. However, a scorching-hot stretch has cemented the 24-year-old in the leadoff spot of late. In each of the Twins' last 14 contests, Keaschall has been perched atop the lineup, regardless of the handedness of the opposing pitcher. It came after a four-month stretch during which the outfielder rarely batted higher than sixth. You could argue that the move was overdue, as Keaschall has slashed a robust .333/.429/.530 with seven home runs, four stolen bases and a 19:29 BB:K over 49 contests since July 1. The batted-ball data with Keaschall remains unimpressive and has not really improved much during his hot stretch (33 percent hard-hit rate, 86.1 mph average exit velocity), but he's an elite contact hitter who has benefitted from some batted-ball luck (.360 BABIP). Cal Raleigh , C, Seattle Mariners Raleigh finally rediscovered his power stroke in August. Is it too little, too late for the Mariners? In each of the Twins' last 14 contests, Keaschall has been perched atop the lineup, regardless of the handedness of the opposing pitcher. It came after a four-month stretch during which the outfielder rarely batted higher than sixth. You could argue that the move was overdue, as Keaschall has slashed a robust .333/.429/.530 with seven home runs, four stolen bases and a 19:29 BB:K over 49 contests since July 1. The batted-ball data with Keaschall remains unimpressive and has not really improved much during his hot stretch (33 percent hard-hit rate, 86.1 mph average exit velocity), but he's an elite contact hitter who has benefitted from some batted-ball luck (.360 BABIP). Cal Raleigh , C, Seattle Mariners Raleigh finally rediscovered his power stroke in August. Is it too little, too late for the Mariners? Through his first 90 games this season, Raleigh sported a woeful .156/.266/.291 batting line with 12 home runs and a 32.1 percent strikeout rate. In early August, Raleigh had dipped all the way down to the No. 8 spot in the Mariners' batting order on three occasions. Suddenly, though, the reigning AL MVP runner-up has slashed .308/.400/.897 with seven long balls across his last 11 tilts. Included during that stretch was a three-homer game, something Raleigh didn't accomplish last year during his 60-homer season. Raleigh has been back up to the cleanup spot in each of his last three starts, with two of them being against righties and the other against a lefty. Henry Bolte , OF, Athletics A bevy of injuries to their position-player group has left the Athletics' lineup virtually unrecognizable. Part of the fallout is some players getting prime spots in the batting order that they might not have otherwise received, and new leadoff man Bolte is an example of that. Bolte has moonlighted as a leadoff man on occasion this season, usually against left-handed pitching. He's been the everyday leadoff hitter lately, though, occupying the spot in each of the Athletics' last 14 contests and 16 of their last 17 tilts (he batted second in that other game). In the game prior to this stretch, Bolte hit ninth, and he's spent time in every lineup slot other than third and fourth this season. Bolte rebounded from a dreadful July (.164/.243/.224) with his best month thus far in the majors, slashing .310/.366/.451 in August. Christian Moore , 2B, Los Angeles Angels It's a little odd that in yet another rebuilding season for the Angels it's taken them this long to give Moore an extended look in the big leagues, but that opportunity has finally arrived. Upon his promotion from Triple-A Salt Lake in late August, Moore has garnered 10 straight starts at second base. He spent the first two of those starts hitting eighth, but the 23-year-old has crept up since then, hitting cleanup once and fifth twice among his last five starts. The production hasn't been there yet for Moore, as he's collected a .581 OPS with one home run to go along with a 32.8 percent strikeout rate. He does have an 11.1 percent barrel rate and Moore has no issues lofting the ball in the air, so he's capable of going on a home run binge even if it comes with lots of swing and miss. Quick Hits: Jeff McNeil has hit second for the Athletics in 10 of his last 11 starts … Lawrence Butler has batted either third or fourth in his last nine starts … Coby Mayo has hit between the third and fifth slots in 12 of his last 15 starts … The Tigers have handed Hao-Yu Lee 12 consecutive starts … Taylor Trammell has been in the Houston lineup nine of the last 10 times they've faced a righty … Kansas City has included Nick Loftin in its lineup for 12 of its past 13 tilts … Jonny DeLuca has started 12 straight games for the Rays … The Rangers have penciled Cody Freeman into their lineup for 12 consecutive contests. Trending Down Taylor Ward Seattle Mariners Ward has been dreadful during his brief tenure in Seattle, and it seems the Mariners are already out of patience. Top prospect Lazaro Montes was called up Tuesday and homered as part of a two-hit major-league debut in Boston. He was slotted in at designated hitter, while Randy Arozarena Julio Rodriguez and Dominic Canzone patrolled the outfield. The left-handed-hitting Montes is going to play regularly versus righty hurlers, and the other three will rarely come out of the lineup. That seemingly leaves Ward — who did not start against a right-hander Tuesday — stuck in a short-side platoon. The trade deadline acquisition is just 8-for-66 (.121) with a 28 percent strikeout rate since joining the Mariners. Trevor Larnach , OF, Minnesota Twins From mid-June to mid-August, Larnach was slotted in as the Twins' leadoff hitter nearly every time the team faced a right-handed hurler. However, between a poor August (.594 OPS) and the emergence of the aforementioned Luke Keaschall , Larnach has been demoted to a lower placement in the batting order. In the left-handed-hitting Larnach's last nine starts (all versus righties), he's batted sixth five times and seventh on four occasions. The last time he hit that low against a righty came all the way back on April 5. Larnach is slashing .279/.362/.435 against right-handed pitching this season, but he's hit .215/.282/.355 versus all hurlers since the All-Star break, while Keaschall has put up a .321/.412/.500 batting line in the second half. Heliot Ramos , OF, New York Yankees The Yankees acquired Ramos at the trade deadline primarily for his ability to hit left-handed pitching. However, because of injuries to Aaron Judge (rib) and Cody Bellinger (hamstring), the righty-swinging Ramos was forced to play every day and did so from the middle of the batting order. Bellinger is healthy now, though, and in six games against righties since Bellinger came off the injured list, Ramos hasn't started once. Ramos batted cleanup twice and third twice the last four times versus left-handers, but there's no longer room for him in the lineup against right-handers, and it's only going to get more crowded in the outfield soon with Judge possibly nearing a return. In 74 plate appearances since joining the Bronx Bombers, Ramos is slashing only .148/.297/.279 with one long ball. Cam Smith , OF, Houston Astros The Astros are clinging to first place in a bad AL West division, so they need every win they can get down the stretch. That has resulted in less playing time lately for Smith, who has flashed but who has been unable to break through offensively. Smith's quality of contact has improved in his sophomore season, as we've seen his hard-hit rate (40.8 percent to 44.1 percent), barrel rate (6.9 percent to 10.9 percent) and average exit velocity (87.9 mph to 89.1 mph) all go up year-over-year. However, while he has nearly doubled last year's home run total in essentially the same number of plate appearances, Smith's batting average (.236 to .212) and on-base percentage (.312 to .278) are both way down. His slugging percentage is better but still sits at a poor .388. The 23-year-old has been out of the lineup two out of the last three games and three out of the last six contests versus right-handers. Quick Hits: Patrick Bailey has sat out in favor of Austin Hedges in five of the Guardians' last eight contests … Royce Lewis has batted seventh in three straight games, which is the lowest he's hit for the Twins since early June … Nearly all of Trent Grisham 's starts against right-handers this season have come from the leadoff spot, but he batted fifth once and sixth once the last two times the Yankees have gone up versus a righty. articles.body: Who are the top late-round fantasy football sleepers for 2026? We are in full swing of fantasy football draft season with the NFL’s regular season kicking off next Wednesday. Striking gold with some late round picks always puts your fantasy team on a strong path and below, I have featured two of my favorite late-round targets. Let’s break them down. RB Kenneth Gainwell, Tampa Bay Buccaneers After some underwhelming seasons with the Eagles, Gainwell joined the Steelers last season and came alive. The veteran rushed for 537 yards and five touchdowns on 114 carries and he caught 73 passes for 486 yards and three touchdowns on 85 targets, all of which set career highs. Gainwell didn’t miss a game and he generated 13.1 FPTS per game, despite playing behind Jaylen Warren. Gainwell was incredibly efficient, scoring 1.19 FPTS per touch and 0.43 FPTS per snap, both of which ranked top-10 among the running backs who played at least 25% of their team’s snaps. Following this impressive campaign, Gainwell signed a two-year, $14 million deal with the Buccaneers. The back figures to operate behind Bucky Irving in this backfield, but Gainwell seeing 10-15 touches every week like he did with the Steelers is very likely after his big payday. Plus, Irving is coming off a poor season. The back only appeared in 10 games due to foot and shoulder injuries, and Irving averaged a terrible 3.4 YPC, which ranked 62nd of the 65 backs who saw 50+ carries. Irving’s injuries definitely were a factor, but the Buccaneers inking Gainwell to a lucrative deal certainly makes you question the team’s confidence in Irving. Gainwell should be a viable RB3/FLEX play all season in this situation and he is an awesome value with the back slipping to around the 10th round in most formats. QB Malik Willis, Miami Dolphins Willis was widely regarded as one of the top backups in the league last season and he now gets his first attempt at being a starting quarterback, after signing a three-year, $67.5 million deal with the Dolphins. This is a pretty hefty payday for a quarterback that only has six career starts on his resume, but Willis really shined when given a chance last year with the Packers. Willis started once for the injured Jordan Love, facing the Ravens in Week 17 and in that start, Willis completed 18-of-21 passes for 288 yards, one touchdown and no picks, and he rushed nine times for nine yards and a pair touchdowns, resulting a massive 32.52 FPTS. Willis only played 98 snaps last season – which is about two games worth of data – but he was extremely efficient, averaging 12.1 YPA and completing 85.7% of his passes, both of which easily ranked first among all the quarterbacks who dropped back 20+ times. As a rusher, Willis averaged 5.6 YPC, which ranked ninth among the quarterbacks with 20+ carries. Notably, seven of Willis’ 22 carries gained 10+ yards and he rushed the ball on 22% of his snaps. All in all, Willis produced an incredible 1.1 FPTS per dropback, which ranked first among the quarterbacks with 40+ dropbacks and it wasn’t even close. Ranking second was the mighty Josh Allen, who averaged 0.7 FPTS per dropback. Obviously, this is a very limited sample and Willis maintaining this type of efficiency in a full season is impossible, but that doesn’t mean he won’t be a great fantasy asset in Miami. Willis’ lack of pass catchers is a concern, as the Dolphins’ top receivers are Malik Washington, Caleb Douglas and Jalen Tolbert, but DeVon Achane remains at the helm and is a terrific pass catcher out of the backfield. Regardless of Willis’ passing, his ability and willingness to run the ball will give him a strong floor every week. Even if Willis can be just an average passer to complement his rushing, he could average 18-20 FPTS per game. Willis is falling to around the 10th round in most drafts and he is one of the best late-round gambles regardless of position.
