articles.body: Detroit Tigers at Minnesota Twins prediction, pick for Wednesday 9/2/26 Baseball’s most wide-open division, the AL Central, is now down to just two. The Chicago White Sox have been in the division lead for most of the summer, and at varying points, the Minnesota Twins, Detroit Tigers, and Cleveland Guardians have made efforts at chasing them down. However, both the Twins and the Tigers underwent losing streaks in August that effectively ended their chances, and even after taking the first two in a three-game home series against Detroit, Minnesota still trails Chicago by 6.5 games. The Twins will go for a sweep tonight at 7:40 p.m. ET. Drew Anderson will start for the Tigers, and Minnesota will turn to Dean Kremer. Let’s break down this divisional battle with some odds and lines DraftKings Sportsbook Detroit Tigers at Minnesota Twins Best Bets Under 8.5 (+100) As long as Anderson doesn’t completely implode, Detroit’s offense is awful enough that it’s hard to imagine this game going over. The gap between the 29th-place Miami Marlins and the Tigers in OPS over the last 15 days is larger than that between the Marlins and the eighth-place Athletics. Dean Kremer Head-to-Head Strikeouts Moneyline (-129) The Twins have played pretty effective small ball over the last month with their only major power threat, Byron Buxton, sidelined; in August, Minnesota ranked 10th in batting average while striking out the fourth-fewest times. Detroit Tigers at Minnesota Twins prediction, preview After falling 16 games below .500 at the end of May, Detroit started to play like a playoff team in the early summer, coming within one game of .500 on August 11. However, since then, the Tigers have gone just 4-15, and across the last 15 days, they rank dead last in OPS by more than 100 points. Dillon Dingler, who’s emerged as one of baseball’s best catchers this season, has slashed only .176/.239/.276 across his last 27 games, and Javier Báez’s return from injury has been addition by subtraction. Furthermore, Detroit’s bullpen has posted an ERA nearly a full run worse since the All-Star break, with future Hall of Fame closer Kenley Jansen starting to show some signs of his age and Kyle Finnegan giving up five runs while recording just one out in last night’s 15-2 result. Perhaps ironically, it’s only the Tigers’ rotation that has improved relative to the first half of the season; the team sent away both Tarik Skubal and Casey Mize at the trade deadline, but Troy Melton has stepped into the ace role nicely and Jackson Jobe has been good in three of his five starts. The Twins chose the worst time to have their worst month of the season, as they went just 10-17 in August, but given that they underwent one of the most stunning complete tear-downs in MLB history at the 2025 trade deadline, the fact that they were in the playoff race for much of the season represents significant progress. Additionally, Minnesota finished with the sixth-highest OPS even in August, which is impressive given that its best player, Byron Buxton, was limited to just 11 games because of injuries and recorded only a .545 OPS in those games. Luke Keachsall has really come into his own as a batter since the All-Star break, slashing .321/.412/.500, and Kaelen Culpepper’s rookie season is off to a tremendous start. The Twins didn’t pitch well enough to back their offense up, though, ranking fifth-to-last in ERA in August. Joe Ryan, their only starter with better than a 110 OPS+ and more than five starts, has been on the Injured List for the last month, and the rest of their rotation simply hasn’t done enough to compensate. Minnesota’s bullpen has been a mixed bag; closer Yoendrys Gómez has a sub-3 ERA, and trade deadline acquisition A.J. Minter has a 0.83 ERA in 13 appearances, but Andrew Morris had a miserable end to August and Kody Funderbunk had a couple of rough outings as well. RELATED MLB Weather Today (September 2): Forecast, Rain and Wind for All 15 Games Anderson, a converted reliever, shifted into the starting rotation on August 5, after the Skubal and Mize trades, and he’s been decent, recording 22.1 innings pitched across five starts and pitching to a 2.82 ERA. It’s his first extended starting experience in the majors, but he’s quickly gotten acclimated to a full-time starter’s load, and given that he made 30 starts with the KBO’s SSG Landers in 2025 and recorded a 2.25 mark, this performance should be somewhat sustainable. This season, Anderson has pretty favorable advanced numbers, owning a 62nd-percentile xERA and a 71st-percentile xBA. Furthermore, he’s been excellent at generating both chases and whiffs, and the Twins have whiffed at an above-average rate. Anderson has also done a great job forcing grounders, which should combat one of Minnesota’s biggest strengths. He has been somewhat prone to giving up hard hits, sporting a bottom-quartile average exit velocity, but the Twins rank 12th-to-last in that stat and are without Buxton, who’s one of baseball’s best sluggers when healthy. However, the location splits aren’t in his favor; he’s posted an ERA north of 5 on the road, and Minnesota’s offense has been slightly more effective at home. Kremer has been solid since being acquired at the trade deadline, posting a 4.39 ERA in five starts, and he’s had a game score of at least 50 in three of the five. All in all, he sports a 30th-percentile xERA and 21st-percentile pitching run value, but he has his strengths and weaknesses. The right-hander has solid swing-and-miss stuff, posting a 71st-percentile whiff rate, and his ability to generate whiffs should combat one of the Tigers’ biggest strengths. Additionally, Kremer has effectively forced soft contact, with a top-third average exit velocity and hard-hit rate, and Detroit has made softer contact than average overall. His bottom-quintile grounder rate could be a problem, given that the Tigers have been the league’s best team at getting the ball in the air, but he has fairly significant home-road splits throughout his career and his sample size of career starts at Target Field (five games) isn’t large enough to look into. Given how awful the visitors’ offense has been as of late, the caliber of pitcher who I might peg to struggle is far below Kremer’s level. Detroit Tigers at Minnesota Twins pick, best bet Best Bet: Under 8.5 (+100) 12 games is obviously a tiny sample size, but the fact that Detroit has posted a .177/.257/.270 slash line in the last 15 days is pretty eye-popping. It’s not a surprise that each of the Tigers’ last three games had gone under until their pitching imploded on Monday and Tuesday. Strong Lean: Dean Kremer Head-to-Head Strikeouts Moneyline (-129) Across the same span, no team has struck out fewer times than the Twins, and although Anderson’s strikeout rate is higher than Kremer’s, he has struck out more than five batters in a game only once this season. Kremer has struck out at least five in seven of his 12 starts. articles.source_type: Fantasy Premier League news, predictions, player notes
articles.body: Aryna Sabalenka powers her way into the third round of the US Open in just 53 minutes - NBC Sports Skip navigation MLB NFL NBA NHL Premier League NASCAR College Football Men’s College Basketball Player News NFL Player News NBA Player News MLB Player News Scores NFL Scores NBA Scores MLB Scores MLB NFL NBA NHL Premier League NASCAR College Football Men’s College Basketball Player News NFL Player News NBA Player News MLB Player News Scores NFL Scores NBA Scores MLB Scores Login Favorites Sign up to follow your favorites on all your devices. Sign up Aryna Sabalenka powers her way into the third round of the US Open in just 53 minutes Associated Press Associated Press Published September 2, 2026 09:04 PM Facebook Twitter Email NEW YORK, NEW YORK - SEPTEMBER 02: Aryna Sabalenka celebrates against Polina Iatcenko during a Women’s Singles match on Day Four of the 2026 US Open at USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center on Wednesday, September 2, 2026 in Flushing, NY. (Photo by Dustin Satloff/USTA via Getty Images) Dustin Satloff/USTA via Getty Images Aryna Sabalenka came to the U.S. Open struggling and in danger of losing the No. 1 ranking. She heads to the third round looking every bit ready for a three-peat. The top-seeded Sabalenka overwhelmed Polina Iatcenko 6-1, 6-1 in 53 minutes on Wednesday night, putting on a power-hitting display that made it seem her recent problems are in the past. Sabalenka won 15 of 16 points on first serve in the first set and only dropped off a little in the second, finishing 21 for 28 in the match. Sabalenka is trying to become the first player to win three in a row in Flushing Meadows since Serena Williams from 2012-14, but arrived after losing in the fourth round of her past three tournaments. She needs help to stay atop the WTA rankings even if she wins the title. But she made it clear if she loses the top spot, it won’t be without a fight. “Happy with the level I played today, happy with the focus and happy to be through this match,” she said. Jessica Pegula was also quickly into the third round at a rainy U.S. Open where some players were still playing their first-round matches. The No. 3 seed needed only 56 minutes on Wednesday to defeat Sofia Kenin 6-3, 6-1. Kenin, the 2020 Australian Open champion, beat Venus Williams in her first match. “To be out of there in under an hour, it doesn’t always happen,” Pegula said. “So I think I’m just going to take that one and run, I guess, until the next round.” Some players won’t get there for a while. With rain coming down for a second day in New York, play was suspended again for a time on outside courts, allowing only play under the roofs in Arthur Ashe Stadium and Louis Armstrong Stadium to continue uninterrupted. No. 8 seed Ben Shelton followed Pegula on Ashe and beat Hubert Hurkacz 6-3, 5-7, 7-6 (3), 7-5, while No. 7 Daniil Medvedev raced past Sebastian Gorzny — except for a brief delay to protest the chair umpire’s decision to replay a point when two birds sat on the net — 6-3, 6-3, 7-5. Defending champion Carlos Alcaraz was set to follow Sabalenka on Ashe. A three-day first round stretches into a fourth When the U.S. Open switched to a Sunday start last year, it spread out the first round over the first three days, so Wednesday would have arrived with everyone playing in the second round had the weather cooperated. It hadn’t. Alex de Minaur, the No. 6 seed from Australia, said with all the juggling his match was moved twice from the court where he was originally scheduled. He finally started his U.S. Open on Wednesday on Court 11 and beat Italy’s Andrea Guerrieri 6-2, 6-2, 6-4. “It’s been a couple tough days. But I mean, these tournaments, it’s all about adapting and that’s the name of the game,” de Minaur said. “There’s too much to play for to let something like this affect you.” Paula Badosa said she didn’t even know how to prepare for the resumption of her match against Daria Kasatkina, which was halted Tuesday with her one game from winning to set up a second-round match against No. 4 Coco Gauff. “I didn’t know if I was going to play just two points or six, or I don’t know how much, how many I play or one more set,” the Spaniard said Wednesday after finishing off her 6-1, 6-4 victory. “So I knew that if I was winning this match, I’m playing the next day. So, yeah, it was everything a bit different. I was very nervous that I even couldn’t eat, so a lot of different stuff I did today, but sometimes it is how it is, and I tried to play with the things I had there.” At least she got through. No. 12 Rafael Jodar, the 19-year-old from Spain who came in after a strong summer, was routed 6-2, 6-1, 6-1 by Bu Yunchaokete of China when his first-round match was finally completed. “I knew it wasn’t going to be easy because I was waiting a lot yesterday and today as well, but it is what it is,” Jodar said. “We cannot control the rain, so it’s difficult for both players.” The tournament was trying to catch up from Tuesday’s rain delays, with 25 singles matches being played on the men’s side alone. The first round was finally completed Wednesday night. Alex Michelsen pulled off an upset in one of them by ousting fellow American Brandon Nakashima, the No. 16 seed, 6-3, 6-4, 6-4. No. 7 Karolina Muchova, the Wimbledon runner-up, beat Katie Boulter 6-1, 6-0 to reach the third round, while No. 11 Marta Kostyuk got past 2017 U.S. Open champion Sloane Stephens 6-1, 7-5. No. 31 seed Leylah Fernandez set up a matchup of past U.S. Open runners-up against Pegula, with the winner to meet either No. 16 Sorana Cirstea or No. 19 Jasmine Paolini. Police have made an arrest in the case. Via NBC10, authorities have taken 24-year-old Jabir Parker into custody in connection with multiple crimes , including the incident at Barkley’s residence. Parker faces charges in connection with two home invasions and the attempted break-in of a third in Montgomery and Chester counties. In the first two, Parker allegedly stole nearly $800,000 worth of jewelry. The attempted break-in is reportedly the one that targeted Barkley’s home. Parker was arrested on Tuesday. Authorities used “geo-fencing” to place Parker’s phone at each of the three scenes. They also found a recording of Parker’s voice on a nanny cam. articles.excerpt: Everton Under-21s fell to a narrow 2-1 defeat against AC Milan Under-21s at Goodison Park on Wednesday evening. The match – the Blues’ first of their Premier League International Cup campaign – could’ve gone either way. Federico Colombo struck the Italians into a first-half lead, before Braiden Graham’s delightful free-kick levelled the score after the interval. But Milan forward Lorenzo Ossola found a winner for the visitors, taking advantage of an Everton mistake to net a second for his team against the run of play. It was a young Everton line-up taking to the field with plenty of absentees missing the midweek match. The sides shared few chances across the opening 10 minutes, but prolific forward Graham came close in the 12 th , almost latching on to Ceiran Loney’s squared ball into the penalty box. Graham threatened again shortly after when he was picked out by Harvey Foster’s sweeping forward pass. The young Blue cut in from the left, beating his man but striking narrowly wide of the near post. articles.body: Fabrizio Romano: Chelsea 'play down' links with former Liverpool midfielder after Camara disappointment - Sports Mole Menu Loading... Fabrizio Romano: Chelsea 'play down' links with former Liverpool midfielder after Camara disappointment Ben Sully 02 Sep 2026 20:25 , Last updated: 02 Sep 2026 20:41 Â© Iconsport / PictureAlliance/Azzuu Chelsea have reportedly poured cold water over rumours they are interested in signing former Liverpool midfielder Georginio Wijnaldum Xabi Alonso's failed in their quest to sign a replacement for Enzo Fernandez before the transfer window slammed shut on Tuesday. Chelsea were linked with Roma's Manu Kone, although the Italian side have insisted that a move was never close. In contrast, the Blues were on the verge of landing Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara before the Ligue 1 outfit backed out of the deal to Chelsea's frustration. The west London club still sanctioned Fernandez's move to Manchester City after giving their word to their Premier League rivals. © Imago Chelsea dismiss Wijnaldum links The free agent market represents the only avenue for Chelsea to bolster their engine room until the January transfer window. That has led to links over a potential move for Wijnaldum , who is searching for a new club after leaving Saudi Pro League side Al-Ettifaq. Jordan Henderson 's former Liverpool teammate boasts significant Premier League experience after making 217 top-flight appearances during his time at the Reds and Newcastle United. However, according to Fabrizio Romano , there are no plans to reunite Wijnaldum with Henderson at Stamford Bridge. The update claims that Chelsea have 'played down' speculation linking them with the former Netherlands international. © Iconsport / PA Images Who are Xabi Alonso's midfield options? Moises Caicedo, Romeo Lavia, Valentin Barco and Henderson are among Alonso's central midfield options. The Chelsea boss can also field right wing-backs Reece James and Malo Gusto in the middle of the park. With no European football to contend with, Alonso should be able to manage the first half of the campaign with the midfielders that are currently at his disposal, with Chelsea expected to strengthen the position in the January window. articles.body: Los Angeles Dodgers vs. St. Louis Cardinals prediction, pick for MLB on Wednesday 9/02/26 Tuesday’s 13-8 eruption was mystifying for several glorious reasons. First, St. Louis hit five home runs, including two from Thomas Saggese. Second, the combination of Jordan Walker, Ramón Urías and Joshua Baez also went deep. Eric Lauer, in total, surrendered seven runs in three innings for the Dodgers, and utterly detonated the matchup before Los Angeles could even settle into decent pitch counts on the offensive side. Now, the Dodgers still scored eight, led by Mookie Betts’ two doubles and four RBIs. And, most welcome: Will Smith returned after three months and drove in two. These are two hot lineups, but surely they can’t score 20+ runs again tonight—right? Below is my preview, prediction, and pick for today’s baseball game between the Los Angeles Dodgers and the St. Louis Cardinals. Here’s how I’ll play it. I’ll be pumping out these predictions for individual games all season, with plenty of coverage here on DraftKings Network . Follow my handle @dansby_edits for more betting plays. Dodgers vs. Cardinals prediction, preview Yoshinobu Yamamoto should do a lot to suppress the sort of runs Lauer gave up in droves last night. Even on a slightly down year for Yoshi’s pure dominance, he slashes at 12-8 with a 2.56 ERA, 0.89 WHIP and 153 strikeouts across 158 innings. His August line helped make the SL stats look more like jewelry: a 1.95 ERA, 35 strikeouts, and only 20 hits across 32.1 innings. Over his last two starts, he surrendered just three earned runs and struck out 17 across 12.2 innings. He’s eviscerating. To boot: Yamamoto has completed at least six innings in seven consecutive home starts. Oh, and these very Cardinals have faced him twice—twice!—and failed to score at all across 11 innings. Yamamoto’s broad six-pitch mix prevents hitters from getting at all comfortable in the box. His splitter is the tip of the spear at 26.8% usage, holding opponents to .179 and a .223 xwOBA. His four-seamer averages 96mph and slices through batters at a 30.1% strikeout rate. It does, however, have, underneath the hood, .466 expected slugging percentage. Misses over the plate have traveled far. Thus, Jordan Walker’s 28 home runs and Alec Burleson’s 100 RBI-savvy demand finesse in those spots. Yamamoto will answer with cutters, sinkers, and sliders—or just flood the zone with splitters—once either hitter gets ahead. St. Louis can make it difficult and fractured early for the Dodgers’ lineup; it’s a planned bullpen game. Rotating fresh arms should let the Cardinals chase platoon advantages before Los Angeles sees anyone twice. Ryan Fernandez, Cade Winquest, and Gastelum each threw between 23 and 25 pitches Tuesday. Stanek, Soriano, and Riley O’Brien remained fresh. I’d look for most Dodger damage to be done during the innings of bulk relief from one of the aforementioned three available arms. Cardinals vs. Dodgers pick, best bet Los Angeles has scored three runs or fewer in five of Yamamoto’s last six home starts, so he could use a little more support. But the lineup looks like it’s clicking. Last night, Betts drove the baseball, Smith restored length, and the lineup generated eight runs despite playing from behind all night. The other side of the same coin in a bullpen game, I suppose, in this case, is that Shohei Ohtani and Freddie Freeman will face multiple bullpen looks without a starter controlling the matchup. A mild breeze toward center will add carry to liners and fly-balls. The moneyline at -258 asks too much, while the run line demands we pay for Yamamoto’s expected separation. St. Louis may script four clean innings. Covering nine against this order presents a different burden. Yamamoto should hold the Cardinals near two runs, giving Los Angeles several paths to margin. I would play -1.5 through -120 and leave the expensive moneyline alone. Best bet: Dodgers -1.5 at -118. Projected score: Dodgers 5, Cardinals 2. articles.excerpt: Alex Hunter analyzes the Texans' backfield of Woody Marks and David Montgomery for the upcoming NFL season. The post Could Woody Marks have more fantasy value than David Montgomery in 2026? appeared first on DraftKings Network .
articles.source_type: Captain picks ranked with reasoning, gameweek rankings, DFS targets
articles.body: Could Woody Marks have more fantasy value than David Montgomery in 2026? The Texans head into the season with Montgomery and Marks as the team’s top-two backs. Currently for Best Ball drafts on DraftKings, Montgomery carries an ADP of 47.8 while Marks is going way later at 134.1. Based on these ADPs, who is the better fantasy value of these backs for the upcoming season? Montgomery vs. Marks After relying on Marks for most of last season, the Texans went out and traded for Montgomery this spring, giving up a fourth-round pick, a seventh-round pick and offensive lineman Juice Scruggs in the deal. Then, Houston quickly inked Montgomery to a two-year, $16.5 million contract extension, which is a pretty strong indicator that the Texans view Montgomery as their starter for this upcoming season. Montgomery now officially sits atop the depth chart and sat out the entire preseason along with many of the other Texans’ starters. Meanwhile, Marks played in one of the exhibitions with the backups. Marks was a fourth-round pick by Houston last season and while he eventually was given the lead back job with Joe Mixon out for the year, Marks did struggle to produce. The 25-year-old only averaged 3.6 YPC, which ranked 56th of the 65 backs who saw 50+ carries. Marks never rushed for more than 74 yards in a game in the regular season and he only found the paydirt twice with his legs, despite seeing 33 redzone carries. As a receiver, Marks only caught 66.7% of his targets, which tied for dead last among the running backs who saw 20+ targets. He did, however, rank 13th among those players in yard per reception (8.7) and he caught three touchdown passes. While Marks is only entering his second season, the Texans bringing in Montgomery and making him their lead back makes sense after Marks’ struggles a year ago. While Montgomery is entering his eighth season, he is still only 29-years-old and is coming off a strong campaign with the Lions. Playing behind Jahmyr Gibbs, Montgomery averaged 4.5 YPC, which is the second-best mark of his career and ranked 24th of the backs who saw 50+ carries. Montgomery scored eight touchdowns despite playing a secondary role to Gibbs and Montgomery hauled in 24 of his 26 targets, ranking him fifth in catch rate among the backs who saw 20+ targets. Overall, Montgomery finished 26th at his position in FPTS per snap (0.41), whereas Marks finished 48th (0.25). Playing together this season, it’s safe to expect Montgomery to be the primary rusher and redzone option, who also sees some passing down work. Meanwhile, Marks should operate behind Montgomery with some carries and action on passing plays. This feels likely to be a 70/30 split in favor of Montgomery and while he is a far more expensive option for fantasy drafts, Montgomery is the better value over Marks and a compelling pick around the fifth round. Marks has merit his late ADP, but he shouldn’t be viewed as more than a high-end handcuff that may have some solid games here and there. articles.body: US Open 2026: Pegula thrashes Kenin in second round | Flashscore.com All Football Transfer News Premier League US Open Features Champions League Darts Snooker Golf Cycling MLB NFL Most read on Flashscore News Transfer News LIVE: Richarlison set for move to Turkey, Dutch clubs nearing deadline Man City confirm joint British record signing of Enzo Fernandez from Chelsea Aguero backs Jesus to shine at Barcelona: 'He can easily score 10 or 15 goals' Swedish tennis ace collapses twice on court during Challenger event in China Third seed Jessica Pegula eases through in just 56 minutes at US Open Reuters Updated Pegula celebrates her second-round victory IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters / Robert Deutsch World number three Jessica Pegula produced a finely tuned performance to sprint through a second-round meeting with fellow American Sofia Kenin, winning 6-3 6-1 at the U.S. Open on Wednesday. In the first match of the day on Arthur Ashe Stadium, Pegula dropped only three of her first-serve points and never faced a break point. The 2024 runner-up, who is seeking her maiden major title as well as top spot in the rankings, booked a meeting with 2021 finalist Leylah Fernandez. Wildcard Kenin has struggled as injuries and illness saw her tumble down the rankings after her breakthrough 2020 Australian Open win and she was never able to get a foothold in the match as she suffered yet another early exit from her domestic major. Key match stats Flashscore Kenin handed her opponent the break with a double fault in the opening game and Pegula broke her again on set point with a fine forehand before slamming her foot down on the gas. The runner-up at the Cincinnati tune-up tournament was near flawless as she won the first five games of the second set, producing just two unforced errors before closing it out with an unreturnable serve. "I'm going for my spots, I'm going pretty big on second serves," said Pegula, adding that she had put effort into adding more firepower to her serve. "Really excited when I can practise something and it pays off in a match." (Photo by Alyssa McDaniel/MLB Photos via Getty Images) Alyssa McDaniel/MLB Photos via Getty Images Ronald Acuña Jr. hit a three-run homer to become the fastest player in major league history to reach 200 home runs and 200 stolen bases, and the Atlanta Braves beat the Washington Nationals 9-0 on Wednesday. Sean Murphy homered for the third time in five games, a three-run shot in the sixth inning that broke a scoreless tie in a game that was interrupted by a 1-hour, 25-minute rain delay in the fourth. Acuña followed with a drive to left-center in the seventh, his 14th of the season, to make it 6-0. He needed 904 games to reach the 200/200 club. Alfonso Soriano set the previous record at 929 games in August of 2006 while playing for the Nationals against the Braves. Acuña stole the 225th base of his career and 20th of the season, swiping second after his leadoff single in the sixth against Riley Cornelio (2-2), who struck out the next two batters. After Michael Harris II was walked intentionally, Murphy took Cornelio deep to left. Acuña led off the fourth with a single off Nationals starter Brad Lord. A walk and an error loaded the bases before it started raining. When play resumed, Cornelio came in and retired Murphy and Mike Yastrzemski to escape the jam. Grant Holmes needed only 26 pitches to retire the first nine Nationals before the delay. Dylan Dodd worked a scoreless inning and Elieser Hernández (2-0) pitched the next three, allowing two hits, including James Wood’s two-out single in the sixth for Washington’s first hit. Nationals catcher Keibert Ruiz left in the fourth inning after taking a foul ball off his mask. articles.body: Los Angeles Angels vs. New York Yankees prediction, pick for MLB on Wednesday 9/02/26 For all their marquee might, the Yankees’ last five run totals are inconsistent at best, and not always in a bad way: 0, 9, 16, 1, and 7. Tuesday’s barrage did a little more to establish the reputation of the new Bronx Bombers: Spencer Jones reached four times, homered for a second straight night, stole a base and drove in three. Jazz Chisholm Jr. homered, had three hits, just like Cody Bellinger, who scored twice. No Judge, no Stanton. And still this lineup can turn over like that. Below is my preview, prediction, and pick for today’s baseball game between the Los Angeles Angels and the New York Yankees. Here’s how I’ll play it. I’ll be pumping out these predictions for individual games all season, with plenty of coverage here on DraftKings Network . Follow my handle @dansby_edits for more betting plays. Angels vs. Yankees prediction, preview Cy Young-favorite Cam Schlittler should allow New York’s bats, however, to take a night off. He leads the American League with a 2.09 ERA and ranks second with 163.2 innings; he’ll be on the mound against this lineup for most of the night, I’d imagine. Over his last three starts, Schlittler allowed two earned runs and 12 hits across 17 innings. In that same timeframe, however, he’s issued 11 walks. Those are something to monitor, as I’m sure the Yankees will pull him before any cloggy traffic can do too much damage. And, indeed, Schlittler’s fastball deployment looks vicious against this lineup. He throws four-seamers/sinkers 64.1% of the time, and averages 98mph on the gun with both. The four-seamer has held hitters to .183, with a 34.5% whiff rate. His sinker has yielded a .182 average and only a .259 slugging percentage. Los Angeles has the second-most strikeouts against right-handers and carries a .371 team slugging percentage. Zach Neto and Mike Trout can punish the high heater, but most of this order can’t catch up to the sort of premium velocity Schlittler slings. Reid Detmers, however, gives the Angels an exciting counterpunch. His August was, quite simply, superb: a 1.50 ERA, 29 strikeouts, six walks, and a 0.97 WHIP. Sparkling. And, across his last three starts, Detmers only allowed one earned run in 20 innings. Better yet, he’s lined a 0.59 career ERA against New York through 15.1 innings. His slider is his killshot, and it’s limited hitters to .189, with a 35.3% whiff rate and 38% strikeout rate. The Yankees’ bats best shot comes against his four-seamer, which carries a .425 expected slugging percentage. Yankees vs. Angels pick, best bet That leaves the game balanced on starter length, way I see it. Detmers can quiet New York if he’s at his best through six, while Schlittler can choke off an even thinner Angels lineup for all nine innings, if it comes to that. Even so, the relief innings favor New York sharply, with a 3.06 bullpen ERA compared to Los Angeles’ 4.35. Saucedo, Peralta and Natera all worked for the Yanks on Tuesday, while David Bednar rested. Clear skies and a breeze toward right field add a modest boost to the easy-to-reach seats, which keeps betting the total a little risky, especially once Detmers exits. Still, the market dropped this total from 7 to 6.5, and I think the move is justified. Even at that point, two hot starters and New York’s dominant bullpen leave enough room to breathe. The Angels’ relief corps creates the only risk, so I would stop buying in at −110. A total of 6 would be a pass for me. Best bet: Under 6.5 at -107. Projected score: Yankees 3, Angels 2. articles.excerpt: Roma sporting director Tony D'Amico dismisses the suggestion that Chelsea made a serious effort to sign midfielder Manu Kone.

articles.body: Chelsea transfer news: "Nothing happened" claim made as Roma chief opens up on Manu Kone rumours - Sports Mole Menu Loading... Chelsea transfer news: "Nothing happened" claim made as Roma chief opens up on Manu Kone rumours Ben Sully 02 Sep 2026 19:45 Â© Imago / Giuseppe Maffia Roma sporting director Tony D'Amico has dismissed the suggestion that Gian Piero Gasperini stopped Manu Kone from joining Chelsea on deadline day. The Premier League giants prioritised the signing of a new central midfielder in the closing stages of the summer window, but they ultimately failed in their effort to bolster a key area of Xabi Alonso 's squad. They were linked with a potential move for Kone before they turned their focus to Monaco's Lamine Camara. Monaco backed out of the agreed deal for Camara at the final hour, leaving Chelsea without a replacement for Manchester City's new addition, Enzo Fernandez. © Imago / Insidefoto D'Amico reveals Kone was never close to Chelsea move Rumours suggested that Roma boss Gian Piero Gasperini played a key role in Chelsea's failed pursuit of Kone. However, D'Amico has dismissed the notion that Gasperini blocked Kone's exit , insisting that Chelsea never submitted a bid for the France international. “Manu Kone was never close to joining Chelsea," D'Amico said as per Fabrizio Romano "There was not even an official bid. Gasperini didn’t have to put any veto because nothing happened. "The clubs make calls, as we do as well - nothing else. Chelsea didn’t send any bid." © Imago / Nicolo Campo Chelsea could still pursue Kone deal While he has stayed put for the time being, Kone could be the subject of interest when the transfer window reopens in January. According to Sport.FR via Roma Press, Chelsea will continue to monitor the French midfielder ahead of a potential move in the new year. That said, Roma are in a relatively strong position to fend off interest, with Kone under contract until the summer of 2029. Sign up AFC East Buffalo Bills Miami Dolphins New England Patriots New York Jets AFC North Baltimore Ravens Cincinnati Bengals Cleveland Browns Pittsburgh Steelers AFC South Houston Texans Indianapolis Colts Jacksonville Jaguars Tennessee Titans AFC West Denver Broncos Kansas City Chiefs Las Vegas Raiders Los Angeles Chargers NFC East Dallas Cowboys New York Giants Philadelphia Eagles Washington Commanders NFC North Chicago Bears Detroit Lions Green Bay Packers Minnesota Vikings NFC South Atlanta Falcons Carolina Panthers New Orleans Saints Tampa Bay Buccaneers NFC West Arizona Cardinals Los Angeles Rams San Francisco 49ers Seattle Seahawks AFC East Buffalo Bills Miami Dolphins New England Patriots New York Jets AFC North Baltimore Ravens Cincinnati Bengals Cleveland Browns Pittsburgh Steelers AFC South Houston Texans Indianapolis Colts Jacksonville Jaguars Tennessee Titans AFC West Denver Broncos Kansas City Chiefs Las Vegas Raiders Los Angeles Chargers NFC East Dallas Cowboys New York Giants Philadelphia Eagles Washington Commanders NFC North Chicago Bears Detroit Lions Green Bay Packers Minnesota Vikings NFC South Atlanta Falcons Carolina Panthers New Orleans Saints Tampa Bay Buccaneers NFC West Arizona Cardinals Los Angeles Rams San Francisco 49ers Seattle Seahawks Rumor Mill Peacock PFT Shop Aaron Rodgers is in a four-quarterback room for the first time Charean Williams Charean Williams Published September 2, 2026 07:36 PM Facebook Twitter Email The Steelers kept four quarterbacks, declining to expose Will Howard or Drew Allar to the waiver wire. Aaron Rodgers, now in his 22nd season, has never experienced a four-quarterback room. “I was thinking it was a possibility , but I don’t think I’ve been on a roster with four quarterbacks,” Rodgers said Wednesday, via Brooke Pryor of ESPN. “Obviously when you do that, you’re taking away a spot from another place in the team. But at the same time, if the best 53 are going to make it -- and not saying they did -- I think those four are part of the best 53.” The four quarterbacks on the active roster, which include veteran Mason Rudolph, also is a first for coach Mike McCarthy. This season is unique for the Steelers with Rodgers in his final season, leaving the team with an uncertain future at the position. Rudolph, Howard and Allar could compete for the job in 2027. “I’m happy for all those guys,” Rodgers said. “Obviously looking to the future, those other three guys are going to have a chance when I’m done. And with the growth you saw with Will and obviously with Drew being drafted so far, but also playing well in camp, I’m not surprised at all and I’m excited about those guys’ future.” The Packers had a plan with 2020 first-round pick Jordan Love sitting behind Rodgers for three seasons before taking the reins. The Jets had no plan behind Rodgers and started Justin Fields, Tyrod Taylor and Brady Cook last season before trading for Geno Smith to start this season. The Steelers drafted Howard in the sixth round in 2025 and Allar in the third round in 2026. Rodgers watched Howard and Allar on television from his home as they played the third preseason game against the Bills last weekend. “I thought the entire camp, it was never too big for them,” Rodgers said. “They looked really comfortable out there, and I thought they did a lot of good things moving to football, being efficient. “There’s learning experiences, but you look at my first preseason, it was not pretty at all. I didn’t play good until about the second half of the fourth preseason game. So, they’re definitely ahead of where I was at, and mentally, they’re grasping the offense and the checks and the cans, and I’m really proud about those guys.” Rodgers, drafted in the first round in 2005, went 20-of-37 for 172 yards with a touchdown and two interceptions in four games in his first preseason. articles.body: Chicago White Sox vs. Houston Astros prediction, pick for Wednesday 9/2/26 We’ve officially passed the end of August and are into September, meaning the MLB’s postseason race is coming down to the wire. Two division leaders play one more time in Houston tonight as the Astros host the Chicago White Sox for the conclusion of this series, which the two clubs have split thus far. First pitch is scheduled for 8:10 p.m. ET. Let’s dive in with a preview, prediction and pick for tonight’s White Sox vs. Astros game courtesy of odds and lines on DraftKings Sportsbook. White Sox vs. Astros prediction, preview After last night’s win for Chicago, these clubs have now split the series at one game apiece. The White Sox are up to 73-65 with a +45 run differential, taking six of their last 10 games in hand. The Astros, however, are floating just above .500 at 70-69 with a -44 differential and have gone 5-5 over their last 10 outings. RHP Davis Martin (9-6) is set to start for the Sox tonight. He has a 4.32 ERA with a 1.33 WHIP, plus 111 strikeouts across 125.0 IP. His K% is 20.9% with a 7.4% BB%. While he was highly effective over the season’s first half, his ERA has plummeted over six starts in the second half with an 8.03 mark and a 1.50 WHIP, so fatigue seems to be playing a role for him. RHP Hayden Wesneski (4-1) gets the nod for the Stros. He carries a 3.86 ERA and 1.19 WHIP over his 32.2 IP since returning from Tommy John surgery. He’s also struck out 28 hitters for a 21.1% K% with a 9.0% BB%. His chase rate notably remains elite at 36.6%, so it’s clear the injury didn’t sap him of his stuff, too. Both offenses are potent. The White Sox rank eighth in wRC+ over the second half with an OPS of .717 and the seventh-most runs scored. They continue to excel in terms of power with a .166 ISO, and their 52 homers rank ninth over this span. On the full season, they slash .237/.319/.403 with a .722 OPS against right-handers. The Astros aren’t far behind in production over the second half. They sit 10th in wRC+ around the sport with a .714 OPS and a .162 ISO of their own, scoring the 10th-most runs over this same sample. They’re also 10th in homers with 51 since the All-Star break. On the year, they’re slashing .241/.317/.412 with a .729 OPS against right-handed pitching. RELATED Milwaukee Brewers vs. Chicago Cubs prediction, pick for Wednesday 9/2/26 White Sox vs. Astros pick, best bet DraftKings Sportsbook lists the Astros as a -142 Moneyline favorite at home this evening, while the White Sox are a +118 underdog on the road. The total is set at 8.5 combined runs. Personally, I like Houston to eclipse its team total of 4.5 runs tonight. Martin is only just returning from a multi-week absence, and before hitting the IL, he was really struggling as mentioned earlier. He gave up three or more earned runs in five of his eight starts since July, with four outings of four-plus earned runs at that. I think he’ll be a little bit shaky this evening against a club that hits better against right-handers, especially given his poor average exit velocity and hard-hit rates allowed. Factor in that the Astros are marginally better at home with a hitter-friendly park, and it seems they could easily eclipse 4.5 runs. articles.body: Ipswich Town v Liverpool: Prediction, team news, lineups and odds Ipswich Town v Liverpool: Prediction, team news, lineups and odds David Tindall 02 Sep 2026 Premier League Portman Road Ipswich Town Liverpool Ipswich Town v Liverpool: Premier League preview Two games into the new Premier League season and Ipswich Town have something that Liverpool do not: a win. Fresh from promotion, Ipswich Town opened the campaign with a last-gasp 2-1 victory over Sunderland and followed that with a 3-1 Carabao Cup win over Leicester. They were also 1-0 up at Old Trafford in their second Premier League start before some vulnerabilities were exposed as they crashed to a 5-2 loss. Liverpool have trailed 1-0 and 2-1 in both games so far. An injury-time equaliser from Dominik Szoboszlai at Newcastle and a thumping late strike from summer signing Victor Munoz secured 2-2 draws, but two points from six isn’t the start new boss Andoni Iraola wanted. It all means Ipswich start the game in 12th, one spot above the 13th-placed Reds. Ipswich Town v Liverpool kick-off time Ipswich Town v Liverpool kicks off at 8pm BST on Friday, September 4 at Portman Road. Ipswich Town v Liverpool how to watch The game will be shown live in the UK via Sky Sports Main Event and Sky Sports Premier League, with coverage starting from 7pm. TalkSPORT will provide full match commentary. Ipswich Town team news Ipswich Town are likely to play the 4-2-3-1 formation that secured victory over Sunderland in their Portman Road opener. The only real doubt is striker Emersson, who jarred his knee and came off at half-time against Manchester United. Jack Clarke or Sindre Walle Egeli are the two vying to replace him. Zian Flemming is another option up front, although he is more likely to start on the bench after his deadline day move from Burnley. Jaden Philogene (foot/ankle) and Jack Taylor (knee) are both ruled out, but Florentino Luis (calf) and Azor Matusiwa (thigh) could be named in the matchday squad. Liverpool team news It wasn’t the transfer window Liverpool fans wanted but they did at least pull off one star signing with Bradley Barcola coming in from PSG for huge money. He’s declared himself ready to play but the bench looks most likely for the flying Frenchman given his lack of pre-season action. Beyond that, it looks likely that Iraola will field the same starting XI that drew with Nottingham Forest last week. That means Cody Gakpo and Victor Munoz being handed the winger roles. Ryan Gravenberch may have to settle for a place on the bench again with Szoboszlai and Alexis Mac Allister getting the nod in midfield. That’s unless Iraola chooses to switch Szoboszlai to right-back in place of the unconvincing Jeremie Frimpong. Hugo Ekitike, Conor Bradley and Giovanni Leoni remain long-term absentees while Joe Gomez still isn’t ready to return. Ipswich v Liverpool odds Liverpool, who won 2-0 at Portman Road on their last visit (opening game of the 2024/25 season), are 8/15 to bag their first victory of the season. Ipswich are 9/2 while The Draw is 7/2. Liverpool signing among 10 biggest Premier League overpays of 2026 The 15 best footballers out of contract and available for free NOW An outrageous Premier League XI that cost less than £125m Enzo Fernandez Liverpool have drifted out to 16/1 to win the title while Ipswich are 5/4 for relegation. Ipswich v Liverpool prediction Ipswich managed just one home win out of 19 when they were last in the Premier League two seasons ago so they’ve already matched that tally! But Gary O’Neil’s men have never beaten Liverpool in the Premier League at Portman Road, while more damning is the stat that they’ve kept just one clean sheet in their last 36 top-flight games. This is a great chance for Liverpool to get off the mark and it’s worth noting that they did have 27 shots and 36 touches in the opposition box at Newcastle despite having to rescue a draw. Cody Gakpo looked set to depart Anfield in the transfer window but a move didn’t materialise, and that means he’s worth a bet to continue his strong start to the season. So far he’s scored at Newcastle and set up Alexander Isak’s equaliser against Forest. Gakpo to score anytime in a Liverpool win pays 11/4. Those who want to jump straight onto the Bradley Barcola train can back him at 17/5 to register an assist and 7/4 to score. It’s worth waiting for team news though. A third straight 2-2 draw for Liverpool is 14/1. articles.title: 3 Storylines to Watch Most in Ole Miss' Week 1 Matchup Against Louisville
articles.excerpt: The Ole Miss Rebels will battle with a tough Louisville team.
articles.source_type: Gameweek squads, team news round-ups, deadline reminders
articles.body: 3 Storylines to Watch Most in Ole Miss' Week 1 Matchup Against Louisville Ole Miss head coach Pete Golding runs off the field. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect We're just days away from the Ole Miss Rebels kicking off their 2026 season against the Louisville Cardinals. This is the only matchup of the week that features two ranked teams. The Rebels boast a talented roster under Pete Golding, but a challenging schedule lies ahead . Louisville provides Ole Miss with a tough early-season test, so the Rebels must be ready. There are plenty of intriguing storylines heading into the first week of the season. Pete Golding's First Regular Season Game as Head Coach Ole Miss Rebels head coach Pete Golding speaks to the press during SEC Football Kickoff Media Day at the Tampa Marriott. Mandatory Credit: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Golding entered unusual circumstances when he took over as interim head coach during the College Football Playoff last season. Now, Golding begins his first full season as a head coach, and he doesn't get a soft landing zone with the Cardinals. He's had an entire offseason to settle into his new role, but how will that translate on the field? Golding has checked all the boxes so far: Assembled a quality roster, recruited well, and led with confidence on the podium. Now, the real work begins. Golding will be tested this season, and Rebels fans will soon find out if he's ready to take on the challenge. The Battle of Running Backs Mississippi Rebels running back Kewan Lacy runs the ball. Mandatory Credit: Petre Thomas-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Sunday's game will pair elite running backs with Kewan Lacy and Isaac Brown. Lacy is one of the best offensive players in the country, fresh off single-season program records in rushing yards (1,567) and rushing touchdowns (24). Brown posted 884 rushing yards and seven touchdowns, but that was across eight games. He's healthy and ready to go for the season opener. This game could come down to the opposing defenses stopping the run. Ole Miss and Louisville will lean on their star running backs. If you like a good rushing attack, this game is the one for you. Ole Miss Out to Prove Last Season Wasn't a Fluke Mississippi Rebels quarterback Trinidad Chambliss. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Obviously, people believe Ole Miss is a legitimate contender, as proven by their No. 9 ranking in the AP Preseason Poll. But there are still doubts about whether the Rebels can repeat last season's success. One win may not silence the doubters, but it's a step in the right direction. Ole Miss will play one of the toughest non-conference opponents in the country , and the Rebels can make an early statement in Golding's first regular-season game. Ole Miss doesn't have to prove to anyone that this team can become a CFP contender, but that's what the media is watching for in Sunday's game. articles.title: BREAKING: Georgia Bulldogs Announce Striping of Sanford Stadium for Game with Oklahoma Sooners on September 26
articles.excerpt: Kirby Smart's Georgia Bulldogs will will “Stripe Sanford” for the game against the Oklahoma Sooners on September 26th in Sanford Stadium Between the Hedges.
articles.source_type: Gameweek squads, team news round-ups, deadline reminders
articles.body: BREAKING: Georgia Bulldogs Announce Striping of Sanford Stadium for Game with Oklahoma Sooners on September 26 Georgia fans cheer at Sanford Stadium in Athens, Ga | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect ATHENS - The Georgia Bulldogs announced Wednesday that the school would â Stripe Sanford â for the game against the Oklahoma Sooners on September 26th. It isnât the first time UGA has used fans to create a special atmosphere for a game. Georgia fans organically called to â Stripe Sanford â a season ago against Lane Kiffinâs Ole Miss - a wild 43-35 win over the Rebels in October. But the beginning of the modern shading of Sanford Stadium was when former coach Mark Richt called for a so-called Blackout against Auburn in 2007 . Unbeknownst to players and fans alike, Richt had not just called for the Blackout, but he had also ordered special black jerseys from Nike - having them on hand if the opportunity presented itself to use them. The sold out Sanford Stadium crowd was dressed in all black, as requested when the Bulldogs warmed up in their traditional red tops and classic Silver Britches. After the team piled into the locker room and pre-game speeches ended, the Bulldogsâ managers turned off the lights in and a minute later when they came back on, players saw black jerseys in front of them. The locker room frantically slipped on the black tops while the Sanford Stadium crowd awaited them taking the field. The crowd erupted as the Dawgs ran Between the Hedges for the first time in black tops. Georgia then used the fourth quarter to stomp out the Tigers - leading to the Blackout being a legendary event in Georgia lore. Meanwhile, the Bulldogs announced earlier this season that the program will wear all white next weekend against Western Kentucky. It is the first time in modern history the Bulldogs have ever worn white helmets in a game. The white uniforms have been used in recruiting photoshoots for years by Smart and his staff. articles.source_type: Gameweek squads, team news round-ups, deadline reminders
articles.body: Bengals Edge Rusher Returns to Practice Following Month-Long Injury Cincinnati Bengals defensive end Shemar Stewart (94) is assisted off the field with an injury during the first day of Cincinnati Bengals training camp at the Paycor Stadium practice facility in downtown Cincinnati on Wednesday, July 29, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Shemar Stewart is back at practice for the Bengals ESPN's Ben Baby noted his return to the field as he continues to recover from a knee hyperextension that the second-year player suffered during the opening week of training camp. Bengals head coach Zac Taylor stated then the injury would take several weeks to heal. He now returns after a little over a month away with a bevy of practices to get under his belt and ready for the season opener against Tampa Bay. "He fortunately avoided major injury," Taylor said in July. "He hyperextended his knee; it will be several weeks. It's hard to pinpoint exactly how much of training camp that will be." The injury took place on Stewartâs second rep of team drills during that rough day. Stewart got mixed up with now-released backup offensive lineman Cody Ford as the Texas A&M product fell to the ground. The left knee went awry on him, but he was in full pads on Wednesday and doing normal drills. "Very fortunate, because it obviously looked bad. The good news is we'll be getting him back sooner rather than later," Taylor said. Both Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins still aren't practicing as Cincinnati has one more practice tomorrow before a few days off ahead of Week 1. Taylor is ready to see what his team can do at the beginning of the season. He noted Stewart would be on the rehab field this week, but he's already making great progress on that front. "Well, I think we put in really good work. I feel good about that part of it," Taylor said about training camp. "That won't mean anything beyond this first game. We've got to go out there and have a great plan, and we got to understand the plan, and we got to be able to execute it. We've got to be able to put guys in positions to make the plays, because nobody's going to care after this first game how training camp went. We just got to put ourselves in position to win. "So, I feel like we covered a lot of the things that that we set out to cover. So we checked those boxes. Now we've got to check the right (game boxes). Do we have a great plan in place, and are we putting our guys in a position to go execute it, so that we can start 1-0?" articles.title: Blue Jays Put Their Playoff Hopes in Dylan Cease's Hands
articles.excerpt: A clash with the Cleveland Guardians tonight looms large for Dylan Cease for multiple reasons.
articles.source_type: Gameweek squads, team news round-ups, deadline reminders
articles.body: Blue Jays Put Their Playoff Hopes in Dylan Cease's Hands Toronto Blue Jays ace Dylan Cease. Credit: John E. Sokolowski-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect After watching Cleveland Guardians righty Gavin Williams stymie the Toronto Blue Jays to the tune of no earned runs, two hits and 13 strikeouts over seven innings of a 6-1 Cleveland victory, Dylan Cease will now seek a similarly dominant performance on Wednesday night. The Blue Jays' playoff chances and his own Cy Young hopes may depend on it. Cease has been the anchor of Toronto's rotation throughout his first season with the club. But now, amidst a critical series against the team they are chasing in the wild card race, they desperately need him to rise to the occasion once more. bullpen day kept the Blue Jays afloat for most of Tuesday's series opener, as Spencer Miles, Ricky Tiedemann and Spencer Arrighetti combined to hold the Guardians to two runs over 5.2 innings before the doors blew open on Joe Mantiply and Michael Lorenzen. However, Toronto continues to barely get by on a rotation that currently features Cease, JosÃ© Soriano, a 42-year-old Max Scherzer and two bullpen days. Blue Jays Need Cease to Come Through Toronto Blue Jays ace Dylan Cease. Credit: John E. Sokolowski-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect In other words, the Blue Jays need Cease to come through every time through the rotation, but never more than Wednesday's outing vs. Cleveland. A loss tonight would put Toronto 3.5 games back in the race for the third wild card spot, with Soriano, Scherzer and plenty of uncertainty to come. Fortunately, Cease is playing some of his best baseball across what has been an incredibly successful 2026 campaign. The 30-year-old, who is sporting a 9-5 record on the season with a 2.33 ERA and a league-best 217 strikeouts, has gone at least six innings while surrendering fewer than three runs and tallying at least eight strikeouts in each of his past three starts. While the Blue Jays likely weren't envisioning Cease to be this critical to the team's postseason chances late in the season, it's ultimately big moments like this that landed the Milton, Georgia native his seven-year, $210 million contract last winter. Cease's Start Looms Large in AL Cy Young Race Toronto Blue Jays starting pitcher Dylan Cease. Credit: Kamil Krzaczynski-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect If you ask Cease, he would likely tell you that the playoff race is the only one that matters over the final month of the season. But winning his first career Cy Young trophy probably wouldn't hurt, either. Cease is currently seen as being neck-and-neck with Cam Schlittler of the New York Yankees in the AL Cy Young race . Schlitter owns the edge in ERA, WHIP and WAR, but trails in strikeouts and carries some question marks related to his viability down the stretch. His production dipped last season in the final month after a sensational August and he may not see as many opportunities to bolster his candidacy in the season's final games as the Yankees look to get their ace playoff-ready. Needless to say, a standout Cease performance in a key playoff positioning battle could make things very interesting when it comes to the Cy Young. Every game counts the same in the standings across a 162-game season. But with the Blue Jays' ace on the hill and lots on the line, this one is feeling just a little more important. articles.title: Miami Marlins at Kansas City Royals prediction, pick for Wednesday 9/2/26
articles.excerpt: Griffin Wong gives you a preview, prediction and pick for tonight's game between the Miami Marlins and the Kansas City Royals. The post Miami Marlins at Kansas City Royals prediction, pick for Wednesday 9/2/26 appeared first on DraftKings Network .
articles.source_type: Captain picks ranked with reasoning, gameweek rankings, DFS targets
articles.body: Miami Marlins at Kansas City Royals prediction, pick for Wednesday 9/2/26 Realistically, the NL Wild Card race is down to five teams, as in addition to the Philadelphia Phillies and Chicago Cubs (who have effectively secured their spots in the postseason), the San Diego Padres, Arizona Diamondbacks, and Miami Marlins all have at least a one-in-30 chance of ultimately qualifying for the tournament. Miami, in last among the five contending teams, needs to make a run to improve its playoff odds, and it’s off to a good start, beating the hot Kansas City Royals last night in the opener of a three-game set. The middle game of the series is set for tonight at 7:40 p.m. ET. Eury Pérez will take the mound for the Marlins, and Noah Cameron will start for the Royals. Let’s break down this potential pitcher’s duel with some odds and lines DraftKings Sportsbook Miami Marlins at Kansas City Royals Best Bets Miami Marlins Moneyline (-105) This is about as much of a toss-up as it gets, but Miami has won three of Pérez’s last four starts, and I think it has the better overall roster. Under 9 (-115) I’ll also take the under out of respect for Cameron, who’s recorded a sub-2 ERA across his last seven starts, and Kansas City’s bullpen, one of the worst units in baseball, is trending in the right direction. Miami Marlins at Kansas City Royals prediction, preview If Miami ultimately misses the postseason, it’ll come down to the franchise record 12-game losing streak that the Marlins went on between July 10 and July 26, taking them from 10 games over .500 to two games under. Although they’ve bounced back somewhat since then, going 14-14 since the start of August, it might well be too little, too late. Miami had baseball’s sixth-worst offense in August, as trading away catcher Liam Hicks at the trade deadline has proven costly, especially since All-Star Otto Lopez has posted a sub-600 OPS since the Midsummer Classic. However, the Marlins have made up for it somewhat with their pitching; although their bullpen has struggled in the last several weeks, sporting a 4.83 ERA to start the second half of the season, their starters have recorded a sub-3 mark. Pérez, Ryan Gusto, Max Meyer, Sandy Alcantara, and Tyler Phillips all have a sub-4 ERA and at least 14 starts, with Alcantara — the league leader in innings pitched — plausibly in line to receive Cy Young Award votes after winning the award in 2022 if Miami sneaks into the playoffs. The Marlins’ reworked bullpen hasn’t been great, as Cade Gibson (who has a 5.67 ERA) has probably thrown too many innings for his quality, but trade deadline acquisition Victor Vodnik has shown some flashes. In all likelihood, Kansas City’s run will be too little, too late. The Royals fell to 49-73 in mid-August, but they went on a run of 13 wins in 15 games before dropping two in a row. While Kansas City still trails the final Wild Card spot by 8.5 games, it’s a team nobody will want to face right now, given that it finished August with the fifth-highest OPS. Bobby Witt Jr. leads the American League in WAR, Jac Caglianone has made a second-year leap (including a .333/.361/.574 slash line since the All-Star break), and utilityman Tyler Tolbert has quietly maintained an OPS over .800. The Royals have also had an above-average pitching staff to start the second half of the season, as both their rotation and their bullpen have improved by more than 0.7 runs of ERA from the first half of the season to the second. Cameron, Michael Wacha, and Randy Dobnak have been a capable top three, and Nate Pearson and José Cuas have stabilized what had been arguably baseball’s shakiest bullpen. That’s not to mention 38-year-old Craig Kimbrel, who is now playing for his third team in 2026 alone and the 12th of his career, recording 6.1 scoreless innings across six appearances. RELATED MLB Betting Splits and Odds for Wednesday, September 2 Pérez can be inconsistent from start to start, but he’s a pretty good pitcher overall. He struggled in his most recent start, giving up five runs in three innings against the Washington Nationals on August 28, but that ended a 13-start stretch in which he’d allowed one or fewer earned runs 10 times and pitched to a 1.67 ERA. Overall, Pérez ranks in the 66th percentile in expected ERA and the 76th in pitching run value. He’s especially thrived at fooling batters, ranking in the top three deciles in chase, whiff, and strikeout rate, which could present Kansas City’s contact-oriented lineup with more problems than usual. Plus, the Royals aren’t well-suited to take advantage of his biggest weakness, his 23rd-percentile walk rate, as they’ve drawn the fifth-fewest free passes. He has been prone to the occasional hard contact, ranking in the 19th percentile in barrel rate and the 44th percentile in hard-hit rate, and Kansas City ranks third in the latter stat, but I still trust his track record overall. He should be in line for a solid outing, although he’ll have to buck negative location splits, as his ERA is more than a run higher on the road and the Royals have had baseball’s seventh-best road offense this season. Cameron has had a similarly hot second half of the season. Although he gave up seven earned runs in his first start after the All-Star break, he has settled in remarkably well, pitching to a 1.29 ERA across his last seven starts and emerging entirely without damage in four of them. That stretch also included a one-hit shutout on August 16. Advanced numbers suggest that Cameron’s true ability lies somewhere in between his recent form and his mediocre first half of the season, as he owns a 44th-percentile xERA (4.12). To be fair, Cameron only ranks above the league median in two Statcast categories (whiff rate and walk rate), and Miami both earns free passes and whiffs at about a league-average rate. However, Cameron also doesn’t have many notable weaknesses, as he ranks in the 35th percentile or higher in every single Statcast category, and the Marlins aren’t well-suited to take advantage of his struggles to keep the ball down. Like Pérez, he’ll have to overcome unfavorable location splits, as his ERA is more than a full run higher at home. Miami Marlins at Kansas City Royals pick, best bet Best Bet: Miami Marlins Moneyline (-105) As strong as Cameron’s form has been as of late, I just trust Pérez a little bit more, and Miami is a slightly better team overall. Plus, as bad as the Marlins’ bullpen has been, Kansas City’s relievers are no better. Strong Lean: Under 9 (-115) Neither of these offenses inspires quite enough confidence to suggest that the game will go over the total, especially given both pitchers’ strong overall form. The Royals are capable of 13-run outbursts like they put up against the Toronto Blue Jays on August 27, but they’re equally capable of quiet nights, and Miami hasn’t scored more than six runs in a game since August 16. articles.title: How Browns Coach Todd Monken Is Wiping Slate Clean With Deshaun Watson
articles.excerpt: Browns head coach Todd Monken told reporters on Tuesday that he has yet to watch Deshaun Watson's Browns tenure on film
articles.source_type: Gameweek squads, team news round-ups, deadline reminders
articles.body: How Browns Coach Todd Monken Is Wiping Slate Clean With Deshaun Watson Aug 27, 2026; Cleveland, Ohio, USA; Cleveland Browns head coach Todd Monken is seen against the New England Patriots during the second half at Huntington Bank Field. Mandatory Credit: Ken Blaze-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Todd Monken and the Cleveland Browns are looking to start fresh in 2026 as preparation ramps up for week one against the Jacksonville Jaguars. As practice picks up and preparation begins, first-year head coach Todd Monken is wiping the slate clean for quarterback Deshaun Watson . Monken spoke to reporters on Tuesday after practice, stating: "I try to take everything at face value," Monken told reporters that he has not watched any film from Deshaun Watson's tenure in Cleveland despite naming him the starting quarterback just one week ago. Instead, Monken has used preseason matchups and training camp to evaluate his starting quarterback. Todd Monken went on to say, "I want to go into it thinking every player we have is elite." Deshaun Watson, whom the Browns acquired in a massive deal in 2022, has had a rocky tenure, to say the least. Watson missed all of last season with a torn Achilles and has yet to play more than eight games in a single season with the Browns. In 19 games, Watson has thrown for 3,365 yards, 19 touchdowns, and 12 interceptions. Despite Deshaun Watson's rough start to his tenure in Cleveland, Monken is confident he can get the most out of Watson, who was once considered to be a favorite for the MVP Award. "I'm confident in Deshaun and our ability to push the ball down the field," Monken told reporters on Tuesday. Monken has a long history with coaching quarterbacks, most notably Lamar Jackson, who won the MVP Award in 2023 when Todd Monken was the team's offensive coordinator. With the fan base already in an uproar, Todd Monken is making the ultimate gamble by sticking to his guns. Monken has drawn widespread criticism for his decision to name Deshaun Watson as the starter over Shedeur Sanders, who came in for the Browns last season. Sanders was largely thought to be the favorite for the job, but Monken went with the veteran instead, stating, "Deshaun gave us the best chance to move the ball and score points." Deshaun Watson completed 16-of-27 passes for 162 yards and 1 interception in the 2026 preseason. When asked if he was bothered by the fans' reaction to the decision, Monken told reporters, "Absolutely not... that has nothing to do with my decision." articles.title: The Anatomy of How the Rams Built Their 2026 Roster
articles.excerpt: Breaking down how the Rams constructed their 2026 roster through the draft, trades, free agency, undrafted players and development.
articles.source_type: Gameweek squads, team news round-ups, deadline reminders
articles.body: The Anatomy of How the Rams Built Their 2026 Roster May 28, 2025; Woodland Hills, CA, USA; Los Angeles Rams quarterback Matt Stafford (9) gives the play to running back Karen Williams (23) in the huddle during organized team activities at Rams Practice Facility. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Los Angeles Rams officially got their roster down to 53 players following the preseason . With the Rams finalizing their initial roster, it seemed like a good time to look at how they got here. Throughout the Les Snead and Sean McVay era, the Rams have built an âF Them Picksâ reputation, but the roster construction tells a much different story. The Rams have built cohesiveness with their core group of players and added stars around that. Letâs take a look at the anatomy of the Ramsâ 2026 roster.Â The Anatomy of the #Rams 2026 roster: QB Matthew Stafford - TRADE QB Stetson Bennett - DRAFT QB Ty Simpson - DRAFT RB Kyren Williams - DRAFT RB Blake Corum - DRAFT RB Ronnie Rivers - FA WR Puka Nacua - DRAFT WR Davante Adams - FA WR Konata Mumpfield - DRAFT WR Jordan Whittingtonâ¦ â JAKE OLIVER ELLENBOGEN (@JKBOGEN) August 31, 2026 Draftees (26) - The Draft Remains the Foundation of the Ramsâ Roster DT Aaron Donald (1st Round, 2014) TE Tyler Higbee (4th Round, 2016) WR Tutu Atwell (2nd Round, 2021) RB Kyren Williams (5th Round, 2022) S Quentin lake (6th Round, 2022) LG Steve Avila (2nd Round, 2023) EDGE Byron Young (3rd Round, 2023) DT Kobie Turner (3rd Round, 2023) QB Stetson Bennett (4th Round, 2023) RT Warren McClendon (5th Round, 2023) TE Davis Allen (5th Round, 2023) WR Puka Nacua (5th Round, 2023) P Ethan Evans (7th Round, 2023) EDGE Desjuan Johnson (7th Round, 2023) DT Braden Fiske (2nd Round, 2024) RB Blake Corum (3rd Round, 2024) S Kam Kinchens (3rd Round, 2024) DT Tyler Davis (6th Round, 2024) WR Jordan Whittington (6th Round, 2024) iOL Beaux Limmer (6th Round, 2024) TE Terrance Ferguson (2nd Round, 2025) EDGE Josaiah Stewart (3rd Round, 2025) DT Ty Hamilton (4th Round, 2025) WR Konata Mumpfield (7th Round, 2025) QB Ty Simpson (1st Round, 2026) TE Max Klare (2nd Round, 2026) WR CJ Daniels (6th Round, 2026) While the Rams have a reputation for buying and trading for a lot of their players, not enough gets said about how well they develop talent. Despite trading away draft picks, over half of their roster is made up of players theyâve drafted. Out of those 26 players, 13 are starters or key role players.Â Looking at this list, itâs also easy to see why the 2023 draft class is an all-timer. There is a serious argument to be made that it is the best draft class in franchise history. When the Rams collapsed due to injury in 2022, the 2023 draft class helped their immediate turnaround. Several of these players will hit free agency this summer and the Rams will have some difficult decisions to make.Â Free Agents (11) - Free Agency Has Supplemented the Ramsâ Core S Kam Curl (2024) TE Colby Parkinson (2024) WR Davante Adams (2025) NT Poona Ford (2025) LB Nate Landman (2025) OT David Quessenberry (2025) iOL Coleman Shelton (2025) LS Joe Cardona (2026) OL Bill Murray (2026) LB Grant Stuard (2026) CB Jaylen Watson (2026) The Rams have done well with their free agent spending over the last few years. Kam Curl and Nate Landman were both low-value free agents who the Rams ended up signing to large extensions once their initial deals expired. Poona Ford and Colby Parkinson have also become key contributors on their respective sides of the ball. Coleman Shelton was a player the Rams brought back to add some stability to the center position.Â One thing that is worth noting with the Ramsâ free agents is that none of them are necessarily a âcoreâ building block. The Rams arenât building through free agency. Yes, Adams is an important piece of the offense, but the best player at that position group is someone the Rams drafted in Puka Nacua. Watson will be an important piece of the secondary , but the Rams are relying on Trent McDuffie and Quentin Lake, two players the Rams invested draft capital in.Â College Free Agents (7) - The Rams Continue to Find Talent After the Draft OT Alaric Jackson (2021) WR Xavier Smith (2023) S Jaylen McCollough (2024) LB Omar Speights (2024) CB Josh Wallace (2024) LB Shaun Dolac (2025) EDGE Wesley Bailey (2026) This goes back to the Ramsâ ability to develop players. The fact that they were able to find their starting left tackle as an undrafted free agent is pretty remarkable . He may not be a top-tier left tackle, but he is more than serviceable. The Rams were able to move on from Ernest Jones because of their confidence in Omar Speights.Â The Rams have at least one undrafted free agent on the roster from five of the past six seasons. Jaylen McCollough plays an important role as the dime linebacker and Wallace is important depth in the secondary. Wesley Bailey is the Ramsâ latest find. In Week 2 of the preseason, he became one of five players since 2023 to have 10 or more pressures in a preseason game.Â Trades/Waivers (5) - Trades Add Star Power to the Ramsâ Homegrown Core QB Matthew Stafford (Trade, 2021) RG Kevin Dotson (Trade, 2023) CB Emmanuel Forbes (Waivers, 2024) EDGE Myles Garrett (Trade, 2026) CB Trent McDuffie (Trade, 2026) Where Les Snead has done some of his best work is on the trade market. There is no doubt that Matthew Stafford was a big reason for the Rams winning the Super Bowl in 2021. Acquiring Kevin Dotson for a fourth-round pick was a key trade in re-building the offensive line. The Rams will hope that the Garrett and McDuffie trades are just as instrumental in a potential Super Bowl this season. While Forbes has shown some inconsistencies, heâs shown he can be a solid depth piece when needed.Â Practice Squad (3) - Practice-Squad Additions Round Out the Roster OL Dylan McMahon (2025) K Harrison Mevis (2025) RB Ronnie Rivers (2025) Another testament to the Ramsâ development and coaching is the presence of players on the roster who came through the practice squad. McMahon is a player the Rams signed from the Philadelphia Eaglesâ practice squad. As Justin Dedich recovers from an injury, McMahon will take his place. After struggling at the kicker position last year, the Rams signed Mevis and heâs added much needed stability. Some will disagree with the Rams keeping Ronnie Rivers, but the Rams trust him and heâs a solid special teams contributor.Â Sign up for our Facebook , and Instagram for the latest news. articles.body: Detroit Lions Provide Clarity About Brian Branch, Sam LaPorta Extensions Detroit Lions safety Brian Branch (32) walks off the field after practice during training camp | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect The Detroit Lions clearly prioritized securing running back Jahmyr Gibbs and making sure he was among the highest-paid at his position. Now that the speedy offensive weapon secured a lucrative, long-term contract extension, both Brian Branch and Sam LaPorta are next up to hopefully sign new deals. One factor that general manager Brad Holmes must be constantly aware of is the health status of both players. Branch and LaPorta both had significant injuries last year, likely forcing the team to take a more cautious approach. Speaking with local reporters before the start of the 2026 season, Holmes discussed where things currently stand, 11 days before the team takes the field against the New Orleans Saints at Ford Field. Additional Detroit Lions NFL Insider Analysis: 7 Winners, 8 Losers From 2026 Initial 53-Man Roster "So, starting with Gibbs, all of them are unique, especially when it gets up to that magnitude from a financial standpoint. And it was just unique that both of those guys were kind of happening at the same time," said Holmes. "So, it was just more of kind of just being patient. We already knew what we wanted to do and you just had to see who was going to get done first and you got to kind of adjust and pivot off of that. But, we still wanted those other two, we still want to keep those guys around. Those plans hadn't changed," Holmes continued. "There's a couple of factors that we still got to sort through, but in terms of us wanting those guys around, absolutely. Hopefully we can get that done.â LaPorta figures to be among the Lions' top offensive weapons this upcoming season. There is a growing excitement the former second-round pick will shine in Drew Petzing's offense. Unfortunately, Branch suffered a torn Achilles against the Dallas Cowboys, likely pushing back his 2026 debut until the middle of the season. The team was able to sign Chuck Clark and Avonte Maddox returned after a productive 2025 season. articles.body: Tottenham transfer news: Richarlison 'reaches agreement' over Spurs exit after failed Everton move - Sports Mole Menu Loading... Tottenham transfer news: Richarlison 'reaches agreement' over Spurs exit after failed Everton move Ben Sully 02 Sep 2026 19:10 Â© Imago / Every Second Media Tottenham Hotspur striker Richarlison has reportedly reached an agreement over personal terms with Turkish side Trabzonspor Richarlison was linked with a return to Everton in the closing stages of the English transfer window after Roberto De Zerbi revealed the Brazilian forward had asked to leave the club. The 29-year-old addressed his uncertain situation on Sunday, insisting that only he would decide the next steps of his career while revealing his willingness to return to Everton before the transfer deadline. However, a move to Hill Dickinson Stadium ultimately failed to materialise, but Richarlison still appears keen to leave Spurs in the near future. © Iconsport / Action Plus Richarlison gives green light to Trabzonspor According to transfer expert Fabrizio Romano , Richarlison has agreed personal terms with Turkish Super Lig outfit Trabzonspor. The Tottenham man has been offered a lucrative salary that is worth more than three times what he currently earns in north London. Trabzonspor have made Richarlison have priority target for the closing stages of the Turkish transfer window, which will close on Friday, September 4. Despite receiving the green light from Richarlison, Trabzonspor still have significant work to do to prise him away from Roberto De Zerbi's squad, having already failed with offers worth £15m and £20m. They are set to return to test Tottenham's resolve with an improved bid for a player who has entered the final year of his contract. A move to Trabzonspor would see Richarlison play alongside his compatriot Fabinho and another former Liverpool star in Mohamed Salah. © Imago / Mark Pain Should Spurs sanction Richarlison's exit? Richarlison has fallen down the pecking order following Omar Marmoush's arrival from Manchester City. However, Spurs could be left light in the centre-forward position if they allow Richarlison to join Trabzonspor. An exit would leave De Zerbi with Marmoush and Dominic Solanke as his main striker options, the latter of whom has struggled with injury issues during his time with Spurs. With that in mind, Spurs may prefer to keep Richarlison as cover until January, although they must weigh up the benefits of that decision against the cons of having a player who is keen on a departure.
