articles.body: Chelsea reach decision on signing Georginio Wijnaldum after Lamine Camara reacts to transfer collapse Former Liverpool star Georginio Wijnaldum, According to reports, Chelsea have decided whether to sign former Liverpool star Georginio Wijnaldum after missing out on Lamine Camara. Chelsea had a rollercoaster deadline day, having ultimately sold Enzo Fernandez to Manchester City for £125m without signing a replacement. It was widely reported ahead of deadline day that the Blues would open the door to selling Fernandez if they could acquire a replacement, though they opted to agree the midfielder’s sale before it emerged that they could sign Camara. For most of deadline day, it was reported that moves for Chelsea’s leading targets, AS Monaco’s Camara and AS Roma’s Manu Kone, were off the table. However, Monaco changed their mind on selling Camara after Folarin Balogun’s proposed move to Everton hit a snag due to a medical issue. MEDIAWATCH: Enzo Fernandez already causing trouble at Man City as ‘first request denied’ after £125m deadline day move Monaco needed a big-money sale to balance the books and they reached an agreement with Chelsea to let Camara leave, though they dramatically pulled the plug at the eleventh hour after Balogun’s move to Everton once again edged closer to completion. Ultimately, though, neither player left the French side on deadline day. It has since been reported that Chelsea are understandably furious at Monaco’s decision, and this has led to them being linked with veteran midfielder Wijnaldum as an alternative. Chelsea reach decision on whether to sign Georginio Wijnaldum The 35-year-old is a free agent after departing Saudi Pro League side Al-Ettifaq, so he is a player who could join Chelsea outside of the transfer window. Romano reveals how close Chelsea came to Kone deal as ‘mystery player’ is unmasked On Wednesday afternoon, journalist Santi Aouna claimed that Chelsea have made ‘contact’ about signing Wijnaldum. Aouna said on X: ‘Looking for a midfielder, Chelsea has contacted Georginio Wijnaldum in the past few hours, who is a free agent.’ However, Fabrizio Romano has since reported that the Blues will not sign Wijnaldum. Romano said on X: ‘Chelsea will not sign Georginio Wijnaldum. ‘Club currently playing down all reports about the Dutch midfielder.’ And a future move for Camara remains a possibility, w ith our colleagues at TEAMtalk reporting that he was angry at Monaco pulling the plug on his move. The report explained: ‘TEAMtalk has spoken to sources on all sides of the deal and we can confirm that Camara’s camp are ‘furious’ with Monaco’s decision – while Chelsea are also extremely unhappy with how the situation unfolded.’ READ NEXT: Lamine Camara reacts to Chelsea deadline day collapse as Liverpool, Blues told new price Chelsea Georginio Wijnaldum

Jett is scheduled to undergo surgery on September 9, at the Steadman Clinic in Vail, Colorado. three days before the first playoff race in Columbus, Ohio. Should Jett Lawrence sit out SMX to heal? Ryan Villopoto and Chad Reed discuss Jett Lawrence’s recent struggles, whether his ankle is still limiting him and if sitting out SMX could help protect his 2027 season. Jett injured his foot and ankle during a pre-season testing crash and missed the entire Monster Energy Supercross season. He returned for the first race of the Pro Motocross season at Fox Raceway in Pala, California, and finished on the podium in third after struggling, by his standards, with moto results of fourth and third. Jett won the next two Motocross Nationals at Hangtown and Thunder Valley, and continued to sweep the podium in the next six rounds. Jett struggled with pain throughout the season, which forced him to make unaccustomed mistakes. In the final two rounds of the 2026 Motocross season, he failed to stand on the overall podium for only the third and fourth times in his career. “I’ve made the decision with my team to sit out the SMX series to get my ankle back to 100 percent for the longevity of my career,” Jett said in a news release. “I suffered through the summer and did everything I could to win the outdoor championship, but my ankle hasn’t felt right since the start of the season, and it’s even worse now after Ironman. I want to do everything I can to get back to being me. The most important thing is that I get back to being pain free as I work towards next year. I appreciate the patience of my team, family and fans as I do everything I can to make that happen.” In the first three seasons of the SMX Playoffs, Jett has been the only rider to win the championship. His failure to defend the title ensures there will be a new champion. Coming off last week’s Pro Motocross championship, Hunter Lawrence has finished second to Jett in the last two editions of the SMX Playoffs, including in 2024 when he lost the title due to a tiebreaker. Ken Roczen, who won the 2026 Monster Energy Supercross championship, finished second to Jett in the inaugural 2023 season. I will be here every Wednesday to go over important stolen base trends so you can find more speed for your fantasy teams. Stealing a base is as much about the opposing pitcher and catcher as it is the actual base runner themself. So, being able to spot which teams and pitchers specifically are being run on most frequently will help you to figure out who can swipe some bags over the next week. Understanding who’s stealing bases is even more important this time of year because with so much of the season already gone, it’s difficult to find ways to rise up in most categories. Yet, steals often have the least volume of all the categories, so the breadth isn’t as wide and a few shrewd moves can help you earn a lot of roto points. Before we get to this week’s important trends, here is the stolen base leaderboard on the season so far. MLB Roster Expansions: What to expect from Lazaro Montes, Ethan Salas, more Eric Samulski breaks down the noteworthy September call-ups in MLB. Eric Samulski Eric Samulski Full Season Stolen Base Leaders Player Nasim Nuñez Jazz Chisholm Jr. Chandler Simpson Bobby Witt Jr. Pete Crow-Armstrong José Ramírez Fernando Tatis Jr. José Caballero Esteury Ruiz Otto Lopez There have been very few changes to this leaderboard over the past few weeks. So, I’m introducing a new, more timely one right here. Second Half Stolen Base Leaders Player Chandler Simpson Jazz Chisholm Jr. A.J. Ewing Otto Lopez CJ Abrams Jake McCarthy Esteury Ruiz Corbin Carroll Tyler Tolbert Nasim Nuñez Elly De La Cruz Otto Lopez has managed to save a bit of his value during a disastrous second half with plenty of stolen bases. Last Seven Days Stolen Base Leaders Player Jazz Chisholm Jr. Jonah Cox Jorge Mateo Javier Sanoja Chandler Simpson A.J. Ewing Otto Lopez Josh Lowe Griffin Conine Brett Bateman Heriberto Hernandez 15 Others Tied Jazz Chisholm Jr. is 8-for-9 as a base stealer over the last two weeks and is in a great position to swipe the 50 that he promised. Now he only needs 31 home runs over the next four weeks to make his 50-50 dream a reality. Acquired at the trade deadline as part of the return for Kevin Gauman, Brett Bateman has seized the starting center field job for the Blue Jays, has hit lead-off in 14 of their last 16 games, and is a willing base stealer. Stolen Base Disappointments Player Jakob Marsee Zach Neto Julio Rodríguez Luke Keaschall Gunnar Henderson Michael Harris II Shohei Ohtani Steven Kwan Ozzie Albies Francisco Lindor Mookie Betts Julio Rodríguez has just five stolen bases, six home runs, and a .210 batting average since the All-Star Break. Steven Kwan is pacing for his fewest stolen bases in a single season despite currently running a career-high .376 on-base percentage. Fantasy Baseball Stolen Base Targets Both the Red Sox and Nationals allowed 11 stolen bases over the past week, more than any other team. More than half of Boston’s came in one game last Wednesday against the Marlins where Sonny Gray started and Connor Wong caught. Gray was only on the mound for two of those stolen bases with the rest coming against a handful of relievers. He’s been poor in terms of net bases prevented and the 15 bases stolen against him this season are 10th-most among all qualified pitchers Wong has had defensive issues himself too. Anecdotally, nine of the 12 stolen bases attempted against the Red Sox over the last week came with him behind the plate. Plus, Adely Rutschman threw out the only runner they caught. Wong has had poor defensive metrics for a few years and it seems like teams are targeting him. As for the Nationals, eight of the 11 bases stolen against them came with Harry Ford catching. A former top-100 prospect who was acquired for reliever José Ferrer this past offseason, the Nationals called Ford up in mid-July and he’s been splitting reps with Keibert Ruiz behind the plate since. Defense was always considered a concern for Ford as a prospect and there were genuine questions as to whether he’d be able to stick as a catcher long term. He hasn’t quieted those concerns yet with just a 16% caught stealing rate – far worse than the 24% league average. It seems like teams will be challenging him when they play the Nationals. While it’s hard for us to target Wong or Ford as part-time catchers, still look at Josh Lowe Wade Meckler Colton Cowser Dylan Beavers, Coby Mayo (oddly enough), or Xander Bogaerts who all play against the Red Sox or Nationals over the next week if you need cheap speed. Top MLB Betting Picks for September 2: MLB Same-Game Parlays and Props 2026 Regular-Season Betting Record: 10-9-2 (-1.96 units) 2026 Regular-Season Player Props Betting Record: 11-11 (-0.28 units) The Marlins continued their stretch-run push for an NL wild-card spot with a 6-3 win in the opening salvo of this interleague series Tuesday, and the two teams will send a pair of formidable starters to the hill for the middle installment Wednesday night. Both Eury Perez and Noah Cameron have compiled a collection of impressive metrics in 2026, setting up what could be quite the pitching matchup. With the stage set, let's examine a same-game parlay and a player prop for tonight's game: Cash in on the best sportsbook promos available at the best MLB betting sites this baseball season. MLB Picks for Marlins at Royals SGP: Marlins +1.5 and Under 5.5 runs - F5 (-105 on FanDuel Sportsbook) for 1 Unit Eury Perez Over 15.5 Outs Recorded (-132 on FanDuel Sportsbook) for 1 Unit Miami Marlins at Kansas City Royals Best Bets The Marlins have exceeded expectations in manager Clayton McCullough's second season, forging a 70-69 record heading into Wednesday's game and remaining firmly in the NL wild-card race. There have been plenty of key contributors in every facet, and Perez has certainly been one on the pitching side despite the fact he carries just a 7-10 record. Perez has complemented that sub-par mark with a 3.44 ERA, 1.13 WHIP and 9.8 K/9, including an 11.3 K/9 on the road. The right-hander's Statcast metrics bear out how effective he's legitimately been, as he's pitched to a .208 xBA, .298 xwOBA and 3.70 xERA. Perez is also averaging a blistering 98.1 mph on his fastball, a 94th percentile mark. Perez has notably held left-handed hitters — which the Royals are fairly heavy on — to a .178 average and .258 wOBA overall, including .153 and .244 figures in those respective categories on the road. He's also holding the opposition to a .217 average with men on base, and he has ERAs of 4.12 or lower in all but the fourth inning this season when it comes to the first half of games. On the other side, Cameron enters Wednesday in the midst of a particularly impressive stretch of play. The left-hander has authored a 4-0 record, 1.29 ERA, 0.72 WHIP and 0.2 HR/9 across the 48.2 innings covering his last seven starts. He's given up more than two earned runs just once in that span, with that instance a perfectly acceptable four-earned-run outing on the road against the mighty Dodgers. Cameron has also pitched to a .313 xwOBA and 4.11 xERA, the latter figure just slightly above his conventional 3.98 figure. Although the southpaw has actually pitched better on the road than at home, that's largely the result of a pair of especially tough outings at Kaufmann Stadium, and he's yielded only one earned run across the 13 innings covering his last pair of home starts. Additionally, the Marlins have been a mostly underperforming bunch against lefties on the road over the last month of play with a .230 average, .293 wOBA and .087 ISO in that split. Miami is also averaging the sixth-fewest runs per first five innings per road game (2.16), which helps offset some of the trouble Cameron has occasionally had early in games. Given all the factors cited, a same-game parlay that banks on the Marlins being down by no more than one run and no more than five runs being scored in the first five frames is a consideration. Then, considering Perez has recorded at least 16 outs in 14 of 24 starts — and that all but two of the 10 occasions in which he hasn't were before June 1 — the Over on his 15.5 pitching outs is also in play. articles.body: An intriguing Irish Champion Stakes contender and a Glorious Goodwood-winning raider - key takeouts from the Curragh gallops morning | Racing Post Free Bets next race 19:20 Hamilton FREE BETS Check out all our Offers on our Free Bets pages Log in My Bookmakers Free Bets Home Racecards Results News Racing Tips Royal Ascot Bloodstock Sport Tips Greyhounds Shop Statistics Pools Casino Ten To Follow Digital Newspaper Horse Tracker Raceday Live Cheltenham Festival Grand National Guide to Racing Digital Newspaper Horse Tracker My Bookmakers Log in Free Bets next race off next race 19:20 Hamilton FREE BETS Check out all our Offers on our Free Bets pages Log in My Bookmakers Free Bets Home Racecards Results News Racing Tips Royal Ascot Bloodstock Sport Tips Greyhounds Shop Statistics Pools Casino Ten To Follow Digital Newspaper Horse Tracker Raceday Live Cheltenham Festival Grand National Guide to Racing More Irish Champions Festival Home News Festivals Irish Champions Festival An intriguing Irish Champion Stakes contender and a Glorious Goodwood-winning raider - key takeouts from the Curragh gallops morning Hotazhell (right) leads Wyman (centre) and Green Impact in a gallop at the Curragh Credit: Patrick McCann (racingpost.com/photos) to add us to your Google preferred sources or find out more here 1 - Hotazhell raring to go Hotazhell rates a fascinating contender in the Irish Champion Stakes for the Jessica Harrington stable, and assistant trainer Kate Harrington was enthusiastic about the work the dual Group 1 winner did with stablemates Green Impact and Wyman. The Too Darn Hot colt won the Futurity Trophy on heavy as a two-year-old when he beat Delacroix, and the Harrington team are hoping plenty of rain falls in the next week. Harrington is also eyeing the Ascot Champion Stakes after Leopardstown, while stablemate Green Impact is set for the Kilternan Stakes. Classic-winning heroine returns to spearhead powerful Joseph O'Brien team for Irish Champions Festival "We're delighted with Hotazhell, he's come out of his last run in Germany really well," she said. "We couldn't be happier with him and we're delighted with his work today. Shane [Foley] was over the moon with him. We wouldn't be saying no to any bit of rain that falls between now and then." She added: " Green Impact had a lovely run the last day. He's won three at Leopardstown and was just touched off last time, he seems to really like the track. That was his first time over a mile and a half bar the Irish Derby last year and he saw it out really well. Looking at the entries, it's more like a Group 1 than a Group 3." Sparan Nua (far side) goes down narrowly to Kalpana in the Yorkshire Oaks Credit: Edward Whitaker (racingpost.com/photos) 2 - Bolger hoping Sparan Nua can be the star of the show next year It has been 40 years since Jim Bolger saddled Park Express to win the first of the legendary trainer's two Irish Champion Stakes and while Sparan Nua will not be in the line-up this year, Bolger is hoping the filly may be in 12 months' time. Sparan Nua was just touched off in the Yorkshire Oaks last time and is engaged in the Qatar Prix Vermeille this weekend, but Admired Beauty could represent Bolger at the festival in the Ingabelle Stakes. "Sparan Nua won't go," he said. "I don't want to pitch her in this year against the colts but I'd expect she'll line up in the Champion Stakes next year, please God." 3 - Murtagh could have another big festival It's worth paying attention to what Johnny Murtagh saddles at Leopardstown and the Curragh as he came out of last year's festival with three winners. Shaool and Rahmi will return in a bid to follow up their victories last year, while Galway maiden winner Sindagan is an intriguing handicap debutant. "We have a few chances who had a nice gallop this morning," said Murtagh. "Sindagan runs in the Sovereign Path. It's going to be tough for a three-year-old but he could be just a bit better than a handicapper. We've been waiting on a cut in the ground for Chicago Pope "Shaool is in a couple of races and I think she could run in the Blandford. She won the handicap last year and won the Listed race at Leopardstown. I'm thinking she could be another Barnavara and rock up here before going on to France. She loves soft ground. Rahmi and Retracement are back. Asakir is running in the Kilternan and he's been waiting for soft ground." Dr Rascal (nearest): set for the National Stakes Credit: Edward Whitaker (racingpost.com/photos) 4 - Strong British challenge and red-hot Kilternan Oliver Cole joined via Zoom and was extremely sweet on the unbeaten Dr Rascal 's chances in the Group 1 National Stakes, while Charlie Johnston is also set to send over a fascinating team. Pikachu could run in the Golden Fleece, while Johnston says the Blandford has been the main target for Jennifer Jane since she landed the Prix Chloe at Chantilly in July. Timeforshowcasing is also a possible runner but may wait for the Opera on Arc weekend. However, the most intriguing prospect is perhaps Ancient Egypt . articles.body: Tottenham: Romano reveals Richarlison transfer 'agreement' details as Spurs react to £20m 'offer' Fabrizio Romano has brought the latest Spurs transfer news. Fabrizio Romano has revealed details of Richarlison’s proposed move from Tottenham Hotspur to Trabzonspor, with an ‘agreement’ struck. Richarlison is stuck in limbo at Tottenham after the English transfer window shut on Tuesday night. The forward is down the pecking order at Tottenham after they overhauled their attack with the signings of Omar Marmoush, Savio and Mykhaylo Mudryk. In the final few days of the transfer window, Tottenham tried to offload Richarlison to Everton as part of a deal for Iliman Ndiaye, but this did not go through. Spurs reached an agreement with Everton, but the double deal collapsed after Richarlison reportedly could not reach terms with his former club. Thankfully for Richarlison, the transfer window in Turkey does not close until Friday night, and he is attracting interest from Trabzonspor. READ: Premier League transfer window winners: Brentford, Maresca, De Zerbi, Chelsea On Wednesday afternoon, Turkish reporter Yagız Sabuncuoglu reported that Tottenham have received an ‘offer’ from Trabzonspor for Richarlison. He has also stated that Richarlison is pushing for the move and has a ‘verbal agreement’. He said on X: ‘EXCLUSIVE | Trabzonspor has made an offer to Tottenham for Richarlison. The player is warm to the offer but there is no agreement with Tottenham yet. Contacts continue! He later added on X: ‘Richarlison has verbally agreed with Trabzonspor! ‘The Brazilian player wants to join Trabzonspor and is pressuring his club to accept the offer! Richarlison wants to leave Tottenham.’ However, a report from The Athletic t hen stated that Trabzonspor have made a ‘failed effort’ to sign Richarlison in the past 24 hours. Tottenham received deadline day enquiries for 84-game star as Spurs allowed £25m exit They explained: ‘Turkish Super Lig side Trabzonspor have made an unsuccessful attempt to sign Richarlison in the past 24 hours. ‘After their failed effort, it is not clear whether Trabzonspor will make a further attempt to bring in the 29-year-old. While the transfer deadline in England has passed, Turkish clubs are able to buy players until Friday, September 4.’ Fabrizio Romano reveals huge Richarlison exit update That update did not state that a deal was off, and Romano has now provided details of Richarlison’s ‘agreement’ with Trabzonspor. Romano said on X: ‘BREAKING: Richarlison has agreed to join Trabzonspor with salary agreed, x3 more than what he currently earns at Tottenham. ‘Spurs rejected two bids worth £15m and £20m; new proposal anticipated soon. ‘Trabzonspor want Richy as priority.’ READ NEXT: The 10 biggest spenders of 2026 summer transfer window: No sign of Man Utd Tottenham Hotspur Fabrizio Romano Related Articles Lewis Oldham 02 Sep 2026 Tottenham: Richarlison reaches verbal agreement to join Turkish side, pushes Spurs to sanction exit According to reports, Tottenham Hotspur star Richarlison has a ‘verbal agreement’ to join Trabzonspor after a move to Everton collapsed. DeCosta noted today that Humphrey is heading into the final year of the five-year, $97 million contract extension he signed in 2020, and the Ravens are expecting Humphrey to play very well in a contract year — after he fell short of expectations last year. “He’s in the last year of his deal,” DeCosta said. “I would say that he’s been a historic Raven in many ways. Multi-time All-Pro, highly competitive Pro Bowler, a leader here. I think he’s gonna have a great year. Had a great year a couple years ago. Didn’t have his best — he would say, I think he has said, he didn’t have a great year last year. I feel confident he’s going to rebound and have a great year this year.” It’s rare in the NFL for a player to actually play out a full five-year contract extension the way Humphrey is going to this year. Humphrey’s cap hit this year is more than $26 million, and the Ravens could have saved most of that by cutting him. But DeCosta thinks Humphrey is going to give the Ravens their money’s worth this season. “Corners are hard to find, veteran corners who have played at a very high level are hard to find, and we’re excited to see him play this year,” DeCosta said. If Humphrey can return to All-Pro form, that would mean a lot to the Ravens’ defense — and mean a lot for the next contract he’ll sign, in 2027. articles.body: DraftKings UFC Picks & Value Plays: UFC Paris DFS Lineup Strategy | RotoWire DraftKings UFC Picks: UFC Paris DFS Preview Uncover the top DraftKings MMA DFS picks & strategy for UFC Paris on Saturday. Build winning lineups with our predictions, analysis & fighter breakdowns. September 2, 2026 Share By: Jon Litterine @JonLitterine September 2, 2026 DraftKings MMA Mock Draft Simulator Prep for your 2026 Fantasy Football draft with free, unlimited drafts, and real-time grades. UFC Paris DraftKings DFS Preview and Picks Uncover the top DraftKings MMA DFS picks & strategy for UFC Paris on Saturday. Build winning lineups with our predictions, analysis & fighter breakdowns. If you're hoping to turn the event into an opportunity to build your DFS bankroll, DraftKings.com has you covered with a full slate of contests, including a $250k UFC Throwdown with $50k to first place. Players get a $50,000 budget to select six fighters, and the scoring rules are noted at the bottom of the column. Let's get to the action... Main Event - Lightweight Dan Hooker (24-14-0) v. Salahdine Parnasse (23-2-0) DK Salaries: Hooker ($6,700), Parnasse ($9,500) Vegas Odds: Hooker (+455), Parnasse (-625) Hooker has been trending in the wrong direction for the better part of the past half-decade. He's lost two straight and six of his last ten. He doesn't have a victory via any method other than split decision dating back to November 2022. The only thing truly saving him at this point is the fact he's been facing high-end competition the entire time. At age 36, I'm not expecting any sort of significant turnaround to be forthcoming. Parnassee, who will be making his UFC debut, is one of the most decorated free agent signings for the company in recent memory. A former KSW Lightweight Champion and two-time KSW Featherweight Champion, Parnassee's last fight came in May -- a first-round knockout victory on the MVP card headlined by Ronda Rousey and Gina Carano. Parnassee is a legitimate all-around mixed martial artist. He excels at pressuring his opposition and making them uncomfortable. His jab is excellent and he's a terrific counter-striker. Hooker is also at his best when he's pushing forward, but unlike Parnassee, he has issues with any sort of severe volume coming back his way. Dan gets hit took much, and although he's tough as nails and it typically takes a ton to get him out of there, I don't want to be backing a 36-year-old that has been in countless wars over the years. Parnassee has seven career wins via submission. I've always been impressed with the timing of his takedown attempts. I doubt it matters here, but in a close fight down the round, I could see him attempting to steal a tight round with a single, well-timed attempt. If that's not enough, Parnassee will also firmly have the crowd behind him in his native France. His lone loss dating back to January 2021 came at welterweight. The history of these thought-to-be-elite guys coming into the UFC from other organizations has been mixed in recent years. Reinier de Ridder , for example, has had a decent amount of success. On the flip side, a guy like Patchy Mix washed out immediately. The price tag on Parnassee is way too high -- we haven't seen him at this level, plus Hooker is reckless and unpredictable -- but you know the UFC laid out a boatload of money to bring him in, and I'm certain the company booked this fight with the intention of him looking like a future star. Maybe things will work out for Parnassee over the long run, maybe they won't, but I don't think Hooker has the depth to his game to give the newcomer any real problems on his maiden voyage. This fight is a pass for me entirely from a DFS perspective. If forced to choose, I'd rather play Hooker and spread my money elsewhere. I still think Parnasse wins. Perhaps easily. UFC PARIS PICK: Parnassee Think the heavy favorite prevails and want to play the striking totals for this fight on pick'em sites? Check out the Best MMA Picks & Prop Bets by comparing actual betting lines to our projections using the RotoWire Picks & Props tool. Co-Main Event - Lightweight Fares Ziam (18-5-0) v. Axel Sola (12-1-1) DK Salaries: Ziam ($8,600), Sola ($7,600) Vegas Odds: Ziam (-150), Sola (+125) It's an all-French co-main event in what projects to be a highly competitive fight. Ziam had a six-fight winning streak snapped his last time out in June in a truly awful performance against Tom Nolan . He was a decent sized favorite that evening but simply didn't show up. It doesn't help matters than Nolan is far better than he's been given credit for previously. This is a quick turnaround given his struggles that night, although I doubt he was in any position to turn down this type of opportunity. Sola's turnaround will be even shorter than Ziam's, as he submitted Ismael Bonfim in late July. Axel has looked quite good through his three UFC fights, even though his record is only 2-1. He knocked out Rhys McKee in his company debut and put forth a highly competitive performance despite dropping a unanimous decision to Mason Jones in his lone setback. It's worth noting this is Sola's third fight since March 21. Ziam has become increasingly reliant on his grappling of late. He's landed at least three takedowns in three of his past four fights. Sadly, his loss to Nolan was largely the result of his inability to defend a takedown. I've never been particularly impressed with Ziam's get-up game, although he can be effective at times from top position. Sola's style of fighting actually reminds me a bit of Hooker's. He's the type of guy that is willing to eat a strike in order to land two of his own. Sola can wrestle a bit and is tough as nails, but at his core, he's a fighter that seeks to pressure his opposition in hopes of overwhelming them on the feet. These two have a similar size, reach, and were born within six months of each other in 1997, so I'm not sensing a significant edge for either man from a physical standpoint. I'm going with Ziam because I'm worried about Sola's reckless style and how much he's competed in such a short amount of time, but I don't think there's a $1,000 salary gap between the two. Getting Sola for $7,600 when he's only +125 on the Vegas ML seems like a pretty fair deal if you need to save money. UFC PARIS PICK: Ziam Middleweight Michael Page (25-3-0) v. Nursulton Ruziboev (37-9-2, 2NC) DK Salaries: Page ($8,700), Ruziboev ($7,600) Vegas Odds: Page (-165), Ruziboev (+140) Page doesn't quite fit into the same category as Parnasse because he was quite a bit older when he made his UFC debut back in March 2024, but his run with the company has still been quite strong. He's 4-1, with his lone setback being a competitive unanimous decision defeat against Ian Garry , who challenged for the UFC Middleweight Championship last month and put forth a strong showing despite losing to Islam Makhachev . MVP will be 40 years old in April, but he's really displayed no signs of slowing down, largely because the promotion has given him favorable matchups. This is another one. The strength of schedule in this fight favors Page in a major way. Ruziboev's 5-1 UFC mark looks great on paper, but those wins were against Andrey Pulayev, Dustin Stoltzfus Eric McConico Sedriques Dumas and Brunno Ferreira . The loss was a unanimous decision to Joaquin Buckley . I have a bit of time for Stoltzfus and Ferreira, but both those guys are several levels below anyone Page has fought in his five UFC bouts. A large part of Page's success is because he's impossible to prepare for. There's no guy on the roster that fights like him and his style can't be mimiced in sparring. He's a high-level, highly creative kickboxer. Page is deadly at distance. The prettier this fight looks, the more it favors him. Ruziboev has a hysterical 13 career wins via knockout and 21 via submission. That's what happens when you have 50 pro fights. Four of his five UFC wins are via stoppage (three knockouts, one submission), including three in Round 1. That said, I wouldn't call Ruziboev some murderous power puncher. He certainly has some thunder in his hands, but cornering and hitting Page is one of the most difficult things to do in the entire division. This is a guy that absorbs 1.51 significant strikes per minute, a laughably low number for a kickboxer. Page has been knocked out once in 28 pro fights. At 6-foot-5, Ruziboev is a huge middleweight. He can wrestle in a pinch but I don't think he'll be able to pin Page to the mat long enough to win a boring decision. The most likeliest outcome is that Page does enough damage from the outside to win a boring decision. Any Ruziboev win probably comes via knockout, and I'm not going to project anyone to track down MVP and finish him in a three-round fight. UFC PARIS PICK: Page Welterweight Daniil Donchenko (15-2-0) v. Punahele Soriano (13-4-0) DK Salaries: Donchenko ($9,000), Soriano ($7,200) Vegas Odds: Donchenko (-250), Soriano (+205) Donchenko has quietly done a nice job of raising his stock at 170 pounds over the course of his first three fights with the company. He's 3-0, with a pair of knockout wins on his ledger. Overall, Donchenko is riding a seven-fight winning streak and is without a setback dating back to October 2023. The fact Soriano is still with the company is nothing short of a minor miracle. This is a guy that lost four of five from July 2021 to December 2023. Puna would have seemed like an obvious release candidate following that stretch, but the UFC stuck with him and the soon-to-be 34-year-old has rewarded them with four straight victories. Soriano's 31-second January 2025 knockout win over Uros Medic has aged exceptionally well. Donchenko just turned 25 years of age in early August so there's a no-zero chance he could still show some improvements on a fight-by-fight basis. That said, he's essentially just a knockout artist at this point. There's very little depth to his game offensively, although to his credit, Donchenko has never been knocked out himself and his cardio is strong for a guy that likes to keep a super high pace on the feet. I expect Soriano to wrestle here for a variety of reasons. The most obvious is that you don't want to stand in front of Donchenko given his power. Puna has landed at least three takedowns in three of his last four fights and the lone one he didn't was his 31-second victory over Medic. It's a common theme on this card, but this is another fight where I like the favorite to win, but don't like the DK salary. I also disagree with the Vegas line here. I'd have Donchenko lined at perhaps -160 or thereabouts. I will say that if you're sorting through underdogs, I like Soriano more than say, Ruziboev. I'm just not sure Puna will put forth a useable DFS performance even if he wins. I could see it being very boring. Lots of takedowns and control time. If that doesn't happen, I think Donchenko wins via knockout. UFC PARIS PICK: Donchenko Other Bouts Featherweight Morgan Charriere (21-12-1) v. Felipe Lima (14-2-0) DK Salaries: Charriere ($7,300), Lima ($8,900) Vegas Odds: Charriere (+155), Lima (-185) UFC PARIS PICK: Charriere Like this UFC Paris underdog pick? See the salary relief it creates and generate up to 150 unique builds with our DraftKings UFC Lineup Optimizer Featherweight Losene Keita (16-2-0) v. Muhammadjon Naimov (13-4-0) DK Salaries: Keita ($9,200), Naimov ($7,000) Vegas Odds: Keita (-360), Naimov (+285) UFC PARIS PICK: Keita Heavyweight Mario Pinto (12-0-0) v. Ryan Spann (24-11-0) DK Salaries: Pinto ($9,100), Spann ($7,100) Vegas Odds: Pinto (-280), Spann (+225) UFC PARIS PICK: Pinto Featherweight Kurtis Campbell (8-1-0) v. articles.body: Top Free Agent Available Who Could Help Detroit Lions Right Away Indianapolis Colts cornerback Kenny Moore II (23) shoves Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Parker Washington (11) out of bounds Sunday, Dec. 28, 2025, during a game against the Jacksonville Jaguars at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect With initial 53-man rosters now officially set, several notable players find themselves unemployed. As a result, teams like the Detroit Lions have a prime opportunity to pick up a player (or two) who could contribute meaningful snaps right away. Presently, the Lions are set to open the 2026 campaign with multiple holes in the defensive backfield, including at cornerback.Â Defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard's unit currently has question marks both opposite D.J. Reed at outside cornerback and in the slot. Subsequently, it wouldn't hurt Detroit general manager Brad Holmes to add a proven, reliable corner prior to his team's season-opening contest with the New Orleans Saints. If he decides to go that route, former Indianapolis Colts cornerback Kenny Moore should be his top target. The veteran slot corner will be entering his age-31 season in 2026, but still remains productive. In fact, the 10th-year pro is coming off a year in which he amassed 55 total tackles, an interception and six passes defensed across 14 games (seven starts). And for his efforts, he earned an overall grade of 66.7 from Pro Football Focus (the 39th-best mark among 114 qualified corners). Plus, he logged an 84.4 PFF run-defense mark, the fifth-highest mark among all corners in 2025 and the second-best run-defense grade of his career.Â Additional Lions Insider Analysis: What Final Roster Says About Front Office's Vision He also recorded solid Pro Football Focus overall marks of 76.8 and 70.1 in 2023 and 2024, respectively. And on top of all that, Moore impressively compiled at least three interceptions and six passes defensed in five of his nine seasons with the Colts. Undoubtedly, the Valdosta State product has a proven track record of being a plus-defender in the secondary, with the ability to impact the game both in coverage and as a run defender. Consequently, there's no question that he would immediately upgrade the Lionsâ nickel cornerback position with his presence. He could also prove to be a valuable mentor to Detroit's younger corners, such as rookie Keith Abney II and third-year pro Ennis Rakestraw Jr. It's why I'm of the mindset that Holmes could do no wrong inking Moore to a one-year deal prior to the start of the regular season. @detroitpodcast , head on over to our Facebook TikTok, YouTube Channel for daily videos, news, member-exclusive content. Clippers were safe. Until they weren’t. In one of the most stunning examples of ESPN-on-ESPN crime on record, Shams Charania of ESPN reports that the NBA has levied unprecedented punishment on the L.A. Clippers for salary-cap circumvention in connection with Kawhi Leonard: Five first-round picks and a $30 million fine to owner Steve Ballmer. The NBA also has suspended Ballmer and others. The report comes only a few weeks after ESPN reported that the NBA has no evidence of salary-cap circumvention by the Clippers as to Leonard. The only way to harmonize the two reports is this — the NBA must have found a shitload (technical term) of evidence since August 17. It’s the harshest cap penalty ever levied, in any sport. The NFL hasn’t issued one in years (except for a “ clerical payroll error ” by the 49ers in 2024). Most recently, the NFL fined the Broncos a total of $1.918 million and stripped them of two-third round draft picks for a series of salary-cap violations in the 1990s. Before that, the NFL penalized the 49ers for a cap violation in 2000, taking a fifth-round pick in 2001 and a third-round pick in 2002; the league also fined former 49ers (then Browns) president Carmen Policy $400,000, and it fined 49ers vice-president Dwight Clark $200,000. That same year, the Steelers were fined $150,000 for a self-reported salary-cap violation. (Thanks to Team PFT for doing the research on this.) All of those examples pale in comparison to what the NBA has done to the Clippers. And it all traces to the reporting of Pablo Torre, whose efforts secured a Pulitzer Prize for Pablo Torre Finds Out . (After ESPN’s August 17 report, some were suggesting it should be rescinded.) That’s the true value of modern sports journalism. At a time when most are chasing transactional nuggets that will inevitably be announced (sometimes only minutes after the exclusive report), the best stuff to chase is the stuff they don’t want anyone to know about. But for Pablo, the Clippers’ infraction never would have been discovered. Add favorite players, teams, and leagues with an NBCUniversal Profile Continue

articles.title: EXCLUSIVE: Ricardo Gareca on coaching Peru and the 'dream' of working at Independiente
articles.source_type: Live scores, results archive, fixtures and match detail
articles.body: EXCLUSIVE: Ricardo Gareca on coaching Peru and the 'dream' of working at Independiente | Flashscore.com All Football Transfer News Premier League US Open Features Champions League Darts Snooker Golf Cycling MLB NFL Most read on Flashscore News Transfer News LIVE: Richarlison heading to Turkey, deadline approaching for Dutch clubs Man City confirm joint British record signing of Enzo Fernandez from Chelsea Swedish tennis ace collapses twice on court during Challenger event in China Aguero backs Jesus to shine at Barcelona: 'He can easily score 10 or 15 goals' EXCLUSIVE: Ricardo Gareca on coaching Peru and the 'dream' of working at Independiente Gender Vera / Ivy Pozo Ricardo Gareca on the touchline FELIPE ZANCA/PHOTOSPORT / PHOTOSPORT / PHOTOSPORT VIA AFP A World Cup coach and a legend in Peru for taking the national team to its highest ever FIFA ranking, Ricardo Gareca spoke exclusively with Flashscore about his future and his perspective on Peruvian players. After his stint as a streamer on 'La Sustancia', which he described as a very enriching experience, Gareca is now ready to return to the pitch, whether for a club or a national team. 'El Flaco' spoke with Flashscore about his time with the Peruvian national team and everything he considers key to the development of Peruvian football. Q: In '85 you scored the 2-2 goal that qualified Argentina against Peru . More than 40 years later, how do you remember that exact moment? A: "That match was very traumatic, very tough, because Peru had a great team and we were losing 2-1 for Mexico '86, with a very tense atmosphere in the stadium. "Burruchaga, from midfield, crossed the ball into the box - we were all-out attacking, you know. Passarella controlled it on his chest and crossed it with his right. Acasuzo was Peru's goalkeeper, he got his fingertips to it and the ball hit the post and rolled along the line. Then I rushed in and pushed it in. "It was very traumatic because it was the 2-2 and that draw gave us the chance to qualify for Mexico '86, that's how the whole play unfolded." You played under Menotti and Bilardo, two almost opposite football philosophies. If you had to pick one lesson from each to explain how you coach today, what would it be? "They're quite different, though similar in some ways. They differ in how they communicate, but both liked good football, playing well, you know. The thing is, one is more obsessive about details than the other; for example, Bilardo could repeat a play countless times until it came out right. "Menotti emphasised the player's confidence. He was more about communicating, talking, persuading with words; and Bilardo was very hands-on on the pitch, leaving nothing to chance: sometimes we'd repeat a corner 30 times until it worked. Menotti too, but he was more persuasive through communication and convincing the player. "They were both very important coaches, though I was more influenced by Bilardo because I was with him from the start of the Mexico '86 qualifiers to the end; with Menotti it was a short time during the Spain '82 era, when I wasn't doing well in my career, but he still gave me the chance and I really enjoyed being with him." You had a good spell at Universitario. If you had to pick one player from that time, who would it be and why? "Dony Neyra. He was a guy who started as a right-back, a defender. I saw he had a great pass and shot, a great vision of the game; so, when you have a player with such vision and shooting ability, like he had, I moved him further forward, into an attacking role. "Just as Mayer Candelo got injured, Dony took his chance. He started playing in that position and became a great provider for Hurtado and Malingas, you know, and also scored a couple of important goals, so we kept him there. You could say he was a key player for Universitario in that era." Cienciano is back in the Sudamericana quarter-finals, 23 years after that historic title. How do you feel when you see a team from the provinces competing like that internationally? "Not only are Cienciano strong at home, they also get points away; they don't just use the altitude, they know how to handle it, and away from home they've become a tough team, you know. "That makes you think it's not just the coach doing things right, but he's also got the best out of players like Hohberg, whom I know and called up myself, and now he's having a brilliant spell as the team's playmaker. The coach has given him a free '10' role and allowed him to be the creative force for Cienciano. "And on top of that, it's a team that plays compact, builds from the back, uses crosses well, etc. So, without a doubt, coach Melgarejo and his staff deserve a lot of credit. Plus, there's Christian Ruggeri, who's Oscar Ruggeri's nephew: I know how he works and I know he's a great tactical expert, so together they've made Cienciano a team that earns merit both home and away." Time with the Peruvian national team The start of the Russia 2018 campaign was tough: what didn't you change despite the pressure, and what did you have to fix? "Having worked in Peru helped me a lot. I knew Universitario and was convinced of the quality and creativity of the Peruvian player. Then we had to break down several myths that were deeply ingrained, like that Peruvian players don't run or that they have to play in the best leagues or else they can't compete... We started breaking down those myths and proved that they could. "We put cameras in every stadium. People said Peruvian players don't run, but they do - even in the toughest conditions: they run and play at over 3,000 metres altitude, play in the heat, run on artificial turf that burns your feet. "That idea that they don't run was ingrained, but we showed it was all a lie, you just had to convince the players, tell and show them they could, and that's what happened. The players started to believe, and technically, they're very good. That had to be proven internationally." During that period, from the seventh matchday, you left out established names like Pizarro, Zambrano, or Vargas, and the team took off, reaching the play-off and beating New Zealand 2-0 after 36 years without a World Cup. Of all the decisions you had to make in those seven years, was that the toughest call you made as Peru coach? "It could be. It was a complicated situation, but we had the support of then FPF president Edwin Oviedo. "That was key because we started the qualifiers badly and one day Oviedo invited me to lunch and told me I wasn't going to leave the national team, that he trusted the project and that even if we didn't qualify this time, I'd stay on for Qatar, that I should work calmly. "Oviedo wanted to break the habit of constantly changing coaches, something Peru always did, and he wanted to give continuity, to give confidence, and I quickly got the message. So he gave me the freedom to make any decision, and the first thing we did was get to know the local players better and give some guys with spectacular quality a chance. "So, to function as a team, we started bringing in several new guys and I had to leave out the established ones; but I had the president's support, even with the media pressure to get rid of me. "With Paolo, we decided to keep him because we wanted him to be the figurehead, the captain, and we backed him. We had to make some very tough decisions and that was the hardest, but the local players responded and a new priority emerged, because we never doubted that the guys gave everything on the pitch." Ricardo Gareca and Paolo Guerrero at a press conference during Copa America Brazil 2019 RAÚL ARBOLEDA / AFP / AFP / Profimedia "What we didn't like was everything beforehand, like when we arrived at camp and saw that the national team was a chance to meet up with family and friends. So the pre-match preparation wasn't what we wanted, we wanted total focus on the match, you know. "We managed to get them to focus completely on the game and that was all that mattered at that moment. We gave families a space at the hotel to visit, to see them, for the kids to come; but once the first player arrived, we locked in and didn't leave until the two qualifiers were over. "We were very focused and they understood. Then we brought in Farfan and Advincula, we added Carrillo and all of them, who later became key to qualifying. Claudio was there too, but every time he came he always had a problem or an injury. That made it impossible for him to train normally and we started betting on Raul Ruidiaz. We looked at everything and, in the end, we found a very solid group." In Russia 2018 you lost narrowly to Denmark and France , and finished with a 2-0 win over Australia . If you had to pick one match from that World Cup to explain the whole process to someone, which would you choose? "I think in all three matches we never gave up playing our game and now that you ask, we didn't deserve to lose to Denmark, because we had lots of chances. Against France we played well, but France at times outplayed us, just like Denmark, though it was back and forth because we controlled most of the match. "At no point did we stop playing, we always tried to play on equal terms, even against France, who were world champions. Australia was tough, but we ended up winning. "I think you could say it was a bit contradictory, but even though we didn't get past the group stage, we left a good impression; in terms of attitude, commitment, the way we played, and you could see Peru's style: the team had an identity and that's why the fans supported us all the way. I still feel we could have done more, but we left a good image." What were your feelings during your second spell with the national team, being runners-up at the 2019 Copa America but losing in the 2022 World Cup play-off? "It's important for people to know that Peru was around 60th in the world ranking. When you're that far from the top, you can't really compete. When you face a powerhouse, you might win or play well, but overall it's very hard to get a positive result. "What we achieved in 2017 was to be among the top 10 teams in the world, and for Qatar we kept that up. Peru was always among the top 20 in the FIFA ranking. If you're in the top 10 you can achieve anything, and if you're in the top 20 you're potentially competitive. "We managed to maintain a level that allowed us to compete with France, who were world champions; then we beat Croatia , who were World Cup runners-up; we beat Brazil , played well against Argentina too... "When you put yourself in that kind of environment, you're at a super high level and you can compete with any team, so we reached that level and became a very competitive national team." You coached more matches than any other manager in Peru's history. If you had to sum up your football philosophy in one non-negotiable idea, what would it be? And what advice would you give to Mano Menezes? "We had a very clear style, recognised by both the international and local press, and overall we had support. Then there was another part of the media that, well, was hard to convince because, I don't know... it was like they were against me traveling abroad, for example, to watch the guys playing outside Peru, they were against certain things they thought should be done differently. "The players thought the national team should give everyone a chance and I didn't give everyone a chance, we gave it to those we thought had a real shot at being in the team, because even if they played great, they had to meet important requirements like being in top physical and technical condition, because where we were going to compete were top leagues and the demands were higher. "We had our critics, who unfortunately didn't trust that much even though there were results, but they recognised how Peru played, respecting its historic style. What we tried to do was respect the way Peruvians like to play; not such a vertical game, what interested me was to bring out the creativity

articles.body: Liverpool: Late striker signing confirmed, as reason for no announcement emerges Andoni Iraola is the new Liverpool manager. Liverpool wrapped up a striker signing in the final days of the summer transfer window, though why the club haven’t officially confirmed the move can now be revealed. Liverpool sealed two late signings, though only one was announced. 18-year-old goalkeeping phenom, Lucca Brughmans, signed on the dotted line by way of Genk. Brughmans’ deal – worth roughly £30m – was officially confirmed on Liverpool’s website , and the 6ft 7in stopper will now spend the remainder of the 2026/27 season loaned back to Genk. Once his loan concludes, Brughmans will enter into a fierce battle with Giorgi Mamardashvili for the starting spot at Liverpool. Alisson Becker’s current contract expires at season’s end. But while Brughmans’ transfer was publicly confirmed, no announcement was made regarding the signing of Saint-Etienne striker, Djylian N’Guessan. The 18-year-old’s move was verified by transfer guru Fabrizio Romano on August 31 , and why Liverpool kept quiet has now emerged. N’Guessan will spend the rest of the current campaign loaned to French side Brest. However, he’s being loaned to Brest from Saint-Etienne and not from Liverpool. Why Liverpool haven’t announced Djylian N’Guessan signing revealed L’Equipe reported: ‘Young Saint-Etienne striker Djylian N’Guessan, bought by Liverpool this Tuesday, will be loaned to Brest.’ The French report went on to state: ‘Djylian N’Guessan has experienced the most intense moments of his young career. ‘The 18-year-old Saint-Étienne striker has been transferred to Liverpool. The English club intends to develop this young player, whose profile is comparable – in some ways – to Hugo Ekitike. ‘To further develop their new signing, Liverpool’s management opted for a loan. N’Guessan will be on loan at Brest until the end of the season.’ The Liverpool Echo subsequently explained the reasoning behind this unusual transfer plan, and it relates to the number of overseas loans a club can sanction. MORE LIVERPOOL COVERAGE ON F365… Ornstein hints at double Liverpool midfield deal in 2027 – ‘watch this space’ Redknapp disagrees with Neville after claim Liverpool ‘left Iraola well short’ in one area Liverpool have just received some good news about signing Lamine Camara in 2027 The Merseyside outlet reported: ‘Liverpool have agreed to sign 18-year-old striker Djylian N’Guessan from Saint-Etienne – but not until his contract expires at the end of the season. ‘N’Guessan will spend this campaign on loan at Ligue 1 side Brest with the Reds keen for him to gain further top-flight experience. ‘That, though, will be a temporary move from Saint-Etienne rather than Liverpool, with the Anfield side having filled their full allocation of foreign loan slots with Harvey Elliott’s season-long switch to Spanish outfit Valencia. ‘N’Guessan will then sign a pre-contract agreement with Liverpool in January and complete his transfer to the Reds next summer.’ Liverpool

articles.body: Chelsea transfer news: 'Contact made' with former Jordan Henderson teammate available as free agent - Sports Mole Menu Loading... Chelsea transfer news: 'Contact made' with former Jordan Henderson teammate available as free agent Darren Plant 02 Sep 2026 17:00 Â© Imago / Nexpher Images Chelsea have reportedly identified Georginio Wijnaldum as a surprise transfer target. The Blues attempted to sign a new midfielder on deadline day as they watched Enzo Fernandez finalise a £125m transfer to Manchester City However, despite having a deal in place to sign Monaco's Lamine Camara, the Ligue 1 club scrapped the agreement during the closing minutes of the transfer window. Monaco's sporting director Thiago Scuro has since explained why Chelsea did not take the Senegal international to Stamford Bridge. With Xabi Alonso having at least six midfield options at his disposal, the expectation was that he would settle for what is available to him until 2027. © Imago Chelsea chasing Wijnaldum signing? Instead, according to Foot Mercato , the Spaniard is open to adding Wijnaldum to his squad. The former Netherlands international is available on a free transfer after leaving Saudi Pro League club Al Ettifaq. Despite now being 35 years of age, Wijnaldum contributed an incredible 38 goals and 17 assists in 101 appearances across all competitions. He is best known for his time at Liverpool - when new Chelsea signing Jordan Henderson was a teammate - where he lifted a Premier League title and Champions League crown during his stay. Chelsea would presumably view Wijnaldum as a short-term option for the season, while the assumption is that the player would be interested in making the move to West London. © Imago / Every Second Media Are there any negatives to Chelsea signing Wijnaldum? Moises Caicedo, Reece James, Romeo Lavia, Henderson, Malo Gusto and Valentin Barco are viewed as Chelsea's six midfield options. The argument for signing Wijnaldum is that those half-a-dozen players do not offer the same goal threat as he can. Age is most certainly a factor. Alonso would not be able to give Henderson and Wijnaldum the platform to reignite their successful Liverpool partnership. At the same time, if Wijnaldum is prepared to sign a one-year contract and accept a backup role, there are minimal negatives to a deal taking him to the capital. articles.body: Steve Ballmer suspended one year, Clippers to lose 5 first-round picks in Kawhi Leonard endorsement scandal - NBC Sports Skip navigation MLB NFL NBA NHL Premier League NASCAR College Football Men’s College Basketball Player News NFL Player News NBA Player News MLB Player News Scores NFL Scores NBA Scores MLB Scores MLB NFL NBA NHL Premier League NASCAR College Football Men’s College Basketball Player News NFL Player News NBA Player News MLB Player News Scores NFL Scores NBA Scores MLB Scores Login Favorites Sign up to follow your favorites on all your devices. Sign up Odds by Schedule Scores Player News ATLANTIC Boston Celtics Brooklyn Nets New York Knicks Philadelphia 76ers Toronto Raptors CENTRAL Chicago Bulls Cleveland Cavaliers Detroit Pistons Indiana Pacers Milwaukee Bucks SOUTHEAST Atlanta Hawks Charlotte Hornets Miami Heat Orlando Magic Washington Wizards NORTHWEST Denver Nuggets Minnesota Timberwolves Oklahoma City Thunder Portland Trail Blazers Utah Jazz PACIFIC Golden State Warriors Los Angeles Clippers Los Angeles Lakers Phoenix Suns Sacramento Kings SOUTHWEST Dallas Mavericks Houston Rockets Memphis Grizzlies New Orleans Pelicans San Antonio Spurs ATLANTIC Boston Celtics Brooklyn Nets New York Knicks Philadelphia 76ers Toronto Raptors CENTRAL Chicago Bulls Cleveland Cavaliers Detroit Pistons Indiana Pacers Milwaukee Bucks SOUTHEAST Atlanta Hawks Charlotte Hornets Miami Heat Orlando Magic Washington Wizards NORTHWEST Denver Nuggets Minnesota Timberwolves Oklahoma City Thunder Portland Trail Blazers Utah Jazz PACIFIC Golden State Warriors Los Angeles Clippers Los Angeles Lakers Phoenix Suns Sacramento Kings SOUTHWEST Dallas Mavericks Houston Rockets Memphis Grizzlies New Orleans Pelicans San Antonio Spurs Fantasy Betting Standings Player Stats Team Stats Player Stats Team Stats Videos Steve Ballmer suspended one year, Clippers to lose 5 first-round picks in Kawhi Leonard endorsement scandal Kurt Helin Kurt Helin Published September 2, 2026 05:00 PM Facebook Twitter Email Facing a mountain of evidence, the NBA had to bring the hammer down hard on Clippers owner Steve Ballmer and the Clippers in the salary cap circumvention case involving Kawhi Leonard and former team sponsor Aspiration, among others. If not, 29 other team owners would have gotten the message that the price for circumventing the salary cap was worth it. Adam Silver has thrown the book at Ballmer and the Clippers with the harshest penalties in league history. The NBA released its findings and penalties, and it hits the Clippers hard: • The Clippers forfeit five first-round draft picks (2029, 2030, 2031, 2032, and 2033; Note the 2029 pick was one the Clippers got from Indiana in the Ivica Zubac trade, it does not revert to the Pacers, it is just voided). • The Clippers are fined $30 million. • Owner Steve Ballmer is suspended from “all league and team activities for one year for knowingly seeking to help Mr. Leonard obtain off-court income opportunities, for approving a business deal that he knew was a precondition for Aspiration to enter into an endorsement agreement with Mr. Leonard, and for his failure to create conditions under which his organization abided by the NBA’s circumvention rules.” • Clippers President of Business Operations Gillian Zucker is suspended for one year without pay. • Clippers President of Basketball Operations Lawrence Frank is suspended without pay for six months. • Kawhi Leonard must pay the league $700,000. • Leonard’s already-fired business manager, Dennis Robertson (better known as “Uncle Dennis”), is banned from conducting NBA business for five years. Ballmer and the Clippers plan to fight this, as they said in a statement: “We vehemently reject the NBA’s findings, which are the result of a heavily biased investigation seeking to justify a predetermined narrative rather than facts and evidence. What the league told us privately differs from what it announced today publicly, and they have not held themselves close to the standard Commissioner Silver set at the start of this investigation to ensure it’s fairness and accuracy. “For the past year, we cooperated fully and in good faith and we will now fight just as hard to demonstrate our innocence. “We intend to vigorously challenge these findings and penalties through every avenue available to us and look forward to an ethical and impartial arbitration process.” The Clippers’ attorney also sent a lengthy, scathing letter to Silver saying the “process was designed to substantiate a predetermined outcome.” While the Clippers, Ballmer and the NBA had been talking, the sides were nowhere close to agreeing on a punishment, a league source told NBC Sports. The Clippers said they were blindsided by this announcement. Ballmer can — and almost certainly will — take this issue to court, but there will be no arbitration through the CBA. Both the NBA and NBPA have agreed on the details and punishments involving Leonard, which means there is no arbitration case coming — that is only for the players, not the franchise, and the players’ union signed off on this. Leonard is accepting the punishment — a $700,000 fine for endorsement deals that brought him more than $30 million — and released this statement on Instagram “Integrity and respect for this game are fundamental to who I am. I accept full responsibility for lapses in judgment by people within my inner circle and regret the distraction this situation has caused the fans and my family. “I entered into my contract with the Clippers as well as the agreements in question in good faith, fully committed to fulfilling my obligations and with no knowledge of any intent on anyone’s part to circumvent the salary cap. “For 15 years, my priority has been giving everything to my family, the game, and those I share the court with. As I return to Toronto, I am focused on what I can control, closing this chapter, and moving forward with a clean slate.” Leonard does not face a suspension or voiding of his contract, only the fine. That means the trade that would send him to Toronto for Brandon Ingram and Gradey Dick likely goes through in the coming weeks. “The NBA’s collectively bargained system for determining player compensation is a fundamental component of the basketball competition that the league oversees for the benefit of the teams and players and ultimately the fans,” NBA Commissioner Adam Silver said in a statement. “I am deeply disappointed by the flagrant violations of our rules and by the Clippers’ institutional and leadership failures that led to this misconduct. The severity of the penalties reflects the seriousness of the violations.” The report, compiled by the law firm of Wachtell Lipton, found that “uncle Dennis” pressured the Clippers, on Leonard’s behalf, “to assist him in obtaining off-court income opportunities, successfully obtaining those opportunities, and failing to reimburse payments by the Clippers for personal expenses.” Formally, the report found that the Clippers: • Initiated and helped facilitate endorsements and off-court income opportunities between Mr. Leonard and four companies doing business with the team: Aspiration Partners, Boingo Wireless, Daktronics, and Lockton Insurance. • The Clippers induced “the companies to enter into these agreements by offering them business from the team.” • The Clippers paid “personal expenses on behalf of Leonard and his representatives” and failed “to report improper solicitations for off-court income opportunities made on Mr. Leonard’s behalf through his then-business manager, Dennis Robertson.” What led to this finding It was essentially an open secret around the NBA dating back to 2019 — when Leonard was a free agent, ultimately signing with the Clippers — that Uncle Dennis was asking for all kinds of things to circumvent the salary cap. Other teams shot him down, and the Clippers were investigated by the league at the time, but no evidence was found. That started to change post-pandemic with Aspiration, a former Clippers sponsor and green bank company that has since gone bankrupt. The story was driven by reporting on the Pablo Torre Finds Out podcast . Clippers owner Ballmer made a $50 million investment in Aspiration not long before Leonard signed a $28 million endorsement deal with the company. Ballmer and other Clippers executives made other investments in the company over the years, even as there were signs the business was failing. Several former Aspiration employees told Torre Leonard signed a “no-show” endorsement designed to funnel more money to Leonard and circumvent the NBA salary cap without him having to do work. There is no evidence Leonard did any promotional work for the company. Eventually, Aspiration’s house of cards collapsed and its founder, Joe Sanberg, was convicted of defrauding investors and sentenced to 14 months in prison. The Clippers argued that Ballmer and the franchise were duped like other investors and had done nothing wrong. It wasn’t just Aspiration. Pablo Torre Finds Out later reported that Leonard had an endorsement deal with Daktronics, the makers of the Halo board inside the Inuit Dome. This was odd because Daktronics does not do consumer-facing advertising and had never had a celebrity endorser previously. As noted above, both Boingo Wireless and Lockton Insurance also appeared to have no-show endorsement deals with Leonard. The Clippers have maintained their innocence throughout this process. That said, a mountain of oddly timed, circumstantial evidence — plus comments from employees at Aspiration — points to questionable endorsement deals. articles.body: Enzo Fernandez Takes Huge Burden of Man City Legendâs Jersey Number Enzo FernÃ¡ndez will now wear a lighter shade of blue. | Manchester City Not content with the millstone of being the joint-most expensive signing in Premier League history, Enzo FernÃ¡ndez has gone in search of even more pressure by taking on Kevin De Bruyneâs iconic No. 17 jersey at Manchester City. After a tiresome transfer saga which veered toward a toxic conclusion, FernÃ¡ndez belatedly left Chelsea for the cool sum of $169 million (Â£125 million). The Argentina international had never worn the No. 17 in his senior club career, mostly switching between 13 and 8 across his lucrative moves between River Plate, Benfica and Chelsea. However, with those digits taken in Manchester, FernÃ¡ndez had to go in search of a new number at the Etihad Stadium. There were several openings in a squad which has undergone extensive surgery this summerâFernÃ¡ndez is part of a completely new-look midfield. But rather than taking on something more prosaic like No. 4, 7 or even Rodriâs vacant 16, the World Cup winner has taken on the challenge of emulating the greatest player in Cityâs modern history. The Impossible Legacy Left by Kevin De Bruyne at Man City Appearances : 422 Goals : 108 Assists : 177 Major Trophies : x1 Champions League, x1 Club World Cup, x6 Premier League, x2 FA Cup, x5 EFL Cup When De Bruyne was first handed the No. 17 for City in 2015, there was no guarantee of his success. Despite an impressive spell tearing up the Bundesliga with Wolfsburg, most in England still remembered the Belgian as the fair-haired flop from Chelsea a few years earlier. It only took a few months for that perception to radically shift. âObviously it is very satisfying. I come here today with a very different view than people had of me last year. It shows that a lot can happen in one year,â De Bruyne beamed toward the end of a maiden season which would produce 16 goals and 12 assists. âEverybody had a view of how I came out of Chelsea so, yeah, it gives me satisfaction that people have changed their minds.â De Bruyneâs standing within the game which reach new heights under Pep Guardiola. The pair lifted six Premier League titles in nine years together as well as at least one of every other major trophy. âThe first meeting I ever had with Pep,â De Bruyne recalled, âhe sat me down and he said, âKevin, listen. You can beâeasilyâa top five player in the world. Top five. Easily.ââ It was an accurate prediction. Whether Enzo Maresca would have the same faith in FernÃ¡ndez remains to be seen, but there is certainly a level of immense respect between the pair. âVery ImportantââFernandez Explains Motivation Behind Record-Breaking Move Â£100m. Twice over. pic.twitter.com/MuPDAM6pAo â Sports Illustrated FC (@SI_FootballClub) September 1, 2026 FernÃ¡ndez made little secret of his desire to leave Chelsea toward the end of last season, although his preferred destination was clearly Madrid. As the Buenos Aires native was all too willing to explain, the Spanish capital is a place he âwould like to live.â âPlayers live where they want,â he explained. âIâd live in Madrid. I get by in English, but Iâd be more comfortable in Spanish.â FernÃ¡ndez will have to keep getting by in his second language in Manchester, although he can at least speak to Maresca, once of Sevilla and MÃ¡laga, in Spanish. âHe is a top manager, honestly,â Cityâs record arrival said of his new manager, who spent six years total of his own playing career in Spain. âI had him at my previous club. They were incredible moments. I learned so much with him. Heâs very similar to Latin people, very passionate. So, for me, itâs a pleasure to work with him. âIâm also grateful because he was very important in bringing me here. So itâs a huge pleasure for me to work alongside him and enjoy it. To be honest, we were both very eager for it to happen, because it wasnât easy for me to be here today. But I know he also made a big effort, speaking to the club, and Iâm grateful that he did that. âIt was a long few days, but in the end Iâm here and Iâm very happy to be joining this club.â Add us as a preferred source on Google Follow Published 4 minutes ago | Modified 4 minutes ago GREY WHITEBLOOM Grey Whitebloom is an Associate Editor for SI FC. articles.body: A 2027 top 10 prospect has set an official visit to Kentucky Kentucky coach Mark Pope works the sideline against Florida during their quarterfinal game of the 2026 SEC Menâs Basketball Tournament at Bridgestone Arena in Nashville, Tenn., Friday, March 13, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Itâs official visit season for recruits around the country. Kentucky already has a few coming up over the next few months and another has been added. Big Blue Madness is just around the corner on Oct. 5 and usually includes a list of recruits visiting. One has now been added. 2027 top 10 prospect Nasir Anderson has scheduled his official visit to Kentucky for the weekend of Big Blue Madness on Oct. 5. The five-star prospect also recently announced his top 10 schools and obviously the Wildcats made it. Others included are UConn, North Carolina, Indiana, Florida, Providence, Georgia, Tennessee and Virginia. One of the top point guards in the class, these visits coming up will provide a lot of clarity as to where things stand. Mar 19, 2026; St. Louis, MO, USA; Kentucky Wildcats head coach Mark Pope speaks during an interview at the practice session ahead of the first round of the men's 2026 NCAA Tournament at Enterprise Center. Mandatory Credit: Jeff Le-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Anderson had a tough summer as an injury cut his AAU season short. Now, heâs fully focused on his high school season as he gears into a fall full of basketball and visits. As for when to expect a decision, that is still unclear at the moment as he still has a number of visits to take. Here is what Anderson had to say about Kentucky in a recent interview with 247 Sports: "It is a great program, a blue blood. I would love to play for a team like that, so I'm keeping them in mind. Coach Pope has been great during the recruiting process." Here is a scouting report on Anderson from 247 Sports' Adam Finkelstein:Â "A lefty power guard who plays with a distinct downhill style, Anderson can bully his way to the rim more effectively than arguably any other guard in the national class. Heâs built almost like a football player, with a tremendously powerful upper body, good positional size, and long arms, which allows him to initiate, and then absorb, all types of contact going to his dominant side. Heâs virtually unstoppable with the ball in the open court, and while he looks physically mature, heâs actually young for his grade, having turned 17 in July before his senior year. Beyond his physicality, Anderson has a tight handle, terrific balance, and body control, both on the ground and in mid-air, along with an advanced lay-up package and the vertical explosiveness to rise-up when he has momentum." Nasir Anderson has been the engine of adidas 3SSB's 2-0 start at the NextGen Finals in Athens. The 6-foot-4, explosive 16-year-old point guard is averaging 18.5 points, 10 assists and 8 rebounds per game. pic.twitter.com/mKznzKSrJz â Jonathan Givony (@DraftExpress) May 22, 2026 Kentucky will now get a visit from a top point guard that theyâve had their eyes on for a while. articles.body: Jordan Chiles hints at LA 2028 comeback with Michael Jordan-narrated video - NBC Sports Skip navigation MLB NFL NBA NHL Premier League NASCAR College Football Men’s College Basketball Player News NFL Player News NBA Player News MLB Player News Scores NFL Scores NBA Scores MLB Scores MLB NFL NBA NHL Premier League NASCAR College Football Men’s College Basketball Player News NFL Player News NBA Player News MLB Player News Scores NFL Scores NBA Scores MLB Scores Login Favorites Sign up to follow your favorites on all your devices. Sign up NBC Olympics Olympics on Peacock LA 2028 Team USA Jordan Chiles hints at LA 2028 comeback with Michael Jordan-narrated video Nick Zaccardi Nick Zaccardi Published September 2, 2026 04:57 PM Facebook Twitter Email If Jordan Chiles is planning to return to elite gymnastics competition, she is pulling out all the stops. Chiles, whose last elite gymnastics competition was the 2024 Paris Olympics, made a social media post captioned, “LA 2028... WHY NOT?” with a video narrated by Michael Jordan. “Why again?” Michael Jordan says in the video. “Because the dream is still there. Why continue? Because there’s still more to give. Why now? Because not every chapter ends when people expect it to. Why her? Because she’s that girl. Some decisions don’t need permission. Just one more bet on herself. So when the world asks why she’s back for a third time, the answer is simple.” The video ends with Chiles saying, “Why not?” and then flashing an LA 2028 grill. “I’ve learned that there’s no timeline for when you’re supposed to be done dreaming,” Chiles said in a statement, according to ESPN.com . “LA28 has always been somewhere in the back of my mind, but I needed to take the time to figure out what coming back would mean for me and, more importantly, why I wanted to do it. LA28 isn’t about proving anything to anyone. It’s about betting on myself one more time, enjoying the journey and seeing just how far I can take this. I still love this sport, I still have more to give and getting the chance to potentially do that in L.A., the city I now call home, makes it even more special. I’m excited to see what’s possible when I bet on myself one more time.” Chiles, who was named after Michael Jordan, has owned more than 100 pairs of Jordan shoes. The basketball legend also messaged Chiles before the Paris Games to wish her luck. LA 2028… WHY NOT? ✨🇺🇸 🎥Avery Hall 📸Jamie Bruce ✨️A Special Thank You to Normani, Winnie and THE Michael Jordan. https://t.co/H2XGVVHLmi — Jordan Chiles (@ChilesJordan) September 2, 2026 The post came a day after it was announced that Chiles will be a student coach next year for UCLA after winning four NCAA titles for the Bruins during her college career that wrapped up this past season. Chiles, a 25-year-old from Vancouver, Washington, attended the Xfinity U.S. Championships last month in Phoenix, where she said “the wait is still on” about a possible comeback. “I definitely am going on a lot of vacation, so stay tuned for that,” she said then. “I think right now my mind is just focusing on me, personally, mentally.” Three of Chiles’ four teammates from Paris are definitely bidding for LA 2028 — Hezly Rivera, who last month repeated as U.S. all-around champion; Jade Carey, who was a student assistant coach at Oregon State last season, then returned to elite competition this season and Suni Lee, who announced her return to the gym in July and could return to competition as early as next spring. Simone Biles has not announced whether she plans to join them in coming back. There is precedent for a gymnast to become a coach and then make an Olympic team. Alicia Sacramone was a volunteer assistant at Brown in 2008 before competing at the Beijing Games that year. Suni Lee: ‘I’m back’ for LA 2028 Olympic bid Suni Lee teased a return to gymnastics training, two years before the LA Olympics. Brown grew apart Charean Williams Charean Williams Published September 2, 2026 04:25 PM Facebook Twitter Email Jalen Hurts acknowledged the obvious: He and wide receiver A.J. Brown grew apart. It took prompting, but the Eagles quarterback finally told GQ magazine in an interview published Tuesday that the two weren’t as close last season as they once were. “There’s no surprise that it was talked about ,” Hurts told GQ when asked if he and Brown had grown apart. The reporter then asked Hurts again whether the two had grown apart. “I mean, clearly,” he told the magazine. The Eagles traded Brown to the Patriots in June, and the wide receiver told reporters last month that he and Hurts had not spoken since the trade. Hurts and Brown did briefly catch up after the second of two practices between their teams. The two men initially met when Hurts hosted Brown on a recruiting trip at Alabama. After they became Eagles’ teammates, following the Titans’ trade of Brown to Philadelphia, Hurts became the godfather to Brown’s daughter, Jersee. In four seasons with the Eagles, Brown caught 339 passes for 5,034 yards and 32 touchdowns. He became frustrated with Hurts and his role in the offseason in 2024, and the Eagles eventually granted Brown’s request for a trade.
