And Swinney made clear on Tuesday that he is not a fan of the way NCAA eligibility rules have changed to make that possible. “It’s kind of embarrassing, honestly. It’s just embarrassing that that’s where we are. I doin’t blame the kids, people trying to take advantage of the system, I just think it’s embarrassing where we are with college football, and we’ve been there for a while,” Swinney said. Swinney said he’d like to see college football establish clear rules that can won’t get overturned by judges, as has happened repeatedly when players have sued to regain NCAA eligibility. “It’s embarrassing. I mean, it really is. We have no rules. There’s no governance. I mean, it’s a joke. There’s zero rules. And when you enforce rules someone just goes and finds a judge to say, ‘No, you can’t enforce that rule.’ Never did I think we’d be living in an era like this, but that’s where we are,” Swinney said. LSU has been attempting to add pass rusher Jack Pyburn, who was in training camp with the Buccaneers, and tight end Dae’Quan Wright, who was in training camp with the Browns. Pyburn was claimed on waivers by the Chiefs and now plans to stay in the NFL. Whether Wright will play against Clemson remains to be seen. “I actually got to go watch practice in June with the Browns, so I’m probably going to get turned in for tampering,” Swinney joked. “Been watching the preseason games with the Bucs and the Browns and all that.” Add favorite players, teams, and leagues with an NBCUniversal Profile Continue

articles.title: 5 Thoughts From No. 14 Purdue's Sweep of Defending National Champion Texas A&M
articles.excerpt: Purdue picked up a huge victory on Tuesday night, defeating Texas A&M in three straight sets. What stood out most from the Boilers' big win at Mackey Arena?
articles.source_type: Gameweek squads, team news round-ups, deadline reminders
articles.body: 5 Thoughts From No. 14 Purdue's Sweep of Defending National Champion Texas A&M Purdue Boilermakers middle blocker Dior Charles (9) chest bumps outside hitter Mimi Mambu. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect More than 10,000 fans packed Mackey Arena on Tuesday night to watch 14th-ranked Purdue battle No. 12 Texas A&M, the reigning national champions. The only thing hotter than the conditions inside the iconic venue was the volleyball coming off the hands of the Boilermaker hitters. Purdue swept Texas A&M in three hard-fought sets, earning its first victory of the 2026 campaign. That win was significant for head coach Dave Shondell, who became the winningest coach across all sports at the university. The Boilers found themselves in some tough situations throughout the night, but squeaked out victories 27-25, 25-23 and 25-20 to take down the defending champs. What did we learn from that performance in the team's first match of the Big Ten-SEC Challenge? Closing out tight sets Purdue Sophomore Ryan McAleer (3) digs a ball. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Last season, Purdue earned a reputation as a team that refused to quit. That has carried over into the 2026 season, and it became clear on Tuesday night. The Boilermakers trailed Texas A&M 15-11 at the first media timeout of the opening set, but battled back to earn a 27-25 victory. In the second game, Purdue found itself in a similar predicament, trailing 20-17 before storming back and stealing the second set, 25-23. The Boilers were never in any danger of dropping the third set, though a late run from the Aggies made the score closer than necessary. For a team that has become dependent on freshman Addy Tindall and sophomore Mimi Mambu at the outside hitter positions, it was impressive to see the fight across all three matches, especially against the defending champs. Taylor Anderson showed her aggressive side Purdue's Taylor Anderson and Bianka Lulic block. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Shondell has spoken frequently about Anderson being more aggressive offensively. She delivered in a big way for the Boilermakers on Tuesday night. She finished the match with 36 assists and four digs, but it was her work on the block and her attacks that really stood out. Anderson tallied five kills on seven attacks with no errors. She also accounted for seven total blocks against the Aggies, showing her range as more than a setter. "The first match against Creighton, I thought Taylor was just OK," Shondell said. "But tonight, she was the Taylor that we need. She was fabulous." Anderson helped Purdue win the first set with great service placement on the 27th point, closing it out to give the Boilers a 1-0 advantage. When the Boilers trailed 20-18 in the second set, the senior accounted for a block and a kill, pulling Purdue to within one point at 21-20. She closed out that set with a kill to give her team a two-set lead. "I definitely like to set them because they're great, but I think over my years here I've gotten more comfortable with it," Anderson said. "Now, knowing the game and knowing our opponents really well, I l know when I score it takes the load off them, and it opens them up later." High hitting percentages all night Purdue Boilermakers middle blocker Dior Charles (9) hits the ball. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Purdue got off to a bit of a sluggish start hitting the ball, but just like the temperature inside Mackey Arena, the swings started to heat up. The Boilermakers hit .333 or higher in each of the three sets, finishing the match with a .388 hitting percentage and a .480 kill percentage. Tindall was the most impressive, hitting .536 on 28 swings. Kate Hansen finished at .545 and Anderson hit .714. Mimi Mambu and Dior Charles were both at .333 hitting percentages for the night. Texas A&M lost a lot from last year's championship team, but it built a reputation as a talented blocking squad at the net. It didn't bother the Boilers on Tuesday. Transfers stepping up Purdue Boilermakers outside hitter Lameen Mambu (21) looks on. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Hansen and Mambu both made some big plays throughout the night. Mambu totaled 12 kills on 30 attacks. She seemed to be in more control than she was on Friday night when Purdue dropped the five-setter to Creighton Hansen was a monster at the net alongside Anderson. She also had some timely kills, closing out the night with seven kills and six blocks. She had just two total errors, one on the block and one attacking. "She's just a very mature person who has a competitive edge to her," Shondell said of Hansen. "It feels like she's reborn to be here ... she gets to come here and play in front of that kind of crowd against this level of competition and prove what she's capable of doing. She's someone you can just count on. She's in the right spot all the time." Addy Tindall looks like the Freshman of the Year Purdue Boilermakers outside hitter Addy Tindall (18) hits the ball. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect We're only two matches into Purdue's season, but it's not too early to make this type of prediction. Tindall has been stellar through the first two matches against tremendous competition. If she's not the best freshman in the conference, she's close. "She has grown beyond expectations this early. I mean, she's playing like a third-year outside hitter," Shondell said. "She's passing, she's playing defense, she's blocking. I think she had one hitting error all night ... That's quite an accomplishment." Through two matches, Tindall has accounted for 38 kills and just four errors, maintaining a .493 hitting percentage. She's only going to improve as the season continues, too. articles.source_type: Live scores, results archive, fixtures and match detail
articles.body: Frodin hopes to meet idol Serena Williams after US Open debut | Flashscore.com All Football Transfer News Premier League US Open Features Champions League Darts Snooker Golf Cycling MLB NFL Most read on Flashscore News Deadline Day LIVE: Balogun decides against Everton move as Sunderland tie up Fofana Swedish tennis ace collapses twice on court during Challenger event in China Flashscore sources: Everton still keen on Grealish after Richarlison agreement Man City confirm joint British record signing of Enzo Fernandez from Chelsea Frodin hopes to meet idol Serena Williams after US Open debut Reuters Thea Frodin during US Open debut Amber Searls / Reuters Thea Frodin made her U.S. Open debut on Tuesday ⁠but one dream remains unfulfilled for the 17-year-old, who is still waiting to meet Serena Williams five years after appearing ‌as the American's tennis double in the film "King Richard". Serena , a 23-time Grand Slam champion, ‌returned to the court for the first time in ‌nearly four years at the Queen's Club Championships in London in June ‌and is back at Flushing Meadows competing in doubles with ‌sister Venus. "Hopefully I can get the chance soon to get the opportunity to meet her," Frodin told reporters after losing 6-1, 6-1 to world ‌number two Elena Rybakina on Arthur Ashe Stadium. Frodin-Rybakina matchup stats Flashscore Frodin ⁠earned a wildcard for the ‌U.S. Open by winning the USTA Girls' 18s National Championships, and while ​her Grand Slam debut against Rybakina was a harsh introduction to life at the elite level, she said it ​was a valuable lesson for her career. "It was a fun experience to kind of see how the best players in the ⁠world, how they hit ​their balls and their shots," she said. "My goal on court is always to have an aggressive game style. Today I feel like it was a bit harder to bring that out. Hopefully the ‌next time I can be more experienced and see what I can do." Frodin said she had managed to handle the attention surrounding her unusual connection to Serena, though acknowledged it was difficult to escape the headlines before her debut. "I think it's hard to get away from all of that. It's kind of just about accepting it and not letting it get to you," she added. Actor Will Smith, who won an Academy Award for playing Serena's ‌father, Richard Williams, in the film, reposted one of Frodin's social ​media posts before her match, something she described as "pretty cool." Frodin ‌plans to play the girls' U.S. Open next week and finish high school before deciding whether to turn professional or play college tennis. "I'm not rushing into kind of making a decision with all that," she said. "I'm taking this year and ⁠next year to finish high ⁠school and then see ‌where I am then." US Open 2026 The US Open is the fourth and final Grand Slam of the tennis season, running from August 30th to September 13th. It is a hard-court tournament held at Flushing Meadows in New York City. articles.title: Lazaro Montes Shows Exactly What He Can Add to Mariners' Lineup in MLB Debut
articles.excerpt: One of the Seattle Mariners' top prospects, outfielder Lazaro Montes, made his MLB debut against the Boston Red Sox. Here's how he performed.
articles.source_type: Gameweek squads, team news round-ups, deadline reminders
articles.body: Lazaro Montes Shows Exactly What He Can Add to Mariners' Lineup in MLB Debut Sep 1, 2026; Boston, Massachusetts, USA; Seattle Mariners designated hitter Lazaro Montes (99) hits a one-run RBI single against the Boston Red Sox during the third inning at Fenway Park. Mandatory Credit: Eric Canha-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Seattle Mariners outfield prospect Lazaro Montes made a strong first impression in his MLB debut. Montes, Seattle's No. 5 prospect on MLB Pipeline , went 2-for-4 with a walk, two RBIs, and two runs scored in the Mariners' 9-6 victory over the Boston Red Sox on Tuesday. Most notably, though, the 21-year-old crushed his first home run in the big leagues. The lefty-swinging slugger drilled a 407-foot solo shot to dead-center field that exploded off the bat at 106 mph. In doing so, he became the youngest Mariner in franchise history to homer in his MLB debut, according to ESPN Insights on X/Twitter. Before launching his first long ball in the majors, Montes got his first MLB hit by smacking a ground ball between first and second base for an RBI single. While he's obviously just one game into his first stint in the big leagues, the young outfielder's performance on Tuesday should offer a brief preview of the offensive boost he can provide for Seattle in the final month of the 2026 regular season. This is just the beginning for Lazaro Montes Sep 1, 2026; Boston, Massachusetts, USA; Seattle Mariners designated hitter Lazaro Montes (99) reacts as he runs the bases after hitting a home run during the fifth inning against the Boston Red Sox at Fenway Park. Mandatory Credit: Eric Canha-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Mariners officially promoted Montes on Tuesday when active MLB rosters expanded. And based on his numbers in the minors this year and the show he put on in his first game, Seattle fans can likely expect to see plenty more of the 6-foot-5 outfielder down the stretch. So far in 2026, Montes produced a .249 batting average, a .369 on-base percentage, and a .928 OPS with 38 homers, 96 RBIs, and eight stolen bases in 123 games in the minors. The only minor leaguer with more home runs right now is Milwaukee Brewers infield prospect Andrew Fischer . The Seattle prospect launched 25 of those home runs in 79 Double-A games before being called up to Triple-A for the first time in July. And in just 44 Triple-A games, the 21-year-old hit .274 and posted a .941 OPS with 13 homers. Following their win on Tuesday, the Mariners are now 65-74, 5.5 games back of the last American League Wild Card spot. If Montes can stay hot at the plate during his first stint in the majors, he could be a major contributor to Seattle's final push for a postseason berth. articles.body: NFL keen for 'at least one game per year' in Australia | Flashscore.com All Football Transfer News Premier League US Open Features Champions League Darts Snooker Golf Cycling MLB NFL Most read on Flashscore News Deadline Day LIVE: Balogun decides against Everton move as Sunderland tie up Fofana Swedish tennis ace collapses twice on court during Challenger event in China Flashscore sources: Everton still keen on Grealish after Richarlison agreement Man City confirm joint British record signing of Enzo Fernandez from Chelsea NFL keen for 'at least one game per year' in Australia Reuters Former LA Rams player Todd Gurley recently visited the MCG to promote next Friday's NFL game. DANIEL POCKETT / GETTY IMAGES VIA AFP The National Football League (NFL) is looking to bring a game to Australia every season as part of its international strategy and sees the nation as ⁠a strategic growth market for American football, a senior executive told Reuters on Tuesday. Australia hosts its first NFL game at the 100,000-seat Melbourne Cricket Ground (MCG) on September 11 with the LA Rams opening their season ‌against the San Francisco 49ers in the first of a record nine-game international schedule across seven countries. The MCG game is part of a ‌multi-year contract with Australia's Victoria state, which includes two confirmed games over four years and the option ‌for a third. The timing of the second one is still to be decided but Gerrit Meier, managing director and head of ‌NFL International, said the league's preference would be for annual games in Australia, much as Britain ‌has had for most of the last two decades. I think that would be the plan, right? " Meier said in a video call from New York on Tuesday. "Overall, we're working off the hypothesis that we need to make a commitment to a market ... We believe that ‌at least one game per year should be something that we should ⁠be having in the markets that we commit to. And maybe ‌over time, as we have, maybe, greater inventory, then maybe you play two games (per season) or so Meier said the longer-term ​scheduling of NFL games in Australia had to consider the players' experience, whether the clubs saw value in the journey and how satisfied the hosts would be with the economic impact. The teams coming ​back, they need to be healthy. They need to have a great experience. It needs to be a great game because in the end it counts. It's not an exhibition game, " he said. The Victorian government's bid for ⁠the NFL games works out to about ​A$10 million to A$15 million per game, Melbourne newspaper the Age reported this month, citing figures obtained by the newspaper. Government officials have declined to disclose the cost but see the games as a huge opportunity to showcase the state and expect " significant economic returns " on the investment. The first game in Melbourne will kick off at 10:35 a.m. on a ‌Friday to suit the U.S. TV audience, but the MCG is expected to be packed to near capacity. Nearly half of the crowd will travel from other Australian states or from overseas, including some 10,000 U.S.-based fans, the NFL estimates. Meier said the NFL believed the idea of a regular season-opening game in Australia was " very, very special " but would need conversations with the state government's tourism arm Visit Victoria and the Australian Football League (AFL). The AFL is the governing body for professional Australian rules football, the most popular winter sport in the nation's southern states. Multiple AFL games are played almost every week at the MCG through to the end of September. We're going to sit with the larger region and city and (ask) what all of you thought. Was it good? Was it not good? ‌Would you want to have us back? " said Meier. And ... we want to see how the grass is holding ​up. We want to kind of see how the overall setup has been working. The NFL set up ‌a local office for Australia and New Zealand in 2022 and opened its second international academy on the Gold Coast in 2024, having launched the first in England in 2019. Australian punters are common in NFL teams, and Philadelphia Eagles offensive tackle Jordan Mailata became the country's first to win a Super Bowl as a participating player last year. Meier said in a few years operating in Australia, the NFL's perception of ⁠the nation's potential had changed. It's kind of moved from ⁠being an interesting market to actually being a ‌strategic growth market, " he said. We have a fast-growing fan-base ... The game itself is just a catalyst. Second-round play begins Wednesday, while players involved in first-round matches that got suspended or postponed due to Tuesday's rain try to play catch-up in an action-packed slate on the hard courts of New York City's USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center. An underdog coming off the biggest win of his career tries to score another upset, while an all-American women's clash presents a value opportunity. All Tennis Odds & Lines below are taken from DraftKings Sportsbook , but you can sometimes find more favorable odds for tennis betting by checking other best sports betting sites and sports betting apps . We offer exclusive sportsbook promos in states where sports betting has gone live. All men's singles matches at Grand Slams such as the US Open are best of five sets, while women's singles matches are best of three sets. A mix of players' previous hard court results, recent form and stylistic matchups can help pinpoint intriguing betting opportunities, both among favorites likely to cruise to victory and underdogs ready to pull off upsets. The aforementioned underdogs are highlighted in the Upset Alert section, the Lock It In section covers players who can safely be viewed as favorites, while the Value Bets section recommends enticing options in matchups that are considered closer to toss-ups. US Open Tennis Picks: Upset Alert Mariano Navone (+158) vs. Matteo Berrettini Navone is coming off the biggest win of his career, having outlasted Novak Djokovic in a grueling battle that went nearly four hours through four sets and ultimately took 4:30 to complete. The 25-year-old Argentine has had his best results on clay, but he backed up his serve like a hard-court specialist against the consensus best returner of all time, holding 21 of 25 service games. Navone's confidence on this surface is at an all-time high, and he beat Berrettini in the lead-up to the US Open, notching a 6-3, 6-7 (5), 6-3 win on the hard courts of the Canadian Open less than a month ago. Hubert Hurkacz (+190) vs. Ben Shelton Shelton does a great job taking care of his serve, but he can struggle as a returner, so generating break chances won't be easy against the big-serving Hurkacz. The ninth-ranked American lefty will also have less of an advantage than usual directing forehands to his opponent's backhand, as the backhand is Hurkacz's superior wing off the ground. This will be the first meeting between these two, and while Shelton is rightfully favored given his excellent 20-6 hard-court record this year, the 47th-ranked Hurkacz is a former top-10 player himself with no shortage of big wins under his belt. Hurkacz comes in riding a five-match winning streak, as he won a Challenger event in Cancun leading up to the US Open prior to knocking off Damir Dzumhur in the first round Honorable Mention Taylah Preston (+299) vs. Taylor Townsend US Open Tennis Odds: Lock It In Jiri Lehecka (-291) vs. Toby Samuel Lehecka reached the quarterfinals here last year and made a hard-court Masters 1000 final earlier this year at the Miami Open . The 18th-seeded Czech is 15-9 on hard courts this year and has a .588 career win rate on this surface. Samuel won his first-round match easily against Tomas Machac , who is working his way back from an injury and hasn't won a match since the French Open in May, but the 23-year-old Brit had won only two ATP Tour matches in his career prior to that victory, both on grass in his home country. Samuel has yet to crack the top 100 in the rankings in his career. Stefanos Tsitsipas (-253) vs. Lloyd Harris Tsitsipas improved to 10-4 in his last 14 matches with his first-round win over 10th-seeded Arthur Fils . The former world No. 3 has been rolling under new coach Thomas Perrin, and Tsitsipas is unlikely to slow down against the 139th-ranked Harris, who hadn't played an ATP Tour-level match in 2026 prior to beating 394th-ranked American teenager Jack Kennedy in the first round . Harris got as high as No. 31 in the rankings back in 2021, but injuries have sapped some of the big-serving South African's abilities. She's back in the top 30 and is looking to add to her success at the US Open, where Navarro has an 8-2 record in her last 10 matches. Her 65th-ranked compatriot McNally has found more success in doubles than singles, topping out at 50th in the singles rankings so far in her career. Navarro's superior court coverage and consistency are likely to make the difference in this fifth matchup between these two Americans. They have split the previous four meetings, though Navarro leads their hard-court head-to-head 2-1, with McNally's lone win on this surface coming back in 2020. Daniel Merida (+115) vs. Andrey Rublev Merida has flown under the radar relative to other members of the next-gen Spanish wave led by Carlos Alcaraz and Rafael Jodar , but the 21-year-old Madrid native is starting to close the ranking gap with his higher-profile compatriots, as Merida has propelled himself into the top 40 with a 19-9 record in 2026. That mark includes a 6-2 run across the pair of hard-court ATP 1000 events in Montreal and Cincinnati during August, where Merida notched three top-50 wins while losing to top-20 Americans Learner Tien and Taylor Fritz . The slumping Rublev has dropped out of the top 20 while going just 3-3 in his last six matches, all against players ranked outside the top 45. Rublev needed a fifth-set tiebreak to get through 109th-ranked lucky loser Otto Virtanen in the first round. articles.title: Everton wake up to an attacking nightmare after late Balogun transfer blow
articles.source_type: Line-ups, goal scorers, cards, substitutions, possession and xG per match
articles.body: Soccerway All Transfer News Premier League LaLiga Ligue 1 Serie A Bundesliga Champions League Europa League Conference League World Cup Everton wake up to an attacking nightmare after late Balogun transfer blow Dean Jones Everton suffered a string of deadline day setbacks. Action Images via Reuters/John Sibley Anyone associated with Everton Football Club will wake up Wednesday morning wondering quite how their transfer window came to this. There was a point in the final hours of the summer business period when everything seemed to be falling into place. By the deadline, everything had fallen apart. The worst situation surrounds Folarin Balogun who was targeted to join from AS Monaco to add to Everton 's goal threat. The player dramatically changed his mind on the move as the transfer deadline passed. Now, the club must pick themselves up and hope their paper-thin squad can hold their own through to the winter. Initially, Everton agreed a £40m fee with Monaco for USA striker Balogun. But after he failed a medical, they tried to renegotiate the deal. Rather than simply walk away, Everton kept working on it, and Monaco eventually agreed to let him move for an adjusted fee. At the same time, the Toffees had been exploring a move for Joshua Zirkzee from Manchester United It was a back-up plan to Balogun that could have proven quick and easy. They knew United and Zirkzee were open to him leaving, and thought they had a loan lined up. It was an insurance policy for the Balogun deal that made sense. But then United pulled back. They decided it would be more beneficial to keep Zirkzee around than let him solve a problem for a rival Premier League club - especially one they face this coming weekend. It did not seem to matter too much at the time, as the Balogun deal was back on. A deal sheet was submitted to the Premier League - which was signed by Balogun and allowed Everton extra time to complete the transfer beyond the 23:00 deadline. However, Balogun decided he did not want to proceed. His change of heart is intriguing, considering he has spent the entire summer angling for a transfer and has not been involved at all at Monaco this season as he has been waiting for his next landing spot to open up. To make matters more frustrating, Everton also made an enquiry about Aston Villa Tammy Abraham , but could not find any breakthrough on a deal. And other attacking options had already moved on. Star attacker Iliman Ndiaye signed for Manchester City for £60m, while a deal for Richarlison that had been worked on at the end of last week was confirmed as dead. He stayed at Tottenham That was not the end of it as Beto left too, joining Fiorentina for a package worth around £15.4m. Every attacking transfer decision had gone badly wrong. There was one ray of light as Everton secured Jack Grealish on loan from Manchester City for the remainder of the season. That could prove significant as Grealish brings Premier League experience, creativity and the ability to change games. Grealish also now brings much-needed depth, joining Tyler Dibling Brennan Johnson Tyrique George and Thierno Barry among Everton's front line options. The club will get a chance to make up for their transfer problems when the window reopens in January. But right now, Everton's squad - particularly the attack - looks worryingly thin. He has been a journalist on leading UK newspapers and websites over the past 20 years, establishing himself as an authoritative and trusted voice in the industry. articles.title: North Melbourne express 'desire to want more' after sacking Alastair Clarkson
articles.source_type: Live scores, results archive, fixtures and match detail
articles.body: North Melbourne sack Alastair Clarkson | Flashscore.com All Football Transfer News Premier League US Open Features Champions League Darts Snooker Golf Cycling MLB NFL Most read on Flashscore News Deadline Day LIVE: Balogun decides against Everton move as Sunderland tie up Fofana Swedish tennis ace collapses twice on court during Challenger event in China Man City confirm joint British record signing of Enzo Fernandez from Chelsea Flashscore sources: Everton still keen on Grealish after Richarlison agreement North Melbourne express 'desire to want more' after sacking Alastair Clarkson Aaron Murphy Updated Former North Melbourne head coach Alastair Clarkson speaking to his players in Round 24. DARRIAN TRAYNOR / AFL PHOTOS / GETTY IMAGES VIA AFP North Melbourne have parted ways with 58-year-old head coach Alastair Clarkson after four successive seasons with no finals appearances. Shortly before breaking up for their end-of-season leave, North Melbourne players and staff were called into an extraordinary meeting at Arden Street shortly before midday on Wednesday to be informed that they will be playing under a new coach next year. Four-time Premiership-winning coach Clarkson spent four years at the club and won only 20 of his 82 matches in charge, albeit taking over a very youthful squad and being afforded the patience and low expectations that would come with a long-term rebuild. The Kangaroos began this season with the fourth-youngest squad by average age, with 26 members of their AFL list having started 2026 with fewer than 50 games of experience. They recorded their best season under Clarkson in 2026, winning nine of their 23 matches, and it was widely expected that the veteran would see out his contract through to the end of 2027 having proven that the side's on-field results were on the up. It was their most successful season on the field since winning ten out of 22 games under Rhyce Shaw in 2019. Clarkson publicly implored his bosses to stay the course under his tutelage in 2027, pointing to other coaches such as Justin Longmuir, Chris Fagan and Sam Mitchell, all of whom have tasted the fruits of a patient and steady rebuild. It's done best when you've got stability and continuity, " he said in early August. "We just know that (success) takes time. Those that are prepared to be patient will be rewarded for that patience. I’ve been on record many times over the last two or three years saying how much difficulty there is in trying to go to the bottom of the ladder to the top The sacking means that North Melbourne are taking a costly gamble on their short-term future by terminating Clarkson's contract with a year to run, forcing the club to pay out a salary reported to be in the vicinity of $1 million. We asked Alastair to give our club stability and strength and help return us to the top of the AFL ladder, ” Club President Dr Sonja Hood said in a statement on Wednesday. “Four years later, we have created an environment where our staff and players want to be at our club. This is a testament to the culture Alastair has helped create and the belief that he has built in this group. “Although we have clearly made progress and won more games, we won't shy away from our desire to want more from this talented group. We are incredibly grateful to Alastair for the work he’s done over the last four years and we wish him all the very best for his next chapter. Former North Melbourne players Adam Simpson (306 games) and John Longmire (200 games) are amongst those immediately considered to be frontrunners for the job, with Simpson taking West Coast to six consecutive finals series as a head coach and Longmire winning the 2012 flag with Sydney in the second of his 12 finals series as a coach. Both men left their respective posts in 2024, with Simpson playing a prominent role in the media since as well as a part-time mentoring role at Carlton in 2026. articles.body: Gael Monfils celebrates 40th birthday with first-round win at US Open | Flashscore.com All Football Transfer News Premier League US Open Features Champions League Darts Snooker Golf Cycling MLB NFL Most read on Flashscore News Deadline Day LIVE: Balogun decides against Everton move as Sunderland tie up Fofana Swedish tennis ace collapses twice on court during Challenger event in China Man City confirm joint British record signing of Enzo Fernandez from Chelsea Flashscore sources: Everton still keen on Grealish after Richarlison agreement Gael Monfils celebrates 40th birthday with first-round win at US Open AFP Gael Monfils gestures during first round of 2026 US Open Adam Hunger / CTK / AP France's Gael Monfils turned back the clock Tuesday, making the most of a US Open wild card and an adoring New York crowd to advance to the second round. Playing on his 40th birthday, Monfils opened shakily against Adolfo Daniel Vallejo of Paraguay, but decisively turned the tables after the first set for a 2-6, 6-1, 6-2, 6-0 win. Monfils, who will retire after this season, played with his trademark showmanship, offering exaggerated bows after embellishing a putaway shot in the fourth set with a leap in the air. Match stats: Vallejo vs Monfils Flashscore Evidence of approval came when the crowd joined an impromptu performance of "Happy Birthday" after the match. "You guys always make it electric, amazing," Monfils said in an on-court interview. "Let's keep it going for the second one." This is Monfils' 18th appearance at the US Open. His best showing came in 2016 when he reached the semi-finals and lost to Novak Djokovic Monfils, who reached a career-high ranking of sixth in 2016, is down to 311th, having only played a handful of tournaments in 2026. In contrast to Monfils, who is playing in his 70th Grand Slam tournament, Tuesday marked just the third of the 22-year-old Vallejo. articles.source_type: Live scores, results archive, fixtures and match detail
articles.body: Tiger Woods to change DUI plea | Flashscore.com All Football Transfer News Premier League US Open Features Champions League Darts Snooker Golf Cycling MLB NFL Most read on Flashscore News Deadline Day LIVE: Balogun decides against Everton move as Sunderland tie up Fofana Swedish tennis ace collapses twice on court during Challenger event in China Flashscore sources: Everton still keen on Grealish after Richarlison agreement Man City confirm joint British record signing of Enzo Fernandez from Chelsea Tigers Woods to change 'not guilty' plea in upcoming hearing for DUI case AFP Tigers Wood pleads guilty to DUI Andrew Redington / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA Tiger Woods, who pleaded not guilty to driving under the influence after crashing his car in Florida in March, is expected to formally change his plea, court documents showed Tuesday. "change of plea" hearing early Wednesday morning was added to the golf superstar's case docket at a Martin County court, online records showed. Woods ' lawyer did not immediately respond to AFP's request for comment about the nature of the change of plea. The 15-time major winner crashed his SUV into a trailer being pulled by a pickup truck near his Jupiter Island home in March. He was assessed to be impaired by officers at the scene and had opioid painkillers with him. Woods pleaded not guilty to misdemeanor charges of DUI with property damage and refusing to submit to a lawful test, telling authorities he was looking at his phone and changing radio channels when he crashed. Days later, he said he was "stepping away" to seek treatment and focus on his health. He was cleared by a judge to travel overseas to an inpatient facility, reportedly in Switzerland. Woods made his first public appearance since his arrest at the PGA Tour's Travelers Championship in June. The following month, a judge ruled that prosecutors could review Woods' hospital treatment, as well as the golfer's prescription drug records. In both cases, the information can be reviewed only by prosecutors, designated law enforcement officers, experts, and Woods's defense team. Woods has undergone multiple back operations and surgeries on severe leg injuries suffered in a separate, 2021 California car crash. articles.body: 49ers DC Raheem Morris Gushes Over This Defensive Lineman Jan 4, 2026; Atlanta, Georgia, USA; Atlanta Falcons head coach Raheem Morris on the sideline against the New Orleans Saints in the second quarter at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Brett Davis-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect With Nick Bosa out of practice, the 49ers have been able to take a closer look at their other defensive ends. One player who has been seeing a healthy amount of starting reps is defensive end Sam Okuayinonu. He was a bit of an underrated player for the 49ers last year.Â It seems heâs been taking it up a notch throughout training camp. Defensive coordinator Raheem Morris was asked about Okuayinonu stepping up with Bosa out, to which he replied with a gushing answer.Â âI think just the pitbull mentality that he has. Heâs a barnyard bully. He can do whatever you want him to do,â Morris said. âHeâs kind of got that role where he can be that spinner we talked about. He can play at the line of scrimmage, plays with great strength, is able to go out there and shed blocks, be able to cause havoc.Â âHis ability to turn and run and get to the ball. I think weâve seen a big-time screen. Thatâs a standard type play for the 49ers and what heâs able to do. So, Iâm really excited about all of those guys and him getting his opportunity to go out there and do some of those things if it presents itself I know heâll be ready.â Okuayinonu receives a pretty big vote of confidence from Morris. Maybe heâs embellishing a bit because Okuayinonu may be in for a good chunk of playing time in Week 1. Bosaâs status to play in Australia is up in the air. In any case, if Okuayinonu has been stepping up and impacting like Morris is making him out to be, then itâll be huge. The 49ers need someone at defensive end to step up. Okuayinonu can do it. He would flash a few times a game last season, despite the defensive front being mediocre. Heâs decent against the run and the pass. Thereâs some explosiveness and good strength when he snaps off the ball. He was a player I advocated for the 49ers to bring back in free agency. Sure enough, they recognized that they have a solid rotational player on their hands. However, Okuayinonu must now face the reality of being one of the lead rushers with Bosa possibly out. articles.title: Gauff feeling 'incredible' after advancing to second round of US Open
articles.source_type: Live scores, results archive, fixtures and match detail
articles.body: Gauff feeling 'incredible' after advancing to second round of US Open | Flashscore.com All Football Transfer News Premier League US Open Features Champions League Darts Snooker Golf Cycling MLB NFL Most read on Flashscore News Deadline Day LIVE: Balogun decides against Everton move as Sunderland tie up Fofana Swedish tennis ace collapses twice on court during Challenger event in China Man City confirm joint British record signing of Enzo Fernandez from Chelsea Flashscore sources: Everton still keen on Grealish after Richarlison agreement Gauff feeling 'incredible' after advancing to second round of US Open AFP Coco Gauff during US Open first round Marcin Cholewinski / Zuma Press Coco Gauff opened her 2026 US Open campaign with a solid straight-set win over Turkey's Zeynep Sonmez that showcased her improved serve. The fourth-seeded Gauff , who won the New York Grand Slam in 2023, was broken only once to top the 53rd-ranked Sonmez 6-3, 6-4 in a hard-hitting battle fought mostly from the baseline. "It's incredible to be back on this court," an exuberant Gauff told the on-court interviewer. "I love playing in this atmosphere." Sonmez-Gauff matchup stats Flashscore Gauff, whose service woes last year contributed to a fourth-round exit, came into Flushing Meadows this time feeling much better about the stroke, having won the WTA 1000 event in Cincinnati this month. The American star blazed through the opening set without facing a break point, with Sonmez often unable to return Gauff's serve or offering only a weak reply that could be batted off easily. Gauff said she had worked to make the toss more consistent under the tutelage of biomechanics expert Gavin Macmillan, who previously helped Aryna Sabalenka retool her serve, improvements that helped the Belarusian rise to number one. "It's been a gradual change with the serve," Gauff said. "Slowly it's adapting to maybe the way it should look." Gauff broke early in the second set, but the Turkish player raised the level of her game with heavy ground strokes and sneaky forays to the net to finish points with deft volleys. Sonmez broke back for 2-2 and briefly took the lead. But at 2-3, Gauff fought off multiple break points in a lengthy game that the American eventually nabbed with another big serve. Gauff called the hold for 3-3 as "real important." "I like to challenge my opponent to let them keep up the level the whole match, and if they do, you know I clap my hands, and I walk off court with my head held high," Gauff said. "But I was able to settle down." US Open 2026 The US Open is the fourth and final Grand Slam of the tennis season, running from August 30th to September 13th. The rest of the NFL has *six* combined . He leads the NFL in passing touchdowns since 2022. Still only 31 years young, DraftKings has Goff's passing yards over/under (4,099.5) 100 yards higher than any other QB, and his passing touchdown over/under (29.5) ranks third. Lions rank in Supporting Cast Rating 2022: 9th 2023: 2nd 2024: 2nd 2025: 7th Additionally, there's not much reason to expect an overly run-heavy approach in 2026 considering: 1) Petzing's Cardinals led the league in pass attempts in 2025, and 2) The team's decision to trade David Montgomery this offseason. Goff's utter lack of a rushing floor will continue to make him cheap in drafts and cause fantasy nerds to claim he has "no upside." Well, Goff has eight top-5 finishes the last two seasons, which literally only trails Lamar Jackson Josh Allen Jalen Hurts and Joe Burrow . That's it. That's the entire list. I'd say the man is pretty capable of putting up big point totals! For up-to-the-minute updates on injuries, news and everything going on around the NFL, head to RotoWire's NFL Fantasy Football News Today or follow @RotoWireNFL on X. Kyler Murray, Vikings ADP: QB18 (pick 118.6) Kyler Murray hasn't exactly played to the best of his abilities in recent years. His highs in 2020 and 2021 were quite awesome and helped him secure that initial $230.5 million bag from the Cardinals, but unfortunately, things simply haven't been as good in recent years. We can see this quite clearly with adjusted net yards per attempt, which factors in touchdowns, interceptions and sacks into the traditional pass yards-per-attempt equation. So yeah, REALLY not great in 2025 — BUT it's also not like we've been looking at an overly stable situation here both in terms of Kyler's offensive environment as well as his own health. Murray suffered a torn ACL on Dec. 12, 2022 HC Kliff Kingsbury was fired following the 2022 season The Cardinals hired HC Jonathan Gannon and OC Drew Petzing prior to the 2023 season Murray suffered a foot injury in early 2025 that landed him on the sideline for what wound up being the entire season Of course, the latter injury was viewed as a "soft benching" with Jacoby Brissett generally doing a good job of leading this passing offense. This is the toughest obstacle for Kyler truthers to get around: Our most recent sample size of the 2025 season was ROUGH any way you cut it. That said: There's still reason for optimism thanks to three key factors. 1. Some advanced stats still painted Murray in a positive light in 2025. Specifically, EPA per dropback (+0.06, 15th) and PFF passing grade (69.5, tied 22nd). The former mark was better than guys like Joe Burrow Trevor Lawrence and Justin Herbert , while the latter cleared the likes of Lamar Jackson Daniel Jones and Baker Mayfield 2. This remains one of the position's most dangerous rushers. Last season, Murray actually averaged his most rushing yards per game (34.6) since his ACL injury. The film reflects the reality that this is still a dangerous man in the open field . Overall, Murray's average of 8.5 yards per scramble was good for the position's eighth-best mark last season and ranked ahead of guys like Patrick Mahomes and Jaxson Dart 3. Kyler didn't get a ton of help from his friends last season. Specifically, the alleged generational WR Marvin Harrison Jr., who had some rough ( and I mean ROUGH ) moments early in 2025. Overall, this Cardinals offense simply wasn't very QB-friendly. It finished 28th in my " Supporting Cast Rating ," which is the average of every team's rank in PFF rushing, receiving, run-blocking and pass-blocking grades (everything except passing). Good news: Minnesota finished 13th in Supporting Cast Rating last year! You could even argue they're higher when considering the schematic impact that renowned QB whisperer Kevin O'Connell has had on his passing games over the years. The potential for Kyler to improve his passing thanks to this new-and-improved offensive environment and keep on keeping on as a rusher paints the picture of an exciting late-round fantasy QB option in 2026. Malik Willis, Dolphins ADP: QB21 (pick 133.7) Yes, we are dealing with a small sample size with Malik Willis . Originally drafted by the Titans in the third round in 2022, Willis has just six career starts and 155 career pass attempts to his name. Also yes, Willis was absolute nails with his opportunities in Green Bay. Obviously, Matt LaFleur and the offense's plethora of playmakers deserve a lot of credit, but either way: We're looking at a guy who has literally functioned as the NFL's most-efficient passer during the last two seasons. Overall, Willis leads all QBs in yards per attempt, adjusted yards per attempt, yards per completion, completion rate, passer rating and explosive pass play rate since 2024 And yet, it's his performance in two additional stats — EPA per dropback and completion percentage over expected — that are most impressive. That's him all the way up in the top-right-hand corner in the chart below. Not too shabby! Even more impressive was the manner in which he picked up yards in 2025. His 2024 film was definitely a bit gadgety (7.5 average target depth) and featured the Packers HEAVILY lean on their run game, but we saw a legit increase in aDOT in 2025 (9.7 yards!), which reflected the reality that he was hardly being schemed to success. There are downfield DIMES all over the film. And hey, all that is cool before even considering the massive plus that Willis brings to the run game thanks to his explosive rushing ability While he didn't run at the combine, Willis reportedly ran a 4.37-second 40-yard dash at Liberty's Pro Day Willis has averaged the position's fourth-most yards per scramble (8.9) the last two seasons Nobody has averaged more yards per rush (10.6) on read options This latter tool is particularly important when projecting Willis' fantasy impact in Miami. Since 2016, there have been 28 QBs with 100-plus rush attempts in a season, and 26 (93%) finished as a top-12 fantasy QB in fantasy points per game There's also at least some optimism that Bobby Slowik can rekindle some of his 2023 magic; he has spent the better part of the last 15 years working with Kyle Shanahan and Mike McDaniel after all. That said: Willis certainly doesn't check every box we look for. The Dolphins ' cheap/bad WR and TE rooms give them a good case as having the league's worst group of pass-catchers, and Vegas fully expects this offense to be one of the lowest-scoring groups in the league (29th). And yet, the re-draft price is cheap. There should be a weekly borderline QB1 floor here if the history of high-volume dual-threat QBs holds true. Fade these WR/TE busts. Draft season rewards discipline, not headlines. Every year a handful of wide receivers and tight ends get bid up past what the tape and the target competition actually support, and this year's group of overpriced names has some big ones. Fantasy Football Busts 2026 None of the six players below are bad players. They are just priced for outcomes that require the tape, the target competition or their own recent history to cooperate, and I do not like those odds at their current cost. Jameson Williams, WR, Lions - ADP: 60.2 Jameson Williams turned in back-to-back solid seasons, going from a 58-catch, 1,001-yard, seven-touchdown campaign in 2024 to 65 catches for 1,117 yards and seven scores in 2025. That kind of steady growth usually earns a bump in draft rooms, and it has this draft season, but context matters more than the box score suggests. Sam LaPorta 's health did a lot of the heavy lifting last season. With LaPorta on the field, Williams' role shrank to a modest 4.3 targets and 10.2 PPR points per game. Once LaPorta went down, that number jumped to 7.9 targets and 18.4 points. Betting on Williams at this price means betting LaPorta gets hurt again. Williams also posted a drop rate among the worst of any starting wide receiver in 2025, and Detroit's offensive line took a hit this offseason when longtime left tackle Taylor Decker retired. If his replacement struggles protecting Jared Goff 's blind side, the deep shots that fuel Williams' ceiling get harder to complete. Bottom line: Fade Williams. Both of his big seasons had an outside factor propping them up, either a defense in freefall or an injury to the player ahead of him, and he's being drafted as if that production was entirely his own doing. I would rather bet on likely regression than pay this price. For up-to-the-minute updates on injuries, news and everything going on around the NFL, head to RotoWire's NFL Fantasy Football News Today or follow @RotoWireNFL on X. Davante Adams, WR, Rams - ADP: 50.4 Davante Adams found real chemistry with Matthew Stafford in their first year together, scoring 14 touchdowns despite Stafford missing most of training camp. That production kept his price respectable, but the underlying trend points the other way. Adams turns 34 in December and is coming off back-to-back seasons compromised by hamstring injuries. Even before the hamstring injury cost him time last year, his per game numbers had already slipped to 4.3 catches and 56 yards. Scheme is the bigger issue. The Rams went from 46 percent to 50 percent of snaps in 13 personnel after their Week 8 bye, a personnel package that squeezes Adams' snap share. If Stafford's 46-touchdown season regresses even slightly, Adams absorbs the hit directly. Bottom line: Fade Adams. He's a Hall of Fame talent, but betting on a receiver about to turn 34 with recent injury history, in an offense trending toward heavier personnel, does not make sense at his cost. Check out our Fantasy Football ADP Report for a comprehensive tool with live-updated ADP data for multiple league formats and sites. Mike Evans, WR, 49ers - ADP: 67.6 Mike Evans has scored at least 11 touchdowns in each of the last two full seasons, and touchdown production like that tends to keep a receiver's price propped up in fantasy drafts even as everything else about his profile ages. The everything else is the problem. Evans has missed 12 games in his last two seasons and ranks in the bottom-5 percent of the league in yards after catch. Before last year's injuries limited him, he averaged just 11.3 PPR points and 47 yards per game. He has already dealt with two injuries in August. Now he lands on a new team with a new quarterback in Brock Purdy and a new scheme built to create space for receivers rather than lean on the contested catch profile that is all Evans has left. Recent history for receivers his age changing teams and schemes does not favor a smooth transition. Bottom line: Fade Evans. I love him as a player, but Father Time and a scheme mismatch are already working against him. I am not paying a top-30 wide receiver price for one in decline. Brian Thomas, WR, Jaguars - ADP: 83.5 Brian Thomas looked like a foundational piece after an 87-catch, 1,282-yard, 10-touchdown debut. The follow-up season told a different story, with production collapsing to a 48-catch, 707-yard, two-touchdown line as target competition and a changing offense caught up to him. The bigger concern heading into 2026 is role. Jacksonville's staff seems settled on using Thomas primarily as an outside deep threat rather than having him run the full route tree, an approach that caps his weekly target count by design. That profile can produce big plays, but it does not produce the target floor a top wide receiver price requires. Travis Hunter could eat into Thomas' snaps, and the target competition that already ate into Thomas' role last year is not going away. Bottom line: Fade Thomas. A capped role by design plus real target competition is a bad combination at his current price. I would rather find that upside later in the draft. Kyle Pitts, TE, Falcons - ADP: 75.0 Kyle Pitts finally delivered the breakout last season everyone waited years for, catching 88 passes for 928 yards and five touchdowns, the first time he posted more than 53 catches and 667 yards since his rookie season in 2021. That leap shows up in the efficiency marks too, with Pitts ranking in the top 13 percent of tight ends in route efficiency and the top 6 percent in target volume at the position. The path back to that ceiling has real friction this year. Drake London still commands a significant share of the target pie, the quarterback competition between Michael Penix and Tua Tagovailoa is unresolved, and the passing scheme in Atlanta is not built to funnel high raw volume through any one weapon not named London or Bijan Robinson . Remember, Pitts had a massive chunk of his fantasy production when London was injured. Pitts was slightly above his career norms when London was healthy. None of that makes Pitts a bad player. It makes him a tight end whose price assumes last year's leap simply repeats, when the target competition and quarterback uncertainty argue for a steadier, more capped outcome. Bottom line: Fade Pitts. I would rather bank a cheaper floor at the position than pay for a repeat of last year's ceiling with this much target competition and offensive uncertainty in the way. Let him go a round later. Jake Ferguson, TE, Cowboys - ADP: 111.1 Jake Ferguson posted 82 receptions and eight touchdowns last year, both career highs. But his touchdown production says more about touchdown luck than a repeatable role, as his receiving scores have swung wildly since 2023, with five and zero the two years before last season. Ferguson ranks in the bottom 4 percent of tight ends in explosive play rate, his average depth of target sits at just 4.6 yards, and he did not record a single deep completion all season. His yards per reception have declined every year, from 10.7 to 8.4 to 7.3. The role split matters too. With CeeDee Lamb healthy, Ferguson's per game production drops to 7.0 PPR points, and he faded hard down the stretch, failing to top 20 receiving yards in any of his final four games. He is a clear third read behind Lamb and George Pickens when both are healthy. Bottom line: Fade Ferguson. Eight touchdowns on a bottom-of-the-league efficiency profile will not repeat, and he is a name-value pick riding a career year that his underlying numbers do not support. articles.title: More Curious Managing Decisions Cost Orioles Dearly In Loss At Colorado
articles.excerpt: Rookie skipper Craig Albernaz hasn't shown he is up for this, and couldn't get out of his own way in a big spot against the lowly Rockies
articles.source_type: Gameweek squads, team news round-ups, deadline reminders
articles.body: More Curious Managing Decisions Cost Orioles Dearly In Loss At Colorado Sep 1, 2026; Denver, Colorado, USA; Baltimore Orioles pitcher Kyle Bradish (38) pitches in the first inning against the Colorado Rockies at Coors Field. Mandatory Credit: Christopher Hanewinckel-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect It was nothing short of curious that Craig Albernaz would opt to give a 23-year old kid who had barely worked as a reliver in the minors his MLB debut in a 2-2 game in the worst pitching park in MLB, but also totally in character for him. Heâs performed like an overmatched puppet all season â the third handpicked novice baseball exec Mike Elias installed in eight years â and as the moments got bigger for the Orioles on this winning tear to potentially make something of their season, you just knew the skipper would come up small. Giving Luis DeLeon the 7th inning right after Baltimore tied the game was dubious enough. But he also chose not to keep Coby Mayoâs hot bat in the lineup, newly acquired $5M waiver claim Luis Robert Jr. play at all â the lineup came out ridiculously late, in hopes he might one assumes â and we got the return of Heston Kjerstad to the majors for the first time since June 2025 before weâd see Robert make his Orioles debut . Yeah, one is a lefty and the other is a righty â I get the match-ups of it all - but Albernaz didnât handle this like the playoff game it was, his suspect lineup came up short again and the Orioles lost, 4-2, to lowly Colorado at Coors Field. "We had a bunch of guys down because of the workload," Albernaz said, trying to explain why this kid got his debut in that spot. Of course, this being Albernaz, wonderfully out his depth, he couldn't even stick to his own story, again, as before the game he said of De Leon: "We're not going to ambush him and throw him in the fire right away." A victory would have taken them above .500 for the first time since April 14 and secured their second five-game win streak of the season, but Albernaz chose to get experimental instead. They fell to 69-70 and 1.5 games behind the Guardians for the final Wild Card spot. Kyle Bradish, staked to a $100M contract extension, continued to show obvious signs of having not pitched even 40 innings either of the last two years due to Tommy John surgery, and labored to escape five innings, and Elias better get serious about a six-man rotation NOW, Holliday Giveth And Taketh The Orioles barely scratched out two runs Monday in Colorado against a bad starter and horrible staff, needing Colton Cowserâs miracle catch to negate a game-winning homer. They were worse Tuesday against an even worse starter (Gabriel Hughes this time). They scored once Tuesday with Pete Alonso staying in a pickle long enough for a run to score. The other came off Jackson Hollidayâs bat, a solo homer to tie the game (he had three hits against the Rockies, one of his fatherâs former teams, after a great series start in St. Louis, where his dad, Matt, also starred). But Holliday dropped an absolutely routine pop up to start the seventh, with De Leon making his first pitches ever on an MLB mound and only recently converting to the pen in preparation for what he projects to here. Mickey Moniak wheeled all the way to second and two batters later TJ Rumfield hammered a center-cut slider for a two-run lead. The Oâs were lucky it wasnât worse and Bradish was lucky he was facing a bad team (Colorado snapped a 10-game losing streak at home). Bradish couldnât miss bats, again (8 swing and miss), and he couldnât throw enough strikes and he was pitching out of jams starting in the first inning. Albernaz left him out to dry last time out when he was clearly not right after consecutive walks and he needed 95 pitches to survive five innings here. Bradish threw 48 sinkers (more than half his total) and got a total of eight called strikes and whiffs with that pitch. That wonât play, and is troubling. "Battling command a little bit," is what Albernaz mustered, still probably not seeing Bradish's situation for what it is. Bradish isnât getting any ground balls (two in this game) and heâs allowed 47 hits inÂ 34 2/3 innings over his last seven starts, allowing five homers in that span. He has just 27 strikeouts in those starts and he and Brandon Young and Wednesdayâs starter, Trevor Rogers, are all showing serious signs of fatigue. articles.body: New Jersey Devils trade for Luke Evangelista | Flashscore.com All Football Transfer News Premier League US Open Features Champions League Darts Snooker Golf Cycling MLB NFL Most read on Flashscore News Deadline Day LIVE: Balogun decides against Everton move as Sunderland tie up Fofana Swedish tennis ace collapses twice on court during Challenger event in China Flashscore sources: Everton still keen on Grealish after Richarlison agreement Man City confirm joint British record signing of Enzo Fernandez from Chelsea New Jersey Devils acquire Luke Evangelista from Predators for draft picks Eric Himmelheber Nashville Predators' Luke Evangelista George Walker IV / CTK / AP The New Jersey Devils acquired forward Luke Evangelista from the Nashville Predators in exchange for a 2028 conditional first-round pick and a 2028 second-round pick. Evangelista , 24, has spent all four years of his NHL career with the Preds. The Toronto, Ontario, native is coming off a career season after posting 56 points with 12 goals and a career-high 44 assists, which shattered his previous best of 23. After being selected 42nd overall in the 2020 NHL Draft, Evangelista wouldn't make his debut until the 2022-2023 season, when he put up seven goals and eight assists in 24 games, putting together an average ice time of 16:34, which was almost a full three minutes more than the following two seasons. Despite averaging 13:57 of ice time in his second season, Evangelista put up what is still a career-high 16 goals, along with 23 assists, in 80 games. He would have a down season in 2024-2025 (10g, 22a) after missing four weeks with a lower-body injury, playing in 68 games, before bouncing back this past year. The Devils needed a top-six winger. Now Evangelista has a chance to help both the Devils and himself. The right wing playmaker is currently in the final year of his two-year, $6 million deal and is set to become a restricted free agent after this season. articles.title: Tiger Woods' Son Charlie Helps Benjamin Win American Heritage Invitational
articles.excerpt: Charlie Woods opens his senior season helping The Benjamin School win the American Heritage Golf Invitational as the Buccaneers chase another FHSAA Class 1A title.
articles.source_type: Gameweek squads, team news round-ups, deadline reminders
articles.body: Tiger Woods' Son Charlie Helps Benjamin Win American Heritage Invitational Charlie Woods, the son of Tiger Woods, is trying to help The Benjamin School pursue another Florida golf state championship | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect There are still plenty of rounds ahead for Charlie Woods, including those that will eventually take him from high school golf to Florida State. But his final season at Benjamin School has begun in a familiar place: with his team holding a trophy. Woods Helps the Buccaneers Open the Season with a Win Woods helped Benjamin win the American Heritage Golf Invitational in Plantation, Florida, as the Buccaneers opened another season with championship expectations. Woods and teammate Brooks Colton led Benjamin to the team title, an early marker for a program attempting to repeat as FHSAA Class 1A state champion. Woods and Colton tied for first, each shooting a 3-under par 69. The Son of Tiger Woods Has Long Endure the Spotlght For Woods, the tournament also represents the beginning of the last chapter of a high school career that has unfolded under considerably more attention than most. That comes with the last name. The son of 15-time major champion Tiger Woods has spent years playing junior tournaments and appearing alongside his father at the PNC Championship, where every swing can become a highlight and every result can become a headline. His senior season at Benjamin offers something slightly different. This is his team. His school. And one final opportunity to chase a state championship before college golf begins. Florida State Will Be His Next Stop Woods committed to Florida State last year, choosing the Seminoles as the next stop in a golf career that has been watched closely since long before he was old enough to drive himself to the course. Before Tallahassee, however, there is still work remaining with the Buccaneers. Benjamin captured the Class 1A state championship last fall â Woods carding a 4-under 68 in the final round â and he enters his senior year as one of the recognizable faces of a program attempting to do it again. The American Heritage Invitational is only an early-season tournament. It will not define Woods' senior year, and it certainly will not tell us what kind of golfer he will become at Florida State or beyond. But senior seasons are collections of lasts: last first tournament, last regular season, last run toward a state championship with the teammates who helped make high school feel like something more than a waiting room for whatever comes next. For Charlie Woods, the last first has already ended with a tournament win. Add us as a preferred source on Google Follow Loading recommendations... articles.body: Ipswich vs Liverpool Prediction, Lineups & Team News | RotoWire Ipswich Town vs Liverpool Prediction, Predicted Lineups & Team News Ipswich Town vs Liverpool prediction, predicted lineups, team news, injuries, odds and tactical analysis for Friday’s Premier League match at Portman Road. September 1, 2026 Share By: Adam Zdroik @RotoZdroik September 1, 2026 Game Previews Mock Draft Simulator Prep for your 2026 Fantasy Football draft with free, unlimited drafts, and real-time grades. Ipswich Town vs Liverpool Prediction, Predicted Lineups & Team News Ipswich Town host Liverpool at Portman Road on Friday night with the visitors still searching for their first Premier League win of the season. Liverpool have taken two points from two matches, but both required late rescue acts: a 99th-minute penalty at Newcastle and an 82nd-minute equalizer against Nottingham Forest. That is why our Ipswich Town vs Liverpool prediction leans toward a draw despite Liverpool entering as heavy favorites. Andoni Iraola's side have struggled to control games for long stretches, while Ipswich have scored in both league matches and already shown they can make bigger sides uncomfortable. Victor Munoz has been Liverpool's new difference-maker, producing the decisive moment in both games, and he is projected to start again Friday. Bradley Barcola is also available after completing his blockbuster move from Paris Saint-Germain on Monday, giving Iraola another option as Liverpool try to turn late recoveries into a complete performance. This preview covers predicted lineups injury news , head-to-head history, the tactical matchup and a score prediction for Friday's Premier League game in Suffolk. When & Where to Watch (USA) Friday, Sept. 4 at 8:00 PM BST / 3:00 PM ET / 12:00 PM PT Venue: Portman Road, Ipswich English TV: USA Network Streaming: Peacock, Fubo, Sling Blue, DirecTV Stream Ipswich Town vs Liverpool Lineups & Injury News Ipswich Town vs Liverpool Predicted Lineups Predicted lineups: Ipswich are projected to name the same XI that started at Old Trafford, though Emersonn is a genuine doubt after limping out of that game. Liverpool are projected in a 4-2-3-1 with Victor Munoz and Cody Gapko again starting on the wings, and Barcola available but not in the XI five days after signing. This widget updates automatically when official lineups drop. Ipswich Town IPS Liverpool LIV Predicted Predicted Ipswich Town Predicted Lineup not yet posted Check back closer to kickoff Liverpool Predicted Lineup not yet posted Check back closer to kickoff Confirmed Predicted Lineups via RotoWire Ipswich Town predicted starting XI (4-2-3-1): Kjell Scherpen Dara O'Shea Issa Diop Jacob Greaves Leif Davis Sasa Lukic Marcelino Nunez Abdul Fatawu Julio Enciso Daizen Maeda Emersonn Liverpool predicted starting XI (4-2-3-1): Alisson Jeremie Frimpong Jeremy Jacquet Virgil van Dijk Milos Kerkez Ryan Gravenberch Dominik Szoboszlai Victor Munoz Florian Wirtz Cody Gakpo Alexander Isak Check the Premier League injury table and the player news feed before kickoff because there are still some questions. Ipswich Town Team News & Injuries Emersonn is the one to watch. Ipswich's club-record striker scored on his Premier League debut against Sunderland, then jarred his knee in the first half at Old Trafford and came off. Gary O'Neil was hopeful rather than reassuring afterwards: "we're hopeful it's not serious. It was like a landing and a jarring of the knee." He also conceded "it could be anything at this stage." Chuba Akpom , who scored the consolation at Old Trafford, is the alternative. Jaden Philogene is out with an ankle problem into the middle of the month, which matters beyond his absence because he is second on Ipswich's penalty list. Azor Matusiwa and Jack Taylor are both unavailable, and Florentino Luis , the 16 million pound arrival from Burnley, is still a fitness concern. Exequiel Palacios is the newest option. Ipswich signed the Argentina midfielder from Bayer Leverkusen on Aug. 27 on a deal to 2030, and he is a World Cup winner, though the club were awaiting visa clearance when they announced him. Emersonn does not make it, Ipswich lose the only player who has scored a goal from open play for them this season and the shape becomes Akpom or nothing. Liverpool Team News & Injuries The headline is an arrival rather than an absence. Bradley Barcola completed a move from Paris Saint-Germain on Monday for 106 million pounds rising to 123 million, signing a five-year deal and taking the No. 29 shirt, and he was expected to train with the group before Friday. He is not in the projected XI, which makes his involvement the first real selection question Andoni Iraola has had to answer. Munoz is the other one. He replaced Ngumoha on 63 minutes at Newcastle and won the penalty that rescued a point in the 99th, then came on against Nottingham Forest and scored the equalizer in the 82nd. Iraola singled out his work off the ball: "Victor has played really well. Defensively and offensively he did a very good job and was always a threat." The injury list is long but stable. Conor Bradley is out after knee surgery and Giovanni Leoni is still working back from an ACL injury, so Frimpong covers right back. Hugo Ekitike is out until 2027 with a ruptured Achilles and Federico Chiesa has a back problem. Joe Gomez is closest to a return. Curtis Jones has gone, completing a move to Inter Milan. The XI therefore looks settled apart from one place, and the 106 million pound winger is sitting behind it. Ipswich Town vs Liverpool Head-to-Head Record These clubs have met 74 times, with Liverpool winning 39 to Ipswich's 14 and 21 drawn. The relevant run is longer than most: Ipswich have not beaten Liverpool since Dec. 10, 2000, a nine-game winless stretch spanning nearly 26 years. Portman Road is worse. Liverpool are unbeaten in their last seven visits and have not lost a league game here since the 1985-86 season. The two meetings in Ipswich's last top-flight campaign both went Liverpool's way, 2-0 here in August 2024 in Ipswich's first top-flight match in 22 years, and 4-1 at Anfield in January 2025. Ipswich Town vs Liverpool Tactical Analysis Liverpool are 13th with two points, and the way they got them is the reason this game is live. They trailed at Newcastle and needed a stoppage-time penalty, then trailed twice at home to Forest and equalized in the 82nd minute. The first-half numbers against Forest were alarming for a side at Anfield: 0.25 expected goals to 1.29, and no big chances to three. Iraola has not tried to dress it up. "We were quite passive without the ball," he said afterwards, and pointed out that both Forest goals came from throw-ins that Liverpool "didn't defend properly." His closing line was blunter still: "I hope this serves as a lesson for the future." He also has the strangest possible context for the job, because his Bournemouth side finished sixth last season, three points behind the Liverpool team whose manager he replaced. Liverpool finished fifth, sacked Arne Slot a year after winning the title, and lost Mohamed Salah Ibrahima Konate and Andrew Robertson on free transfers. Ipswich are 12th, a point above them, and their two games have been opposites. They beat Sunderland with seven new signings in the starting XI, then conceded five at Old Trafford after leading through Leif Davis . O'Neil's own diagnosis was about duration rather than quality: "we lost control of the momentum. How we respond for the last half-hour is what we need to get better at." That is the question Friday asks, because a promoted side leading Liverpool at home on a Friday night has to survive the last half-hour to get anything out of it. What Ipswich do have is a spine built from O'Neil's last job. He arrived from Strasbourg in June and Ipswich then signed two players from there, Julio Enciso for around 30 million pounds and Abdoul Ouattara for 17 million. Enciso has been their best player, setting up the move for the winner against Sunderland and looking lively at Old Trafford, and O'Neil has been unusually warm about him: "it's rare to find a player like him. He's desperate to help the team." Ipswich Town vs Liverpool Odds Liverpool are around -180 on the road and Ipswich are out past +400, with the draw near +340. For more markets and the rest of the matchweek, see RotoWire's soccer betting page and the best sportsbook promos Ipswich Town vs Liverpool Key Matchups Alexander Isak Issa Diop and Jacob Greaves Isak scored his first of the season against Forest and is the one Liverpool player whose finishing can settle a game like this without the rest of the performance being any good. Diop and Greaves kept Sunderland to a single goal and then had an afternoon at Old Trafford neither will want back, with Greaves putting through his own net off a Harry Maguire shot. The pairing defends the box reasonably well and struggles when it has to defend space, which is precisely what Isak wants. If Ipswich sit deep and compact he will have a quiet hour. If they push out to chase the game, he decides it. Julio Enciso Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai Enciso is the most likely source of anything Ipswich create, and Liverpool's double pivot is where Iraola says his team went passive. Gravenberch is one of the better ball-carrying midfielders in the league but Liverpool conceded both Forest goals from throw-ins, which is the sort of second-phase sloppiness a No. 10 with Enciso's close control punishes. Ipswich also have Marcelino Nunez and Sasa Lukic behind him rather than in front, so Enciso gets to play facing forward. Whoever wins that zone decides whether this is a Liverpool possession exercise or a genuinely awkward Friday night. Ipswich Town Corners & free kicks: Leif Davis Sasa Lukic Abdul Fatawu Marcelino Nunez Jack Clarke Penalties: Julio Enciso Jack Clarke Jaden Philogene Liverpool Corners & free kicks: Dominik Szoboszlai Cody Gakpo Florian Wirtz Alexis Mac Allister Penalties: Dominik Szoboszlai Alexander Isak Enciso could be Ipswich's main PK taker, though that information has yet to be revealed. Szoboszlai has already converted one for Liverpool this season, in the 99th minute at St James' Park. Ipswich Town vs Liverpool Prediction Liverpool are the better side, but they have not controlled either league match yet and Ipswich have scored in both of theirs. Portman Road on a Friday night is exactly the kind of game that can punish a side still searching for rhythm. If Emersonn misses out, Ipswich lose some punch, but Liverpool have yet to keep a clean sheet and I'm not ready to trust either defense. articles.body: Indiana vs North Texas: How to Watch the Season Opener Brady Quinn welcomes fans during the BIg Noon Kickoff before the Indiana versus UCLA football game at Memorial Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 25, 2025. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect College Football is finally back, and the focus can shift from the courtroom to the field. Indiana Hoosiers fans will have their program spotlighted on national TV as FOX's Big Noon Kickoff game on Saturday against North Texas - after all, Indiana the defending national champion. How to Watch Indiana vs North Texas Who: No. 6 Miami (0-0) vs. North Texas (0-0) When: Saturday, Sept. 5, 12 p.m. ET Where: Bloomington, Indiana TV: FOX (Gus Johnson, Joel Klatt, Jenny Taft) Radio: IU Radio Network (Don Fischer and Buck Suhr) Series history: Tied 1-1 Last meeting: The Hoosiers and Mean Green have met twice in their histories. The last meeting came in 2014 when Kevin Wilson was guiding the Hoosiers and Nate Sudfeld threw for over 300 yards in a 49-24 win for Indiana. Last Time Out: Both teams will be playing their first game of the 2026 season. As good as Indiana has been, it hasn't started the first two seasons under Curt Cignetti like it might have wanted to - Indiana beat FIU 31-7 in the 2024 season opener, and 27-14 over Old Dominion last year. Indiana is coming off a 16-0 season that saw the Hoosiers raise the national championship trophy after defeating Miami 27-21. While many of the heroes from 2025 have moved on to the next level, there will be plenty of star power on the field. Indiana returns All-Americans on both sides of the ball, headlined by offensive lineman Carter Smith. While quarterback Josh Hoover is the new guy in town, he has over 9,000 passing yards and 71 touchdowns to his name. Hoover will have plenty of weapons to throw to as Charlie Becker returns and is joined by Nick Marsh and Tyler Morris. The running game has its weapons too, with Turbo Richard coming in from Boston College to join Khobie Martin and Lee Beebe Jr. The Indiana defense may be one of the best units in the country. Isaiah Jones and Rolijah Hardy man the middle of the defense while Tyrique Tucker heads up a strong defensive line unit. Playoff hero Jamari Sharpe returns to lock down opponents' top wide receivers. Indiana is riding a 15-game home winning streak and will see a sellout crowd fill the stands in Memorial Stadium for the fifth-straight home game. Fans will be treated to several special events that will celebrate Indiana's run to the national title last season. Add us as a preferred source on Google Follow Loading recommendations...
