articles.title: Blue Jays Bring Up Ricky Tiedemann, Sean Keys in Flurry of September Moves
articles.excerpt: The Blue Jays promoted Ricky Tiedemann and Sean Keys, activated Joe Mantiply and Josh Smith, and designated Daz Cameron for assignment.
articles.source_type: Gameweek squads, team news round-ups, deadline reminders
articles.body: Blue Jays Bring Up Ricky Tiedemann, Sean Keys in Flurry of September Moves Ricky Tiedemann walks back to the dugout against the New York Yankees Credit: Nick Turchiaro-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Toronto Blue Jays geared up for the final month of the season with a flurry of roster moves. The team recalled left-hander Ricky Tiedemann and infielder Sean Keys while activating Joe Mantiply and Josh Smith from the injured list. Outfielder Daz Cameron was designated for assignment, while right-hander Simeon Woods Richardson cleared waivers and elected free agency. Tiedemann and Keys are the two biggest beneficiaries of todayâs moves, and both can use September to show why they should factor into Torontoâs roster plans for 2027 and beyond. Two Youngsters Get Their Chance To Shine Sean Keys celebrates hitting a three-run home run against the New York Mets Credit: Nick Turchiaro-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Tiedemann looked solid in his lone Major-League appearance, pitching 1 2/3 innings against the New York Yankees on Aug. 15. Questions remained about how his stuff would look following Tommy John surgery; his fastball provided an encouraging answer, averaging 96.2 mph according to Statcast . His stay was brief, however, as roster logistics forced Toronto to option him back to Triple-A when Brendon Little returned from the paternity list. Since being sent down, Tiedemann has worked exclusively out of the bullpen, posting a 4.50 ERA. The change in usage is still worth noting, though. The 24-year-old originally rose through the minors as a starter, so Toronto's decision to give him regular relief work could offer a glimpse of another role for him moving forward. Keysâ questions are less about health and more about where he can find playing time. The 23-year-old struggled during his first MLB stint, going 6-for-36 with one home run, but he has been excellent in Triple-A, posting a .303/.422/.622 slash line across 51 games. Keys is most accustomed to playing first and third base, but he has also received reps in the corner outfield, giving Toronto several ways to work his bat into the lineup. Utility man Josh Smith returns after dealing with hamstring inflammation. He has struggled overall this season, hitting .220/.303/.305, but his limited time with Toronto has been considerably better. In 14 games with the Blue Jays, Smith is hitting .250/.323/.464 with a .787 OPS. Joe Mantiply is another useful addition. The veteran has posted a 2.04 ERA out of Torontoâs bullpen this season, relying more on movement and location than overpowering velocity. His primary pitch, a sinker, averages just 88.8 mph, while his breaking pitches generally sit in the low 80s. The sinker has actually been his most vulnerable offering, with opposing hitters batting .346 and slugging .500 against it. Daz Cameron ended up being the odd man out. The 29-year-old struggled to make much of an impact during his time with Toronto, posting a lowly .575 OPS in 24 at-bats. With more depth pieces returning and younger players getting opportunities, Cameron became expendable. The Blue Jays have played well over their last 10 games, going 6-4, but they still sit last in the AL East and 1.5 games behind the final American League Wild Card spot. Toronto is hoping the incoming reinforcements are enough to help them sneak into the postseason. Add us as a preferred source on Google Follow Loading recommendations... articles.title: Ole Miss’ National Marketing ‘Means a Lot’ to Trinidad Chambliss and Kewan Lacy
articles.excerpt: OXFORD | Throughout the offseason Ole Miss has magnified its star offensive backfield by marketing Trinidad Chambliss and Kewan Lacy at every opportunity it could.
articles.source_type: Gameweek squads, team news round-ups, deadline reminders
articles.body: Ole Missâ National Marketing âMeans a Lotâ to Trinidad Chambliss and Kewan Lacy Ole Miss RB Kewan Lacy and QB Trinidad Chambliss featured on the electronic billboards in the streets of New York City in August. | Ole Miss Athletics OXFORD | Throughout the offseason Ole Miss has magnified its star offensive backfield by marketing Trinidad Chambliss and Kewan Lacy at every opportunity it could.Â In July, the program ignited its Heisman Trophy campaign by selling buttons, stickers and yard signs reading âH6I5MENâ. The two also joined Pete Golding in Tampa, Florida for SEC Media Days later in the month, shortly after each inked NIL deals with Nike. Towards the end of August, Ole Miss marketed its offensive stars nationally by putting their faces and images all over Times Square in New York City and the Sphere in Las Vegas.Â âItâs been crazy,â Chambliss said following Tuesdayâs practice. âSeeing my face and seeing Ole Miss football on the billboards and on the screens and Times Square â then obviously the Sphere as well was just unbelievable. Never wouldâve thought that my face or my team would be in that position.âÂ Â Â Â âIt means a lot,â Lacy added. âJust having the opportunity to be on that platform in New York and Las Vegas is just amazing. Being one of the candidates with Trinidad is just a great opportunityâ¦.I just try to focus on the main thing. God first and just being prepared for the moment because I know that the day is going to come when we go back on the field and just have fun and play ball.âÂ A Growing Bond Ole Miss running back Kewan Lacy smiles as quarterback Trinidad Chambliss asks him a few questions during the CFP and Fiesta Bowl Media Day at the JW Marriott Scottsdale Camelback Inn Resort & Spa, in Scottsdale, Ariz., on Tuesday, Jan. 6, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Back when Chambliss was on his initial visit to Oxford last spring, as a little-known quarterback brought in to be a one-year backup, Lacy was the first teammate that met with him and his family.Â Â âKewan was the first Rebel that we ended up having lunch with during the recruitment,â Trinidadâs father, Trent Chambliss, previously told Ole Miss On SI. âJust a fine young man since day one. Hardworking as well (and) highly skilled. From my understanding, just a great individual overall.â âI feel like our bond just keeps getting better and better. I had lunch with him and his family on his visit here. It was great just meeting him before everything, and then just seeing him grow has just been amazing,â Lacy explained Tuesday. âItâs just super exciting knowing that itâs more to come. Iâm just super excited for me and him.âÂ The Rebelsâ first round hopeful running back has seen plenty of growth from his quarterback since that lunch.Â Â âReally just his growth as a leader,â Lacy said of Chambliss. âI feel like he stepped into that role early on, but he wasnât a starter coming into the season. Now having a whole spring, fall camp (and) summer under his belt, I feel like he stepped (further) into the leadership role.â As the summer heat starts to wind down and the calendar turns to September, No. 9 Ole Miss remains just five days away from spotting the ball against No. 24 Louisville in what will be a pivotal start in Nashville. After all of the up and down offseason talk from national talking heads, Chambliss and Lacy are just ready to see a defense other than Pete Goldingâs for the first time since the Fiesta Bowl back in January.Â The star duo have their full attention on the Cardinalsâ defense.Â Â âReally just how physical they are,â Lacy said of Louisvilleâs defense. âTheyâre competitive, so itâs going to be a good game. Good, hard, game.â âVery high motor,â Chambliss added. âThey play hard, they play physical. They beat Miami last year. Theyâre a well coached team, very high motor and they got some good guys over thereâ¦Itâs kind of been the same mindset the whole offseason, knowing that Iâm QB1. But, I mean, Iâm not going to attack any other way that it was last year. Itâs just another game and Iâm going to attack it the same way I did all the other games last year.â Kickoff between the Rebels and Cardinals on Sept. 6 is set for 6:30 p.m. CT on ABC.Â Sign up to Facebook and for the latest news surrounding the Ole Miss Rebels. articles.title: Jack Grealish Is One Big-Money Signing Man City Won’t Make Any Return on
articles.excerpt: Everton have re-signed the winger on a second season-long loan deal.
articles.source_type: Gameweek squads, team news round-ups, deadline reminders
articles.body: Jack Grealish Is One Big-Money Signing Man City Wonât Make Any Return on Jack Grealish is out of contract in Manchester in 2027. | Marc Atkins/Getty Images Jack Grealish will spend a second season on loan at Everton from Manchester City, taking the winger to the end of his contract and into free agency next summer. While Manchester City have been making a killing from selling fringe and unwanted playersâdeals for James Trafford, Tijjani Reijnders, SÃ¡vio and Nico GonzÃ¡lez alone this summer will raise up to $317 million (Â£234 million)âGrealish is a former record-signing that City cannot now recoup anything for. By the time this loan ends next June, his contract at the Etihad Stadium will also be up, leaving Evertonâor an alternative suitorâin position to recruit him permanently on a free transfer Manchester City triggered a release clause in Grealishâs Aston Villa contract in 2021 to make him the clubâs first nine-figure signing only surpassed since by Elliot Anderson . He has made 159 appearances, including two this season after returning from a first Everton loan, and played a major role during the 2022â23 Premier League, FA Cup, Champions League treble campaign. Grealish suffered from injuries and a loss of form in the subsequent two seasons, coinciding with the rise of electric Belgium international JÃ©rÃ©my Doku. Pep Guardiola expressed hope that the player, who turns 31 next week, would rediscover himself and rise again, but it didnât happen while he was still in Manchester. That paved the way to join Everton on a 12-month deal last summer. Grealish Central to Evertonâs European Hopes Jack is BACK! ð pic.twitter.com/gz1x19oLHS â Everton (@Everton) September 1, 2026 That first Everton move was exactly the rejuvenation Grealish needed. He started last season at 100mph, registering four assists in his first three appearances for the club and won Premier League Player of the Month for Augustâthe first such award of his career. But Grealish suffered a foot injury in January that both prematurely ended his season and killed any chance of playing his way back onto the England roster in time for the 2026 World Cup. By returning to Everton, now back at full health, he will hope to pick where he left off nine months ago. Grealish also stands to benefit from Iliman Ndiaye heading in the opposite direction in an $88 million (Â£65 million) deal, because it puts more of the creative responsibility onto him. Without Grealish, Everton lacked a final push in the finishing straight of last season and slipped from eighth to 13th in the Premier League standings, missing out on European qualification that had been within reach. The Toffees havenât participated in a UEFA competition for almost 10 yearsâsince 2017â18âand Grealish could be the juice they need to break that streak. For him personally, playing a home European Championship with England in 2028 is also a possibility if things go well. articles.title: Mariners’ Lázaro Montes Makes MLB Debut vs. Red Sox Amid Playoff Desperation
articles.excerpt: Lázaro Montes makes his MLB debut for the Mariners against the Red Sox, bringing elite power, major swing-and-miss risk and a badly needed September jolt.
articles.source_type: Gameweek squads, team news round-ups, deadline reminders
articles.body: Marinersâ LÃ¡zaro Montes Makes MLB Debut vs. Red Sox Amid Playoff Desperation Feb 20, 2025; Peoria, AZ, USA; Seattle Mariners outfielder Lazaro Montes poses for a portrait during media day at Peoria Sports Complex. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images | USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Connect The Mariners have reached the point of the season where their last hope arrives wearing No. 99 and carrying only 44 games of Triple-A experience. LÃ¡zaro Montes is in Seattleâs lineup today at Fenway Park, batting seventh and serving as the DH against the Red Sox. The 21-year-old is no longer something Mariners fans have to dream about. Heâs here, and heâs immediately being plugged in a lineup that needs to become more interesting. As exciting as his debut sounds, we need to be realistic about what it represents for the Mariners. This is an act of desperation. And thatâs not to say Montes didnât earn the call. But the temperature in the room says it all. The Mariners will enter Montesâ debut at 64-74, riding a five-game losing streak and sitting 5.5 games behind the final AL Wild Card spot. Theyâre asking a kid who began the year in Double-A to provide the jolt their established lineup never consistently found. Lazaro Montes is all set to make his MLB debut! #TridentsUp pic.twitter.com/8NCF7YPE67 â Seattle Mariners (@Mariners) September 1, 2026 LÃ¡zaro Montes Must Adjust Quickly to Major-League Pitching It makes perfect sense. Montes earned this opportunity by hitting the ball absurdly hard. He finished his minor-league season with 38 home runs and a .928 OPS across Double-A Arkansas and Triple-A Tacoma. He hit 10 homers in 25 August games alone, posting a 1.054 OPS during his final month with the Rainiers. He also did that by hitting from launching pads in the Pacific Coast League. The power isnât a myth. Montes produced a 94.9 mph average exit velocity and a 57.5 percent hard-hit rate at Triple-A. When he barrels one up, expect fireworks. Itâs a threat Seattle desperately needs. Montes has the ability to flip a game with one at-bat and one swing. Bringing the boom. #TridentsUp pic.twitter.com/ba3KcNxCqb â Mariners Player Development (@MsPlayerDev) September 1, 2026 Then comes the obvious concern: the first look at Montes could be a complete dud. That isnât rooting for failure. Itâs accepting the other side of the coin here. Montes struck out in 30.6 percent of his plate appearances this season, while his 34.3 percent in-zone whiff rate was the highest among 360 Triple-A hitters who saw at least 750 pitches. Elevated fastballs and breaking balls below the zone have given him problems, and left-handed pitching has been particularly difficult. Major-league pitchers will find those holes quickly. We should expect some ugly at-bats. Colt Emersonâs rookie season already reminded us that even an advanced young hitter can get buried by major-league swing-and-miss. The two prospects have different offensive profiles, but the lesson remains that patience has to come with the package. With Montes, weâre going to have to take the towering home runs with the empty swings. There could be nights when he walks back to the dugout three times without touching the ball. Seattle has to live with that. The timing of this debut exposes the larger organizational failure. The Mariners scored eight runs Monday, carried an 8-5 lead beyond the seventh inning and still lost 9-8 in extras. One day earlier, they managed one hit in a 7-0 loss to Toronto. This team can find completely different routes to the same miserable destination. The veteran roster was supposed to keep Seattleâs season stable while prospects such as Montes developed. Now the prospect is being asked to supply the spark. Batting him seventh at DH is the right opening move. More importantly, keep him in the lineup. Seattle has indicated that his playing time will be evaluated day to day as he adjusts to major-league pitching, but that evaluation cannot be made over his first few games. Montes deserves enough runway to struggle, adjust and show whether his power can play at this level. A rough first week cannot become an excuse to bench him. articles.title: Tulane's Hall is "Concentrating on Us" Leading Up to Duke
articles.excerpt: The first of September brought the first pre-game press conference for the Wave, starting with head coach Will Hall
articles.source_type: Gameweek squads, team news round-ups, deadline reminders
articles.body: Tulane's Hall is "Concentrating on Us" Leading Up to Duke Sep 16, 2023; Hattiesburg, Mississippi, USA; Former Southern Miss Golden Eagles head coach Will Hall gestures in the second half against the Tulane Green Wave at M.M. Roberts Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Chuck Cook-USA TODAY Sports | USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Connect Tulane Football Schedule 2026 Week 1 - Â at Duke , September 5 Week 2 - Â South Alabama , September 12 Week 3 -Â at Kansas State , September 19 Week 4 -Â Southern Miss , September 26 Week 5 - OPEN DATE, October 3 Week 6 -Â at Army , October 10 Week 7 -Â Memphis , October 16 Week 8 -Â UTSA , October 24 Week 9 -Â at Charlotte , October 30 Week 10 -Â Tulsa , November 7 Week 11 -Â at Rice , November 14 Week 12 - North Texas, November 21 Week 13 - at South Florida, November 27 Sign up for the weeklyÂ On Si Tulane "[The season's] been a long time coming, and I know we're really ready to play," head coach Will Hall opened with during Tuesday's press conference. Tulane's first game against Duke is this Saturday at 2:30pm CT , and we'll have much more coverage to come. So stay tuned to On SI Tulane for all of your Green Wave news. The Looming Season What we've seen on social media at On SI is that there is a lot of valid questions regarding this new Tulane team. Travelling into the ACC champion's house and coming out with a victory is no easy feat for any team in college football, so TU will have to be prepared for a gritty, grind-em-out game against the Blue Devils. "(We've) got a tremendous challenge coming this weekend, everybody knows that. Duke (is) a really good team..." is what coach Hall closed his opening statement with. When asked about how he felt about the upcoming season, in general, he replied: "I'm just blessed man... Just trying to take advantage of everyday, and get better every day. That's how I live my life." He continued: "Our guys are going to play hard (on) Saturday. I know that everyone's going to play their tail off for each other. That's what we do at Tulane." Not Just a Rematch Although the Green Wave faced the Blue Devils last season, the rematch really isn't the story here. The story is about two conference champions facing off in week one. We believe it is amplified even more when you take into account that Duke is a P4 champion (ACC), and Tulane is a G6 champion (American). When asked about the perspective of this title heavy bout, Hall had to say, "Maybe so. Honestly, I really don't look at what everybody is talking about. I know we've got a good football team (and) I know we've got to prove that... I know Duke has a good football team... We've got an exciting schedule in front of us, but it's one we're excited about." Speaking to last year's game, Hall acknowledged the story and weight behind last year's match up, specifically regarding Mensah's return to New Orleans after transferring to Duke. More importantly, however, coach Hall was more focused on the here and now, "Obviously (these are) two different teams... The thing we're doing is, we're concentrating on us... We're looking forward to showing what we've got." The Keys If TU wishes to start their season with a statement win in Durham, they'll first have to stop second year running back, Nathan Sheppard We talked about Sheppard extensively during our opponent previews, but if Tulane wants success, they'll have to hold him in check. "[He's] really hard to tackle." Hall said. "We know that we'll have to rally to tackle him, he rarely ever gets tackled by just one person, so he presents a lot of challenges," he finished. Another key will be the quarterback play, which has been of concern for quite some time. Until last Monday , there had been no announcement as to who would start week one for the Green Wave. Ultimately, the job would fall into Zeon Chriss-Gremillion's hands to take the reigns of this Wave offense. Coach Hall said more of the same when it came to Zeon and what he wants out of his starting quarterback. Zeon will need the "right eyes" because if his eyes aren't right, then he's failed the first step at being a good quarterback. Coach Hall repeated what he had said at an earlier press conference this Fall, "There's going to be about five opportunities in every game for a quarterback to win the game." Hall wants his quarterback dialed and locked in with little mistakes. Talkin' Duke "Their head coach ( Manny Diaz ) runs the defense," Hall responded after being asked what stuck out about the Blue Devil defense. "I've got a lot of respect for him... we know they're going to play hard," he finished. When asked about San Jose State transfer and starting Duke quarterback, Walker Eget , Hall said, "He really can (throw the ball)... He made some great throws while he was at SJS, (and) he's coming off an injury." Coach Hall had a lot of respect for the transfer quarterback and his experience, and if the Wave wish to throw him off his game, this young defensive line will have to get active and physical. "(Eget has) seen it before." Hall spoke more to Eget's experience with yet another analogy: "People can tell you what it's like to ride a bike, but until you ride one you just don't understand it, and (Eget has) ridden the bike a lot." articles.title: Nebraska Center Justin Evans Earns Prestigious Honor From Teammates
articles.excerpt: Evans is the acknowledged leader of the offensive line. He was voted a single-digit jersey and even though he can’t wear it, it shows the respect he has earned
articles.source_type: Gameweek squads, team news round-ups, deadline reminders
articles.body: Nebraska Center Justin Evans Earns Prestigious Honor From Teammates Nebraska center Justin Evans is the established leader of the Huskers' offensive line. | Nebraska Athletics Beyond an effective quarterback, running backs and receivers, football offenses â Nebraskaâs included â need a quality offensive line to make the motor purr. Nebraskaâs offensive line dominated much of the offseason talk . Improvements were needed. Money was invested. Leadership of the new offensive line falls on the broad shoulders of center Justin Evans . Centers tend to be O-line leaders, but Evansâ leadership comes from his personality and many other intangibles. He was one of three Huskers who went to Big Ten Media Days in Chicago this summer. He was voted by his teammates to wear the Huskersâ famous single-digit jersey. And even though he canât wear it because of college football rules, the vote shows in what esteem Evans is held. Talking about leadership only goes so far. A tangible act of the single-digit jersey is slam-dunk proof of Evansâ value to the Huskers. âIt just shows how much my teammates respect me and I have so much respect for my teammates,â Evans said at a press conference Tuesday. âFor them to even know that I canât wear a single digit and for them to vote me just means everything to me. And Iâll do anything for this team. âAnd I know itâs just I love my team. So it shows that they just trust me and anything to lead this team.â Justin Evans talks about leadership Evans is a 6-foot-2, 315-pounder from East Orange, N.J., who is in his final year of eligibility. He started all 13 games at center in 2025. He is expected to be a high draft pick in 2027. Evans recognizes his own growth as a leader. Earning the single-digit vote was a great tribute for a player on whom the Huskers are counting on greatly. âIâve grown so much just understanding my team and who Iâm playing with and getting to know them on a another level,â Evans said. âItâs the first important step of leadership is just knowing who youâre playing for and knowing who they are playing for and that brings us together as a team.â New offensive line coach Geep Wade understands leadership and how important for his charges to take charge. He works closely with Evans. âEven now heâs still pushing me to be the vocal guy on the team and just encouraging guys on and off the field, more so on the field, just keeping guys going, you know, when we may get into those lulls in the game and just keeping a voice, a positive voice for the guys in the room,â Evans said. Changes on offensive line Throughout the spring and early summer, the offensive line starters were believed to be set. That changed Monday when Nebraska released its first depth chart for 2026 Nebraska's Gunnar Gottula is the listed starter at right tackle going into the season. | Nebraska Athletics The most notable change? Gunnar Gottula is the starter at right tackle with South Carolina transfer Tree Babalade â the expected starter â now below Gottula. Gottula has been making strides throughout the summer and this starting nod shows that. âGunnar has been, from when he first got here to now, has been another great leader,â Evans said. âHeâs somebody who I look up to in the room. He helps me out a lot and heâs very smart as well. âSo if I have any questions, Iâm going to Gunnar asking him like, âHey, like what do you think I should do here?â âAnd I have nothing but respect for him. Being a hometown kid, all he wants to do is play football here. So Iâm really proud of his progress that he has shown throughout this offseason.â O-line eager to face Ohio The new offensive line will get its first test Saturday against Ohio at Memorial Stadium. âGoing into our first game this week, weâve built a pretty cohesive unit, playing as one with guys coming in from different conferences and played for different coaches,â Evans said. âTheyâve came in and embraced the process with us and itâs been a great long couple of months getting to know those guys and just helping them understand the process of how we do things here at Nebraska.â Clicking with Rhule Evans said he has a good relationship with head coach Matt Rhule. They have a connection. âMe and Coach Rhule, I mean us East Coast guys are always going to stick together no matter what,â Evans said with a smile. Nebraska coach Matt Rhule and center Justin Evans, both East Coast guys, have developed a relationship that goes beyond the field. | Kaleb Henry âI have so much respect for Coach Rhule and how intentional he is with the game and how he wants the players to understand the game. Not just play football, but understand the situations on why we do things or how he wants to put us in better positions of success and heâs always going to put the teamâs best interest first.â Evans said he also has clicked with quarterback Anthony Colandrea. âOur relationship has grown a lot too, you know, from him first getting here to now,â Evans said. âThatâs probably one of my closest friends on the team, and he pushes me to be better, and Iâm going to push him to be better. Itâs a two-way street with us, and Iâm excited to see him go out there and ball.â Stay up to date on all things Huskers by bookmarking Nebraska Cornhuskers On SI , subscribing to HuskerMax on YouTube and visiting HuskerMax.com daily. articles.excerpt: For Fantasy managers who prefer high-floor and safer options at running back, Javonte Williams and two more running backs are perfect for their selection.
articles.source_type: Gameweek squads, team news round-ups, deadline reminders
articles.body: Javonte Williams Leads Group of High-Floor, Safe Mid-Round Fantasy Football Running Backs Dallas Cowboys running back Javonte Williams (33) runs with the ball in the second quarter against the Philadelphia Eagles at AT&T Stadium. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Sometimes going with the safer option with a high floor in Fantasy Football can lead to a championship-caliber season. Fantasy managers should consider these mid-round running backs, who offer a high floor thanks to their bellcow workload. Javonte Williams Williams RB 16, 35 ADP ) will continue his workhorse usage this season after tallying 287 touches last season. The Dallas Cowboys recently released Jaydon Blue , who figured to be Williams biggest threat to touches this season. With Blue out of the picture, Williams is lined up to carry the bulk of the load among Cowboys running backs.Â In his first season with the Dallas Cowboys, Williamsâ workload consisted of a top-ten 252 rushing attempts , which led to a RB 11 finish in standard formats. With CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens on the outside, Williams will benefit from light boxes in his rushing attempts. Williams benefits the most near the goal line as being the main back led to extensive touches near the goal line. Last season, Williams finished eighth in the NFL in rushing touchdowns. Williams is set to repeat another workhorse season with Blue out of Dallas. Javonte Williams, that man has a family!! pic.twitter.com/mlrgoQS6Yv â Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) December 25, 2025 David Montgomery Montgomery (RB 20, 50 ADP) finally gets the chance to work as a lead back after spending the last three seasons as Jahmyr Gibbsâ backup. In Detroit, Montgomery was used extensively as a goal-line back, finishing with at least eight rushing touchdowns each season. Montgomery gets the chance to continue his goal-line work along with expanded touches outside the red zone in his first season with the Houston Texans. A benefit Montgomery will receive in being the starting running back in Houston is the shorter starting field positions the offense will have thanks to the defense.Â The Texans defense finished first in yards allowed per game and third in turnover forced with 29. Having a shorter average field position will lead to more red-zone visits for the Texans offense where Montgomery truly shines.Â David Montgomery getting shifty in the open field ð pic.twitter.com/9PjJY0Rd41 â Nico (@elitetakes_) August 1, 2026 Quinshon Judkins Judkins (RB 23, 54 ADP) produced a decent rookie campaign that was cut short due to injuries. In his rookie season, Judkins averaged 16.4 rushing attempts per game, finishing with 12.1 FPPG in PPR leagues.Â Judkins' high rushing attempts should continue with new head coach Todd Monken at the helm.Â During Monkenâs tenure with the Baltimore Ravens, running back Derrick Henry was always near the top in rushing attempts Judkins is no Henry, but with Monken running the ship, expect a heavy dosage of Judkinsâ rushing attempts for the Browns offense.Â Judkins' usage is compounded with the lack of efficient quarterback play in Cleveland.Â Itâs no secret that Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders arenât in the upper-echelon on QB play. With lesser QB play around him, Monken will turn to Judkins to be the lead horse back for his offense.Â Fantasy managers can expect a similar work rate of 16.4 rushing attempts per game by Judkins in his sophomore season, making the running back a safe option in the mid rounds.Â Quinshon Judkins so far: 10 rushing attempts 71 yards 1 TD pic.twitter.com/X1fmS0JlJ5 â Underdog NFL (@UnderdogNFL) October 19, 2025 More Fantasy Sports on SI News Add us as a preferred source on Google Follow Published 41 minutes ago | Modified 41 minutes ago JEFF SALCEDO Jeff Salcedo is a writer for Fantasy Sports on SI with extensive experience covering the NFL, MMA, NBA, and soccer. A dedicated fantasy sports enthusiast, he has competed in fantasy leagues and daily fantasy sports (DFS) contests for more than a decade. Before joining Fantasy Sports on SI, Salcedo worked as a senior sports reporter for BYU's student newspaper, The Daily Universe. Follow Jsalcedosports Home News

articles.title: Notre Dame vs. Wisconsin Game Notes - Key Storylines for Season Opener
articles.excerpt: Notre Dame and Wisconsin will battle at Lambeau Field on Sunday. Key notes from both squads to get you ready for the big-time battle.
articles.source_type: Gameweek squads, team news round-ups, deadline reminders
articles.body: Notre Dame vs. Wisconsin Game Notes - Key Storylines for Season Opener DUPLICATE***Wisconsin Badgers wide receiver Danny Davis III (7) drops a pass against Notre Dame Fighting Irish cornerback Clarence Lewis (6) during their football game Saturday, September 25, 2021, at Soldier Field in Chicago, Ill. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Contrary to popular belief, Notre Dame and Wisconsin will not battle for a rivalry trophy in the likeness of Jack Coan or Barry Alvarez this Sunday night, but will play in one of football's greatest venues - Lambeau Field in Green Bay. It's the second time these two have met in a Shamrock Series game, the first coming in 2021 at Soldier Field in Chicago, when Notre Dame rattled off 31 straight fourth-quarter points to beat the Badgers, 41-13. While that was fun, Sunday promises to be its own chapter as both teams start seasons they hope will define their head coaches careers. For Notre Dame, it's about finally getting over the final hurdle and knocking down the national championship door for the first time since 1988, while for Wisconsin, the growing pains are supposed to be over and a friendlier schedule should allow the Badgers to take a step back in the right direction under Luke Fickell With those storylines in mind, here are a few game notes courtesy of the great folks in both the Notre Dame and Wisconsin sports information departments. Notre Dame vs Wisconsin - All-Time Series History Sunday night will be the 18th all-time meeting between Notre Dame and Wisconsin. The Fighting Irish hold a slight edge, 9-6-2. Notre Dame won the last two meetings, including the 2021 matchup at Soldier Field, 41-13. The meeting previous to that was all the way back in 1964 when Notre Dame routed the Badgers 31-7 at Camp Randall, in Ara Parseghian's first game as head coach. Notre Dame-Wisconsin Coaching Connections Marcus Freeman was Luke Fickell's DC at Cincinnati. The Wisconsin head coach was asked about the Notre Dame coach leading up to their big Week 1 matchup at Lambeau Field. pic.twitter.com/9dG9vBpo2G â Big Ten Football (@B1Gfootball) August 31, 2026 Notre Dame head coach Marcus Freeman was the defensive coordinator on Luke Fickell's staff at Cincinnati before departing for Notre Dame in 2021. Also on that Cincinnati staff were offensive coordinator Mike Denbrock, quarterbacks coach Gino Guidugli, and wide receivers coach Mike Brown. Notre Dame Coaches Who Coached and/or Played at Wisconsin A few more Notre Dame assistants called Wisconsin home in different ways previously. Chris Ash was previously a defensive coordinator for the Badgers while offensive line coach Joe Rudolph held the same position at Wisconsin after starring on its 1994 team that went to the Rose Bowl. Finally, defensive backs coach Aaron Henry was a two-time All Big Ten selection for the Badgers. Notre Dame All-Time vs Big Ten Opponents Sunday will be Notre Dame's 512 all-time game against a Big Ten opponent. It has gone 319-170-22 in the previous 511 and 19-9-3 against Big Ten schools on neutral fields. Wisconsin's Return to Lambeau Field Despite the rich history of the Green Bay Packers, the Badgers don't have much of a history at Lambeau Field. Wisconsin has played just one game there previously, upsetting No. 5 LSU to open the 2016 season, in which Wisconsin would go on to win the Cotton Bowl. New Look Badgers for 2026 Part of the reason for hope for Wisconsin in 2026 after a disappointing 2025 is because of how active the team was in the transfer portal. Wisconsin added 34 players via the portal, the third most of any team in the Big Ten. Former Sun Belt Star QBs Badgers The most important of those 34 players is quarterback Colton Joseph, who comes to Wisconsin after winning the Sun Belt's Offensive Player of the Year award. He threw for over 2,000 yards while rushing for more than 1,000 in 2025. Easier 2025 Outlook for Wisconsin? Wisconsin should get some schedule relief by default in 2026 after facing 10 teams that qualified for bowl games last year. Fixing Wisconsin's Offensive Woes A season ago, Wisconsin's offense was putrid, reaching the 20-point mark just twice all year. Once in a 42-10 rout of Middle Tennessee State, and the other in a 27-10 victory over Illinois. His 9.35 yards per pass attempt were second in the nation last season, while his 14.06 yards per completion were fourth best. Notre Dame's Preseason Hype Notre Dame's No. 4 ranking in the preseason AP Poll is the highest Notre Dame has been ranked to start a year since being No. 2 in 2006. Meanwhile, this is the third-straight season Wisconsin has begun the year unranked. Notre Dame's Dominating Close to 2025 Notre Dame won its last 10 games of the 2025 season after starting the year 0-2. It's the first time in over 100 years that a Notre Dame team has won 10 straight games all by 10 or more points (1921 into 1922). Notre Dame's Middle Eight Domination Coaches often talk about the middle eight of a game and how important it is to control the final four minutes before halftime as well as the first four minutes out of the break. Marcus Freeman has discussed this from jump street and his team has followed, outscoring teams 403-117, a +286 margin and average difference of +5.3 points per game since he was named head coach. articles.body: FPL GW3 Wildcard Drafts - Pros, Cons, Tips and Players to Target Skip To Content Trending Now forwards for gw3 best midfielders for fpl gw3 top defenders for fpl gw3 TC fpl fpl gw3 freehit draft FPL GW3 Wildcard Drafts – Pros, Cons, Tips and Players to Target FPL GW3 Ultimate Guide and Tips FPL Wildcard FPL Wildcard Drafts Game week Preview Wildcard September 1, 2026 September 1, 2026 allaboutfpl FPL GW3 Wildcard Drafts – Pros, Cons, Tips and Players to Target GW3 has emerged as a popular Gameweek to wildcard amongst FPL managers due to a variety of reasons. Bruno or No Bruno? Palmer now or Palmer Later? Lots of questions to answer. In this blog, we look at the Pros and cons of the FPL GW3 Wildcard, the Ideal FPL GW3 Wildcard Drafts, and the Players to target in your Gameweek 3 Wildcard team. Link to all our FPL GW3 blogs including scout picks, players to target, buy, hold, sell analysis, differentials, captaincy metrics, best forwards, and more. Completely free to access as well! FPL GW3 Wildcard Guide Pros & Cons of Wildcarding in FPL GW3: Pros of GW3 Wildcard: Projections from Fantasy Football Hub Get Haaland in ahead of COV(H) and long term if you started with No Haaland in GW1. Attack Teams with Good Fixture runs and have cheap assets like Newcastle(Wissa, Elanga, Hall, Dedic) and Brighton(De Cuyper, Verbruggen, Gross) Catch good price changes(Eg. Konsa) who might be a starter now or even later at just 4.4 million. Cons of GW3 Wildcard: Chelsea and Arsenal play each other and it will be a really difficult match to call with respect to Goals and Clean sheets. You will want to have Double Arsenal defense and Double Chelsea attack long term but it will be a trickier call to take in GW3 on who to bench/start. You will be up against managers who are likely to have Haaland as Triple Captain vs COV(H). You can’t use more than one chip in a single Gameweek. Wildcard might be needed later for other fixture swings- Like GW6 or around GW15 as highlighted in our Chip Strategy article. Bruno or No-Bruno, Palmer or No Palmer will be a tough decision to make. Bruno has had an absolutely massive 23 points in GW2 vs Ipswich, courtesy of 3 goals and 1 Assist. But there is an argument that can be made to not captain Bruno Fernandes in the next 5-6 weeks and switch between Palmer and Haaland. No Bruno- Captaincy Ticker: GW3- Haaland vs COV(H) GW4- Palmer vs HUL(H) GW5- Haaland vs SUN(H) GW6- Palmer vs BOU(H) GW7- Haaland vs IPS(H) GW8- Haaland vs AVL(A)/Palmer vs TOT(H) The other alternative is to wait out a week and Wildcard in GW4 after Chelsea and Arsenal have played each other. Here are some of the Pros of a GW3 Wildcard vs Pros of a GW4 Wildcard. GW3 Wildcard vs GW4 Wildcard: GW3 Wildcard GW4 Wildcard Helps you target Manchester City assets ahead of COV(H). Works better in case of no Haaland in GW1 Helps you skip the Chelsea vs Arsenal fixture in GW3 and target them full-fledged in GW4 on Wildcard. Triple up on both Chelsea (Attack) and Arsenal (Likely defense) without them facing each other. Can catch lots of Price Changes(City assets, Arsenal defenders) One more week of information regarding assets that are tricky with minutes in the long term, like Konsa, De Cuyper, Dedic, etc. Good entry points for teams like Man City, Brentford Better Entry points for Teams like Chelsea, Newcastle, Brighton, and Better Exit points for Man United, Liverpool This is how a GW4 Wildcard Draft would look like. FPL GW4 Wildcard Draft: Players to Target on FPL GW3 Wildcard: Goalkeepers: Raya, Verbruggen, Hornicek Defenders: Calafiori, Konsa, Gabriel, De Cuyper, Hall, Thiaw, Dedic, Ajer, Egan, Thomas, Muharemovic, Canvot, Andersen, Castagne, Tarkowski Midfielders: Bruno Fernandes, Palmer, Rogers, Cherki, Mbeumo, Foden, Szoboszlai, Wirtz, Elanga, Gross, Dewsbury Hall, Sangare, Slater Forwards: Haaland, Pedro, Wissa, Calvert-Lewin Fantasy Football Hub(FFHUB) Fantasy Football Hub is a high-quality FPL website offering a wide range of FPL content, tools, data, planners, and more. Memberships are available for the 2026/27 season at a 50% discount along with a win-your-mini-league or get-your-money-back guarantee T&C Applicable (Click on the image above to claim the offer) FPL GW3 Wildcard Drafts FPL GW3 Wildcard Draft 1 with Bruno Fernandes This is a Template GW3 Wildcard Draft covering all the bases- Haaland, Pedro, Bruno, Palmer, Szoboszlai, Wissa, and Double Arsenal defense. Goal Keeper and Defenders: Verbruggen is the Budget GK with a good run of fixtures. Calafiori picks himself with 2 assists and 2 clean sheets and is the next nailed defender in the Arsenal lineup after Gabriel. He is also 2.5 million cheaper than Gabriel, which makes him an easy lock. Konsa is the second Arsenal defender. At just 4.4 million, you have to take up that risk to get an Arsenal defender. He should be first choice in the long term and can play both CB and RB. With Mosquera injured(Watch out for PC updates), He could be in for a start as soon as GW3. Ajer and Hall are two of the total 4 defenders who have hit DEFCON in both games. Ajer is always good for DEFCON when he plays at CB, and Hall also carries an excellent attacking threat(with a good run of fixtures from GW4). Brentford and Newcastle defenders also rotate really well, as seen below. Dedic is also looking really good with 🅰️🅰️🅰️ in 3 games. And just for £4.5. Livramento is back in training, though, but according to Newcastle fans, Livra doesn’t walk in directly, and Dedic is likely to keep starting games at least in the short-medium run. Midfielders: Palmer is an easy lock in most of the GW3 Wildcard Drafts(unless on GW4 Free Hit). Chelsea Bruno Fernandes is coming on the back of 23 points haul courtesy of 3 goals and an assist in GW2 vs Ipswich. He is in red-hot form and has multiple routes to points. Pascal Gross and Szoboszlai are midfielders who have multiple routes to points- penalties, Set Pieces, and DEFCON. On top of it, they also have a good fixture run. Slater is the 4.5 Midfielder enabler in this draft who is a starter for Hull and is also on set pieces. Forwards: Haaland and Joao Pedro pick themselves in every Wildcard Draft. Wissa also should be a lock according to me, as Newcastle have a good run of fixtures playing HUL(H), COV(A) in GW5 and GW6. Calvert-Lewin is also another option to consider if you want a set-and-forget option. Isak is a good shout with good fixtures in GW3 and GW4, but it is a difficult price point to swap later on, and he hasn’t shown much to warrant a gamble. The money is used to upgrade and get Cherki as well ahead of COV(H). Cherki got 2 brilliant goals vs Palace in GW2 and is the man in form. In this draft, Cherki to Foden is also an option, and that will allow you to upgrade Hall/Muharemovic to Calafiori, completing the elite Arsenal defense triple-up. Anderson comes in as the cheaper alternative to Cherki, and the funds are used in a defence upgrade with O’Reilly coming in as another Premium Defender ahead of COV(H). articles.title: Ndiaye Leaves Everton
articles.excerpt: Everton can confirm Iliman Ndiaye has signed for Manchester City on a permanent deal for an undisclosed fee. The Senegalese winger joins Enzo Maresca’s side after two years with the Toffees, featuring 74 times across all competitions and scoring 17 goals. Signed from Marseille in July 2024, Ndiaye made history by becoming the last-ever goalscorer for an Everton Men’s player at Goodison Park when he struck twice in the Blues’ 2-0 victory over Southampton in May 2025. He again entered his name into the Club’s illustrious history at the start of last season, netting the first goal for Everton at Hill Dickinson Stadium during the Toffees’ 2-0 win against Brighton & Hove Albion. Ndiaye – a Senegal international who featured at this summer’s FIFA World Cup – played 32 times for Everton in the Premier League during 2025/26, recording six goals and three assists. The Club thanks Iliman for his contributions to Everton across the past two years and wishes him success for the future.

Updated on September 1, 2026 4:24PM EST Share By: Ian Hartitz @Ihartitz Updated on September 1, 2026 4:24PM EST NFL Observations Mock Draft Simulator Prep for your 2026 Fantasy Football draft with free, unlimited drafts, and real-time grades. Preseason results are just like the points from Whose Line Is It Anyway?: They don't matter. Still, we can occasionally get at least some additional insight into team-by-team player usage and schematic strategy from teams willing to play their starters at least some of the time. This brings us to today's goal: Six bigger-picture takeaways from preseason that may or may not ultimately matter, but hey, there's no football this week, and I found them interesting, so maybe you will too! Preseason Trend No. 1: The Mike McDaniel Impact is REAL in Los Angeles Mike McDaniel's ability to largely get the most out of Tua Tagovailoa and the Dolphins over the years has made him a bit of a rock star in the play-caller streets. One of his key schematic principles was the use of pre-snap shift/motion as well as play-action: He easily ranked first in both of these metrics during the 2022-2025 seasons . The other teams near the top of the leaderboard ( Lions Rams 49ers Packers Chiefs ) reflect the reality that offenses consistently clicking these "easy buttons" are among the most well-schemed groups in the league. Well, at least based on our three preseason data points, it sure looks like McDaniel's Los Angeles hasn't fallen far from the tree. This is true for pre-snap shift/motion 2025 Chargers: 64.3 percent motion - 18th 2026 preseason: 83.8 percent - 1st … as well as play-action rate 2025 Chargers: 25.1 percent - 17th 2026 preseason: 36.6 percent - 2nd Hell, we also saw McDaniel REALLY lean into outside size (56.1%, 1st) relative to what the Chargers did last season (17.6%, 29th), and Los Angeles also emerged as a leader in multi-TE formations (37.1%, 4th) just one year removed from ranking 31st in percentage of plays with two or more tight ends on the field. Now, none of this is guaranteed to produce a juggernaut offense — especially if the offensive line (again) struggles to overcome injuries — but hey, it's certainly a good start! I'm holding firm on my bold prediction that the Chargers finish as the league's No. 1 scoring offense this season, and have accordingly loaded up on their fantasy-relevant talents of most shapes and sizes throughout draft season. For up-to-the-minute updates on injuries, news and everything going on around the NFL, head to RotoWire's NFL Fantasy Football News Today or follow @RotoWireNFL on X. Preseason Trend No. 2: The Raiders are MOVING People on the Line of Scrimmage This one is admittedly a bit more performance-based, but an improvement from the Raiders' big uglies up front does profile as relevant considering just how dire things were last season. I'm also more inclined to put some extra attention on these numbers considering each of the team's starting five offensive linemen played 30-plus snaps this August. Anyway: We saw a pretty big improvement here in the pass blocking department. Raiders pressure rate allowed: 2025: 37.8 percent - 30th 2026 preseason: 28.6 percent - T-9th And ESPECIALLY in run blocking. Raiders RB rush yards before contact per carry: 2025: 0.61 - 31st 2026 preseason: 1.66 - 3rd Overall, Klint Kubiak's squad joined the Seahawks, Cowboys and Chiefs as the only teams to rank top-10 in both of these categories this preseason. The Raiders' devotion to running plenty of multi-TE sets (43.4%, 3rd most) could help explain why. Here's to hoping Ashton Jeanty (ankle) is healthy enough to take advantage of this come Week 1! Check out our Fantasy Football ADP Report for a comprehensive tool with live-updated ADP data for multiple league formats and sites. Preseason Trend No. 3: This Commanders Offense Didn't Look Great! Particularly on the line of scrimmage: Washington ranked 21st in both pressure rate and RB yards before contact per rush in the preseason. The former was even more concerning considering the Commanders allowed the third-fastest time-to-pressure of any offense. Reminder: LT Laremy Tunsil (triceps, IR) is expected to miss a significant portion of the season. RotoWire offensive line rankings have this group ranked just 27th coming into the season. We only saw Jayden Daniels take two dropbacks in preseason … and they resulted in two pressures and a sack. There were two additional data points that I didn't love from this group: Washington had an NFL-low 30.3 percent pass play rate on first downs this preseason. Last in the league by a whopping 7.5 percentage points. Not great! The Commanders only had a 20.6 percent play-action rate (24th). That's a pretty big decrease (-9.2%) from last season when they ranked sixth. This is all even more concerning when we've had beat reporters be VERY open about the offense's lackluster performance during training camp. Here's to hoping Jayden Daniels is ready to put his Superman cape on — he's going to need to shoulder plenty of the load here for this offense to re-reach 2024 heights if the preseason is any indication of what we should expect from this offensive line and scheme. Use RotoWire's interactive Mock Draft Simulator to prepare for every scenario in your 2026 fantasy football drafts. Preseason Trend No. 4: Death, Taxes, Brian Daboll not using Pre-Snap Shift/Motion Maybe the Titans were truly just keeping things vanilla in preseason. Beat reporters said they saw more pre-snap movement in training camp. Then again, it's not like this August's scheme looks too different from what Daboll has always done over the years. While he has generally increased his pre-snap window dressing come September, this has still been a pretty stale offense relative to the rest of the league. Brian Daboll pre-snap shift/motion: 2026 preseason: 18.8 percent - 32nd 2025 Giants: 46.4 percent - 32nd 2022-2025 regular season Giants: 49.3 percent - 29th 2022-2025 preseason Giants: 29.7 percent - 29th The team's inability to get No. 4 overall pick Carnell Tate a single reception, or Cam Ward a completion thrown 10-plus yards downfield, also doesn't add a ton of confidence to the idea that this group is ready to hit the ground running. Here's hoping Daboll and company are ready to open things up come Week 1! Get ready for your draft by visiting our Custom Fantasy Football Rankings for a list of the top players for the season ahead, customized for your league. Preseason Trend No. 5: Finally Some Play-Action in Cincy? The Bengals' offense has obviously been nothing short of awesome with a healthy Joe Burrow over the years, but there has been a rather startling lack of play-action usage. Consider: The Bengals rank 31st in play-action rate (19.5%) since drafting Burrow first overall in 2020, and they were last in 2025 (17.2%). But then something funny happened this preseason: coach Zac Taylor had the boys embracing some play action for once! Overall, the Bengals' 34.9 percent play-action rate was good for fourth highest in the preseason … though we did see them also post a top-5 mark last August (28.7%, 5th). Still, I'm at least somewhat optimistic here based on the fact that Burrow specifically utilized *three* under-center, play-action dropbacks during his seven dropbacks (43%). Quite the increase from what we saw throughout last season (24 total, 8.3% of dropbacks)! We'll check back in on this trend in October and see if Taylor and company actually stick with it this time around. Preseason Trend No. 6: Matt Nagy and the Giants did Some Good Things! Specifically, Nagy leaned into the very pre-snap shift/motion that Daboll never did. Giants pre-snap shift/motion: 2026 preseason : 54.9 percent - 10th 2022-2025 regular seasons : 49.3 percent - 29th 2022-2025 preseasons : 29.7 percent - 29th Additionally, the offensive line played pretty great on its way to allowing a minuscule 21.2 percent pressure rate — good for the second lowest of preseason! That's quite an improvement over what we saw during the 2022-2025 regular seasons (40.1%, 32nd) and preseasons (34.7%, 29th) alike. Similar to the Raiders: There's at least some extra reason for optimism with this sticking considering all key members (other than stud LT Andrew Thomas ) got a decent bit of run this preseason. articles.body: Who Should I Draft: Travis Etienne vs Cam Skattebo | RotoWire Who Should I Draft: Travis Etienne vs. Cam Skattebo (2026 Fantasy Football) Should you draft Travis Etienne or Cam Skattebo? Projections are tight but I really like the upside of Skattebo and here's why. Updated on September 1, 2026 4:23PM EST Share By: Tyler Huntington @tylerhuntington Updated on September 1, 2026 4:23PM EST Who Should I Draft? Mock Draft Simulator Prep for your 2026 Fantasy Football draft with free, unlimited drafts, and real-time grades. Two backs, projected within three points of each other, going within a couple picks of each other in the fourth round of most fantasy football drafts. This is as even as the widget gets - Etienne at 203 half-PPR points, Skattebo at 206 - so the tiebreakers are the whole story, and they point somewhere the projection total doesn't. All half-PPR below. The scoring section matters a little here, because one of these guys catches meaningfully more passes. Travis Etienne Fantasy Outlook vs ADP: RB19 Etienne is the steady vet in this pair, and the projection reflects a real workhorse role: 203 half-PPR points on 226 carries for 1070 yards and seven scores. He even holds a razor-thin edge in total projection and floor, so if your instinct is 'give me the established guy with the known workload,' Etienne rewards it. Alvin Kamara is already expected to miss time in 2026 so the newest New Orleans Saint is locked and loaded for a full time role. The issue is what happens above the median. His 249 point ceiling is nearly 40 points below Skattebo's, because his profile is volume-forward and grounded - lots of carries, modest passing-game work (34 catches), not a lot of week-winning spike. He's a solid RB2 whose best weeks look like everyone else's good weeks. In a vacuum that's a perfectly good pick. Very close floor projection, but it isn't an edge - it's noise, and it's the only row Etienne clearly wins, aside from ADP. Alvin Kamara is already expected to miss time in 2026 so the newest New Orleans Saint is locked and loaded for a full time role. The issue is what happens above the median. His 249 point ceiling is nearly 40 points below Skattebo's, because his profile is volume-forward and grounded - lots of carries, modest passing-game work (34 catches), not a lot of week-winning spike. Very close floor projection, but it isn't an edge - it's noise, and it's the only row Etienne clearly wins, aside from ADP. Bottom Line: A dead-even projection with a workhorse's carry count, but the lower ceiling and less receiving juice. The safe half of a coin flip. Cam Skattebo Fantasy Outlook vs ADP: RB18 Skattebo is coming off a brutal leg injury, and normally I'm the one waving people off the guys that are riddled with injury histories - but the numbers here earn it. Same projection as Etienne to within a rounding error, and a ceiling of 288 that towers nearly 40 points above him. That gap is built on passing-game work and big plays. Pass-catching backs carry the highest ceilings in fantasy because the receptions stack on top of the rushing floor, and in a modern offense that usage is exactly what turns a fine RB2 into a league-winner. The tool hands Skattebo the coin-flip edge on that ceiling, and he's going a hair earlier than Etienne to boot. He's a risk, and the week-to-week can wobble. But the receiving role is the tell, and it's pointing up. Bottom Line: The same projection with a 40-point-higher ceiling and more pass-game work. The tie-breaking upside is real. Travis Etienne vs Cam Skattebo: The Verdict The tool below has these two in a dead heat on projection - scroll to the ceiling and receiving rows to see what breaks the tie. The tool calls it a coin flip and gives Skattebo the nod on ceiling, and I'm coming down the same way: Skattebo is my pick. When two backs project dead even, I take the one with the pass-catching role, because those catches are both the safer floor and the higher ceiling - it's the profile that wins you a week and rarely craters. Etienne is the pick if you'd rather have the vet's known workload and you're allergic to variance, and I understand the impulse at an even projection. But 'even projection, way higher ceiling, more receptions, going a touch earlier' is four boxes, and Skattebo checks the ones that decide close calls. What flips me: a training-camp signal that Skattebo's receiving role is smaller than projected. Strip the pass-game edge and this reverts to the vet. As long as those targets are real, take the ceiling. Best Ceiling: Cam Skattebo - 295.8, nearly 60 points clear Best Floor: Travis Etienne - by a hair, part of a near-tie Receiving Edge: Cam Skattebo Most Proven Workload: Travis Etienne My Pick: Cam Skattebo Travis Etienne or Cam Skattebo PPR Scoring Skattebo's receiving edge means full PPR widens his lead and makes this pick more comfortable. Standard scoring strips the reception points and pulls the two nearly even on their almost-identical rushing lines - close enough that Etienne's proven role becomes a fair tiebreak. So: Skattebo in half and full PPR. In a standard league, it's a genuine coin flip and I wouldn't argue with the vet. Fantasy Football Tools Everything you need to dominate your draft, in one place. articles.body: 'I know this is the perfect fit' - Ndiaye completes £65m move to Man City Skip to content Football News Premier League News ‘I know this is the perfect fit’ – Ndiaye completes £65m move to Man City City have swelled their attacking ranks on deadline day. Nicholas McGee Last Update: 36 minutes ago 2 min read Add us as a preferred source on Google Manchester City have completed the signing of Senegal winger Iliman Ndiaye from Everton Ndiaye has made the move to the Etihad Stadium on a five-year deal after City agreed a £65million with the Merseyside club. The 26-year-old was at one point set to join Tottenham, with Spurs striker Richarlison going the other way. But City swooped in after that transfer fell through, with Ndiaye delighted to have the chance to prove himself for Enzo Maresca’s side after excelling in his time with Everton. “I’ve worked my whole life for an opportunity like this,” he told City’s official website “City are one of the best clubs in the world and I’ve seen them win everything as I’ve grown up. “To be able to write my own chapter in a story that special is the chance of a lifetime and I’m determined to grab it with both hands. “It’s not always been easy in my career, but I always had the belief that I could play for a team challenging for the biggest prizes and now I’m here. It feels so good. “I love to play with the ball on the floor in an attacking team that wants to score as many goals as possible. That’s why I know this is the perfect fit. “City fans can rest assured that I will give my all to bring more success to this incredible club.” Ndiaye scored 17 goals and provided four assists for Everton after joining from Marseille in 2024. He could make his debut when City host Coventry City this weekend, having won each of their opening two games. Topics Everton F.C. Manchester City F.C. Stay updated on key player injuries and how they impact fantasy football lineups each week. September 1, 2026 Share By: Jeff Stotts @InStreetClothes September 1, 2026 Injury Analysis Mock Draft Simulator Prep for your 2026 Fantasy Football draft with free, unlimited drafts, and real-time grades. NFL teams have trimmed down their rosters to 53 players, with injuries and health influencing countless decisions around the league. For the first in-season NFL injury report, understanding transactional terms used in the process can be beneficial on draft day especially for opportunistic fantasy managers able to draft a player at a discounted rate. The first thing to understand for is the Physically Unable to Perform (PUP) list. With training camp over the Active/PUP list is no longer available to teams. Instead, franchises must now utilize the Reserve/PUP list for these designated players. Players placed on the Reserve/PUP do not count toward the team's 53-man roster and cannot appear in the team's first four regular season contests. This season, players can participate in a 21-day practice period while still stashed on the Reserve/PUP list after the team has played in two regular season games. This allows medical teams to better evaluate players in anticipation of their return following the team's fourth game played. If the player is not activated to the 53-man roster during this window, they must sit out the remainder of the year. Notable players starting the year on the Reserve/PUP include Green Bay's Micah Parsons and Seattle running back Zach Charbonnet . Receiver Alec Pierce was activated off the PUP list late last week and is hoping to be ready for Week 1 after undergoing offseason ankle surgery. If a player is ineligible for the PUP list but becomes injured, teams must now consider using the injured NFL teams have trimmed down their rosters to 53 players, with injuries and health influencing countless decisions around the league. For the first in-season NFL injury report, understanding transactional terms used in the process can be beneficial on draft day especially for opportunistic fantasy managers able to draft a player at a discounted rate. The first thing to understand for is the Physically Unable to Perform (PUP) list. With training camp over the Active/PUP list is no longer available to teams. Instead, franchises must now utilize the Reserve/PUP list for these designated players. Players placed on the Reserve/PUP do not count toward the team's 53-man roster and cannot appear in the team's first four regular season contests. This season, players can participate in a 21-day practice period while still stashed on the Reserve/PUP list after the team has played in two regular season games. This allows medical teams to better evaluate players in anticipation of their return following the team's fourth game played. If the player is not activated to the 53-man roster during this window, they must sit out the remainder of the year. Notable players starting the year on the Reserve/PUP include Green Bay's Micah Parsons and Seattle running back Zach Charbonnet . Receiver Alec Pierce was activated off the PUP list late last week and is hoping to be ready for Week 1 after undergoing offseason ankle surgery. If a player is ineligible for the PUP list but becomes injured, teams must now consider using the injured reserve (IR). Like the PUP list, any player placed on the IR must miss a minimum of four weeks. A player can only return from an IR designation twice a season, and each team is granted a total of eight IR-to-return designations for the year. The number grows to 10 if they make the playoffs. Like the PUP list, these players can utilize a three-week window to ramp up their activity level. At the conclusion of the 21 days, the player must be activated, placed on season-ending IR, or be released or traded. Several big names were allotted IR designations entering the regular season including James Conner Tank Dell Jordyn Tyson and Christian Kirk IR and PUP list designations may be frustrating, but it does provide a degree of clarity regarding a player's status. Once a player is placed on either list, those willing to invest in him know they will have to proceed without the individual for at least four weeks. The use of the IR can also be used as a good indicator of the health of another player on the team's roster. For example, Conner's designation in Arizona suggests the team feels good about Jeremiyah Love 's availability for Week 1. The rookie running back is working his way back from a high-ankle sprain suffered August 13 but is "progressing really well" according to head coach Mike LaFleur. Turf Burns Emeka Egbuka : The second-year wide receiver has been sidelined since August 12 when he suffered a toe sprain in practice. Toe sprains, particularly those involving the big toe, can be extremely limiting, especially for wideouts. The big toe is crucial in driving the foot off the ground when running or jumping while also withstanding the high amount of stress that comes with weight bearing. Egbuka's Week 1 availability remains in doubt, and I'm moving him down my draft board just a bit. Puka Nacua : The Rams wideout has been limited by soreness in a specific muscle in his core. Nacua's injury involves the psoas muscle. The psoas sits just under the ribs at the lower spine. Its fibers run down through the pelvis, anchoring to the upper femur. It merges with another muscle, the iliacus, to form the iliopsoas, one of the primary hip flexors. Based on this location, a psoas injury can result in pain in the lower back, groin or hip, and be very limiting. Fortunately, Nacua was able to return to practice Sunday, and it looks like he will avoid any missed time. Look for the Rams to handle him conservatively in the days leading up to Week 1. Luther Burden : In Chicago, Burden is recovering from a groin injury sustained in the early days of training camp. The timeline suggests Burden's injury was a more moderate strain. He has resumed limited practice, and the team is optimistic he will be in uniform for Week 1. Chris Olave : Given Olave's checkered NFL injury history, his fans had to hate seeing him leave practice early last week. The team relayed he simply had the wind knocked out of him and it opted to be cautious with his care. He was back at practice the next day and remains the top target in New Orleans. Wan'Dale Robinson : The Titans receiver appears to have avoided a concussion after taking a hard hit in a joint practice with the Bears . The medical staff will monitor his status for any late developing signs or symptoms, but for now he appears okay. Zach Charbonnet : We know Charbonnet will miss at least the first four weeks of the regular season as he recovers from the anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) tear sustained in postseason. The timing of his injury made a Week 1 return unlikely, and an exact target date remains uncertain. Rookie Jadarian Price is expected to start for Seattle with George Holani also set for carries. If Price runs well, the Seahawks could opt for an even more cautious approach with Charbonnet's care to ensure his long-term health. As a result, Charbonnet's fantasy value seems tied to the success of Price. Patrick Mahomes : The former MVP avoided the IR and is on track to start Week 1. As discussed last week, quarterbacks are one of the positions best poised to return to a high level of play following an ACL tear, and I'm bullish on Mahomes entering the year. He may not put up the same numbers he did when he first burst onto the scene, but he remains a reliable fantasy quarterback with a high ceiling. An early season bye in Week 5 should also help him better navigate his comeback. Draft Pass The Draft Pass unlocks this article and every draft tool we build. Patterson made his Toffees debut in an FA Cup fifth-round victory over Boreham Wood in March 2022, and the following year, played 19 Premier League matches in his first full season on Merseyside. A highlight of that campaign arrived when the young Scot started in Everton’s emphatic 5-1 victory at Brighton & Hove Albion in May 2023, when Patterson excellently tamed tricky winger Kaoru Mitoma. On the international stage, the defender helped Scotland qualify for this summer’s 2026 FIFA World Cup finals, where he earned caps against Haiti, Morocco and Brazil. Everyone at Everton thanks Nathan for his commitment to the Club across the past four-and-a-half years and wishes him all the best for the next step in his career.

articles.title: Ryan Poles Defines Bears' Trade of Gervon Dexter as Ideal Timing
articles.excerpt: The Bears GM has learned how to get rid of drafted players who may not fit, and getting back something in return made trading their defensive tackle possible.
articles.source_type: Gameweek squads, team news round-ups, deadline reminders
articles.body: Ryan Poles Defines Bears' Trade of Gervon Dexter as Ideal Timing Shedeur Sanders pulls away ffrom Gervon Dexter but falls for a sack last year at Soldier Field. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The confluence of several factors made it possible for GM Ryan Poles to trade defensive tackle Gervon Dexter for a fifth-round pick and cornerback Clark Phillips III. The major one was obviously defensive tackles Jordan van den Berg and Jayden Loving making huge statements, but it's obvious the Bears had no intention of paying a big contract in the future for Dexter, who has only flashed his talent at times throughout three seasons. "That deal was more about timing than anything," Poles said Tuesday during his annual post-preseason state-of-the-team address. "Timing and fit. "You know we had some young guys really pushing that came in this year with Jordan and Loving. They did a really good job, and we felt like it was a good fit as we moved forward." Final thoughts on the Gervon Dexter trade. The Gervon Dexter trade was about Dexter the rookies just made it easier. Dexter wanted an extension. Chicago didnât want to pay him, solid pass rusher. Not great vs the run. His 44.0 PFF run D grade ranked 107th/134 IDL. For aâ¦ pic.twitter.com/2Pe0Eny0I5 â Clay Harbor (@clayharbs82) September 1, 2026 The timing in this case was the Bears owed Dexter a huge deal by next year and at this point felt they could afford to lose a player chosen in Round 2 because they're looking at using lower-priced, promising players this year. The money in the future will be needed for something important, like an extension for quarterback Caleb Williams. Also, the trade now could bring back a little more than a trade at the deadline, and maybe a lot less then if Dexter had been injured. Confident in current group None of that would matter if the Bears GM and coach Ben Johnson thought they lacked the defensive tackles to shut down the run or rush from the interior. They are convinced about both van den Berg and Loving, but also the veteran group including Grady Jarrett, Neville Gallimore and Kentavius Street. Also, they have added back veteran defensive tackle James Lynch to the roster, for now, at least. Ryan Poles said the Gervon Dexter trade was largely due to Jordan van den Berg and Jayden Loving looking great in camp. pic.twitter.com/owVDoIztDw â Caleb Williams Fan Club (@CalebFC18) September 1, 2026 "I have a ton of confidence in those guys," Poles said. "They did a good job this preseason. I still think itâs a unit thatâs going to have to work together, whether itâs our blitz packages or the twists and games that we play. Those guys bring it, they have really good motors and they have the skillset to get into the backfield and get some pressure on the quarterback, and the defense is going to have to play as one unit. Thatâs important." As for the trade itself, Poles admitted he has gained the ability dump off parts who may not fit or who failed. In this case, that's Dexter. Still, it doesn't say much for the GM when they've been dumping off draft picks after a year or two. "I think I've been pretty quick to, if there's something that doesn't work out, I think we are pretty good about being honest about that and moving on," Poles said. "I don't think we are an organization, or I'm a GM, that's going to hold on just because it was a draft pick or a trade that you made and now I have to make it work and we are just going to keep that player here when it's not working. That will hurt the team. "I think I mentioned before that the locker room always knows. So we hold true to that. We want to put the best group together regardless of how they are acquired." In Ryan Polesâ first 4 years (2020-2024) heâs had 16 picks from 2nd-5th round Thereâs 7 on the roster at this moment Kyler Gordon Braxton Jones Roschon Johnson Tyrique Stevenson Noah Sewell Austin Boooker Tory Taylor Name one thatâs even an average starter or healthy #Bears â Jake (@Jake_B30) August 30, 2026 It's obvious Phillips was a throw-in on the deal from the way Poles talked about the cornerback addition. He couldn't classify him as a fit for a specific spot. "Most of his tape in Atlanta was outside (as opposed to slot)," Poles said. "In college, he was inside. I liked what that tape looked like, too. Heâs capable of both, but since heâs been in the league, heâs been outside. So weâll see where we start him off and go from there..â Phillips could get a look at slot The obvious need right now is at slot cornerback. The Bears are going with rookie Malik Muhammad, another player who has been outside for the most part. Poles even mentioned they have given safety Xavier Woods a look there and also Cam Lewis and Wrookie safety Dillon Thieneman for a few downs. "I really love this guy as a player. I don't know how anybody can look at this and see any sort of downside" - @adamrank on Clark Phillips #thesickpodcast pic.twitter.com/VS4NdA9rEf â The Sick Podcast with Adam Rank (@sickpodadamrank) September 1, 2026 What he's certain of is they don't have starter Kyler Gordon for now, as he works through his injury. Through the trade, the defensive line has shaped up. Health is returning, although Poles can't yet say defensive end Austin Booker will be available for Week 1 or when defensive tackle/end Shemar Turner will be back from knee surgery. Turner is in the later stages of his rehab, though, Poles added. The defensive line has been labeled a weakness throughout the offseason and losing a veteran player with talent can't be construed as a victory for this season. What the Bears have to hope now is they have benefited in the long run by giving two younger players a chance for playing time earlier in a rotation than they might have had, as they mix with one of the NFC's less impressive veteran tackle groups. While the Bears have been working on cutting down the roster to 53 players, I watched some film on cornerback Clark Phillips III. articles.body: Arsenal: Deal to sign next Kvaratskhelia secured by man who unearthed PSG star Arsenal have signed the next Khvicha Kvaratskhelia Arsenal have agreed a deal to sign Georgian playmaker Andria Bartishvili – the next Khvicha Kvaratshkelia – with the man who unearthed the now-Paris Saint-Germain star key to the transfer. The Gunners have made a habit of signing youngsters who they think can become stars this summer. So far, they’ve landed Igor Tyjon from Blackburn, Vincent Joseph from Liverpool, Axel Donczew from Cardiff, Elijah Upson from Tottenham, and Mylo Bernard from Crystal Palace. They will also see Ecuadorian twins Edwin and Holger Quintero and Irish midfielder Victor Ozhianvuna join when they turn 18. And their latest signing will also do the same, joining from Kolkheti 1913. The Athletic Arsenal correspondent James McNicholas reports the Gunners have secured the services of 17-year-old Georgian playmaker Bartishvili. The young Georgian is already being labelled the next Kvaratskhelia, after the PSG superstar, and there is a strong link between the compatriots. Per McNicholas, the pursuit at Arsenal has been led by the assistant to sporting director Andrea Berta, Mauricio Micheli. The now-Arsenal man was the scout at Napoli who is credited with helping to identify Kvaratskhelia when he joined the Italian club from Dinamo Batumi in 2022. The winger went on to win Serie A with Napoli twice before making a big move to PSG, where he’s now a two-time European champion. Arsenal will hope that Bartishvili can have a similar impact for them to what his compatriot has had for the clubs he’s played for since leaving Georgia himself. Andria Bartishvili confirms Arsenal news Barthishvili himself has confirmed the news of his transfer on social media. Posting on his Instagram story, he said: “A very big thank you to everyone for the congratulations.” The 17-year-old is on loan with Iberia 1999 until December. There, he has two goals and three assists in 24 appearances. He will join Arsenal in 2027, when he has turned 18. It’s likely that he’ll play in the academy side to start with, or be sent on loan to another senior side, before being introduced into the Arsenal senior side at some juncture beyond that.
