articles.title: Is Jordan Mason or Aaron Jones the Vikings’ No. 1 RB heading into Week 1?
articles.excerpt: Alex Hunter analyzes the Vikings' backfield of Jordan Mason and Aaron Jones heading into Week 1 of the NFL season. The post Is Jordan Mason or Aaron Jones the Vikings’ No. 1 RB heading into Week 1? appeared first on DraftKings Network .
articles.source_type: Captain picks ranked with reasoning, gameweek rankings, DFS targets
articles.body: Is Jordan Mason or Aaron Jones the Vikings' No. 1 RB heading into Week 1? Once again, it’s a debate on who will be the lead back for the Vikings this season between Mason and Jones. Jones sits atop the depth chart, but will the 31-year-old actually be the RB1 over the 27-year-old Mason heading into the regular season? First off, let’s look at how these backs were used and performed last season. Last Season Jones has always been one of the most efficient rushers in the league during his career, but he slowed down in his ninth season in 2025, averaging a career-worst 4.2 YPC. Mason was more effective at 4.8 YPC, but this was also a career-low for the 27-year-old. Despite Mason being more productive on the ground, Jones held an edge in rushing usage. In the 11 games these two backs played together, Jones out carried Mason 105-85. However, Mason was trusted more in the red zone, outcarrying Jones 15-10 in that area. As a result, Mason rushed for six touchdowns while Jones only found the paydirt twice with his legs. In the passing game, Jones was the unquestioned primary receiving back over Mason. Jones saw 33 targets on 175 routes, whereas Mason only saw eight targets on 65 routes. Overall, Jones outsnapped Mason 331-207. As you can see, when both these backs were healthy last season, Jones was the lead back in every department, outside of red zone rushing, but will this continue this season? Week 1 Outlook After being the lead back last season, Jones drew the start in the lone preseason game that he and Mason both were active for this summer. That being said, these two backs usage was nearly identical. Jones saw three carries and one target on five snaps while Mason saw three carries on four snaps. Albeit a preseason game, this may be an indicator that Jones and Mason are going to split the rushing workload pretty evenly this season, which makes sense, after Mason was the more productive rusher a year ago. If Mason will see more carries, it’s hard to imagine he doesn’t retain his role as the primary rusher in the red zone, giving him more touchdown equity over Jones. Although, Jones should continue to be the main pass catching back for this offense, given the major difference in their receiving usage last season and simply because Jones has always been a reliable pass catcher throughout his career, compared to Mason, who has never done much in this department. This should once again be a two-man backfield with positive game scripts favoring Mason and negative game scripts favoring Jones. For next Sunday’s regular season opener vs. the Packers, the Vikings are a 1.5-point home favorite on DraftKings Sportsbook . This is an optimal setup for Mason to produce. Minnesota will likely want to rely on their run game if they get ahead and while it likely won’t be by much, Mason should finish this game with more touches, even if Jones technically gets the start. Make no mistake, though, this backfield will be tough to predict on a weekly basis when both Mason and Jones are healthy, and even if Mason begins 2026 with a better performance in Week 1, that doesn’t mean he is the Vikings’ RB1 for the season. articles.title: 2026 NFL Win Total Prediction, Pick: Atlanta Falcons
articles.excerpt: Keagan Smith takes a look at the Atlanta Falcons' win total for the 2026 NFL regular season and breaks down the best bet for the over/under. The post 2026 NFL Win Total Prediction, Pick: Atlanta Falcons appeared first on DraftKings Network .
articles.source_type: Captain picks ranked with reasoning, gameweek rankings, DFS targets
articles.body: 2026 NFL Win Total Prediction, Pick: Atlanta Falcons Mediocrity has been a consistent theme for the Atlanta Falcons in recent years. For the first time in a while, though, the team knocked the hiring of a head coach out of the park and could be positioned to turn things around. There are plenty of standout pieces on offense, but the quarterback and the defense do remain more uncertain when evaluating team success. Now, the question is whether Kevin Stefanski will live up to his status as a two-time Coach of the Year winner. Here’s a look at the Falcons’ win total over/under for the 2026-27 NFL season with a top betting pick. Atlanta Falcons 2026 win total, best bet When the Falcons hired Kevin Stefanski as the franchise’s new head coach, there was plenty to be excited about. The two-time Coach of the Year kept the Cleveland Browns relevant for several years even despite operating with his hands tied at times, and he’s well-regarded as one of the NFL’s better names in terms of the coaching hierarchy. Giving him Bijan Robinson, Drake London and Kyle Pitts had, and still has, many fans salivating. It’s tough to not get excited, but then you consider the rest of the context surrounding this team. The quarterback play is a massive unknown. Incumbent starter Michael Penix Jr. didn’t live up to expectations in the pros before tearing his ACL again, so how he fares coming off the injury is anyone’s guess. The team signed former Miami Dolphin Tua Tagovailoa to compete for the starting job, but his limitations are known and his preseason performance was one for the ages – not in a good way, either. When some fans are clamoring for an UDFA like Jack Strand, it says a lot about the situation under center. Then there’s the defense. Atlanta has been relatively pedestrian in that regard over the last few years, ranking 15th in yards per game (326.6) and 19th in points per game allowed (23.6) last season. While the Falcons’ pass rush was excellent with a franchise-record 57 sacks in 2025, two key EDGE talents are facing shortened campaigns – Jalon Walker tore an ACL and will miss the full season while James Pearce Jr. will serve an eight-game suspension to begin 2026. The club signed help in the front seven, adding Za’Darius Smith, Christian Harris and Samson Ebukam at linebacker while trading for defensive tackle Gervon Dexter Jr.; losing a combined 16 sacks between Walker and Pearce is tough, though. On the back end, A.J. Terrell and Jessie Bates reprise their roles as the top to players in the secondary. Drafting Avieon Terrell, the brother of A.J., also brings a high-upside pick into the mix. There’s room for this unit to improve this year, especially with Stefanski in the mix and Jeff Ulbrich retained at defensive coordinator. They’ll just have to prove it while overcoming the loss of Walker and weathering the storm of Pearce’s suspension. RELATED 2026 Fantasy Football Rankings: Top 160 players for PPR drafts and redraft leagues DraftKings Sportsbook lists the Falcons’ over/under total at 7.5 wins, with the under favored at -140 odds and the over at +120. Atlanta does see the benefit of playing in a weak NFC South, so that’s a bit of a boost in terms of the win total. No team in this division was above .500 last season, with all three of the Carolina Panthers, Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Falcons finishing 8-9. The New Orleans Saints also went 6-11 last year. There’s not a strong case for improvement from Carolina, but it’s fairly easy to see a world where both Tampa Bay and New Orleans wind up with a winning record. Due to that weak division, the Falcons do have the fourth-easiest schedule in 2026 based on opponents’ 2025 winning percentage (0.465). That certainly sets the team up to play competitive football, but the question is twofold – can they trust either of these quarterbacks, and can the defense stay afloat without two of its top talents on the edge. Those tasks may be easier said than done. Assuming the Saints and Bucs get back to winning games in the NFC South, the Falcons should stay under this win total of 7.5 in 2026. articles.title: Beto Departs Everton
articles.excerpt: Everton can confirm Beto has left the Club to join Serie A side Fiorentina on a permanent transfer for an undisclosed fee. The 28-year-old striker – who signed for Everton in August 2023 – played 113 times across all competitions for the Toffees, netting 25 goals and proving a popular figure with Evertonians. After signing from Udinese three years ago, Beto scored on his Blues debut against Doncaster Rovers in the Carabao Cup. His first of 20 Premier League goals arrived in December 2023, striking against Newcastle United in a memorable 3-0 victory at Goodison Park. In February 2025, Beto – a Guinea Bissau international – opened the scoring in Goodison’s last-ever Men’s Merseyside derby – a dramatic 2-2 draw on an iconic night under the lights at the Grand Old Lady. Everyone connected with Everton thanks Beto for his dedication, commitment and service throughout his time at the Club and wishes him all the best for the next chapter of his career in Italy.

articles.excerpt: Bryan Armetta offers up a preview, prediction and pick for Tuesday's MLB game between the Milwaukee Brewers and Chicago Cubs. The post Milwaukee Brewers vs. Chicago Cubs prediction, pick for Tuesday 9/1/26 appeared first on DraftKings Network .
articles.source_type: Captain picks ranked with reasoning, gameweek rankings, DFS targets
articles.body: Milwaukee Brewers vs. Chicago Cubs prediction, pick for Tuesday 9/1/26 The Cubs (78-60) took care of business in dominant fashion on Monday. Chicago racked up 17 runs and a whopping nine homers during a blowout win over the Brewers (85-53). Milwaukee, responsible for the best record in baseball, will be eager to turn the page on Tuesday. Can the visitors even up this series tonight at Wrigley Field? The Cubs are favorites (-123) over the Brewers; the over/under is set at ten runs . Below, I’ve laid out my preview, prediction, and best bet for Tuesday’s showdown between Milwaukee and Chicago on DraftKings Sportsbook Brewers vs. Cubs pick, best bet today Cubs ML (-123) : Chicago, fresh off of Monday’s rout, looks the part of a World Series contender. It’s difficult to envision baseball’s highest-scoring offense slowing down tonight at home against a middling arm such as Gasser. Brewers vs. Cubs prediction, preview Robert Gasser will get the nod this evening for the visitors. Over 82.1 innings of work (15 starts), the right-hander has notched a 4.59 ERA, 1.30 WHIP and 78 strikeouts (8.5 K/9). Despite middling numbers, the 27-year-old isn’t a complete pushover on the mound. He’s allowed three earned runs or less in six of his last seven appearances. Still, it’s difficult to get too excited when it comes to Gasser’s chances tonight. He ranks inside the 40th percentile or worse in xERA (4.22), xBA (.253), chase rate (29.4%) and ground ball rate (32.8%). That last statistic could prove consequential on Tuesday. Gasser’s inability to keep the ball on the ground doesn’t bode well heading into today’s matchup. The Cubs are one of baseball’s most power-happy clubs, leading the majors in home runs (196). In fact, the North Siders smacked 62 dingers during August. That’s a National League record for one club over the course of a single month. Chicago hitters have posted a 29.0% fly ball rate, third-highest in baseball. Gasser’s knack for giving up the long ball (1.4 HR/9) makes navigating tonight’s opponent a difficult task. MVP candidate Pete Crow-Armstrong and third baseman Alex Bregman are both swinging hot bats. RELATED Best Home Run Props for Tuesday 9/1/26 As for the other side, Matthew Boyd will take the hill tonight. The former All-Star has battled injuries for much of 2025. However, when healthy, he remains an above-average arm. The southpaw has notched a 3.99 ERA, 1.22 WHIP and 76 strikeouts (7.1 K/9) during 97.0 innings of work. That’s not to say the veteran has been perfect; he’s surrendered at least four runs in three of his last five appearances. However, he remains above-average when it comes to limiting free passes (2.8 BB/9). Whether or not he’s at his best, Boyd should provide Chicago with some length. The lefty has tossed six innings or more in nine of his previous ten outings. Milwaukee’s lineup, while unorthodox, gets the job done. Despite a lack of home run power, this group is at its best when stringing together base hits. The Brewers are third in runs scored (686), third in batting average (.255) and second in on-base percentage (.338). However, tonight’s contest could present some difficulty for the NL Central leaders. The Brew Crew have put up a .700 OPS against left-handed pitching, 13th-worst in the big leagues. Best Bet: Cubs ML (-123) Gasser doesn’t inspire much confidence. His propensity for fly balls should have this homer-happy Cubs lineup licking its chops on Tuesday. Boyd is far from an ace, but this isn’t the most intimidating matchup. The Brewers haven’t been the most dangerous group at the plate against lefties. Equipped with the superior starter and deeper lineup, Chicago makes plenty of sense this evening at home. Chelsea are shipping out an underwhelming duo, but why are Spurs so eager to take them? (Image credit: Getty Images) Facebook Pinterest Email Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Even after relegation scares in back-to-back seasons, the most pessimistic of Spurs supporters probably wouldn't have predicted being rock bottom after two games, with a -5 goal difference. Or perhaps they would have, from recent trauma build-up. Still, Tottenham Hotspur ’s summer incomings have been impressive, and arrived with an expectation of achieving European football this season. But the North London club, at best, could be considered slightly overzealous in regard to its expenditure this summer, and their haste in helping to solve Chelsea ’s wage bill issue is worrying, to say the least. Tottenham Hotspur secure services of Chelsea duo, but why? Spurs are in the process of signing Tosin Adarabioyo (Image credit: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images) Ahead of Tuesday’s transfer deadline at 11pm BST, Spurs look set to secure the services of Chelsea duo Mykhailo Mudryk and Tosin Adarabioyo. Their London rivals are willing to shift the pair in an effort to solve their wage bill issues, and Spurs seem all too eager to aid them in this regard. Xabi Alonso has a fine squad to work with this season, and he's successfully shifted deadwood (Image credit: Getty Images) Mudryk will sign on a season-long loan, while Adarabioyo is expected to move on a permanent transfer for around £7 million — combined, they recorded zero goals and zero assists in 23 Premier League appearances last season. Chelsea, in contrast to the North London club, are fourth in the Premier League table, having taken two wins from two against Brighton and Fulham — blockbuster 3-2 and 4-3 victories. The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week. Last season, they finished in 10th, accumulating just nine additional points to Spurs’ tally of 41, which saw them capable of being relegated all the way until the Premier League’s final gameweek. If you stare hard enough, you’ll find that there was likely an expectation for the two clubs to perform as peers this season, yet Tottenham Hotspur have, rather alarmingly, found themselves vacuuming the crumbs up off the floor in Chelsea’s kitchen. And that should worry fans of the North London club — after an initially serious summer in which Spurs secured the services of Sandro Tonali, Mateus Fernandes, Savio, Jan Paul van Hecke, Omar Marmoush, and further Premier League-proven talent, this is a concerning sign. Omar Marmoush has also arrived on loan, but that is entirely different (Image credit: Alamy) It’s one thing to take players from Manchester City ; Enzo Maresca’s men will likely challenge for the Premier League title this season, and the Savio-Marmoush duo bring multiple top-level seasons of experience under Pep Guardiola’s wing to London. But a pair of 'B squad' players from Chelsea with little observable Premier League impact? What benefits could this duo bring that outweigh the positive impact it will have on the Blues’ wage bill, and their rivals’ ability to compete? How good can Mudryk and Tosin possibly be, for paying £7m and the pair’s wages, to prevent Chelsea from getting the last laugh here? During a summer in which Spurs appeared determined to turn a page, their performances on the pitch have scarcely improved, and their transfer business will conclude on a sour note. And while fans of the North London club will surely stay focused on seeing the likes of Fernandes, Tonali, Savio and Marmoush come good, they should keep a closer eye on the duo that Chelsea appear overwhelmingly likely to have fleeced them for. It clearly bothered him When head coach Todd Monken subsequently named Watson QB1 to start the season, fans found more ways to show their displeasure While Watson didn’t play in the Browns’ preseason finale last Thursday, he was on the sideline and spent most of his time with a towel over his head — perhaps trying to be as incognito as possible. But does it bother Monken that Cleveland fans clearly have not wholly embraced his choice for starting quarterback? “Absolutely not,” Monken said in his Tuesday press conference, via transcript from the team. “Would I prefer that we would all be on the same page? Yeah, but that has nothing to do with my decision, and it can never have anything to do with my decision. “My decision has got to be about what’s best for the Browns in Week 1 and all the way through the season, and as long as I’m the head coach here.” To that end, Monken said he has confidence Watson will be able to push the ball down the field to create explosive plays. “You’re not going to be elite on offense and score points if you can’t create explosives,” Monken said. “It’s so hard to drive the football the length of the field without an explosive. You can look at the studies in terms of percentage of scoring a touchdown or getting a field goal with one explosive in a drive. Obviously, that comes after you’ve gotten the first first down. Every coordinator is going to say we’re chasing explosives, and everyone runs with, ‘Oh [you’re] chasing explosives.’ Well, no shit. Everyone’s chasing explosives and trying to not to turn it over. And that’s what you’re trying to do. What’s the defense trying to do? Turn you over and not allow explosives. That’s really the big chess match is that. The ways that you win. “So, obviously having explosive players helps that. Being able to scheme it up against certain looks and then being able to execute because your protection has to hold up when you get those opportunities. I’m confident in Deshaun and our ability to push the ball down the field, otherwise we wouldn’t be starting him.” Add favorite players, teams, and leagues with an NBCUniversal Profile Continue

The 76ers announced Wednesday that they have signed Tacko Fall, Jameer Nelson Jr., and Saint Thomas to contracts. we have signed Tacko Fall, Jameer Nelson Jr., and Saint Thomas. ✍️ pic.twitter.com/1vIxBv5QBe — Philadelphia 76ers (@sixers) September 1, 2026 Those are Exhibit 10 contracts, which are training camp contracts where a player can get a bonus (up to $85,000) if they sign to play with Philadelphia’s G League affiliate, the Delaware Blue Coats. All three of Fall, Nelson and Thomas have two-way eligibility left, and the 76ers do have one open two-way contract spot they could give out if someone stands out in training camp. Fall, the 7'6" fan-favorite center, spent two seasons in Boston and one in Cleveland, but has been out of the NBA since 2022, playing overseas. He also played in the NBA All-Star Friday Night Celebrity Game last February in Los Angeles. Nelson is the son of former NBA player and current 76ers Executive Vice President of Basketball Operations Jameer Nelson. He was in the Spurs’ training camp two years ago and then with their G League team, then in the Kings’ training camp last season and played for their G League affiliate, the Stockton Kings. Last season with Stockton, he averaged 19.9 points and 3.7 assists per game. Thomas, a 6'7" wing, was in training camp last season with Philadelphia and averaged 12.5 points and five rebounds a game for the Blue Coats when he played with them. Unlike the NFL or other sports, there are very rarely training camp battles for a roster spot in the NBA, and in this case, Philadelphia’s roster is set. It has 14 players under contract for next season and plans to enter the season at that number, deciding whether to add a 15th player down the line. For De Zerbi, who has faced a frustrating start to the 2026/27 campaign following consecutive losses to Brentford and Newcastle , Kulusevski’s return provides a boost to Tottenham’s attacking options. The versatile attacker’s ability to operate as a direct right-winger or more of a central playmaker offers De Zerbi the options his side has lacked for quite some time. Given that Kulusevski has spent 477 days away from first-team action, realistic expectations must be maintained. Re-integrating into high-intensity Premier League football following two surgical procedures and a prolonged period of inactivity will require significant patience from Spurs supporters, and it will inevitably take time before he recovers full match sharpness and rhythm. Plenty has changed at Spurs since Kulusevski last featured, including the personnel (Image credit: Getty Images) Nevertheless, stepping back onto the training pitch alongside his teammates is a significant milestone. "After 477 days I came back to full team training," Kulusevski wrote on social media. "Everything is impossible until is [sic] not. Want to see a miracle. Be one. See u soon." Sign up AFC East Buffalo Bills Miami Dolphins New England Patriots New York Jets AFC North Baltimore Ravens Cincinnati Bengals Cleveland Browns Pittsburgh Steelers AFC South Houston Texans Indianapolis Colts Jacksonville Jaguars Tennessee Titans AFC West Denver Broncos Kansas City Chiefs Las Vegas Raiders Los Angeles Chargers NFC East Dallas Cowboys New York Giants Philadelphia Eagles Washington Commanders NFC North Chicago Bears Detroit Lions Green Bay Packers Minnesota Vikings NFC South Atlanta Falcons Carolina Panthers New Orleans Saints Tampa Bay Buccaneers NFC West Arizona Cardinals Los Angeles Rams San Francisco 49ers Seattle Seahawks AFC East Buffalo Bills Miami Dolphins New England Patriots New York Jets AFC North Baltimore Ravens Cincinnati Bengals Cleveland Browns Pittsburgh Steelers AFC South Houston Texans Indianapolis Colts Jacksonville Jaguars Tennessee Titans AFC West Denver Broncos Kansas City Chiefs Las Vegas Raiders Los Angeles Chargers NFC East Dallas Cowboys New York Giants Philadelphia Eagles Washington Commanders NFC North Chicago Bears Detroit Lions Green Bay Packers Minnesota Vikings NFC South Atlanta Falcons Carolina Panthers New Orleans Saints Tampa Bay Buccaneers NFC West Arizona Cardinals Los Angeles Rams San Francisco 49ers Seattle Seahawks Rumor Mill Peacock PFT Shop Brian Gutekunst: Packers haven’t seen the Josh Jacobs video Mike Florio Mike Florio Published September 1, 2026 02:58 PM Facebook Twitter Email The misdemeanor battery case against Packers running back Josh Jacobs includes surveillance video from a camera in his garage. The police report strongly suggests that the video includes images of the alleged assault. On Tuesday, Packers G.M. Brian Gutekunst was asked at a press conference whether the team has seen it. We have not seen the video ,” Gutekunst said, via Rob Demovsky of ESPN. “Again, those are legal things going on right now, so we’ll let those play out. That’s really not for us, but in the appropriate times, if those things become available, we’ll figure that stuff out when that time comes.” Gutekunst also was asked whether the team needs to see the video before making a decision about Jacobs’s future with the team. “Again, we’re going to lean on the legal process and let that happen, but we’ll take things as they come,” Gutekunst said. The situation brings back memories of the weeks preceding the release of the notorious Ray Rice elevator video. The league, as of August 2014, had not seen the video. We argued that it would be easy for the league to get it. It was part of his case file, and Rice ultimately controlled his case file. If the league told Rice he couldn’t play until his lawyer made the video available for review, the league would have quickly gotten it. It sparked a somewhat spirited debate by phone with a league official. The conversation ended with this prediction: “If you don’t get that video, TMZ eventually will.” (By early September, TMZ had gotten it — and then all hell broke loose.) In this case, it would be even easier for the league or the team to inspect the video. It came from Jacobs’s house. He owns the footage. Why wouldn’t the Packers want to see it? Coach Matt LaFleur recently said regarding Jacobs, "[W]hat he tells me, I believe him and I trust him. I’m going to do that until proven otherwise.” One way to be proven otherwise, or to have LaFleur’s current belief confirmed, would be to tell him to produce the video. General Manager Ryan Poles was asked today if Gordon will play for the Bears. Poles answered, “I don’t know.” “I would hope so,” Poles continued. “I still have hope there. He’s going to have to continue to work hard and come back to play football again.” Poles emphasized the need for Gordon, who was out all summer with a calf injury, to push through the discomfort of rehabilitation. “Any time you have an injury and you’re coming back from something, there’s discomfort that you have to push through. And that’s what it comes down to. So we haven’t been able to get over that hump and we’re not progressing as fast as we would like. That’s really all I have to say about that,” Poles said. The Bears signed Gordon to a three-year, $40 million contract extension last year, and Gordon played in just three games last season as he struggled with groin, hamstring and calf injuries. articles.title: ROSELLA AYANE IS A BLUE
articles.excerpt: Ipswich Town Women is excited to announce the permanent signing of Rosella Ayane from Leicester City. The experienced forward, who has spent most of her career in the Barclays Women’s Super League, arrives at Town on an initial one-year deal. Rosella came through the Academy at Chelsea and made her senior debut for the club at the start of the 2013/14 campaign during a win over Doncaster Rovers Belles. Loan moves to Millwall, Bristol City and Everton soon followed before a permanent switch to Apollon Limassol in Cyprus, where she scored 19 goals in 19 games. Rosella returned to England to re-sign for the Robins for a season before joining Spurs at the start of the 2019/20 campaign. Across six years in North London scored 12 goals in 109 appearances and also helped the side to a Women’s FA Cup final against Manchester United in 2024. Rosella also brings international experience into the group, having played 35 times and found the net 11 times for Morocco. Diggins hasn’t played since she scored 19 points in a 98-90 loss at Las Vegas on July 3. Chicago (15-25) was eliminated from playoff contention on Aug. 23. It has four games left when the WNBA returns from its break for the FIBA World Cup. “We’re in full support of Skylar and want to make sure we are steadfastly prioritizing her health,” general manager Jeff Pagliocca said Tuesday in a statement. “Skylar made a strong effort to get back to the court this season. She’s been in constant communication with us through the entire process.” Diggins, who turned 36 on Aug. 2, signed with Chicago on the first day of free agency in April. She averaged 14.2 points and 4.9 assists during a rocky season with the Sky. Following a June 7 loss at Toronto, Diggins called for more leadership and maturity from players and coaches. When coach Tyler Marsh made plans to use the seven-time All-Star as a reserve, Diggins posted on Instagram about her frustration with the decision. The injury sidelined Diggins before she could play in a reserve role with Chicago. She started each of her 19 games this season. Stroud during season Josh Alper Josh Alper Published September 1, 2026 02:17 PM Facebook Twitter Email The Texans are taking a page from the Steelers’ book on contract negotiations The Steelers have long refused to engage in contract negotiations with players during the regular season and Texans General Manager Nick Caserio said that Houston will take the same approach with quarterback C.J. Stroud this year. Caserio said in July and again on Tuesday that the team has had talks with the 2023 first-round pick about a new deal, but that those talks will be put on hold when the Texans face the Bills in Week 1. “If we don’t get it figured out before the season starts, then it’ll be something we address in the offseason ,” Caserio said, via DJ Bien-Amie of ESPN.com. The Texans have already picked up their option on Stroud’s contract for 2027, so the quarterback will remain under contract regardless of how things play out on the field this year. A strong season would make it harder for the Texans to continue playing the waiting game, but anything resembling Stroud’s postseason performance from last season would lead to a lot of questions about the future of the quarterback position in Houston. If Salas appears behind the plate, he will be the youngest catcher in the big leagues since Ivan Rodriguez, who was 19 when he debuted with the Texas Rangers on June 20, 1991. Salas, who signed with the Padres in 2023 for a record $5.6 million bonus as a top international prospect, has progressed quickly through their minor league system despite a back injury that caused him to miss most of the 2025 season. The Padres’ top prospect batted .286 with seven home runs, and 37 RBIs in 72 games this year at Double-A. After being promoted to Triple-A on July 29, Salas hit .326 with three homers and 24 RBIs. Arsenal , who will strive to retain the Premier League title for the first time in the North London club’s history this season, are willing to part ways with their 19-year-old prospect. Borussia Dortmund ’s interest in Nwaneri pre-dates the signing of Giannis Konstantelias; however, the Gunners youngster is expected to receive greater playing minutes after the Greek attacker sustained a recent injury. Konstantelias suffers ligament injury, Nwaneri travels for medical to Dortmund The 19-year-old will be hoping this move is more fruitful than his loan period with Marseille (Image credit: Getty Images) According to transfers expert David Ornstein , the 19-year-old is travelling today to Dortmund to undergo his medical exam. Konstantelias is braced for a lengthy sideline spell after sustaining an anterior cruciate ligament injury in his debut Bundesliga appearance versus Hamburger SV — in which he also hit his first goal. Dortmund found themselves needing an additional attacking player (Image credit: Kristian Skeie - UEFA/UEFA via Getty Images) Dortmund prevailed 2-0 on the day, with Konstantelias scoring his side’s second: a glorious right-footed effort from just inside the box. Following the Greek’s injury, Dortmund reached out to Arsenal and made it clear that Nwaneri’s arrival had become a priority, before an arrangement was ironed out. The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week. Prior to this heightened interest, the youngster was reportedly considering a loan move to Fulham , prioritising a stay in the Premier League. This will no longer happen. The 19-year-old did not appear in the squad for the Gunners’ 3-0 pre-season victory against Manchester City in the Community Shield, missing out alongside Gabriel Martinelli. The Brazilian has since departed for Saudi Arabia, and Nwaneri is now Bundesliga-bound, with Arteta’s side hoping that the 19-year-old is able to develop further with Dortmund. Martinelli also failed to make the Community Shield squad, and has since made the move to Saudi Arabia (Image credit: Marc Atkins/Getty Images) The youngster spent the second half of the 2025/26 season on loan with Marseille in Ligue 1 , scoring twice, and assisting once, in nine French top-flight appearances. Nwaneri also scored against Dortmund for Arsenal in pre-season, during a 3-2 loss in the Emirates Cup — and converted his penalty in the post-match shootout. Since making his Premier League debut for the North London club in 2022, aged just 15, Nwaneri has failed to break into a side that has competed for the English top-flight title in four successive seasons. He has made 51 appearances for Arsenal, scoring 10 and assisting two, with Mikel Arteta confessing in August that he would like the 19-year-old to stay, but that he needs to receive further opportunities. The club reportedly weighed up the benefits of selling their youngster outright, however, a loan period has been agreed. Should Nwaneri seize the chances he will receive at Dortmund, a sale or place in the first team are both possible for him upon his return to London. articles.title: Ibrahim Mbaye’s first interview with VillaTV
articles.excerpt: Ibrahim Mbaye has spoken of his happiness at joining Aston Villa and is looking forward to linking up with compatriot Nicolas Jackson in claret and blue. Mbaye joined Villa from Paris Saint-Germain on Tuesday, completing his move to the midlands from the back-to-back UEFA Champions League winners. And the attack-minded talent, 18, is excited to have made the switch to Villa Park. “I feel good,” he told VillaTV, completing his first interview in English, as he spoke after signing on the dotted line. “I’m happy to join this team and I hope it will be good playing in this team.” Mbaye added: “I’m happy. “Aston Villa is a big team, last year won the Europa League. “I feel good and I hope it will be good.” Mbaye enjoyed a goalscoring World Cup bow for Senegal in the summer, stepping off the bench before netting an impressive finish against France in the group stage. It was the first of four appearances at the tournament, taking his total to 15 caps since making his international debut late last year. articles.title: Under-17s off to winning start in Premier League Cup
articles.excerpt: AFC Bournemouth under-17s got off to a winning start in the U17 Premier League Cup, thanks to a 3-2 victory over Southampton. Goals from Leyland Waite, Denzel Decardi-Nelson and Fikayo Solanke secured the three points for the Cherries. It ensures the Cherries get off to the strongest possible start in a group that also contains Chelsea and West Ham United. After the game, under-18s assistant coach, Elliot Head, spoke to afcb.co.uk: "The first half was a tight game with chances for both teams. "We regained the ball high up the pitch a few teams that lead to some good chances which we weren't quite able to capitalise from." The Cherries went into the interval level at 0-0, after tight first-half. Scoring in the 50th and 55th minute, the Cherries were then forced back into their own half, as Southampton brought the score level. The winner came in the 88th minute and secured all three points for the Cherries. Head continued: "The lads showed fantastic attitude throughout the game and had to dig deep after coming off the back of four games in ten days." The next under-17 cup game is away at Chelsea on 15th September.

articles.title: Doku, Cherki, and Now Ndiaye? Man City’s Penchant for Dribblers Is No Coincidence
articles.excerpt: Manchester City are loading up on players known for their dribbling ability, with Iliman Ndiaye seemingly their next new face. The post Doku, Cherki, and Now Ndiaye? Man City’s Penchant for Dribblers Is No Coincidence appeared first on Opta Analyst .
articles.source_type: xG methodology, expected points tables, head-to-head records, supercomputer projections
articles.body: Doku, Cherki, and Now Ndiaye? Man City’s Penchant for Dribblers Is No Coincidence | Opta Analyst Manchester City are loading up on players known for their dribbling ability, with Iliman Ndiaye seemingly their next new face. For a while, a fairly popular theory suggested Manchester City was a place that suffocated individual creativity in favour of focus on positional football and “the system”. It was a theory (myth?) that led to some believing Pep Guardiola simply didn’t value dribblers. Of course, the reality was almost certainly never quite as black and white as that, but there was a notable moment a few years ago. When City signed Jérémy Doku in 2023, the Belgian was not thought of as the type of winger Guardiola would typically go for, in that his primary strength was beating his man and tallying a high volume of dribbles. He didn’t score lots, his end product was called into question, and there were questions about how he’d fit into a team built around passing ability and possession retention. But he steadily developed into one of the Premier League’s best and most effective one-v-one wingers, and 2025-26 suggested his level was only continuing to rise. Whereas there’s a perception some players had certain individualistic qualities limited by Guardiola, with Jack Grealish the most common example, Doku feels very similar – just more mature – to the player they signed from Rennes. Last year, City then added Rayan Cherki , arguably even more of a maverick than Doku, and the Frenchman enjoyed a brilliant first season in the Premier League. Antoine Semenyo was another frequent dribbler who joined City in January from Bournemouth, and now they appear to be adding Iliman Ndiaye to form a formidable foursome of dribble-first attackers – and that’s ignoring the fact Phil Foden is pretty handy on the ball, and new signing Allan is highly regarded for his ball carrying. Guardiola may have gone, replaced by Enzo Maresca, but the club’s thinking has apparently been unchanged. Assuming Ndiaye’s reported £65 million move from Everton is completed, City will have the Premier League’s top three players from 2025-26 for dribble attempts: Doku (162), Semenyo (144) and Ndiaye (136). Similarly, they’ll have four of last season’s top eight for most dribbles completed: Doku (84), Ndiaye (65), Semenyo (59) and Cherki (51). And it’s worth saying that Elliot Anderson , another of City’s summer recruits, was only just behind Cherki on 50 (though admittedly from almost twice as many minutes). This seems far too deliberate for it to be a coincidence. Guardiola did say in the past that he felt the “future of football” would steer away from his possession dominance ideology and instead be defined by more transitional styles – and there’s certainly an argument these players can help City make that transition, or at least be more unpredictable. Dribblers bring chaos, and City are a team who’ll frequently be tasked with breaking through compact defences and low blocks; in fact, they spent 23.4% of their build-up time last season against a low block, the third-greatest proportion in the Premier League. Sure, maybe you can find a way through with an extra five or 10 passes; or perhaps someone like Ndiaye can slice the opposition open in a fraction of the time with a mere swivel of the hips. It seems highly unlikely City will completely abandon Guardiola’s possession-oriented principles, but some of their signings in recent years suggest an attempt to diversify their threat, and Ndiaye would be a continuation of that. In fairness to Guardiola, the story goes that when he first joined City, his initial instruction to the club’s recruitment team was to “find me players who can dribble”. And actually, several of his title-winning teams were full of players willing to attempt taking on their marker. In 2021-22 (782), 2020-21 (845), 2018-19 (801) and 2017-18 (797), City ranked in the top six for dribble attempts in the Premier League while also winning the title – otherwise, though, there’s been little correlation between the two elements. City obviously aren’t alone in valuing ball carriers or dribblers, but you’d do well to find a squad with a greater concentration of such talent in the Premier League if they can add Ndiaye to their ranks. articles.body: Barcelona complete signing of Gabriel Jesus from Arsenal Skip to content News Football Transfer News, Rumours & Gossip Barcelona complete signing of Gabriel Jesus from Arsenal Gabriel Jesus has joined Barcelona. Mitch Fretton Last Update: 1 hour ago 3 min read Add us as a preferred source on Google Barcelona have completed the signing of Gabriel Jesus from Arsenal on a permanent deal for a reported fee of £8.6m. The 29-year-old had fallen down the pecking order at Arsenal in recent seasons amid a series of injury problems, while Kai Havertz and Viktor Gyokeres had become the club’s preferred options at centre-forward. Napoli had also shown an interest in Jesus, but the former Manchester City striker has opted to continue his career in Spain. Jesus joined Arsenal from Manchester City in 2022 and scored 32 goals while providing 22 assists in 123 appearances for the Gunners. Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta confirmed before his side’s win over Aston Villa that Jesus was no longer training with the first-team squad. Jesus becomes Barcelona’s third signing from a Premier League club this summer, following the arrivals of Anthony Gordon from Newcastle and Rodri from Manchester City. GJ is blaugrana. 🤙 pic.twitter.com/brzvMFKTJb — FC Barcelona (@FCBarcelona) September 1, 2026 Table of Contents When does the summer transfer window 2026 close? What time does the Premier League transfer window shut on transfer deadline day? When does the summer transfer window close around Europe? When does the 2026/27 winter transfer window open? Can Premier League clubs sign players outside of the window? When does the summer transfer window 2026 close? The window opened on Monday June 15 and will shut on Tuesday September 1. After that, every Premier League club can register a squad of up to 25 players, 17 of whom are allowed to be non-Home Grown Players. A Home Grown Player has been registered with any club affiliated to the English or Welsh Football Association for three entire seasons or 36 months across their career before his 21st birthday, or the end of the season during which they turn 21. Under-21 players do not count towards the 25-man limit. What time does the Premier League transfer window shut on transfer deadline day? The deadline is 23:00 BST in the Premier League, but clubs can have an extra two hours to file the remaining documentation if they submit a deal sheet confirming that an agreement has been reached. The deal sheet must arrive fully completed before the transfer window closes. For international transfers, clubs also have to comply with the FIFA Transfer Matching System deadline of midnight. When does the summer transfer window close around Europe? There are slight variations between the major European leagues. Here’s when they shut. League Date BST close Premier League Sept 1 23:00 18:00 15:00 LaLiga Sept 1 22:59 17:59 14:59 Serie A Sept 1 19:00 14:00 11:00 Bundesliga Aug 31 19:00 14:00 11:00 Ligue 1 Aug 31 19:00 14:00 11:00 When does the 2026/27 winter transfer window open? The Premier League winter transfer window opens on Friday January 1, 2027 and closes on Monday February 1, 2027 at 23:00 BST. Can Premier League clubs sign players outside of the window? Clubs can only add players outside of transfer windows who are free agents and if they have room in their 25-man squad. Premier League teams can still announce deals with other clubs, but those players will not be registered to play until the window re-opens. This means there is usually little to no movement when the window closes, with four months to wait until the window re-opens. Players can be released by Premier League clubs at any time, but the usual rule is that they cannot sign for another side outside of the market. When nothing materialized, Richardson reported to the offseason program and has been competing to be the team’s backup behind Daniel Jones with Riley Leonard. Richardson’s feelings may or may not have changed. But at this point, the Colts do not intend to trade him. “He is going to be an Indianapolis Colt this year ,” General Manager Chris Ballard said in his Tuesday press conference. Richardson, 24, has continued to make strides in his development, Ballard said. “We forget how young he is sometimes. Really proud of his growth,” Ballard said. “ There were two times in camp where I thought, OK, he’s starting to really show some poise. So the two-minute against New England, we’re backed up, I think it was 38 seconds left on the clock. Gets us in field-goal range to give us a chance to get points. And then during the Atlanta scrimmage, he had a tremendous two-minute [drive] also. “So, it’s been fun to watch Anthony’s growth.” Ballard did not declare whether or not Richardson, the No. 4 overall pick of the 2023 draft. will serve as the backup, deferring to head coach Shane Steichen. But when it comes to Richardson’s status with the team at large, Steichen said the quarterback is “in a good spot.” “He’s a phenomenal teammate — and I don’t use that word lightly,” Ballard said. “Like, he is a great teammate. He likes to be around the team. He likes being part of the team. There’s never been a point — even going back into last year when he didn’t win the job — there’s not been one point where I’ve seen him hang his head and get salty. Sign up France’s Tronchon sprints to Vuelta stage win and Mas retains lead gifted by Pogacar’s crash Associated Press Associated Press Published September 1, 2026 01:04 PM Facebook Twitter Email Highlights: 2026 Vuelta a España, Stage 10 September 1, 2026 02:30 PM Relive the top moments from Stage 10 of the 2026 La Vuelta a España, where riders took on a 184.7km journey through the hills from Alcaraz to Elche de la Sierra. ELCHE DE LA SIERRA, Spain — French rider Bastien Tronchon got a career best result winning Stage 10 of the Spanish Vuelta, and Enric Mas retained the leader’s red jersey he was gifted by Tadej Pogacar’s race-ending crash. The 24-year-old Tronchon sprinted clear over the final 20 yards of a hilly 115-mile stage between Alcaraz and Elche de la Sierra. Magnus Cort was second and Thibau Nys placed third. Wout van Aert was fourth. Tronchon put his right hand to his helmet in surprise crossing the line and sobbed tearfully when his Groupama-FDJ United teammates congratulated him. Mas retained his overall lead of 1 minute, 18 seconds ahead of Primoz Roglic, the 36-year-old Slovenian who is chasing a record fifth Vuelta title. Felix Gall stayed 1:39 back in third. The Vuelta was upended over the weekend when Pogacar, the leader and overwhelming favorite to win the three-week race, crashed out and fractured his left collarbone. Stage 10 crested three third-category climbs and let a seven-man breakaway, only one of them within an hour of Mas’s overall time, build a lead of more than two and a half minutes. The peloton reeled in the last of the breakaway inside the final 3.5 miles and caught further attempts by riders to steal away for the win. Stage 11 is a flat stage suiting the sprinters over 96 miles from Cartagena to Lorca. The Vuelta finishes in Granada on Sept. 13. Previously, they fell to the Cityzens in 2022/23 after leading for the campaign’s bulk, again in 2023/24, then to a Mohamed Salah-led Liverpool in 2024/25. The Gunners , who secured the English top-flight crown with 85 points in May, have never retained the Premier League title, however, their quest to do so now appears slightly easier, and less expensive, following an accidental discovery versus Aston Villa Do Arsenal really need a left winger? Eze put in a solid shift at Villa Park (Image credit: Getty Images) Mikel Arteta’s men emerged victorious on Monday evening, taking home three points following a 1-0 victory at Villa Park. New signing Christos Tzolis, who began his Gunners career with two assists in Arsenal's Community Shield final victory versus Manchester City , was hooked at half-time against Villa, with the score tied at 0-0. Tzolis may have to fight for his position (Image credit: Getty Images) In came Eberechi Eze, who featured on the left wing for the second half’s duration, in which Arsenal took the lead, and then maintained it, through Bukayo Saka. Arteta’s side are not short on attacking depth, despite the loss of youngster Ethan Nwaneri to Borussia Dortmund on loan , and the departure of Gabriel Martinelli to Saudi Arabia. The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week. That was evidenced by both players being absent from the Community Shield final squad, in which the North London club ran riot from an offensive perspective, scoring three in under 50 minutes. On the bench that day were Eze, Saka, Viktor Gyokeres and Declan Rice, with Kai Havertz, Noni Madueke, Bruno Guimaraes and Tzolis handed starts versus Enzo Maresca’s side. And with Eze’s appearance against Villa, it appears that any fears regarding reinforcement on the left flank have been alleviated, with the Englishman well-adjusted to challenge for the role. Arsenal's depth is staggering, however, late outgoings threatened their left flank (Image credit: Getty Images) The statistics painted a clear picture: 80% pass accuracy, three duels won, seven carries for a total distance of almost 100 metres, one of which being progressive, and six kilometres covered. And, more importantly, three points for the Gunners after a dominant second half — limiting the chasing Villans to 0.24 Expected Goals (xG) while Arteta’s side racked up 0.7, and bagged the deciding goal. Much has been made of Arsenal’s strength in the position, yet Eze’s appearance now certainly warrants consideration as an alternate to Tzolis. The Gunners reportedly tried their luck with Malick Fofana at Lyon , but were rebuffed after low-balling for the player. That appears to have allowed Sunderland to sign the winger for a price the French club deem more acceptable, in one of the strongest deals of the summer transfer window Positioned second in the Premier League table, and yet to concede a goal, the future appears bright for Arteta’s side. And fans would be forgiven for interpreting Eze’s cameo as a firm statement — Arsenal can retain their top-flight title, and they already hold all the necessary keys to do so. articles.body: Whitworth makes permanent switch to Wigan Athletic Skip navigation Whitworth makes permanent switch to Wigan Athletic Announcement 12 hours ago Crystal Palace goalkeeper Joe Whitworth has completed a permanent transfer to Wigan Athletic. Whitworth joined Palace in November 2016 at the age of 13 and progressed through the Academy. He became the club’s youngest-ever Premier League ‘keeper, making his debut away at Brighton & Hove Albion in March 2023 before starting against Arsenal at the Emirates Stadium. Having captained Darren Powell’s side to Premier League International Cup glory against PSV Eindhoven, he was named Under-21s Player of the Season in 2023/24. The ‘keeper spent the past two seasons on loan with Exeter City and won their Player of the Season award in his first campaign. He now joins Gary Caldwell’s Wigan following their strong finish to last season in League One. Everyone at Crystal Palace would like to thank Joe for his efforts and wish him every success in the next chapter of his career. Sign up AFC East Buffalo Bills Miami Dolphins New England Patriots New York Jets AFC North Baltimore Ravens Cincinnati Bengals Cleveland Browns Pittsburgh Steelers AFC South Houston Texans Indianapolis Colts Jacksonville Jaguars Tennessee Titans AFC West Denver Broncos Kansas City Chiefs Las Vegas Raiders Los Angeles Chargers NFC East Dallas Cowboys New York Giants Philadelphia Eagles Washington Commanders NFC North Chicago Bears Detroit Lions Green Bay Packers Minnesota Vikings NFC South Atlanta Falcons Carolina Panthers New Orleans Saints Tampa Bay Buccaneers NFC West Arizona Cardinals Los Angeles Rams San Francisco 49ers Seattle Seahawks AFC East Buffalo Bills Miami Dolphins New England Patriots New York Jets AFC North Baltimore Ravens Cincinnati Bengals Cleveland Browns Pittsburgh Steelers AFC South Houston Texans Indianapolis Colts Jacksonville Jaguars Tennessee Titans AFC West Denver Broncos Kansas City Chiefs Las Vegas Raiders Los Angeles Chargers NFC East Dallas Cowboys New York Giants Philadelphia Eagles Washington Commanders NFC North Chicago Bears Detroit Lions Green Bay Packers Minnesota Vikings NFC South Atlanta Falcons Carolina Panthers New Orleans Saints Tampa Bay Buccaneers NFC West Arizona Cardinals Los Angeles Rams San Francisco 49ers Seattle Seahawks Rumor Mill Peacock PFT Shop Tony Romo pleads no contest to OWI charge in Wisconsin, vows to return to CBS Mike Florio Mike Florio Published September 1, 2026 12:44 PM Facebook Twitter Email Less than a week after an unnamed spokesperson issued a statement on behalf of former Cowboys quarterback and CBS broadcaster Tony Romo, Romo has addressed his July arrest for operating while intoxicated directly. On Tuesday, Romo posted a statement on Instagram. In the message, he discloses that he has pleaded no contest. He also explains that pain medication from multiple back surgeries created an “over-reliance” on alcohol. Romo also vows to return to CBS, “in time.” It’s unknown wheter CBS is on board with that part of the plan; the network placed him on leave eight days after the incident, and it has promoted J.J. Watt into Romo’s spot on the top NFL broadcast team. Here’s the full text of Romo’s statement: “Football has shaped nearly every meaningful part of my life. I played for more than 20 years, including 14 in the NFL with the Dallas Cowboys. After my retirement, CBS gave me the profound honor of staying close to the game through broadcasting. “Playing taught me the power of relationships, the strength of a team, and the toughness to face failure head-on with honesty, resilience, and the determination to do better. “This is one of those moments when I am leaning on everything football taught me. “This morning, I faced a recent personal failure by pleading no contest to a civil offense for OWl in Wisconsin. I own this completely. “Multiple back surgeries ended my career earlier than I expected and left me with constant, debilitating pain. That pain led to a dependence on pain medication, and my efforts to get off those medications led to an over-reliance on alcohol. “As I have taught my three young sons: when you fall short, you stand up and take full responsibility. This is an important first step. The harder and more important step is examining the path that brought you here and making the changes necessary to move forward. “That path requires honesty. “None of this is an excuse. These are my failures, and I take responsibility for them. “The past month has been difficult, but it has also been personally significant. It has required me to confront and own my mistakes fully — to the Lord, to myself, to my family, and now to the public. “I am working closely with a team of doctors to address my health and make the necessary changes. I am deeply grateful for the support of my family, my friends, and the NFL community including players, coaches, and owners. Your encouragement has meant more to me than you know. “As I turn my attention to my health, my family, and, in time, my return to CBS, I kindly ask for privacy during this period.” We wish Romo the best as he addresses the issues that led to the OWI charge. And we applaud him for speaking on the issue directly, and not through an unnamed P.R. firm. Owning the situation is perhaps the biggest step toward resolving it. Whether Romo’s candor resolves the situation with CBS to his satisfaction hinges entirely on CBS. Add favorite players, teams, and leagues with an NBCUniversal Profile Continue

Sign up NBC Olympics Olympics on Peacock LA 2028 Team USA Benjamin Karl, after epic shirtless gold medal celebration, reverses retirement decision Nick Zaccardi Nick Zaccardi Published September 1, 2026 12:43 PM Facebook Twitter Email Austrian Benjamin Karl, who won Olympic snowboarding gold at age 40, then became a global sensation for his shirtless celebration, is reversing his decision to retire after the 2026 Olympic season. Karl, who races parallel giant slalom, plans to compete in the 2026-27 season, highlighted by a home World Championships in Montafon in March. “It has been a long and difficult journey from competing in regional races all the way to the very top of the sport,” Karl said, according to a social media post . “I have been snowboarding for 30 years, and over time, many things started to feel almost like a given. But my recent experiences have shown me that nothing should ever be taken for granted. “I have learned to appreciate again just how much support I have received over all these years — support that is anything but a given. Now I am really looking forward to continuing my career.” At the Milan Cortina Games, Karl broke the record for oldest individual Winter Olympic gold medalist. Later in the Games, 41-year-old American Elana Meyers Taylor broke Karl’s record with monobob gold. Karl considered a switch to cycling after the Games. “However, a number of things happened over the summer that I simply could not have foreseen,” Karl said in the post. “At the same time, I increasingly came to realize that, quite simply, I am a snowboarder who loves riding his bike.” Karl previously won Olympic medals in 2010 (silver), 2014 (bronze in parallel slalom) and 2022 (gold). In 2017-18, he averaged 23.1 points and 4.3 assists per game for the Pacers, won Most Improved Player and was an All-Star, an All-NBA and an All-Defensive Team player. Then the next season he ruptured his quadriceps tendon, and he was never physically right again. Oladipo, now 34, hasn’t played in the NBA in three seasons. In an open letter to general managers at The Players Tribune , Oladipo said it took a long time for him to stop chasing what was lost and just be patient and get his body right. He said he is finally in that place, can still contribute to a winning basketball team, and wants that chance. “Me, in this moment of my life, at 34 years old. The version of her dad that got kicked all the way down the mountain, then spent years trying to climb back up, only to get kicked back down, again and again … but never once quit trying to climb. The version of her dad that, let’s be real, is probably getting counted out by a lot of people, and is probably getting laughed at by a few of them … but has managed to keep his faith, and keep his purpose. The version of her dad that’s finally found the perspective, and the humility, to write a letter like this one. “To say to any GM who’s willing to listen: I believe my body is finally right. I believe I still have GREAT (and more importantly, WINNING) basketball in front of me. I believe I can be a valuable contributor to an NBA locker room. And what I’m asking for right now is an opportunity to prove it.... “So that’s where I’m at with everything. I don’t know how my journey here is going to end....... Maybe a team out there will give me a chance. Maybe no team will. That’s really up to you all. But if you’re in an NBA front office, and you took the time to read this: Thank you from the bottom of my heart.” Oladipo has been linked to Sacramento as a potential backup to rookie Darius Acuff Jr., but nothing official has come of that. Oladipo played in the G League for the Wisconsin Herd part of last season and averaged 13.5 points per game in the regular season, shooting 32.5% from 3-point range. He has also played some in China in recent years. Oladipo faces the reality many older players do: Most teams would rather give a bench point guard spot (or any position) to a young player they can develop and hold on to for years than to one on the back end of a career. Still, there is a real role for mature, quality veterans in the locker room who can still contribute something on the court. Whether Oladipo is that guy and gets a chance remains to be seen, but he’s made his pitch. Mentions Victor Oladipo Add favorite players, teams, and leagues with an NBCUniversal Profile Continue

Now they’re three key members of the Rams’ defense. McDuffie was traded to the Rams in March, Garrett was traded to the Rams a couple months later, and Donald just came out of retirement. McDuffie told Andrew Siciliano of NFL Media that he wouldn’t believed it was possible for Rams General Manager Les Snead and head coach Sean McVay to bring all three of them onto the same team. I probably would’ve said you’re lying , for real,” McDuffie said. “There’s no way you can get me. There’s no way you can get Myles. There’s no way you can get A.D. But, hey, hat off to Les. Hat off to Sean. Those guys are masterminds and they did it.” The 25-year-old McDuffie has already been a first-team All-Pro once and won Super Bowl rings twice in his first four NFL seasons -- and he’s the least accomplished of the trio: Garrett has been named the NFL’s Defensive Player of the Year two of the last three years, while Donald is one of only three players in NFL history to win Defensive Player of the Year three times. Most teams don’t add even one player with those kinds of credentials to their defense in an offseason. The Rams added three. McDuffie is still having a hard time believing it’s real. He can do without fame that comes with greatness Associated Press Associated Press Published September 1, 2026 12:19 PM Facebook Twitter Email Scheffler: FedExCup a 'nice way to finish' year August 30, 2026 08:29 PM Scottie Scheffler recalls his Round 4 comeback at the Tour Championship to win his second career FedExCup, calling his performance in the playoffs "a nice way to finish off the season." ATLANTA — Scottie Scheffler’s final act of the season was to sign his winning scorecard. After a few minutes to exhale, his wife and two sons having come into the room, he placed his cap over the fixed camera the PGA Tour now installs in previously private scoring areas. Content is king. It wasn’t quite the level of Brian Harman smirking and shooting the bird at the camera in Minnesota, which made Scheffler chuckle and pump his fist. Both were playful moments, and yet East Lake shed a little light on Scheffler’s incredible staying power. Scheffler loves what it takes to be the best player in golf, even the tedious work. He just doesn’t care for all the noise and notoriety that accompany greatness. “I have a tendency to keep my head down and kind of stay in my own lane when I’m out there playing,” he said during the trophy presentation at the Tour Championship. “It’s really fun when you’re able to win and celebrate with the fans in moments like these, and have my family here.” Still, his priority is to crush more than to engage. So he added somewhat apologetically, “I feel bad sometimes. I really do keep my head down and try to focus as much as I can. But I really do hear all the cheers, and I’m very thankful for all of them.” The RBC Heritage at Hilton Head is reputed to be among the most chill tournaments on the schedule, the perfect place to decompress right after the Masters. During the pro-am that week, Scheffler said he felt a calmer vibe at Augusta National despite the enormous pressure, mainly because of the space inside the ropes and spectators (patrons) who cheer, not scream. When he reached the ninth tee, fans at Hilton Head were screaming his name as he waited for the fairway to clear to tee off. Scheffler turned and smiled. It’s part of the deal, and he knows that by now. But this extraordinary run of dominance allows for speculation how long he can keep it up as the attention gets brighter. Winning is hard. The trappings that come with it can be exhausting. The way Scheffler showed up seemingly every week — he finished first, second or third in half of the 20 tournaments he played — and then capped off the season by winning two of the three postseason tournaments was satisfying. It also makes him a shoo-in to be voted PGA Tour player of the year for a fifth straight time. That would tie Tiger Woods for winning the most in a row. Best comparison with Tiger is separation Comparisons with Woods, just like athletes in any sport across generations, are for pool halls and podcasts. Scheffler brushed off the inevitable moment of passing Woods at No. 1 on the PGA Tour career earnings list, a spot Woods held for nearly 26 years. “I wouldn’t really consider that a Tiger record being broken,” Scheffler said. “I think it just shows one of the many effects he had on the game of a golf in a positive way.” Woods never played for a prize fund of $10 million in his peak years from 1997 through 2009. Scheffler played for an average purse of $19.25 million this year. When it comes to money records, it just isn’t a fair fight. The real benchmark — 82 tour wins — is still a long way off. Scheffler has gone three straight years with three wins or more. Woods went 10 out of 11 years winning at least four times. Scheffler, however, has separated himself in a similar manner as Woods. His points average in the world ranking is more than double that of Rory McIlroy at No. 2. This is his 171st week in a row at No. 1 in the world. Woods holds the record with 281 consecutive weeks at No. 1. A milestone that for years looks untouchable is now at least thinkable. Practice makes close to perfect for Scheffler There is not much drama with Scheffler, and he likes it that way. His obsession is such that he once said he had to force himself to find something other than golf to think about. Having two young boys have helped. “Part of what’s great about golf and part of what’s very frustrating about golf is it’s kind of an endless puzzle you’re always trying to solve,” Scheffler said. “I feel like in order to become good at this game, you have to really enjoy the harder parts of it, the stuff that’s a little bit more mundane.” For Scheffler, that would be the first 10 minutes on the stationary bike. Cardio work is not his favorite. Neither is a cold plunge at 5:30 a.m. “Do I want to go in there and freeze? No, but I do it,” he said in January. Practice, however, doesn’t get old. Neither does competing. His caddie, Ted Scott, once told of a round they played at Cypress Point early in 2025. Scheffler was returning from slicing open his right hand when he tried to use a wine glass to cut ravioli. He showed Scott no mercy that day, prompting the caddie to say, “Scottie don’t play games when he’s playing games.” It’s all about getting the most out of every day, from the cold plunge to the bike to the range to the first tee. Scheffler is relentless and it’s a matter of how long he can keep up this pace. “I don’t feel like I take days off. I’m highly competitive, and I’m very proud of being able to have the consistent results I’ve had over the years,” he said. “I feel like it’s a gift to play out here on the PGA Tour, and I don’t want to take it for granted. ... I don’t want to look back at the end of my career and feel like I could have done more in order to play well.” Add favorite players, teams, and leagues with an NBCUniversal Profile Continue

articles.source_type: Sage press conferences, named XIs, injury updates
articles.body: Palace sign Honest Ahanor on loan Skip navigation Palace sign Honest Ahanor on loan Announcement 1 day ago Crystal Palace are delighted to announce the loan signing of talented young defender Honest Ahanor. A senior Italy international at just 18-years-old, Ahanor joins Palace on loan from Atalanta until the end of the 2026/27 season. The left-footed defender came through Genoa’s youth system and made his senior debut in Serie A as a 16-year-old, starting against Juventus in September 2024. Having featured six times for Genoa, Ahanor last summer transferred to Atalanta, where he has since played 35 times in all competitions – including nine times in the UEFA Champions League. The teenager impressed to such an extent that, in June, Ahanor won his first two senior international caps for Italy, keeping clean sheets in wins against both Luxembourg and Greece. Ahanor said upon joining: “I'm very happy to be here and to be a part of this great family. "To be at one of the best clubs for young players in the Premier League is something which makes me grateful and excited." Chairman Steve Parish said: “Honest is an exciting young talent whose arrival offers further competition for places ahead of another European campaign at Selhurst Park. "We are pleased to have him with us in South London.” Related News Announcement Club First-team Signings Honest Ahanor Related News More News

articles.title: First Interview: Ahanor sets out target for Palace
articles.excerpt: Honest Ahanor is targeting more continental glory for Crystal Palace this season, in his first interview after joining on loan from Atalanta.
articles.source_type: Sage press conferences, named XIs, injury updates
articles.body: First Interview: Ahanor sets out target for Palace Skip navigation First Interview: Ahanor sets out target for Palace Video 1 day ago Honest Ahanor is targeting more continental glory for Crystal Palace this season, in his first interview after joining on loan from Atalanta. Speaking to Palace TV, the talented 18-year-old defender believes the Eagles can build upon their recent successes in the FA Cup and UEFA Conference League with Europa League glory this season – and wants to play a key part in helping them do so. Ahanor said upon signing: “I'm really excited to be here. The Premier League is one of the most important leagues in the world. “To be at one of the best clubs for young players in this league is something which makes me grateful and happy. “To come here on loan, and try to be the best player I can in this league, is something which makes me grateful. “I think that for the team, the important thing is to be top – to do our best. Last year, Crystal Palace won the Conference League. This year, we're going to play in the Europa League. "We're going to try to get to the final and try, maybe, to win the cup – why not?!” Quote Icons I hope that we can... do a lot of things together Honest Ahanor Ahanor has some impressive credentials to his name despite his tender years, having spent much of his career thus far playing up the age groups – culminating in him playing 35 times for Atalanta last season, including nine times in the UEFA Champions League. The teenager said of his own game: “I think that from a young age, I'm very calm. I'm very hungry about football. I like to play. I like to let all the people feel my passion. “I hope to play in the next few weeks at the stadium, to feel the passion of the fans and to be with them. “I think that for all players, the passion of the fans is really important. To feel the club, to feel the shirt, to feel all the city… it's something that can improve you, improve the team to keep working, to try to improve. “I hope soon to play in the stadium, to feel the passion of the fans. I hope that we can be a family and try to do a lot of things together.” You can watch Ahanor’s first full Palace TV interview above! September 1 257 comments 1 September 2026 257 comments As Manchester City prepare to host Coventry City in Gameweek 3, many Fantasy Premier League (FPL) managers are set to deploy the Triple Captain chip on Erling Haaland (£15.5m). Indeed, the leading chip in our Gameweek 3 poll is the Triple Captain . Around 30% of responders say they’re playing that chip this week. Here, we take a look at some of the pros and cons of using the Triple Captain chip on Haaland in Gameweek 3. Cherki, Mbeumo, Newcastle players: Buy, keep or sell in Gameweek 3? Score More Points. Win More Mini Leagues. Join FFScout. PROS ALREADY OFF THE MARK Haaland is up and running. He scored twice in the 4-1 away victory at Crystal Palace in Gameweek 2. First, he found the net with a looping header, before a powerhouse finish late on. Prior to that, he blanked at home to Bournemouth, but on another day, he scores plenty. With no signs of rustiness after the World Cup, Haaland has recorded nine shots in the box in the first two Gameweeks, the most of any player in FPL. Above: Erling Haaland’s shot map in 2026/27 HOME COMFORTS Haaland is usually a reliable option on home turf. Under Pep Guardiola last season, he amassed 120 points, with 15 goals and four assists in 17 matches at the Etihad Stadium. In that period, he supplied six double-digit hauls and averaged 7.4 points per match. Paired with elite underlying numbers, the Norwegian penalty-taker probably has the best Triple Captain credentials of any player. NEWLY-PROMOTED OPPOSITION Moreover, it’s newly-promoted Coventry at home in Gameweek 3. Frank Lampard’s men have lost both of their first two matches, having conceded four times to Arsenal and Hull City. They’ve failed to find the net, too. In truth, Coventry’s start to the 2026/27 season hasn’t been terrible, but they have lacked physicality and goal threat, a concern ahead of Saturday’s trip to City. It also sounds like playmaker Rayan Cherki (£7.7m) will be going all-out to assist Haaland in this match. “When I saw Enzo [Maresca] was going to change me, I didn’t like that and I need to show them that I want to play and want to score and give assists for Erling. Today I didn’t give a lot of balls for him [Haaland]. The next time I want to give Erling a lot of balls.” – Rayan Cherki in Gameweek 2 The chance that Haaland may get a Double Gameweek in the first half of the season is extremely unlikely, so using the Triple Captain chip at home to newly-promoted opposition looks like a solid play. TAKE ON THE WILDCARDERS This is a simple one. Plenty of engaged Fantasy managers are on a Wildcard this week, mostly those who opted not to start with Haaland. They can’t Triple Captain him because they are already playing a chip, so this could be an opportunity to take them on. GOOD XMINS Haaland has completed the full 90 minutes in both matches so far this season. That might not be the case later in the season, especially when you factor in Europe. For example, City host Ipswich in Gameweek 7. But on either side of that encounter, they have Champions League fixtures against Paris Saint-Germain and AEK Athens, followed by an early Saturday kick-off away at Aston Villa. His minutes are probably going to be more uncertain, then.
