articles.body: City complete Enzo Fernández signing from Chelsea Manchester City Official App Manchester City FC Ltd Manchester City have completed the signing of Enzo Fernández from Chelsea on a five-year contract. The Argentina international’s deal means he will remain at the Etihad Stadium until the summer of 2031. At just 25, Fernández is armed with a wealth of top-level experience, having won four major trophies during his time playing on homeland with both Defensa y Justicia and River Plate, before helping Benfica on their way to Primeira Liga success and becoming a key member of the Chelsea team that won the UEFA Conference League and FIFA Club World Cup in 2025. Indeed, during his time in west London he developed a reputation as one of the most technically gifted central midfielders in the Premier League. And at international level, he won the 2022 World Cup and 2024 Copa America with Argentina, before appearing in another World Cup final this summer as La Albiceleste lost to Spain in the final. Fernández says he could not be happier to have joined City at this stage of his career. On joining Manchester City, Fernández said: “Manchester City are the most successful club in England in recent times. “Every player wants to be part of a club like this because everyone knows how well-run City are. “I could not be happier to be here, and I am ready for the challenge of helping City continue winning trophies. This is a club built for success. “If you look across the squad, City have quality in every area. I want to learn from my new teammates and become a better player. “I pride myself on continually improving my game. Anyone who’s worked with me will know how hard I train every single day and how much I put into matches. I give absolutely everything and I can promise Manchester City that will continue now I’m here. “I want to thank Hugo, Enzo, Khaldoon and everyone at City who has made this deal possible. I want to take the faith shown in me and repay it as soon as possible.” Director of Football Hugo Viana added: “At Manchester City, we are always looking to bring in world-class players and Enzo fits the bill. “He is a complete midfielder: technically gifted, hardworking, tenacious and a goalscorer. “He is adept at playing different styles of football. He is comfortable playing a possession-based game, and he can play on the counter effectively, too. “To have played in two World Cup finals and won major trophies in multiple countries at just 25 says everything you need to know about his mentality, professionalism and technical quality. “We are delighted to bring him here and feel very strongly he will improve our team.” Everyone at City would like to send a warm welcome to Enzo and wish him well during his time here. We all look forward to seeing him play in sky blue very soon. The complete midfielder Born in Villa Bonich, San Martin, part of the Buenos Aires metropolis, Enzo Fernández was gripped by football from an early age. His family is largely made up of River Plate obsessives - in fact, he’s named after the famous River attacking midfielder Enzo Francescoli. Fernández had a ball at his feet as soon as he could and football was the only life he has ever envisaged for himself. He joined River aged just six and gradually worked his way through the youth ranks at his boyhood club, before moving to Defensa y Justicia on a two-year loan switch when he was 18. At Defensa y Justicia he played under manager Hernan Crespo, the former Parma, Inter and AC Milan striker - an icon of Argentinian football. Fernández gradually established himself as a regular and won the 2020 Copa Sudamericana and the 2021 Recopa Sudamericana. It was a transformative loan move for Fernández, who returned to River a better, more complete player and helped them win the league title in 2021. A star was truly born. European clubs were soon swarming, and it was Benfica who captured his signature, joining the Portuguese giants in the summer of 2022. Handed the No.13 shirt synonymous with club legend Eusebio, he transitioned to European football effortlessly. But it was the 2022 World Cup that saw Fernández catapulted to global fame. Argentina won their third trophy, and Fernández was exceptional. He was just 21, yet the fullness of his game became a huge talking point across football. It seemed he could do everything: a fighter, a goalscorer and a player who controls matches. As a result of his performances and just six months after moving to Portugal and with Benfica on course for title success, he made his move to the Premier League with Chelsea, where he went on to win the Europa Conference League, the FIFA Club World Cup and established himself as one of the division’s finest talents. He also won the Copa America with Argentina in 2024 and appeared in another World Cup final this summer as La Albiceleste lost to Spain in the final. He currently has 49 caps and has scored eight goals. It’s a glittering CV for a man his age. And now comes a move to Manchester City. So, what are City getting? In short, a winner and a world-class talent. Fernández is arguably the perfect modern midfielder – a player comfortable in possession, with outstanding technique, wonderful vision, a great range of passing and the ability to score goals. He gets involved in games and never shies away, a leader who thrives on big occasions and in pressure situations. His knack of arriving in the box late and getting on the end of balls is perhaps his most striking asset. He scored 15 goals and contributed seven assists for Chelsea last season in 54 games across all competitions. A matchwinner of the highest calibre. One thing is for certain: City will be a more complete proposition with Fernández in the side. Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta is off to the perfect start in 2026/27 (Image credit: Getty Images) Facebook Pinterest Email Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Few pundits or supporters could see anything other than Arsenal retaining the Premier League trophy this season before opening day. Mikel Arteta has strengthened his squad in all areas of the pitch, whilst the managerial changes at their major rivals over the last eight months have left them not yet in a position to challenge. The Spaniard’s side weren’t the most attractive title winners last term, as tension crept into their approach as they chased their first championship in 22 years, but they have started this campaign with renewed confidence. Arteta at Villa Park on Monday night (Image credit: Getty Images) Last season, Bukayo Saka , Kai Havertz and Martin Odegaard all had their lowest goal contributions in the last three years, so ensuring those attackers stay injury-free will naturally make some improvement. However, there are also clear indications that they are evolving stylistically, with new signings Bruno Guimaraes and Christos Tzolis adding more creativity. Back-to-back titles? You wouldn't bet against them (Image credit: Getty Images) The sample size for this season is still relatively small, but the midfield seems to be progressing the ball forward more quickly, as they show signs of greater variation in their attacks. Arsenal have only added centre-back Ezri Konsa this summer, though their full-backs are another area where they can increase their output in the final third. The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week. Arteta likes to purchase full-backs who are comfortable in central areas, with Riccardo Calafiori, Jurrien Timber and Piero Hincapie all having spent considerable time at centre-back throughout their careers. This enables them to not only offer cover in the centre of defence, but also make runs inside their wingers, invert into central positions in possession and provide physicality from set-pieces. Calafiori is perhaps the most interesting example, as he was one of the best centre-backs in Serie A during the 2023/24 campaign. Riccardo Calafiori (Image credit: Getty Images) Under the management of Thiago Motta at Bologna , he illustrated his ability to carry the ball forward and make line-breaking passes, whilst simultaneously intercepting opposition attacks and winning duels against robust strikers. After moving to the Emirates, he switched back to the role which he had predominantly played in his formative years at Roma At Villa Park on Bank Holiday Monday, Unai Emery had clearly devised a plan to nullify his influence, with John McGinn playing on the right-hand side directly against him. John McGinn (Image credit: Getty Images) The Scotsman was happy to track him more centrally, whilst Boubacar Kamara and Matty Cash also took on the responsibility of monitoring the Italian as he glided into their area of the pitch. However, just before the hour mark, substitute Eberechi Eze played a pass inside and Calafiori displayed his athleticism to wrap his foot around and scoop the ball into the path of Saka, who bundled it past Aston Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki. After a discussion with Arteta, Calafiori and Arsenal almost repeated the move when Eze played him in once more, only for the offside flag to be raised just after the left-back had cleverly dragged the ball past a trailing Alysson. In the 97 minute, he was the furthest Arsenal player up the pitch as his team went in search of scoring a second. The Italian has been directly involved in a goal in his last three games, including his early finish in the Community Shield against Manchester City. "It was very different," said Arteta after the match when reminded his team had lost on their last visit to the ground. "That shows our maturity, and it shows we have players who can change the momentum and understand what is needed in the game." Calafiori is one of those players, and it would be a huge surprise if he didn’t record a seasonal best for goal contributions in Arsenal’s pursuit of back-to-back titles. Spending the 2017/18 season at VfL Bochum, the forward joined the academy of TSC Eintracht Dortmund, spending three years with the club before continuing his youth career at Sportfreunde Siegen for the 2021/22 campaign. Transferring to SC Paderborn in 2022, the forward made his Under-19s debut in the opening matchday of the 2022/23 A-Juniors Bundesliga West, playing the first half of a 1-1 draw against Duisburg. Also netting a stoppage-time winner against his former side VfL Bochum, Ansah was promoted to the reserve team of Paderborn. The Germany Under-21 international netted twice on his top-flight debut in a 2-1 win over VfB Stuttgart before finding the net against TSG Hoffenheim, Eintracht Frankfurt and RB Leipzig. Born in Lüdenscheid, Ansah broke through at SC Paderborn, helping the reserve team win promotion from the Oberliga to the Regionalliga, scoring six goals in 10 outings during the 2022/23 campaign. Making his senior bow in the 2. As a result, it is Maresca’s men who will see the Senegalese forward among their ranks this season, having swooped in and found an agreement for £60 million, and an additional £5 million in add-ons, according to BBC Sport Richarlison was expected to return to the Toffees; instead, it will be Grealish (Image credit: Getty Images) Instead of Richarlison returning, it will now be Grealish, who registered two goals and six assists for the Toffees in 22 appearances during the 2025/26 season. The 30-year-old endured a foot injury in January, mid-way through his loan period from the Cityzens, playing in what appeared to be his final game for Everton versus Aston Villa on the 18th of that month. Grealish has since made a recovery, making an appearance from the bench in Manchester City’s 3-0 Community Shield final loss versus Arsenal, and another in the club’s 2-1 win against Bournemouth. The winger is set to return for another season-long loan period, according to BBC Sport , and Everton are also looking to make additional attacking signings, with USMNT star Folarin Balogun on their radar, before the transfer deadline. articles.body: Grealish returns to Everton for second loan spell Manchester City Official App Manchester City FC Ltd Jack Grealish has joined Everton on a season-long loan deal. Having spent the 2025/26 season on loan with the Toffees, Grealish will now return to the Hill Dickinson Stadium outfit for a second successive campaign. He makes the latest move up the M62 having made 159 appearances for City, scoring 17 goals since joining in the summer of 2021. After making the move to City from Aston Villa, the England winger subsequently went on to play a key role during what proved the most successful period in the Club’s history. In that time, the 30-year-old helped City win seven major trophies, a haul that included three Premier League titles, the FA Cup, UEFA Champions League, UEFA Super Cup and FIFA Club World Cup. Grealish’s maiden season at the Club in 2021/22 saw him play his part as City claimed what was a fourth Premier League title under Pep Guardiola with the Birmingham-born wide man featuring 39 times overall. However, his Etihad career truly took flight the following term with Grealish going on to prove a key component of the side that secured the historic Treble of Premier League, FA Cup and a maiden UEFA Champions League success. Grealish started both the 2023 FA Cup final where City beat Manchester United 2-1 and 2023 UEFA Champions League final which saw the Blues memorably beat Inter 1-0 to claim a first European Cup and with it the Treble. More notable success was to follow for the attacking winger in 2023/24. Grealish was part of the City teams that lifted both the 2023 UEFA Super Cup and 2023 FIFA Club World Cup, in the process becoming the first English side to secure the Big Five of league, FA Cup, Champions League, UEFA Super Cup and FIFA Club World in the same calendar year. And another memorable season was capped with Grealish helping City create yet more history by becoming the first English men’s side to win four Premier League titles in a row. A further 32 appearances followed in what proved a frustrating 2024/25 season for City before Grealish then spent the 2056/26 campaign on loan at fellow Premier League side Everton where he made 22 appearances in total before a foot injury cut short his campaign. Everyone at Manchester City would like to wish Jack the very best of luck during his time at Everton. articles.title: Ndiaye signs for City
articles.source_type: Club-published FPL Scout Report each gameweek, team news, kick-off info
articles.body: Ndiaye signs for City Manchester City Official App Manchester City FC Ltd Manchester City are delighted to announce the signing of Iliman Ndiaye on a five-year deal. The 26-year-old Senegal international arrives at the Etihad Stadium armed with significant Premier League experience after two years at Everton. Before that, he represented Marseille and shone in the Championship with Sheffield United during their 2022/23 promotion campaign. He has also represented his country on 44 occasions, including at the 2022 and 2026 World Cups. An attacking threat who can play on the wing or through the middle, Ndiaye is two-footed and a source of creativity and goals. Indeed, his dribbling ability has seen him garner a reputation as one of the most entertaining players in England’s top-flight. And now he’ll take his place as part of Enzo Maresca’s reshaped City squad as we look to have a successful 2026/27 season. “I’ve worked my whole life for an opportunity like this. “City are one of the best clubs in the world and I’ve seen them win everything as I’ve grown up. “To be able to write my own chapter in a story that special is the chance of a lifetime and I’m determined to grab it with both hands. “It’s not always been easy in my career, but I always had the belief that I could play for a team challenging for the biggest prizes and now I’m here. It feels so good. “I love to play with the ball on the floor in an attacking team that wants to score as many goals as possible. That’s why I know this is the perfect fit. “City fans can rest assured that I will give my all to bring more success to this incredible club.” Director of Football Hugo Viana added: “Iliman is a very talented footballer. “He’s had to work incredibly hard to reach this level and in my first conversation with him it was immediately obvious how grounded he is and the determination he has to be the best player he can be. “I’ve no doubt City fans will get a thrill seeing him in action for us. “We know this Club develops players. We make a commitment to every single player we sign that we will make them better footballers. “I am really excited to see the level Iliman can reach in the years ahead because I know for sure working with Enzo and his staff is going ensure he becomes a top-class Premier League player.” Special talent, boundless belief Iliman Ndiaye catches the eye on the football pitch. Few can match his skill and close control whether in tight spaces or one-v-one against elite Premier League defenders. And while that showmanship is a key facet of what makes him an attractive prospect, it doesn’t tell the whole story. Ndiaye’s route to the very top of the tree in European football has been unusual to say the least. Born in France, he represented his hometown of Rouen at first before moving to Marseille in the south of the country and then on to Dakar in Senegal. He then moved to London as a teenager and had trials with several of England’s biggest clubs but to no avail. Instead, he joined non-League side Boreham Wood and made something of a name for himself on the Rising Ballers YouTube channel. Son of a dancer and choreographer, it’s easy to see where his agility and flair came from. Stepovers, flicks, seal dribbles galore. But under all that was a steely determination to carve out a professional career. Eventually he was spotted by Sheffield United scouts and he had his big break. In 2022/23, he was the Blades’ Player of the Year as they sealed promotion to the top-flight before he got his move back to Marseille, who he had followed since being there as a boy. However, he was back in England 12 months later with Everton. In his two years with the Toffees, he’s regularly had fans, pundits and opponents drooling of his command of the football while City fans may recall a special strike at the Etihad Stadium on Boxing Day 2024. But now he’ll bring both that brilliance and dedication to City as he makes his latest step up. Andoni Iraola (Image credit: Getty Images) Facebook Pinterest Email Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google At the start of the summer, most Liverpool supporters and observers would have identified three key areas of the team that needed addressing in the transfer market. The obvious was a winger to effectively replace Mohamed Salah. In signing Bradley Barcola, Liverpool have done that but on the opposite wing. Barcola , though, you could argue, is actually the replacement for Luis Diaz, who departed the year before. Liverpool's glaring right-back issue Trent Alexander-Arnold holds the Premier League trophy amid Liverpool's title celebrations at Anfield in May 2025 (Image credit: Getty Images) The next two positions that most supporters would have wanted to see addressed also revolved around the lack of replacing other previously departed legends. Fabinho left Liverpool three years ago now, but still his role in midfield as a defence-first player hasn’t been replaced. Have Liverpool replaced Fabinho yet? Many fans don't think so (Image credit: Getty Images) While Trent Alexander-Arnold left a year ago and no matter how hard he tries, Jeremie Frimpong simply isn’t a replacement, or even an actual right back. Liverpool, though, have gone through the summer seemingly without any desire to add either a midfielder or a right-back, despite the clear need in each instance. The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week. Arguably it’s at right-back which is the biggest issue, although both full-back positions are areas of major concern and this was highlighted in the 2-2 draw with Nottingham Forest - Andoni Iraola's first home game in charge. Frimpong and Milos Kerkez were hooked in the 72nd minute, with Liverpool 2-1 down at the time. Now, there are potentially several other reasons (not least youngster Trey Nyoni's impressive cameo in midfield) why Iraola’s team enjoyed their best 20 minutes of the game from that point on, but certainly a contributing factor was the full-backs being replaced. Szoboszlai can learn like Milner - and become a better midfielder Dominik Szobsozlai, as he was regularly last season, moved to right-back, immediately giving Liverpool a player who can actually put in a cross and also be defensively stronger than the player he was replacing. The Hungarian might not necessarily like playing there, but Iraola could do far worse than have the same conversation Jurgen Klopp had with James Milner in 2016 in explaining how he wanted the midfielder to be his left-back for the season ahead. A year later, Milner explained what he learned in the new position: “But at times you have to curb that and adapt to the match situation and maybe sometimes hold back a bit if the time of the game suits that. I think sensing danger early is the biggest thing to learn. When you play in midfield you’re obviously always switched on to defending.” Dominik Szoboszlai was occasionally used at right-back by Arne Slot last season (Image credit: Getty Images) Those words about “sensing danger early” are incredibly timely, with Iraola’s pre-Nottingham Forest press conference featuring a very similar message when discussing his midfield’s need to find a balance after being caught out twice by Newcastle in the opening fixture. “There are players that are very good, they’re smelling, ‘OK, there is real danger, I can’t take the risk of going (forward),” explained Iraola. “Now I think I have to stay’. “Recognising those situations is the job we have to do now.” A season at right-back, then, would actually help Szoboszlai learn that side of his game and make him a better midfielder in future. That should be the message Iraola gives him in order to get the Reds’ No. 8 to buy into the role. Would Szoboszlai particularly enjoy it? Probably not, but it’s about what’s best for the team, as Milner succinctly explained: “It’s about whatever’s best for the team and ultimately I just want to be out there playing games, contributing and helping this football club.” And if Szoboszlai has designs on becoming Liverpool captain after Virgil van Dijk departs, then a selfless season at right back would show he puts the team first and give him a new understanding of the team and overall patterns of play. Liverpool solve two issues with Szoboszlai role change Dominik Szoboszlai (Image credit: Getty Images) For Liverpool, they’d be getting a far more reliable outlet on the right, who can produce crosses like the one Szoboszlai did for Alexander Isak against Forest, which the £125 million man couldn’t get on the end of. No Liverpool player had more touches, created more chances or made more accurate crosses than Szoboszlai against Forest. He made three stat-recorded accurate crosses, while Frimpong and Kerkez made none between them. The duo attempted six, with none of them finding their target. It was a similar story against Newcastle the week before. Of course, stats on crossing is pretty flawed, a player can produce a wonderful cross but if the forward doesn’t get on the end of it, it’s recorded as a failed cross. The eye test tells us that Szoboszlai’s crossing was significantly better than Frimpong’s versus Forest. Of that there is no doubt. He can also move inside more to create numbers-up situations in midfield, again more akin to Alexander-Arnold did. Liverpool’s focus on signing attacking wingers for Iraola this summer has neglected the right-back and midfield positions, but moving Szobsozlai fixes both, at least temporarily. If Iraola is serious about getting the best out of his squad, and Szoboszlai is serious about being a team player, it’s a change that would significantly benefit Liverpool this season. As well as writing about Liverpool for FourFourTwo he also contributes to other titles including Yahoo and Bleacher Report. He is a lifelong fan of the Reds. articles.body: McCarthy says men's U21s will have learned a lot from Arsenal draw CLUB TICKETS SHOP Main Club Sponsor TICKETS SHOP McCarthy says men's U21s will have learned a lot from Arsenal draw The Gunners scored a late equaliser in Monday's Premier League 2 game. 2026-09-01T09:30+01:00 Jason McCarthy believes his players will have learned a lot after letting a slip lead against Arsenal. ð·Simon Roe. Albion menâs U21s coach Jason McCarthy was disappointed that his side could not hold out for a first victory of the season in Premier League 2 after Arsenal scored a late goal to secure a 2-2 at the American Express Elite Performance Centre on Monday. But he believes that the match will provide a good learning experience for his young players. Albion came from 1-0 down to lead 2-1 after 62 minutes thanks to goals from Younes Ibrahim and half-time substitute Bailey Palmer. But Arsenalâs own sub, Evan Mooney, tied the scores in the 88th minute. âI thought we played really well,â McCarthy said. âThe data tells me, and my eye tells me, that we were the better team against a very strong Arsenal side. So I think we can be really pleased about that. âWe probably allowed one too many transitions in the game, and that's a strength of theirs. That meant that after 75 minutes we started to fatigue, and they came into the game. Bailey Palmer came off the bench to equalise against Arsenal. ð·Paul Hazlewood âWe ended up with a very young back five, but that was a really good experience for them, and a great test and a good marker for us to see where we're at. Arsenal will be up there at the end of the season, but hopefully we will too.â The team reacted well to going behind and kept the momentum going after half time. âI thought we had really good solutions for their press in the game,â he added. âWe were very good at finding the spare man, and then changing the tempo.â A feature of Albionâs best spell was how regularly they were able to release left-back Sean Keogh down the wing in the same way that the first team have deployed Maxim De Cuyper in recent weeks. âIt's the wonderful thing about our club,â Jason said. âThere's alignment running from the first team right the way through to the younger age groups in the academy. Vivianne Miedema of Manchester City (Image credit: Kate Green - WSL/WSL Football via Getty Images) Facebook Pinterest Email Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Vivianne Miedema helped Manchester City break Chelsea’s six-year Women’s Super League winning streak last season as they claimed victory under new manager Andree Jeglertz. Manchester City claimed their first WSL title since 2016 last term, before going on to complete a domestic double by beating Brighton to lift the FA Cup. Miedema, who joined from Arsenal in 2024, says the achievement represented the culmination of a period of change at the club and something she wanted to help the City achieve when she moved from WSL rivals Arsenal. Latest Videos From FourFourTwo Watch full video here: 'People didn't expect City to do as well as we did' Miedema joined Man City two years ago after seven years with Arsenal (Image credit: Getty Images) Miedema claimed her second WSL title, having previously won with Arenal in 2019. She joined City in summer 2024 and after an injury-affected first season, last season scored 10 goals and made five assists to help City win their first league title in a decade. “Every single league title is special for different reasons,” Miedema said. Vivianne Miedema goes through on goal (Image credit: Getty Images) “For me, after having left Arsenal after seven years and moving to City, I wanted to come here and help the club win things because they hadn't done that in a while. “And my first year was tough personally with injuries, but also as a team with all the injuries we had and we didn’t get the result that we wanted to get. The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week. “So coming back last season and doing what we did definitely felt like a full circle moment. It was really special to be part of it and to be able to celebrate the league and FA Cup win as well.” After six years of dominance, it was going to take a lot to knock Chelsea off their pedestal. But new manager Jeglertz, aided by a lack of Champions League football due to a fourth-placed finish in the 2024/25 season, helped City do just that. “Coming in last summer, there were a lot of changes, new people coming in and a new coach coming in. But I think we showed so much progress over the year. Miedema in her Arsenal days (Image credit: Getty Images) “We always believed that we could do really well, but a lot of people didn't expect us to do as well as we did. Throughout the season, we adjusted and grew and that led us to win the league and the FA Cup too. “For this year, regardless of if we are the champions or if we were chasing it, it doesn’t change our goals. Some of the girls haven’t been in this position before and it will be different. “And looking at all the signings that other clubs are making, I think the league is going to be extremely exciting to see how it's going to pan out.” Miedema (R) swaps shirts with Bournemouth's Kenni (L) (Image credit: Charlie Crowhurst - The FA/The FA via Getty Images) 'Isn't that why we love football?' This year, the league has expanded by two teams to a field of 14 teams. A number of high profile players have also joined the WSL this season, something Miedema says speaks volumes of where the league is at. “It’s amazing to see that so many big players want to come play in England and that the league has increased by two teams as well,” she added. “It’s only going to get more exciting and more difficult to actually win it. To be in the league now and try to be successful again is going to be extremely difficult. But isnt’t that why we love football? “That’s the reason every good player wants to come to England, because you want to measure yourself against the best.” After a season away from Champions League football, City will be back competing against Europe’s best. “I’m really excited to be back but it's going to be tough because you're going to be travelling a lot, you're going to be playing a lot of games. “I think some of the girls will have to get used to it. But it's a competition you want to be playing and you want to measure yourself with the best in Europe. “I can't wait to see how we do in the Champions League because it’s a completely different challenge to playing in the WSL.” TOPICS Ayisha Gulati Women's Football Writer Ayisha Gulati is the women's football writer at FourFourTwo . Fresh from a summer covering the Lionesses’ triumphant Euro 2025 campaign in Switzerland, she brings a passion for all things WSL, UWCL, and international women’s football. She has interviewed names including Alessia Russo and Aitana Bonmati and enjoys telling stories that capture the excitement on and off the pitch. articles.title: Ndiaye: I want to get fans off their seat and help City win games
articles.source_type: Club-published FPL Scout Report each gameweek, team news, kick-off info
articles.body: Ndiaye: I want to get fans off their seat and help City win games Manchester City Official App Manchester City FC Ltd New signing Iliman Ndiaye says he’s keen to entertain City fans while winning games of football. The 26-year-old has put pen to paper on a five-year deal at the Etihad Stadium and follows the likes of Elliot Anderson, Gerónimo Rulli, Ayyoub Bouaddi and Allan in bolstering Enzo Maresca’s young, hungry squad. A prodigiously talented attacking midfielder who can play on either wing, Ndiaye has garnered a reputation as one of the most enjoyable players to watch in the Premier League over the last two terms at Everton. Asked in his first City Studios interview to describe the way he plays, Ndiaye lit up. “A really skilful player who likes to dribble,” he began. “I like to get fans off their seat but most importantly, to help the team win. And by using my best attributes, I feel like I can do that here.” Our new man took an unusual route to the top of the game. Growing up in northern France, he initially moved to Marseille in the south of the country before heading on to Dakar in Senegal. He then came to the UK, where he started playing for Boreham Wood and with the Rising Ballers before starting his path in the professional game at 19. With all that in mind, Ndiaye credits his dad – a dancer and choreographer - with building a lot of the foundations for the way he dribbles and moves on the pitch. “With my dad, I’ve been practicing it since I was young. Obviously until now, it’s natural. Whatever I do, it comes from everything I was doing when I was younger,” he said. “I was really keen on that dribbling side, watching the best dribblers in the world on tapes and then just practicing it on the pitch with my dad. “Pele. Maradona. Zidane. Messi. All these dribbling players. Obviously Neymar, Ronaldinho, Ronaldo the Brazilian. All the best ones. “If you want to be the best you have to look at what the best people do and that’s where my dribbling is coming from. “My dad has been really important. From my first training. From my first team in France. “He’s always been by my side, with my mum, with my sisters, they’ve always been there and had that belief in me that one day I could make it. “Obviously they believed what I believed too in me wanting to be one of the best players in the world, reaching the top level, so they’ve been really important for me and they’ve helped me get to where I am today.” Ndiaye enjoyed a strong relationship with Everton fans and believes it’s vital that the players and fans work together if a side is to be successful. “It’s really important,” he stated. “They help you on the pitch, you help each other, they give you a boost and fire. “As much as you already have that fire to win for the team, you want to win for the fans. You want to see them happy and be able to connect with them.” Share More like this Topics News Men's Team Iliman Ndiaye New signing Further reading Most read Update: Vivianne Miedema City seal signing of winger Allan Elias Manchester City and PUMA unveil the 2026/27 Third Kit Pre-Match Collection Etihad Player of the Month: August nominees revealed! articles.title: Ndiaye: My heart was set on joining City
articles.source_type: Club-published FPL Scout Report each gameweek, team news, kick-off info
articles.body: Ndiaye: My heart was set on joining City Manchester City Official App Manchester City FC Ltd New signing Iliman Ndiaye has expressed his joy at sealing a summer transfer deadline day move to the Etihad, declaring: ‘There was nothing else I wanted other than to join Manchester City.’ The Senegalese international has become City’s latest 2026 summer recruit, further bolstering Enzo Maresca’s exciting new-look squad after sealing a move from Everton where he has shone bright for the past few seasons. The 26-year-old attacking midfielder/winger has signed a five-year contract, one that will keep him at City through to the summer of 2031. After putting pen to paper on the deal, Ndiaye revealed how immensely proud he was to have joined City. And he revealed that after speaking with both manager Enzo Maresca and Director of Football Hugo Viana, his heart had been set on coming to the Etihad and how he was convinced he and City made for the perfect fit. “It’s easy to make the decision about whether you want to be at Manchester City or not,” Ndiaye said. “You can see the recent history; you want to be part of that project. “They talked to me about where we could go, what we could achieve with me in the team, and I was interested from the beginning. “There was nothing else that I wanted other than joining Manchester City. “Obviously, you want to be part of this new project. I’ve seen recently what they’ve been doing, and I feel like I will fit right in it. “I’m super excited to start. “It’s an unbelievable moment. I’ve worked so hard to get to this point and I’m super excited and really grateful for this opportunity.” Now that he has clinched the move up the M62, Ndiaye said his hopes and ambitions were simple and clearcut. Namely to play his part in helping the Club go on to achieve even more silverware looking both to this season and beyond. “Wherever you are, you want to win games and trophies,” Ndiaye pointed out. “You have your solo targets as well but most importantly; it’s the team target. “When you think about the team, if you work hard, it will come naturally. “If you have the mindset to do it for the team and the fans, then the targets will come by itself.” Share More like this Topics News Men's Team Iliman Ndiaye Manchester City New signing Further reading Most read Update: Vivianne Miedema City seal signing of winger Allan Elias Manchester City and PUMA unveil the 2026/27 Third Kit Pre-Match Collection Etihad Player of the Month: August nominees revealed! articles.title: 10 things you might not know about Iliman Ndiaye
articles.source_type: Club-published FPL Scout Report each gameweek, team news, kick-off info
articles.body: 10 things you might not know about Iliman Ndiaye Manchester City Official App Manchester City FC Ltd Iliman Ndiaye is a City player! The versatile forward has joined City after two years at Everton. Here’s a few things to help you get to know our new man a little better… Birthplace Ndiaye hails from Rouen in the north west of France. The city was one of the most powerful in Europe during medieval times and was where Joan of Arc was tried and executed. It remains an architectural hotspot for tourists, despite being damaged during World War II. Ndiaye spent the first 11 years of his life there before moving to the south of France with Marseille and then to Senegal as a teenager. Unusual route Our new man has taken the path less trodden to the very top table of European football. After returning to Europe following two years as a teenager in Dakar, he wound up in the youth side at non-league north London outfit Boreham Wood. That’s where he got his first contract before catching the eye of Sheffield United scouts and then eventually moving on to Marseille and Everton. Bouncing back Beyond that very specific path into football, Ndiaye has had to have a thick skin throughout his life. In an interview with Everton last year, he told of all the clubs who passed up the opportunity to sign him as a youngster. “I went to trial with Southampton, Reading, Tottenham, Chelsea, Crystal Palace. I used to be very small and they said they had similar players. People told my dad to his face that I will never be a football player.” Moves like Ndiaye Iliman is the son of a dancer and choreographer and, in an interview with Sky Sports, our new man put a lot of his silky skills and eccentric movements with the ball at his feet down to his dad’s influence. “He told me everything I know,” he said. “With his dancing and choreography, he added it into the way I do things like stepovers. He used to tell me when you do stepovers, your body can still go like this and that.” Big family Ndiaye is one of nine siblings. He shared a house with seven sisters and one brother growing up but he says that shaped a lot of who he has become. “Family is important to me,” he said in an interview with Everton. “They’ve always been behind me through everything. The hard times and the good times and now I’ve got my own family. I love it.” Rising Ballers Ndiaye also spent time with Rising Ballers, the famous YouTube team, during his development. During one particular video with them seven years ago, footage of his famous skills and mind-blowing control of the ball can be seen on a cage in London. In that video, he credits his time in Senegal and the uneven surfaces there with teaching him how to adapt to unfamiliar and difficult conditions. Choices Born in France to a Senegalese father and French mother, Ndiaye could have represented either nation. However, he chose Senegal and has gone on to play for them 44 times since his debut in 2022. In that time, they’ve finished third at AFCON 2024 and he’s been to both the 2022 and 2026 World Cups. Breakthrough year As City were winning an historic Treble in 2022/23, Ndiaye was enjoying a season that very much put him on the map. He was named in the Championship Team of the Year and as Sheffield United’s Player of the Year as the Blades earned promotion to the top-flight. There was plenty of excitement at Bramall Lane about how he’d fare in the Premier League but he wouldn’t get the chance to show what he could do, leaving for Marseille that summer. Record v City City fans may remember one stunning goal that Ndiaye struck at the Etihad Stadium. With City 1-0 up on Boxing Day in 2024, Ndiaye controlled a cross with his right foot, allowed it to bounce and immediately took a snapshot with the same peg. It flew into the top corner before anyone could react and was a perfect example of the unorthodox but wildly entertaining way in which he plays the game. That’s his only goal in five games against us – four coming for Everton and one for Sheffield United. Squad number history Ndiaye has worn lots of different squad numbers during his career. He’s had 10 since arriving at Everton in the summer of 2024 but before that, he wore 29 at Marseille and Sheffield United as well as 25 with Boreham Wood. For Senegal, he dons the number 13. articles.body: Events Explainer: Be part of Sunday's season opener against Birmingham! Manchester City Official App Manchester City FC Ltd The wait is over... City are back in WSL action at the Joie Stadium this Sunday! Join us from 14:30 (UK) as the WSL and WSL 2 champions lock horns on a memorable opening weekend of the campaign. City ended the 2025/26 campaign with a 100% home record and the best attacking record in the division, but Birmingham will be keen to cause an upset on their return to the top flight after a four-year hiatus. get your City v Birmingham tickets It promises to be a thrilling afternoon of action and entertainment both on and off the pitch. With limited tickets remaining, make sure you secure your seat and be part of the moment, with a rundown of how the day will look below... 13:00 – Gates open Arrive early to make the most of everything happening around the stadium before kick-off. Head under the Jumbo Screen as soon as the gates open, where our Playmakers will be looking for supporters to take part in some exciting pre-match activations on the pitch. You could even find yourself at the heart of the matchday entertainment! We have two Fan Zones this weekend, each offering something different... Behind the West Stand – Kids Fanzone Perfect for younger fans, with face painting, inflatables, Dream Team activities and plenty of football fun. Behind the South Stand – NEW - Additional Fanzone A dedicated space for those fans looking for something a little different. Enjoy our food market with plenty of snacks refreshments available, including sweet treats and coffee options. There are also activities for everyone to enjoy, including a photobooth and the chance to see both of the WSL and FA Cup trophies up close! 13:45 – Team News Revealed Be in your seat as City’s first starting XI of the season is revealed live inside the stadium, followed by a pre-match chat with Head Coach Andrée Jeglertz. You’ll also be among the first to discover our brand-new matchday look for the 2026/27 season... a fresh look to represent an exciting new chapter in our history! 13:50 – Warm-ups begin The players take to the pitch to begin their preparations, accompanied by music from our resident DJ Laura Dean. For this game, we are also giving fans the chance to help soundtrack matchdays by suggesting the songs you’d love to hear at the Joie Stadium by submitting songs here: Create your playlist for City v Birmingham 🎵 Some of our players’ favourite tracks will also be included throughout the pre-match build-up, so stay tuned to hear an exciting mix of tracks across the afternoon! 14:00 – City Quiz returns Don’t miss our pre-match quiz either, where one lucky supporter could win a signed Manchester City shirt! Each quiz focuses on one of our players... can you answer the most questions correctly and in the shortest amount of time to come out on top? 14:15 – The countdown begins As kick-off approaches, make sure you’re in your seat for an exclusive pre-match ceremony. Enjoy a reminder of the City team, our exciting new blue button and a special ceremony to welcome the reigning WSL champions, before the players take to the field. It’s a moment you’ll want to experience from the stands, so make sure you’re ready for the action in plenty of time! 14:30 – Kick-off Watch the WSL champions in action as we look to get our defence of the title off to a flying start! Half-time – Revolut Wheel of Wishes returns The popular Revolut Wheel of Wishes is back! One lucky fan will have the opportunity to spin the wheel at half-time and win some incredible prizes. To be in with a chance of taking part, make sure you have a Revolut account and submit your RevTag before Thursday. Coming with little ones? Don’t miss our Joie Buggy Park Our free Joie Buggy Park is available once again, allowing supporters to safely leave their prams during the match before collecting them after full-time. The dedicated area is available below the West Stand at the Joie Stadium. Food and drink There will be a wide range of food and drink options available throughout the Joie Stadium, with additional vendors around the concourse to help you fuel your matchday. Following the successful trial last season, supporters can once again enjoy alcohol inside the seating bowl, making it the perfect way to spend a Sunday afternoon. Please note that supporters seated in Blocks W1, W2 and W3 are located within the Alcohol-Free Zone and alcohol cannot be taken into these areas. Sun 06 Sep Barclays WSL Man City 14:30 BST Birmingham Plan your visit With strong demand expected for our opening fixture, don’t leave it too late to secure your ticket and make sure you’ve planned your trip in advance. We can’t wait to welcome you back to the Joie Stadium for what promises to be a spectacular start to the new season! get your City v Birmingham tickets Share More like this Topics News Women's Team Birmingham City Women Birmingham City Manchester City Further reading Most read Update: Vivianne Miedema City seal signing of winger Allan Elias Manchester City and PUMA unveil the 2026/27 Third Kit Pre-Match Collection Etihad Player of the Month: August nominees revealed! articles.body: Etihad Player of the Month: August nominees revealed! Manchester City Official App Manchester City FC Ltd It’s the first Etihad Player of the Month vote of the 2026/27 season! August ushered in a new era as Enzo Maresca took charge of his first matches since replacing Pep Guardiola as City boss. The Italian has overseen Premier League victories over Bournemouth and Crystal Palace since the Community Shield defeat to Arsenal. Here are our three nominees this month… Rayan Cherki With star turns in both of our league wins, Cherki has had a fine start to his second campaign in England. He came on in the second half of the opening weekend clash with Bournemouth with City behind in the game. Two assists later, including a bamboozling run and pass for Joško Gvardiol’s late winner, and the game was flipped. He started a few days later at Crystal Palace and ran the show from the off, with two stunning goals playing a big role in our 4-1 win. Marc Guéhi Guéhi’s role in the Bournemouth game was perhaps Maresca’s biggest tactical tweak so far. A centre-back by trade, he appeared in midfield alongside new man Elliot Anderson and looked at home throughout, even cropping up with the equaliser. He was back in his trusty defensive role at Selhurst Park. It might have been his former stomping ground, but Guéhi was pivotal to City’s victory over his previous employers. Joško Gvardiol Despite starting from left-back, Gvardiol remains a real headache for opposition defences. Marauding forward to provide an extra man in attack, the Croatian looks so at home in the final third. He demonstrated that with his composed finish late on to beat Bournemouth as well as picking up an assist against Crystal Palace, all while doing his due diligence out of possession. The poll is open until 17:00 (UK) on Friday, when we’ll reveal your winner. Cast your vote below! articles.body: Scottie Scheffler, Rory McIlroy or Matt Fitzpatrick? Have your say on who should win PGA Tour's Player of the Year award | Golf News | Sky Sports Skip to content Scottie Scheffler, Rory McIlroy or Matt Fitzpatrick? Have your say on who should win PGA Tour's Player of the Year award Who will be crowned the 2026 PGA Tour Player of the Year? Have your say! Scottie Scheffler, Rory McIlroy and Matt Fitzpatrick among names who could claim honour Tuesday 1 September 2026 11:32, UK Image: Who will be crowned the 2026 PGA Tour Player of the Year? Rory McIlroy insists it’s 'all to play for' in the race to be crowned PGA Tour Player of the Year, but who is still in contention for the coveted Jack Nicklaus Award? Ahead of the BMW Championship, McIlroy said there was 'no chance' he should be considered, despite defending his title at The Masters and placing tied-for-fourth at the Tour Championship. Scottie Scheffler has won the award - determined by a vote by PGA Tour members - each of the last four seasons and is in the running to win his fifth consecutive title, after the world No 1 secured a three-stroke victory at the Tour Championship on August 30 , to claim his second FedExCup title How Scheffler clinched thrilling FedExCup victory Scheffler overtakes Woods in PGA Tour career money list Latest PGA Tour news, reports and highlights Get Sky Sports stream golf with no contract Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player After defending his Masters title and finishing tied-fourth at the Tour Championship, Rory McIlroy finds himself in the mix to be crowned the Player of the Year Clark, Matt Fitzpatrick, Chris Gotterup and Cameron Young are all multiple winners on the PGA Tour in 2026 and are also in contention to win the coveted award. Who will be crowned the 2026 PGA Tour Player of the Year? Take a look at the potential contenders and have your say… Monterosa This content is provided by Monterosa , which may be using cookies and other technologies. While he may not have won as many tournaments on the PGA Tour as he did in 2025, when he dominated winning six events, it's still been an excellent campaign, with the world No 1 also winning the FedEx St. Jude Championship in August. Also See: PGA Tour 2026 - tournament schedule Stream the PGA Tour with no contract When is golf live on Sky Sports? Listen to the Sky Sports Golf Podcast The 30-year-old's triumph at the Tour Championship also saw him overtake Tiger Woods in the PGA Tour's career money list and become only the third player, alongside McIlroy and Woods, to win multiple FedExCups. Image: Scheffler overcame a three-shot deficit on the final day of the Tour Championship, before going on to win his third PGA Tour event of the season What's been most remarkable about Scheffler this season is his consistency. The world No 1 has placed as a runner-up five times on the PGA Tour in 2026, and became the first-ever PGA Tour player to secure three consecutive solo runner-up finishes at The Masters, the RBC Heritage and The Cadillac Championship. Enable Cookies Allow Cookies Once Rory McIlroy Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player McIlroy said there was 'no chance' he should be considered for the Player of the Year award, but has enjoyed a fine season McIlroy has won this award three times, and after successfully defending his Masters title in April , he once again finds himself a contender to be crowned the PGA Tour's Player of the Year. He's played some fantastic golf this season, notably dazzling fans with his incredible distance off the tee at The Open , and has enjoyed some great results too, including a tied-second finish at the Genesis Invitational top-ten finishes at the PGA Championship and Genesis Scottish Open After struggling with his game at the FedEx St. Jude Championship , McIlroy bounced back to wrap up his PGA Tour season with two brilliant finishes, securing third place at the BMW Championship and ended his week at the Tour Championship tied for fourth at 11 under par. Matt Fitzpatrick Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Matt Fitzpatrick (left) won three events on the PGA Tour this season, his most successful year on the US circuit It's been Fitzpatrick's most successful PGA Tour season to date, with the 2022 US Open Champion clinching three PGA Tour victories, while placing as a runner-up twice, notably just missing out on winning The Players After being denied by Young at TPC Sawgrass, Fitzpatrick went on to win in his next PGA Tour start at The Valspar Championship , before later claiming back-to-back titles at the RBC Heritage and the Zurich Classic of New Orleans alongside his brother Alex At the Tour Championship, Fitzpatrick performed well over the first three rounds, going eight under par through 54 holes, before he came unstuck in his final round, posting a three-over 73 to finish five under par and tied for 21st. Wyndham Clark Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Wyndham Clark triumphed at Shinnecock Hills to win his second US Open title Clark joined Fitzpatrick at tied for 21st at the Tour Championship, but despite slipping down the leaderboard in the PGA Tour's end-of-season event, it's been a brilliant year for the American. Like the Englishman, has also enjoyed his most fruitful PGA Tour season, winning three events in 2026, including a two-stroke victory at the BMW Championship The American's first victory of the year came at the CJ Cup in May , before he won his second US Open title at Shinnecock Hills , with Clark showcasing his incredible putting skills to beat Sam Burns by one shot. Cameron Young Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Cameron Young outlasted Fitzpatrick by a shot to win The Players Young picked up the second and third victories of his PGA Tour career in 2026, winning The Players in March and outscoring Scheffler to win The Cadillac Championship in May. He came close to winning his first major championship at The Open in July, where he finished one shot back from winner Ryan Fox , in second place. After placing Tied-61st at the Wyndham Championship and finishing outside the top 30 at both the FedEx St. Jude Championship and the BMW Championship, Young rose up the leaderboard to finish tied for 11th at the Tour Championship, six shots back from Scheffler. Chris Gotterup Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Chris Gotterup has three victories on the PGA Tour so far this season Gotterup got his 2026 campaign off to a fast start, winning the season-opening Sony Open in Hawaii in January, before he beat Hideki Matsuyama in a play-off to win the WM Phoenix Open the following month. The 27-year-old's third win came later in the season at the John Deere Classic , making this his most successful season on the PGA Tour yet. Gotterup would miss the cut at the Rocket Classic, and finish tied-30th at the FedEx St. Jude Championship, before he wrapped up what's been a stellar season with back-to-back tied-fourth finishes at the BMW Championship and the Tour Championship. What's coming up in September? After the PGA Tour season came to a climax at the Tour Championship, attention now turns to the DP World Tour, the Solheim Cup and the Presidents Cup. Here's what's coming up on Sky Sports in September: Omega European Masters , September 3-6, all four rounds live on Sky Sports, with day one live on Sky Sports Golf from 12.30pm Walker Cup, September 5-6, both tournament days live on Sky Sports, with day one live on Sky Sports Golf from 8.30am Amgen Irish Open , September 10-13, all four tournament days live on Sky Sports, with day one live on Sky Sports Golf from 1.30pm Solheim Cup , September 11-13, all three tournament days live on Sky Sports , with day one live on Sky Sports Golf and Sky Sports Main Event from 6.30am BMW PGA Championship , September 17-20, all four tournament days live on Sky Sports, with day one live on Sky Sports Golf and Sky Sports Main Event from 12pm FedEx Open de France , September 24-27, all four tournament days live on Sky Sports , with day one live on Sky Sports Golf from 12.30pm Presidents Cup , September 24-27, days one, three and four live on Sky Sports, with day one live on Sky Sports Golf from 5.30pm Don't miss out on any of the action! articles.body: Gabriel Jesus: Arsenal forward completes Barcelona transfer in £8.6m deal on Deadline Day | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to content Transfer Gabriel Jesus: Arsenal forward completes Barcelona transfer in £8.6m deal on Deadline Day Gabriel Jesus leaves Arsenal having scored 32 goals in 123 appearances for Arsenal since his £45m move from Manchester City in 2022; Jesus' move is not expected to impact Barcelona's desire to sign Julian Alvarez Tuesday 1 September 2026 20:02, UK Image: Gabriel Jesus has signed a deal at Barcelona until 2029 Gabriel Jesus said he has fulfilled a "dream" after completing his move to Barcelona from Arsenal. The Brazilian moves to the Spotify Camp Nou in a deal worth £8.6m (€10m), where he has penned a deal until June 2029. The Jesus deal may not end Barcelona's pursuit of Julian Alvarez. Sky Sports News has been told they are completely separate. Jesus, who joined Arsenal from Manchester City in a £45m deal four years ago, had also been subject of interest from Napoli. Transfer Centre LIVE! Latest on YOUR PL club! Premier League fixtures & scores FREE PL highlights Got Sky? Watch Premier League games LIVE on your phone Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals stream PL games with no contract Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Barcelona boss Hansi Flick gives his verdict on the imminent arrival of Gabriel Jesus from Arsenal. He scored 32 goals in 123 appearances for Arsenal, but managed just three Premier League starts last season. The 29-year-old missed most of last year after picking up a knee injury in a January 2025 FA Cup tie against Manchester United. Jesus has made 64 international appearances for Brazil but has not featured for the Selecao since November 2023. Also See: Transfer Centre LIVE on your phone! Papers - latest headlines Premier League ins and outs Download the Sky Sports App Jesus delights at 'dream' move Speaking at his Barcelona unveiling, Jesus expressed his delight at the move having been training separately from his team-mates at Arsenal due to the uncertainty surrounding his future. "I have strong faith in God and I knew that if I did things well, anything could happen," he said. "I have always been a guy who respects everyone so I thought things would turn out well. I was working very hard at Arsenal, separately from the other players of course. "I kept giving my best because I knew a good thing would happen, and now it's happened. A week ago, I received the message that it could happen. When I started to think it was a real possibility, it made me very excited and made me want to be here a lot." Jesus confirmed he spoke to countryman Raphinha and former Manchester City team-mates Joao Cancelo, Rodri and Eric Garcia when finalising the move. "They only had good things to say about Barcelona, the dressing room, the players, the staff, the coaching," he added. "I have the opportunity now to be here at Barca now. I had the opportunity 10 years ago, but life took me in a different direction. But now, I can be here. It's a dream for me." Arsenal confirm Vieira sale Arsenal also confirmed the sale of Fabio Vieira Hamburg on Deadline Day. The deal for the midfielder is worth £7.7m. The Gunners signed Vieira from Porto for up to £34m in June 2022. articles.body: Iliman Ndiaye transfer news: Man City sign £65m winger from Everton as Jack Grealish joins Toffees on loan | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to content Transfer Iliman Ndiaye transfer news: Man City sign £65m winger from Everton as Jack Grealish joins Toffees on loan Manchester City have completed the £65m signing of winger Iliman Ndiaye; City had an £80m bid for Liverpool's Cody Gakpo rejected on Monday and moved for Ndiaye as an alternative; Jack Grealish joins Everton on season-long loan which will take him to the end of his Man City deal Wednesday 2 September 2026 01:36, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Iliman Ndiaye speaks for the first time after signing for Man City for £65m from Everton. Credit: Man City TV. Manchester City have confirmed the £65m signing of winger Iliman Ndiaye. The deal comprises a £60m guaranteed payment plus £5m in bonuses. Ndiaye, who had also been wanted by Tottenham, has signed a five-year contract at Manchester City. Transfer Centre LIVE! Latest on YOUR PL club! Premier League fixtures & scores FREE PL highlights Got Sky? Watch Premier League games LIVE on your phone Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals stream PL games with no contract Jack Grealish has gone the other way in a separate deal, returning to Everton on a season-long loan that covers the final year of his Man City contract. Image: Iliman Ndiaye (left) has joined Man City from Everton with Jack Grealish going the other way in a separate deal But Manchester United have rejected Everton's offer to take Joshua Zirkzee on loan. Sky Sports News understands Everton offered to pay a total fee of around £10m for Zirkzee, which included his wages for the season and a loan fee. Ndiaye's City arrival comes after Liverpool rejected Manchester City's £80m bid for Cody Gakpo. Also See: Man City news and transfer latest Man City fixtures Transfer Centre LIVE on your phone! Download the Sky Sports App Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Re-live all the thrills and spills from Transfer Deadline Day on Sky Sports News. Sky Sports News understands Liverpool were concerned about their chances of bringing in a replacement for the Dutchman. Manchester City wanted to sign a wide forward and a central midfielder before the window closes, with the club agreeing a joint-British record deal for Chelsea's Enzo Fernandez on Deadline Day. City allowed Savio and Omar Marmoush to join Tottenham earlier this month, reducing Enzo Maresca's options on the wing. City did not name a winger on their bench in Friday's win over Crystal Palace and started with Phil Foden - who Enzo Maresca admitted is not a winger - out wide at Selhurst Park. Ndiaye: Man City perfect fit for me Ndiaye, who becomes Manchester City's seventh summer signing, said: "I've worked my whole life for an opportunity like this. "City are one of the best clubs in the world and I've seen them win everything as I've grown up. "To be able to write my own chapter in a story that special is the chance of a lifetime and I'm determined to grab it with both hands. "It's not always been easy in my career, but I always had the belief that I could play for a team challenging for the biggest prizes, and now I'm here. It feels so good. "I love to play with the ball on the floor in an attacking team that wants to score as many goals as possible. That's why I know this is the perfect fit." Manchester City director of football Hugo Viana added: "Iliman is a very talented footballer. He's had to work incredibly hard to reach this level and in my first conversation with him it was immediately obvious how grounded he is and the determination he has to be the best player he can be. "I've no doubt City fans will get a thrill seeing him in action for us." Play Super 6 to win £1m! Play Super 6 for a chance to win £1m! Enter for free. articles.title: Matias Fernandez-Pardo to Newcastle: Signing from Lille is 'very fast' with 'unbelievable power' like Jeremy Doku
articles.source_type: Team news, season previews, transfer and injury reporting
articles.body: Matias Fernandez-Pardo to Newcastle: Signing from Lille is 'very fast' with 'unbelievable power' like Jeremy Doku | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to content Analysis Matias Fernandez-Pardo to Newcastle: Signing from Lille is 'very fast' with 'unbelievable power' like Jeremy Doku As Newcastle United complete the £51m signing of Matias Fernandez-Pardo from Lille, Adam Bate speaks to the player's former coach to find out what makes the Belgian forward so good: "You could compare him a little bit to Jeremy Doku. He is very explosive, very fast" Adam Bate Football Features Writer @ghostgoal Tuesday 1 September 2026 23:05, UK Image: Belgium international Matias Fernandez-Pardo is making the move to the Premier League with Newcastle United There is one special quality that will have convinced Newcastle United that Matias Fernandez-Pardo can thrive in the Premier League. "He is very explosive, very fast," his former coach Arnar Vidarsson tells Sky Sports . "He has this unbelievable power." Indeed, Vidarsson, who worked with Fernandez-Pardo at Gent prior to his move to Lille, sees similarities with another Belgian winger who has become a Premier League star. "You could compare him a little bit to Jeremy Doku. They have a similar profile," he says. "It is that power, that speed, that ability to go past people without needing space." That Doku trademark of slowing the defender down and then suddenly speeding up? He has it too. "Matias can go past people in one or two metres because of this explosiveness." Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports analyses Newcastle's new signing Matias Fernandez-Pardo Got Sky? Watch Premier League LIVE on your phone No Sky? Get Sky Sports stream with no contract on NOW The reason why Newcastle have been persuaded to pay £51m to bring the 21-year-old Belgium international to the Premier League is that Fernandez-Pardo has shown that he can bring goals too. He has evolved into more of a forward than a winger. Image: Matias Fernandez-Pardo's heat map and shot map for Lille in European competition "In my opinion, his best position is central," says Vidarsson. "That is how he scored most of his goals and how Lille scouted him in his last season with Gent." It happened fast. He made his full league debut in March 2024 and played his last game for the club that August. A run of eight goals in 11 games did that. "The coach started to use him as a striker. Before that, he had always been on the wing. He made a good decision because Matias started to score a lot. After that spell playing centrally, there was big interest in him." Vidarsson's relationship with Fernandez-Pardo pre-dates that first-team breakthrough. The Icelandic coach, now working in coach development for FIFA, was responsible for talent management at Gent as well as working with the development squad there. Also See: Download the Sky Sports app Transfer Centre LIVE! Get Sky Sports Stream Sky Sports with NOW He remembers a quiet boy, one well supported by his family. "His relationship with his father was strong. His father was all in, basically his assistant, driving him everywhere and taking good care of him. Matias did not talk too much." He came alive on the pitch. The young Fernandez-Pardo was a wide player for Gent's second team. It was a learning process. "His decision-making on the wing was not always the best," Vidarsson recalls. "That is something that Doku, for example, also had when he was at Anderlecht." Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Matias Fernandez-Pardo arrives in Newcastle ahead of his move from Lille He caveats it by saying this was a few years ago. "Players develop. But he was going past people and not knowing when to cross, when to cut inside, when to go outside, when to find space in behind. And sometimes he did not have the mentality to run for the team." Vidarsson puts that down to the fact that he had probably outgrown the level and was itching for the first-team opportunity that he soon seized. "That is typical of a young player who was being asked to go from the first team to play for the second team." The breakthrough came in early 2024 when Gent sold three attacking players for significant sums of money. Malick Fofana and Gift Orban both moved to Lyon. Hugo Cuypers was sold to Chicago Fire. "That freed up the space for Matias to play," he explains. The rest is history and Fernandez-Pardo earned his own switch that summer. "I think it was a great move for him to go to Lille," says Vidarsson. After a promising first season adjusting to the level, he played a key role in qualifying Lille for the Champions League. Given that achievement, there is some surprise within football that Fernandez-Pardo has been so keen to leave. Certainly, there is a feeling that playing a season of Champions League football with the French club would have aided his development. Vidarsson himself preaches caution in expecting too much on Tyneside, at least in the short term. "I would say they are taking, not a risk, but let's say giving him an opportunity," he says, rather diplomatically. This is another step up for him, after all. "He has the potential but I really do believe that he will need one season to adapt before he can shine and become a top player in the Premier League. Because everything in the Premier League is faster, more intense. Everything there happens at a faster tempo." There is a belief that Matthias Jaissle's vertical style of play could suit Fernandez-Pardo - if he is used in the channel rather than just stuck out on the wing. "It will probably always be better for Matias to play in a system as one of two strikers," argues Vidarsson. "Because of his speed, he needs space. On the wing, you can direct him in one direction and then he becomes a little easier to mark." That might change, of course. In part, because he can "grow into a bigger club, into a bigger environment" at Newcastle. Transfer Centre LIVE! Choose the Sky Sports push notifications you want! The World Cup felt like a missed opportunity as Fernandez-Pardo was restricted to just three appearances off the bench for Belgium. Tired of waiting, he has pushed for the club move that he craved and the chance now to play in the Premier League. There is much to learn and much to prove. But Newcastle supporters have reason to be excited. Not because Fernandez-Pardo is the finished article, but because he isn't. And because he possesses that one quality that means he always has the capacity to excite. "What he has, of course, is that special thing that a lot of clubs are looking for in modern football, that speed, that ability to go past people and do something in small spaces. He has those attributes and they are really difficult to create. You are just born with it." Play Super 6 to win £1m! Play Super 6 for a chance to win £1m! Enter for free. articles.title: SEMEDO JOINS CLERMONT ON PERMANENT TRANSFER
articles.excerpt: Luis Semedo has joined French Ligue 2 side Clermont on a permanent transfer. The 23-year-old forward moves to Les Lanciers after three years on Wearside. Semedo arrived at Sunderland in the summer of 2023 from Benfica and made 23 appearances for the Black Cats, including four starts. He also spent time on loan during his spell in the North East, making 21 appearances for Moreirense in Portugal last season. Everyone at Sunderland AFC wishes Luis well for the next chapter of his career.

articles.title: Emery: We must keep going forward
articles.excerpt: Fixtures Aston Villa Vs. Arsenal - Mon, Aug 31 2026, 20:00 Unai Emery felt there were positives to take from Monday night’s clash against Arsenal at Villa Park. There was little to choose between Aston Villa and the reigning champions in a Premier League game decided by Bukayo Saka just before the hour mark. Emery walked away disappointed with the outcome but heartened by what he saw from his team. “There were very positive things – not the result. Of course, it’s painful when we are losing and we’re not happy,” he said. “We must keep going forward and move on with the very good news we can have. Today I think we competed fantastically collectively, tactically as well the team responded fantastically. This is the way. “Individually, we added some players for their debuts, really playing fantastic and feeling comfortable, like Suzuki and Jackson. As well, the players who were here last year showed their capacity to take more responsibility playing, for example Ross Barkley. “John McGinn, like always, was being the leader we need. Adingra SUN 4.9m 28/08 Chadi Riad CRY 4.4m 28/08 Cherki MCI 7.6m Scout Picks - Bus Team FPL Gameweek 3 early Scout Picks: Piling up on Man City August 31 421 comments 31 August 2026 421 comments We’ve put together our Scout Picks ‘bus team’ for Gameweek 3 of Fantasy Premier League (FPL). The upcoming Scout Squad nominations , as well as the pre-match press conferences, will help shape our finalised picks. However, this early draft, at the very least, offers an insight into the players and teams who will be under consideration. There are, as ever, certain restrictions for our squad: An £83.0m overall budget for our starting XI An overall squad limit of £100.0m No more than three players per team A reminder, too, that the Scout Picks are for the upcoming Gameweek in isolation. GAMEWEEK 3 FIXTURES Using our free-to-all ticker, here is the Gameweek 3 difficulty ranking – although unbeaten Hull City may have something to say about this… THE LIKELY LADS Although he has a trickier fixture away at Everton, Bruno Fernandes (£12.0m) has to be here after Sunday’s epic haul . It sent a reminder to FPL managers about why he should never be easily overlooked, nor confidently sold. The fact that Everton have conceded a league-second-worst 10 big chances in the first two Gameweeks is also in Bruno’s favour. Not that there’ll be any captaincy debate this week, as Erling Haaland (£15.5m) surely dominates the armband discussion, at home to Coventry City. In fact, the main questions are whether it’s time to activate Triple Captain, and which Manchester City colleagues should complete a triple-up. Antoine Semenyo (£8.5m) very likely starts, as he always does, but Phil Foden (£7.0m) and Rayan Cherki (£7.6m) are cheaper – and the latter is setting FPL pulses racing. As this is a one-week lineup, we’ll go with Cherki – but be careful about permanently buying the Frenchman. He didn’t start in Gameweek 1, and spoke on Friday night about nearly being substituted at half-time . It’s a sign of Cherki’s quality that he’s already on two goals and two assists, but the possible purchase of Cody Gakpo (£7.0m) could ultimately mean he and Foden will be fighting for the same ‘number 10’ role. Sticking with Enzo Maresca’s lot, there’ll be some defensive coverage too. Ideally, an ‘out of position’ Nico O’Reilly (£6.5m), but Josko Gvardiol (£5.6m) saves a bit of money and, in fairness, has delivered an attacking return in both outings. IN CONTENTION Gameweek 1’s top scorer, Maxim De Cuyper (£4.6m), remained on the wing against Chelsea. Not that he was involved in Brighton and Hove Albion’s three goals, but next up is Leeds United and Coventry. On these days, it’ll be hard to resist such out-of-position appeal. Sticking with the Seagulls, Pascal Gross (£5.5m) helped them scrape a respectable result, having found themselves 3-0 down after 32 minutes . He assisted an own goal before heading in a stoppage-time consolation to reach 13 points. But it’s his only shot so far, and Leeds are tough to break down. The Whites have allowed only two big chances. Meanwhile, Dominik Szoboszlai (£7.0m) is ticking along nicely for owners. Scoring from the spot and securing a defensive contribution (DefCon) reward nicely showcases his ‘all-roundedness’. Liverpool attackers need considering, as Ipswich Town have just conceded five at Old Trafford. Could the as-yet-unpriced Bradley Barcola tempt anyone on his debut? We like several Brentford assets for their hosting of Sunderland. Kristoffer Ajer (£4.5m) is one of four defenders to have achieved DefCon success in both Gameweeks, while Mamadou Sangare (£5.6m) has done the same in midfield Kevin Schade (£6.0m) already boasts eight shots inside the box, and Igor Thiago (£8.0m) is the biggest expected goals (xG, -1.81) underachiever. But perhaps picking more than two of these is excessive. In 2025/26, Thiago replaced Yoane Wissa (£6.1m) as the Bees’ main striker. The latter had an awful debut campaign at Newcastle United, but seems reinvigorated under Matthias Jaissle . He already has a goal, an assist and a price rise to his name. Just be aware that the Magpies haven’t won any of their last eight league meetings with Bournemouth. Above: Recent matches between Newcastle and Bournemouth, from FotMob On Saturday, penalty-taking Morgan Gibbs-White (£7.9m) hauled at Anfield , continuing the late-season form that brought seven goals in his final seven starts. The opportunity to go against an under-construction Tottenham Hotspur is tempting. After three successive clean sheets, it’s probably still worth contemplating one Arsenal representative at the back – David Raya (£6.0m), Riccardo Calafiori (£5.6m) or the cheap-as-chips Ezri Konsa (£4.4m) – even though Chelsea have netted seven times. The Gunners still ride high in the clean sheet odds, too… With the Blues conceding five goals in two Gameweeks, might Bukayo Saka (£9.5m) make a late charge for the Picks, as well? THE LONGER SHOTS Chelsea’s goalscoring form is why it’s hard to truly say no to Joao Pedro (£7.6m), despite meeting a defensive wall. He’s bagged a goal and an assist in both matches, and the Brazilian is hard to bench with such a high ownership. Other interesting strikers include departing Blues man Nicolas Jackson (£6.5m), away to Hull City, and Gonzalo Garcia (£6.0m) at home to an increasingly poor Crystal Palace. With Fernandes and intense Man City representation, Liverpool duo Alexander Isak (£9.0m) and Virgil van Dijk (£6.5m) might be too costly. Not that the Reds are defending well anyway… they conceded twice in both outings. Finally, the alternative goalkeeper picks to Raya are Caoimhin Kelleher (£5.0m) and Zion Suzuki (£5.0m). articles.title: Aznou Seals Malaga Loan Switch
articles.excerpt: Adam Aznou has joined Malaga on loan for the 2026/27 season. The temporary switch for the 20-year-old – who signed for Everton in July 2025 – represents a return to La Liga for the full-back. A senior international with Morocco, Aznou is a youth product of Barcelona’s famed La Masia academy, spending three years as a teenager with the Spanish giants, before heading to Bayern Munich in the summer of 2023. While in Germany, the young left-back earned appearances in the Bundesliga, Champions League and the Club World Cup. After signing for Everton, he made his Toffees debut in January 2026, coming off the bench in an eye-catching cameo against Sunderland in the FA Cup third round. Aznou now heads to Andalusia, Spain to continue his development, linking up with newly-promoted La Liga side Malaga for the remainder of their season.
