articles.title: Catesby Joins Accrington Stanley On Loan
articles.excerpt: Everton Under-21s winger Joel Catesby has signed for League Two club Accrington Stanley on loan. In August 2024, Catesby penned a first professional contract, signing with the Toffees until the end of June 2027. A part of the side’s training camp in Scotland in July, Catesby was on the bench for the Blues’ 4-0 victory over Dundee. He now links up with John Doolan’s Stanley for the maiden loan move of his career.

articles.title: Boro beaten as Cherries make it two from two in Premier League 2
articles.excerpt: Goals from Harold William, Jonny Day and Dane Ndimukum meant AFC Bournemouth made it two wins out of two to start life in Premier League Two, with a 3-1 success against Middlesbrough. William’s header and Day’s neat finish put the Cherries in the box seat after just 13 minutes at Wyatt Homes Stadium, despite the latter being forced off through injury shortly after. Middlesbrough pulled a goal back through Cruz Ibeh after 52 minutes, with the Cherries left with 10 players after Eugene Nyarko was sent off just before the hour mark. But some resolute defending and two top-drawer saves from goalkeeper Mack Allan kept Alan Connell’s side in front before a slick move made it 3-1 in the 90th minute. Substitute Ndimukum applied an assured finish after meeting Remy Rees-Dottin’s neat flick on the edge of the box. Victory meant the Cherries have taken a maximum six points from their two Premier League 2 fixtures, after stepping up to Category One level this summer. They beat Chelsea in their league curtain-raiser earlier this month. AFC Bournemouth make the trip to Leicester City in the Premier League Cup on Friday (7pm kick-off). Carvalho doubled Brentford’s advantage nine minutes into the second half, calmly slotting home after Furo won possession and picked out the midfielder inside the box. Sunderland responded three minutes later through Charlie Dinsdale, who squeezed a fierce effort past the goalkeeper from an acute angle. However, Furo restored Brentford’s two-goal lead in the 67th minute, meeting Gustavo Nunes’ corner near the edge of the six-yard box and heading home. articles.body: Skip navigation Five reasons to watch Palace U21s v PSG on Wednesday (19:00 BST) Academy 31 Aug 2026 Crystal Palace Under-21s begin their Premier League International Cup campaign against none other than Paris Saint-Germain on Wednesday, 2nd September (19:00 BST) – and there are plenty of reasons to be at Sutton United’s Borough Sports Ground or watching live on Palace TV+! Here are five of them… Buy PSG tickets here! 1. PSG are coming to Sutton Come on, it’s PSG! The French giants are the reigning European and French champions, having won the UEFA Champions League for a second successive season and secured a fifth consecutive Ligue 1 title. Their academy was also named France’s best for 2025/26 by the French Football Federation, showcasing the remarkable talent coming through their ranks. So, while you might not get to see the likes of Ousmane Dembélé or Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, there is every chance you’ll be watching some of the next generation of Parisian stars. And you can do it all for just £1 - 2. It’s £1 to watch future stars It’s not every day you get the chance to watch a European heavyweight in South London, but you can do exactly that on Wednesday – and it’ll cost as little as £1. Season Ticket+, Gold and Junior Gold Members can also enjoy free entry to selected Academy home games, including the International Cup. So whether you’re a regular Academy supporter or have never been to a U21s game before, there’s never been a better time to give it a go. Buy PSG tickets here! Can’t make it to Sutton? You can watch the game LIVE on Palace TV+. 3. A squad full of history-makers The Young Eagles’ squad is packed with players who have enjoyed a memorable 12 months – and plenty more who are ready to make their mark. Last season’s U18 Player of the Season Chuks Okoli could feature alongside Jasper Judd, Charlie Walker-Smith, Euan Danaher and Makai Bernard-Ferguson, who were all part of the side that lifted the club’s first-ever U18 Premier League Cup. There could also be a chance to see Joel Drakes-Thomas, who became Palace’s youngest-ever Premier League player when he featured against Leeds United last season. He was one of four Young Eagles – alongside captain George King, Dean Benamar and Benji Casey – to make their senior debuts in the UEFA Conference League against KuPS. King enjoyed an especially memorable campaign, being named U21 Player of the Season, while Casey was crowned Scholar of the Year after scoring 19 goals in 18 appearances. New signing Amaari Sealey could also make his International Cup debut. The attacking midfielder joined Palace from AFC Wimbledon this summer after registering 47 goal contributions during an extraordinary 25/26 campaign in which the Dons’ U18s completed an unprecedented national quadruple. And that’s before you even consider the talent PSG will bring to Sutton. 4. Palace have history in this competition The Premier League International Cup has already produced some memorable nights for the Young Eagles – and Palace will be hoping there are more to come. The first taste of a final came in 22/23, when Palace reached the showpiece at Selhurst Park, only to suffer a 3-1 defeat to Jong PSV. A year later, they had their chance for revenge. Franco Umeh’s deflected second-half strike secured a 1-0 victory over the Dutch side, sending Palace to the trophy for the first time. After an early group-stage exit in 24/25, the Young Eagles bounced back last season, topping their group with wins over Juventus, FC Nordsjælland and Borussia Mönchengladbach. Their run eventually came to an end in the quarter-finals, where they narrowly lost to Real Sociedad. Now, PSG, PSV Eindhoven, RSC Anderlecht and FC Porto await in Group C – and another European adventure is ready to begin. 5. You’ve got to be there There’s something different about watching Academy football live – and Wednesday’s clash with PSG is your first chance to watch the Young Eagles on Palace TV+ or at Sutton this season. Palace’s first two Premier League 2 fixtures have both been away from home, with the trip to Arsenal unavailable to watch live due to the Premier League broadcast blackout and the Aston Villa clash taking place on the same night as the first team’s opener against Manchester City. Now, the Young Eagles are finally coming home. It’s a chance to see Palace’s next generation up close, experience the atmosphere around the Young Eagles and watch players at the beginning of their journey towards senior football – with one of Europe’s biggest clubs providing the opposition. With four European opponents heading to Sutton this season, the Premier League International Cup offers a unique chance to see some of the continent’s biggest clubs without leaving South London. Tickets are available for as little as £1 , while you can enjoy all the action live on Palace TV+! articles.title: FOREST COMPLETE SIGNING OF DANIEL MUÑOZ
articles.excerpt: Nottingham Forest is delighted to announce the signing of Colombia international Daniel Muñoz on a three-year deal with the club holding an option for a further year. The 30-year-old right-back becomes the latest addition to Oliver Glasner's squad, bringing extensive Premier League, European and international experience to the City Ground. Muñoz began his professional career in his native Colombia with Águilas Doradas, making his senior debut in 2017, before joining Atlético Nacional in 2019. A move to Europe followed in 2020 when he joined Belgian side Genk. During his time at the club, Muñoz established himself as one of the division's most effective attacking full-backs, making 122 appearances and scoring 16 goals. He also helped Genk lift the Belgian Cup in 2021. After almost four years in Belgium, Muñoz joined Crystal Palace in January 2024 and quickly became a pivotal member of the first team. He played a key role in their FA Cup success in 2024/25, providing the decisive assist in the 1-0 victory over Manchester City in the final, where he was named Player of the Match. articles.body: Daniel Muñoz leaves Crystal Palace Skip navigation Daniel Muñoz leaves Crystal Palace Announcement 31 Aug 2026 Crystal Palace F.C. can confirm that Daniel Muñoz has completed a permanent transfer to Nottingham Forest. The Colombia international joined Palace in January 2024 and won a firm place in the hearts of supporters with 11 goals and 16 assists in 109 matches, winning the FA Cup, Community Shield and UEFA Conference League with the club. Muñoz’s impact during his time with us will go down in history, having provided the assist for Ebere Eze’s FA Cup-winning goal against Manchester City and won the Man of the Match award on that historic day. He also went on to win both the fans’ Player, and Players’ Player, of the Season awards in the 2024/25 campaign. During that season, he netted vital goals against Millwall and Brighton & Hove Albion – the latter completing Palace’s first-ever top-flight league double over our rivals. Muñoz impact continued last season as he scored the club’s first-ever goal in major continental competition against Dynamo Kyiv and went on to feature 12 times in our trophy-winning debut European campaign. Chairman Steve Parish said: “Danny has given us many magical moments down the years and rightly earned his place in the club’s history books. “Everybody at Selhurst Park thanks him for his service and wishes him well.” Related News Announcement Club First-team Related News More News

articles.title: HENRY WINTER: Everton is a footballing institution and community asset... the fact the owners nearly sold Harrison Armstrong shows a lack of understanding and arrogance
articles.excerpt: Rule one for owners: never kill hope, never ruin fans’ chance to dream. That’s what Harrison Armstrong represents to Everton fans: hope, a chance to dream. The 19-year-old midfielder is a local lad, hailing from West Derby, one of their own and fulfilling their own dreams by pulling on the famous royal blue shirt of the club they love. Rule two for owners: don’t sell cherished home-grown talent. Evertonians gathered at the Vitality on Saturday made their anger about the proposed sale of Armstrong to Nottingham Forest for £35m very clear to their unthinking owners, The Friedkin Group (TFG). “Don’t sell Armstrong, Harrison Armstrong, I just don’t think you understand,” they sang. “If you sell Armstrong, Harrison Armstrong, you’re going to have a riot on your hands”. Everton’s manager, David Moyes , was clearly against the sale. TFG saw and heard the backlash, woke up to the folly of the plan, and called off the sale of a player widely considered Everton’s best home-grown talent since Wayne Rooney . Everton looked set to sell 19-year-old Harrison Armstrong to Nottingham Forest for £35m - before pulling out of the deal (Image credit: Getty Images) Facebook Pinterest Email Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Rule one for owners: never kill hope, never ruin fans’ chance to dream. That’s what Harrison Armstrong represents to Everton fans: hope, a chance to dream. The 19-year-old midfielder is a local lad, hailing from West Derby, one of their own and fulfilling their own dreams by pulling on the famous royal blue shirt of the club they love. Rule two for owners: don’t sell cherished home-grown talent. Evertonians gathered at the Vitality on Saturday made their anger about the proposed sale of Armstrong to Nottingham Forest for £35m very clear to their unthinking owners, The Friedkin Group (TFG). “Don’t sell Armstrong, Harrison Armstrong, I just don’t think you understand,” they sang. “If you sell Armstrong, Harrison Armstrong, you’re going to have a riot on your hands”. Everton’s manager, David Moyes , was clearly against the sale. TFG saw and heard the backlash, woke up to the folly of the plan, and called off the sale of a player widely considered Everton’s best home-grown talent since Wayne Rooney . Armstrong’s definitely worth keeping and fighting for. Everton fans made their feelings about the proposed sale of Harrison Armstrong to Nottingham Forest clear (Image credit: Getty Images) “The potential sale of Harrison Armstrong goes against everything our fanbase stands for, a young talented Scouser who is the future of our club,” the Everton fans’ group The 1878s, said in a statement. It threatened to stop organising the flags and tifo displays that contribute so much to match-day atmosphere. TFG was toying with the very fabric of Everton life. Also: what’s best for the player’s own development? Moyes looks after young players well, handling the precocious Rooney as best as possible when the bullish teenager launched himself so memorably on the scene in 2002. Moyes tries to shield such prospects in almost a paternal, certainly a pastoral, way. Moyes knows they will leave the footballing family home at some point so tries to prepare them while getting the best out of them. David Moyes was against the proposed sale of Harrison Armstrong (Image credit: Getty Images) Moyes showed vital support for a teenaged Ross Barkley when the teenager suffered a double break of his leg in 2010, even ensuring a new contract for a kid in a hospital bed worried about his future. Moyes will feed Armstrong in and out of the team, not putting too much physical or mental strain on the 19-year-old. Armstrong looks like he can handle the pressure. That is partly down to the learning acquired when sent by Moyes on loan to Preston North End last season. The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week. A broader dynamic is at work here, one that affects all supporters. Financial sustainability regulations are not fit for purpose when it comes to the development of young talent. From FFP to PSR to SCR, a rethink is required on content as well as lettering. The “pure profit” element to sales of academy starlets is so tempting to the more short-sighted owners. It was one of the reasons why a frustrated Eddie Howe was forced to sacrifice Elliot Anderson in a hurried sale to Forest. It’s why TFG considered offloading Armstrong. The player becomes an accounting item not a sporting asset. Everton needed a late James Tarkowski goal to rescue a point against Bournemouth (Image credit: Getty Images) TFG needs to balance the books at a club which has recorded alarming figures in some recent years, and been punished for it, but there are other more acceptable ways, others who could be sold. From a Premier League perspective, it would make sense if clubs were more incentivised to retain “one of our own”. One way would be to allow the first few years – perhaps 50 first-team games - of an academy graduate’s salary to be offset against SCR calculations. There would then be a financial incentive to keep home-grown talents. Evertonians rightly take great pride that a local player has featured in every league campaign since the Football League commenced in 1888. It actually predates that. The likes of Liverpool-born goalkeeper, Charles Joliffe, played for Everton from 1885 until he was eventually replaced by Robert Smalley, a recruit from Preston. Moyes handled Wayne Rooney well when he broke through as a teenager (Image credit: Getty Images) Armstrong is more than a player to Evertonians. He’s a symbol of the area, almost an antidote to the big-monied modern game. Connection with the community matters hugely, especially in an era where the Premier League is so heavily populated by overseas players. Everton’s owners must have known there would be outrage. If TFG wasn’t aware, then it needs better advisors – or better channels of communication with fans. This is one of the most concerning elements of the whole story: TFG’s lack of understanding in the first place. It’s almost arrogance. Everton Football Club are more than a business; they are a footballing institution, a community asset, a developer of local talent and a beacon of hope. The Armstrong story highlighted that. Owners take note. TOPICS Henry Winter Writer Henry Winter is one of football's most popular and respected writers. Previously the Chief Football Writer for The Times and a Football Correspondent for The Daily Telegraph, his work now primarily features on his Substack. August 31 88 comments 31 August 2026 88 comments Two days after Savio (£6.5m) did the same, forward Omar Marmoush (£7.0m) joined Tottenham Hotspur from Manchester City. The 27-year-old Egyptian’s initial loan has an obligation to become permanent for up to £60 million next summer. Can Savinho be a good FPL buy at Spurs? So, have big-spending Spurs invested wisely, or overspent again? We’ll attempt to help out Fantasy Premier League (FPL) managers below. Score More Points. Win More Mini Leagues. Join FFScout. CAREER SO FAR Marmoush started his career at Cairo-based Wadi Degla and soon moved to the Bundesliga with Wolfsburg, stepping up to their first team in 2020. However, having been loaned out to St Pauli and Stuttgart, his only notable campaign for Die Wölfe came in 2022/23. Even that season was more about cameos than starts. So he decided to join Frankfurt on a free transfer. They gave him the platform to shine against the likes of Bayern Munich, Borussia Dortmund + RB Leipzig, as well as in continental competitions. STARTS (SUB) GOALS ASSISTS FPL POINTS 2025/26 Manchester City Premier League 8 (13) 2024/25 Manchester City Premier League 14 (2) 2024/25 Eintracht Frankfurt Bundesliga 17 (0) 2023/24 Eintracht Frankfurt Bundesliga 27 (2) 2022/23 Wolfsburg Bundesliga 15 (18) A particularly electric start to 2024/25 caught the attention of several clubs and, in January, he chose Man City, who hadn’t yet replaced Julián Álvarez. The £59 million man scored an early hat-trick versus Newcastle United and, soon after, brought in 12 FPL points against Brighton and Hove Albion. Yet there was a mixed end to the season. Missing a penalty in their FA Cup final defeat, followed three days later by a stunning 30-yard ‘Goal of the Season’ strike at home to Bournemouth. A lot of those early months had Marmoush based on the left-hand side, but a quiet 2025/26 saw him basically be Erling Haaland ‘s (£15.5m) backup. WHERE MARMOUSH FITS IN AT SPURS Showcasing his versatility, FPL keeps switching Marmoush between being a midfielder and a forward. This time, he’s the latter, and that could be how Roberto De Zerbi classifies him. “I think he can play as a central striker. Number 10… different number 10 than Gallagher or Maddison, more of an attacker, but he is a player of big qualities.” Roberto De Zerbi when asked if he sees Omar Marmoush as more of a striker or ’10’ Indeed, in his Gameweek 2 debut against Newcastle United, the Egyptian was stationed up top. Above: Omar Marmoush led the line for Spurs in Gameweek 2, although there was plenty of him drifting deep and left Marmoush’s hot streak at Frankfurt was mostly up front, albeit in a partnership with Hugo Ekitike (£7.5m). Good at receiving passes over the top of opposing defenders, both he and De Zerbi mention his pace in interviews with the club website “Omar is exactly the kind of player we want at this club – ambitious, hungry and determined to make a difference. He brings pace, intelligence and a real threat in front of goal, and I believe he can take our attacking play to another level.” – Roberto De Zerbi Dominic Solanke (£6.0m) presents his only real competition up top, and it feels likelier that Marmoush will be battling for the striker’s role as Richarlison (£6.0m) is on his way out. Compare that to the attacking midfield trident behind the striker, with Savio, Mohammed Kudus (£6.5m), James Maddison (£6.4m), Dejan Kulusevski (£6.5m), Mathys Tel (£5.9m), Xavi Simons (£6.0m) and the potentially incoming Iliman Ndiaye (£6.0m) all options when fit, and Marmoush surely doesn’t add to that melange. LOTS OF SHOTS AT CITY – BUT NOT MANY GILT-EDGED CHANCES Marmoush was a Fantasy midfielder last season and, among his positional peers, he had the best rate of shots per 90 minutes (3.49). Of course, he spent much of his time up front, but even compared to the forwards, Erling Haaland (£15.5m) was the only meaningful name who could better that figure. Above: FPL midfielders sorted by shots per 90 minutes in 2025/26 (min. 500 minutes) It was more volume than quality of chances, though. His average xG per shot was 0.09. For context, Yoane Wissa ‘s (£6.1m) figure was up at 0.27. Above: Omar Marmoush’s xG shotmap in 2025/26, with the bigger circles representing better chances. Green = goal. Blue = blocked/on target. Red = off target. He is, at least, capable of scoring from distance/low-percentage efforts. There were three direct free-kicks in 10 days for Frankfurt. He scored three goals from outside the box in his first half-season at City in 2024/25. And, crucially, he’s overachieved on the xG front in each of the last three seasons. The pinnacle of that came in his final half-campaign at Frankfurt : Above image from Fotmob ANY CHANCE OF PENALTIES OR SET PIECES? Spurs didn’t benefit from a single Premier League penalty last season. They did, however, get four of them in the Champions League: Date Competition Player Outcome On pitch 18/03/2026 Champions League Xavi Simons Scored 09/12/2025 Champions League Xavi Simons Scored 09/12/2025 Champions League Mohamed Kudus Scored Richarlison, Simons 04/11/2025 Champions League Richarlison Missed Simons, of course, is currently injured, while Richarlison is on his way out. Solanke, meanwhile, was off the field when all four of the above spot-kicks were awarded. He’d taken and scored three in April/May of 2024/25, so on paper he should be first in line – but will the striker even start in this new-look Spurs side? Spot-kick duties could be up for grabs, then. Marmoush has a decent record from 12 yards (nine scored, two missed), although his last attempt was a miss in the 2025 FA Cup final. Ndiaye, with his unblemished record of five penalties scored, could also be in the mix if he joins, along with Kudus. As for direct free-kicks, Marmoush is a fan of those. He took three for City in his limited pitch-time in 2025/26. Pedro Porro (£5.5m), Kudus, Maddison and, when fit, Simons provide the competition. Tel might be off them now Corners seem much less likely. He was only a sporadic taker of those at City, and on Saturday, he didn’t deliver any of Spurs’ nine corners. ANY FPL POTENTIAL? The FPL community is just waiting for Spurs’ attack – still goalless after two Gameweeks – to become convincing again. Adding Marmoush and Savio to the mix certainly helps, as will the returns to fitness of Maddison and Kudus, and the potential arrival of Ndiaye. It might just need a little patience! We should have more of a clue by Gameweek 7, when Spurs handily embark on a promising fixture run. Four home matches in seven versus Coventry City, Crystal Palace, Ipswich Town and Fulham, for a player whose 10 Premier League goals have all come at home. The problem with Marmoush is his price. The likes of Ndiaye and Savio could quite easily match or better Marmoush for FPL points, and at a cheaper price, too. Then there are the other FPL forwards. Wissa is £0.9m cheaper and has an excellent fixture run now. Joao Pedro (£7.6m) is only £0.6m more expensive and his own great stretch of matches from Gameweek 4. Marmoush has much to do to wriggle his way into the FPL conversation, then, even if his xMins have been given a serious shot in the arm by this move. 88 Comments Login to Post a Comment Saka Potatoes 01 1 day, 15 hours ago What do you think about this FH squad? articles.title: Tarkowski Reveals Message To Everton Squad Before Late Equaliser
articles.excerpt: James Tarkowski has reflected on the “incredible” moment of striking his 91 st -minute stoppage time leveller against Bournemouth on Saturday – and says he always felt Everton were “going to get a chance”. His late goal at the Vitality Stadium sealed a 1-1 draw for the Toffees, cancelling out Alex Scott’s first-half strike. “It’s always nice not to lose a game when you’ve been 1-0 down for quite a while,” he told evertontv . “We stuck at it. “I thought we defended brilliantly in the second half. We stayed strong, put bodies on the line. Jordan made a few big saves in big moments. “I always felt we were going to get a chance. I was trying to get that message to the lads on a lot of corners they were having, just to say: ‘We’ll punish them. Stick at it, keep defending and we’ll punish them.’ “Thankfully, we did.” Thanking the travelling Toffees for their superb support, he added: “It’s incredible. To score a goal like that in front of those fans is an amazing feeling. “I’d like to watch that footage back now and see those celebrations!”

articles.body: Okoli, Sealey and Somade ready for PSG test Skip navigation Okoli, Sealey and Somade ready for PSG test Match previews 31 Aug 2026 Crystal Palace Under-21s are set for a taste of European football on Wednesday night (KO: 19:00 BST) when Paris Saint-Germain visit Sutton United’s Borough Sports Ground in the Premier League International Cup. Ahead of the Young Eagles’ Group C opener, Chuks Okoli, Amaari Sealey and Sean Somade looked ahead to the challenge – from facing one of Europe’s biggest clubs to the different demands of taking on overseas opposition. With Season Ticket+, Gold and Junior Gold Memberships, you’ll be able to enjoy free entry to selected Under-18 and U21 home games! Buy PSG tickets here It is a particularly exciting occasion for Okoli, who has been with Palace since the age of seven and was named the club’s 2025/26 Under-18 Player of the Season. For the versatile midfielder, the pedigree of the visitors is clear. “Obviously a big European team, a lot of pedigree,” he said. “Quite a lot of talent as well, and I know that obviously they've won quite a lot of things, Champions League, a lot of Ligue 1 titles, so I'm expecting a lot of quality from them.” PSG arrive in South London as the reigning European champions and French champions, having won the UEFA Champions League for a second successive season and secured a fifth consecutive Ligue 1 title. Their academy was also named France’s best for 25/26 by the French Football Federation. Sealey, meanwhile, knows the size of the challenge awaiting him on what could be his competitive debut for Palace. The attacking midfielder joined the Young Eagles from AFC Wimbledon over the summer after an outstanding 25/26 campaign, registering 47 goal contributions as the Dons’ U18s completed an unprecedented national quadruple. “Yeah, I'm sure everyone knows that, you know, they're French giants, they're huge in their country and worldwide,” he said. “Obviously their success in European competitions, so obviously it's the perfect test for us.” Somade, a powerful centre-back capable of also playing at right-back, has been at Palace since joining at Under-14 level and is relishing the opportunity to face unfamiliar opposition. “Obviously they have a lot of background, a famous team, known for being good,” he said. “It's going to be a good game.” Quote Icons I'm extremely excited Chuks Okoli The International Cup provides something different from the U21s’ usual domestic schedule. Palace primarily compete in Premier League 2, which features the development sides of all 31 Category One academies, while they will also compete in the EFL Trophy this season The International Cup, meanwhile, brings together 16 Premier League 2 sides and 16 invited European clubs. The teams are split into four groups of eight, with each English side facing their four overseas opponents once. Palace are in Group C alongside PSG, PSV Eindhoven, RSC Anderlecht and FC Porto, with all four fixtures taking place at Sutton. For Okoli, that change of scenery also brings different tactical and physical demands. “I think obviously playing against international foreign teams, they come up with different tactics, different play styles, different type of quality,” he said. “So I'm expecting it to probably be faster, more technical, probably even a bit stronger, more physical, so yeah, extremely excited.” Sealey expects the quality across the competition to make for a stern test, but believes Palace can thrive. “Yeah, I feel like there'll be higher quality because I feel like all the teams will try and play good football, including us,” he said. “I feel like most teams will be of such a good nature that it's going to be a hard competition to be in, but I feel like we can do well.” For Somade, simply facing a team from outside England will provide a new experience. “Obviously them being a foreign team, we're not used to playing teams outside of the country,” he said. “I feel like it'll be a different type of challenge and it'll be good.” Quote Icons It's everyone's dream to play in front of fans Amaari Sealey With the first European challenge of the season almost here, all three players were keen to stress the importance of having Palace supporters behind them. Okoli believes that backing could be particularly valuable for a group containing several players experiencing the competition for the first time. “I think it'll be very important for us, especially for us first years of going into a new competition,” he said. “Some of us haven't played yet, so having those people behind us, those people to support us and cheer us on should be good.” Sealey echoed that call, describing playing in front of supporters in a competition such as this as a dream for young players. “Yeah, hugely important for us because, you know, it's everyone's dream to play in front of fans in such big competitions,” he said. “I feel like it's the next step for us, so yeah, come and watch.” And Somade has a simple message for anyone considering making the trip to Sutton or even tuning in on Palace TV+. “I think it'll be good for them to come watch. We'll give our all and as long as they're there, I think we'll try our hardest.” Tickets for the game are available from just £1 - If you can’t make it to the game against PSG on Wednesday, you can watch all the action LIVE on Palace TV+ - Match ticket prices: Adults (21-64): £5 Young Adults (17-21): £1 Seniors (65+): £1 Juniors (2-16): £1 Academy Founder Members: Free Adult Gold, Junior Gold & Season Ticket+ Holders: Free Tickets are available here and will be issued as PDF print-at-home tickets at the point of sale. Please note: One free ticket per Membership/Season Ticket+ Holder. Adingra SUN 4.9m 28/08 Chadi Riad CRY 4.4m 28/08 Cherki MCI 7.6m Scout Reports Bouaddi to Man City – could it affect O’Reilly? August 31 0 comments 31 August 2026 0 comments Manchester City last week continued their midfield rebuild by signing highly rated teenager Ayyoub Bouaddi (£5.5m) from Lille. The 18-year-old Morocco international drew plenty of global interest after a promising display at the World Cup, and it was Enzo Maresca’s side who won the race for his signature on a deal reportedly worth up to £86m. It’s all change in the City midfield, then. Fellow big-money signing Elliot Anderson (£6.4m) has arrived but long-serving stars Rodri and Bernardo Silva are gone, as are Nico Gonzalez (£5.5m) and Tijjani Reijnders. So, what are Bouaddi’s prospects from a Fantasy Premier League (FPL) perspective? BRIEF HISTORY Bouaddi joined Lille’s Academy in 2021, signing his first senior contract with the club two years later and earning a first-team debut just days after his 16th birthday. Bouaddi then became one of Ligue 1’s youngest debutants in history during the 2023/24 campaign, going on to make 96 total senior appearances for Lille across all competitions. That included nine appearances in the 2024/25 Champions League, seven of them as a starter, including a home win over Real Madrid on his 17th birthday. BOUADDI’S LEAGUE APPEARANCES FOR LILLE Season Team Starts (sub apps) Mins Goals Assists 2025/2026 Lille 28 (2) 2331 2024/2025 Lille 11 (13) 1149 2023/2024 Lille 1 (8) 128 After representing France at youth level, Bouaddi elected to play for Morocco’s senior international team and subsequently started five of the country’s six World Cup matches this summer. WHERE DOES BOUADDI FIT IN – AND WILL HE START? Above: City’s starting line-ups in the first two Gameweeks, via BBC Sport As a deep-lying midfielder – one who has already drawn comparisons to the great and often unheralded Sergio Busquets – that appears remarkably comfortable in possession despite his young age, Bouaddi’s likeliest route to the first team is to slot into the base of City’s midfield alongside Anderson. We’ve seen defenders Marc Guehi (£6.0m) and Neco O’Reilly (£6.5m) in those roles in Gameweeks 1 and 2. Either way, the transfer fee suggests this is a player that City and Maresca intend on rebuilding their midfield around in partnership with Anderson, so we would expect him to become a regular starter at some point in the future, especially given the loss of Rodri, Reijnders, Bernardo and Gonzalez. Still, the continued presence of an experienced figure like Mateo Kovacic (£5.5m) – as well as a few versatile defenders – does give Maresca options if he elects to ease Bouaddi into Premier League action. The teenage Moroccan was on the bench in Gameweek 2, replacing Anderson late on. O’REILLY CONCERN? One thing to watch out for is the impact on O’Reilly. If Bouaddi eventually comes in alongside Anderson, where does that leave the £6.5m FPL defender? His two starts in 2026/27 have both come in midfield, the first as a ’10’, the second slightly further back. The form of Rayan Cherki (£7.6m) makes the first unlikely to happen much again. O’Reilly back to left-back, then? Possibly, but Josko Gvardiol (£5.6m) has started there in Gameweeks 1 and 2. The Croatian is reportedly viewed as a ‘pillar’ by Maresca. O’Reilly does offer something that Bouaddi and Anderson don’t, in a box-crashing attacking sense. A pairing of the latter two does seem somewhat conservative, and may only be preserved for the ‘bigger’ games. Only ‘mild peril’ for O’Reilly for now, then – but a move for Enzo Fernandez (£6.9m) would really upset the applecart! NOT MUCH GOAL THREAT – BUT WHAT ABOUT DEFCON POTENTIAL? Whenever he does make a starting XI spot his own, Bouaddi’s career to date suggests his main appeal from an FPL perspective comes from his potential for defensive contribution (DefCon) points. The teenage prospect’s total expected goal involvement (xGI) was a miserable 3.33 in 2025/26, so we’ll move swiftly on from attacking threat. Here are his ‘DefCon per 90’ figures from his last two full seasons: Season DefCons per 90 2025/2026 10.55 2024/2025 10.66 Pretty consistent, then, but still some way short of the leading FPL midfielders in 2025/26: Above: FPL midfielders sorted by DefCons per 90 minutes in 2025/26 OVERALL FPL POTENTIAL – AND ANDERSON IMPACT? Bouaddi is an FPL no-go at present. Not only are there game-time concerns, but a repeat of his so-so DefCon rate at Lille wouldn’t compensate for the lack of attacking threat. Mamadou Sangare (£5.6m), for instance, is streets above Bouaddi in those respects right now. So, the Moroccan’s arrival is more about the impact on O’Reilly – who we’ve already discussed above – and Anderson. Anderson is a known and valued commodity when it comes to DefCon points, so it will be interesting to see the effect Bouaddi’s integration may have on the former Nottingham Forest star. Could the newcomer take on the brunt of the defensive work, freeing up Anderson to offer more from an attacking standpoint? That certainly seems more likely than the vice versa option, given Bouaddi is yet to score a senior international goal and also registered just a single assist for Lille last term. Granted, leaving the teenager to fend for himself as a sole No 6 – at least early doors – may be considered too much of a baptism of fire in the Premier League. Bouaddi was in a two-man pairing for Lille, regularly in a 4-2-3-1, so it is maybe likelier that we see him continue in a similar set-up alongside Anderson, with the defensive workload shared between the two. It’s worth monitoring the midfield DefCon numbers – in addition to Bouaddi’s minutes, of course – over the coming weeks’ promising fixtures , then, to assess the impact of City’s possession-based style on the DefCon potential of both Anderson and Bouaddi. 0 Comments Login to Post a Comment No comments have been submitted for this post yet. David Luiz's second Chelsea spell ended in 2019 (Image credit: Alamy) Facebook Pinterest Email Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google During two trophy-laden spells at Chelsea, David Luiz turned out for the club almost 250 times, helping the Blues win the Champions League, Premier League, FA Cup and Europa League. But shortly after signing a new contract in 2019 and just weeks after he started in Chelsea’s 4-1 Europa League final win over Arsenal , the Brazilian defender signed for the Gunners in an £8million deal. The reason for making this bold move across the capital with the ink on his new deal still wet was a simple one - the hiring of his former teammate Frank Lampard as Chelsea boss. Pick the ultimate 4-4-2 line-up from players in FourFourTwo's definitive Top 100 List Luiz on why Lampard’s Chelsea wasn’t for him Luiz has recently turned 30 when Lampard, fresh from a stint on charge of Derby County, was handed the Stamford Bridge top job, but age was not a factor for Luiz, who is still playing as a 39-year-old for Cypriot side Pafos. “I was already over 30 and had renewed my contract with Chelsea,” Luiz tells FourFourTwo . “No-one had ever broken the club policy of renewing for two years after the age of 30, and I renewed for two years. Luiz swapped Chelsea for Arsenal after Frank Lampard's arrival (Image credit: PA) “Then after two months, I went to Arsenal. It was down to the decision to bring Frank Lampard in as manager. In pre-season, I already could see the way he was going to play wasn’t going to leave me happy. “At that age, I thought “I want to enjoy the game in the way I play it”, so it was better to leave.” The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week. For Luiz, this was a decision made as a matter of principle. “There are two kinds of workers in life,” he continues. “Those who work to protect themselves and the job, and those who want to do something different. In any company, 90 per cent protect the job, but I want to be part of the 10 per cent. “It would have been easy to have stayed quietly at Chelsea, but I’m not like that. So I sat down with Frank Lampard and said ‘I want to leave – the way you’re going to play won’t be good for me, and the way I’d play in your system won’t be good for you either’.” Luiz did not see himself fitting into Lampard's system A year after playing his final match for Chelsea against Arsenal in the Europa League final, there was another twist of fate for Luiz. “Life is so funny – later that season, the FA Cup final was between Arsenal and Chelsea. I leave, telling the manager I don’t think his philosophy would suit me, that maybe it wouldn’t work to win anything, then at the end of the season the final is against him. “So if I won, in theory I was right. If I lost, I wasn’t. Thank God, we managed to win, and I was very respectful in the way I behaved, not celebrating, and respecting the history I built at Chelsea.” TOPICS Joe Mewis For more than a decade, Joe Mewis has worked in football journalism as a reporter and editor. Mewis has had stints at Mirror Football and LeedsLive among others and worked at FourFourTwo throughout Euro 2024, reporting on the tournament. In addition to his journalist work, Mewis is also the author of four football history books that include times on Leeds United and the England national team. Now working as a digital marketing coordinator at Harrogate Town, too, Mewis counts some of his best career moments as being in the iconic Spygate press conference under Marcelo Bielsa and seeing his beloved Leeds lift the Championship trophy during lockdown. articles.title: Under-18s looking to "bounce back" after defeat to Ipswich
articles.excerpt: AFC Bournemouth under-18s Lead Coach, James Lowy, says his side will "bounce back" after a 6-2 defeat away at Ipswich Town. Goals from a trialist and Harley Simpson saw the Cherries go into half-time level at 2-2, before Ipswich secured the three points in the second-half. James Lowy spoke to afcb.co.uk: "It was a game of two halves. I thought we competed really well in the first-half and put ourselves in a good position. "We created a number of opportunities through pressing and regaining the ball high, but we didn't capitalise on those opportunities. "For us to compete at this level, they are chances that we would need to take. "In the second-half, we struggled to compete in our duels. In and around the final third we lacked some quality and could have done better with some chances too. "Ipswich defended well, and the difference was in both boxes today. "It's been a really tough period for us physically, with games coming thick and fast. "We have a young squad and some injures, so it is important for us now to rest and recover and put ourselves in the best position going into West Ham on Saturday." Lowy's players are back in action this Saturday (5th September).

The former West Ham striker’s iconic hat-trick saw the Three Lions conquer the world at Wembley 60 summers ago, but just months earlier, his place at the 1966 World Cup was far from assured. It would take patience, preparation and an unfortunate injury to Jimmy Greaves for Hurst to get his opportunity under Sir Alf Ramsey. Geoff Hurst on waiting for his England chance Hurst didn't make his England debut until February 1966 (Image credit: Getty Images) As Hurst looks back on his rise into the England starting XI that summer, he admits that he was eager to keep his expectations in check in the run-up to the tournament, “Well, you don't get too far ahead of yourself,” Hurst tells FourFourTwo . “You might find it surprising but, although we were successful at West Ham, it was never really on my radar." Jimmy Greaves was England's No.9 going into the tournament (Image credit: Getty Images) Hurst’s approach of letting his club football at Upton Park do the talking would pay off, though, as the call did come just in time. “It was quite a surprise when I received a letter from the FA in December ‘65 saying I was picked for the game in February against West Germany at Wembley . You come and play and do your best, and hopefully the manager sees enough in you. The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week. “Thankfully, he did. It wasn’t just me, either. Martin Peters , my team-mate at West Ham and room-mate on England duty, played his first game in May that year. He went on to score the other goal in the final, of course. We were cutting it fine!” While Hurst was named in Ramsey’s 22-man squad for the World Cup, he didn’t actually start a game until the quarter-final win over Argentina, after first-choice striker Jimmy Greaves injured himself in the final group game. But was that a source of frustration for Hurst? “Not for one second,” he insists. “I was honestly just so ecstatic to be in the squad for a home World Cup. Alf Ramsey with the Jules Rimet trophy after England's 1966 World Cup victory (Image credit: Alamy) “I often joke that Alf Ramsay picked two average players ahead of me, in Jimmy Greaves and Roger Hunt, before finally getting it right. But, of course, those two were phenomenal strikers and I was thrilled to support the team however I could. “That was a good attitude because, when your chance comes in life, you have to be ready to take it and I did. “Saying that, I was honestly so sad for the great Jimmy Greaves, who damaged his leg against France. He deserved to play on.” TOPICS Joe Mewis For more than a decade, Joe Mewis has worked in football journalism as a reporter and editor. Mewis has had stints at Mirror Football and LeedsLive among others and worked at FourFourTwo throughout Euro 2024, reporting on the tournament. In addition to his journalist work, Mewis is also the author of four football history books that include times on Leeds United and the England national team. Now working as a digital marketing coordinator at Harrogate Town, too, Mewis counts some of his best career moments as being in the iconic Spygate press conference under Marcelo Bielsa and seeing his beloved Leeds lift the Championship trophy during lockdown. articles.title: Chelsea 4-3 Brighton Stats: Cole Palmer Decides Seven-Goal Thriller as Xabi Alonso’s Men Stay Perfect
articles.excerpt: Chelsea overcame Brighton in a seven-goal thriller at Stamford Bridge. Re-live this game with our Chelsea vs Brighton stats page. The post Chelsea 4-3 Brighton Stats: Cole Palmer Decides Seven-Goal Thriller as Xabi Alonso’s Men Stay Perfect appeared first on Opta Analyst .
articles.source_type: xG methodology, expected points tables, head-to-head records, supercomputer projections
articles.body: Chelsea 4-3 Brighton Stats: Cole Palmer Decides Seven-Goal Thriller as Xabi Alonso's Men Stay Perfect | Opta Analyst Chelsea beat Brighton in a seven-goal Premier League epic on Sunday, with Cole Palmer and João Pedro both on target again. Relive all the moments from the game with our Chelsea vs Brighton stats page. Cole Palmer scored what proved to be the winner as Chelsea remained perfect in the Premier League under Xabi Alonso, beating Brighton 4-3 in a thriller at Stamford Bridge. It looked like being a routine outing for the Blues when Romeo Lavia, Pedro Neto and João Pedro struck to put them 3-0 up inside 32 minutes. But former Brighton striker João Pedro also scored at the wrong end following a sumptuous volley from Malick Yalcouyé , as Brighton threatened a stunning comeback. Palmer gave Chelsea breathing room once more when he found the bottom-left corner in trademark fashion, though, and Pascal Gross’ header came too late for Brighton as the hosts climbed to third in the early-season table, with two wins from two matches. Chelsea had only needed 31 seconds to make the breakthrough in their season-opening win over Fulham, and though they had to wait a little longer on Sunday, another fast start left Brighton shellshocked. Lavia was on hand to tap home in the fourth minute after Mats Wieffer nodded João Pedro’s header off the line, and only 10 minutes later, Neto met Morgan Rogers’ left-sided cross with a first-time finish off the outside of his right boot. Joao Pedro – who was jeered by the away fans throughout – missed a glorious chance to make it 3-0 when he stroked wide with time and space inside the area, but he celebrated in front of his former supporters when he took in Jorrel Hato’s pass and finished soon after. Emiliano Martínez’ first test in the Chelsea net was to catch Yalcouye’s effort on the stretch, but his hopes of a clean sheet were dashed when the former Swansea City loanee hammered a volley in off the post, on the rebound from Charalampos Kostoulas’ saved lob. Huge chances came and went at both ends early in the second half. Diego Gomez headed wide after being left unmarked from Olivier Boscagli’s free-kick, while Palmer could not keep his shot down when Rogers dug out a cross to find him in front of an unguarded net. Brighton had renewed hope when Gross beat the offside trap following a recycled set-piece and crossed low, with a flick off João Pedro catching out Martinez, and the former Aston Villa goalkeeper then had to be alert to push Boscagli’s drive to safety. But Palmer eased Chelsea’s nerves with a marauding run and finish in the 74 minute, and there was barely time for the game to restart following Gross’ late header. João Pedro the Centre of Attention as Alonso’s Men Entertain Again Playing their first home Premier League game under Alonso, Chelsea could hardly have asked for a better start. Lavia’s goal made them just the second team to begin a Premier League campaign by scoring in the opening four minutes of both of their first two matches, after Bolton Wanderers in 2002-03. That strike also came four years to the day since Lavia’s only previous goal in the competition – which came against the Blues for Southampton. But Brighton refused to go away without a fight, even after going 3-0 down. João Pedro was heavily involved at both ends, registering a goal, an assist and an own goal. He is only the sixth player to do so in a single Premier League game and the first since Son Heung-min against Manchester City in December 2023, while he is the first to ever do so for Chelsea. But it was Palmer’s cultured finish that proved decisive, and he has now netted six times against Brighton in the Premier League – more than he has against any other club. And if they continue in this vein, both Chelsea and Brighton could lay claim to being the Premier League’s chief entertainers. Alonso is only the fourth manager to see his team score seven or more goals in his first two Premier League games, after Bobby Robson (eight in September 1999), Michael Laudrup (eight in August 2012), and Marcelo Bielsa (seven in September 2020). Fabian Hurzeler’s Seagulls, are only the second side since 1950 to score four goals in their first game of an English top-flight season, and then concede four in their second, after Blackpool in 2010-11 (won 4-0 versus Wigan, lost 0-6 to Arsenal). Our Opta match centre delivers you all the Chelsea vs Brighton stats from their Premier League meeting at Stamford Bridge on Sunday 30 August 2026. The match centre below includes team and player stats, expected goals data, passing networks, an Opta chalkboard and more. It gives you everything you need to do your own match analysis. Underneath the match centre you can find the official Opta stats on the game as well. Chelsea vs Brighton: Post-Match Opta Facts Chelsea have won both of their first two games of a top-flight season while scoring 3+ goals each time for the fourth time, after 1936-37, 2010-11, and 2018-19. Chelsea’s Xabi Alonso is only the fourth manager to see his side score 7+ goals in his first two Premier League games, after Bobby Robson (8 in Sep 1999), Michael Laudrup (8 in Aug 2012), and Marcelo Bielsa (7 in Sep 2020). Brighton have lost three consecutive away games in the Premier League for the first time since May 2021 under Graham Potter. Chelsea are only the second side ever to score in the opening four minutes of both of their first two Premier League games of a season, after Bolton Wanderers in 2002-03. Chelsea have gone 18 games without a clean sheet in the Premier League, their longest run without a shutout in league competition since a run of 31 matches between November 1960 and August 1961. Brighton’s possession of 74.4% was the highest on record (from 2003-04) by any side in a Premier League game against Chelsea. Indeed, Chelsea completed 146 passes in this match, their lowest home or away in a Premier League game since 2003-04. Enjoy this? articles.title: Post-Sunderland Press Conference
articles.excerpt: Álvaro Arbeloa knows improvements are needed if his Fulham side are to have a successful season in the Premier League. It was a relatively even contest on the whole in Sunderland on Sunday afternoon, but a greater cutting edge from the hosts saw them eke out a 1-0 win. “It wasn't our game, for sure,” our Head Coach admitted. “We were far from our level. We were talking during the half-time, that obviously you can have some bad days or even come here in a difficult stadium against a European team, and maybe you have a bad day with the ball, like it was in the first half, but you need to put more energy, better attitudes, better mentality. “So, we improved during the first 20-25 minutes of the second half, but then we concede a [shot off the] post, and four minutes later the goal. So yes, we need to improve in many things of our game, soon. “And the first thing is that we need to know what you have to do to win games – put more energy and, like I said, better mentality and attitude as a team. articles.title: Markham bags brace as Cherries beat Hashtag
articles.excerpt: AFC Bournemouth maintained their perfect start to their FA Women's National League campaign, with a 4-1 victory over Hashtag United. A Jenna Markham brace plus one apiece from Tamara Wilcock and Charlotte Harris secured the three points, in a game Helen Bleazard's team were on top for large periods and deserved the three points they walked away with. Wilcock was the first to test the Hashtag United goalkeeper. Cutting in from the left, her right-footed effort forced a strong save to tip it round the post. Elena Cole was close to a headline making long-range effort, but her shot was pushed over the bar. Nevertheless, it was a strong opening 15 minutes from Bleazard’s players. In the 17 th minute, Markham did what she does best and put the Cherries infront. Bella Hall broke free down the right and put a dangerous cross into the box. Former Cherry Kelci Bowers just about got her head to it, but only clearing the danger as far as Issy Bryant, the winger crossed onto the head of Markham, who beat Laura Hartley in the Hashtag goal. articles.excerpt: Fixtures Coventry City Vs. articles.title: Sunderland 1-0 Fulham
articles.excerpt: Fulham were beaten 1-0 by Sunderland at the Stadium of Light on Sunday afternoon. Chances were at a premium throughout the game, with Josh King going closest in the first half, firing over after his smart run was found by Alex Iwobi. The Black Cats offered much more after the break, and following a Wilson Isidor warning sign when he struck the post, the striker snatched the only goal of the game with quarter of an hour remaining. Álvaro Arbeloa made one change to the side that met Chelsea on opening day, with Joachim Andersen preferred to Jorge Cuenca in defence, having served his suspension. A low key beginning to the match didn’t give fans of either side too much to get excited about, with a dragged Enzo Le Fee strike and an easy save for Bernd Leno from Thomas Meunier sandwiching Iwobi’s blocked volley at the other end. The first decent chance of the game fell Fulham’s way on 26 minutes when King’s intelligent run was picked out by Iwobi. This was proved evident in the fact that City were able to see off AC Milan , one of that era’s greatest sides, to Kinkladze’s signature. Georgi Kinkladze joined Manchester City in 1995 (Image credit: Getty Images) Facebook Pinterest Email Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google When Georgi Kinkladze arrived at Manchester City in the summer of 1995, the Georgian playmaker was one of Europe’s most promising young attacking talents. It didn’t take long for the former Dinamo Tbilisi midfielder to become a cult hero at Maine Road, with the signing coming just as the still-young Premier League was beginning to establish itself as a viable destination for some of the continent’s best players. This was proved evident in the fact that City were able to see off AC Milan , one of that era’s greatest sides, to Kinkladze’s signature. Kinkladze on snubbing AC Milan for City City saw of AC Milan to land Kinkladze (Image credit: Getty Images) “There was interest from Italy, but [City chairman] Francis Lee was very determined,” Kinzladze tells FourFourTwo as he looks back at his 1995 move to England. “He flew to see me and convinced me that City was a place where I could be the main man. I didn't know much about Manchester, but I liked the idea of a challenge in England.” Kinkladze quickly became a City fans' favourite (Image credit: Getty Images) It quickly became clear to the young Kinkladze that English football was very different to anything he had previously experienced. “When I arrived, the football was very different. It was much faster and more direct. The weather and the food were hard to get used to, but the fans made it easy. From the first day at Maine Road, they treated me like one of their own. That connection was instant.” The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week. Alan Ball was the City manager at the time, having spent the previous season in charge at Southampton, famously building his team around Matt Le Tissier , instructing his side to ‘Just the ball to Le Tissier.’ So was that similar with Kinkladze at City? “Alan Ball was very important in my development as a player,” he continues. “He loved technical players and wanted the team to play with flair, even if we were struggling in the table. “The 90s were a different time and sometimes I was targeted by foul play. If you tried to dribble, someone would try to kick you. Vinnie Jones and the Wimbledon Crazy Gang were famous for it. Former England international Alan Ball was in charge of City at the time (Image credit: Alamy) “But I had played in the streets of Tbilisi so I knew how to jump over a tackle. I always thought that if they couldn't catch me, they couldn't hit me.” Those early Premier League days saw a number of big-name foreign players join the league, with Kinkaldze admitting that it was an exciting time to be involved. “It was the start of something new,” he adds. “Seeing Gianfranco Zola , Dennis Bergkamp and Juninho arrive in the Premier League was exciting and it felt like the league was opening up to creative players. “The long ball reputation of English football was changing.” TOPICS Joe Mewis For more than a decade, Joe Mewis has worked in football journalism as a reporter and editor. Mewis has had stints at Mirror Football and LeedsLive among others and worked at FourFourTwo throughout Euro 2024, reporting on the tournament. In addition to his journalist work, Mewis is also the author of four football history books that include times on Leeds United and the England national team. Now working as a digital marketing coordinator at Harrogate Town, too, Mewis counts some of his best career moments as being in the iconic Spygate press conference under Marcelo Bielsa and seeing his beloved Leeds lift the Championship trophy during lockdown. I arrived at White Hart Lane and someone stopped me in my car, opened my door and offered to park my car. I thought it was a wind up. The Premier League was changing, so things had to change and modernise. “But to move out of Wimbledon just didn't seem right. It just didn't seem right to take Wimbledon away from Wimbledon. George Graham had got us to the final but then Glenn Hoddle took over. Daniel Levy had just taken over the club, so there were a lot of changes going on at the time. “We’d go on to finish in the bottom half of the table so, while we had a talented side, it wasn’t a strong period. articles.body: Palace in Europe: Get to know our league phase opponents Skip navigation Palace in Europe: Get to know our league phase opponents First-team 30 Aug 2026 Crystal Palace's eight opponents for the league phase of the UEFA Europa League have now been confirmed – here's the first of two guides, looking at four of the teams we'll be facing. Lyon Country: France Year founded: 1950 Nickname: Les Gones Best European performance: Champions League semi-finals (2009/10 and 2019/20) Pierre Sage faces a reunion with his former team after Palace were awarded a trip to Lyon in the league phase draw. The French side have serious European pedigree from their golden spell in the 2000s, where they won seven straight top-flight titles. During the latter part of this decade, Lyon regularly survived the winter in the Champions League and reached the last 16 of the old format – only beaten by Bayern Munich in the semi-finals in 2010. Despite selling star player Rayan Cherki to Manchester City in the summer of 2025, Lyon enjoyed a decent season in Ligue Un last term, finishing in fourth place to ensure European qualification. They competed in the Europa League last season and started strongly by topping the league table in the first round. However, their journey would end in the last 16 last season where they were eliminated by Celta Vigo. Real Sociedad Country: Spain Year founded: 1909 Nickname: La Real Best European performance: Champions League**** semi-finalists 1982/83 Based in San Sebastian in the Basque region of Spain, Sociedad are UEFA Cup / Europa League regulars, although they are yet to lift a European trophy. They enjoyed a memorable Copa del Rey triumph in 2025/26 to qualify for European football, defeating Atlético Madrid on penalties after a 2-2 draw in the final. Managed by American Pellegrino Matarazzo, la Real finished in 10th place last season in La Liga. Their standout player is Mikel Oyarzabal, who scored the winning goal against England in the final of Euro 2024, who is also their captain. Current Chelsea manager and former Liverpool and Real Madrid star Xabi Alonso came through the ranks at Sociedad – arguably their most famous academy graduate. TSG Hoffenheim Country: Germany Year founded: 1899 Nickname: Die Kraichgauer Best European performance: Europa League A club that has enjoyed one of German football's most remarkable rises in the 21st century. Hoffenheim only won promotion to the Bundesliga for the first time in 2008, but have played in Europe regularly over the last decade. Their first taste of the Champions League was a play-off defeat to Jurgen Klopp's Liverpool in 2017, but they reached the group stage proper for the first time in 2018/19, facing the likes of Lyon and Manchester City. Christian Ilzer took over as manager in 2024 and led them to a fifth place finish in his first full season in charge last term. The most familiar name in their ranks is club legend and Croatia international Andrej Kramarić, who has an impressive 119 caps for his country. Kramarić was actually part of Leicester City's Premier League title winning squad in 2015/16, but left the following summer and been with the German club ever since. Beşiktaş Country: Turkey Year founded: 1903 Nickname: Kara Kartallar Best European performance: European Cup semi-finalists One of Turkey's big three, Beşiktaş may be fourth seeds for the 2026/27 Europa League, but are normally competitive in European competition regardless of their seeding. They did miss out on European football a year ago after a defeat in the Conference League play-offs to Lausanne-Sport, a defeat which saw former Manchester United head coach Ole Gunnar Solskjær leave the club. His replacement Sergen Yalçın did a good job of steadying the ship. Under his management, Beşiktaş finished 4th in the Turkish Super League, winning precisely half of their 34 league games. Yalçın was replaced in the summer by former Fiorentina coach Vincenzo Italiano. His first competitive European tie saw the Turkish side see off Midtjylland in the second qualifying round. Further wins over Hradec Králové and Kauno Žalgiris ensured they booked a place in the league phase of the Europa League. Their marquee signing this summer is a familiar name from the Premier League – Leandro Trossard arriving from Arsenal for £15m. Another familiar name is former Leicester midfielder Wilfred Ndidi. Beşiktaş have won the Turkish championship 16 times, most recently in 2020/21. Related News Club First-team Related News More News

articles.title: Coventry City sign Stephen Mfuni on loan from Manchester City
articles.excerpt: Coventry City are delighted to announce the signing of Stephen Mfuni on a season-long loan from Manchester City. The 18-year-old, who can play at left-back and centre-back, made his senior debut for the Citizens last season in the 10-1 victory over Exeter City in the Emirates FA Cup. Mfuni gained further experience on loan at Championship side Watford, where he made eight appearances during the second half of last season. He’s also featured against EFL sides in the Vertu Trophy for City’s Under 21s and has also been named as a substitute for Premier League and UEFA Champions League matches. The defender has progressed through the ranks at the Etihad Stadium and capped off his youth career by scoring in the FA Youth Cup final, which saw City lift the trophy after a 4-0 triumph over Leeds United in 2024. The talented defender has also been recognised at international level and has represented England from Under 16s through to Under 19s and started all three matches at the 2025 UEFA European Under-19 Championship. articles.body: Skip navigation All you need to know about the International Cup Academy 30 Aug 2026 Crystal Palace Under-21s face Paris Saint-Germain, PSV Eindhoven, RSC Anderlecht and FC Porto in this season’s Premier League International Cup – here’s everything you need to know about the Young Eagles’ opponents and the competition. The Premier League International Cup Fancy a taste of European football without leaving England? The Premier League International Cup is back! The competition pits the top 16 sides from last season’s Premier League 2 against 16 invited clubs from across Europe. The 32 teams are split into four groups of eight, with four English sides and four European sides in each group. Palace will play each of their four European opponents once, with all group-stage fixtures taking place in England. The Young Eagles will not face the other three English teams in their group. The top two sides from each group progress to the quarter-finals, with the knockout stages decided over one leg. Extra-time and penalties will be used if required. This is Palace’s sixth appearance in the competition, having lifted the trophy in 23/24 after finishing runners-up in their first campaign in 22/23. The Young Eagles have been drawn in Group D this season, with PSG, PSV Eindhoven, Anderlecht and Porto standing between Darren Powell’s side and another run at the trophy. PSG The French giants were named France’s best academy for 25/26 by the French Football Federation, continuing a remarkable record of developing players for the highest level. Ten PSG academy graduates have featured for the club’s first team, while 12 have played in the UEFA Champions League and more than 20 have received call-ups to France’s youth teams. The club’s academy has also produced more than 30 players aged under 23 who are now under professional contract with clubs in the top two divisions of Europe’s top 10 leagues. PSG’s Espoirs have already faced English opposition this season, beating Manchester City 1-0 in pre-season. They finished fourth in their group last season, despite making an excellent start. A 2-0 win over Newcastle United and 3-1 victory against Chelsea put PSG in a strong position, but draws against Brighton & Hove Albion and defeat to Nottingham Forest ultimately ended their hopes of progressing. They’ll be hoping to go further this time around! One to watch: Fabio Domingos. The Luxembourg-born winger joined PSG from Metz in 2025 and has represented Luxembourg at youth level and Cape Verde at senior level. Domingos featured for PSG’s U19s last season as they won the Championnat National U19 title for a third successive year, and has since continued his development with the Espoirs. Match Details Palace U21s v PSG U21s Wednesday, 2nd September KO: 19:00 BST The Borough Sports Ground Premier League International Cup Watch LIVE on Palace TV+! RSC Anderlecht RSC Anderlecht’s academy has produced a host of household names, including Jérémy Doku, Romelu Lukaku and Vincent Kompany, as well as Belgian legends Paul Van Himst and Jef Mermans. Their reserve side, RSCA Futures, compete in the Challenger Pro League – Belgium’s second tier – alongside professional and other reserve sides. Anderlecht made their Premier League International Cup debut in 24/25, becoming the first Belgian club to enter the competition in nine years. Palace came out on top when the sides met in the group stages that season, with Zach Marsh, Mofe Jemide and Jemiah Umolu all on target in a 3-1 victory for the Young Eagles. One to watch: Nunzio Engwanda. The 18-year-old centre-back has already made first-team appearances in the Belgian Pro League and has become a regular for RSCA Futures. Match Details Palace U21s v RSC Anderlecht U21s Wednesday, 14th October KO: 19:00 BST The Borough Sports Ground Premier League International Cup Stream details to be confirmed PSV Eindhoven Next up is a familiar face: PSV Eindhoven. One of Dutch football’s giants, PSV have enjoyed remarkable success in recent seasons, winning three successive Eredivisie titles. They have been crowned Dutch champions 27 times and have a long-standing reputation for producing top-level talent, making Jong PSV another intriguing test for the Young Eagles. Palace and Jong PSV have plenty of history in this competition. The Dutch side edged a dramatic 22/23 final after 120 minutes before winning on penalties, but the Young Eagles got their revenge the following season. In front of more than 2,000 supporters at Selhurst Park, Franco Umeh’s deflected second-half strike secured a 1-0 victory and handed Palace their first Premier League International Cup title Jong PSV have already begun this season’s competition too, drawing 1-1 with Sunderland at the Stadium of Light. One to watch: Keziah Ogene. The 18-year-old attacker recently joined PSV from Eintracht Frankfurt and caught the eye against Sunderland, producing an acrobatic finish in the 1-1 draw. Match Details Palace U21s v PSV Eindhoven U21s Tuesday, 19th January KO: 19:00 BST The Borough Sports Ground Premier League International Cup Stream details to be confirmed FC Porto FC Porto are one of Portugal’s biggest clubs and have won more than 30 league titles, alongside a glittering collection of domestic and European honours. Their B team - who could conclude Palace's 26/27 International Cup group-stage - compete in Liga Portugal 2 and have a unique place in Portuguese football history, having become the first reserve side to win the second tier. Porto B are also no strangers to this competition. They are the record winners of the International Cup, lifting the trophy in 16/17 and 17/18. With another European heavyweight waiting in the final group fixture, Palace will face a serious test from start to finish. One to watch: Tiago Andrade. The winger joined Porto as an Under-15 player and has progressed through the club’s academy to the B team. Andrade has already been involved around Porto’s first team and has made an impact at the start of the new campaign. The date for Palace’s meeting with Porto will be released in due course. Ticketing and broadcast details for the confirmed fixtures, meanwhile, will be announced separately.
