Easter Island (a) (Image credit: Unknown) Facebook Pinterest Email Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google In a new book, Paul Watson regales some of the planet's weirdest footballing tales, including the club with a suspected drug lord in midfield, fans who dress up as squirrels and a Benin side itching for revenge. Read on for 20 barely believable stories from all four corners of the globe... Easter Island (A) When watching the cup draw, any team is keen to avoid a potential banana skin, so Santiago Wanderers probably weren't too thrilled when they pulled out a trip to the remote Juan Fernandez Islands in the 2024 Copa Chile. The fixture meant a journey to Robinson Crusoe Island, 400 miles off the Chilean coast and named after the famed Daniel Defoe novel, which tells the story of a shipwrecked English merchant stranded on a remote island for 28 years. There weren't enough commercial routes available for Santiago Wanderers to reach the island, so they had to call upon a Chilean navy supply ship, the Aquiles, to face unknown opposition. Juan Fernandez's team had been hastily assembled from recreational teams on the island, but were hampered by players missing training for lobster harvesting. They still made their professional opponents sweat though, only narrowly losing 2-1. Easter Island's Estadio de Hanga Roa before its 2014 redevelopment (Image credit: Joe Mewis) It was the second time a team from the country's remote islands had entered the Copa Chile. In 2009, a team from Rapa Nui, more commonly known as Easter Island, hosted Colo-Colo , who are widely regarded as the nation's most successful club. Colo-Colo returned home 4-0 winners, but the most memorable moment was Rapa Nui's pre-match Polynesian war dance, on a field flanked by two of the island's famous Moai statues. Too bad to take part When a club is kicked out of their league, you generally presume they've cheated to win, but for Sueca United it was the reverse – thrown out of the lower levels of Valencia's league system for being so bad they were accused of not trying. The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week. The club were the brainchild of eccentric actor Pau Codina and offered a chance to those who may not have got a game elsewhere. As admirable as that was, it left Sueca outmatched week after week. Over 11 seasons, they lost more than 300 games in a row, letting in more than 4,000 goals. The average scoreline throughout the club's history was 24-0. Come September 2023, the Valencian Football Federation had lost patience and expelled Sueca United after just two games, including a 40-0molly-whopping. Enough! A derby on a ferry?! Football players stand at a football pitch on the lower deck of a ferry on its way from Hiiumaa to mainland, Estonia, on March 30, 2013 (Image credit: AFP via Getty Images) The Estonian islands of Saaremaa and Hiiumaa have always had a fierce but good-natured rivalry. When they decided to play a football match in 2013, neither side was willing to surrender their home advantage, so they came up with a novel approach to a neutral venue – the game was played aboard the M/S Muhumaa passenger ferry connecting the islands. A grass lawn was laid down on the boat's deck, but there was only room for five-a-side, which probably reduced the risk of any challenges going, erm, overboard if things heated up. Hiiumaa won 4-1 – a surprise, as Saaremaa is home to FC Kuressaare, who play in the Estonian top flight. Unusually, they train in Tallinn but host home games on their island, meaning home matches often require longer journeys than away trips. Have boots, will travel Sudanese side Al Hilal recently achieved an unprecedented feat – winning the league in three different countries, in the space of just two seasons. Displaced from their homeland by a brutal civil war, they and Sudanese rivals Al Merrikh joined Mauritania's Super D1 League for 2024-25. The two countries aren't exactly neighbours, situated around 3,000 miles apart, but Al Hilal duly finished top of the table, albeit only recognised as “honorary champions”, with locals FC Nouadhibou technically the title winners. The two Sudanese clubs then briefly returned to their own country, with Al Hilal winning the Elite League – a short-form event to determine which clubs would represent the nation in continental competitions. Both then joined the Rwanda Premier League for 2025-26, where Al Hilal comfortably completed an unlikely treble. Pick the ultimate 4-4-2 line-up from players in FourFourTwo's definitive Top 100 List Oxygen required There was endless talk about the effects of playing at altitude before England's World Cup win in Mexico City this year, but that was trivial compared to a visit to Peruvian side Union Minas. From the 1980s to the early 2000s, the Cerro de Pasco side reached the summit of Peruvian football with their squad of jobbing veterans and nearly men, aided by substantial home advantage. The Estadio Daniel Alcides Carrion is the highest stadium in the world at around 14,000 feet above sea level – that's about 2,126 Dan Burns, and less than 4,000 feet lower than the base camps on Mount Everest. Opposition teams were so overwhelmed by the altitude that they would frequently be incapacitated, with oxygen masks a common sight in the visiting dressing room at half-time. Union briefly led the top tier standings in the 1998 season, but the decline of the mining industry hit the area hard and they slid down the leagues before halting operations in 2011, only returning last year. Six titles and a funeral Some clubs evoke strong feelings of animosity from their rivals without it being entirely obvious why. For others, it's more apparent. Take Maltese club Valletta FC, for example. The Lilywhites are one of Malta’s most successful clubs – they’ve won 25 league titles and in 2000-01, they laughed in the face of Gerard Houllier’s Liverpool cup treble by winning an almost unheard of domestic sextuple, at once securing the Premier League, Rothmans Trophy, Super Five Cup, Lowenbrau Cup, Super Cup and the Centenary Cup. But it's the way Valletta celebrate their success that antagonises opponents – whenever they win the league, fans hold a mock funeral street parade for their beaten rivals, carrying coffins with the insignia of their rivals through the streets. It was no great surprise then that when Valletta suffered the first relegation of their history in 2023-24, a healthy dose of schadenfreude was expressed by other clubs. Free trip to Tahiti Beautiful Bora Bora (Image credit: Getty Images) Since 1961, the Coupe de France has allowed entrants from French territories around the world, creating some of the most epic away days in world football. The French Football Federation covers the costs, but amateur teams still have to brave getting time off from their day jobs for what could be a lengthy jaunt. In 2024-25, fourth-tier Normandy side US Avranches landed an away match with AS Dragon from Papeete in Tahiti – flying nearly 10,000 miles from rainy northern France to a tropical paradise island in the Pacific Ocean, only to lose on penalties after a 2-2 draw. The wrong club While players will always try to pretend that a transfer is motivated by a previous love for their new club, in reality there are often unspoken reasons behind switching teams. One of the strangest was the case of Congolese winger Thievy Bifouma's move to Iranian side Esteghlal Khuzestan in 2024. The former West Bromwich Albion loanee explained he put pen to paper because he wanted to face Cristiano Ronaldo in the Asian Champions League. “I reviewed the calendar and realised they had a game against Al Nassr – I said to myself this was where I wanted to go,” he told Iranian media. The slight issue was that Al Nassr had a date with Esteghlal FC, based in Tehran, not Esteghlal Khuzestan, a completely different team situated hundreds of miles to the south. “I had no idea there were two teams named Esteghlal,” Bifouma admitted. “When I arrived, my countryman Gael Kakuta called me and asked where I was.” Kakuta played for Esteghlal FC – the pair quickly realised that they wouldn't be team-mates after all. "We got out of jail today, lads" A Young male detention centre for under-20-year-olds known as "Fundaçao Casa" or Febem, established by the Sao Paulo city government to help young offenders back to society (Image credit: Getty Images) There are a fair few prison-based football teams around the world, but Welsh side HMP Prescoed are a rarity – their players aren't made up of guards or support staff, they're inmates at the Category D, or open, prison. The team competes in the Gwent Central League, where a cursory glance at the league table suggests they appear to have an excellent home record, but abysmal away form. The reality is that HMP Prescoed aren't allowed to travel to away matches, for obvious reasons – they play them on their own field but must forfeit every game 5-0 and take a three-point deduction. As a result, the best-case scenario for the season is to finish on zero points. Last season they ended on minus five, having bagged five wins and a draw from their 14 fixtures. Amercian nightmare When the small Caribbean island of Antigua was given a chance to enter a club in the United Soccer League, the third tier of US football, it seemed like a great opportunity. By the time of their ill-fated third campaign in 2013 though, Antigua Barracuda's dream had turned into a nightmare. The league was supposed to be ‘international', but three teams from Puerto Rico were removed during the 2011 season, and by 2013 Barracuda were forced into relocation to the US mainland just to participate at all. The cash-strapped team lived in a cramped hotel in Tampa, Florida, making journeys of up to 10 hours in a tiny minibus to fulfil fixtures. At one point they even had to train in their hotel's car park, as they didn't have access to a pitch. They lost 26 games out of 26. Okinawa's number two team Third-tier Japanese side FC Ryukyu come from the island of Okinawa, famed for its beaches, coral reefs and a well-known Second World War battle. articles.body: U21s preview: Palace host PSG in International Cup opener Skip navigation U21s preview: Palace host PSG in International Cup opener Match previews 30 Aug 2026 Crystal Palace Under-21s begin their 2026/27 Premier League International Cup campaign against Paris Saint-Germain on Wednesday (2nd September, KO: 19:00 BST) – and there’s plenty to look forward to at Borough Sports Ground. It’s not just the first team flying the flag in Europe this season, with Season Ticket+, Gold and Junior Gold Members able to enjoy free entry to selected Under-18 and Under-21 home games. Buy PSG tickets Story so far... Darren Powell’s U21s have made an unbeaten start to the 2026/27 campaign, drawing 1-1 with Arsenal before securing their first victory with a 2-0 triumph at Aston Villa on Friday night. First-team star Zavier Gozo opened his account for the season at Arsenal, finishing a swift counter-attack to put Palace ahead, before the hosts levelled in the second half. The Young Eagles pushed for a winner late on but had to settle for a point. Palace started Bank Holiday weekend by producing a disciplined display at Villa. Harry Lee was outstanding as the hosts applied sustained pressure after the interval, making a string of excellent saves before Benji Casey broke the deadlock against the run of play. Adler Nascimento then put the result beyond doubt with a superb late finish. Those opening two fixtures came in a new-look Premier League 2, which now features all 31 Category One academies in a single division, with each side playing 20 matches before the top 16 progress to a single-elimination play-off. Now Palace turn their attention to the International Cup, a competition that has already delivered a memorable chapter in the Academy’s history. After finishing runners-up to Jong PSV in 22/23, the Young Eagles went one better the following season, defeating the Dutch side to lift the trophy. Palace’s title defence ended at the group stage in 24/25, while last season they progressed to the quarter-finals, where Real Sociedad got the better of them. There will be hopes that Powell’s side can go even further this time around, beginning with Wednesday night’s intriguing test against PSG! Our opposition – PSG They don’t come much bigger in European football than PSG. The French giants were named France’s best academy for 25/26 by the French Football Federation, showcasing the remarkable conveyor belt of talent coming through their ranks. Ten academy graduates have featured for PSG’s first team, while 12 have played in the UEFA Champions League and more than 20 have represented France at youth level. The club’s reach extends well beyond Paris, too, with more than 30 players aged under 23 developed by PSG now under professional contract with clubs in the top two divisions across Europe’s top 10 leagues. The Espoirs have already had a taste of English opposition this season, beating Manchester City 1-0 in a pre-season friendly, and will be hoping for another positive result on English soil on Wednesday. Last season, PSG finished fourth in their International Cup group. They began with a 2-0 win over Newcastle United before beating Chelsea 3-1, with Housni scoring twice. A 2-2 draw with Brighton & Hove Albion left them needing victory at Nottingham Forest on the final matchday to progress, but a 2-0 defeat brought their campaign to an end - they’ll be aiming to go one better this time around. Premier League International Cup explained Fancy some European football? You’re in the right place. Launched in 14/15, the Premier League International Cup gives Premier League academies the chance to go head-to-head with some of the best young sides from across Europe. The 26/27 competition features the top 16 Premier League 2 sides from last season alongside 16 invited European clubs. The 32 teams are split into four groups of eight, with four PL2 sides and four overseas teams in each. Every club plays four group-stage matches, all hosted in England, with the top two in each group advancing to the quarter-finals. Likely line-up Expected PSG line-up: Vignaud, Zague, Mfutila, Olax (c), Bastaraud, Diyinu Nzinga, Ghalleb, N’Guessan, Nsoki, Bezeme, Domingos. Team news PSG’s International Cup squad is their U21 side, known as the Espoirs. It features players progressing through the club’s academy towards senior football. Several members of the group have already gained experience at Under-19 level as they continue their development in Paris. Last time out… Palace put PSG to the sword in their last meeting, running out 7-3 winners in the International Cup group stages at Dulwich Hamlet’s Champion Hill in September 2022. Paddy McCarthy was in charge of the Young Eagles, with John-Kymani Gordon leading the charge with a hat-trick. Victor Akinwale, David Omilabu, Maliq Cadogan and Fionn Mooney were also on target as Palace extended their unbeaten run to nine matches in all competitions. It also sent the Young Eagles top of their International Cup group. Can history repeat itself on Wednesday? Key player – Fabio Domingos Fabio Domingos is one to watch for the visitors, with the Luxembourg-born winger joining PSG from Metz in 2025 after representing Luxembourg at youth level and Cape Verde’s senior side. Domingos was part of PSG’s U19 side last season, helping them win the Championnat National U19 title for a third successive year. He has featured for both the U19s and U21s this season, continuing his progression through the Parisian academy. The manager – Jean-François Vulliez Jean-François Vulliez leads PSG’s Under-21s and the Frenchman brings extensive experience in youth development, having spent more than a decade at Lyon, including six years as the club’s academy director. He later moved into senior football, working as an assistant coach at Lyon before taking up the same role at Danish side AC Horsens. Vulliez joined PSG last summer. How to follow The match will be streamed LIVE on Palace TV+ on Wednesday, with coverage beginning at 18:45 BST ahead of the 19:00 BST kick-off. Supporters can also follow live commentary on our Academy X page , with a full match report and reaction published shortly after full-time in our Academy news section Highlights and extended reaction will be available on Palace TV+ Match details Crystal Palace U21s v Paris Saint-Germain U21s Wednesday, 2nd September 19:00 BST Premier League International Cup Borough Sports Ground Match ticket prices Adults (21-64): £5 Young Adults (17-21): £1 Seniors (65+): £1 Juniors (2-16): £1 Academy Founder Members: Free Adult Gold, Junior Gold & Season Ticket+ Holders: Free Tickets are available here and will be issued as PDF print-at-home tickets at the point of sale. articles.body: Tottenham Hotspur 0 Newcastle United 2 | NUFC Match Report. Tottenham Hotspur 0 Newcastle United 2 Published 3 days ago Team Men Second-half strikes from Anthony Elanga and Yoane Wissa sealed a 2-0 win for Newcastle United in Saturday's Premier League clash against Tottenham Hotspur. Luke Vinton Written by After a goalless first half at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, Elanga's swivelled finish fired the visitors in front shortly after the hour mark. Wissa's improvised finish, his first competitive goal since January, doubled United's advantage as Matthias Jaissle recorded his first Premier League win in charge of the Magpies. The German head coach made six changes from Wednesday's 3-2 win against West Bromwich Albion in the Carabao Cup, with Nico González making his Magpies bow following his transfer from Manchester City. Targeting a third successive away win against Spurs, Newcastle went close to taking the lead inside the opening 60 seconds. Elanga, who netted his first Premier League goal for Newcastle in last weekend's 2-2 draw against Liverpool, latched onto Amar Dedić's clever header following Nico González's long-range pass but the Swedish winger's cross-cum shot was turned out by Archie Gray at the back post. Lukáš Horníček produced a strong stop to prevent Mathys Tel from breaking the deadlock as the French forward cut inside from the left flank before his curling effort was pushed away by the Czech shot-stopper. Lewis Hall produced a heroic last-ditch block to prevent Pedro Porro from firing Spurs ahead minutes later, turning the Spanish full-back's close-range effort over the crossbar. The Spurs full-back went close in front of goal as the Magpies defence were unable to clear from a short corner before his volley from the edge of the box flew wide of the target. Wissa went close to netting his first Premier League goal since December as the DR Congo international attempted to fire a shot at goal inside the six-yard area after Elanga nodded the ball into the African striker's path but his effort was blocked by Micky van de Ven. Horníček carried out two terrific saves before the half-time whistle, beating away Andy Robertson's low drive from an acute angle. From the resulting corner, the Czech 'keeper was alert to pushing away Jan Paul van Hecke's close-range header. Lewis Hall went close to breaking the deadlock shortly after the restart as the left-back cut inside on the edge of the box before his curling right-footed effort flew over the crossbar. In the 62nd minute, Elanga broke the deadlock for United. After Nico's impressive long-range pass flew into Dedić's path, the Bosnian full-back nodded the ball into Elanga's path before the Swedish frontman produced a neat turn before firing the ball into the net via the left-hand post. Horníček prevented Porro from drawing Spurs level as the Spaniard's fierce drive from the edge of the box was tipped over the crossbar by the 24-year-old 'keeper. In the 72nd minute, Newcastle extended their advantage as Wissa netted his first goal of the 2026/27 campaign. After Hall's inviting corner from the right flank was nodded towards substitute Nick Woltemade, Wissa was on hand to turn the ball home from close-range. Horníček ensured a first clean sheet of his Magpies career in the closing stages, holding Omar Marmoush's volley after Mateus Fernandes' cross found the unmarked Egyptian inside the penalty area. There was a brief Premier League debut for Bazoumana Touré as the Ivorian winger, who scored on his competitive Magpies bow during Wednesday's win against West Brom, was introduced in stoppage-time. Newcastle United: Lukáš Horníček, Lewis Hall, Sven Botman, Nico González (Sean Steur 71), Yoane Wissa (Jacob Ramsey 82), Harvey Barnes (Bazoumana Touré 90), Malick Thiaw (c), Anthony Elanga (Jacob Murphy 82), Joe Willock (Nick Woltemade 71), Amar Dedić, Lewis Miley. articles.title: Scott: We had chances to go and win the game
articles.excerpt: Midfielder Alex Scott felt AFC Bournemouth “deserved to win the game” after they were pegged back late on in a 1-1 draw against Everton. The Cherries midfielder struck in the opening half at Vitality Stadium, capping off a slick counter-attack after brilliant work from Evanilson. But the Toffees found a leveller in second-half stoppage time through James Tarkowski, meaning Marco Rose’s side were left to settle for a point in their opening home game of the season. Speaking post-match, Scott said: “I think we deserved to win the game. A mistake at the end and it’s cost us three points, which in this league, between three points and one, that’s the margin. “We had chances to go and win the game and we didn’t take them. Now it’s time to focus on Newcastle next week. “I think we were the better team on the day and probably deserved the points but they got stuck in there and got the goal at the end.” Reflecting on his goal. articles.title: POTM MCATEE DISCUSSES POINT AGAINST LIVERPOOL
articles.excerpt: McAtee discusses Forest’s point against Liverpool Reds took the lead twice at Anfield Midfielder scooped POTM award from the game James McAtee says the Nottingham Forest players didn’t know how to feel after picking up a point against Liverpool. McAtee was named Player of the Match after an outstanding individual display, but the playmaker was full of praise for his teammates for sticking together and taking a point from the game. “We don’t really know how to feel. To come here and get a point is amazing, but the game was in our hands twice. “There’s a bit of disappointment because we could have got the points, but we’re also happy with the performance. We came here, we stuck together and we put a good point on the board. “It was a credit to the players for taking the lead again after they equalised. But when you come here anything can happen, so we can’t be too disappointed. “We stuck to the game plan, we tried to get in scoring positions, which we did. Alisson made an unbelievable save from Igor which would have seen us 2-0 up at the break.

articles.source_type: Manager team-news updates with named injuries and return timelines
articles.body: Confirmed line-up: Debut for González at Spurs | NUFC Latest. Confirmed line-up: Debut for González at Spurs Published 3 days ago Team Men New signing Nico González has been handed his Newcastle United debut ahead of Saturday's Premier League clash away at Tottenham Hotspur (kick-off 5:30pm BST). The Spanish midfielder, who arrived on Tyneside from Manchester City earlier this week, is one of six changes from Wednesday's 3-2 win against West Bromwich Albion in the Carabao Cup. Goalkeeper Lukáš Horníček, who made his Premier League debut in last week's 2-2 draw against Liverpool, replaces Ewen Jaouen in-between the sticks. Head coach Matthias Jaissle has named an unchanged backline for a third consecutive game, with Malick Thiaw and Sven Botman situated at the heart of United's defence, while Amar Dedić and Lewis Hall are set to play on the respective flanks. González, who made his Premier League bow against Newcastle in February 2025, will line up alongside Lewis Miley in the middle of the park. Harvey Barnes, who netted a second half brace against West Brom, as well as Joe Willock and Anthony Elanga are named in the starting 11 as they aim to provide attacking support for Yoane Wissa, who has three goal involvements in his last three league outings against Spurs. Jaissle has a number of options to deploy from the substitutes' bench if required, including Jacob Ramsey who netted the winning goal in last season's 2-1 victory at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. Nick Woltemade, who scored in United's 2-0 win against Tottenham in the Carabao Cup last season, is also named on the bench as well as Bazoumana Touré, Jacob Muphy, Sean Steur and Aladji Bamba. Fabian Schär and Leo Shahar, the latter targeting his Premier League debut, are defensive reinforcements. Newcastle United: Lukáš Horníček, Lewis Hall, Sven Botman, Nico González, Yoane Wissa, Harvey Barnes, Malick Thiaw (c), Anthony Elanga, Joe Willock, Amar Dedić, Lewis Miley. articles.excerpt: Good afternoon everyone, and welcome back to the Stadium of Light for our first home game of the season against Fulham. Last season, we created memories that will stay with us forever, and you stood with us every step of the way. We achieved something special, and now we have the opportunity to build on that with Premier League and European football ahead of us. We know what you expect from us. Ultimately, I want to win, but we know that doesn’t just start at the weekend – it starts on the training ground earlier that week. It’s a process and a project, and we can’t turn it off and on. Diego Forlan's brace settled the 2010 Europa League final Facebook Pinterest Email Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google During his two-decade career as a professional footballer, Diego Forlan has played in eight countries across three continents and turned out in a World Cup semi-final on his way to winning more than 100 international caps. This journey has thrown up plenty of career highlights, but for the former Manchester United man, the 2010 Europa League final remains a particular standout. The forward was a key part of Atletico Madrid’s 2-1 extra-time success over Fulham in Hamburg that night, scoring both goals for his side, including a 116th-minute winner to end the Cottagers' fairytale run to their first European final. Forlan on firing Atletico to Europa League glory Forlan joined Atletico Madrid in 2007 (Image credit: Alamy) “That night in Hamburg was one of the best of my career,” Forlan tells FourFourTwo . “A dream final. Not so much because it was a brilliant match, but because of the script.” Fulham’s remarkable run to the final in just their second-ever European campaign had seen them first navigate a group containing Roma , CSKA Moscow and Basel, before Shakhtar Donetsk, Juventus , Wolfsburg and Hamburg were accounted for in the knockouts. Roy Hodgson had led Fulham to the Europa League final (Image credit: PA) “Fulham arrived as the underdog, but they made life very difficult for us,” Forlan continues. I scored after half an hour, Simon Davies equalised, and the final went to extra time.” With the clock continuing to run down, penalties loomed, only for Forlan to deliver when it mattered most, as he took full advantage of a chance that fell his way deep in the second half of extra time. The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week. “When everything seemed to be heading for a penalty shootout, Sergio Aguero battled for a ball out wide and spotted me in the heart of the box,” he continues. “I managed to get the tip of my boot to it to give Atletico the title.” Forlan’s reaction to the goal was as instinctive as his finish. “I took my shirt off and threw myself onto the turf as if it were a swimming pool,” he recalls. Forlan scored 96 goals in five seasons with Atletico (Image credit: Getty Images) For Forlan, the significance of the goal stretched further than just adding another title to Atletico’s roll of honour. “That goal tasted like glory, because it also marked a turning point for a club that started to feel important again,” he believes. “Spain’s capital, a city used to seeing Real Madrid celebrating titles, was painted red and white, and thousands of fans gathered at Plaza de Neptuno in a huge display of pride.” TOPICS Joe Mewis For more than a decade, Joe Mewis has worked in football journalism as a reporter and editor. Mewis has had stints at Mirror Football and LeedsLive among others and worked at FourFourTwo throughout Euro 2024, reporting on the tournament. In addition to his journalist work, Mewis is also the author of four football history books that include times on Leeds United and the England national team. Now working as a digital marketing coordinator at Harrogate Town, too, Mewis counts some of his best career moments as being in the iconic Spygate press conference under Marcelo Bielsa and seeing his beloved Leeds lift the Championship trophy during lockdown. articles.title: Under-18s Defeated By Manchester United
articles.excerpt: Everton Under-18s were beaten 3-0 by Manchester United at Finch Farm on Saturday morning. James McEvoy had the ball in the net early on for the visitors but it was ruled out for offside, before United got one that did count midway through the first half, as the dangerous Edson DeJonge-Seiros crossed from the left and Jariyah Shah slammed into the back of the net. Everton grew into the contest and Harry Brookes saw an effort blocked, while Dafi Pemberton spun cleverly on the edge of the penalty area before pulling his shot wide of the target. The Blues' Rodney Aduda then saw his header well saved after being picked out by Harvey Billington. United had chances, too. Juame Camacho wasn’t far away with a snapshot and Nathaniel Junior-Brown failed to hit the target after catching the hosts' in possession. Early in the second period, Blues' goalkeeper Ted Wilcox safely gathered an attempt from DeJonge-Seiros and, at the other end, a John Dodds close-range volley was athletically turned away by United shot-stopper Charlie Hardy. The second United goal came on 56 minutes – James McEvoy heading home from a dangerous corner. Genuine opportunities were at a premium after that. Freddie Murdock

Matthias Jaissle was confirmed as Eddie Howe's replacement at Newcastle United this summer (Image credit: Newcastle United v Getty Images) Facebook Pinterest Email Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Less than two years ago, FourFourTwo sat inside the bowels of Al Ahli's inner city training ground in Jeddah, and whispers abounded. “If he loses this game, the manager might well be sacked,” one Saudi Pro League expert told us that evening, as we waited for Matthias Jaissle to arrive for his latest pre-match press conference. Al Ahli had won only three of their first eight games of the new league season, and sat eighth in the table before the Jeddah derby with title-challenging Al Ittihad – a fixture that would attract a raucous crowd of 52,546. Given that Jaissle's club were one of the Saudi Pro League's big four – all owned by the country's Public Investment Fund (PIF) – their results were below expectation. Back then, the main focus of our visit to Al Ahli had been the recent signing of Ivan Toney , rather than Jaissle, who was largely unknown to British audiences in October 2024. Our question was whether he could help his new frontman make England's next World Cup squad – Jaissle knew Thomas Tuchel, having played for him in the youth teams at VfB Stuttgart. “Let's see if Thomas calls me and asks how Ivan is doing,” the smartly dressed Jaissle told FFT . “Ivan has the potential, definitely – he must deliver here to be seen in the UK, and we're doing our best to bring him into the best shape.” Prior to this summer's World Cup, Tuchel did indeed call Jaissle to discuss Toney, revealing the “fantastic feedback” he received was enough to persuade him to pick the 30-year-old in his squad. By then, though, Jaissle could easily have been long gone as Al Ahli boss. He did lose that Jeddah derby against Al Ittihad, a tetchy game interrupted by a sandstorm that blew dust from the nearby desert into the stadium. He avoided the sack, but was reportedly on his way out two months later after a loss at Al Kholood, with Max Allegri said to be his long-term replacement. Pick the ultimate 4-4-2 line-up from players in FourFourTwo's definitive Top 100 List That was until ultras protested at the training ground, putting up a banner declaring “Enough failure, leave!” The message was aimed at the club's hierarchy, rather than the manager. Jaissle stayed, and became an Al Ahli legend within months. The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week. Jaissle was a central defender during a playing career that saw him help Hoffenheim to the Bundesliga for the first time in 2008, when he'd just turned 20. He'd been expected to be alongside Mesut Ozil, Mats Hummels and Manuel Neuer as part of the Germany under-21 squad that thrashed England in the final of the Euros in 2009, but damaged his ACL shortly before the tournament and would never be the same player again. Further injuries forced him to retire in 2014, aged 25, before he got a job as a youth coach at RB Leipzig – his former Hoffenheim manager Ralf Rangnick had since become a key man in Red Bull's football project. Jaissle adopted a similarly high-pressing style, and has taken it with him ever since. After a stint as assistant at Danish club Brondby, he joined Red Bull Salzburg, led their feeder side FC Liefering to a joint-highest finish, then was handed the reins at the main club, replacing Jesse Marsch in 2021. Matthias Jaissle poses after leading FC Red Bull Salzburg to the Austrian championship in 2023 (Image credit: FC Red Bull Salzburg via Getty I) Working with young players such as Benjamin Sesko , Karim Adeyemi, Noah Okafor and Brenden Aaronson, he took Salzburg to a double in his first season, plus the Champions League's knockout stage for the only time in their history. They lost 7-1 at Bayern Munich in the last 16, while Jaissle was still only 33. A season later, they went 30 matches unbeaten on the way to yet another domestic triumph. It was Salzburg's 10th straight title, but they haven't won the league since Jaissle left that summer. The German joined Al Ahli just a month after they'd been one of four clubs to be taken over by the Saudi PIF – together with Al Ittihad, Al Hilal and Cristiano Ronaldo' s Al Nassr. Jaissle's new club had been Saudi Pro League champions in 2016 but relegated since, only returning to the top flight in the same summer as his arrival. They quickly signed Riyad Mahrez, Roberto Firmino, Edouard Mendy, Franck Kessie and ex-Newcastle winger Allan Saint-Maximin, finishing an encouraging third in Jaissle's first season – enough to qualify for the Asian Champions League. Ivan Tony scored 72 goals in two seasons under Jaissle (Image credit: Getty Images) Then came Toney's arrival, and that tricky start to 2024-25 when Jaissle so nearly lost his job. He knew the pressure he was under when we visited, but didn't let it show – remaining professional throughout, even taking time to greet visiting European media afterwards. It was hard not to warm to him. “Things take time – the club has a long-term vision,” Jaissle told us, subtly calling for patience as he attempted to turn around results, while nodding to his ability to improve young players. “I hope we can do better by implementing the philosophy from the top down to the academy, because at some point we'll need the young talents. In my eyes, that is the right approach. “A lot of signings were made before I arrived, so it's important as a coach that you're flexible enough to adapt to a new country, culture and player profiles. In the long run, it's important everyone is aligned, that you improve your squad and players in the way you want to play.” Jaissle replaced Eddie Howe at Newcastle United this summer (Image credit: Getty Images) Jaissle was afforded time to do that. Their progress to the knockout stage of the Asian Champions League had been a factor in him avoiding the sack – Al Ahli had a stronger second half of the league campaign, improving to fifth, then surprisingly became kings of Asia for the first time ever. The Champions League's final three rounds all take place in Jeddah, giving Al Ahli a home advantage that helped, but they still had to defeat reigning Saudi champions Al Hilal in the semis, before a final victory over Japanese side Kawasaki Frontale – conquerors of Ronaldo's Al Nassr. Last term, while finishing third in a three-way domestic race, they went all Brian Clough's Nottingham Forest and became continental champions again. Toney was key, scoring 72 goals in two seasons under Jaissle. When PIF-owned Newcastle were looking for a manager to replace Eddie Howe this summer, it shouldn't have been a surprise that they opted for the German. Howe will be a tough act to follow, having delivered the Magpies a first major honour in 56 years. Why have a manager who's won one historic trophy, though, when you can have a gaffer who's won two? articles.body: Matthias Jaissle's team news update: González an 'optio... | NUFC Latest. Matthias Jaissle's team news update: González an 'option' for Spurs trip Published 5 days ago Team Men Newcastle United head coach Matthias Jaissle says new signing Nico González is an 'option' as he weighs up whether to hand the Spanish midfielder a debut at Tottenham Hotspur on Saturday (kick-off 5.30pm). United travel to the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium this weekend for their first away game of the new Premier League season, having been denied a win over Liverpool on the opening day by Dominik Szoboszlai's last-gasp penalty in the dying seconds of the 2-2 draw. The German boss also spoke about his ahead of the trip to the capital, where Newcastle won 2-1 last term. Jaissle spoke to the media on Thursday evening ahead of the clash with Roberto De Zerbi's men, who could hand a home debut to former Magpie Sandro Tonali. Here are some of the main talking points from his pre-match briefing: On former Manchester City man González... "He trained with us and he looked sharp. He's an option. "He is a smart player, he has huge potential, and already he brings huge quality to the squad." On Spurs... "We will be facing a top team. It is a difficult change. "We will not change our approach. We are facing a really strong opponent. With our playing style, we can cause any opponents problems." On his start to life at Newcastle... "I was really blessed with the warm welcome they gave me. "I have seen the atmosphere in the stadium already from these two competitive matches - it was really special. "This is a special club. We have a clear idea of how we want to play football. We will not change our approach." On the potential in his young squad... "We want to build on what we are building. "With the young lads we need to expect up and downs. I am really much looking forward to this journey. "The lads are very committed. I am really happy with what I am seeing in training - it will be something special to build on." articles.body: EFL Best Bets This Weekend - 29-30 August Seb's EFL Best Bets: Wednesday, Barnet and a Blackpool Shootout Round three of the EFL season and the coupon is starting to tell us things. Eight bets below, and a Weekend Double that pays around 9/5. Championship Middlesbrough v West Brom (Sat 12:30) Boro put three past Doncaster in the cup in midweek without breaking stride, and their league form line - three wins in five - reads better than a side that was scrapping for the play-offs in spring has any right to expect this early. West Brom have been flat on the road. The model makes the home win a 54% chance, which at the price is the best result bet in the division this week. The bet: Middlesbrough to win at 1.71 full match stats here Watford v West Ham (Sat 3:00pm) West Ham's first Championship August in a generation has gone better than the doom-mongers predicted - three wins in five, and the model rates them at 51% to make it another away day to remember at Vicarage Road. Watford have been generous at the back to everyone who has pressed them. The bet: West Ham to win at 1.79 full match stats here Cardiff v Sheffield United (Sat 3:00pm) The goals game of the division. The model's strongest both-teams-to-score number on the entire Championship coupon lands here at 61%, two sides who have started the season allergic to clean sheets. The bet: Both teams to score at 1.57 full match stats here League One Sheffield Wednesday v Bromley (Sat 3:00pm) Three wins from five for Wednesday, and Hillsborough against newly promoted opposition is exactly the fixture a side with their early-season swagger should be winning. The model has the home win at 59% - the strongest single in League One this weekend - and ranks it highly enough to anchor the Weekend Double below. The bet: Sheffield Wednesday to win at 1.79 full match stats here Blackpool v Peterborough (Sat 12:30) Pick a market, any market: the model makes this the most watchable game in the division, with both teams to score at 63% and the overs number a shade higher still. Posh away days have been chaos for years and Blackpool have won three of five scoring freely. Take the goals over the winner. The bet: Over 2.5 goals at 1.62 full match stats here League Two Barnet v Cheltenham (Sat 12:30) Four wins in five for Barnet, and the model makes Saturday lunchtime at The Hive a 58% home win - the top number on the League Two coupon. Sides that come up with momentum tend to keep swinging until somebody stops them, and Cheltenham on the road do not look like the somebody. The bet: Barnet to win at 1.57 full match stats here York v Exeter (Sat 3:00pm) Another of the promoted sides refusing to read the script. York have lost just once in five and the model puts them at 57% here against an Exeter side finding the fourth tier less forgiving than advertised. The bet: York to win at 1.62 full match stats here Shrewsbury v Salford (Sat 3:00pm) Salford's winless start has come with goals at both ends and Shrewsbury's games have been the same story. The model's top goals number in the division lives here at 61%. The bet: Over 2.5 goals at 1.80 full match stats here The Weekend Double The two strongest numbers on the coupon, one from each of the lower divisions: Sheffield Wednesday to beat Bromley and Barnet to beat Cheltenham . The model makes them 59% and 58% respectively, and the double pays around 9/5 (2.81) with bet365 at the time of writing. One from Hillsborough, one from The Hive, both done by tea-time on Saturday. The column takes the strongest numbers, checks them against form, and keeps singles in the 1.50 to 2.60 band. What is the Weekend Double? The two strongest model calls across the divisions, combined into one two-leg accumulator with the combined price quoted at the time of writing. It settles like any double: both legs must win. Do you track results? Yes - every column's bets settle publicly the following week, winners and losers alike, and the season's running record is quoted whenever it is claimed. articles.title: The Story So Far: Mohamed-Ali Cho
articles.excerpt: An in-depth look into our 12 th summer signing, Mohamed-Ali Cho… Born on 19 January 2004 in Stains, a commune in the Seine-Saint-Denis department in the northern suburbs of Paris, France, Mohamed-Ali Cho moved to London at one week old and would begin his footballing journey at West Ham United. Briefly returning to France at the age of six to play for Chantilly in 2010, the forward was picked up by Paris Saint-Germain a year later. articles.title: Fulham Vs Chelsea [2-3] Premier League 2026/2027: How Does Xabi Alonso's New Front Three Work? – Tactical Analysis
articles.excerpt: Chelsea’s new front three of Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers and João Pedro starred in Xabi Alonso’s first Premier League win. This tactical analysis examines their complementary roles, pressing and attacking threat against Fulham.
articles.source_type: Manager tactics breakdowns, team shape, pressing and build-up analysis
articles.body: Fulham Vs Chelsea [2-3] Premier League 2026/2027 - Analysis The final match of the opening gameweek of the 2026/2027 Premier League season saw ex-teammates at Liverpool Real Madrid and Spain face off in the dugouts of Craven Cottage , as new Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso began his tenure as Blues boss against a familiar face in new Fulham chief Álvaro Arbeloa The contest produced end-to-end action that resulted in a five-goal thriller that fell Chelsea’s way. Both teams leave with some serious defensive issues to address. However, the majority of Chelsea fans and neutrals will have left Monday’s match with the stellar performance of Alonso’s new front three firmly in the front of their minds. The contrasting and complementary profiles, all of whom displayed exactly the type of positivity, confidence and intent to solve problems that you want to see from your attackers, posed a constant threat to the Fulham backline from the first whistle (literally, with Chelsea’s opener coming in the very first minute). This Fulham versus Chelsea tactical analysis details how Alonso’s front three functioned in and out of possession in gameweek one. Fulham Vs Chelsea Lineups & Formations Figure 1 Fulham Lineup Vs Chelsea The hosts lined up in a 4-2-3-1 shape with Bernd Leno in goal behind a back four of Timothy Castagne Calvin Bassey Jorge Cuenca and Antonee Robinson , from right to left. Sander Berge and Alex Iwobi started in midfield, behind a creative attacking trio of Oscar Bobb Josh King and César Palacios , with Gonzalo García leading the line. Arbeloa made four changes to his starting XI during the match, the first of which saw Shea Charles replace Bobb in the 67th minute. A double change followed six minutes later, when Kevin and Ryan Sessegnon replaced Palacios and Berge. Then, in the 82nd minute, another forward, Rodrigo Muniz , was introduced for left-back Robinson. Chelsea Lineup Vs Fulham Meanwhile, the visitors set up in a 3-4-2-1 shape with Robert Sánchez in goal behind a back three of Josh Acheampong Maxence Lacroix and Levi Colwill Malo Gusto and Jorrel Hato started as the wing-backs, while Reece James and Roméo Lavia played in central midfield. Chelsea’s attacking trio was Cole Palmer Morgan Rogers and João Pedro Alonso made five changes to his starting XI over the course of the match. In the 65th minute, he introduced Enzo Fernández and Pep Chavarría for Lavia and Hato. Then, 11 minutes later, Pedro Neto was introduced for Malo Gusto. Lastly, in the 82nd minute, Geovany Quenda and Estêvão came on for Palmer and Rogers. Fulham Vs Chelsea Stats While Fulham finished the game on top in the possession department (averaging 60.5% vs Chelsea’s 39.5%) , Chelsea were ultimately more efficient, which is what allowed them to leave Craven Cottage with all three points. The Blues generated more shots ( to Fulham’s ) and a slightly higher xG ( 2.48 vs Fulham’s 2.01 ), but that was enough given the quality in their forward line to make the most of the opportunities. Fulham favoured longer periods of possession, averaging 6.29 passes per possession to Chelsea’s 4.37 , while the Cottagers also had a far lower PPDA of 9.88 to Chelsea’s 17.46 The home side sought to play out from the back and build through the thirds patiently, while Chelsea set up to get the ball into their front three early and aggressively to let their quality on the ball do the work. There weren’t any players in Chelsea’s starting XI you’d really expect to see setting the world alight on the ball outside of that front three, and that showed in how Chelsea played. They looked to find those difference makers all the time, and thanks to some intelligent movement and good progressive passing, they were able to do so often enough to put three past Fulham, while also exploiting Fulham’s possession-based approach with intelligent pressing from the front on the other side of the ball. Chelsea Pass Map & Average Positions Vs Fulham Figure 2 Chelsea’s compact, vertically oriented structure in Figure 2 highlights how their progression had a strong bias towards the right-hand side, particularly running through Reece James (24) in central midfield and Palmer (10), who acted as the key connection into the final third. Though Palmer and Rogers (17) almost mirrored one another on paper, their roles contrasted heavily in practice. From his right-sided position, Palmer assumed the responsibilities associated with a traditional No. 10 far more effectively, acting as the central hub around which Chelsea’s attacks revolved. Rogers was less involved in circulation and played a more dynamic role. An excellent complement to Palmer, Rogers played higher rather than constantly looking to receive and dictate the play like Palmer. He drifted into the half-space and threatened with runs in behind the Fulham backline, resembling more of a second-striker than a traditional No. 10. Chelsea’s Front Three Out Of Possession Chelsea’s out-of-possession strategy required intensity and positional intelligence from their front three, in particular, during all defensive phases, especially the high press. From the first kick of the ball on Monday evening, Chelsea’s front three had clear instructions during the high press: 1. Protect the passing lanes into midfield via their cover shadows. 2. Apply pressure on Fulham’s goalkeeper and centre-backs when receiving on the back foot or in limited space. Figure 3 Figures 3-4 show these pressing tactics in action. Figure 4 The ball makes its way from Leno to Cuenca, with the centre-back positioned very wide. This opens the door for Palmer to close the receiver down and contain him out wide by pressing, with the route to midfield kept in his cover shadow. Chelsea’s midfield and wing-backs, crucially, push up in support of Palmer to prevent Cuenca from escaping via short passing options, which forces the Fulham defender into the long ball, which Chelsea are well placed to deal with thanks to having three centre-backs on the pitch. The resulting recovery led to the opening goal of the game inside the first minute, as Palmer received the ball in space behind Fulham’s midfield line, which had been looking to advance and apply pressure on the second ball following Cuenca’s long pass. Palmer took advantage of this space to receive and turn, while taking advantage of the massive gap that still existed between Fulham’s centre-backs to play João Pedro through to score. This shows how Chelsea’s pressing helped them to take advantage of Fulham’s in-possession tactics throughout the match. Fulham were not set up to go long, quite the opposite, but Chelsea’s coordinated pressing forced them into long balls at times, which created turnovers and opportunities for Alonso’s side to quickly find their front three in transition. This was a recurring sequence throughout the match, with the exact same passage of play that led to the goal recurring just a couple of minutes later, as shown in Figures 5-6. Figure 5 Initially, Chelsea’s front three guard the passing lanes into the centre. Figure 6 When the ball goes back to Leno, João Pedro pounces while keeping the midfielder behind him in his cover shadow. This forces Leno to Cuenca again; Palmer presses while keeping the midfielder behind him in his cover shadow too, leading to the centre-back sending the ball long. Just like the start of the first half, the sequence repeated at the beginning of the second half. articles.title: How to Bet the Carabao Cup Second Round: Rotation, Goals and Team News
articles.excerpt: Tonight's strongest Carabao Cup selection projects higher than anything in the English leagues next Saturday. The card is not the problem - the team sheets are. How to use the projections, which markets are rotation-proof, and the lineup check that decides it.
articles.source_type: Head-to-head player comparison, goalkeeper and position value analysis
articles.body: How to Bet the Carabao Cup Second Round How to Bet the Carabao Cup Second Round: Rotation, Goals and Team News The Carabao Cup second round gets written off as a lottery. On our projections it is not, or at least not for the reason people think. The strongest selection on tonight's seventeen-tie card is Watford at home to Peterborough, projected at 63.4% . The strongest selection anywhere in the four English leagues next Saturday is Wolves at home to Stoke, at 60.2% . The cup card is, if anything, marginally less even than a normal league weekend, because the round pairs teams from different divisions. So the fixtures are not the problem. The team sheets are. Everything below is about that gap. The rotation problem, and why the model cannot solve it Nobody knows who is rotating until the lineups drop. Some managers will field youngsters and a pure second string; others will want to protect league momentum and make one or two changes at most. Two clubs in identical league positions will treat this round completely differently, and neither will tell you in advance. Our projections are honest about their own blind spot here. They are built on league form , and tonight's set was generated on Friday. They do not know who is being rested. When the model says Ipswich are 61.7% to beat Leicester, it means Ipswich's league-standard side against Leicester's league-standard side. That is not a flaw to route around, it is the thing to plan for. It means every number on this page is a starting position , and the last hour before kick-off is where you finish the job. The team news routine Check about an hour before kick-off , when lineups are confirmed. Ours land on the fixture pages as they are announced. Look at the shape of the change, not the count. Six changes with the spine intact is a different proposition to four changes that remove the entire midfield. If you see a teenage midfield, leave it alone. A projection built on league form has nothing useful to say about a side with three academy players in it. Check both teams. A rotated favourite against a rotated underdog is closer to the original number than a rotated favourite against a full-strength one. Where the numbers still help Goals markets sidestep the question This is the most useful thing on the page. A goals market does not care which eleven turns up, and if both managers change things the defending usually suffers before the attacking does. The model's highest both-teams-to-score ties tonight: Tie BTTS 2+ goals Southampton v West Ham 62.4% 81.8% Cardiff v Norwich 61.8% 81.4% Plymouth v Coventry 58.9% 81.3% Watford v Peterborough 57.5% 83.5% Ipswich v Leicester 56.8% 82.3% Blackpool v Lincoln 56.3% 77.2% Walsall v Leyton Orient 55.7% 76.0% Birmingham v Brentford 54.5% 79.5% The ten highest-projected ties on the card all reach 76% or better for two or more goals. That is the shape of a round where nobody is quite settled. Clean sheets are the market to avoid The highest clean-sheet probability on the entire seventeen-tie card is 39.5% , for Wolves away at Sheffield Wednesday. After that it is Fleetwood at 38.9% and Middlesbrough at 38.5%. Not one team on the card is even a 40% chance to keep it out. Backing a clean sheet, a correct score or a to-nil in this round is asking for precision the evening will not give you. If you are backing a winner, back a mismatch Selection Win % Projected goals Watford v Peterborough 63.4% 2.21 Ipswich v Leicester 61.7% 2.12 Middlesbrough at Doncaster 61.1% 2.00 Brentford at Birmingham 58.8% 1.95 Barnsley v Crewe 55.9% 1.80 Wolves at Sheffield Wednesday 54.9% 1.70 Coventry at Plymouth 54.1% 1.91 Note how quickly it flattens. By the seventh name you are at 54%, and below that the card is a coin toss - Fleetwood 45.6%, Lincoln 45.1%, Millwall 44.5%. There is no value in reaching down that list for a favourite; if the model will not commit past the halfway mark, neither should you. How we are playing it Two trebles on today's Daily Acca , deliberately built as opposites. The first takes the three strongest projected winners - Middlesbrough, Watford and Ipswich - and accepts the rotation risk in exchange for a price. The second takes the three highest both-teams-to-score ties and avoids the question entirely: it does not matter who is rested if both ends of the pitch are leaky. Both are staked at a point, both are priced around 4.0, and both are published before team news, which is precisely why the routine above matters. Our record on every acca is public in the column's own ledger , winners and losers alike. Five things to remember The card is not a lottery, the team sheets are. The projections rate tonight's favourites slightly higher than next weekend's league card. Goals markets are rotation-proof. The ten best ties on the card all reach 76% for 2+ goals. Leave clean sheets and correct scores alone. Nothing on the card reaches 40%. Do not chase a favourite below about 55%. The list flattens into coin tosses fast. Check the lineups an hour before. It is the single highest-value thing you can do in this round, and it costs nothing. The small print All projections were generated before team news and are built on league form. They do not model rotation, and we are not claiming they do. Prices quoted are bet365 at the time of writing and will move. A projection is a probability, not a forecast of one evening. A 63.4% favourite loses more than a third of the time. 18+. Premier League Gameweek 1 Fulham Aug 24, 2026 8.00pm HT : Craven Cottage Chelsea Josh King 23' Gonzalo GarcÃ­a 54' Calvin Bassey 76' Timothy Castagne 88' JoÃ£o Pedro 1' Levi Colwill 5' RomÃ©o Lavia 12' Morgan Rogers 41' Cole Palmer 49' Reece JamesÂ 75' Fulham 2-3 Chelsea: Highlights, man of the match, stats as Pedro, Palmer, Rogers light up Craven Cottage Ellis Stevens 24 Aug 2026 21:55 Â© Iconsport / Sportimage Ltd/Alamy Live News Chelsea secured the West London derby bragging rights with a thrilling 3-2 victory over Fulham at Craven Cottage on Monday night. Chelsea raced into the lead after just 31 seconds thanks to Joao Pedro 's delightful dink, and that early goal set the tempo for the half, with the two attack-minded sides trading chances in an energetic, back-and-forth clash. Josh King eventually equalised for Fulham after a spell of pressure, with Robert Sanchez making a costly error, but Chelsea restored their lead just before the break through a debut goal from Morgan Rogers The goals continued to flow in the second half, as Cole Palmer extended Chelsea's lead just five minutes after the restart, only for Gonzalo Garcia to pull one back on his Premier League debut six minutes later. Fulham pushed for an equaliser as the game edged towards full-time, but Chelsea came closest to scoring when Pedro was denied a second for offside, with the Blues ultimately holding on to secure all three points at Craven Cottage. SPORTS MOLE'S VERDICT Regardless of the result, both teams will take plenty of encouragement from their attacking performances, but there may be some concerns over their defensive displays. Chelsea and Fulham both looked dangerous from minute one until minute 90, including their respective summer signings demonstrating their ability and contributing in the final third. Chelsea's trio of Pedro, Palmer and Rogers looked particularly threatening, pressing high and constantly combining in attacking areas - something Chelsea supporters will be hoping to see even more of as the season progresses. However, the Blues did look defensively vulnerable, particularly goalkeeper Sanchez, who made errors in each of Fulham's two goals, while the Cottagers were caught in possession numerous times high up the pitch. Ultimately, Xabi Alonso and Alvaro Arbeloa will be largely pleased with their performances and will be looking to build on the positive aspects in the coming weeks. FULHAM VS. CHELSEA HIGHLIGHTS Joao Pedro goal vs. Fulham (1st min, Fulham 0-1 Chelsea) "A flying start under Xabi Alonso!" Chelsea lead against Fulham after just 31 seconds ? pic.twitter.com/LrkYxOReFB — Sky Sports Premier League (@SkySportsPL) August 24, 2026 Unbelievable start for Chelsea! Pedro scores after 31 seconds! Jorge Cuenca's long ball forward is headed back into Fulham's half to Cole Palmer, who immediately slides a pass through to Pedro. Pedro drives into the box and expertly lobs the onrushing Bernd Leno, finding the bottom-left corner. Josh King goal vs. Chelsea (23rd min, Fulham 1-1 Chelsea) Fulham have equalised against Chelsea thanks to Josh King's low strike ? pic.twitter.com/WCLKB7XqeE — Sky Sports Premier League (@SkySportsPL) August 24, 2026 King equalises for Fulham! Robert Sanchez will not want to watch that back! King picks up the ball on the right side and plays a give-and-go with Timothy Castagne, receiving the ball back and driving into the Chelsea penalty area. The midfielder quickly unleashes a strike towards the front post, catching Sanchez off guard with the keeper guarding the far corner, and the ball flies through the Spaniard's hands into the back of the net. Morgan Rogers goal vs. Fulham (40th min, Fulham 1-2 Chelsea) A goal for Morgan Rogers on his Chelsea debut! ? pic.twitter.com/hphe8y077v — Sky Sports Premier League (@SkySportsPL) August 24, 2026 Rogers restores Chelsea's lead! Palmer skilfully spins away from Sander Berge and plays through Maxence Lacroix, who brilliantly races towards the byline and pulls a pass back to Rogers inside the box. Rogers calmly side-foots his effort into the middle of the gaping goal, beating two Fulham defenders on the line and finding the back of the net. Cole Palmer goal vs. Fulham (49th min, Fulham 1-3 Chelsea) "Cole Palmer back to his best!" Palmer has scored to double Chelsea's lead! ? pic.twitter.com/zo6e0Vdcgq — Sky Sports Premier League (@SkySportsPL) August 24, 2026 Palmer makes it three! Sanchez's long ball is flicked forward by Rogers to Pedro, who races into the Fulham penalty area and squares up his marker. Palmer surges around the outside of Pedro, who waits for the run and plays a perfectly weighted pass to Chelsea's number 10, who clinically finishes through Leno's legs. Gonzalo Garcia goal vs. Chelsea (54th min, Fulham 2-3 Chelsea) Gonzalo Garcia has scored on his Premier League debut after Robert Sanchez spilled Castagne's shot ? pic.twitter.com/BmP6eqwkuN — Sky Sports Premier League (@SkySportsPL) August 24, 2026 Garcia pulls one back for Fulham! Game on! Cuenca's long ball into the Chelsea box evades Levi Colwill and finds Castagne, who strikes a first-time effort towards goal with his left foot. Sanchez parries the ball back into the danger area, and Garcia is there to nod home on his Premier League debut. MAN OF THE MATCH - COLE PALMER © Iconsport / David Klein / Sportimage Both sets of attackers produced impressive performances, but Palmer was certainly the pick of the bunch. Chelsea's number 10 looked at his very best today, consistently beating defenders, taking shots and creating chances, while also putting in a defensive shift. Palmer ended the game with the most completed dribbles (five), most shots (five) and three chances created, as well as registering a goal and assist. FULHAM VS. CHELSEA MATCH STATS Possession: Fulham 61%-39% Chelsea Shots: Fulham 14-18 Chelsea Shots on target: Fulham 6-6 Chelsea Corners: Fulham 6-4 Chelsea Fouls: Fulham 12-7 Chelsea BEST STATS 31 - Timed at 31 seconds, João Pedro has scored the quickest ever goal on MD1 in a Premier League season. Impression. pic.twitter.com/moYzfCa9q4 — OptaJoe (@OptaJoe) August 24, 2026 5 - Morgan Rogers has now also become the first Chelsea player to create five chances on his Premier League debut for the club on record since 2003-04. Inventive. https://t.co/GQpzBzntvC — OptaJoe (@OptaJoe) August 24, 2026 WHAT NEXT? Fulham's attention turns to the EFL Cup with a midweek match against AFC Wimbledon, before returning to Premier League action against Sunderland on Sunday. Chelsea will also appear in midweek against Luton Town in the EFL Cup second round, followed by a clash with Brighton & Hove Albion on Sunday. Arsenal transfer news: Al-Hilal 'getting closer' to finalising Gabriel Martinelli fee, Brazilian left with decision Darren Plant 24 Aug 2026 17:30 Â© Iconsport / ALLSTAR PICTURE LIBRARY, Allstar Picture Library Ltd / Alamy Arsenal and Al-Hilal are allegedly edging nearer to agreeing a deal for Gabriel Martinelli Amid speculation about his future, the long-serving Gunners player has been left out of the club's opening two squads of the season. The Premier League champions are seemingly open to cashing in on the Brazil international, rather than activating an option which would extend his contract until 2028. As well as Galatasaray, Saudi Pro League club Al-Hilal have been heavily linked with a move for the 25-year-old. According to transfer expert Fabrizio Romano , whether Martinelli moves to the Middle East could be a decision left down to him. © Imago / Sportsphoto What fee could Al-Hilal pay for Martinelli? The report alleges that a fee between £50m and £55m has been mentioned during discussions involving the two teams. Club-to-club talks are said to be in their final stages, with Arsenal ready to accept that sum of money for Martinelli. With terms between the clubs likely to be agreed, Martinelli will be left to decide whether he wants to take the opportunity to move to Saudi Arabia. Fellow winger Malcom is the only other Brazilian player in the Al-Hilal squad. A total of 62 goals and 36 assists have been contributed from 278 appearances for Arsenal in all competitions. © Iconsport / PA Images Are Arsenal right to cash in on Martinelli? Christos Tzolis has made a strong start on the left flank since his arrival from Club Brugge, something that has perhaps encouraged Arsenal to part ways with Martinelli. However, with Leandro Trossard having already left the Emirates Stadium and Martinelli having made at least 50 outings in the last two seasons, it feels like Mikel Arteta is taking a risk. Should Arsenal, as expected, choose to reinvest the money in a left-winger who they deem to be an upgrade, they will hope that he can show similar levels of availability to Martinelli over the course of a long season. articles.title: xG Report: The Weekend's Biggest Chance Creators in All Four English Divisions
articles.excerpt: Brentford created the most in England. West Ham created 3.23 expected goals at home and lost to a Charlton side who managed 0.70. The top five chance creators in every English division, plus the early Championship, League One and League Two xG tables.
articles.source_type: Head-to-head player comparison, goalkeeper and position value analysis
articles.body: Weekend xG Report: Championship, League One, League Two xG Report: The Weekend's Biggest Chance Creators in All Four English Divisions Brentford created the most in England this weekend: 3.87 expected goals against Tottenham, from a home side that scored three and could have had more. That is the headline number. The more interesting one is 3.23, which is what West Ham generated at home to Charlton in the Championship. They lost 2-1. Charlton had 0.70 xG and took all three points. That is the weekend in one fixture, and the reason this column exists. Below are the top five chance creators in each of the four English divisions, the biggest gaps between what teams deserved and what they got, and the early xG tables for the Championship, League One and League Two. The top five xG teams in every English division All figures are total expected goals from the weekend's fixtures, with the opponent's xG alongside for context. Premier League Team Scored Match Brentford 3.87 Brentford 3-0 Tottenham (0.59) Liverpool 3.64 Newcastle 2-2 Liverpool (1.27) Brighton 3.19 Brighton 4-0 Aston Villa (0.33) Manchester United 2.19 Hull City 2-0 Man Utd (0.99) Manchester City 2.13 Man City 2-1 Bournemouth (0.57) Liverpool drawing 2-2 at Newcastle having created 3.64 to their hosts' 1.27 is the sort of result that looks like a title-race wobble and reads, in the numbers, like an away performance that deserved more. United's 2.19 without a goal at Hull is the opposite problem, and one we flagged in our Gameweek 1 review Championship Team Scored Match West Ham United 3.23 West Ham 1-2 Charlton (0.70) Millwall 2.93 Millwall 3-0 Norwich (0.96) Cardiff City 2.81 Derby 2-2 Cardiff (1.88) Lincoln City 2.44 Lincoln 1-3 Portsmouth (1.39) Southampton 2.43 Southampton 3-1 Stoke (1.13) Three of those five failed to win. Lincoln lost 3-1 at home having created a full expected goal more than Portsmouth, and just outside the five, QPR drew 0-0 with Bolton having generated 2.09 xG to Bolton's 0.16 - the most lopsided chance count of the weekend anywhere in England. League One Team Scored Match Stockport County 3.01 Stockport 1-2 Blackpool (1.85) Wycombe Wanderers 2.26 Wycombe 1-1 Plymouth (0.93) Luton Town 2.19 Luton 2-2 Notts County (0.55) Huddersfield Town 2.06 MK Dons 1-1 Huddersfield (1.38) Blackpool 1.85 Stockport 1-2 Blackpool (3.01) Stockport against Blackpool was the weekend's clearest case of a game not going the way the chances did. Stockport created more than 3.0 xG at home, Blackpool created 1.85, and Blackpool won. Luton, meanwhile, drew a game in which they had four times their opponents' expected goals. League Two Team Scored Match Bristol Rovers 3.42 Bristol Rovers 5-3 Newport (0.64) Colchester United 2.48 Colchester 2-1 Oldham (0.42) York City 2.19 Rotherham 1-1 York (0.83) Exeter City 2.15 Exeter 2-0 Accrington (0.85) Crawley Town 2.10 Rochdale 1-2 Crawley (0.88) Bristol Rovers had the highest xG in the EFL and the highest score in the country, and the match still produced one of the strangest lines of the weekend: Newport scored three goals from 0.64 expected . Eight goals from a combined 4.06 xG is not a normal afternoon. The biggest gaps between chances and goals Two lists, both from this weekend, across all four divisions. Scored far more than they created Team Goals Match Newport County 0.64 Bristol Rovers 5-3 Newport Barnet 1.38 Shrewsbury 1-3 Barnet Portsmouth 1.39 Lincoln 1-3 Portsmouth Notts County 0.55 Luton 2-2 Notts County Charlton Athletic 0.70 West Ham 1-2 Charlton Created far more than they scored Team Goals Match West Ham United 3.23 West Ham 1-2 Charlton Manchester United 2.19 Hull City 2-0 Man Utd Queens Park Rangers 2.09 QPR 0-0 Bolton Walsall 2.03 Walsall 0-0 Grimsby Stockport County 3.01 Stockport 1-2 Blackpool None of this means the results were wrong. Finishing is a skill, goalkeepers have good days, and a 0.64 xG afternoon that yields three goals is a real three goals. What the gap tells you is how repeatable the performance was - and over a season, teams in the second list usually start scoring more. The early EFL xG tables Two games in. Everything below is a very small sample and should be read as a description of what has happened, not a projection of what will. Full, updating versions live at Championship xG League One xG and League Two xG The tables are ordered by expected points - what a team's chances, and the chances they gave up, were worth on average rather than what the scoreline delivered. Championship Team xGA xPts Actual pts Millwall 6.3 1.4 5.2 Middlesbrough 4.1 1.8 4.2 Wrexham 3.6 1.6 4.1 Wolves 3.6 1.6 4.1 QPR 4.1 2.4 3.9 Southampton 4.0 2.4 3.8 West Ham United 4.8 3.4 3.4 West Bromwich Albion 4.2 3.7 3.2 Millwall are the only side in the division top of both tables: most expected points, and six actual points from two games. At the other end of the same list, Charlton have six points from 1.6 expected - the largest gap in the EFL - and West Ham have one point from 3.4. League One Team xGA xPts Actual pts Sheffield Wednesday 4.5 1.4 4.6 Luton Town 3.9 2.3 3.8 Huddersfield Town 3.1 1.8 3.6 Wigan Athletic 3.7 2.9 3.4 Reading 2.8 2.2 3.2 Stockport County 4.4 3.6 3.1 Wigan are the story here: fourth on expected points and pointless. Bradford , meanwhile, sit 18th on expected points with a maximum six. League Two Team xGA xPts Actual pts Walsall 4.9 2.5 4.2 Chesterfield 4.4 2.1 4.2 Bristol Rovers 5.4 2.7 4.1 York City 4.2 2.8 3.6 Northampton Town 2.0 1.0 3.6 Crewe Alexandra 3.2 2.0 3.4 League Two is the tightest of the three. Bristol Rovers have the division's best raw xG at 5.4 but only three points; Barnet and Crewe have maximum returns from mid-table expected-points figures. How to read this, and what we are not claiming Two matches is not a sample. Our own xG pages hide their over- and under-performance callouts until every team has played six, for exactly this reason. Nothing above is a prediction. xG measures chance quality, not merit. A side that scores three from 0.64 has not got lucky in any moral sense. They have finished well, or been finished against badly. Expected points come from the chances, both ways. A team can top the xG column and sit lower on expected points because of what they conceded at the other end. The data is SportMonks team xG , imported after each round. It lands hours after full time rather than at the whistle, which is why this column runs at the start of the week rather than on Saturday night. If you want the numbers that update themselves rather than a weekend snapshot, the Championship League One and League Two xG tables refresh as each round imports, and our EFL Best Bets column uses the same underlying model.
