articles.body: Super Sub Report: Gameweek 1 Substitution Stats Super Sub Report: What Every Premier League Substitution Produced in Gameweek 1 Martin Ødegaard came off on 76 minutes against Coventry having had three shots, one of them on target, and made three tackles. Mikel Merino replaced him and had two more shots, one on target, in fourteen minutes. Between them: five shots, two on target, three tackles That pairing matters because of how Super Sub works. bet365 call it Sub On Play On, Sky Bet and Paddy Power call it Super Sub, Betfair call it Safe Sub, and on the markets it covers the principle is the same - when the player is substituted, his replacement's tally continues the line. So the figure that counts is the pair's combined total, not the starter's own. We have a full explainer on the rule and which books offer it This is the first edition of a weekly column. Every Premier League round, we take every substitution and publish what the two players produced between them. Gameweek 1 is now complete: ten matches, 90 substitutions Gameweek 1: the pairs Each cell shows what the player who came off produced, plus what his replacement produced, and the player total for the pair. These are twelve of the round's most productive pairings. Match Came off Came on Fouls Shots On target Tackles Arsenal 3-0 Coventry Martin Ødegaard (76') Mikel Merino (14m) 0 + 1 = 3 + 2 = 1 + 1 = 3 + 0 = Brentford 3-0 Tottenham Mathias Jensen (67') Yegor Yarmolyuk (23m) 3 + 1 = 2 + 1 = 1 + 0 = 2 + 2 = Brighton 4-0 Aston Villa Jack Hinshelwood (64') C. Kostoulas (26m) 0 + 0 = 3 + 2 = 2 + 0 = 2 + 1 = Everton 2-0 Crystal Palace JP. Mateta (63') J. Strand Larsen (27m) 2 + 2 = 2 + 1 = 0 + 1 = 2 + 0 = Ipswich 2-1 Sunderland Julio Enciso (71') Jack Clarke (19m) 1 + 0 = 3 + 2 = 0 + 1 = 1 + 1 = Ipswich 2-1 Sunderland Issahaku Fatawu (66') Kasey McAteer (24m) 1 + 1 = 0 + 0 = 0 + 0 = 4 + 1 = Newcastle 2-2 Liverpool Florian Wirtz (63') A. Mac Allister (27m) 0 + 0 = 3 + 0 = 1 + 0 = 1 + 2 = Brentford 3-0 Tottenham Dango Ouattara (67') Jaidon Anthony (23m) 3 + 1 = 2 + 1 = 0 + 0 = 0 + 2 = Brighton 4-0 Aston Villa Yasin Ayari (64') Costinha (26m) 2 + 0 = 2 + 2 = 0 + 1 = 0 + 1 = Nott'm Forest 0-1 Leeds Harry Wilson (66') Noah Okafor (24m) 1 + 1 = 0 + 0 = 0 + 0 = 2 + 2 = Fulham 2-3 Chelsea Oscar Bobb (67') Shea Charles (23m) 1 + 0 = 0 + 0 = 0 + 0 = 3 + 2 = Fulham 2-3 Chelsea Cole Palmer (83') Estêvão (7m) 0 + 0 = 5 + 0 = 2 + 0 = 2 + 0 = The Fatawu and Wilson rows are the ones to sit with. Neither pair troubled the goalkeeper at all, and both produced a healthy tackle count - a reminder that the volume in these markets is defensive far more often than it is attacking. The last row is the counter-example, and it is just as important. Cole Palmer had five shots and two on target before being taken off on 83 minutes at Craven Cottage. Estêvão came on for the closing seven minutes and added nothing to any of the four columns. A replacement is only worth what his minutes allow, and seven of them are worth very little. How often the pair got somewhere the starter did not A second way of reading the same 90 substitutions. For each standard line, how many times did the player who came off finish below it, and how many times did the pair's combined total reach it anyway? Line Starter finished below it Pair total reached it 2+ tackles 3+ tackles 2+ fouls 1+ foul 3+ shots 1+ shot 1+ shot on target 1+ tackle 2+ shots 2+ shots on target That is 100 times across the round, at the time of writing, that a pair's combined figure landed on the right side of a standard line when the starter's own did not. Read the narrow version and it sharpens. Take only the players who came off exactly one short: on 2+ tackles that happened 37 times and the replacement supplied the missing tackle in 14 of them, and on 3+ shots it happened 18 times and the replacement supplied the shot in 8. The market that behaves differently is shots on target. Fifty-nine players came off without one; nine had a replacement who managed one. And on the harder 2+ line, 83 starters finished below it and the replacement got the pair there just twice. It is simply a rarer event to ask of somebody with 25 minutes, which is worth knowing before you decide the rule is worth more than it is. The busiest cameos Substitutes who put up numbers without any help from the man they replaced: Joe Willock (34 mins, Newcastle) - a shot, one on target, two tackles and two fouls. The most complete cameo of the round. Yéremy Pino (35 mins, Crystal Palace) - two shots, two tackles, a foul. Evann Guessand (27 mins, Crystal Palace) - a shot on target, a tackle, two fouls. Anan Khalaili (35 mins, Crystal Palace) - four tackles , more than most starters managed. Mikel Merino (14 mins, Arsenal) - two shots, one on target, in a quarter of an hour. Crystal Palace appear three times. Two down at Goodison, they changed things early and their substitutes chased the game - which is the game-state effect in miniature, and a reminder that what a replacement does is shaped by the scoreline he walks into. What to watch in Gameweek 2 Volume markets carry the effect. Tackles and fouls account for 64 of the 100 threshold crossings above. Shots on target account for eleven. Time on the pitch is the lever. The replacements who put up numbers here mostly had 20 minutes or more. A change on 85 minutes rarely moves anything. The bench decides it. A holding midfielder replaced by another holding midfielder keeps a tackle count ticking. Replaced by a striker because the team is chasing, it stops - and the shot count starts instead. It can go the other way. If the player is his side's best tackler, nobody replacing him matches that rate, and the pair's total grows more slowly than his own would have. The explainer works through that case. Our player projections and the Bet Builder tool model a player's own expected output, which is the right thing to model for an ordinary market and an incomplete picture on one where a replacement's numbers are added to his. What this column does and does not tell you These are match statistics, not bet settlements. Everything above is what players did on a pitch. We do not know which lines a bookmaker offered, whether anybody backed them, whether Super Sub applied to that market, or how any individual bet was settled. Nothing here should be read as a bet won or lost. Market coverage belongs to the bookmaker. Which markets and competitions carry the rule varies by operator and can change. Check the operator's own terms. The numbers move after the match. Provider stat corrections land for days, and they move in both directions. Between two runs of the same query a tackle was added to the Brighton game, and a shot on target came off another, taking the 2+ shots on target count down from three to two. Treat every total here as a snapshot. Updated for the full round. This edition first published with nine matches, before Fulham v Chelsea had been played, and now covers all ten. From Gameweek 2 the column runs on the Tuesday, once the round is complete. Lines overlap. A pair reaching 1+ tackles may also reach 2+. The 100 counts thresholds, not bets. 18+. articles.title: Three Players Who Just Became Very FPL Relevant

articles.body: Three Players Who Just Became Very FPL Relevant Three Players Who Just Became Very FPL Relevant The opening weekend of an FPL season is where template squads meet reality. Erling Haaland, in seven out of ten teams, did not score. Three players owned by barely anyone did. Here are the three whose weekend actually changes something, with what they cost and how many managers already have them. Ownership and prices are from the Statz FPL data at the time of writing. Anton Stach, Leeds, £6.0m, 1.2% owned Stach scored the only goal at the City Ground, winning Leeds the round's sole away victory against a Forest side the model made 44.8% favourites. We flagged him before the season started: in our FPL coverage he was the deep cut, a top-12 projected player in the entire game at £6.0m with ownership that rounded to nobody. That case has not weakened. A midfielder at that price who takes set pieces and arrives in the box is the definition of an FPL differential, and 1.2% ownership means his goals move your rank rather than keeping you level. Jack Hinshelwood, Brighton, £6.0m, 0.9% owned Two goals in a 4-0 win, in a Brighton side missing Baleba, Mitoma and Ferguson. That last part is the important part: Hinshelwood's route into the team came from an injury list, and the question every FPL manager now has to answer is what happens when those three are fit. At £6.0m and under 1% ownership he is the sort of pick that wins you a gameweek. Whether he holds the shirt into September is a different question, and the predicted line-ups will answer it before the deadline rather than after. Maxim De Cuyper, Brighton, £4.5m, 2.7% owned The one that matters most, because of the price. A £4.5m defender who scored and kept a clean sheet in the same afternoon is exactly the profile our budget enablers guide was written about: the cheap slot that quietly funds a premium elsewhere while contributing points of its own. The honest caveat One gameweek is one gameweek. Two of these three owe their minutes at least partly to somebody else's injury, and a single haul is not a projection. The way to judge them is the same as it was in July: look at the expected minutes first and the points second. The Statz Season Rankings model both across all 38 gameweeks, and the Team Planner will tell you what any of them is projected to add to your specific squad rather than to a hypothetical one. articles.body: FPL Gameweek 1 Review and Takeaways - Don’t Overreact - Full90 FPL Skip to content FPL Gameweek 1 Review and Takeaways - Don’t Overreact The FPL General picked the wrong season to go without the two-mium. If he had started without Haaland and Bruno Fernandes this season he would be laughing. And that kind of summarises gameweek 1. Outside of the Arsenal picks, and Szoboszlai nobody owned by more than 25% of managers returned. If Pedro doesn’t return tomorrow this will have been one of those good weeks to have a bad week. So, I can’t be too upset to be on 46 points all out. Though obviously I am frustrated, I am trying not to overreact to anything. Just look how crazy some of the opening day results are based on our pre-season expectations. We know almost nothing. If you had a plan coming into this season, stick to it. As most of the PL teams now know, stability matters… Don’t Overreact The clear caveat is that this is still only one week’s worth of information I am going to do some conjecture with it. We will likely see in a couple of weeks what is the “truth.” I’m writing this at the top so that I don’t have to say “we will see” after every statement. Just remember, Reijnders looked like the next De Bruyne after gw1 last season… Did Bench Boost 1 Work? Well, it wasn’t great for me but it was fine and I am happy it’s done. I got 9 points which is about the minimum you expect. Joe smashed it with 18 points though – good for him, the little bastard. Match-By-Match Reviews I watched 4 games this weekend and the highlights for the rest. I’ve also reviewed all the stats so we can see who was lucky and who wasn’t. Arsenal 3-0 Coventry xG 1.88-0.20 Arsenal Smash Coventry The first game of the season was a bloodbath. It was hard to tell whether Arsenal were just elite or Coventry were just dreadful. I suspect a bit of both. On xG, it was only 1.88-0.20 so maybe we shouldn’t read too much into this. But it’s hard not to when you add this performance to the Community Shield performance – Arsenal’s attack was just way better than I remember it being last season. Partly that is down to newboy Tzolis who had 4 shots for 0.19 xG and 3 key passes for 0.14 xA – if you watched the game you’ll be shocked about how low that is because he looked electric. He was even stepping into a sort of second striker role when Arsenal worked the ball down the right, which they frequently do when Saka is playing. He didn’t make a full 90, getting hooked at 76 mins for Eze which is a bit of a concern. My conclusion on him is this then, if you picked him then it was a good one but I am not desperate to get him in right now. That’s pretty much how I feel about Odegaard too who also put up 3 key passes for 0.1 xA and 3 shots for 0.21 xG. The thing about Ode is that he is so involved in everything that he takes the bonus points too. But he also went off at 76 mins for Merino As expected, neither Saka nor Rice made it much past 65 mins. Until they play a 90, I just don’t think we can go there. In defence, they looked solid of course. None of them got DefCons but Coventry were really bad so I’m not surprised. Of course Cala got the goal and was a good pick but it didn’t help my nerves about rotation when he went off before 90. Are Coventry Fucked? As for Coventry, I think they were really, really shit. I know that Arsenal were the winners of the Premier league last year but that was some weak, pathetic shit we saw from Coventry. It’s probably not an original thought to say I don’t think that Lampard is a great coach but this terrible performance reminded me. Thomas got defcons at least. Hull City 2-0 Man United xG 1.01-1.83 Disastrous Start for Man United In complete contrast to Coventry, Hull looked properly up for this game. If you watched the highlights you’d be forgiven for thinking that Hull dominated but United were better on xG and put up 21 shots to Hulls 8 shots. But still. Cunha started up top and had 3 shots for 0.24 xG and 2 key passes for 0.21 xA. He was hooked after 80 mins. Mbeumo put up 4 shots for 0.5xG and 0.23 xA and lasted the full 90 mins. Dorgu started left wing and put up 0.47 xG from three shots in a single half before being replaced with Rashford who didn’t get a single shot off. Sesko played 23 mins and only got 1 shot off for 0.04 xG. Bruno Fernandes put up 3 shots for 0.08 xG – all from miles outside the box – and 3 key passes for 0.26 xA. A lot of these guys then outperformed the Arsenal boys on underlyings but just failed to actually put the ball in the net. They lacked a lot of energy and just seemed to be so slow – letting Hull grab the ball far too often. I don’t think we should worry too much about Mbeumo and Bruno – they both played 90 and put up reasonable numbers. But, I am a little worried about how much depth Man United have because that means that any of these guys, besides maybe Bruno, could get hooked before 90 and we really want 90 mins. None of the back line got close to defensive contribution points and they were obviously not that great either. Perfect Premier League Start for Hull Realistically, I can’t see us going for any Hull assets regularly but I want to call out two interesting players. Firstly, Slater took corners and set pieces for only 4.5 – he could be a great pick for that 8th attacker slot that just sits on your bench. Obviously he also got an assist. Secondly, McBurnie had two shots in the first 20 mins, and was pretty unfortunate not to get a goal in my opinion. Again, he’s a rotation option (or Draft option). Included here, plus the mid-season refresh The Midweek Fixture No ads Across the whole site and every tool, while you are a member Still free for everyone: the fixture ticker Ipswich 2-1 Sunderland xG 1.80-0.66 Ipswich Catch the Black Cats Napping Literally. The first goal was a fantastic counter-attack that saw Enciso drive forward and assist Emersonn who put up 0.82 xG from 3 shots in just 66 mins. Enciso went off injured and Jack Clarke came on and scored the second. O’Shea got 18 defensive contributions from right back and Nunez got 12 defcons in 80 mins. Sunderland confirm fears? I said multiple times coming into the season that I was worried about these guys – they’re underlying numbers suggest they were pretty poor last season, potentially this result confirms those fears. However, they did most of their good work at home so maybe not. Angulo took the free-kick for the goal and it was brilliant. But that was about all he did and he only lasted 59 mins. Brobbey had 2 shots for 0.3 xG but was taken off after 67 mins. Le Fee did basically nothing and got subbed at 80 mins. My hero Granit Xhaka got defcon points and an assist after being fouled for the free kick. Ballard narrowly missed out on defcon points and O’Nien was replaced on 67 mins. Brentford 3-0 Spurs xG 3.87-0.57 Spurs Still Suck We’ve just reviewed all the promoted teams and NONE of them conceded this much in terms of xG. They conceded 26 shots. 26! It was an almost completely new backline of Robertson, Senesi, van Hecke and Gray – Robbo and Senesi got defcon points and van Hecke was only 1 away from getting the points. But obviously, they conceded 3 times… And, as you can tell from the expected numbers, they were woeful going forward. Their attack is a hard avoid at the moment. Brentford’s Stability Prevails 10 of Brentford’s players were regulars from last season. Schade smashed Dango out of the water in terms of underlying numbers – 0.52 xG from 5 shots v.s. 0.05 xG from 2 shots. The latter was subbed off after 67 mins for Anthony top cap off basically every Dango owner’s fear come true. In a rare turn of events, Thiago hit the post with a pen to finish with no returns from an xG of 1.0. There was only one newbie to Brentford’s team and he absolutely smashed his debut. Sangare got defcons, one real assist and one FPL one. He was great but it is worth noting his xA was only 0.33. At the back, Ajer got DefCons but might not keep his spot when van den Berg is back. Kayode had 4 shots for 0.5 xG and walked away with a goal. Lewis-Potter played left-back and scored from his 2 shots and 0.77xG. Everton 2-0 Palace xG: 1.12-1.96 Everton Ride Their Luck A bit like last season then. They somehow give up a tonne of xG but walk away with a clean sheet. Nobody got defensive contribution points but Tarkowski was only one off and Branthwaite was only two off. Ndiaye was the best 6.0 going into this week because he got a full 90 and an assist. Dewsbury-Hall scored off 0.12 xG and Barry scored off two shots and 0.45 xG. Palace Falter The big news is that Ismalia Sarr didn’t even make the starting lineup after Galatassaray made a bid for him. Munoz was still in the team (despite the transfer rumours around him). He had a couple of shots in the first half but was subbed at 55 mins. Richards, Wharton, and Kamada all walked away with DefCon Points. As expected, Mateta didn’t play 90 and was subbed at 63 mins for Strand Larsen after two shots for 0.70 xG. Man City 2 – 1 Bournemouth xG: 2.36-0.63 Maresca’s Fifa Career Enzo Maresca is playing Fifa. Either that, or he’s taking tips from Thomas Tuchel. By my count, he started six defenders – with Guehi playing DM and O’Reilly playing in the 10. Foden was playing on the right-wing which I think was also weird. The goal they conceded didn’t do anything to convince me that the defensive frailties witnessed in the Community Shield were a one-off. As if they wanted to make City feel better for being bad in defence, Bournemouth left Guehi open whilst two of them wrestled Ruben Semenyo was the only midfielder to make 90 mins and he switched from the left to the right when Grealish came on for Foden on the 82nd minute. Cherki got the assist after coming on got O’Reilly in the 63rd minute. He found Gvardiol in the box basically playing second striker which is REALLY interesting if he can lock down a starting spot. Of course, Haaland blanked which basically meant that nobody got a return from their captain in gameweek 1 Bournemouth Brilliant? Well. No. Not really. They looked competent and good, like they normally do. But they didn’t create that much and relied on counter-attacking. Evanilson got the assist to the goal but didn’t get a shot off. Tavernier was the one who scored and the only one of the front four to make it to 90 mins. Silva got defensive contributions. Brighton 4 – 0 Villa xG: 3.67-0.31 Villa Are In Trouble The xG numbers show that the final scoreline doesn’t lie. Villa were shit. It’s probably not escaped your attention that they have been gutted by transfers out but I expected that Emery would just pull something out of the bag and put on a decent performance, even if they lost. Well that was wrong. Watkins must be on his way out because I don’t see any good reason not to start him. That hopefully will make Jackson a good pick if he goes over there. Brighton Actually Brilliant 21 shots, 6 big chances, 3.67 xG and a 4-0 win against an Emery team. Hats off to them. None of them got close to defcon points but that’s probably not a shock given how bad Villa were. Rutter started at striker but I’d still be nervous about going there until the transfer window closes. Hinshelwood got two goals from 3 shots for 1.41 xG. He was quite overlooked before the season began, including from me, despite how high many of us were on him at the end of last season. De Cuyper played on the wing which is interesting if that carries on. Gross did nothing which made me happy and most man

articles.title: Elche vs Barcelona Predictions and Betting Tips - La Liga
articles.excerpt: Barcelona are the model's champions and they visit a side projected to spend the season in the survival scrap. Every price in the game reflects that, and then some.
articles.source_type: Head-to-head player comparison, goalkeeper and position value analysis
articles.body: Elche vs Barcelona Predictions & Betting Tips Elche vs Barcelona Predictions and Betting Tips - La Liga Barcelona start the season as the model's champions: 53.8% in our La Liga projection , the best attack in the division, and a first assignment at Elche, who the same model expects to spend the year in a six-club scrap to stay up. You know how this is supposed to go. So does the market, which is the problem with betting on it. Kickoff is 8:30pm UK on Sunday. Numbers from the live Statz match centre Lineups and Player News As with all La Liga fixtures, Statz does not publish a predicted XI the way it does for the Premier League, so the names below are the players our props board expects to be involved rather than a confirmed team sheet. Barcelona 's expected group includes Joan García in goal, Koundé, Eric García and Balde across the back, Marc Bernal and Fermín López in midfield, with Lamine Yamal and Raphinha providing the width. Elche are expected to feature Dituro, Affengruber, Chust, Sangaré and Valera. No confirmed absences have been published for either side at the time of writing. Recent Form Barcelona's closing five read WWLWL, Elche's DLWDD. The projections are emphatic: 2.21 goals to 1.00, with Elche given a 10.9% chance of a clean sheet , one of the lowest numbers on the weekend's board anywhere in Europe. Barcelona win this in 64.3% of simulations. Elche take it in 15.2%, which is a bigger number than a 9.00 price suggests. Statz Team Projections See the live Statz numbers for this fixture Interesting Player Stats Marc Bernal to be carded at 3.75 is the standout, and it is not close: a 32.3% projection is the highest on either side's board. A young midfielder holding the middle of the pitch while his side chases the ball for long spells is a booking waiting to happen, and Elche will be running at him. Eric García at 5.50 is the same argument at a bigger price. Beyond that the board leans on fouls markets from our commentary-parsed data, which are noisier than the cards and shots lines and are worth treating as softer evidence. Statz Bet Builder See the live Statz numbers for this fixture Betting Angles Barcelona at 1.30 implies a 77% chance. The model says 64.3%. Over 2.5 at 1.44 implies 69% against a 62.3% projection. Both teams to score at 1.75 is the closest thing to a fair price in the game, and even that is a shade the wrong side of the line. Which leaves one number the model genuinely likes, and it is the one nobody wants: Elche at 9.00 , where a 15.2% chance is being sold as an 11.1% one. That is a real edge on a bet that loses six times out of seven. Summary The bet: no bet on the result, and a small one on Elche at 9.00 if you must. I am not going to talk you into a 9.00 shot on the opening weekend, and I am certainly not going to talk you into 1.30 about a side that lost two of its last five. Some games are priced so that the honest answer is to watch them. If you want an angle rather than a bet, Marc Bernal's card at 3.75 is the soundest number on the board and has nothing to do with who wins. articles.title: Espanyol vs Real Madrid Predictions and Betting Tips - La Liga
articles.excerpt: Real Madrid start a title chase they cannot afford to drift through, away at Espanyol on Saturday night. The model likes them. It likes the price a good deal less.
articles.source_type: Head-to-head player comparison, goalkeeper and position value analysis
articles.body: Espanyol vs Real Madrid Predictions & Betting Tips Espanyol vs Real Madrid Predictions and Betting Tips - La Liga Real Madrid begin a season in which second place will not be forgiven. Our La Liga preview has them winning the title in 39.3% of simulations against Barcelona's 53.8%, a gap of less than two projected points across 38 games. In a race that tight, a Saturday night in Cornella is not a warm-up. It is one of the 38 games that decides it. Espanyol are the sort of opponent that has quietly ruined title bids before: awkward, at home, with nothing expected of them. The model gives them 18.1%, which is more than you might think. Kickoff is 8:30pm UK. Numbers from the live Statz match centre Lineups and Player News Statz does not publish predicted line-ups for La Liga the way it does for the Premier League, so treat the names below as the players our props board expects to be involved rather than a confirmed team sheet. On that basis Real Madrid 's expected group is built around Courtois in goal, a back line featuring Alexander-Arnold, Huijsen, Konaté and Cucurella, with Valverde and Güler in midfield and Mbappé and Vinícius Júnior ahead of them. Espanyol 's side is expected to include Riedel, Expósito, Núñez and Álvaro Calatrava. No confirmed absences have been published for either side at the time of writing. Recent Form Madrid closed last season WLWWW, Espanyol LWWDW at home. The projections split them clearly: 1.86 goals to 0.95, with Madrid given a 38.8% clean sheet against Espanyol's 15.6%. That is a comfortable enough read, and it is worth holding onto the gap between it and the price. A 57.9% chance is not the same thing as a formality. Statz Team Projections See the live Statz numbers for this fixture Interesting Player Stats The pick of the board belongs to the home side. Álvaro Calatrava 1+ shot on target at 2.10 carries a 50.8% projection and a last-five line of two, three, zero, two and four. Espanyol will not see much of the ball, but he is the man they aim at when they get it, and a shade over evens for a player who has hit the target in four of his last five is the most sensible number in this match. The braver version is his 2+ at 7.00. For Madrid, Trent Alexander-Arnold to be carded at 5.50 (21.3%) is the one the model rates, and Dean Huijsen at 4.50 carries the higher projection at 25.9% - centre-backs against a side that will be countering all night. Statz Bet Builder See the live Statz numbers for this fixture Betting Angles Here is the thing about this game: the market has taken it away from you. Real Madrid at 1.44 implies a 69% chance. The model says 57.9%. That is not a small disagreement, and it is the wrong way round for anyone wanting to back the favourite. The goals markets are no kinder. Over 2.5 at 1.62 implies nearly 62% against a projection of 53.2%. The only two prices on the board that the model actually rates are under 2.5 goals at 2.30 (46.8% against an implied 43.5%) and Espanyol at 7.00, where an 18.1% chance is priced as a 14.3% one. Summary The bet: Under 2.5 goals at 2.30. Madrid should win. They will probably win without ever going through the gears, which is precisely the shape of game that finishes 2-0 rather than 4-1, and the under is the one price here that the model prefers to the market's version of it. If you want the lottery ticket, Espanyol at 7.00 is genuinely underpriced by the model's reckoning. Just do not confuse underpriced with likely. articles.title: The FPL Team Planner That Does Your Homework For You: Import, Project, Optimise
articles.excerpt: Every FPL manager runs the same loop: check fixtures, second-guess transfers, wonder if the armband is right. The Statz Team Planner runs that loop for you - import your real squad in seconds, see projected points on every player for the next six gameweeks, and let the optimiser propose transfer plans with the reasoning attached. Here's everything it does.
articles.source_type: Head-to-head player comparison, goalkeeper and position value analysis
articles.body: FPL Team Planner - Import Your Squad & Optimise Transfers The FPL Team Planner That Does Your Homework For You: Import, Project, Optimise Every FPL manager runs the same weekly loop. Check the fixtures. Second-guess two transfers. Wonder whether the captaincy is right. Do it all in your head, on a bus, four minutes before the deadline. The Statz FPL Team Planner exists to run that loop properly: your actual squad, projected points on every player, fixtures for the run ahead, and an optimiser that proposes your next moves - with its reasoning shown. It's the piece of the Statz FPL toolkit that ties everything else together, and this is the full tour: what it does, how the optimiser thinks, and why the managers using it are making decisions with numbers the official app simply doesn't have. Get your squad in, in seconds Three ways in, no typing your team out player by player. Enter your FPL Team ID and the planner pulls your real squad, bank and chips. Start from scratch if you're planning a draft. Or - the party trick - upload a screenshot of your team from the official app, and the planner reads the players off the image and rebuilds your squad automatically. Once you're in, your squad, transfers and plans save to your account, so the plan you sketch on your laptop is waiting on your phone at the deadline. The pitch view: your team, with the numbers switched on The planner's home screen looks like your team - a proper pitch, shirts, bench - but every player carries the number the official app never shows: projected points for the gameweek , from the same Statz model behind the Season Rankings . The header runs the totals for you: your bank, free transfers, a Team Rating out of 100 , and your squad's total projected points for the gameweek. The pitch view: projected points on every shirt, captaincy marked, and your gameweek total in the header. Step forward through the gameweeks with the arrows and the whole squad re-projects against each week's fixtures - so "should I hold this transfer?" becomes a question you can answer by looking. Chips live in the header too, so a Wildcard or Bench Boost can be planned into a specific week rather than panic-played. And the camera button exports your squad as a shareable image for the group chat. The transfer market, sorted by what actually matters The Players panel is a transfer shortlist with projections built in: search anyone, filter by position, club or price, and sort by projected points over the next six gameweeks rather than last season's totals. One column tells you what a player is likely to do for the week ahead; the six-gameweek column tells you what he's worth across the run - which is the number transfers should actually be bought on. The player market, sorted by six-gameweek projected points - the number a transfer should be judged on. Fixtures as a heatmap, three ways The Fixtures tab turns the run-in into a heatmap you can read at a glance, with a gameweek range slider and three modes: projected goals per fixture, clean sheet percentage , and classic FPL FDR if you want the official difficulty view. Totals rank every club across your chosen window, so "whose fixtures turn?" stops being folklore and becomes a sorted column. The fixtures heatmap in projected-goals mode: every club's run, quantified and ranked over your chosen gameweeks. Optimise: the feature that earns the bookmark Then there's the button that separates this from every fixture ticker and rate-my-team thread: Optimise . It works in two modes. Starting fresh - or holding a wildcard - it builds the best £100m squad for the next six gameweeks outright, with its projected total attached, and loads it straight onto your pitch to tweak. With your real squad in, it proposes a concrete transfer plan instead: which players out, which in, in which gameweek, whether a points hit is worth taking, and what the whole package is projected to gain. Draft mode: the optimiser's best £100m squad for the opening six gameweeks, projected total attached, one tap to load. Two things make it trustworthy rather than a black box. First, every move shows its working : the incoming and outgoing player's projected points for each of the next six fixtures, side by side, with captaincy-ceiling weeks flagged. Second, the "Why these moves?" panel says it in plain English - a fixture swing, a captaincy upgrade, value released from the bank - and the arithmetic is printed at the bottom: points in, points out, minus any hit, equals the net gain. Agree with it and one tap applies the plan; disagree and you've still learned exactly where the model thinks your squad is leaking points. Plans, leagues and the weekly routine Everything you sketch saves as a Plan - so you can keep a safe route and an aggressive route side by side and decide on deadline day, with an undo button for every experiment along the way. The Leagues tab brings your mini-league into the planner, because half of FPL is knowing what the manager above you is likely to do next. Under the hood it's the same engine as the rest of the toolkit: projections built on expected minutes first (the Season Rankings model), refreshed as new data lands, sharpened by the predicted line-ups behind Team News . The planner is where those numbers stop being a leaderboard and start being your decisions: fifteen minutes a week, squad in front of you, projections on every option. The planner is free to try with your own squad at statz.ai/fpl/my-team - full projections and the optimiser are part of FPL Pro FAQs What is the Statz FPL Team Planner? A squad-planning tool at statz.ai/fpl/my-team that loads your real FPL team and adds what the official app doesn't have: projected points on every player, multi-gameweek fixture heatmaps, chip planning, saved transfer plans and an optimiser that proposes your next moves with the reasoning shown. How do I import my FPL team into the planner? Three ways: enter your FPL Team ID and it pulls your squad automatically, build a squad from scratch, or upload a screenshot of your team from the official app and the planner reads your players off the image. What does the FPL optimiser do? It analyses your squad, bank, free transfers and the projections for the coming gameweeks, then proposes specific transfers - including when a points hit is worth it - showing the six-gameweek projection for every player in and out, plus a plain-English explanation and the net expected points gain. Is the FPL Team Planner free? Importing and building your squad is free with a Statz account. Full player projections and the optimiser are part of FPL Pro. articles.body: Newcastle vs Liverpool Predictions & Betting Tips - PL Gameweek 1 Newcastle vs Liverpool Predictions and Betting Tips - Premier League Football rarely writes a script this neatly. Alexander Isak, the striker Newcastle turned into one of the most valuable players in Europe, walks back into St James' Park on Sunday afternoon wearing a Liverpool shirt. Whatever the reception is, it will not be muted. Underneath the noise is the best fixture of the weekend and the model's strongest goals call of the round. Liverpool are favourites, but only just, and both defences look considerably less trustworthy than either club would like. Kickoff is 4:30pm UK, live on Sky. Numbers from the live Statz match centre Lineups and Player News Liverpool's front four is frightening and their treatment room is fuller: seven players are out , including Ekitiké, Bradley, Gomez, Leoni and Bajcetic. Wirtz, Szoboszlai and Gakpo line up behind Isak, with Van Dijk marshalling a back line that has Frimpong and Kerkez as its full-backs. Newcastle's rebuilt side tells the story of their summer. Our season preview has them projected twelfth after sales reported beyond £240m, and the XI hands starts to Bamba, Ramsey and William Osula. Livramento is a doubt, Miley is out. Newcastle predicted XI (4-3-3): Horníček; Burn, Botman, Thiaw, Hall; Bamba, J.Ramsey, Joelinton; Barnes, Elanga, Osula. Liverpool predicted XI (4-2-3-1): A.Becker; Kerkez, Virgil, Araujo, Frimpong; Mac Allister, Gravenberch; Gakpo, Wirtz, Szoboszlai; Isak. Recent Form Neither side arrives in form: Liverpool WLDLD, Newcastle LWDWL. The projections are close, 1.55 goals to 1.35 in Liverpool's favour, and the clean-sheet numbers are the interesting part - 25.9% and 21.2% , both weak, in a game that will be played at a hundred miles an hour. Statz Team Projections See the live Statz numbers for this fixture Interesting Player Stats The pick of the board is Dominik Szoboszlai to be carded at 4.75 , a 25.9% chance in a fixture with this temperature. He is the Liverpool midfielder most likely to be chasing the game physically, and referees rarely get through this fixture without reaching for a pocket. If you would rather back a shot than a card, William Osula's 2+ shots on target at 4.50 carries a 25.3% projection, and he has hit two in two of his last five. Isak, inevitably, is priced as though he will score, and there is no value left in it. Statz Bet Builder See the live Statz numbers for this fixture Betting Angles Liverpool at 1.90 is a shade shorter than the model's 40.7% strictly earns. The market is paying for the front four and ignoring a bench that has been gutted by injuries. The number that shouts is both teams to score at 58.4% (1.44 at the time of writing), the strongest BTTS call of the entire round. Two soft defensive projections, two sides who will attack each other, and a crowd that will demand Newcastle throw everything at the man who left. Summary The bet: Both teams to score at 1.44. The game of the weekend, and the clearest goals game on the coupon. Liverpool are probably the better side, even with seven players missing, but this is not an afternoon for control. Isak will get his moment, one way or another. So, I suspect, will Newcastle. articles.body: Man City vs B'mouth Predictions & Betting Tips - PL Gameweek 1 Man City vs Bournemouth Predictions and Betting Tips - Premier League Spare a thought for Bournemouth. Numbers from the live Statz match centre Lineups and Player News City's summer rebuild is on display: Gianluigi Donnarumma in goal for his home debut, Marc Guéhi alongside Rúben Dias, and Antoine Semenyo joining Doku and Foden behind Haaland. Rodrigo is out and Grealish is a doubt. Bournemouth are missing three squad players plus the suspended Christie, which is not what you want before a trip to the Etihad. The projections are brutal: 2.29 goals to 1.01, clean sheets 36.4% against 10.2%. Statz Team Projections See the live Statz numbers for this fixture Interesting Player Stats The board for this fixture is thinner than you would expect, largely because the market has already priced City's stars into oblivion. Among the starters, Elliot Anderson 2+ shots at 2.10 is the one worth a look on a 49.4% projection - a summer signing the model rates as a top-ten player in the whole game, in a match City will spend camped in the opposition half. Phil Foden to be carded at 10.00 appears on the value list but has not been booked in any of his last five, which tells you what the model thinks of it. Statz Bet Builder See the live Statz numbers for this fixture Betting Angles City at 1.48 for a 64.9% chance is fair rather than generous, and short prices about teams with Community Shield rust and a World Cup summer behind them are not where I want to be. The goals number is the bet. Over 2.5 at 64% (1.44 at the time of writing) is the model's strongest call anywhere on the round, and the logic is not complicated: City will score, Bournemouth's shot map says they will have their moments on the break, and neither of those things stops after the opening goal. Summary The bet: Over 2.5 goals at 1.44. City by two is the likeliest outcome and the market knows it. The value is in the total, not the result. Bournemouth will get a couple of chances on the counter, because everyone does at the Etihad, and City will keep going long after the game is won. articles.body: Brentford vs Spurs Predictions & Betting Tips - PL Gameweek 1 Brentford vs Tottenham Predictions and Betting Tips - Premier League New managers get honeymoons. They rarely get them at Brentford. Roberto De Zerbi takes charge of his first Premier League game for Tottenham on Saturday teatime, at a ground where visiting sides with grand plans have been getting bullied for years. Spurs closed last season in their best form of the campaign and the market has priced in a good chunk of optimism about the new era. The model has not: it still leans Brentford, at 41.3% against 30.2%. Kickoff is 5:30pm UK, live on Sky. Numbers from the live Statz match centre Lineups and Player News Brentford are close to full strength, with only Milambo doubtful, and line up as you would expect: Kelleher behind a settled back four, Thiago leading the line, Damsgaard pulling the strings. Spurs are the unknown. Kulusevski, Xavi Simons and Odobert are all out , with Kudus a doubt, and our team news desk expects De Zerbi to go with three at the back given the centre-back depth available to him, with Tonali and Fernandes in the engine room and one of Tel or Maddison supporting Solanke. That is a lot of new information to process in one afternoon. Brentford predicted XI (4-2-3-1): Kelleher; Hickey, Collins, Ajer, Kayode; Sangaré, Jensen; Anthony, Damsgaard, O.Dango; Thiago. Spurs predicted XI (3-5-2): Kinsky; Van de Ven, Senesi, Van Hecke; Udogie, Gallagher, Fernandes, Tonali, Pedro Porro; Solanke, Maddison. Recent Form Spurs' closing WWDLW is the better recent line, but the model still favours Brentford at home: 1.49 projected goals to 1.25, and a 28.8% clean sheet to 22.6%. A brand new system cuts both ways, and Brentford's team-strength numbers have always held up in this fixture. Statz Team Projections See the live Statz numbers for this fixture Interesting Player Stats The props board here is thin, which is itself worth knowing. Among the starters, Aaron Hickey 1+ shot at 2.00 is the one the model likes, on a 55.5% projection, with Brentford's wing-backs getting forward relentlessly against a Spurs shape nobody has seen yet. Michael Oliver takes charge, and his games run hot: 27.5 fouls and 4.25 cards a game . Mika Kayode's fouls-drawn line at 2.75 reflects that, though fouls come from our commentary data and are noisier than shots. Statz Bet Builder See the live Statz numbers for this fixture Betting Angles Brentford at 2.40 sits a shade under the model's 41.3%, so there is a small edge on the home win if you want it. I understand the temptation to oppose a brand new system on day one. The firmer call is both teams to score at 55.2% (1.57 at the time of writing), the second-strongest BTTS number of the round. Two attacking sides, a referee who lets the game breathe, and a Spurs back three still learning each other's habits. Summary The bet: Both teams to score at 1.57. De Zerbi's Spurs will be worth watching by October. Whether they are worth backing in their first away game, in a tight ground, against a side built to punish exactly this kind of afternoon, is another question entirely. Brentford at 2.40 is defensible. Goals at both ends is the bet I actually want. articles.title: Wilfried gnonto joins acf fiorentina on loan
articles.source_type: Manager fitness updates, injury detail and expected return timelines
articles.body: Wilfried Gnonto joins ACF Fiorentina on loan - Leeds United Previous Mens Wilfried Gnonto joins ACF Fiorentina on loan 01 Sep 26 Forward heads to the Serie A. Share Leeds United can confirm Wilfried Gnonto has joined ACF Fiorentina on loan until the end of the 2026/27 season. The forward links up with the Serie A side on a temporary basis and in doing so returns to his home nation of Italy, having left in 2020. Gnonto joined the Whites in August 2022 and has been a regular member of the squad since arriving, amassing just short of 150 appearances for the club. A hugely popular member of the team, Willy played a key role in helping the club to achieve promotion back to the Premier League in the 2024/25 campaign, scoring nine goals and grabbing six assists as the Whites lifted the Sky Bet Championship trophy. Last term, the Italy international made 29 appearances across all competitions, helping United retain their Premier League status and reach the semi-finals of the Emirates FA Cup. Gnonto heads to a Fiorentina side who will be looking to improve on last season’s 15th-place finish in Serie A under the newly appointed Fabio Grosso. In the previous campaign, the Viola also reached the semi-finals of the UEFA Conference League. Willy now heads out on loan with the best wishes of everyone at Elland Road during his time in Florence and we look forward to seeing his progress while away from the club. articles.body: Match Officials Appointed: Brighton (A) - Leeds United Previous Next Matchday Match Officials Appointed: Brighton (A) 02 Sep 26 Appointments confirmed. Share The match officials for Saturday’s Premier League meeting with Brighton have been announced, with Stuart Attwell set to take charge at the Amex. The 43-year-old began the new campaign with a UEFA Conference League Qualifying tie between Qarabağ and Dynamo Kyiv before overseeing the dramatic late draw between Newcastle United and Liverpool on the Premier League’s opening weekend. Vastly experienced at the top of the game, Attwell has refereed 244 Premier League games and was in the middle for the 2025 FA Cup Final. The Whites have a mixed record from their 25 fixtures to involve Attwell, winning 12 of those and drawing on three occasions. Three of those fixtures came last term, including a memorable 2-1 home victory over West Ham United at Elland Road that brought goals from Brenden Aaronson and Joe Rodon. Brighton, meanwhile, have won 13 of 31 matches officiated by the Warwickshire-based referee, losing 10 times. Most recently, the Seagulls drew 2-2 with Tottenham towards the end of the previous season. Running the touchlines are Constantine Hatzidakis and Nick Hopton with John Busby appointed as Fourth Official. Keeping up with the action from Stockley Park is VAR James Bell and Additional VAR Edward Smart. 2026/27 stats: Games (all competitions): 2 Yellow cards issues (all competitions): 11 Red cards issued (all competitions): 0 Other match officials selected: Assistant referees: Constantine Hatzidakis & Nick Hopton Fourth Official: John Busby Video Assistant Referee: James Bell Additional Video Assistant Referee: Edward Smart Related Content Pre-match thoughts: Brenden Aaronson Matchday Pre-match thoughts: Brenden Aaronson 30 Aug 26 Team news: Daniel Farke names XI for Brentford clash Matchday Team news: Daniel Farke names XI for Brentford clash 30 Aug 26 Back on home turf! articles.title: Leeds united women pair surprise foundation participants
articles.source_type: Manager fitness updates, injury detail and expected return timelines
articles.body: Leeds United Women pair surprise Foundation participants - Leeds United Previous Community Leeds United Women pair surprise Foundation participants 02 Sep 26 Girls' Camps took place in the summer holidays. Share Over the summer holidays, the Leeds United Foundation continued to deliver its Football Camps at various locations across the wider Leeds area. One week of the Girls’ Camp in particular was hosted at The Grammar School at Leeds, where attendees were given a surprise visit from Leeds United Women midfield duo Monique Watson and Alice Hughes. Delivered by the Foundation, the camp was open to girls aged seven to 15 of all abilities. Running throughout the school holidays, the camps use football and sport to help young people develop their skills both on and off the pitch. Watson and Hughes joined the girls on the indoor pitch, getting involved in the action before hosting a Q&A session where the pair shared their experiences of playing football and offered advice on how to manage the pressures that can come with the game. For some of the attendees, the session provided the perfect preparation for their evening, with a number of them making the short trip to watch what would become Leeds United Women's 3-2 victory over Halifax Women. After the session, the pair spoke to leedsunited.com. "It’s a privilege to be able to attend the camps, see the next generation of talent and answer all the girls’ questions," Hughes began. "They’ve got so much energy and passion and being able to feed into that is something we all enjoy. "Most of us, when we were younger, didn’t have female role models in football, and if we did, access and visibility was almost non-existent so I think it’s important for those girls to be able to interact with us so that they know there’s a pathway forwards for them in football if they want it." Watson continued: "For me, attending the camps is always a really positive experience and a great opportunity to see the impact the Foundation has within the next generation. As players, we’re in a fortunate position where we can inspire and connect with young people from many different backgrounds and show them what’s possible. "I think it’s really important to continue to build that connection between the club, Foundation and the community, as football can open so many doors both on and off the pitch. Hopefully, by spending time and answering questions we can leave them feeling inspired with whatever they want to do in life." articles.title: Largie ramazani joins burnley on loan
articles.source_type: Manager fitness updates, injury detail and expected return timelines
articles.body: Largie Ramazani joins Burnley on loan - Leeds United Previous Next Mens Largie Ramazani joins Burnley on loan 01 Sep 26 Forward makes Championship switch. Share Leeds United can confirm Largie Ramazani joined Burnley on a season-long loan, which will become a permanent transfer next summer, based on the winger making an achievable number of appearances for the Sky Bet Championship side. The forward arrived at Elland Road ahead of the 2024/25 title-winning season, signing for an undisclosed fee from UD Almería. The Belgian made his debut for the Whites in a victory over Yorkshire rivals Hull City on home soil before opening his account for the club with a goal in the away win at Cardiff City. Ramazani featured 29 times in the second tier and scored six times in a memorable year which saw United crowned champions and return to the Premier League. With his game time in West Yorkshire limited last term, the 25-year-old enjoyed time on loan at La Liga side Valencia CF. Whilst at the Mestalla club, Ramazani netted six goals in 31 appearances across all competitions. A hugely popular figure behind the scenes at Thorp Arch and Elland Road, Largie departs the club with the best wishes of everybody. We wish him well during his time in Lancashire and beyond. articles.body: EFL Cup Ticket Information: Chelsea (A) - Leeds United Previous Next Ticketing EFL Cup Ticket Information: Chelsea (A) 02 Sep 26 Details for Stamford Bridge clash. Share We can now confirm ticket and ballot information for our Carabao Cup Round Three away fixture against Chelsea at Stamford Bridge on Wednesday 9th September, KO 8pm. IMPORTANT INFORMATION: Our ticket allocation for this fixture will be digital tickets. A digital ticket will be emailed to each ticket holder. Digital tickets will be sent out by close of business on Monday 7th September . Digital tickets can only be downloaded once. Please note, screenshots of digital tickets will not work. All supporters are encouraged to arrive early for this game and ensure that they have downloaded their digital ticket to their Apple /Google wallet on their smartphone before arriving at Stamford Bridge. Any supporters who require assistance with their digital tickets on matchday, must ensure that they travel with their photo identification as this will be required by the Chelsea Box Office team to verify that they are the ticket owner. AWAY SEASON TICKET HOLDERS: Any Away Season Ticket Holders who are enrolled on the Away Auto Cup Scheme will automatically have their payment card charged and their ticket dispatched. Away Season Ticket Holders not enrolled on the Away Auto Cup Scheme are guaranteed a ticket, but must purchase their reserved away ticket online between 10am on Thursday 3rd September and 9am on Saturday 5th September. How to purchase a reserved away ticket: 1. Login to your online ticketing account – 2. Hover over your name (top right) and click ‘My Account’ 3. Click ‘Reservations’ 4. Select the Chelsea ticket and click the ‘Confirm Reservation’ button 5. Proceed and pay for your ticket. BALLOT APPLICATION DATES: Due to the limited timescales, the usual sales window is shorter for this fixture. Online ballot application dates: Thursday 3rd September - Tracker Ballot Ballot opens at 10am and closes at midnight Supporters who attended 6 or more away games in the 2025/26 season can apply 50% chance of success Friday 4th September - Tracker Ballot Run Tracker ballot will be run and successful applicants notified by midday. Friday 4th September - Season Ticket Holders / Members Ballots Separate ballots will open at 1pm; one for Season Ticket Holders and one for My Leeds Members. These ballots will close for applications at midnight. Season Ticket Holders and Members who are unsuccessful with their Tracker Ballot application can submit a further application during this window. Saturday 5th September - Season Ticket Holders / Members Ballots Run The Season Ticket Holders and Members ballots will be run and successful applicants notified by midday. Please note, we can only guarantee that we can allocate adjoining seats for those supporters who apply within the same ballot application. TICKET ALLOCATION: 4046 MATCH TICKET PRICING: £35 Adult £27 Senior 66+ £27 Under 23 years £17 Junior under 20 years Please note that all supporters under the age of 16 must be accompanied by an adult over the age of 18. Any supporter under the age of 16 unaccompanied by an 18 year will not be allowed entry to the stadium. All supporters regardless of age will need a valid ticket. ACCESSIBILITY: Accessible Tickets There are 30 wheelchair spaces, these are priced at the above relevant age category with a free personal assistant where required. Ambulant seating is available. Accessible Parking 9 accessible car parking spaces are available, (6 Stamford bridge underground, and 3 Fulham Broadway) they can be pre-booked on a first come first basis via Chelsea FC online form found here and is available to both home and away supporters. Supporters can apply until 3 days prior to the fixture. IMPORTANT INFORMATION: Refunds The deadline for any match ticket refunds for this fixture is midday on Monday 7th September. Coaches There is a limited area for supporter coaches in Chelsea FC coach park area (Imperial Road). Imperial Road is now part of the South Fulham Traffic Congestion and Pollution Reduction Zone, so access is usually restricted to borough residents and other specially authorised vehicles. To ensure a coach parking space is allocated and avoid the risk of incurring a Penalty Charge Notices (PCNs) please following this link Book Coach Parking – Chelsea FC - Coach Parking – Imperial Road (gotocsp.com). Please note Chelsea FC cannot accommodate more than 20 away supporter coaches. All coach and minibuses must be booked onto the system no later than 12 noon, three days prior the fixture date. Coach drivers are required to remain with their vehicle throughout the match in case they need to move it. Bag Policy Supporters are reminded that no bags larger than A4 will be permitted into the stadium. This equates to 30cm x 20cm x 10cm, about the size of a standard handbag. Please note there is no baggage deposit facilities available for any larger baggage items. Away Section The entire away section is designated a safe standing area, and supporters will have an allocated position that they must occupy. Supporters in safe standing area are required to comply with our Supporter Code of Conduct, a copy of which is available at www.chelseafc.com/tickets/conditionsofissue. Visiting Supporters Guide The visiting supporters guide can be found below should you require more information for your supporters: https://www.chelseafc.com/en/tickets-guides-policies-and-forms. articles.body: FPL Price Change Predictor 2026/27: Live Guide The official FPL Price Change Predictor is now live for 2026/27. Log in to Fantasy Premier League and select Price Changes to see which players are moving towards a price rise or fall. The predictor uses official FPL transfer activity and updates every 15 minutes. It is a timing guide rather than a guarantee, so use it alongside minutes, fixtures and team news before making a transfer. The feature was launched by the Premier League after the Gameweek 1 deadline . For other squad-building data, visit our free FPL tools , including the FPL DEFCON comparison tool What is the official FPL Price Change Predictor? The predictor is an official Fantasy Premier League page that tracks every player's progress towards the next price rise or drop. It shows current progress as a percentage calculated from official transfer activity. After a calibration period of at least one Gameweek, FPL says it will also show a predicted progress percentage. Labels such as “Very Likely to Rise” and “Likely to Drop” translate the data into a quicker status. This is the first official FPL tool dedicated to predicting price changes. Third-party services have estimated changes for years, but they have had to infer the unpublished thresholds from player ownership and observed changes. Is the FPL Price Change Predictor live? Yes. The predictor became available after the Gameweek 1 deadline on 21 August 2026. To find it: log in on the Fantasy Premier League website select Price Changes in the main navigation; and filter the table by your team, your watchlist or all players. Player prices were locked before the Gameweek 1 deadline. They can now rise or fall at the daily price-change update. What does the predictor show? The main table lists every player and can be filtered to show: players in your team; players on your watchlist; or the full player pool. Price-change status also appears on individual player profiles. FPL says the Pick Team and Transfers screens will include a price-change view, letting managers check their own squad as part of the normal transfer workflow. What does a percentage over 100 mean? According to the Premier League, anything above 100 per cent indicates that the player is expected to pass the rise or fall threshold at the next 00:00 UK update. It still does not guarantee a change. For example, a player could display 105 per cent shortly before midnight, then receive enough late transfers in the opposite direction to move back below the estimated threshold. FPL explicitly describes the predictor as a guide. Treat the status as evidence for timing a move, not a promise that the price will change. How often is the FPL predictor updated? The predictor page updates every 15 minutes. Player price changes happen once per day at 00:00 UK time The percentage can move in either direction as managers continue buying and selling players. A stale screenshot or an update from earlier in the day may no longer represent the current position. The most important limitation remains the same: predicted progress is not the only factor in a good transfer. Should you make an early transfer to avoid a price rise? Sometimes, but price protection has a cost. An early transfer can secure a player before a rise and preserve team value. It also exposes your squad to injuries, rotation news and other information that arrives before the next deadline. Before moving early, consider: whether the player is likely to start; whether either club has another match before the FPL deadline; how much the possible price change affects your planned move; whether you would still want the player at the higher price; and whether you have a free transfer or would take a points hit. A predicted rise can make the timing urgent, but it does not make the underlying transfer good. Decide on the player first, then use the predictor to decide whether waiting is worth the risk. Official predictor versus third-party price-change sites The official tool has one major advantage: it is built from official FPL transfer data and integrated into the game. That does not necessarily make every independent tool redundant. Third-party services can still differentiate through: notifications before a likely change; historical prediction accuracy; daily price-change histories; combined transfer, fixture and expected-points analysis; and alternative views for planning several moves. FPL has also said its own prediction remains a guide. The value of any predictor should be judged by how clearly it communicates uncertainty and how accurately it performs after calibration. When do FPL prices change? FPL price changes happen at 00:00 UK time Official FPL price-change rules say a player can rise or fall by £0.1m in one daily update and by up to £0.3m in a Gameweek. The predictor's percentage is designed to show who is approaching the next change. Check it close enough to the update to use current information, but do not let a possible £0.1m move override a better transfer decision. Our FPL defensive contribution guide explains another new-season factor to consider when comparing players. If your group would rather draft unique squads and trade players during the season, Draft Fantasy for the Premier League supports auction and snake drafts, waivers, trades and custom scoring. Read the 2026/27 launch guide for the full setup. Create a 2026/27 Premier League Draft Fantasy league FPL Price Change Predictor: quick answers Where is the FPL Price Change Predictor? Log in to the Fantasy Premier League website and select Price Changes in the main navigation. Does 100 per cent guarantee a price change? No. It indicates that a player is expected to pass the threshold, but transfers can move the percentage before the midnight update. How frequently does the predictor update? The predictor page updates every 15 minutes. Player prices change at 00:00 UK time. How much can an FPL player's price change? A player can rise or fall by £0.1m per day and by up to £0.3m in one Gameweek. Want a fantasy game where players move between managers through waivers and trades instead? articles.body: Summer transfers 2026: All the Chelsea ins, outs and new contracts so far | News | Official Site | Chelsea Football Club With the 2026 summer transfer window now open, we keep you updated with all the deals done so far this summer... Chelsea new signings - Summer 2026 Honest Anahor Chelsea have agreed a deal to sign Italy international Honest Ahanor from Serie A side Atalanta, with the 18-year-old defender officially joining in 2027. Valentin Barco Versatile midfielder Barco arrived from Strasbourg, signing a contract until 2033. He has previous experience of English football with Brighton. Pep Chavarria The 29-year-old Spaniard joined Chelsea early in August following four seasons with Rayo Vallecano. Jordan Henderson The experienced England international joined the Blues in August after leaving Brentford, agreeing a two-year deal at Stamford Bridge. Maxence Lacroix Lacroix made the short journey from Crystal Palace to Chelsea towards the end of July, fresh from his involvement for France at the 2026 World Cup. Lacroix's deal lasts until 2032. Emiliano Martinez Chelsea managed to secure the services of one of the best goalkeepers in the world when they signed the 2022 World Cup winner from Aston Villa on a contract which will run until 2029. Marco Palestra The Italian international became our first signing of the summer when he joined on a permanent deal from Atalanta at the start of July. Palestra signed a contract through to 2033. Geovany Quenda The winger's move to Chelsea was first confirmed in March 2025, before officially completing his move from Sporting Lisbon this summer. The Portuguese teenager signed a contract until 2034. Morgan Rogers England international Morgan Rogers signed from Aston Villa in July 2026, penning a contract until 2033. He has played 22 times for the Three Lions, including at this summer's World Cup, and established himself as one of the top attacking talents in the Premier League. Dastan Satpayev Dastan Satpayev completed a transfer to Chelsea after his 18th birthday, having been a part of our pre-season tour in Australia and Asia. He subsequently joined Burnley on loan. Danny Welbeck Joining from Brighton and Hove Albion, where he had impressed in recent seasons, striker Welbeck became our fifth signing of the summer. His contract runs to 2028. Harrison Bettoni 18-year-old Bettoni joined from Wigan Athletic on a contract until 2030. The attacking midfielder featured 27 times for the Latics last season, scoring four goals. Alfie Osborne Osborne, 18, joined from Hearts in Scotland and put pen to paper on a contract with the Blues until 2030. Chelsea new contracts - Summer 2026 Toby Bell Toby Bell signed his first professional contract. The goalkeeper made his Under-18 debut in November 2024 and has represented England throughout his development pathway. Jesse Derry The young winger commited his long-term future to Chelsea by signing a new contract until 2032, shortly before agreeing a loan switch to swap London for Lisbon in the 2026/27 season with a spell at Sporting. Sol Gordon Academy attacker Sol Gordon signed a new contract until 2029. Having joined Chelsea's development centre at Under-8 level, Gordon has progressed through the Academy ranks to become a regular for our Under-18s and has also featured for the Blues' Under-21s. Jashayde Greenwood Academy striker Jashayde Greenwood signed his first professional contract with the club following his 17th birthday and after a successful maiden campaign at Chelsea. Ollie Harrison Harrison, an Academy midfielder who established himself as a regular for our Under-21s last season as we lifted the Premier League 2 title, signed a new contract until 2029. He later joined Wimbledon on loan. Charlie Holland Our midfielder signed his first professional contract with the Blues following his 17th birthday. He has been with our Academy since Under-8s level. Shumaira Mheuka The 18-year-old striker signed a deal which will keep him at Chelsea until 2031, having made nine senior appearances for the club so far. He will spend this season on loan with Celtic. Justin Osagie Academy defender Osagie signed a new contract keeping him at the club until 2029. He established himself as an important member of our Under-21 side last season. Joao Pedro Ahead of the campaign starting, Joao Pedro signed a new contract with Chelsea until 2034. The Brazilian netted 20 goals in his debut season at the Bridge and was voted our Player of the Year. Hudson Sands Before joining Dulwich Hamlet on loan, Academy goalkeeper Sands signed a new three-year contract. Dante Waite After captaining Chelsea Under-18s to victory in the Under-18 Premier League national final in 2026, the centre-back signed his first professional contract with the Blues. Chelsea loans - Summer 2026 Genesis Antwi The 19-year-old Academy player embarked on his first loan in August 2026, joining Ligue 1 side Strasbourg for the forthcoming campaign. Benoit Badiashile The defender, who has played 71 times for the Blues, joined Napoli on loan for the season. Axel Disasi Disasi has joined fellow Premier League side Crystal Palace for this season, having spent the second half of last term with West Ham United. Kiano Dyer Dyer will spend this season on loan in League Two with Chesterfield. The 19-year-old midfielder made his senior Chelsea debut in our Conference League win over Almaty in December 2024. Dario Essugo The midfielder was another to join Strasbourg on loan for the 2026/27 season. Essugo helped us win the Club World Cup shortly after his arrival in the summer of 2025 before injuries hampered his maiden campaign. Alejandro Garnacho The Argentina international joined Aston Villa on loan for 2026/27 having scored eight goals in 43 appearances in his first season at Stamford Bridge. Ollie Harrison Academy midfielder Harrison signed for League One side AFC Wimbledon for the season, embarking on his maiden loan away from the Bridge. Filip Jorgensen The goalkeeper has moved to Strasbourg on loan for the season. Ryan Kavuma-McQueen The 17-year-old winger departed on his maiden loan spell in the senior game, signing for Portsmouth ahead of the Championship season starting. Max Merrick Young goalkeeper Max Merrick embarked on his third loan away from the Bridge by joining Hartlepool United of the National League for the season. He has been in our first team matchday squad on 11 occasions in recent years. Shumaira Mheuka After signing a new five-year-contract, the 18-year-old striker made the move to Scottish champions Celtic for this season, where he will gain further experience to add to his nine senior appearances for the Blues so far. Mykhailo Mudryk The winger is heading on loan to London rivals Tottenham Hotspur, where he will link up once again with his former Shakhtar Donetsk manager Roberto De Zerbi. The Ukraine international has made 73 appearances for the Blues and scored ten goals since joining from Shakhtar in January 2023. Harrison Murray-Campbell Chelsea Academy defender Murray-Campbell, who made his senior Blues debut against Shamrock Rovers in the 2024/25 UEFA Conference League, will spend the coming season gaining further experience of men's football with KV Kortrijk in the Belgian first division. Dujuan Richards The forward has joined League One side AFC Wimbledon on a season-long loan. The Jamaica international is heading back out on loan after spending the second half of last season at Leicester City in the Championship. Ishe Samuels-Smith The defender has joined Notts County of League One for the 2026/27 campaign, following his loan spell with Swansea City last term. Robert Sanchez The goalkeeper has completed a season-long loan move to Serie A side Como. Sanchez has made 112 appearances for the Blues during his three years at the club, helping us win the Club World Cup and Conference League in the summer of 2025. Hudson Sands The young goalkeeper signed a new contract until 2029 and joined non-league side Dulwich Hamlet on a youth loan. Mamadou Sarr The defender will spend this season in Spain, after joining Real Sociedad on loan. He has made seven appearances for Chelsea since arriving from Strasbourg. Dastan Satpayev After completing his transfer to Chelsea, the Kazakh attacker moved to Burnley on loan for the season. Reggie Walsh Walsh, who played four games for our senior team in 2025 including as a 16-year-old, will spend the season on loan at Wigan Athletic in League One this season. Caleb Wiley The American has made a season-long loan move to Championship side Preston North End, having previously represented Watford on loan in that division. Kaiden Wilson Wilson embarked on his first loan in senior football in July 2026, joining newly-promoted League Two side Rochdale for the forthcoming campaign. Chelsea departures - Summer 2026 Tosin Adarabioyo The centre-back has completed a permanent transfer to Tottenham Hotspur. The 28-year-old made 70 appearances for the Blues following his signing on a free transfer from Fulham in July 2024. Chris Atherton The winger left for Ipswich Town after a season playing for our Academy sides. Jeremiah Berkeley-Agyepong The teenager came through the ranks at the Chelsea Academy from Under-8s level and featured for our Under-18s in pre-season. He has now joined Reading. Trevoh Chalobah Chalobah completed a permanent transfer to Como in August, bringing his time as a Chelsea player to an end after nearly two decades with the Blues. He won four trophies, having established himself in our first team ahead of the 2021/22 campaign. Marc Cucurella The Spaniard left for Real Madrid after four successful seasons at Stamford Bridge during which he won the Club World Cup and the UEFA Conference League, as well as helping Spain triumph in the 2024 Euros. Liam Delap Delap departed for Nottingham Forest after 14 months with Chelsea. The striker played 41 times for the Blues, including six of our seven games during last summer's victorious FIFA Club World Cup campaign. Enzo Fernandez The midfielder has completed a permanent transfer to Premier League side Manchester City. The Argentine international made 170 appearances during his time at Stamford Bridge and struck 31 goals. David Fofana The Chelsea striker has joined Swiss club Servette on a permanent deal. Fofana signed for the Blues from Molde in January 2023, scoring 17 goals and providing three assists during his time at the Bridge and on loan. Tyrique George The winger made his loan move to Everton permanent this summer, departing Chelsea after progressing through our Academy and making 37 appearances for the senior team. Marc Guiu The striker has joined Bundesliga side RB Leipzig on a permanent deal. The 20-year-old joined from Barcelona in the summer of 2024 and scored eight goals in 29 appearances for the Blues. Brodi Hughes The versatile defender spent 13 years in our Academy having joined as an Under-8. He was released at the end of the 2025/26 season, which he spent on loan at AFC Wimbledon. Nicolas Jackson The Senegal striker completed a permanent transfer to fellow Premier League side Aston Villa. Jackson was part of the Chelsea squads that won the Conference League and Club World Cup, scoring against Real Betis in the final of the former. Omari Kellyman The attacking midfielder made a permanent move to France with Ligue 1 club Strasbourg, after spending last season on loan with Cardiff City, where he helped them earn promotion to the Championship. Jimmy-Jay Morgan The Academy forward completed a permanent move to Championship side West Bromwich Albion after impressing on loan at Peterborough last season. Morgan had returned to Chelsea, where he spent time in our Academy as a youngster, in February 2023. Richard Olise Olise also moved on after a decade with the club. Signed by Chelsea as an Under-9, Olise featured throughout the age groups in our Academy and was named in the first-team squad for our UEFA Conference League trip to Astana during the 2024/2

articles.body: Shumaira Mheuka signs new Chelsea contract and joins Celtic on loan | News | Official Site | Chelsea Football Club Shumaira Mheuka has signed a new contract with Chelsea through to 2031 and joined Scottish champions Celtic on loan for the 2026/27 campaign. The striker joined Chelsea aged 13 and now has nine senior appearances for the Blues since his debut in a UEFA Conference League win at Astana in December 2024. The 18-year-old was named the 2025/26 Premier League 2 Player of the Season after captaining Chelsea Under-21s to a first-place league finish, scoring 18 goals in 19 appearances in that competition. Mheuka will now spend the current campaign gaining further senior experience with Celtic, who have made a strong start to their Scottish Premiership title defence, winning each of their first three league games. All at Chelsea wish Shim luck in Scotland and look forward to monitoring his continued progress at Celtic Park.

articles.title: Romeo lavia on how xabi alonso is trying to find that extra one per cent
articles.source_type: Head coach team news ahead of each fixture, injury updates, official previews
articles.body: Romeo Lavia on how Xabi Alonso is trying to find that extra one per cent | News | Official Site | Chelsea Football Club Romeo Lavia is feeling great. But best of all for Blues fans, the midfielder believes he is going to get even better with the support of his team-mates and new manager. The 22-year-old has now started both Premier League games under manager Xabi Alonso and is enjoying making an impact on the pitch, something he did from the off last Sunday when he tapped home his first Chelsea goal to open the scoring against Brighton as the Blues won 4-3 at the Bridge. Having made it two wins in two in the league, Lavia highlighted the Blues’ developing mentality, which he believes is making the difference. ‘Our mentality has been great so far, starting from pre-season,’ Romeo opened. ‘And the manager has really been big on that to help us get that extra per cent to help us get the three points on the weekend. So far, it's been great. ‘It's all about building confidence. Obviously, my team-mates are giving me a lot of it, and the manager as well. It's just about building game by game, and I feel great, so hopefully it can continue forever.’ Even the cool, calm and collected Lavia couldn’t hide his joy after scoring his first for Chelsea, admitting he might have the video on loop! He continued: ‘It means a lot to score my first – a lot. I’m very happy – to score at the Bridge as well. For a first one, it can't get any better. I think I'm going to rewatch the goal a few more times. It's not the best-looking goal, but I'll take it every day. ‘It was a fantastic reaction from the fans, and from my team-mates as well. I really felt the love, so it was an amazing feeling.’ In a game that saw the visitors peg the Blues back, Lavia recognises the group will only get better in time, with all eyes on our trip to the Emirates this weekend, where we’ll go head-to-head with London rivals Arsenal. ‘We know our colleagues, and when we know that our colleagues can take over, we just need to make sure the rest goes with it,’ he added. ‘We realise that it's automatic – that we just push each other. We know our colleagues will take over in the end. It's honestly a great group to be in, and the demands in training every single day make it easier to then perform on the weekend. ‘There's a lot of work that goes behind the scenes, and it was just about putting that into practice. And we're happy that they came off well [against Brighton], so I’m very happy.’
