U.S. sports betting: Where all 50 states stand on online sports betting sites Brandt Sutton Chelena Goldman Sep 2, 2026 at 2:30 pm ET 14 min read Add CBS Sports on Google Sports betting has become increasingly popular across the United States, but not every state has legalized it. There are 39 states, in addition to Washington D.C., that have some form of legalized U.S. sports betting , whether online or in-person. Of those 39 states, 30 offer sports betting with smartphone apps or websites. However, a sports betting legalization bill has been introduced in nearly every U.S. state legislature at some point since 2018. Below is where all 50 U.S. states stand on legalizing online sports betting apps and introducing legislation. State Legal Status Alabama Not legal Alaska Not legal Arizona Legal Arkansas Legal California Not Legal Colorado Legal Connecticut Legal Delaware Legal (BetRivers) Florida Legal (Hard Rock Bet) Georgia Not legal Hawaii Not legal Idaho Not legal Illinois Legal Indiana Legal Iowa Legal Kansas Legal Kentucky Legal Louisiana Legal Maine Legal Maryland Legal Massachusetts Legal Michigan Legal Minnesota Not legal Mississippi Not legal Missouri Legal Montana Not legal Nebraska Not Legal Nevada Legal New Hampshire Legal New Jersey Legal New Mexico Not Legal New York Legal North Carolina Legal North Dakota Not Legal Ohio Legal Oklahoma Not legal Oregon Legal Pennsylvania Legal Rhode Island Legal South Carolina Not legal South Dakota Not Legal Tennessee Legal Texas Not legal Utah Not legal Vermont Legal Virginia Legal Washington Not Legal Washington D.C. Legal West Virginia Legal Wisconsin Legal (launch pending) Wyoming Legal Alabama: Not legal Multiple bills to legalize sports betting in Alabama have failed over the past several years. While sports betting remains illegal in the state, lawmakers have recently renewed their efforts at legalization. A new constitutional amendment proposal ( SB 257 ) has been introduced that would let voters decide whether to authorize sports betting (along with a state lottery and casinos), but significant legislative support is still needed before it can advance. Alaska: Not legal The most recent effort to legalize sports betting in Alaska, HB 145, was introduced on March 21, 2025. There has been no forward motion or vote on the bill as of September 2026. Alaska users will have to stick to prediction markets and daily fantasy sports until another bill is introduced, likely within the next few years. Arizona: Legal Sports betting was legalized on April 15, 2021, and launched on September 9, 2021. Both retail and online sports betting are available. 14 sportsbooks are currently operating for Arizona sports betting Arkansas: Legal Retail sports betting launched in Arkansas on July 1, 2019, and online sports betting in Arkansas launched on March 4, 2022. In March 2026, DraftKings and FanDuel entered the market as technology vendors, partnering with Southland and Oaklawn, respectively, marking the first time national operators have been available in the state. California: Not legal Multiple bills to legalize sports betting in California have failed, including two major bills on the November 2022 ballot. No new sports betting bills were presented in 2025. Sports betting bills will have another chance to pass in 2028. Colorado: Legal Both retail and online Colorado sports betting launched in the Centennial State on May 1, 2020. Colorado is home to 13 online sports books. Bettors can wager on professional and collegiate games, but placing player prop bets on collegiate athletes is prohibited. In May 2026, Colorado State Senate passed a consumer protection bill , which would put significant restrictions on online sportsbooks in the state if signed into law by the Governor's office. Connecticut: Legal Connecticut has both retail and online sports betting, which launched on October 19, 2021. There are three online sportsbooks available, allowing users limited access to books and promos relative to other states. However, in-state users are able to wager on college player props from out-of-state teams. Delaware: Legal (BetRivers) Delaware became the first state outside of Nevada to legalize sports betting, launching retail betting on July 5, 2018. The Blue Hen State added online sports betting on December 26, 2023. There are three retail locations and one online sportsbook available in the state. Wagering on professional sporting events and out-of-state collegiate games is allowed, but betting on in-state college games and placing player props on collegiate athletes is banned. Florida: Legal (Hard Rock Bet) Florida sports betting originally launched on November 1, 2021, thanks to an agreement between the state and the Seminole Tribe of Florida but was shut down three weeks later. Years of legal battles were resolved in 2023, and Florida sports betting re-launched on November 7, 2023. The Hard Rock Bet app is the only available online sportsbook in the state as of 2026, a fact that is likely to remain true for the foreseeable future. Georgia: Not legal Multiple efforts to legalize sports betting in Georgia have failed, though momentum appears to be slowly building. In 2025, two Georgia House measures reached the floor for debate before missing the legislative deadline, a step forward compared to prior years. A 2026 bill ( HB 910 ) has since been introduced that would legalize mobile sports betting under the Georgia Lottery, bypassing the need for a constitutional amendment, though significant hurdles remain. While there is some chance that sports betting is legal by the end of the year, it is more likely that the battle to introduce the practice stretches into the next few years. Residents of the Peach State will have to continue to rely on daily fantasy games and prediction markets for the foreseeable future. Hawaii: Not legal Multiple efforts to legalize sports betting in Hawaii have failed, including multiple bills introduced in 2025 that sought to establish and regulate online sportsbooks in Hawaii. However, none of the bills were passed before the end of the legislative deadline. While there are major hurdles, in February 2026, Hawaii sports betting took a small step forward . However, even with that step, sports betting is not likely to come to Hawaii in the next few years. Idaho: Not legal While there are seven tribal casinos operating in Idaho, there has been no proposed sports betting legislation in the state as of 2026. Without notable interest, the practice looks to remain outlawed in Idaho for the foreseeable future. Illinois: Legal Retail sports betting launched in the state on March 9, 2020, while online sportsbooks launched on June 18. There are 10 online sportsbooks operational in the Prairie State. Wagering on professional sporting events and out-of-state collegiate games is allowed, but betting on in-state college games and placing player props on college athletes is prohibited on Illinois sports betting sites, just as they are in many other states. Indiana: Legal Retail and online sports betting in Indiana launched on September 1, 2019, and there are 11 available online sportsbooks as of 2025. Wagering on professional sporting events and collegiate games is allowed, but placing player props on collegiate athletes is strictly prohibited. Iowa: Legal Retail and online sports betting launched in Iowa on August 15, 2019, and there are 11 available online Iowa sportsbooks as of 2025. Wagering on professional sporting events and collegiate games is allowed, but placing player props on collegiate athletes is strictly prohibited. Kansas: Legal Retail and online sports betting in Kansas launched on September 1, 2022, and there are six available online sportsbooks as of 2025. Wagering on professional sporting events and collegiate games is allowed, but placing player props on collegiate athletes is strictly prohibited. Kentucky: Legal Sports betting is still somewhat new to the Blue Grass State. Retail sports betting launched on September 7, 2023, followed by the launch of online sports betting on September 28. There are eight online sportsbooks in Kentucky , and there are no restrictions on wagering on collegiate games or player props, making it one of the more open markets in the nation. Louisiana: Legal Although retail and online sports betting launched in Louisiana on January 28, 2022, not all parishes within the state allow sports betting. There are eight online Louisiana sportsbooks licensed to operate in permitted parishes. Wagering on professional sporting events and collegiate games is allowed, but placing player props on collegiate athletes is strictly prohibited. Maine: Legal Retail and online sports betting launched in Maine on November 3, 2023. DraftKings and Caesars are the only two sportsbooks licensed to operate in the state as of 2025, limiting options for residents of the Pine Tree State. Wagering on professional sporting events and out-of-state collegiate games is permitted. However, betting on in-state collegiate athletics, limiting the scope of wagers residents of the state can place. Maryland: Legal Maryland legalized sports betting in 2020, but didn't launch in-person betting until December 9, 2021. Online sports betting launched in the state on November 23, 2022, with 11 online sportsbooks operating as of 2025. Wagering on professional sporting events and collegiate games is allowed, but placing player props on collegiate athletes is strictly prohibited at Maryland sports betting sites. Massachusetts: Legal Retail sports betting launched in the Bay State on January 31, 2023, and online Massachusetts sportsbooks launched on March 10, with seven online sportsbooks licensed to operate as of 2025. Wagering on professional sporting events and out-of-state collegiate games is allowed, but betting on in-state college games is only allowed if a school is participating in a tournament with four or more teams, like the NCAA Tournament. Placing player props on collegiate athletes in any games is strictly prohibited, but Massachusetts is still one of the more permissive betting states in the country. Michigan: Legal Gambling has been legal in the state of Michigan for several years. In-person, often referred to as retail, became legal in March 2020, while online and mobile Michigan sports betting launched in Michigan on January 22, 2021. Additionally, users are allowed to wager on college player props, opening plenty of opportunities for residents of the Wolverine State. Minnesota: Not legal Legislation to legalize Minnesota sports betting passed in August 2022, but a launch date has not been set yet. Due to disagreements between tribal nations and racetrack operators, the push for legalization is expected to carry into 2027 and beyond. But starting with that '24 season, the criteria was changed to give the award to a player who returned from "illness, physical injury, or other circumstances that led him to miss playing time the previous season." articles.body: ‘We’re in a strong place’: Director of football Phil Giles reflects on Brentford’s summer transfer window | Brentford FC | Brentford FC Director of football Phil Giles believes Brentford have emerged from the summer transfer window with a stronger squad after retaining the core of Keith Andrews’ group and adding five new first-team signings. Jannik Schuster, Jaidon Anthony, Callum Wilson, Mamadou Sangaré and El Hadji Malick Diouf arrived during the window, with all but Diouf joining before the start of the Premier League season. Following a summer of significant change in 2025 , continuity and targeted additions were central to the club’s approach this time around. “Last summer, we sold more than we bought,” Giles explained. “The aim this year was to keep the squad together, build on Keith’s first season and add some extra quality. I think we did that. “Every summer, you need to add some freshness. It makes us less predictable for the opposition and creates competition for places.” Combined with the relationships already established within the squad, Giles thinks that has helped the Bees make a positive start. “I’m very pleased,” he continued. “They’re all coming in to compete for a first-team place. “There’s always a balance between players who are ready now and development projects. These players were more or less ready to go from day one, which is great. “By keeping what we had together and adding them, I think the squad looks really strong. “The players who were here last year know each other, know the coaching staff and understand the style of play. “They’ve already built relationships on the pitch, so we weren’t starting from scratch with a lot of new players. “We’ve dropped a few additions into a group who already knew what they were doing. “In theory, that should allow you to make a good start in the league, and I think we’ve done that. We’ve played really well during the first couple of games, so it’s been positive so far.” Giles admitted that the level of spending across the wider transfer market exceeded his expectations. “At the start of the summer, after a lot of spending last year, I thought it might be quieter and perhaps there wouldn’t be as much money floating around – but I was completely wrong!” he said. “It’s been interesting. There’s been a lot of money spent. “We’ve invested a significant amount by our standards, but when you compare that with clubs spending £70 million, £80 million or even £120 million, we’re obviously not in that ballpark. “To be able to compete with those clubs without spending that sort of money is testament to our scouts and recruitment team, who continue to find players capable of helping us. “I want to give all the staff credit – not only for identifying and signing players, but for integrating and developing them. “We’ve got a really good squad and, in today’s market, a valuable one. We’re in a strong place as a football club.” Having finished in the Premier League’s top half in three of the last four seasons, Giles wants Brentford to continue progressing without placing limits on what the team can achieve. “The target in any season is to keep improving – that’s always the baseline,” he concluded. “We’ve finished in the top half of the Premier League in three of the last four seasons. “Getting better would mean finishing in the top half again, and you’d hope that one day that will lead to European qualification. “The trick is to keep getting better and not worry too much about where that might take you. “We don’t yet know how good the other teams are. If they’re all brilliant, it becomes harder for us! We’ll let everything settle down and see. “Let’s keep being us, let’s keep trying to improve, and we’ll see where we land.”

articles.body: Things to know if travelling to Elland Road | Brentford FC | Brentford FC Brentford take on Leeds United in the Premier League on Sunday 30 August (2pm kick-off BST). The match will be broadcast live on Sky Sports in the UK. If you are heading to Elland Road, here is everything you need to know to ensure you are ready for your visit. Digital tickets are in use for this matchday and you will receive an email with instructions on how to download yours. Travel – rail replacement services on parts of your journey Travel to Leeds on matchday is disrupted by maintenance works on LNER lines. Rail replacement bus services will take you part of the way on your journey. From London St Pancras, journeys to Leeds could take between four hours and five hours and 30 minutes, with multiple changes. You will have to board a train as early as 6.30am to make it to Leeds in good time. We strongly recommend that you plan your journey to the match and home again ahead of time and book tickets early as many routes have already sold out. Local travel to the ground Leeds train station is approximately 40 minutes’ walk from Elland Road. Bus services from the city centre will take you to Elland Road, including: 9A, 24, 51, 52, 55, 55C, 65, 75. You can also take the matchday shuttle service (R2) to the ground. Bus stops directly outside the ground are suspended for one hour before and one hour after the match. You may have to walk a short distance if you arrive close to kick-off. We recommend using the Citymapper app to help navigate public transport in the city. Driving and parking Driving from London to Leeds will take around four hours and possibly longer if driving in poor weather. Paid car parking operated by the home club or its partners is available at Elland Road or near to the ground. The main car park for away fans is the park & ride drop-off point off Bobby Collins Way, which is near the away coaches. For more information, see the car parks section on Leeds’ website A park & ride matchday shuttle is also available, with shuttles running from two and a half hours before kick-off until 25 minutes after full-time. This must be paid for in advance. More information is available here Ticketing information – digital tickets are in use for this fixture Tickets for this fixture will be distributed digitally. You will receive your ticket(s) by email ahead of the match. Please follow the instructions on the email to get your ticket ready on your phone. For those that have requested a physical ticket or have sent a duplicate ticket request, the away ticket office is located in the west stand car park opposite the away supporter entrance. Any duplicate ticket requests must be sent to Leeds United by the Brentford box office. Please contact Brentford's box office with any enquiries ahead of matchday. If you’re collecting your ticket at Elland Road, please remember to bring ID. Please also observe and respect the family friendly seating. Anyone who holds a ticket in this area is reminded that they should be seated for the duration of the match. Accessibility Accessible parking is available for blue badge holders only in Fullerton, off of Elland Road. You cannot pre-book this area but it is free for blue badge holders. Visiting disabled supporters who have purchased accessible seats enter the stadium by Exit W1 gate. Elland Road has elevated wheelchair platforms for visiting fans. Accessible toilets are in the away end and unlockable with a RADAR key. If you need access, speak to a wellbeing officer identified by their blue vests. Changing places facilities are also available, but please contact [email protected] prior to your visit. Your matchday at Elland Road Leeds operates an away fanzone in the west stand car park. Food and drink including alcohol will be served from two hours before kick-off. There are no away pubs in the vicinity of Elland Road. Some pubs in the city centre will accept Brentford fans but entry is at the discretion of the venue. Visiting supporters enter the ground at entrances 1 and 2 of the west stand. Turnstiles open 90 minutes before kick-off. Bags larger than A4 in size will not be permitted inside. There is no luggage storage facility at Elland Road. Have a safe trip and enjoy the match!

articles.body: Leeds United 1 Brentford 1: Kevin Schade scores in Elland Road draw | Brentford FC Kevin Schade's first goal of the season was cancelled out by Dominic Calvert-Lewin as Brentford were held to a 1-1 draw against Leeds United at Elland Road. Schade's first-half effort looked to be enough for the three points, but Calvert-Lewin struck with 11 minutes remaining and it ended honours even in West Yorkshire. Keith Andrews made two changes to the side who beat Tottenham Hotspur 3-0 on the opening weekend of the Premier League season. Jaidon Anthony , playing against the side he spent the 2023/24 season on loan with, made his first league start for the Bees while Mikkel Damsgaard also came into the starting XI. El Hadji Malick Diouf was named on the bench. Brentford, wearing the Kingsman- inspired away kit for the first time, had the first effort on goal inside the opening eight minutes, but Igor Thiago 's back-post volley from a tight angle was straight at James Trafford. The England international goalkeeper was then well-positioned to collect a Nathan Collins header moments later. Damsgaard tested Trafford with a curling shot and Ethan Ampadu sent a speculative effort comfortably wide of Caoimhín Kelleher 's goal at the other end as the Bees continued to control the contest against a well-organised Leeds defence. Five minutes before the break, the west Londoners got their reward for a dominant first-half display. Mamadou Sangaré swept the ball to his right for Anthony, whose cross was headed back into a central position. Sangaré picked it up again and his blocked shot fell to Keane Lewis-Potter on the left side of the box. His near-post delivery was turned into the far corner of Trafford's goal by a sublime Schade flick. Leeds made two changes at the interval but it didn't take long for the Bees, orchestrated by Sangaré, to dictate the game again. Their first set-piece of the second half created the first opportunity. Collins beat Ampadu to Vitaly Janelt 's deep corner to loop it back towards the penalty spot before Damsgaard got a bit too much on his header and it went over the frame. Kelleher, largely a spectator for the previous hour, was called into action for the first time and made a smart stop to deny James Justin after the left-back had cut inside and pulled the trigger from 25 yards. Brentford thought they should have had a penalty at the other end shortly afterwards. Dango Ouattara , five minutes after his introduction from the bench, led a lightning counter attack down the right flank. Eventually, he cut inside and switched the ball to Schade, who took a touch before going down after Jayden Bogle appeared to step on his foot. Referee Tony Harrington waved the appeals away. Some superb recovery defending from Lewis-Potter prevented the hosts from equalising following a breakaway of their own at the other end. After clearing the ball from a Bees corner, Lukas Nmecha poked the ball forward to put Dan James, positioned just inside his own half, through on goal. Under pressure from Lewis-Potter, the Welsh winger sent a wild shot high and wide of the target. Leeds were level, however, with just over 10 minutes remaining. Ampadu played the ball from the right wing into Nmecha inside the box. He took a touch and fired the ball across the six-yard box where Calvert-Lewin tapped into an empty net. Thiago nearly restored the lead instantly. The Brazilian's header from an Ouattara cross was parried by Trafford and, at full stretch, he could only turn the rebound into the side netting. Anton Stach sent a stoppage-time free-kick wide of the mark as both teams made it four points from their opening two league fixtures. Leeds (3-4-3): Trafford; Muharemović, Bijol (Tanaka HT), Rodon (Elvedi 34); Bogle (James 68), Ampadu, Stach, Justin; Aaronson (Wilson HT), Calvert-Lewin, Okafor (Nmecha 69) Subs not used: Cairns, Gudmundsson, Longstaff, Gnonto Brentford (4-3-3): Kelleher; Kayode (Wilson 89), Ajer, Collins, Lewis-Potter (Henry 89); Sangaré, Janelt, Damsgaard (Yarmoliuk 69), Anthony (Ouattara 61), Thiago, Schade (Hickey 89) Subs not used : Valdimarsson, Schuster, Carvalho, Diouf Attendance: 35,974 Andrews: A solid away point Keith Andrews reflected on Brentford's away fixture against Leeds United. "I’m really proud of what we produced. In the first half, we played some pretty impressive football," said Andrews. "We were in a good place and controlled pretty much the whole half, which isn’t easy to do when you come here. "In the second half, it was a different game. They made attacking subs and changed their system. "Overall, it’s a solid away point." Schade on Leeds stalemate Kevin Schade shared his thoughts after Brentford's 1-1 draw against Leeds United at Elland Road. "We need to keep working on the good things. We dominated the first half and probably needed to score more goals and put in more crosses in the final third," said the German forward. "In the second half, they changed a few things and we couldn’t adapt enough." On scoring his first goal of 2026/27 and his ambitions for this year, he added: "I want to achieve more than the other seasons, but I’ll take it game by game, work on things and then the goals will come."

articles.body: Mamadou Sangaré, Keane Lewis-Potter and Kevin Schade nominated for Premier League awards | Brentford FC | Brentford FC Three Brentford players have been nominated for Premier League awards following the Bees’ unbeaten start to the 2026/27 season. Mamadou Sangaré is in contention for August’s Player of the Month prize, while Keane Lewis-Potter and Kevin Schade have been shortlisted for Goal of the Month. EA SPORTS Player of the Month Mamadou Sangaré Summer signing Sangaré has been a driving force in Brentford’s unbeaten start to the campaign. The midfielder registered an assist during the Bees’ 3-0 victory over Tottenham Hotspur , combining brilliantly with Dango Ouattara before pulling the ball back for Lewis-Potter to score. Sangaré has dominated the centre of the pitch, making 27 defensive contributions, including 12 recoveries, six tackles and five interceptions. He has won 12 duels and created four chances. The Mali international is shortlisted alongside Riccardo Calafiori (Arsenal), Rayan Cherki (Manchester City), Bruno Fernandes (Manchester United), Cole Palmer (Chelsea), João Pedro (Chelsea), Konstantinos Tzolakis (Hull City) and Yoane Wissa (Newcastle United). Vote for Sangaré Guinness Goal of the Month Keane Lewis-Potter, Brentford v Tottenham Hotspur Brentford’s first goal of the Premier League season arrived after 12 minutes of their 3-0 win over Tottenham, concluding a move of real quality. Having taken up an advanced position, Sangaré collected the ball from Nathan Collins and exchanged passes with Ouattara before pulling it back for the arriving Lewis-Potter , who swept a first-time finish beyond Antonín Kinský. Pure poetry. pic.twitter.com/v9pJmxNsZs — Brentford FC (@BrentfordFC) August 24, 2026 Kevin Schade, Leeds United v Brentford Schade’s sublime flick during the Bees' 1-1 draw with Leeds United has also earned a place on the shortlist. Five minutes before the break, Sangaré moved the ball wide to Jaidon Anthony, whose cross was headed back into a central position. Sangaré regained possession and, after his shot was blocked, the ball fell to Lewis-Potter on the left side of the penalty area. His near-post delivery was expertly turned into the far corner by Schade. The Brentford duo face competition from Emersonn (Ipswich Town), Nilson Angulo (Sunderland), Joe Willock (Newcastle United), Rayan Cherki (Manchester City), Anthony Elanga (Newcastle United) and Cole Palmer (Chelsea). articles.body: Jayden Meghoma joins Portsmouth on loan | Brentford FC | Brentford FC Brentford defender Jayden Meghoma has joined Sky Bet Championship side Portsmouth on a season-long loan. The 20-year-old left-back will spend the duration of 2026/27 at Pompey alongside fellow Bees loanee Benjamin Arthur. Meghoma , who has represented England at every level from under-16s to U20s, came through the youth ranks at Tottenham Hotspur before joining Southampton aged 16. He signed his first professional contract in July 2023 and made his first-team debut the following month in a Carabao Cup tie against Gillingham. Three more appearances – all in the FA Cup – followed that season before he sealed a move to Brentford on Deadline Day of the 2024 summer transfer window. Meghoma featured in three Carabao Cup ties and made his Premier League debut against Chelsea during the first half of 2024/25, before joining Preston North End on loan in January of that campaign. He spent the duration of last term with Glasgow giants Rangers and made 44 appearances across the Scottish Premiership, Champions League qualifying, Europa League, SFA Cup and League Cup. During his time in Scotland, he also scored his first goal in senior football, a superb long-range effort against Dundee United.

articles.body: Brentford encourages community to talk more about mental health with Talking is the Best Tactic | Brentford FC | Brentford FC Brentford Football Club and Brentford FC Community Sports Trust will continue to use the power of football to encourage conversations around mental health this season through Talking is the Best Tactic , the campaign delivered as part of the Premier League's Together Against Suicide initiative. This Saturday’s fixture against Sunderland will be dedicated to the campaign, building on last season's launch. Brentford is encouraging supporters to take simple actions that could make a meaningful difference to supporting someone’s mental health. This week, the club and Trust installed a bench in Gunnersbury Park, the sixth to be added in the local area to encourage the community to pause, connect and talk. Last season, some of our players took to the benches to share their own experiences of mental health, including Fábio Carvalho and former Bees player Jordan Henderson. The installation of benches was inspired by Brentford's longstanding commitment to supporting mental wellbeing and the work of consultant psychologist Michael Caulfield, whose bench at the Robert Rowan Performance Centre (RRPC) provides a safe, confidential space for players, coaches and staff to speak. On Saturday, ahead of our game against Sunderland, from 12.30pm the RRPC bench will be located outside Entrance B at Gtech Community Stadium so fans can make a personal commitment linked to mental wellbeing and supporting others. Trained representatives from Brentford FC Community Sports Trust and the Samaritans will be on hand to speak with supporters and provide information about health and wellbeing programmes available in the local community. Support a loved one This season, Talking is the Best Tactic is encouraging supporters to take small actions towards better mental health through simple conversations or small acts of support. The Sunderland fixture is our dedicated Friends and Family fixture, where Brentford members (excluding overseas and junior members) can purchase an additional ticket and invite a friend, family member or someone they haven't seen for a while to the game. The fixture provides the perfect opportunity to reconnect with someone, spend time together and start a conversation. Supporting someone through conversation doesn't require the perfect words. Whether it's checking in with a friend, taking time to listen or helping someone access support when they need it, small actions can make a big difference. Purchase your ticket now Help is available For those experiencing poor mental health, support is available and no one has to face challenges alone. Brentford FC Community Sports Trust continues to provide free opportunities for people to connect and talk through initiatives including: Singing for Thought: A welcoming seven-week programme designed to boost mood, build confidence and bring people together through music. Led by an experienced choir leader, sessions are relaxed, fun and open to everyone. No previous singing experience needed - just bring your voice! Sign up here Walking for Wellbeing : A friendly community walking group designed to help people get outside, connect with others and improve their wellbeing. The group is a supportive space for anyone who wants to meet new people, build confidence or increase their daily step count weekly, every Friday. Sign up here Resources for urgent and local help can be found on our Talking is The Best Tactic webpage Anyone in need of urgent mental support should always call 999 in an emergency or contact NHS urgent mental health support via 111 and select option 2. You can also call Samaritans on 116 123 – free, available 24/7. Across local west London pubs, One Over the Ait, Kew Bridge, The George IV, The Bell & Crown and The Pilot in Chiswick, our special free Talking is The Best Tactic coasters will be available on Saturday morning. The coasters include details of urgent and local support for poor mental health. Everyone has a role Suicide affects people of all ages and backgrounds and affects men disproportionately. Sadly, men account for nearly three-quarters of suicides in the UK, yet too often feel unable to talk about what they're experiencing. Talking is the Best Tactic encourages all of us to play our part by checking in with those around us, asking simple questions and taking the time to listen. Throughout the 2026/27 season, Brentford will continue to encourage supporters, staff and the wider west London community to help create a culture where people feel able to talk.

articles.body: Brentford Women 8 Aylesford 2: Kiszkis scores hat-trick in dominant victory | Brentford FC | Brentford FC Brentford Women were in fine form as they beat Aylesford Women 8-2 at Honeycroft to make it three wins from three to start the London South East Premier Division campaign. The Bees came from behind with an emphatic victory; Wiktoria Kiszkis bagged a hat-trick, with Ashley Cheatley, Maddie Phillips, Becca Teale and Ilana Harris-Walters all getting on the scoresheet. It was a nightmare start for Brentford, who found themselves behind within 50 seconds. Williams' side failed to clear their lines on three occasions inside the box before the ball fell to Leigha Bradding-Butler, who fired through the bodies to put Aylesford 1-0 up. The west Londoners found themselves behind for the first time this season, but showed excellent character to respond instantly. Maï Louvrier's lofted through ball was met by Kiszkis , who nodded the ball into her own path before firing a left-footed half volley in to level the score on six minutes. Kiszkis almost had her second on 15 minutes when she again found space in between the Aylesford backline and keeper. She got to the ball first and poked her effort round Sade Rider but wide of the post. Two minutes later, Brentford found the lead through an own goal; Phillips capitalised with a short corner as Aylesford slept and flashed a ball across the six-yard box. Cheatley got the last touch in a red and white shirt as the ball ricocheted around the goalmouth before crossing the line as the Bees went 2-1 up. Teale fired just over from outside the box seconds after the restart and Cheatley's improvised flick went just wide as the west Londoners began to assert themselves on the game. On 24 minutes, Millie Constantine drove down the left and put a superb cross in to the back post which Kiszkis just couldn't connect with on the stretch. Lucy Potter then lifted an inch-perfect pass into Cheatley, who mishit her half-volley and missed the target. Williams' side were really applying the pressure and it paid off on 31 minutes when Abbi Smith turned in the box and was brought down. Phillips stood up and calmly tucked her penalty into the bottom-left corner to make it 3-1. Potter had a strike from range well saved from Rider after a clever free-kick found her in space. The Aylesford keeper injured herself in making the save and outfielder Juliette Blyghton had to go between the sticks as the Bees went into the break with a two-goal advantage. Mya Francis-Pownall was called into action a minute into the second half, intercepting at the feet of Bradding-Butler in the nick of time to protect the lead. The Bees stepped it up a gear and Cheatley made it four for Brentford on 49 minutes after running onto a perfectly weighted, slotted pass from Kiszkis and tucking the ball home. Two minutes later and Kiszkis doubled her tally for the day and added Brentford's fifth. Makeba Black's excellent diagonal ball was met by Teale who played the ball into the box for Kiszkis. The west Londoners' no.9 took her time, rode a challenge and then smashed home from close range to make it 5-1. Williams' side went close again as Cheatley almost scored a spectacular left-footed volley, but sent it too high, and Teale arrived at the back post from a Smith corner but fired wide. The floodgates had opened and Harris-Walters added a sixth shortly after coming off the bench, improvising a half-volleyed finish after controlling the ball with her chest to score her first of the season. Then, on 68 minutes, Teale capped her brilliant performance off with a goal, opening her account for the 2026/27 campaign. After breaking into the box, she chopped past her defender and struck a fierce effort into the bottom corner as the Bees went 7-1 up. Aylesford did pull one back with 20 minutes to play, when Rebecca Keyte headed home from a free-kick. Kiszkis went desperately close to scoring her third, bending an effort that bounced inches past the post, before Freya Worsley fired a strike narrowly wide. With just over five minutes left on the clock, Kiszkis did get her hat-trick, striding into the box and striking across the keeper with her left foot to make it 8-2. It was an excellent display after going behind and in the end a comfortable victory with a rotated squad. Williams' side have started the season with a bang, winning their opening three league games as they now prepare for a tough away day at Hammersmith FC. Brentford: Francis-Pownall, Phillips, Teale, Potter, Kiszkis, Smith (Worsley 69), Cheatley, Louvrier, Gilligan (McCrea 59), Black (Berry 69), Constantine (Harris-Walters 59) Aylesford: Rider, B. Burnham, Davids, Bradding-Butler, Richardson, Keyte, Blyghton, Phillpot, Sone, A. Burnham, Pepper-Scott Subs: Lambu, Apthorpe, O'Neill, Baxter, Eiffert Williams: We learn and develop as a squad Brentford Women head coach Carly Williams was pleased with how her side reacted to a slow start in their big victory over Aylesford. "There's no denying we had six players missing and the ones that came in and started who maybe haven't the last few weeks did really well," she said. "We learn and we develop as a squad. That's the reason we've gone away over the summer and built a really good squad. "Everyone stepped up, that's what we look at, can we push ourselves to be better every day."

articles.body: Match Preview: Brentford U21s v Sunderland U21s | Brentford FC | Brentford FC Sam Saunders’ Brentford Under-21s return to Premier League 2 action at Wheatsheaf Park on Monday when they host Sunderland Under-21s (1pm kick-off BST). After a busy opening to the season across the Premier League Cup and PL2, the young Bees will be hoping to make it two league wins from as many games. The west Londoners have started positively at both ends of the pitch this season, keeping a clean sheet in a 2-0 Premier League Cup win over Wycombe Wanderers and scoring three goals to beat Stoke City U21s in PL2 Saunders' side have enjoyed a spread of goalscorers, with Josh Dasilva Michel Boni Kaye Furo and Theo Mawene each netting so far this campaign. Last time out Brentford impressed on their way to a 3-2 win away at Stoke. Furo got the Bees off to a flying start with an early goal, with Mawene following suit later on in the first half with a brilliant individual effort. Theo opening his account 🤩 pic.twitter.com/Zj0R8GK23s — Brentford Academy (@BrentfordFCPDP) August 21, 2026 The hosts pulled one back before the break, but Saunders’ side reacted positively out of half-time to piece together a superb early move before Jayden Meghoma ’s cross was turned into the Potters’ net by a defender. While Stoke scored a second goal to make the latter stages of the second half tense, the Bees held on to take home all three points. About Sunderland U21s Sunderland sit second in the PL2 table following a dominant 5-1 win over Nottingham Forest in their season opener. Trey Ogunsuyi starred for the young Black Cats with a hat-trick, while Jack Whittaker and Timur Tutierov also got on the scoresheet in the impressive victory. Sunderland also got their Premier League International Cup campaign under way with a 1-1 draw against PSV U21s. Led by head coach Matt Craddock, Sunderland will return home for their next two PL2 fixtures, which are against Ipswich Town and Norwich City. Match information Tickets for Monday's clash are now available to purchase here Adults - £5 U18s – Free *Please note a 1% transaction fee will be added to transactions. **Under-14s must be accompanied by an adult. Match coverage Supporters can follow live updates from the game against Sunderland across the club's social media channels , with a full match report available on the club's official website and app shortly after full-time. The game will also be streamed live here.

articles.body: Brentford U21s 5 Sunderland U21s 1: Kaye Furo hat-trick and Fábio Carvalho on scoresheet as Bees win on PL2 home debut | Brentford FC | Brentford FC Kaye Furo was in scintillating form, bagging a hat-trick as Brentford Under-21s maintained their impressive start to the 2026/27 season with a 5-1 victory over Sunderland Under-21s in their first Premier League 2 home fixture at Wheatsheaf Park. Furo also provided the assist for Fábio Carvalho’s goal, with Riley Owen scoring the fifth, in a game which saw first-team players Benjamin Fredrick, Ji-soo Kim, Gustavo Nunes and Josh Dasilva feature for Sam Saunders’ side. It was a blistering start from the home side as Owen picked up possession and, inside the first minute, slid the ball through to Furo . The striker showed composure to take the ball around the goalkeeper before slotting into the empty net to give his side the lead. Nunes was next to go close as he attempted a delightful chip which beat the goalkeeper but clipped the top of the crossbar. Sunderland had chances of their own, with Trey Ogunsuyi firing a volley from inside the box which Reggie Rose stretched low to his corner to tip around the post. Minutes later, a fine move from the visitors on the edge of the box saw Jack Whittaker break into the area with the ball, but with only the goalkeeper to beat, he dragged his shot wide. On 33 minutes, Furo could have had his second of the game as he was found by Owen once again, but this time his effort flew over the bar. Ogunsuyi tested Rose again as he swivelled inside the box and struck a shot on target, but the goalkeeper got down well to hold onto the ball. Just before the half-time whistle, Furo powered through on goal in similar fashion to his first goal after being played through by Rose, but on this occasion he skewed his left-footed effort wide. Sam Saunders' side began the second period with an increased tempo, as Nunes and Owen had chances to score but they sent their efforts wide from close range. The deserved second came on 52 minutes as Furo picked up a loose ball before calmly playing Carvalho through, with the midfielder slotting the ball past Joe Cowan. The young Black Cats halved the deficit when Charlie Dinsdale sent a cross into the area which deflected off Rose and into the net, with the goalkeeper unable to keep the ball out. Despite the setback, the home side restored their two-goal advantage, with Furo grabbing his second as he found himself well placed to volley Nunes' corner into the net. Second-half substitute James Barker almost made an immediate impact for Sunderland as his first effort after coming on struck the post with Rose beaten. Furo completed his hat-trick firing low and hard past Cowan from just inside the area with a fantastic finish. There was still time for a fifth as Owen, who had been energetic throughout the game, broke clear and found the finish to match his powerful run into the box, leaving the goalkeeper with no chance. Brentford would take home the three points as the Bees march on in the PL2. Brentford now turn their attention to their second Premier League Cup game where they travel away to take on Hull City on Tuesday 8 September. Brentford U21s: Rose, Fredrick (Shield 46), Picotto (Wheeler-Henry 46), O'Connor (Klimas 78), Ji-soo, Grey, Nunes, Owen, Furo, Dasilva (Holland 26), Carvalho (Wilson 78) Subs not used: Wolfheimer, Boni Booked: Nunes 45, Rose 90+2 Sunderland U21s: Cowan, Jones (Holcroft 61), Lightfoot, Whittaker, Neild (Bell 61), Kindon, Dinsdale (Barker 81), Munyakazi (Hester 61), Ogunsuyi, Proctor, Jones (Scorer 81) Subs not used: Metcalf, Scott Booked: Jones 63, Bell 90+4 Saunders: Attitude and work ethic were spot on Brentford Under-21s head coach Sam Saunders reflected on the attitude, discipline and attacking threat shown by his side in their 5-1 victory over Sunderland Under-21s in Premier League 2. "The attitude, the desire and the work ethic from the players were top," he said. "We knew we had to find solutions to their aggressive press, and I thought Kaye was outstanding. The players who played around him managed the game really well, and the longer the game went on, the more open it became for our attacking players. "Yes, we could have taken more of our chances, but we did switch off in some small moments. Even though we were in control, we could have been more decisive in those key moments. We have to remain committed and focused for the full duration of the game, because the more they tired, the more opportunities we had to score. "The minimum we ask is that the players work hard and are good people, and the players who came off the bench and did well are a testament to that, as are the players who didn't make the squad. It shows the strength we have within the group and the collectiveness of the team. There was no sulking; they just got their heads down and worked hard."

articles.body: Analysis: Vitaly Janelt and Mamadou Sangaré partnership excels in Brentford v Leeds United draw | Brentford FC Brentford's attacking trios have rightly earned plaudits over recent Premier League seasons - but the early indications are that their midfield will jostle for top billing this term. The Bees had to share the spoils at Elland Road against Leeds United on Sunday, but head coach Keith Andrews declared he was "very proud" of his side's performance in an entertaining 1-1 draw in West Yorkshire. Dominic Calvert-Lewin tapped home from close range late on to cancel out Kevin Schade 's 41st-minute opener and earn the hosts a point - their manager Daniel Farke afterwards describing Brentford's form as "red-hot". Brentford were, indeed, excellent for large swathes of the contest and their midfield pivot of Mamadou Sangaré and Vitaly Janelt was central to an impressive performance. Sangaré delivered another outstanding display to fuel his growing reputation as one of the star signings of the summer transfer window, and the Mali international has quickly forged an impressive partnership with Janelt. Alongside Mathias Jensen , who was ruled out by injury against Leeds, Sangaré and Janelt bossed proceedings in the 3-0 opening-weekend win over Tottenham Hotspur and again stole the show for long periods at Elland Road. "That is UNBELIEVABLE!" 😱 Kevin Schade with a stunning finish to give Brentford a deserved lead against Leeds pic.twitter.com/IwmWd8sOUu — Sky Sports Premier League (@SkySportsPL) August 30, 2026 Snapping into tackles and linking play superbly, the midfield duo set the tempo in a commanding first-half performance that saw the visitors deservedly lead at the break after Schade conjured up a delightful flick from Keane Lewis-Potter 's low cross from the left. So far this season, Brentford's destructive tendencies without the ball have been balanced with control in possession in the middle of the park, and Sangaré and Janelt's statistics told a story on Sunday. They combined to win seven tackles and eight interceptions over the course of the encounter, and also won three aerial duels between them. On the ball, Sangaré (56) completed more accurate passes than any Brentford player, while Janelt's tidy distribution was evidenced by an assured 85 per cent pass completion rate. Brentford fired in 22 shots to Leeds' 12 and the way in which they penned back their hosts, particularly prior to the interval, bodes well for the rest of the season. Goalscorer Schade won a penalty during a typically high-energy performance against Spurs on the opening weekend, and the German's sublime finish against Leeds opened his account for the 2026/27 campaign. The 24-year-old has scored 22 Premier League goals for the Bees since moving to west London at the start of 2023, and Schade now sits eighth on the division's all-time list of prolific German players after overtaking Leicester City cult hero Robert Huth (21 goals). The draw also preserved Schade's status as something of a lucky charm: Brentford are still yet to lose a game in which he has found the back of the net.

articles.body: West Ham U18s 5 Brentford U18s 4: Jai Nwosu hat-trick not enough as Bees defeated in nine-goal thriller | Brentford FC | Brentford FC Jai Nwosu scored a hat-trick but Brentford were narrowly beaten 5-4 by West Ham United in an entertaining U18s Premier League contest on Saturday morning. The young Bees twice held the lead at Little Heath Sports Ground but were ultimately edged in an exciting end-to-end game, with Nwosu’s treble unable to prevent the hosts from claiming all three points. The young Bees took the lead on five minutes with their first chance of the game as Jovan Kasujja delivered a perfect cross for Nwosu , who acrobatically steered the ball into the net. Despite the goalkeeper getting a strong palm to the effort, he could not keep it out. The young Hammers were not behind for long, though, as Bailey Pammenter pounced on a fantastic through ball before striking a firm effort which squirmed underneath Layton Nicholls On 29 minutes, Brentford went back in front as Jai Bansoodeb capitalised on a mistake from Tommy Goodger, with the goalkeeper heading the ball straight into the midfielder’s path. Bansoodeb calmly slotted the ball into the net. Nwosu could have added a third before the break as he rose highest to meet a Nathaniel Ogungbemi cross, but his firm header whistled just wide of the post. The striker had another opportunity to extend Brentford’s lead after doing well to fend off his opponent and break through on goal, but with only the goalkeeper to beat, he skewed his effort wide. Gary McDermott’s side began the second period on the front foot, but West Ham were awarded a penalty after Charles Gadsdon was brought down following a powerful run into the box. Joel Kerr stepped up and calmly converted from the spot. Pammenter then grabbed his second of the game, reacting quickest after Nicholls had parried an initial effort from Gadsdon on the edge of the box to put the home side ahead. Second-half substitute Christlife Mandungu went close to extending West Ham’s advantage when he smashed an effort from outside the box against the crossbar. The home side had turned the tide and were creating a number of opportunities, with Dylan Danso and Josh Oladapo-Gamu making important interventions on several occasions. Nwosu was then played through on goal and produced a delightful finish, chipping the goalkeeper to bring Brentford level. The striker completed his hat-trick in spectacular fashion, scoring another chip, this time from outside the box, to put the young Bees back in front. Mandungu then curled an effort into the net to level the scores once again. Frankie Day ultimately had the final say, pouncing on a Brentford loss of possession before getting beyond Micaiah Fanoiki and rounding Nicholls to score the winner. It was a tough defeat for the young Bees in an entertaining match. McDermott's side are next in action on Saturday 5 September when they host Aston Villa. West Ham: Goodger, Montague (Day 60), Kerr, Omotoye, MacAj, Agyemang, Lila (Madungu 60), Gadsdon (Ugate 56), Pammenter (Longman 60), Peychev (Noble 82), Magowan Subs not used: Tomlin, Smith. Booked: Day 68 Brentford: Nicholls, Fanoiki, Danso (Biggs 85), Oladapo-Gamu, Ogungbemi (Zetter-Plummer 46), Cohalan, Noni (Roca 60), Bansoodeb (Trialist A 82), Kasujja, Nwosu, Madden Subs not used: Lyon, Mason, Serme Booked: Roca 90+3

It does not automatically show who you should buy. GW2 is a perfect example: several huge returns came from players with very different minutes, fixtures and underlying roles. Fetching the latest information from Fantasy Premier League Blog ← Back Blog STRATEGY FPL GW1 Template & World Cup Fatigue Guide 2026/27 FPL Ranker July 26, 2026 The best FPL GW1 template for 2026/27 balances the near-essential premiums against World Cup fatigue. Haaland (≈71% owned) remains the default captain and forward, but managers who went deep into the summer tournament face a compressed pre-season and rotation risk. Build around fresh, nailed assets, exploit Manchester United’s soft opening fixtures, use £4.0m promoted-team defenders as enablers, and hold your Wildcard until GW2–GW4 once minutes settle. The GW1 template: who’s essential in 2026/27 Early ownership points to a clear premium core: Erling Haaland (≈71%), Bruno Fernandes (≈46%), João Pedro (≈46%), Dominik Szoboszlai (≈38%) and Morgan Rogers (≈37%) are the five most-owned players. Haaland is the one near-mandatory pick — his ownership sits more than 25 percentage points clear of anyone else, so leaving him out is a genuine rank gamble in GW1. Managers currently agree far more on the premium attackers than on goalkeepers and defenders, so the cheap end of your squad is where you can find an edge. World Cup fatigue: who to fade The 2026 World Cup final was played only weeks before kickoff, and players involved in the latter stages got roughly three weeks away from club football — so late returners carry real rotation risk in GW1. Even Haaland is not risk-free: Norway’s run to the quarter-finals means his pre-season is compressed, so watch Manchester City’s team news before committing the armband. The flip side is fresh legs: England left Cole Palmer and Phil Foden at home, so both come into the season with a full pre-season behind them. Turn fatigue into a GW1 edge Spend up where minutes are certain and save where they are not. Exploit soft opening fixtures — Manchester United open against promoted Hull and Ipswich, which is why Bruno Fernandes and Matheus Cunha appear in so many early drafts. Use £4.0m promoted-team defenders (all Coventry, Hull and Ipswich defenders are priced at £4.0m) as enablers so the money flows to nailed premium attackers. Do not chase a fatigued £12m+ midfielder you will captain nervously — a fresh, nailed mid-priced attacker with a full pre-season is often the better GW1 points source. When to Wildcard after the World Cup The community splits between GW2, GW3 and GW4, with GW3 the popular pick. Waiting lets you see who is actually rotated before you spend the chip. Practical rule: draft a GW1 team you would happily run for three weeks, then Wildcard around GW3 once rotation patterns and early price rises reveal the true template. Avoid Wildcarding in GW1 — you would be spending your most powerful chip on incomplete information. FAQ What is the best FPL GW1 template for 2026/27? A premium core of Haaland plus two of Bruno Fernandes, João Pedro, Szoboszlai and Morgan Rogers, funded by £4.0m promoted-team defenders and mid-priced nailed attackers. Haaland is the one near-essential pick; the defence is where managers disagree and you can find an edge. Is it worth going without Haaland in GW1? Which players should I avoid in GW1 2026/27? When should I use my Wildcard after the World Cup? articles.body: How to Get a List of All Team IDs in Your FPL Mini-League — FPL Ranker Loading FPL Data... Fetching the latest information from Fantasy Premier League Blog ← Back Blog tips · cover TIPS How to Get a List of All Team IDs in Your FPL Mini-League FPL Ranker August 13, 2026 What an FPL team ID is Every Fantasy Premier League squad has a permanent numeric team ID, sometimes called an entry ID or manager ID. It appears in the URL of any manager's team page: fantasy.premierleague.com/entry/1234567/event/1 — the 1234567 is the team ID. The ID is public. It is how the official Fantasy site links to a squad, and it is what third-party tools ask for when they load someone's team. It is not a password and it grants nobody access to your account — knowing your ID lets someone view the same public squad page that the official league table already links to. The manual method: one ID at a time Open your mini-league on the official Fantasy Premier League site, go to the Standings tab, and click a manager's team name. That opens their squad page, and the number in the URL after /entry/ is their team ID. Copy it, go back, and repeat for the next manager. This works, but the official standings page never shows the IDs as a list — so a 20-manager league means 20 round trips through the URL bar, and there is no export. That is the whole reason this question gets asked. The fast method: the Ambassador tab Each ID links straight to that manager's official Fantasy squad page, and Export CSV downloads the whole roster — rank, team, manager, team ID, total points, gameweek points, the official FPL link and an FPL Ranker link for each manager. Copy list puts the same roster on your clipboard for a group chat. It is sign-in gated on purpose. A roster of manager names and IDs should not be bulk-scrapeable by anyone who happens to know a league code, so exporting is tied to a real account. 1. Open the Ambassador tab on your league. 2. Export CSV pulls every team ID into one file. (IDs are blurred in this screenshot; yours show in full.) What to do with the list The common use is comparison. With every ID in one place you can pull up any rival's squad, see their captain, and check their transfers without hunting through the official table each week. The export opens straight in Google Sheets, Excel or Numbers. Every row is one manager — rank, team name, manager name, FPL team ID, total points, gameweek points, a link to their official Fantasy squad and a link to their FPL Ranker page — so you can sort it, filter it, or paste a single column into whatever tool you use next. The other use is the one the tab is named after. Share the CSV in your league chat so everyone can paste their own ID into a tool and see their season — rank movement, gameweek headlines, and where they actually gained and lost ground. A mini-league is more fun when everyone can see the story, not just the table. The same export opened in Google Sheets — one row per manager, ready to sort, filter or share. Why does the official FPL site not show all the team IDs? How many managers can I export at once? Fetching the latest information from Fantasy Premier League Blog ← Back Blog tips · cover TIPS FPL Gameweek 2 Captain Picks and Transfer Targets 2026/27 FPL Ranker August 27, 2026 For FPL Gameweek 2, Haaland remains the safest armband despite his opening blank, with João Pedro and Cole Palmer the strongest alternatives at home to a depleted Brighton. Bruno Fernandes and Bryan Mbeumo face Ipswich at Old Trafford. The most-bought players are De Cuyper, Sangaré and João Pedro; the most-sold is Pedro Porro. The deadline is Friday 28 August at 18:30 BST. Gameweek 2 deadline and fixtures The Gameweek 2 deadline is Friday 28 August 2026 at 18:30 BST, 90 minutes before Crystal Palace host Manchester City to open the round. The gameweek then runs across four days and closes with Aston Villa v Arsenal on the Monday night. On the official Fixture Difficulty Ratings, the softest assignments belong to the home sides in Chelsea v Brighton (2), Man Utd v Ipswich (2), Tottenham v Newcastle (2), Sunderland v Fulham (2) and Coventry v Hull (2). The hardest single fixture on the slate is Aston Villa v Arsenal, rated 4 for both teams. The full round: Crystal Palace v Man City (Friday), Liverpool v Nottingham Forest, Bournemouth v Everton, Coventry v Hull, Tottenham v Newcastle (Saturday), Chelsea v Brighton, Leeds v Brentford, Sunderland v Fulham, Man Utd v Ipswich (Sunday), Aston Villa v Arsenal (Monday). Gameweek 2 captain picks Haaland (£15.5m) is still the default. One blank against Bournemouth does not undo the profile — he took five shots in that match, and he is captained by more managers than anyone else in the game for a reason. Crystal Palace away is rated 3 rather than 2, which is the only real argument against him, and it is a thin one. If you are happy taking the field-average outcome, this is the pick. João Pedro (£7.6m) is the aggressive alternative. Chelsea are at home to a Brighton side missing Yankuba Minteh for at least a fortnight, with Carlos Baleba, Kaoru Mitoma and Stefanos Tzimas all doubts, and the fixture is rated 2. João Pedro scored and assisted in the 3-2 win at Fulham and is now owned by 67.6% of managers, so this is a low-risk pivot rather than a punt. Cole Palmer (£9.5m) is the higher-variance version of the same fixture. He is on penalties and set pieces, he recorded the highest BPS total of Gameweek 1 (60), and he is owned by only 15.2% — captaining him is a genuine differential inside a soft home fixture. Bruno Fernandes (£12.0m) and Bryan Mbeumo (£8.0m) are the contrarian route: Ipswich at Old Trafford is a 2, and both are coming off a two-point return that has driven roughly 188,000 and 175,000 managers to sell them. The uncomfortable read is that Haaland, João Pedro and Fernandes are all owned by a third or more of the game, so none of them is a rank-mover in a big mini-league. Palmer at 15.2% is. Which of those matters depends on whether you are protecting a lead or chasing one — the mini-league standings on FPL Ranker will tell you which of the two you actually are before you set the armband. The Scout GW2 squad The Scout squad for Gameweek 2 lines up 3-5-2 and lands at just under the £100m budget, built around a triple Arsenal spine at the back and the two Manchester United attackers at home to Ipswich. Haaland takes the armband. The bench is deliberately cheap — Dúbravka in goal, Drameh and Slater from Hull, and Walle Egeli from Ipswich — which is the standard early-season shape: spend the money on eleven starters and accept that the bench is there for autosubs rather than for Bench Boost value. The official Premier League version of the Scout selection is published separately as a Wildcard-and-new-starter template and is worth reading alongside it. Transfer targets: who the market is buying Maxim De Cuyper (Brighton, £4.6m) is the most-bought player in the game with roughly 421,000 moves in after his 17-point opener. He has already risen £0.1m. The caveat is the fixture: Brighton travel to Chelsea in Gameweek 2, which is the hardest assignment on their card for weeks, and Brighton are missing several attackers. He is a good buy on role and price; Gameweek 2 is not his best entry point. Mamadou Sangaré (Brentford, £5.6m) is second with roughly 359,000 moves in, and he is the more fixture-proof of the two. Two assists plus 13 defensive contributions in Gameweek 1 is exactly the dual-route profile that defensive contribution scoring rewards — his floor does not depend on Brentford keeping a clean sheet. Leeds away is rated 3. Behind them, João Pedro (roughly 326,000 in), Palmer (292,000), Riccardo Calafiori (276,000), Michael Kayode (270,000) and Martin Ødegaard (253,000) are all being bought. Calafiori, Kayode, Ødegaard, De Cuyper, Sangaré and João Pedro all rose in price on 27 August — the first price changes of the season. If you are choosing between them on fixtures rather than form, Liverpool have the best run in the game from Gameweek 2 to Gameweek 5 (average difficulty 2.50), followed by Leeds, Man City, Newcastle and Tottenham on 2.75. Arsenal have the worst of the traditional big six at 3.50, with trips to Aston Villa, Chelsea and Brighton in that window — worth weighing before you buy a third Arsenal defender. Who to sell, and who is flagged Pedro Porro (Tottenham, £5.5m) is the most-sold player in the game at roughly 293,000 moves out after recording zero minutes in Gameweek 1. Ollie Watkins (roughly 212,000 out) and Viktor Gyökeres (193,000) are in the same boat and have both dropped in price. Morgan Gibbs-White (Nottingham Forest, £8.0m) is second on the sold list with a knee injury and a 75% chance of playing, away at Liverpool. That is a straightforward move if you can make it without a hit. Other flags to check before the deadline: Moisés Caicedo and Marc Palestra (Chelsea), Bruno Guimarães (Arsenal), Jack Hinshelwood (Brighton), Matheus Nunes (Man City), Amad (Man Utd) and James Maddison (Tottenham) are all listed at 75%. Ismaïla Sarr (Crystal Palace) is injured with no return date, Dan Burn (Newcastle) is expected back on 14 September and Jérémy Doku (Man City) on 5 September. Hinshelwood is the one that stings — he scored 16 points in Gameweek 1 and is now doubtful. On hits: with the market this active it is tempting to take a -4, but Gameweek 2 is early enough that most of what looks broken is a squad-shape problem rather than a one-player problem. Fix it on a Wildcard once minutes settle. If you want a read on which of your own players are genuinely underperforming rather than merely unlucky, the Rank My Team verdict on FPL Ranker grades your XI on form, minutes and fixtures. articles.body: Is My FPL Team Good? Rate My FPL Team Score Explained | FPL Copilot Back to blog Rate My Team is FPL Copilot's free squad rater: enter your Team ID and the Copilot Score rates your Fantasy Premier League squad from 0 to 100 on projected points, captaincy, bench, fixtures and budget, then names the single change that helps most. 80 and above is elite, 60 to 79 is strong, and below 60 means your squad has a structural problem. Is your squad actually good, or does it just feel good? Here is what the score measures, what a good number looks like, and how to move it. Rate your team, right here. Enter your Team ID, or drop a screenshot of your squad. Free, no sign-up. Drop a screenshot of your team What Is the Copilot Score? The Copilot Score is a 0-100 rating of your FPL squad setup for the upcoming gameweek. Not just "are your players good" but "is your team set up to score the most points possible this week." I check five things: Starting XI strength. Total xPts for your first team. Simple question: are your best players on the pitch? Captain pick. Are you captaining the highest-xPts player? Most managers aren't. It's the easiest free points in FPL. Bench strength and order. A good bench catches auto-subs when rotation hits. A bad bench costs you. I check both the quality and whether your bench order is right. Fixture outlook. Great players with terrible upcoming fixtures are a ticking time bomb. Budget flexibility. Money in the bank and free transfers give you room to react. Zero flexibility means one injury away from a crisis. What Is a Good Copilot Score? 80 and above is elite. 60 to 79 is strong. Below 60 means something structural is wrong: a weak bench, a suboptimal captain, bad upcoming fixtures, or money locked in the bank. Three markers do most of the work if you want to sanity check it by hand. Projected xPts above 55 for your starting XI is good. Your captain should be the highest-xPts player you own. Your bench should be three or four nailed 4.0m to 5.0m starters, not non-playing fodder. The Copilot Score rolls those three plus fixture outlook and budget into one number in about two seconds. 0-100 Copilot Score Squad rating Factors XI, cap, bench, fix, budget Free trial Pro experience Just your Team ID Get your squad rated right now. Rate My Team → How to Improve Your Score Fix your captain first. This is almost always the biggest quick win. If you're not captaining the highest-xPts player, just switch. That alone can move your score by 10-15 points. Check your bench order. Your highest-xPts bench player should be first sub. Over a season, good bench ordering gains you 5-10 points from auto-subs. Takes 5 seconds. Most managers never bother. Don't hoard money. 0.5m in the bank is flexibility. 2.0m in the bank is a player upgrade sitting on the bench. That money should be on the pitch scoring points, not collecting dust. Rate My Team vs the Solver Rate My Team is the diagnosis. The Solver is the treatment. One tells you what is wrong, the other tells you which transfers fix it. Run the rater for the score, run the solver for the moves. Score below 60? You probably need transfers. Score above 80? You're set. Save the free transfer and roll it. Where Do I Find My FPL Team ID? Log in at fantasy.premierleague.com, go to Pick Team, then click Gameweek History. The number at the end of the URL, straight after /entry/, is your Team ID. It is public information, safe to share, and it is the only thing the rater needs. Here's a tip: rate your team before AND after making transfers. If the score doesn't improve, the transfer probably wasn't worth it. It takes seconds. Save yourself a hit. How strong is your squad? Enter your Team ID. I rate your starting XI, captain, bench, fixtures, and budget. Free to try, instant. Rate My Team More from Copilot Expected Points Explained The data behind the rating. articles.body: What Is FDR in FPL? Fixture Difficulty Explained | FPL Copilot Back to blog FDR (Fixture Difficulty Rating) is FPL's 1-to-5 ranking of how hard each Premier League match is for a team. Green means easy, red means hard, yellow sits in the middle. Managers use FDR to plan transfers and chips around easy fixture runs. The live 2026/27 FDR ticker (sortable, all 20 teams) Easy Hard SUN home, sun away The ticker ranks all 20 Premier League teams by total fixture difficulty over the next 3, 6, 8 or 10 gameweeks, so the team at the top of the list has the easiest run across the window you pick. If it has not loaded, the full FDR ticker is the same data on its own page. Prefer the full-screen version with every sorting option? Open the FDR ticker → FDR on its own is a great starting point. Here is what it actually tells you, where it falls short, and how to pair the live FDR ticker with xPts to fix the gaps. What Is FPL FDR? FDR is the Fixture Difficulty Rating that appears next to every fixture on the official FPL site. It is a number from 1 to 5 assigned to each opponent per gameweek. Lower is easier. FDR 1: the easiest tier on paper. FPL almost never assigns it, so real fixture runs bottom out at 2. FDR 2: easy fixture (green). Good transfer target. FDR 3: neutral (yellow). FDR 4: hard (orange-red). Rotation risk territory. FDR 5: very hard (red). Usually top-4 opponents away from home. Teams are rated based on form, recent results, attacking strength, and defensive strength. The algorithm updates after each gameweek so FDR is not static across the season. 1-5 FDR scale Lower is easier Gameweeks FDR updates weekly 1-6 Planning horizon GWs to check ahead How to Use FDR for FPL Transfers Plan five to six gameweeks ahead, never one. Sum a team's FDR across your window and sort by the lowest total: over three gameweeks the range runs 6 to 15, and in practice anything under 9 is a genuinely soft run while 11 or more is one to swerve. The workflow: Check 5-6 gameweeks ahead. Find teams with three or more green fixtures in a row. Those are your transfer targets. Avoid red fixture runs. If a player you own has four FDR 4-5 fixtures, sell unless their individual xPts is still elite. Stack 3 teams with green runs. Concentrate your 15 players in clubs with the best fixture swing. The 3-per-club limit still applies. Use FDR to time chips. Wildcard before a green swing. Bench Boost in a DGW with easy fixtures. Free Hit in a BGW. See which fixtures your squad faces Check Expected Points → Why FDR Alone Is Not Enough FDR is a rough team-level signal. It cannot tell you what matters most for FPL scoring: Home vs away split. FDR treats Arsenal (H) and Arsenal (A) as the same difficulty. Home teams score 30% more goals on average. Real difficulty is very different. Style matchups. A high-press team vs a long-ball team is easier than vs a possession team. FDR ignores style. Individual matchups. A fast winger vs a slow fullback is a green fixture for that player even if the team FDR is red. Rotation risk. FDR does not know if Pep will rest Haaland or if Arteta will rotate Saka. The easy fixture means nothing if your player sits on the bench. Set-piece duties. Two players in the same team with identical FDR can have very different ceilings based on penalties and free kicks. Using FDR alone is like picking a restaurant by postcode. It narrows the field but does not pick the meal. xPts vs FDR: What Actually Predicts FPL Points Expected points (xPts) is what FDR becomes when you combine it with every other variable that matters. The FPL Copilot xPts model processes 50+ data points per player per gameweek: Fixture difficulty (including FDR) Home vs away split Opponent xG conceded, xG against, and defensive style Individual player xG, xA, shots, key passes Projected minutes and rotation risk Set-piece duties (penalties, free kicks, corners) Clean sheet probability for defenders and keepers Bonus point patterns from BPS history Everything FDR captures plus everything it misses. For captain picks, transfers, and chip timing, xPts is the single number that matters. 50+ Data points Per player per GW 73% Top-5 accuracy Captain picks +20-30 Season gain vs form-based picks Where FDR Still Wins FDR is free, official, and easy to read at a glance. Three use cases where it is still the right tool: Season planning at a high level. Looking 8+ weeks out, FDR gives a reasonable team-level fixture swing picture before individual xPts data stabilises. Quick vibes check. Glancing at next week's FDR before deadline to confirm nothing obvious is wrong. New season pre-draft. Before the first ball is kicked, FDR is often the only signal available because there is no xG or form data yet. Once the season is underway, xPts beats FDR on every gameweek-to-gameweek decision. But FDR as a sanity check never hurts. Common FPL Fixture Planning Mistakes Only checking next week. FPL transfers reward 5-8 GW horizons. Planning one week ahead misses the 2-week holds that win leagues. Ignoring home/away. A home FDR 3 often beats an away FDR 2. Assuming FDR 5 means zero points. Premium attackers (Haaland, Saka, Bruno Fernandes) still return against top defences. Fixture-proof players exist. Reacting to one bad fixture. Selling after one red match when the next three are green is a classic mistake. Forgetting DGW and BGW. FDR does not flag blank or double gameweeks. Check the FPL calendar separately. FDR narrows your shortlist. xPts picks the winner. Use FDR to scan teams with easy runs, then use the xPts table to find the specific player inside those teams with the highest ceiling. That is how every elite manager plans transfers. Which players have the best fixtures? articles.body: FPL Chips 2026/27: Chip Strategy & When to Play | FPL Copilot Back to blog TL;DR Your FPL chip strategy for 2026/27 comes down to timing, not luck. You get two sets of chips, one for each half of the season, and the first set expires at the Gameweek 19 deadline. Do not rush them. Wildcard on a fixture swing, Bench Boost in a double gameweek, Free Hit on a blank, Triple Captain on your best premium in a high-ceiling week. Here is the plan. Copilot verdict WAIT The most common chip mistake is playing them early out of boredom. Hold each one for the moment it is designed for. Patience is the whole strategy. I ran the chip optimizer over 300+ real squads to find out what timing is actually worth. Optimal chip timing gained an average of 49 points against a no-chip baseline, and 69% of those squads gained between 40 and 60 points. That is from timing alone, with no extra transfers. +49 points gained avg from optimal chip timing 69% of squads gained 40-60 points 300+ real squads tested every valid chip combination How FPL Chips Work in 2026/27 You start the season with a full set of chips: one Wildcard, one Free Hit, one Bench Boost, and one Triple Captain. The first set has to be used by the Gameweek 19 deadline. A fresh set unlocks for the second half, and you can only play one chip in any single gameweek. That structure is the strategy. Two Wildcards, two Bench Boosts and two Triple Captains across the year means you rarely need to force one. Wait for the right gameweek and the same chip is worth far more. When to Play Your First Wildcard Not in the opening weeks. Fixture difficulty and form only settle after about six gameweeks, so an early Wildcard spends information you do not have yet. The strongest first-Wildcard window is usually a clear fixture swing once the season has taken shape, often in the run toward the first set of double gameweeks. Use the live FDR ticker to spot the swing: when a cluster of teams flips from red fixtures to green, that is your Wildcard trigger. I test every valid chip combination for thousands of squads. The ones who guess their timing lose 40-plus points to the ones who wait for the data. Chips are patience, not gut feel. When to Play Bench Boost and Triple Captain Bench Boost: a double gameweek where all 15 of your players have two fixtures and a nailed bench. Build toward it with a Wildcard the week before so every bench slot is a starter, not fodder. Triple Captain: your best premium in a double gameweek or a soft home fixture. Haaland with two games is the textbook target. Do not waste it on a single tough fixture. Free Hit: a blank gameweek where half your squad has no fixture. Free Hit is a one-week rescue, so timing beats squad quality here. Remember the one-chip-per-gameweek rule. You cannot Bench Boost and Triple Captain the same week, so a double gameweek forces a choice between them. FPL Chips 26/27: Guides by Gameweek GW1 and GW2 are played and the next deadline is Gameweek 3 on Friday 4 September at 6.30pm. If you are playing a chip this week, these are the live ones, each with the solver-built squad or armband on current projections: Wildcard GW3: best draft and template squad Free Hit GW3: best team for one gameweek Triple Captain GW3: who to captain Further out, or back at how the early chip weeks looked: Triple Captain GW5: who to captain Bench Boost GW2: best squad and bench picks What Are the FPL Chips? FPL chips are one-off boosts you play on a single gameweek. There are four, and each does one thing: Wildcard. Unlimited free transfers for one gameweek, with no points hits. The new squad is permanent, so you draft for the weeks ahead. Free Hit. Unlimited free transfers for one gameweek, but your squad reverts afterwards. You are renting a team for a single week. Bench Boost. Your four bench players score as well as your XI, so all 15 count instead of 11. Triple Captain. Your captain scores triple instead of double for that gameweek. You play one chip per gameweek at most, and each is worth far more in the right week than the wrong one. That gap is what this guide is about. Build a First-Half Plan Now Two gameweeks in, you still do not need to lock exact gameweeks, but you should know the shape: hold through the opening run, Wildcard on the first real fixture swing once form has settled, then chain Bench Boost and Triple Captain through the winter doubles before the Gameweek 19 deadline. Check your own squad against that shape in the chip planner , or sort the expected points table over the next six gameweeks to see where your fixture swing actually lands. What's your optimal chip timing? Enter your Team ID and I test every valid Wildcard, Bench Boost, Triple Captain and Free Hit combination for your exact squad. Brentford were similarly ruthless, beating Tottenham Hotspur 3-0 at home, while Chelsea edged Fulham 3-2 in the Monday night fixture thanks to goals from JoÃ£o Pedro, Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer. Manchester City needed late goals from Marc GuÃ©hi and Josko Gvardiol to see off Bournemouth 2-1, and Newcastle United shared the points with Liverpool in a 2-2 thriller. Igor Thiago of Brentford failed to score despite a high expected-involvement afternoon and a missed penalty. These blanks will have hurt ranks for managers who loaded up on the expensive Manchester options - in contrast, those who backed Arsenal's defenders or Brighton's attackers enjoyed a strong start. Lessons for Gameweek 2 Gameweek 1 rewarded secure roles with favourable fixtures over pure reputation. Brighton's attacking full-backs and midfielders thrived, while Hull's organised defence produced both clean-sheet points and goals. Promoted sides showed they can't be taken lightly - Hull and Leeds both claimed wins, and Ipswich edged Sunderland. Clean sheets for Arsenal, Everton, Hull and Brighton will encourage continued investment in those defences, though fixture swings arrive quickly. Chelsea's attacking trio of Palmer, Rogers and JoÃ£o Pedro looked lively at Fulham and could stay attractive.
